102827.name: Blaze
102827.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Blaze is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Blaze has shown fearful behavior in his time at the care center, including collaring, backing away, and head whipping when handlers attempted to place it. He has also displayed hard barking with a tense, forward body toward an unfamiliar staff members and is generally shutdown in the care center. Blaze has additionally been observed heavily panting and pacing in his kennel, suggesting difficulty settling in his kennel. Outside of these situations, Blaze walks well, accepts treats, and has shown no reactions to dogs or people on walks. Medically, Blaze has an ear infection and suspected chronic dermatitis.

Blaze was surrendered by his previous owner due to moving into a building that didn't allow animals. His previous family described him as a dog with a medium energy level, is not picky, and will eat most foods or treats. He enjoyed cuddling with his people and seeking attention; he can be very affectionate and prefers to spend his time around people. He is noted to hard bark at new people and takes time to settle. On walks, he is reported to hard bark and lunge at other dogs and strangers. During his intake, Blaze escalated to hard barking and hard staring at staff and would not settle. After being placed in his kennel, he began growling and snapping at the hook that was used to remove the leash. Blaze has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

107337.name: Pepper
107337.summary:
Meet Pepper!
Pepper is an 11-year-old sweetheart who has spent the past several years in foster care, getting lots of love, learning new things, and experiencing different homes. Her fosters all describe her as deeply loyal, loving, and full of personality. She is now more than ready for a forever home where she can finally settle in and enjoy her golden years.

Personality
Pepper is a loving and intelligent girl who really enjoys connecting with her people. Her foster shares that she is very communicative and often "talks" with her body language, including adorable head tilts when she is trying to understand what you are saying. She is very tuned into her humans and loves being part of daily life.

She is also clever and has a funny way of training her people too. If she wants to be near you, she may move between her bed and you until you bring her closer, showing just how much she enjoys companionship. She is affectionate, observant, and happiest when she is included.

Home Life
Pepper is a loving couch companion who enjoys both relaxed days inside and calm outdoor adventures. She is fully house trained and does not destroy things in the home. She enjoys toys and is food motivated, which makes her very engaged in learning new cues and behaviors.

Once she learns a routine, Pepper does well staying home alone for periods of time as long as she understands her person will return. Her foster describes her as adaptable and very in tune with household rhythms.

Social Behavior
Pepper loves her people deeply but prefers slow introductions with new individuals. Once she feels comfortable, she becomes very affectionate and enjoys belly rubs, ear scratches, and quiet companionship on the couch.

She does not get along with other dogs and can become nervous around them, so she needs to be the only pet in the home. She has been working on redirecting her attention back to her handler and continues to improve with support.

My Ideal Home
Pepper will do best in a calm adult or teen only home as an only pet in a quiet neighborhood. She thrives in peaceful environments where she can relax, bond closely with her person, and feel secure. She would love someone who enjoys a steady routine, cozy couch time, and a loyal shadow by their side.

Things to Know
Pepper is treat motivated and enjoys learning new cues. She is smart, attentive, and enjoys working with her people. She has been in multiple foster homes who all adore her and would happily support her transition into a forever home. She is a long stay pup with a reduced adoption fee and is more than ready to finally have her own family.

Fun Fact
Pepper's foster says she is basically a professional cuddle partner and couch companion. Her favorite place in the world is right next to her person, especially if belly rubs are involved. She has a big heart and is just waiting for the right home to finally call her own. 🐾

110052.name: Lulu
110052.summary:
A volunteer writes:
I met Lulu when she was only 6 month old. She was a real ball of fiery fun(see her video). Five years down the line, we met again. Although I really enjoyed the young and bold Lulu, I so much prefer her mature version. Lulu's owner became increasingly allergic to her dander and had to bring her back to the Manhattan Care Center. Lulu is now a bit on the heavy side and a tinsy winsy shy in the busy and noisy shelter environment.She comes right away to salute me, head bunting my hand, leaning into pets and purring loudly(see her new video). She sometimes retreats in her cubby but comes back right away for more cuddles. She even drops to her kennel floor for more in depth petting. I really like Lulu who without any doubt will make a most loving and loyal companion and for many years to come. Lulu is already spayed, apparently healthy(beside being overweight) and did very well on her behavior evaluation. She is sooo ready to go home with you..today. Come and meet Lulu very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!
Addendum:love, Love,  love Lulu. We had the greatest and sweetest time in the interaction room. She LOVES being with a visitor and makes you feel soooo welcome(see second video). Lulu deserves a great home and a great home deserves Lulu!!!!!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!

116078.name: Autumn
116078.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!
My purr motor is always running!
Autumn is at the front of the den, looking out curiously in the loaf position, sweet and relaxed. She ate squeeze-up treats and enjoyed petting and gave a little head bunt to the assessor's hand. She was calm when pet on her cheek and along her back and remained in place, sweet and fairly relaxed. She's a sweet kitty. After the kennel door was opened, she came out of the den to eat more treats and was then coaxed farther out with more squeeze-up. She arched her back with back petting, gave another head bunt, and was calm when briefly picked up and set back down.

Autumn interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

118683.name: Kobe
118683.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! 


Meet Kobe!
Kobe is a fun-loving, affectionate guy who has unfortunately found himself back at ACC after first coming through our doors as a puppy. Most recently, he was found roaming loose on his own looking for help, and now he's hoping his next home will truly be forever. Kobe is full of personality, absolutely adores people, and never says no to cuddles, treats, or a chance to learn something new.

My Ideal Home
Kobe is looking for an experienced, active adopter who can continue building on the training he's already started. He's incredibly food-motivated, eager to learn, and has made great progress with cues like "sit," "off," and "leave it." He'll thrive with someone who enjoys reward-based training and can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and structure to help him channel his enthusiasm.

Good with Other Pets?
Kobe previously lived with other pets. At the shelter, he enjoys meeting other dogs but can become a little overexcited and sometimes struggles to read when another dog wants space. Slow introductions are recommended, and ACC advises against dog parks so he can build appropriate relationships at his own pace.

Good with Kids?
Although Kobe previously lived with children and was described as wonderful with them, his current shelter behavior shows he's still working on his impulse control. Because of his jumping, mouthiness, and resource guarding, ACC recommends an adult-only home where he can continue his training successfully.

Things to Know
Kobe is an energetic, affectionate dog who loves toys, treats, and being close to his people. He's currently enrolled in ACC's Shelter Scholar program, where he's making fantastic progress learning new skills, including relaxing on a mat and settling himself. He's highly responsive to positive reinforcement and continues to improve his leash manners every day. Like many shelter dogs, Kobe can feel anxious in the kennel environment, but with patience, consistency, and continued training, he's already showing just how much he's capable of learning.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes:
We met Kobe the day before a big blizzard, but it wasn't our first meeting. We first met him five years ago when he was just a puppy with his whole life ahead of him. Back then he weighed only 43 pounds and looked adorably lanky in our photos. Today he's a handsome 78-pound adult, and we still believe his best years are ahead of him.

After recently being found running up to a kind stranger with two small dogs looking for help, Kobe found his way back to ACC. Despite everything, he's still the same affectionate boy who happily sidles up for cuddles. This time around, we also discovered how much he loves toys! Watching him learn, play, and lean into affection reminds us what a wonderful companion he can be.

Kobe's story isn't unique. Adult dogs are often overlooked, even though they have so much love to give. Thankfully, Kobe is making the most of his time by participating in ACC's Shelter Scholar program, where he's learning valuable skills that will help him thrive in a home. Every day he shows just how smart, eager, and deserving he is. Now all he needs is someone willing to give this lovable goofball the forever home he's been waiting for.

119114.name: Deuce
119114.summary:
A volunteer writes: Good boy Deuce was brought to us when his owner became ill and could no longer care for him. Deuce has been fearful in the shelter environment, and he can get excited around other dogs, jumping up and sometimes a bit too exuberant. We think that Deuce would be the best dog in a home with calm, supportive adults, who can go slow and give Deuce the option to walk away from any social interaction, at his own pace. Deuce should never be forced to approach anything that he is uncomfortable with, such as petting or handling. Deuce would do best in a quiet home environment where he can acclimate to his new surroundings. We'd love to see this middle-aged guy back on the couch in a home where he belongs! 


What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

119182.name: Beau
119182.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Beau is on the at-risk list due to behavior. Although he is displaying social behaviors in the shelter, Beau does have a multiple bite and scratch history in his previous home. It would be in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience managing cats who rough play and may be prone to overstimulation.

A volunteer writes:
Beau is a handsome tiger with beautiful eyes and elegant stripes who was adopted as a kitten and relinquished into our care as his rough play and manners could not be managed by his owner anymore. At the care center, Beau is calm in his kennel, well mannered and comes to meet his visitor as soon as his door is open. He is vigilant, paying attention to moves and sounds but appreciates petting, head bunting my hand and leaning although never rolling on his side. He really gets excited with catnip toys and feather wands, his tail slightly quivering. Beau has been for a while at the care center, I guess because of his past history but also the fact that he is on a special diet(likely for the rest of his life to prevent urinary blockage) for crystals in his urine. Beau needs a home, not a cage, an experienced owner, a calm while stimulating and nurturing home to thrive as a loving and easy to handle pet. Could it be with you?



Beau is at the front of the kennel, leaning against the door to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he immediately comes forward to greet the assessor with soft head bunts. Beau allows and leans into all petting, occasionally tail flicking but not escalating with extended petting. He calmly walks out of the kennel and is easily picked up, remaining calm when held and continuing to tolerate all further attention when placed back into the kennel.  

Beau interacts with the observer, solicits/ appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Beau go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in rough play, new home adjustment, and overstimulation.

119915.name: Champ
119915.summary:
There is an adorable video of me on ACC's TikTok page. Click here to experience the cuteness! 

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
Champ is a bundle of love! He can't wait to snuggle up and pass out on your lap after a good kissing and licking session! He loves people and is easy to be around. Very well mannered and easy going guy. He can work on being around other dogs and after he's found his forever home his anxiety will likely subside as well. He's a one of a kind dog overall!

My foster writes: 
Champ is, well, a Champion of many things. But above all - he is a champion cuddler. A crowned cuddle king, who will literally leave a bowl of food behind if it means he has a chance to snuggle next to you and get a belly rub. He loves so deeply and unrelentingly, even shortly after you meet him - he'll gaze at you with soulful eyes and lick your face if you let him. Champ seizes any chance to love and be loved by his human. He's like a heated and weighted blanket combo, ready to comfort you. Champ has a huge heart that matches his huge head. He's smarty (of course his head is so big, it holds his smarts!) - he picks up on training cues quickly, whether working on his tolerance for being left alone. He's learning leash manners with positive reinforcement and clicker/treat training. When he hears the click and gets it right, he stamps excitedly and smiles, awaiting his "good boy!" Followed by a treat. This Champ doesn't need a cheerleader but if you want to see him do his stamp, wide-smile victory dance, definitely cheer for him! He seems to trust humans more readily than other dogs, but with the right dog and slow introduction, Champ might also love a canine friend - but he's fully content just being with his human. He sleeps through the night, even when he's not next to you. But I'm sure he'd prefer to be by your side. He's also a great ride-along boy, hanging (and sometimes sleeping) quietly in the backseat with his seat belt buckled. Potty trained and not destructive when left alone, Champ is a solidly wonderful boy whose love and devotion are so unrelenting, you'll wonder how you ever got so lucky to be his friend.


Dogs with Level 2 determinations are believed to be suitable for adopters with some previous dog experience. They will have displayed behavior in the shelter (or have owner-reported behavior) that requires some training, behavior management or modification. Dogs with a Level 2 determination may have multiple potential challenges and these may be presenting at differing levels of intensity, so careful consideration

He's smarty (of course his head is so big, it holds his smarts!) - he picks up on training cues quickly, whether working on his tolerance for being left alone. He's learning leash manners with positive reinforcement and clicker/treat training. When he hears the click and gets it right, he stamps excitedly and smiles, awaiting his "good boy!" Followed by a treat. This Champ doesn't need a cheerleader but if you want to see him do his stamp, wide-smile victory dance, definitely cheer for him! He seems to trust humans more readily than other dogs, but with the right dog and slow introduction, Champ might also love a canine friend - but he's fully content just being with his human. He sleeps through the night, even when he's not next to you. But I'm sure he'd prefer to be by your side. He's also a great ride-along boy, hanging (and sometimes sleeping) quietly in the backseat with his seat belt buckled. Potty trained and not destructive when left alone, Champ is a solidly wonderful boy whose love and devotion are so unrelenting, you'll wonder how you ever got so lucky to be his friend. Dogs with Level 2 determinations are believed to be suitable for adopters with some previous dog experience. They will have displayed behavior in the shelter (or have owner-reported behavior) that requires some training, behavior management or modification. Dogs with a Level 2 determination may have multiple potential challenges and these may be presenting at differing levels of intensity, so careful consideration

129302.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Dylan Piper, a pretty and plump four year old Tortie was adopted from us as a tiny kitten. For some unclear reason, she was spotted roaming for days a backyard without food and water. She is safe now within the care center where she is charming everybody with her sweet personality(she was not a fan of the veterinary team, though but she enjoyed her ride in a police car). What a lovely gal, gentle, quiet but curious and sociable, happy to have a visitor she treats with head bunting, purring and biscuits making. Dylan Piper is a real treat, a lovely kitty with no known history but who has a chance to turn a new and happy page in her life...with you! Come and meet Dylan Piper very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!

132206.name: Roy
132206.summary:
My Foster writes: Regal Roy is a king or maybe just a prince. As the photos show he is handsome, well kept, suuuuper soft and a great pal around my apartment. He's really good at NOT scratching anything but the sisal cat tree furniture I have in my living room. He also is good about the litter box. I made sure to change the litter from pine to clay. Now I make it a mixture of corn and fragrance free clay, and we are golden. He's my little shadow and likes to trill/chat with me sporadically throughout the day. Interesting behavior he luvs cheek rubs on both sides and he doesn't purr.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Roy interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience, demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: Roy looks around like he's double checking that it's ok that he's here. He wants to fit in and do his best, but seems to always be asking if it's alright. Our enthusiastic reassurance that we love having him here takes a few moments to click but once it does, Roy demonstrates his well known practice of practically nosediving into our arms. Taking up the space he should, Roy rolls around like a baby seal, reveling in his time as the center of attention. He's known to be an exuberant playtime enthusiast with a whole roster of fun games he knows and wants to play. Roy has been with us before and we know that he's going to shine in his forever home.

132683.name: Dymond
132683.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!

A volunteer writes: Our videos of Dymond are filled with exclamations about how stinking cute she is over and over again. She lets us dress her up in a little polka dot frock with a matching headband and the colors compliment her bright doe eyes and white and brindle fur. But her beauty isn't just skin deep. At ten years old, she is a gentle and unassuming soul who eagerly awaits her turn for walks or time in the play yard.

Dymond was originally adopted in 2021 after being found as a stray. Her guardians say that she has been friendly with the children in the home. She spent most of her time in the bedroom or in her crate. She is accustomed to 4-5 walks a day. Dymond was known to be vocal in the household, alert barks at strangers and had a penchant for stealing bites of her human's food. Due to some handling sensitivity and reported anxiety in the home, Dymond is available to a L3 home with kids over the age of 13. She has met numerous dogs while in the shelter and has been friendly and playful but at times more interested in getting treats from handlers.

135802.name: Rasputin
135802.summary:
My foster writes: Rasputin is a velvet-pawed gentleman who will steal your heart (very quietly). This stunning white beauty is a professional hide-and-seek champion who starts off as a shadow under the couch, but once he trusts you hes a total love bug! He'll flop over for belly rubs, roll around like a total goof, chatter back at you in the sweetest meows, loves a good brush, and chases wand toys in hilarious circles like a kitten chasing his own tail.
Rasputin dreams of a calm, low-traffic forever home with patient humans who will give him the time he needs to blossom. If you've ever wanted a cat who goes from mysterious Russian mystic to rolling cuddle monster the moment he knows he's safe... Rasputin is waiting to cast his spell on you.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Rasputin is in the back of his den, laying horizontally and observing the assessor with slightly dilated pupils as the den cover is lifted. When attempting to pet him he flinches on initial contact, allowing all petting but remaining tense, turning his body to face the back wall and avoid contact. He allows light pressure on his abdomen but is not able to be coaxed out of his den, so pickup is unable to be attempted. 

Rasputin tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will likely need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

136762.name: Juno
136762.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Juno is on the at risk list for medical reasons. He is a friendly senior cat who was diagnosed with diabetes at the shelter. Juno will require long-term medical management for this disease. Juno has allowed for all medical handling and solicits attention during his exams.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!

What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!

A volunteer writes: Showing me his belly and his chirpy little purr, Juno introduced himself to me by rolling over onto his side. A very sweet senior who finds himself here for the second time through no fault of his own, Juno has been trying his best to show how much he has to offer and all that can be if only he can find someone to give him a little chance. Friendly and outgoing around new people, he's said to seek quality time and will stretch out on the sofa in his efforts to be close. Most adorably, Juno loves to play and will do so very gently in an effort to respect everyone else's boundaries. We'd love so much for Juno to get a chance at a forever home. Please come and meet him at the Queens Care Center.

138738.name: Safari
138738.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Senior Safari is with us as his house counted too many pets. More of his friends are scheduled to join us in the near future. Safari is a handsome and welcoming gent who stops what ever he is doing to meet his visitor. He likes presents(treats) of course but cuddling is what he is really after. He was a bit reserved when I first met him but it is 100% history. Safari is a well mannered and collected kitty who keeps clean quarters and uses his litter box. According to his former owner, Safari was not allowed by his housemates to share the litter box and this is why, to prevent spraying, the owner kept him in a crate. At the care center, we have not observed this issue. Although well dressed  and apparently healthy(he does have senior teeth, though), Safari is a bit on the thin side. He aced his behavior evaluation and could go home today with you which would make this day, the most beautiful one in his whole life! Safari is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!








What my friends at ACC say about me:
I love getting pets!
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
Safari was at the front of the kennel, looking curious and sweet. He enjoyed treats, which he seemed to enjoy very much, while also appreciating petting. He was then reasonably calm when picked up, struggling slightly, and remained curious at the front when set back down, where he resumed eating treats.

Safari interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience, provided they are counseled on spraying behavior likely connected to being unneutered.

143426.name: Mandarin
143426.summary:
My foster writes: Hi! I am a kind and happy cat who loves cuddling and gentle play. I'm middle-aged so I don't have the energy of a young kitty, but I'm very well-behaved, calm, and affectionate. I am quite curious about new people and new environments but I'm not destructive, and I don't have an aggressive personality.
I am quite independent during the day, but will come to you to cozy up at night (I'll reach out around your neck with my paws for cuddles, and let you hug me for hours). I'm always up and ready for playtime in the morning too (I love my toy mice and feather fishing-rod). I am very tidy, potty-trained, and groom myself frequently.
I have never lived with other animals or children, so I may not be suited for those kinds of environments.
If you want a well-trained cat with a gentle demeanor, a loving and trusting personality, and big, beautiful eyes, I'm your man!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a shy, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

A volunteer writes: With a hopeful kitty smile, Mandarin made his way over to the front where he nuzzled the door and lowered his head to sweetly headbutt my hand. Mandarin doesn't ask for so much but watching him try so hard to get something small kind of breaks my heart. Mandarin has been with us before, though through no fault of his own, and he knows very well that he might have to work a little bit harder to stand out in a sea of bright and sparkly kittens and standing right at the front of his condo, that's exactly what Mandarin's been trying to do. He's a soft and cuddly boy who just needs another chance.

I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

A volunteer writes: With a hopeful kitty smile, Mandarin made his way over to the front where he nuzzled the door and lowered his head to sweetly headbutt my hand. Mandarin doesn't ask for so much but watching him try so hard to get something small kind of breaks my heart. Mandarin has been with us before, though through no fault of his own, and he knows very well that he might have to work a little bit harder to stand out in a sea of bright and sparkly kittens and standing right at the front of his condo, that's exactly what Mandarin's been trying to do. He's a soft and cuddly boy who just needs another chance.

143570.name: Keroppi
143570.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Keroppi :) he is the quietest dog you'll ever meet, with the most playful energy. He is around 5-6 years old but he gives off such puppy energy. He is the most perfect indoor dog, he is an angel in the house. No accidents, does well with commands especially with a toy or treats, knows his bed, only goes for his toys to chew.
With puppy energy sometimes gives puppy behavior. He does need some work on the leash. He gets excited and will pull especially on a good scent. He will try to chase after ANY ball he sees in the park. Treats and/or toys on a walk work to advantage, he does better with an incentive.
He has room for improvement but he is the most amazing dog to have around. He brought so much love into our house and anyone will be lucky to have him


Keroppi is a fun-loving and clever pup enrolled in our Shelter Scholars program, where he's working on polite exchange, learning how to trade toys or treats calmly and cooperatively. Through consistent training and trust-building, Keroppi is mastering cues like drop it and trade, proving that sharing really does bring more rewards.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I need a home without cats or small animals.

145118.name: Mika
145118.summary:
Hi!  My name is Mika! Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Apply for me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! Here's what my friends at ACC say about me: 

My foster writes:
Mika is a very loving and sweet dog. She wants nothing more than to lay with you on the couch or bed and snuggle up to you or to bring her ball to you and play. She has been learning to walk nicely on the leash and absolutely loves being outside. She is friendly to people and kids and greets everyone with her tail wagging. Mika does snore when she sleeps and can even snore when she's awake! She takes treats very gently and knows how to sit, stay or give paw for treats. She will benefit from plenty of exercise, food puzzles and interaction with you. She should be the only pet in the home and, because of her strength and excitability, a home with no small children.

My foster writes: If I had to describe Mika in a single word, it would be exuberant! She is a joyful and loving companion who wants to become friends with every living creature she meets. While she is certainly energetic she is also equally cuddly, and is happy following a good round of exercise with cuddling close on the sofa to watch a show. She's also so eager to please that she learns quickly, having picked up several new commands with minimal effort. She would be certain to brighten any home she enters!

Mika is a fun-loving pup who loves to explore her surroundings. She is still adjusting to being around other dogs, cats, and squirrels, and is working on her leash manners. Mika has a lot of energy and would benefit from a patient, experienced owner who can help her reach her full potential.  With the right home, Mika could thrive and become a loyal companion


My ideal home: Mika will succeed in an experienced home without tiny humans or other animals.

145664.name: Neima
145664.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Lovely Neima was adopted as a kitten from the Manhattan Care Center. She was surrendered with housemate Comet as allergies became a growing issue in their home.
Neima is said to be a timid gal, gentle with everybody around and very friendly with Comet who is quite an outgoing cat. Neima is shy, it is a given but she is slowly getting used to her new surroundings. She loves to be talked to, slow blinks and leans softly into my hand. Neima clearly is a very sweet gal who still needs time to find her bearings. Neima is already spayed, did well on her behavior evaluation(that points to her shyness in the shelter), is apparently healthy and could go home today with you. Ask to meet Neima when you visit us at the care center!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.

5/26/26
Neima has improved since her first assessment, and even though she gave a single hiss on the initial approach, she sniffed treats and then gave slow blinks while allowing petting. The petting went on for some time on her head, and she relaxed her body, becoming softer and slowly closing her eyes. She's doing well and just needs a gentle approach.

Neima tolerates and seems to appreciate attention and petting but appears to be moderately nervous or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

146665.name: Bruno
146665.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Bruno is at risk for behavior reasons. Bruno was surrendered because he was not getting along with a member of the household. Bruno had escalated to giving this person a warning bite, which did not break the skin. He is reactive to other dogs, and on one occasion bit a dog while on a walk. This bite did not break the skin. He requires an experienced owner familiar with managing his reactivity. Bruno has done well with staff and volunteers in the care center, warming up quickly with a considerate approach. Medically, he is over conditioned and has some dental disease.  

Meet Bruno, a handsome and loyal dog looking for the right experienced home. Bruno will thrive with an owner who understands dog behavior and is comfortable managing leash reactivity. He can be reactive toward other dogs while on walks, and due to his size and strength, he will do best with someone who has experience working with and continuing to train dogs with these behaviors.

Bruno is seeking an adult-only home where he can enjoy a predictable environment and build a strong bond with his people. One of Bruno's great qualities is that he has previously lived successfully with cats, showing that he can coexist peacefully with feline companions. With the right guidance, structure, and commitment, Bruno has the potential to be a wonderful companion for someone willing to invest in his success.

150048.name: Nilah
150048.summary:
The foster writes:
Nilah is a sweet girl with a mysterious past. Although a bit fearful, you can tell she always wants attention and to be loved. She will talk back when spoken to and will follow you around your home- at a distance!

Nilah is the sweetest lovebug there is! Although shy, she will love you with her entire being once she gets comfortable. She loves spending time with you and will always want attention and pets. She's a proper lady that won't get into any trouble or be aggressive. Check out her cute elevator butt and ability to engage in a 2-way conversation!

Nilah is a quiet gentle adult cat. She loves being touched and loves brushing especially berry massages, she loves so much that she can groom you back to continue your massaging her. She can't tolerate holding. She inspects the entire apartment and will report you back with the results with a cute meow. Nilah can surprise you with how a shy and fearful cat can transform in time to be friendly, learn new tricks, play with toys, and start showing her love of humans. She needs extra time to adjust to new environments, but you will love to spend time with her.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

150628.name: Nena
150628.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Meet Nena!
Nena is a gentle girl who came to the care center when her owner could no longer care for her. She is looking for a patient, understanding home where she can take her time to feel safe and build trust at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Nena would do best in a calm home with a predictable routine and a patient adopter who will let her open up slowly. She can be shy in new environments, so she'll thrive with gentle encouragement, consistency, and space to decompress as she adjusts.

Good with Other Pets?
Nena has been noted to ignore dogs on walks and has a history of living with another dog. However, during some introductions she has shown stiffness with unfamiliar dogs, so slow, careful introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to Nena's shy and cautious nature, she would do best in a home without very young children (under 5). Older, respectful children may be considered once she has had time to settle in.

Things to Know
Nena can be timid when first meeting new people and environments, often showing a tucked tail and soft body language. Once comfortable, she allows handling and may approach with coaxing. She walks well on leash with no pulling and does best with slow, positive introductions to new experiences. Nena is still learning to fully relax in unfamiliar settings, so patience and routine will be key in helping her gain confidence and feel secure.

Fun Fact
Nena may be shy at first, but she has a quiet, gentle presence that shines through once she feels safe. She's looking for someone who will let her bloom at her own pace.

151788.name: Coco
151788.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Coco is on the at-risk list due to medical concerns. Coco has a large, ulcerated mass on his side that is suspected to be cancerous.  He also has moderate-severe dental disease.  He will need further evaluation with a veterinarian for dental treatment and mass removal.  Mass removal may be palliative but not curative. Behaviorally, Coco has been sweet and tolerant of handling in care. His owner reports Coco is fearful, loud noises (fireworks, thunderstorms) are difficult and had one bite incident when he was in a confined space without a way to retreat.

Coco is a friendly, affectionate male dog who loves being around people. He has a playful, active personality but also enjoys settling in for a relaxing nap, making him a great mix of adventure buddy and couch companion. Whether he's following his family around the house or spending time in the basement, Coco is happiest when he's part of the action.

Coco rides wonderfully in the car, making him an excellent companion for errands or road trips. He knows his name and responds to cues such as "sit" and "lay down." His previous owner shared that one of their favorite things about Coco is that he has stayed playful and full of spirit despite his recent changes.

Coco has a large mass which will require follow up care. If you're looking for a loyal, affectionate dog who loves to play, enjoys car rides, and is always happy to be close to his people, Coco may be the perfect companion for your home.

152588.name: Piccolo
152588.summary:
My foster writes: Don't let the face fool you - Piccolo might look like he's judging your life choices, but underneath that adorably grumpy expression is one of the most affectionate cats you'll ever meet.
Piccolo is all about closeness - snuggled up right next to you, leaning into every pet, and while laying his body across you he makes for a good weighted blanket! When it's time to play, Piccolo is all in. He throws his whole body into it, sometimes falling into the wall with how excited he is to chase after whatever you throw at him. Piccolo also has a real talent for flopping into the most ridiculous positions, including his favorite carefree belly-up legs splayed out sprawl.
With his unbothered scowl and heart full of love, Piccolo is the perfect mix of sass and sweetness.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I came in with my friend Monkeybread and would love to find a home with them!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

153042.name: Cedar
153042.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Apply for me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

There is an adorable video of me on ACC's Instagram page. Click here to experience the cuteness! 

My foster writes:
Are you ready to welcome a bundle of happiness into your life? Look no further, because Cedar is here to steal your heart and fill your days with endless joy! This lovable companion is eagerly waiting to find her forever home, and she's bound to be the perfect addition to any family.

Cedar's incredible demeanor makes her an ideal companion for all your daily adventures. Housebroken and well-mannered, she understands the rules and won't jump up on furniture, ensuring a seamless transition into your home. Her favorite game is a spirited game of tug, and you'll find immense joy in sharing these playful moments with her.

Cedar's crate training adds an extra layer of convenience to her adaptable nature. Whether you're working from home or heading out for errands, she's content and secure in her crate. And speaking of working from home, Cedar is the ultimate coworker. She's more than happy to snooze by your feet as you work, providing both companionship and comfort.

Strolls around the neighborhood are a true delight with Cedar by your side. She approaches walks with a leisurely pace, savoring every moment and taking in all the captivating scents along the way. Her curiosity and appreciation for the world around her are a constant reminder to find joy in life's simple pleasures.
Cedar's endearing qualities have won the hearts of everyone she meets, making her a favorite among shelter volunteers. Her unwavering spirit and genuine affection make her an exceptional companion that's ready to fill your life with happiness.

Don't miss your chance to adopt Cedar and make her a cherished member of your family. Her playful antics, loving nature, and heartwarming presence are sure to bring a smile to your face every day.

Cedar is the ultimate couch potato and professional snuggler. She could spend the whole day curled up next to you while you catch up on your favorite shows or get lost in a good book. She's a total homebody-happy with a couple of short walks, a game of tug, and plenty of treats. She's also housebroken and, despite being a bit of a big girl, does just fine in smaller spaces as long as she's with her people.

She's incredibly loving once she knows you, but she can be a little shy with new people. She needs slow introductions and a little patience, but once she trusts you, she's all in. Cedar tends to feel more comfortable around female-presenting folks

154929.summary:
The foster writes:
Bun Bun is a very sweet and friendly bunny
He loves when you give him lots of love
He especially loves when you give him full body rubs
When he gets comfortable he cuddles into a little loaf
He is litter trained. Bun Bun loves making new friends and he is great when many people are playing with him.

157433.name: Oreo Diplo
157433.summary:
Meet Oreo Diplo!
Oreo Diplo was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now this easygoing sweetheart is ready for his next chapter. His previous family described him as "the best," and it's easy to see why! He's a low-key guy who loves people, enjoys a comfy place to lounge, and still has a playful side when the mood strikes.

My Ideal Home
Oreo Diplo would love a home where he can enjoy the simple things in life like cozy naps, tasty treats, leisurely walks, and spending time with his people. He'll thrive with positive, reward-based training and a family that can continue reinforcing his good manners while giving him plenty of love.

Good with Other Pets?
Oreo Diplo has lived successfully with other dogs and is described as friendly with familiar canine companions. At the shelter, he enjoyed playful interactions with another dog, engaging in mutual play with appropriate breaks. As with any new friendship, slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his enthusiastic greetings and occasional mouthiness when excited, ACC recommends a home with no young children.

Things to Know
Oreo Diplo is a social, affectionate dog who loves meeting people and can get a little bouncy when he's excited. He may become protective of especially valuable food or objects, so trading for something equally exciting instead of taking items directly from him will help him continue building positive habits. He also enjoys staying engaged with his surroundings on walks and will benefit from continued reward-based training and enrichment.

Fun Fact
Despite being a self-proclaimed couch potato, Oreo Diplo still knows how to have fun. Whether he's making new friends, showing off his playful side, or curling up for a well-earned nap, he's happiest when he's with his favorite people.

163999.name: Dakota
163999.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Apply for me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:

Affectionate, curious and caring, Dakota has it all.

Fully housetrained, Dakota can be left alone for several hours on her own without any risk of incident.

Dakota loves everyone. She came to ACC after getting glowing reviews from her previous home, one that included multiple adults, children and other dogs. She has also done well when subsequently being introduced to cats in a foster setting.

She wants to know what you're thinking and will cutely tilt her head when you speak. And she will attentively play with various toys, while also listening to commands like "sit", "paw" and "down". She will let you know when she wants to receive some affection with gentle pawing or resting her head nearby or on your knee.

On walks, she can be excitable on leash when passing larger dogs within tight settings because of her loyalty, but the rest of the time she's as docile as can be. She is excellent in the open space of the dog park, and even comes to the defense of other dogs when they are being bullied. While she has high energy when outside, she is very relaxed inside the home.

If you're looking for a jogging companion, Dakota is happy to run alongside you. You can see in her profile she enjoys running along the water and even on NYC bridges. She also is great in a car and loves a good hiking experience for outdoor recreation.

Dakota is super cute and happy to get dressed up in various outfits. She is a big fan of the Giants, Yankees, Knicks and Rangers, and she doesn't hate the Jets and Mets. She's allegiant but would be open to adopting a new team. She's also happy to wear festive holiday attire. Even without the outfits, she gets lots of compliments while on walks just for being who she is.

She may take a small amount of time to warm up to new people, but once she does, she will love you forever. While she was living with children in her previous home, she has yet to be introduced to children in a household setting since being fostered.

She of course loves to be pet and encouraged, but Dakota also really enjoys a "spa day" in the bathtub and getting belly rubs. And she appreciates her beauty sleep (and it's been working!). On a typical day, Dakota will sleep in until being woken up, sometimes even late into the morning. She is typically curled up on the couch and happy to be pet as she is waking up. Then she is patient as her caretaker is getting ready themselves while waiting to be given breakfast and go out for her first walk.

Dakota is truly ready to breathe life into a fresh home and can't wait to be a great addition to her new family!

164311.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with dogs.
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Please check here for updated adoption hours.
I can go home today!

A volunteer writes: Two adorable young joyful dogs were left tied up together in front of our shelter. The first is Unicorn, who looks like a baby. She's white and gray and teeny tiny. About one year old, she is highly social, and super fun. She zoom zoom zooms around the yard, stretching her legs and getting her steps in! When introduced to dogs, she offered the other dog play bows and bounces. She can be a tad shy at times, but is a lovely girl ready for a level 2 home. 

A volunteer writes: Is it too on the nose to dress a dog named Unicorn in a unicorn costume? Not when the nose is this cute we say! 

Unicorn does not protest when we dress her in this silly costume, she is far too happy to just be outside with people showing off her impeccable wiggles. Just about every single thing she does we find delightful, from her big mouthed grin to the way she flops onto our laps. 

She has true unicorn status: she is said to be social with dogs, tolerant of cats and friendly with kids. The 🦄 trifecta! At the shelter she has proven to be an easy breezy happy girl, walkable by even our newest volunteers. 

This is Unicorn's second time at the shelter. In 2023 she arrived to our Brooklyn location after being found tied up with another dog. She was adopted and has lived happily in a home since then but was surrendered again after her owner was unable to afford her medical care (she has some dermatitis that will need medical attention).  She is reported to love car rides and being close to any people in a room. She is available to a Level 2 adopter in a home with children over 5 years old.

165161.name: Pikachu
165161.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Pikachu is at risk due to behavioral concerns. While Pikachu has readily accepted treats with a soft mouth and is somewhat easy to remove from the kennel, he has not acclimated well to the shelter environment. He has shown concerning levels of escalation towards handlers when returned to his kennel. When attempting to conduct his handling assessment, Pikachu began growling at the assessor when they greeted him. His warning was respected, and he was returned to his kennel. Once in his kennel, he spins around on the handler, growling, hard barking, lunging, snapping, and on one occasion briefly thrashed coming out of the kennel, but needed to be stiff-armed upon return. Medically, Pikachu is underweight and has mild-moderate dental disease.

Pikachu came into the care cneter as an owner surrender due to his owner not having time for him anymore. In the prior home it is noted that Pikachu knows the cue "sit" and loves car rides. He is not bothered by being handled and allows his family to bathe him with ease. He enjoys quality time and will likely be in whatever room has people in it. Pikacu has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

167649.name: Minosh
167649.summary:
My foster writes: Minosh is a curious adventurer with a playful spirit. Always ready to explore new nooks and crannies, she's also a professional batter of scrunched up receipts - she loves to play this game! With a knack for finding the sunniest spots in the house, she brings warmth and joy to her humans with just a lil touch of spicy to keep you on your toes!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Minosh  is shy but calm and was in the den looking out, poked her head out to sniff treats, and then ate treats in the den while enjoying gentle petting, leaning in for cheek rubbing. She could not be coaxed out while the assessor was present but did come out for treats after he had stepped away but then went back into her den when she was done eating.

Minosh tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately nervous or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
Please check here for updated adoption hours.

A volunteer writes: Minosh isn't loving the Care Center and she's trying her best to navigate it. And just like any of us, her best looks different everyday. Minosh was brought to us because her person passed away and, with so many big changes, we know she needs some time to find her footing. Minosh likes to play it safe, so I often see her thinking strategy in her cubby. Minosh knows she has to find her forever family, but she's not completely sure on how to put herself out there. She'll come forward for sniffs and treats, but she might also retreat for a moment to gather her thoughts. She's a kitty who wants to carefully consider all perspectives, so she's looking for a patient family who can follow her lead when it comes to pets, cuddles, and playtime. After a few minutes together, Minosh nuzzled my hand and I felt a sense of accomplishment. I love making friends with kitties who feel a little unsure, but Minosh is a kitty who sometimes needs a little reset after meeting new friends. So, after a couple of pets, she returned to her cubby to dream about meeting you.

His original owner described Balto as gentle, loyal, and playful, he enjoys spending time with family, going for walks, and relaxing by your side. Balto walks nicely on leash, loves car rides, and is house-trained, making him an easy companion to have around the home. He knows several cues in both English and Spanish and is eager to please, especially when rewarded with praise, belly rubs, and attention. Balto enjoys walks in the park, playing with toys, and snacking on his favorite treats. If you're looking for a loving dog who will happily be your shadow and best friend, Balto may be the perfect match.

175474.name: Brock
175474.summary:
Meet Brock!
Brock was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and has since shown himself to be a smart, social, and affectionate "brindle potato" with a big heart and an even bigger personality. He's a true people-lover who enjoys making friends wherever he goes and settles into routines quickly.

My Ideal Home
Brock would do best with an adopter who understands resource guarding and can manage mealtime and high-value items appropriately. He thrives with structure, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He especially enjoys food-based activities like training games and puzzle toys, and will benefit from calm, consistent handling around valued items.

Good with Other Pets?
Brock has shown mixed but generally social interactions with other dogs in care, including loose and playful moments. His comfort level can vary, so slow, supervised introductions are recommended if living with another dog. He has shown strong reactions to cats and would likely do best without feline companions.

Good with Kids?
Due to resource guarding behaviors and mouthiness with food, Brock would do best in a home without young children.

Things to Know
Brock is a highly food-motivated, intelligent dog who learns quickly and enjoys working with his people. He can be clumsy and excitable at times, but also knows how to settle in and enjoy quiet companionship. He benefits from clear routines and positive reinforcement, especially around food and high-value items. With guidance, he is a wonderful mix of goofy energy and calm couch cuddles.

Foster Notes
My foster writes: Meet Brock, a beautiful brindle potato with a heart of gold! Brock was so sweet and trusting with us from the get go, and I believe he will easily bond with anyone who shows him love and takes good care of him. He is very smart and observant and picks up on routines quickly, knows lots of commands such as sit, stay, come, down and paw, and has a lot of potential for further training as he is VERY food motivated and lives for a tasty treat! Brock is a social butterfly and loves all people, making friends and admirers everywhere he goes. Despite being a seasoned older gentleman he retains a playful, puppy-like energy when he's excited, but he also loves being a couch potato and will happily lounge with you and lay his big head in your lap while you watch TV. Brock has brought so much love and joy into our lives as a foster, and whoever adopts him will be so lucky to have him!

176521.name: Milo
176521.summary:
Meet Milo!
Milo was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. He is a sweet, social older gentleman who enjoys being around people and is known for his affectionate, easygoing nature once he is comfortable in a home environment. He can be vocal and expressive, but he is very people-oriented and enjoys companionship.

My Ideal Home
Milo would do best in a calm and loving home that can match his lower energy level and appreciate his affectionate, homebody personality. He enjoys being close to his people and thrives with routine, gentle structure, and continued support for his mild anxiety when left alone.

Good with Other Pets?
Milo is friendly with familiar dogs but may react to unfamiliar dogs on leash. He should be monitored around other animals and would do best with controlled introductions.

Good with Kids?
Due to his reactivity toward unfamiliar animals and need for a calm environment, Milo is recommended for a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Milo is a low-energy, affectionate companion who enjoys relaxing at home, following his people around, and spending most of his day lounging. He is housetrained, enjoys car rides, and has experience with grooming and basic cues like sit and stay. He can be anxious when left alone and may bark or become vocal, so continued support around separation anxiety will be important. He walks with only mild pulling and is otherwise tolerant of handling and daily care. With consistency and reassurance, Milo shines as a loyal, loving companion who enjoys the simple comforts of home life.

Fun Fact
Milo's favorite things include dressing up for photos, celebrating birthdays, and lounging like the perfect little couch companion with his people nearby.

A volunteer writes: The first time I meet Milo I am smitten by the way his little ears take flight on our walk, flapping in the breeze, as he shows off his loose leash skills. It's when we go spend time in the yard together, though, that I discover Milo is an exceptional conversationalist. As he meanders toward me he sends delicate little yips into the air followed by a full on serenade of glorious howls, worthy, in my opinion of a Metropolitan Opera soloist. 

This is not Milo's first time in our shelter unfortunately. He was surrendered once before due to a domestic violence situation and then again due to health issues in his family. He is reported to have done well with the children and small dog in his previous home  and is a "playful yet lazy couch potato" who "loves chicken".  His hobbies included "dressing up in costumes for holidays and taking selfies" and "celebrating his birthday with party hats and cakes". He has also spent some time in foster where it was said he "was friends with all the doormen". 

Medically, he has a mass which will need to be checked out.

177585.name: Kassy
177585.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
Kassy is the perfect combo of chill + playful. She will happily lounge on her bed all day (although she would love to go to a home where she can cuddle on the couch) or go on an ice long walk and play. Whatever you're in the mood for, she is ready! She did great on hikes and stayed alongside us and loved to explore the water (fetching leaves and splashing around). She is great with other animals and children (she lives with a foster cat now, and she is great with my son)! She would make a great companion for a single person or a family. She is VERY affectionate and loyal. She loves belly rubs and will lay very still on her back to ask for rubs. She will check in on you while you're in the bathroom and grunt when there is a noise at the door. This sweet girl would love to find her forever home!

A volunteer writes: Kassy is a total sweetheart, easygoing and fun-loving! She has the playfulness of a puppy and the good manners of a calm, stable dog who just wants to be your best friend. Anyone who gives her kindness (and belly rubs!) would get an amazing companion in return.

Please check here for updated adoption hours.
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I am playful and cute!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

179442.name: Brow
179442.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Brow!
Brow is an owner surrender who is looking for a calm, patient home where he can finally relax and feel understood. He can be a little unsure when things are new, but once he has a moment to settle, his sweet and thoughtful personality starts to come through.

Personality
Brow is a gentle, sensitive boy who appreciates a soft approach and a little time to warm up. He's not pushy or demanding, more of a "take things at your pace" kind of dog. Once he feels safe, he begins to check in with his handler and engage in a quiet, steady way that shows his softer side.

He can be a bit cautious with handling at first, but he does well when people move slowly and give him space to choose interaction. His best moments come when he feels no pressure and can just settle into the moment.

Out and About
Brow walks nicely with no pulling and generally stays focused on his handler. He can get a little tense when he sees other dogs and may try to move toward them, so structured walks and calm guidance help him feel more secure. With consistency, he settles into a steady walking rhythm.

Social Behavior
In new spaces, Brow may start off a bit reserved and will often need encouragement to approach. Once coaxed, he does engage and shows curiosity about his environment. He's happiest when interactions are calm, gentle, and unforced, giving him the chance to open up at his own pace.

Home Life
Brow will do best in an adult only home that can offer patience, structure, and a peaceful environment. He thrives with slow introductions and a predictable routine that helps him feel safe and confident over time.

He also benefits from enrichment like puzzle feeders and thoughtful activities that help keep his mind busy in a positive way.

Things to Know
Brow does best with a gentle, force-free approach and continued support around leash skills and confidence building. He's still learning that the world can be a safe and steady place, and he does best with people who are willing to go at his pace.

Fun Fact
Underneath his cautious exterior, Brow has a sweet, curious side that shines through when he feels comfortable, like a quiet little companion slowly learning to trust his world. 🐾

179720.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Gia!
Gia was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and she's hoping her next chapter leads to a forever home. She can be a little shy at first, but she's very treat-motivated and begins to warm up with gentle encouragement. Once she feels comfortable, she's ready to show off her sweet side.

My Ideal Home
Gia would do best with a patient adopter who will give her time to settle in and build trust. A calm environment, predictable routine, and positive reinforcement will help her feel safe and confident.

Good with Other Pets?
Gia has previously interacted positively with other dogs. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended with any future canine siblings.

Good with Kids?
Because Gia can be fearful and needs time to feel comfortable, ACC recommends an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Gia has some resource-guarding tendencies around high-value treats and will need her belongings respected. She's also working on her manners and mouthiness, so force-free training and appropriate toys will help her learn good ways to interact. With patience and understanding, Gia can settle into a routine and become a wonderful companion.

185783.name: Madame Jenny
185783.summary:
Meet Madame Jenny!
Madame Jenny, also known as MJ, is a long stay pup with a reduced adoption fee and a whole lot of love to give. She has been in foster care for a few years now, and during that time her foster has watched her grow into a confident, social, and deeply affectionate senior dog who is truly ready for her forever home.

Personality
MJ is playful, smart, and full of charm. She enjoys engaging with people and has a joyful, affectionate nature that makes her very easy to fall in love with. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but it does not take her long to warm up and show her loving side. Once she feels safe, she is social, engaging, and very people oriented.

Home Life
MJ is an active senior who still enjoys play and daily walks. She loves games like tug of war and enjoys going out for walks where she can trot happily alongside her person. She is also very affectionate and enjoys quiet time close to her people.

She is intelligent and enjoys learning, especially when training is paired with patience and positive reinforcement. She continues to benefit from structure and consistency in her routine.

Social Behavior
According to her foster, MJ can do well with other dogs and even cats when introduced slowly and at her own pace.

She may be a bit reserved when meeting strangers, but she warms up and becomes affectionate once she feels safe. She enjoys connection with people and thrives in environments where she feels secure and understood.

My Ideal Home
MJ will do best in an adult home where she can be the center of attention and enjoy a calm, stable environment. She would thrive with someone who appreciates a loving companion who enjoys both playtime and quiet bonding moments.

She needs continued guidance around resource guarding, as she does not always like to share food, toys, or bedding. A patient, experienced adopter who can provide structure and positive reinforcement will help her continue to succeed.


Fun Fact
MJ's foster says one of her most special traits is her intuition. She always seems to know when her person needs comfort, whether they are feeling down or just in need of a little extra affection. She is the kind of dog who naturally shows up at exactly the right moment, offering love, presence, and a calming energy that makes her truly unforgettable.
185783.summaryHtml:
Meet Madame Jenny!
Madame Jenny, also known as MJ, is a long stay pup with a reduced adoption fee and a whole lot of love to give. She has been in foster care for a few years now, and during that time her foster has watched her grow into a confident, social, and deeply affectionate senior dog who is truly ready for her forever home.

Personality
MJ is playful, smart, and full of charm. She enjoys engaging with people and has a joyful, affectionate nature that makes her very easy to fall in love with. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but it does not take her long to warm up and show her loving side. Once she feels safe, she is social, engaging, and very people oriented.

Home Life
MJ is an active senior who still enjoys play and daily walks. She loves games like tug of war and enjoys going out for walks where she can trot happily alongside her person. She is also very affectionate and enjoys quiet time close to her people.

She is intelligent and enjoys learning, especially when training is paired with patience and positive reinforcement. She continues to benefit from structure and consistency in her routine.

Social Behavior
According to her foster, MJ can do well with other dogs and even cats when introduced slowly and at her own pace.

She may be a bit reserved when meeting strangers, but she warms up and becomes affectionate once she feels safe. She enjoys connection with people and thrives in environments where she feels secure and understood.

My Ideal Home
MJ will do best in an adult home where she can be the center of attention and enjoy a calm, stable environment. She would thrive with someone who appreciates a loving companion who enjoys both playtime and quiet bonding moments.

She needs continued guidance around resource guarding, as she does not always like to share food, toys, or bedding. A patient, experienced adopter who can provide structure and positive reinforcement will help her continue to succeed.

186647.name: Ava Marie
186647.summary:
My foster writes: 

I may look like Batman with my perfect mask, but I am cautious and somewhat scared.  I've improved over time but any sudden movements or the doorbell indicating a stranger on the other side of the door, will have me running for safety.  Even when I'm scared, my foster has never once heard me hiss, and I do not bite or scratch.  Instead, I'll either hide or freeze in the hope that I'll become invisible.

The secret to stealing my heart is to just love me a lot and give me space and encouragement.  If you do, I'll let my guard down enough to invite you to pet me; I'll follow you around; I may even sleep next to you if you're ok with that; and I'll zoom from one end of the home to the next when I'm in my extra happy place.  Another happy place for me is a window with a view.  I'll start the day by checking out what's happening in the world outside, have my breakfast, take a nap, or two, and later on you'll most likely find me back at the windowsill taking another nap or checking to see if anything new has happened since I last sat there 🙂

I may never become that furbaby who curls up in your lap to nap but the best thing about me is that I am as gentle as I am cute!

193121.name: Loki
193121.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Loki is on the at-risk list due to behavioral concerns. He has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and is allowing only minimal handling. Loki displays a high level of fearfulness and is highly sensitive to touch and handling. He has also exhibited significant anxiety and, at times, appears to panic during interactions while actively seeking an escape route. Medically, Loki has a corneal scar and pododermatitis.

Loki is a beautiful, active, and playful dog who loves being the center of attention. He enjoys interactive games like fetch, knows several cues including sit, up up, and give me paw, and is always happy to spend time with his people. He also loves chewing on dog bones, making them a great way to help keep him entertained.

Loki is looking for an adopter who understands that he is a very anxious dog, especially in the shelter environment. While in our care, he has shown high levels of anxiety and frequently seeks opportunities to exit his kennel or other enclosed areas. He may need patience and support as he adjusts to a new home and learns to feel safe. Loki is also uncomfortable with grooming and certain types of handling and may react defensively when he feels fearful or uncomfortable. He has been reported to resist bathing and brushing and has attempted to bite during grooming. Additionally, he does not enjoy car rides and may cry while traveling.

Loki will do best with a patient adopter who can provide structure, positive reinforcement, and time to decompress as he settles into his new home. His affectionate nature, playful personality, and love of attention make him a rewarding companion for someone who is willing to work with him and help him gain confidence.
