195419.name: Mamas
195419.summary:
Meet Mamas!
Mamas arrived at ACC after being brought in by officers from the 81st precinct, and despite her uncertain start, she has shown herself to be a sweet, social, and easygoing girl. She has experience living with children and other dogs, and while she may prefer her own space around other animals, she shines brightest with people and gentle companionship.

My Ideal Home
Mamas would do wonderfully in a loving home that can include her in everyday life while also appreciating her independent, easygoing nature. She enjoys walks, relaxing at home, outings, and quiet downtime, making her a flexible companion for a variety of lifestyles. She benefits from continued positive reinforcement, light structure, and opportunities to explore the world at her own pace. She is best suited for structured outings rather than high-arousal environments like dog parks.

Good with Other Pets?
Mamas has lived with other dogs but tends to be more indifferent than social with them, so respectful introductions are recommended if there are resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Mamas has previously lived with children and has been noted to be friendly and gentle with them.

Things to Know
Mamas is a low-to-medium energy, affectionate dog who enjoys people and adapts easily to different environments. In shelter care, she walks politely on leash with mild pulling, explores her surroundings, and checks in with handlers while remaining somewhat distracted at times. She tolerates handling well, shows soft body language, and enjoys attention without being overly demanding. She can show some anxiety in new settings, but responds well to calm structure, enrichment, and reassurance. With consistency and a relaxed home environment, she settles in beautifully and shows her loving, steady personality.

Foster Notes
Where do I even begin...Mamas is THE perfect dog. Some highlights: · Friendly and gentle with all people. · Up for anything! Walks? Yes. Nap? Yes. Cuddles? Yes. Car ride? Yes. · Perfectly housetrained - not a single accident the whole time she was with me. · Endlessly affectionate but not clingy - loves your attention but happy to do her own thing. I've been volunteering at ACC for awhile and have never fallen more head over heels in love than I have with Mamas. I couldn't help but take her home for a long weekend straycation, and it proved to me that she's just as perfect as she appears in the shelter. The moment we jumped in the uber home from the shelter, she laid down and fell asleep (she would have a better uber rating than most people). She spent her first afternoon/evening at a friend's game night and charmed every person she met with her calm, friendly energy. She was happy to be part of the action and get lots of attention, but also to sleep quietly nearby when no one was available to give pets. We spent the rest of the weekend sitting outside coffee shops, hanging out in nearby parks, and at a World Cup watch party. She blended in perfectly at each spot, bringing her chill girl friendly energy everywhere she went. 197776.name: Matilda
197776.summary:
My foster writes: Matilda came to us as a foster from the shelter, initially a scared, territorial, and aggressive bunny. She would get upset when we changed "her" litter box and water or touched her toys. However, she has blossomed into a loving companion who eagerly runs towards her family when they enter the room, stays for snuggles, sleeps in bed with her human roommate, and climbs on people for treats. Matilda is very food-motivated, making bonding with her extra fun. While she isn't a big jumper, she will hop onto the couch to sit with her family (or for treats) and onto the bed (for treats and to snuggle while her human is asleep). She still has occasional territorial moments, and we can share tips on managing those.
Matilda warms up to people but remains especially fond of her immediate foster family. She is excellent at expressing her feelings-whether she's in a loving mood, a quiet one, or even a bit spicy. When she's had enough attention or wants to enjoy a favorite treat in solitude, she retreats to her favorite spot.
Her daily routine includes breakfast with pellets in her dig box, followed by socialization and morning exploration activities, including visits to her working human for pets and treats. She then retreats to her safe space behind the bed for an afternoon rest. Dinner consists of greens and social time with her humans.
Matilda has a healthy appetite and enjoys her hay, pellets, greens, and treats. She drinks plenty of water and has impeccable litter box skills. She loves chew toys and needs lots of enrichment. Some bunny-proofing may be necessary as she enjoys exploring her environment.
Matilda thrives on socialization and would do best in a home where someone is present most days. She prefers quieter spaces and tends to hide away when her foster siblings have louder friends over. We've noticed that she's a bit cranky when left alone for extended periods, though this is quickly remedied with some time together + treats.
We believe Matilda would do best in a home without young children or other pets (though she is okay with other bunnies in a separate room) and where someone is home with her most days.
Matilda has grown so much during her time in foster care, and we want her to find the perfect forever home where her love, intelligence, spunk, and quirks are cherished.

198069.name: Blue
198069.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Blue is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Blue was reported to growl, snap, evade the leash, and thrash once leashed. She displayed similar behaviors during a previous stay after being brought in following a bite incident involving an officer, which resulted in a skin-breaking injury to the officer's hand. According to her owner, Blue is affectionate with cats, children, and people she knows. Medically, Blue is apparently healthy.

Blue came into the care center as an owner surrender due to moving and not being able to keep her due to a no-pet policy. In the prior home, Blue is a friendly, affectionate, very playful and enjoys spending her time where people are. She enjoys playing outdoors and enjoys all grooming by owners. Blue has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

198752.name: Squirrel
198752.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Squirrel is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Squirrel is not open to interaction at this time and does not currently tolerate petting or handling. Because his previous owner reports he is quiet, friendly, and affectionate in a home environment, we believe the behavior seen in the care center is shelter-specific and this cat would make a great pet but is really struggling in the shelter environment. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, home with adopters who are willing to work with a cat who needs time and patience to help him adjust to their new home.

A volunteer writes: What's black and white and pink all over? Squirrel is! But it's hard for you to see him because poor little Squirrel has been in a time-out. It's perhaps true that his behavior in the shelter has been squirrelly. One minute he's thrashing around and the next he's watching quietly and patiently as I work a squeeze-up into a dish for him.  Squirrel would appear to be an example of someone who's just not himself in the shelter. Squirrel's previous parent described him as quiet, friendly, affectionate, and playful, and has been known to pounce on some human feet; and that he likes to be where the action is, preferring to hang out with the humans at home. Squirrel takes a bum rap for some naughty behavior, but I think he might just need to feel safe and have the opportunity to blow off some steam. Squirrel has a lightweight pugilist's ability to paddle the cat dancer at record speeds, which is no easy feat. His fancy paw work is likely the envy of other aspiring feline athletes. He might even be an athlete-scholar, judging from his intelligent, curious, pale green eyes. He enjoys Temptations treats and Squeeze-ups.

199009.name: Velvet
199009.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
In her notes, Velvet's veterinarian noted how polite she is, and SHE IS. In addition to being the sweetest and most loving pup, and she knows how to be patient with people who want to give her attention and with me when I'm preparing her food. The only thing she is not patient about it is when she sees there's a chance that we might be heading toward the park. Then the excited puppy energy takes over.
Velvet loves tennis balls, soccer balls, squeaky toys (she is a very efficient squeaker-remover), fetch, and tug of war. Her tail is powerful and she wags it with gusto when she is happy.
Velvet loves to run but she is also happy as a work-from-companion, having attended many zoom meetings with me and listened in on countless work phone calls. She lounges about during the day for a surprising number of hours. She cuddles me at night (yes, of course, she sleeps in my bed and gets her hair everywhere), and sometimes snores (it's adorable), and has little dreams where she is apparently paddling her paws in a wide ocean or something like that.
Velvet is not a picky eater and takes her meds in half-vienna-sausages with no problems at all. I've only been in two ubers with her and no city buses, but she is making great strides with the subway where she is peaceful and patient and never tires of the public attention her brindle coat guarantees.
She knows perhaps 20 commands and we're working on "privacy" (so a human can use the bathroom in peace) and "slow" when going down stairs.
I love her a lot. She has quickly become my best friend. I am sure you will love her, too.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

199327.name: Racquette
199327.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

My Foster writes: Racquette is a lovely little lady who expresses her affection by sitting near you and rolling over to show you her belly. Some of her favorite activities include: batting around a crinkle toy, active play with cat pole toys, munching on some cat grass, staring out the window, and napping the day away. Racquette is very curious about the outside world and will spend most of the day in the screen house or gazing out the bay window. Racquette might need some time to get used to new places and tends runs away when approached, though she has never hissed or scratched. When she does ask for pets, she is okay with being pet anywhere but especially loves chin and butt scratches. She gets very excited and chatty during meal times and loves her churus though is not as big a fan of dry treats or temptations.
Racquette is a wonderful and easy to care for cat. It's such a joy to come home to her at the end of the day!

199654.name: Rigoberto
199654.summary:
Please check here for updated adoption hours.

A volunteer writes: Rigoberto is a rather majestically handsome two-year-old young man who wears a sleek gray coat. He's fairly tall in stature and has the aspect and carriage of an athlete. He is already neutered, which is an especially good thing in his case because he might qualify as a lady killer. Rigoberto (the name sounds like that of an Italian soccer star and is therefore apt) has a good appetite, is outgoing, and strikes me as highly energetic, even restless. He needs a good amount of play time and reportedly can be a rough player. His high energy also means he can be prone to over-stimulation.

 Update:Rigoberto always puts me in a good mood. He is at his door when he sees staff or volunteers in the room. He calls and sticks his arms through the bars of his kennel in the hope to get some attention, love and playtime. He likes to explore(well he went on two little trips outside his kennel and was brought back without any issue to his den) and plays wonderfully well with feather wands and catnip toys, anything that allows him to interact with a visitor. Rigoberto is not one to hide. He is very social and a fun cat to spend time with. His debuts at the care center were a little chaotic as he was not happy to spend his life in a kennel but time did its job and Rigoberto is really a nice cat toentertain. Ask to meet him when you come to the Manhattan Care Center!

200666.name: Blakey
200666.summary:
My foster writes:
With patience, Blakey's curiosity allows him to come out of his shell. Blakey loves butt rubs and petting, but only for a short period of time. Blakey enjoys strings and wands, as he has a high energy level throughout the day. He loves discovering new hiding spots and coming out to play.

Blakey is loving and gentle boy. Give him a little space to adjust to his new environment and he'll be asking for pets by the end of the day! He's very sweet-tempered, he doesnt mind being picked up every once in a while or getting his nails cut (but he might need a break halfway).
Blakey is full of adorable quirks. He loves to greet you by rolling over on his back to say hi. He also keeps his eyes half closed most of the time so he looks like he's judging everyone (he's not). He loves to come over to you often to ask for pets or butt pats.
He's also a great communicator: he sits by his toys when he wants to play, comes over when he wants pets/butt pats, gently nibbles on your hand when he wants you to stop (or just leaves), rolls over on his back to say that he's happy to see you, and pretends to bite at the curtains when he's hungry.
Playtime is his favorite time of the day. He loves his wand toys, bunny kickers, and spring toys. He loves to play with the wand toy to practice his sneak attack maneuvers. He's addicted to concealed motion toys. He also figured out how to use a walking pad! (Although he doesn't stay on it for long)

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Please check here for updated adoption hours.

A volunteer writes: Leaping all over his condo like it's his personal bouncy house, Blakey loves to play. Brought to us in May, I've watched Blakey's dynamic personality blossom and bloom. I know it hasn't come so easily to him, but I love everything he's shown me and I treasure the opportunities he's shared. I remember when he first came in and hardly left his den. Then, there was when he'd come out for treats and a couple of pets before seeking his cubby. I also remember when Blakey would stretch and look out with open curiosity at Adoptions. With his wide open face, Blakey appeared to be waiting for the best time to jump in. To see Blakey now, dancing at the front of his condo like he's the star of Adoptions, reminds me that I love him and that it's hard to really get to know such a special cat in the shelter. While it's been far too long for him to be without a family to call his own, he seems to be especially grateful for a little love and attention on his own terms. We know there's a forever family out there waiting to welcome Blakey.

To see Blakey now, dancing at the front of his condo like he's the star of Adoptions, reminds me that I love him and that it's hard to really get to know such a special cat in the shelter. We know there's a forever family out there waiting to welcome Blakey.

My foster writes: Tabitha is a shy but sassy girl. She takes a while to open up to you but when she does her sassy side comes out. She likes to give love bites while you pet her. Tabitha loves other animals and is glued to my cavalier king charles spaniel. She is still unsure about humans so she keeps to herself most of the day. She spends her time hanging out in the cat tree I have in my apartment and seeking affection from the other animals in the house. She never has any accidents outside the litter box and doesn't scratch any furniture. She loves using her scratching posts and playing with her laser toy.
My foster writes: Tabitha is a quiet shy girl looking for a patient and understanding adopter. She is good with cats and both small and big dogs. She will do well in an adult only home or one with older children.

My foster writes: Meet our quiet observer! She takes her time getting comfortable and is still working on building trust. While she's shy and keeps her distance, she does enjoy playing with her toys at night. She's a low-maintenance, peaceful cat, perfect for someone who values a calm and quiet companion. Ready to welcome this gentle soul into your home?

A volunteer writes: Lady Tabitha came to us with her sixteen housemates as their owner was taken into care. She is a shy semi senior whose life was turned up side down in a flash. We will never know what place she held in her tribe and in her former owner 's heart. Tabitha is always found at the back of her kennel, likely limiting her movements to visiting her litter box and feeding herself. She might at times move around to stretch her legs when nobody watches. She is a bit wary when someone opens her door but she does not run away or get up to meet her visitor. She waits with some apprehension for the hand that is eager(although gentle) to touch her and make her feel better. She eventually leans at a thirty degree angle into pets and at times, a faint purr can be felt under the fingers. Tabitha is a pretty tabby and white kitty who might very well open up in an experienced home, with the love of a new owner who understands timid felines and in particular when they have been uprooted. Tabitha is waiting for that very special person, hoping to find and give love.

203016.name: Marcus
203016.summary:
Meet Marcus!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Marcus arrived to Manhattan Animal Care Center as a stray with ID. His history is a mystery, but staff describe him as affectionate on his own terms - he loves attention but prefers slow introductions and gentle handling. Marcus can be sensitive around his head and neck, so he does best when people respect his boundaries and move at a calm, predictable pace.

My Ideal Home
A patient, calm home where his people understand canine body language and are willing to use force-free handling and positive reinforcement. Marcus will thrive with consistent daily mental and physical activity (walks, food puzzles, chew toys) and slow, low-pressure introductions to new people and places. A household without very young children is recommended; he may do well with older kids after proper meet-and-greets. Experience with dogs that are handling-sensitive is a plus.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for very young children. Because Marcus can be sensitive to handling around his head and neck, a home without toddlers is best. He could be open to older children once he's had calm, supervised introductions.

Good with Other Pets?
Positive with other dogs in observed meetings - he greeted another dog with a soft body and wagging tail and even rested his head on the other dog's neck. Cat compatibility is unknown and would need careful, supervised introductions.

Leash Manners
Marcus follows his handler readily but can show moderate pulling. He responds well to guided walks and will benefit from continued loose-leash work and consistent, positive training to reinforce good walking manners.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 - Suitable for adopters who are comfortable with a dog that is handling-sensitive and who will commit to patient, force-free training and careful introductions. Not recommended for homes with very young children.

Other Fun Facts
Marcus is a big softie who leans into people and seeks contact on his terms. He becomes receptive to treats during handling, enjoys sniffing out toys, and can be vocal when someone knocks before happily greeting them with a wagging tail. He's affectionate, enjoys one-on-one attention, and shows friendly, social behavior with other dogs.

203047.name: Nala
203047.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Nala is at risk due to behavioral concerns in the previous home. Nala is reported to have had two bite incidents - one with a stranger and the other with the resident child. Neither bite was reported to break skin, but both reportedly occurred very suddenly and with little warning from Nala.  In care, Nala has been shut down and will not easily move over in kennel for staff to clean her area.  Medically, Nala is mildly overweight but otherwise apparently healthy.

A staff member writes:  Nala is a 5-year-old spayed mixed-breed dog seeking placement with an experienced rescue partner. She previously lived in a home for several years and is reported to be house-trained, medium-energy, and social with familiar canine companions. She enjoys her walks, has generally manageable leash manners, and is familiar with living in a home environment.

Nala is a sensitive dog who appears to struggle with fear and anxiety, particularly around unfamiliar people, children, loud noises, and other stressful situations. She has a reported history of two incidents involving people, and due to these concerns, she is not currently considered a candidate for general adoption.

Since arriving at the shelter, Nala has presented as overwhelmed and shut down rather than outwardly reactive. She tends to keep to herself, remaining quiet and observant, and has been able to be leashed and moved by staff without issue. Shelter observations suggest that she may be more comfortable avoiding interactions when she feels uncertain.

Nala would benefit from a calm, predictable environment with experienced caregivers who can allow her time to decompress and build confidence at her own pace. An adult-only placement, thoughtful management, and force-free, reward-based behavior support will be important to helping her succeed. With the right rescue placement and guidance, Nala may have the opportunity to feel more secure and comfortable outside of the shelter environment.

206452.name: Luna
206452.summary:
My foster writes:
I'm Luna, but I also answer to Moo Moo. My hobbies include sleeping under my favorite chair, snuggling, and getting chin scratches. Fun fact about me: the shelter thought I was a girl but when my foster mommy brought me to the vet for spaying, she learned I was a boy! Surprise! The fur still hasn't quite grown back on my belly from the almost-surgery, but that just adds to my cuteness.
I had some serious dental work done the day before Halloween and have healed up like a champ. I love wet food (especially Royal Canin) and will let you know when I'm hungry with plaintive meows and meaningful eye contact.
I love snuggling but prefer to say in my safe place under my favorite chair in the kitchen. Mommy thinks this might be so I can avoid the resident cat. When my foster Mommy carries me from the chair to her bed, I can snuggle all day until I get a ride back.
I'm an older boy and would love to be your solo, quiet lap cat!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
My purr motor is always running!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Luna interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience, demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior. Luna would do best in a home with no young children under the age 5. 

A volunteer writes: Luna's always on the go and ready to talk with anyone. Welcoming me with a story, Luna began chirping out at me as soon as I opened the door. Trying to tell me everything at once, while also keeping an eye on Adoptions, Luna is one busy little kitty who has made progress in leaps and bounds since coming to the Care Center.  The first time I met Luna, she was napping in a circle and hopped onto her cubby when she saw me approaching. Peering down at me like the cutest and most curious little Oreo cookie, I accepted that she wasn't feeling visitors at the moment. I tried again a few days and later and had a very happy Luna nuzzling into my hand and playfully reaching her paws out at me for cuddles. We don't know much about Luna's history prior to coming to the Care Center, but it's clear that with her open mind and open heart, she's ready to meet her forever family.

My foster writes: Dolly is the SWEETEST girl I've ever met. Her goal in life is to make you happy and she thinks she's a small lap dog. She's silly, wiggly, playful, cuddly, lazy - she can do it all depending on what mood you're in. She'll look at you with just pure joy & love in her eyes. She'll wag her tail the second you glance at her. She'd do amazing in almost any home, she'll go with the flow & follow your lead, & follow you everywhere you go.

208262.name: Sid
208262.summary:
My foster writes: Sid is a seasoned sweetheart with a soft heart and soulful eyes. After losing his beloved human, he's been patiently waiting for a second chance at love and a cozy home where he can spend his golden years surrounded by kindness.
He may not be clingy, but Sid has a charming way of making his presence known. He's a great communicator! He'll greet you with a polite meow, and if something's on his mind-like an empty water bowl or a freshly used litter box-you'll be the first to know. Sid is a well-lived gentleman who knows what he wants and isn't shy about letting you know.
He's affectionate on his own terms, happy to keep you company while respecting your space. But he has a soft spot for scratches on the head and behind the ears, and will purr away a storm while being brushed. Whether he's quietly nearby or sharing a tender head bump, Sid offers the kind of companionship that's calm, comforting, and deeply sincere.
If you're ready to open your heart to a wise and wonderful friend, Sid is waiting to meet you!
Meet your future best friend! This sweet senior boy starts out a little shy, but once he's comfortable, he's wonderfully chatty, loves head scratches, and will even show off his belly when he's feeling extra happy. Treat-motivated, gentle, and full of love, he's looking for someone who appreciates a cat with a kind heart and a little personality.

My foster writes:
Sid is a sweet, lovable guy! Perfect cat for someone who lives in a calm environment and is looking for a lowkey companion. He takes some time to warm up to a new place, but once he does, he loves to chat with you! He's not loud and is pretty food motivated. He does not enjoy being picked up, but will come up to you for pets and attention.

My Foster Writes: 
Sid is a lovely and well behaved little gentleman who is looking for a long-term relationship with a patient person. And when that person comes along, they will be rewarded with a sweet and loyal companion who loves being brushed, gobbling up his treats, having his head scratched, and chasing a string. While he does enjoy a good chat at times, he also appreciates sitting together in the quiet, mutual understanding that it's nice to simply enjoy each other's company. He may need a little time to get to know someone new, but he will settle in and show you what a delightful little friend he is.

209294.name: Lola
209294.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
Lola is laying on top of her den in a loaf position, observing the assessor with her forward ears and neutral eyes as they approach. She is initially hesitant to come down from the top of the den but is able to be easily coaxed when she is offered a squeeze up. She comes down from the top of the den and approaches the front of the kennel to eat it, somewhat tense but allowing all petting as she eats. When done eating she continues to allow all petting before walking back into her den, body rippling slightly. The assessor speaks to her a bit more and after a few seconds she begins to head bunt and rub her cheeks against the side of the den but still occasionally body rippling. She is coaxed forward with a bit more squeeze up before pickup is attempted. When attempting pickup, Lola becomes very tense and begins to growl and vocalize. She is placed back down and walks to the back of her den, lip licking and body rippling. She remains tense, so the assessor gives her a few minutes to recover. When she is approached again for further interaction, she does continue to allow more petting on the head and cheeks.

Lola enjoys some attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

210076.name: Kira
210076.summary:
My current foster writes:
Once she gets to know you, she is the sweetest cat ever and will greet you at the door and come over to ask for pets. She will always rub herself on you and loves scratches under the neck! She will also follow you around the house.
She loves to play with different toys especially the fishing rod and is a very curious cat. She is always looking out the window and climbing around spaces. However, she is also a bit clumsy... She enjoys sleeping with you as well. She doesn't really like any treats but loves cheese.
Make sure to give her time in the beginning and respect her space but is otherwise a super easy cat to take care of.

My previous foster writes:
She's always greats you in front of the door and will rub herself
against you all the time. She also loves scratches under the
neck! She's a very smart cat, a bit too smart, and you can find
her lifting up toilet seats or playing with her water fountain. As
long as you respect her space when she's hiding or playing on
her own she will be super loving!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Kira has made spectacular improvements and was lying calmly on top of the den, appeared relaxed, sniffed treats and then allowed all petting, leaning in gently for cheek rubs, a huge contract to when she was first assessed. She was not able to be coaxed off the den but remained calm.

Kira interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.  

A volunteer writes: This week's most improved award goes to beautiful Kira, who arrived at the Care Center standoffish and fractious but soon settled in and became a calm affection monger who eagerly leans in for cheek rubs. We understand why she wasn't happy at first; Kira came from a home, and the sudden change in her surroundings was tough to handle. But this intuitive girl must have realized that there's a real forever home out there for her, and showing off her super manners and social smarts will help her land it. Kira's at that perfect cat age where she no longer has crazy kitten neediness but can entertain herself when she's not scoring pettings and warming the laps of her people. Meet her at the Manhattan Care Center today!

210131.name: Almond
210131.summary:
Meet Almond!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Almond is a 3-year-old large mixed breed who was found as a stray in the Bronx and has since spent time in a foster home. This affectionate and playful girl is eager to find her forever home where she can be loved and cherished.

My Ideal Home
Almond would thrive in a home that provides both structure and activity. She has an energetic personality and would benefit from regular exercise, training, and positive reinforcement. She is best suited for an adult-only home or a home with older children who can respect her space and help reinforce good manners.

Good with Kids?
Almond would do best in a home without young children due to her excitable nature and tendency to jump up in a social manner. Older kids who understand dog behavior may be a better fit.

Good with Other Dogs?
Almond has had mixed reactions to other dogs-sometimes greeting them with a loose, wiggly body and other times barking and jumping at the fence. She would need slow, positive introductions if placed in a home with another dog.

Good with Cats?
Unknown-she has not been tested with cats.

Leash Manners
Almond is strong on the leash and can be reactive toward dogs and small animals while walking. A front-clip harness and reward-based training will help manage this behavior.

Overall Health
She has no ongoing medical concerns, though she is slightly overweight and would benefit from a balanced diet and exercise.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 (Experienced Adopters Recommended) - Almond is a sweet and affectionate dog who loves attention but needs continued training for her manners, anxiety, and leash reactivity. She thrives with positive reinforcement and would do best in a structured environment.

What Her Friends Say
💬 "Almond is very sweet! She loves to play, licks a lot as a show of love, and enjoys belly rubs. She listens to commands like sit, wait, and go." -Her Foster
💬 "She was the perfect Borough Break buddy-affectionate, playful, and well-behaved on leash. She made our day and will make someone very happy!" -Volunteer

If you're looking for a fun-loving, affectionate dog who will bring energy and joy into your life, Almond could be the perfect match for you! Come meet her today! 🐾

A staff member writes: Almond may be a little nutty (in the best way!), but her affection and loyalty are truly unmatched. Whether you're out for a stroll or just relaxing at home, Almond is always by your side, ready to share her love and bring joy to your life. If you're looking for a furry friend who's as sweet as her name and will make your world a little brighter, Almond is your girl!

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Pre-Screener Form

Shango has become difficult to redirect with treats and other reinforcers when returning to kennel. Shango is social with staff and is exuberant but is struggling in the care center. Shango arrived at the care centers due to his previous owners' not being able to care for him anymore. 211802.name: Polkadot
211802.summary:
A volunteer writes: Polkadot was easy to handle when I took her out for playtime. This gorgeous girl ran around and around the pen, and when she was tired, she pancaked for pets. I found her friendly, scoping her area, curiously exploring everything...even climbing on my shoulder. When she released all the energy she had, she laid chilling in the tunnel. She is looking for her forever home. Come see how interesting she is.

My foster writes: Polkadot is an eye-catching girl with lop ears and tufts of lionhead's mane around her face.
Polkadot is very good about using her litter box, with the occasional stray pellets around her pen.
Polkadot is a night owl and active exploring, hopping, and sniffing between 9:30pm and 2am.
Polkadot is a high jumper and can easily clear the 26" baby gates if we don't cover the top! My kids and I created various two story condos out of cardboard boxes for her to use and jump on.
Most of the day, Polkadot is content to laze around. She doesn't seem to be high energy and we haven't observed her to binky. However, she shows she is content by relaxing and stretching out on the open floor of our living room.
Polkadot enjoys her fresh fruits and vegetables. For her favorite treats, she has gradually went from grabbing and running off with them, to eating them from the hand, to jumping into my lap to look for more.
Polkadot is warming up to human company. At the beginning, she would immediately try to hide or zip away from anyone approaching her. After about two weeks, she is not as scared of people or noises but still often startles, thumps, and hops away.
Polkadot will struggle if picked up, but she has come a long way in accepting head and body petting. She seems to have a strong preference to being petted in her litter box. Once she starts getting petted, she will pancake and stretch out with her paws over the side of the litter box. She allows petting while she eats her food and treats.
She would do best in a rabbit-proofed room with lots of hiding places for her to feel safe. She isn't aggressive with young kids but she would likely appreciate a calmer home. I believe given her progress in just two weeks, that she will make a great low-key companion for someone with patience.

211859.name: Roxy
211859.summary:
Another foster writes:
ROXY UPDATE: After time in foster, Roxy has blossomed. While this small girl can still be shy (I've found her napping in the closet!) Roxy is ready to find her way into her family's heart. She may not always want pets, but she knows how to ask you for them, approaching you with big eyes and gently pressing her forehead against your leg until you start petting her. Sometimes she's so excited to get your attention, she'll hop up to meet your hand! She ADORES butt scritches, and once you earn her trust, she may just offer you the opportunity to rub her belly! When she's not snoozing, Roxy spends her time following the sun around your apartment, looking out the window, and having an occasional play session - she has a goofy streak! She's looking for a low-traffic home that will continue to help her grow her confidence, and in return, you'll get her quiet, steady love.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
Roxy tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. 

My foster writes: Roxy is a sweet cat that takes some time warming up to her environment. She moves at her own pace and prefers it that way! Being picked up is scary for her, but cheek scratches will get her purring. Don't mind her loafing in the corner that's just where she's most comfortable. Slow and steady is the key to her heart.

My other foster writes: Roxy is a sweet and independent cat. She likes cheek and tail scratches, likes to find places to sleep during the day, especially on a blanket. She loves feeding time and enjoys a few snacks throughout the day. She likes to carpet to scratch on and rub her cheeks against. She does not like being picked up or being too close but she likes being in the same room and keeps the peace on her own.

A volunteer writes: Roxy's a diamond shining in every direction though she may look a little unsure. And sometimes she even acts a little unsure, especially as she prefers to nap with her little nose pressed against the wall. This is an interesting choice for such a sweetly social cat. I opened the door and Roxy hopped out of her box and came over for just a moment before returning to her cozy little bed. Gently stretching her paws out as she curled into a circle, she tucked her head into my hand and softly sighed. As I watched her relax into some neck scritches, I realized that Roxy's not completely sure how to stand out in the busy Care Center, but I can assure you Roxy's a standout cat. She's known to be affectionate and friendly, a loveable and playful sweetheart.

And sometimes she even acts a little unsure, especially as she prefers to nap with her little nose pressed against the wall. This is an interesting choice for such a sweetly social cat. I opened the door and Roxy hopped out of her box and came over for just a moment before returning to her cozy little bed. Gently stretching her paws out as she curled into a circle, she tucked her head into my hand and softly sighed. As I watched her relax into some neck scritches, I realized that Roxy's not completely sure how to stand out in the busy Care Center, but I can assure you Roxy's a standout cat. She's known to be affectionate and friendly, a loveable and playful sweetheart.

211917.name: Charli
211917.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
Charli was on top of the den, appearing calm, and then allowed all petting, leaning in gently for cheek rubs and arching her back with a high tail. She then ate a squeeze-up treat and was coaxed off the top of the den with the promise of more. She then allowed and enjoyed more petting and gave a minor verbal complaint when picked up and held, but otherwise remained calm and was still calm when set back down.

Charli interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

My foster writes: Charli is a sweet girl who has quite an interest for exploration! You'll find her examining every inch of your home and following you around once she's comfortable with you. She loves her space, but will often sit or nap by your side as she does enjoy company. I like to show her my affection by putting my hand out for her to rub her head and cheeks against (and keep going until she decides she's had enough). She doesn't like to be picked up, however she won't try to hurt you if you must (expect some stress meowing and a slight struggle to get out your hold). It should be noted that she does have a limit for petting. Prepare for soft, adorable meowing and increased affection when Charli is ready for her wet food or misses your company. She's a lovely, mellow girl who will bring love and warmth to her next home!

Charli is a friendly, outgoing cat who is eager to meet you! She enjoys napping, drinking from the faucet, and surveying her domain from the arm of the couch. From her two-tone nose to her white booties, she is an adorable tuxedo cat who is affectionate and easy-going. She is looking forward to finding her furrever home!


My foster writes: Meet Charli, a delightful companion with a heart of gold! This sweet girl loves to sit beside you, embracing your company and happily accepting gentle pets. Though she occasionally enjoys curling up on your lap, you'll often find her contentedly lounging next to you, soaking up the love.
Charli's adventurous spirit shines as she explores her surroundings, turning every day into a fun-filled experience! She's perfectly fine being left alone and warms up to new friends in no time. If you're seeking a charming feline friend who loves companionship and exploration, Charli is the perfect match for you!

"Queen" is THE word to describe Charli. She knows what she wants and will let you know. Listen to her, and she'll be sitting on your lap in no time. (Treats help a lot for sure)
As the Queen she is, she has a bit of a resting B face, but don't let that fool you, she is a sweet girl who loves all your attention and company. In fact, she wants to monopolize your love, so she's best as an only cat.
Meet her today and see her in all her glory!

212282.name: Koshechka / Crystal
212282.summary:
My foster writes:
Crystal wasted no time to get herself familiar with our apartment. Her personalities really came out now after three weeks. She is quite active for a 4.5 year old cat but well behaved, without litter box incident, and has a healthy appetite. She stays quiet at night and really enjoys wand toys!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
Koshechka tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: Reading Koshechka/Crystal's notes, it's clear that she's picked herself up and dusted herself off more times than a kitty should without ever finding a place or family to really call her own, and while some cats are luckier than others, I'm not sure that she'd consider herself unlucky. Koshechka/Crystal bounced around from empty houses to supermarkets to trees to delis in search of the brighter future she deserves. She's continually come up empty pawed, but her relentless optimism that things will improve remains her standout trait. Koshechka/Crystal did her best to remind me she was there by walking around at the front of her condo when I was in Adoptions, eventually settling into her bed to sweetly wait her turn. We cuddled a bit but Koshechka/Crystal is notably and adorably playful, leaping up whenever she can to catch a pipecleaner feather. I could've played with her all day but what Koshechka/Crystal really wants is a chance to finally find her forever home. 
This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

213226.name: Cookie
213226.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Meet Cookie your future cuddle buddy and playtime partner! This sweet, affectionate girl loves people, adores kids, and will happily climb into your lap for snuggles. She's playful, gentle, and full of happy energy, but also knows how to relax and nap the day away. If you're looking for a loving, friendly companion who will greet you with kisses and endless affection, Cookie is your girl! 💕

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A volunteer writes: Cookie 🍪 when I approached her kennel, Cookie looked a bit concerned. She was new to the shelter and didn't know the routine yet. She put her ears away and low wagged her tail. But her concerns quickly melted away as we walked together, and then sat in the yard. We put her in an adorable fleece that she was born to model, and she propped right up onto my lap.

Something that will surprise no one who follows us is that we love a sugary muzzle. And Cookie's is elite especially if you consider her young age of only 6! She's a little cuddle monster and while 53lbs she feels more petite to me.

Cookie came in with her sister Nala. Her guardian reported that she spent a lot of time in her crate or the yard. Now we want a soft life for our sugar faced girl. Couches and beds and blankets galore. Cookie is best as a solo dog.

Cookie is a clever and food-motivated dog participating in our Shelter Scholars program, where she's developing impulse control through the Leave It cue. Whether it's a tasty snack or a tempting object, Cookie is learning to pause and check in instead of grabbing. Her quick thinking and strong focus are helping her excel in this essential skill.

213619.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

The Foster Writes
Dolly- affectionate, adorable, with ears that stop people in their tracks! A pocket sized bundle of joy who loves strangers and cuddles. Dolly is a super star in the house- calm, cool and always wanting to be near the person she loves. She is a very nervous nelly when she ventures outside into the big scary world, but once she is back indoors, she will melt your heart with her perfection! She loves to play fetch and then snooze next to her humans. Dolly would do best in a single dog family, with someone who is willing to let her get close during the cold winter nights and ease her worries away. We rate Dolly A+ in her human and snuggle skills.

214020.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Charlie is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Charlie has been showing reactivity to other dogs during walks, when passing kennels to either leave the room or enter, and occasional leash biting both during walks and when being returned to the kennel. Charlie will hard bark, growl, and pull towards kennels and will also display the aforementioned behaviors in addition to lunging when he sees other dogs on walks. Medically, Charlie has lameness in his right and left hind legs.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I love to play and will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.

214571.name: Rocky
214571.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Rocky is at risk for behavior reasons. Rocky was surrendered to the care center due to his reactivity towards unfamiliar people, other animals and moving objects. Rocky was highly fearful on intake but has warmed up with select staff with a slow approach. Due to his kennel reactivity, he has potential to redirect on handlers. Medically, he is apparently healthy.	

Rocky is a large, energetic German Shepherd with a big heart and lots of love to give-but he's looking for an experienced owner who understands his needs. When first in care, Rocky was highly fearful and reactive in his kennel, often barking and lunging at staff. He may not have had much socialization early on, so he requires a patient, confident handler to help him continue building trust.

Once Rocky feels comfortable, he truly shines. He is a social, affectionate, and playful dog who loves spending time with his family. Grooming is one of his favorite activities, and he enjoys car rides and being part of the action in the living room.

215064.name: Breadstick
215064.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Breadstick is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In his previous home, Breadstick was reported to hard bark, growl, and lunge if his boundaries were pushed. With this noted behavior Breadstick does have a bite history to a child, the incident resulting in breaking skin. His previous owner also reported that he becomes anxious when left alone, crying and chewing on items. 
In the Care Centers, Breadstick has been extremely social with staff, readily engaging in play and rolling around for attention. He has also shown interest in interacting with other dogs and attempted to engage in play during Playgroup. Medically, Breadstick has been treated for an ear infection and has shown lameness in left front leg which resolved with rest. At this time Breadstick is healthy. 

Breadstick was returned into care by his recent adopter due to behavior concerns. Prior to this, his previous owner described him as a social and affectionate dog who preferred to lounge in the living room, allowed his family to groom him, loved car rides, any kind of toys, and learning cues for treats. While in his recent adopter's home, Breadstick was reported to have intially nipped the resident child's ear in a seemingly playful manner. But Breadstick began growling and escalated to biting the resident child on the nose. This did draw blood but was cleaned at home. He was then crated and, after some time, let out. Once out of the crate, Breadstick was reported to chase the child while snapping. During his stay in care, Breadstick has been highly social with staff and handlers. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Breadstick be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope Rescue partner that can allow him the time and space to decompress and acclimate on his own terms.

216896.name: Holly
216896.summary:
My foster writes:
Holly is truly someone's soul dog. She is such a joy to foster and I know she will be a light in someone's life. From couch potato to adventurer, Holly is the whole package in one. Not to mention, she knows no personal space in the best possible way- such a cuddle bug! She is completely house broken and can be left in a crate for hours with no problem. She doesn't bark, is super friendly to both people and animals, and everyone who she has met has completely fallen in love with her. Not only will you fall in love with her, but she will make you feel so loved in return.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Holly is the best! She is a very affectionate, friendly dog and made friends with anyone who stopped to say hi to her. She loves treats and patiently sits to receive a treat. Holly is easy to walk on a leash, doesn't pull when she sees squirrels or pigeons, and is very curious. After a long walk, all she wanted to do was nap on the couch and made the cutest snoring sounds. She wanted to be next to me the entire day and loves to cuddle. Holly would make a great companion as she is the perfect mix of active and couch potato.

217061.name: Tiger
217061.summary: Tiger is a playful and affectionate cat with a moderate activity level, but his rough play and occasional overstimulation require careful management. He is best suited for an experienced adopter who can provide consistent structure, monitor his behavior, and manage any signs of stress. With proper care, engaging play, and mental stimulation, Tiger has the potential to adjust well and become a loving companion in an adult only home.

217700.name: Nino
217700.summary:
Nino tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

My Foster wrote: Meet Nino! This sweet, shy boy is looking for a patient and loving home. He's a bit timid and slow to warm up to new people, but with time and gentle care, he'll show you his more affectionate side. Nino loves to play with his cat toys and enjoys climbing his cat tree, especially when no one is watching-he's most active when you're in another room or out of the house. While he doesn't enjoy being picked up or pet right away, he'll gradually get more comfortable and might even surprise you with a sweet meow! If you're willing to give him the space and time he needs, Nino will make a wonderful companion.

Nino loves to play with his cat toys and enjoys climbing his cat tree, especially when no one is watching-he's most active when you're in another room or out of the house. While he doesn't enjoy being picked up or pet right away, he'll gradually get more comfortable and might even surprise you with a sweet meow! If you're willing to give him the space and time he needs, Nino will make a wonderful companion.

218100.name: Blues Clues
218100.summary:
Meet Blues Clues!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Blues Clues is a six-year-old medium mixed breed with a big personality and an even bigger heart. She's a 56-pound bundle of bounces, wiggles, and affectionate energy who's been patiently waiting for someone to see past the shelter stress and into her goofy, lovable soul. Found as a stray and now fully vetted and spayed, Blues Clues is ready to put her detective skills to good use sniffing out snacks, toys, and a forever home.

My foster writes: Looking for a cuddly and low-key dog- Blues Clue is for you! This 6 year old gem is the perfect lady, respectful at home and happy to doze away on the couch or in a pile of pillows- even better if she has a blanket to keep her cozy! She does show some reactivity to dogs and some wheeled items but is super food motivated. Since we have had her, she will easily let dogs walk by her with the reward of a nice piece of chicken so the behavior is very easy to manage even during busy times of day. We have loved having her in our home and know she will make a wonderful pet for anyone who is looking for a easy-going companion!

My foster writes: Meet Blue's Clues - the strong diva with the cutest puppy dog eyes you've ever seen! She spends her days trying to collect cuddles from every single person she walks past, clearly a lover girl at heart. Blue's Clues is great with humans and has amazing intuition. She really gets you and understands what you're telling her, which makes her a total joy to have around.
Playtime is a non-negotiable in her world. Toss the toy once, and you've just signed up for a lifetime of fetch, she'll never let you forget how much fun it is! She's respectful of boundaries and knows the rules. In our apartment, she understands she's only allowed on one bed, and she sticks to it, no couch surfing or room sneaking here! Blue's Clues is ready for her forever home, with just one simple requirement: a safe, loving space and at least one bed (or couch!) she can call her own. Are you ready to fall in love?

My foster writes: Blue is the best friend you've been looking for. She'll cuddle you when you're down, protect you and keep you company. She'd thrive in a one dog household. She loves going for walks and playing with her toys. You don't have to worry about blue being home alone- she is very respectful of her humans stuff. She's house trained and will let you know if she has to go outside. She's also good with children.

My foster writes: Meet Blue, the cuddly sweetheart with a heart full of love!
This adorable girl adores butt scratches and is always up for a long walk, or even a run if you're feeling adventurous. Blue has a unique way of communicating her needs! She'll give you soulful stares and gentle whines for food, and adorable nose boops when it's time for a potty break outside the normal schedule.
Perfect companion if you live alone or with your partner, Blue is sociable and friendly but would thrive in a pet-free home as she learns to mingle with other dogs. With her love for walks and her laid back nature, she's the ideal companion for someone who enjoys leisurely strolls and cozy cuddles!

218298.name: Chase
218298.summary:
Meet Chase!
At 12 years young, Chase is a mellow gentleman who is looking for a soft place to land after spending his entire life with one family. Surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, this sweet senior still has so much love to give. He enjoys leisurely strolls, gentle attention, and simply being near his people. If you're looking for a calm companion who asks for very little besides love, Chase might just be your perfect match.

My Ideal Home
Chase would love a peaceful home where he can enjoy the simple things in life: comfy naps, relaxing walks, and quality time with his family. He can be a little sensitive when his neck and ears are touched, so a patient adopter who respects his boundaries will help him feel comfortable and secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Chase previously lived peacefully around other dogs and has been described as friendly with both familiar and unfamiliar canine companions. As always, slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Because Chase can be sensitive to handling around his neck and ears, he would do best in a home without very young children, or with older, dog-savvy kids who can respect his boundaries.

Things to Know
Chase is described by his former family as social, affectionate, playful, and wonderfully mellow. He enjoys car rides, knows cues like "sit" and "stay," walks nicely on leash, and has a reputation for being "super chill." His ideal day probably includes a leisurely stroll, a cozy nap, and spending time with the people he loves.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes:
"Chase is someone's dream dog, I just know it." After spending 12 years in one home, Chase is now adjusting to life in a busy shelter, but his gentle personality still shines through. He's a lovable old soul with the sweetest droopy jowls and an easygoing nature that makes everyone smile.

One of his biggest highlights? During a Fourth of July celebration, Chase absolutely demolished a hot dog in record time, leaving everyone laughing as half of it seemed to disappear in one bite! Watching him amble along at his own slow, thoughtful pace is just as charming as you'd imagine.

Chase doesn't need much to be happy. A cozy bed, a loving family, and a quiet place to spend his golden years would mean the world to this deserving senior. He has spent a lifetime being someone's loyal companion, and now he's hoping for one more chance to be someone's best friend.

219456.name: Mama Coco
219456.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Mama Coco is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Mama Coco was recently returned to the care center due to fearful behavior being observed while in foster. It was reported that Mama Coco would struggle settling around strangers, would bark and growl. While in the care center, Mama Coco has been observed to be highly kennel reactive. Noted to pull hard towards the other dogs in the kennel room. After being put into kennel, Mama Coco has attempted to push out in order to continue behavior. While out on walks with handlers Mama Coco will walk on a loose leash, will accept pets, and warms up with slow approach. Medically, Mama Coco has small wound on ear that is healing but otherwise healthy.

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Mama Coco was recently returned to the care center due to fearful behavior being observed. It was reported that Mama Coco would growl and bark towards select strangers. While in the care center, Mama Coco has been observed to be highly dog and kennel reactive. Noted to pull hard towards the other dogs in the kennel room while pushing off the wall. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home. 

My foster writes: Meet Mama Coco! This sweet girl has the gentlest soul and loves nothing more than being close to her people. She's happiest relaxing by your side, soaking up attention, and enjoying a peaceful home. Mama Coco is incredibly loving and has so much affection to give to the right family. With a little patience while she settles in, she's sure to become a loyal, devoted companion. If you're looking for a calm, cuddly best friend, Mama Coco can't wait to meet you!

219556.name: Pops Sanchez
219556.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Pops Sanchez is at-risk due to behavior concerns. During multiple stays in care, Pops Sanchez has repeatedly hard barked, growled, and lunged at anyone who attempts to handle him. As a result, he is unsafe to be handled by staff. The prior owner reports that he hard barks at strangers and other dogs. Pop Sanchez is also reported to hover over food with a tense body. Pops Sanchez was reported to learn to walk politely on leash and passed other dogs with consistent work from trainer once in a steady environment. Medically, Pops Sanchez has dental disease but is otherwise healty. 

Pop Sanchez was surrendered to ACC by his prior owners. He is reported to hard bark at unfamiliar people and dogs and hover over food with a tense body. While in care, he has hard barked, growled, and lunged at anyone who approaches the kennel or attempts to handle him. We recommend that Pop Sanchez be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner due to his intense responses to unfamiliar people. Pop Sanchez would benefit from placement with an experienced rescue partner that can provide a calm, structured environment and support his continued behavioral progress with the use of a certified professional trainer who utilizes positive reinforcement methods only.

220276.name: Desire
220276.summary:
My foster writes:
Desire is a sweet, low key cat. In the mornings, he loves a good snuggle and will follow you around the apartment throughout the day. While he spends most of his day napping or hanging out with his bud Cole, when he is exploring he is often chirping. Funnily, he doesn't care for any non-tube treats (churus are his go to).

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Desire is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. Desire tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents and offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: It's not always easy to find someone who sees you, really sees you, especially in a life that moves fast, but Cole (221057) and Desire have found each other and, seeing them cuddled together in their cubby, we're so happy they have. Brought to us from homes with many other cats, meeting new people isn't always at the top of their to-do list. They're a curious pair who would casually stroll toward me in the Free Roaming Room, choosing not to get particularly close, but, as we know, some cats don't always seek the company of people friends. They will allow some pets, but prefer to play, eat, and cuddle together. When Desire first came in, he would barely even touch the treats we offered in friendship. Staring at us in hopes it would help him to deduce our next move, he began to allow pets with the scratcher tool. Cole would sit with his paws out like a little frog, hopefully waiting for treats. Now they snuggle up together, confident in having done their part to make the Care Center a home as they wait for the next step of their journey to a forever home.

220279.name: Dodge
220279.summary:
My foster writes: Dodge is a sweet, playful girl who's ready to find her forever home. She's polite and well-behaved - no shredded couches or litter box issues here - and she loves being included in whatever's going on. You'll often find her close by, keeping you company with her gentle presence.
She enjoys pets and is still warming up to the idea of hands, but with patience and kindness, she's showing more and more trust every day. Dodge also gets along well with other cats, making her a wonderful addition to a multi-cat household.
If you're looking for a loving, easygoing companion who will brighten your days without causing mischief, Dodge is your girl. She can't wait to be part of a home where she'll be cherished! 💕

220847.name: Colby
220847.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Colby is at risk due to behavioral concerns. While in the shelter, Colby has displayed dog reactivity and, on one occasion in the past, attempted to redirect toward a handler during kennel fighting behavior. On another occasion, he was reported to vocalize loudly and become highly aroused, jumping toward the handler's face. While outside on walks, Colby was observed to balk and briefly thrash on the street. He has shown improvement in the play yard, where he is treat-motivated, receptive to handling, and allows petting while maintaining a neutral body posture. Medically, Colby is apparently healthy.

Colby arrived at the shelter as a stray with limited history.  Upon arrival Colby allowed handling with staff.  Unfortunately, Colby has shown increasingly fearful behaviors and a decreasing threshold for arousal.  Colby was reported to be fearful during his handling assessment and frequently does not walk on sidewalk for relief walks, however he does use the play-yards more comfortably.  Recently, Colby has been showing a decreasing threshold for arousal.  In once instance Colby attempted to redirect on to a handler when kennel fighting.  When outside in the play yard, Colby is treat receptive and allows petting with a neutral body.  We recommend placement with and experienced New Hope Partner that can carefully manage his potential triggers and offer adequate decompression time. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

A Volunteer Wrote: He looks like a character out of a cartoon (kind of like a fox with those whiskers!) and he's got the buoyant personality to match once he high tails it out of the shelter and gets to stretch his legs in the park. There, he practically lights up with joy, being able to graze on the grass, people watch, and have a chance to share a lap and treats. This sweetheart is tucked away in a pop up crate in a small room, when he should be making room in your heart for love and laughter!

221057.name: Cole
221057.summary:
My foster writes:
Desire & Cole are two cuddly friends looking for fun! They are very inquisitive and playful. They love to bird watch, eat and sleep, but a scratches are always welcome. They would do best in a quiet household, with a family who can engage and stimulate but let them roam.

Cole is a curious, sweet cat who rarely sits still. He's always up to something, whether it's looking out a window, playing by himself, spending time with Desire, or demanding pets. He is frequently chirping as he goes about his day. And when he's comfortable he sits with his back legs splayed out. Cole loves treats and being brushed.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Cole is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, he tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people, we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: It's not always easy to find someone who sees you, really sees you, especially in a life that moves fast, but Cole and Desire (220276) have found each other and, seeing them cuddled together in their cubby, we're so happy they have. Brought to us from homes with many other cats, meeting new people isn't always at the top of their to-do list. They're a curious pair who would casually stroll toward me in the Free Roaming Room, choosing not to get particularly close, but, as we know, some cats don't always seek the company of people friends. They will allow some pets, but prefer to play, eat, and cuddle together. When Desire first came in, he would barely even touch the treats we offered in friendship. Staring at us in hopes it would help him to deduce our next move, he began to allow pets with the scratcher tool. Cole would sit with his paws out like a little frog, hopefully waiting for treats. Now they snuggle up together, confident in having done their part to make the Care Center a home as they wait for the next step of their journey to a forever home.
221057.summaryHtml:
My foster writes: Desire & Cole are two cuddly friends looking for fun! They are very inquisitive and playful. They love to bird watch, eat and sleep, but a scratches are always welcome. They would do best in a quiet household, with a family who can engage and stimulate but let them roam. Cole is a curious, sweet cat who rarely sits still. He's always up to something, whether it's looking out a window, playing by himself, spending time with Desire, or demanding pets. He is frequently chirping as he goes about his day. And when he's comfortable he sits with his back legs splayed out. Cole loves treats and being brushed.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I have lived with cats in my previous home.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

Cole is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, he tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people, we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
