221147.name: Croquette
221147.summary:
My foster writes:
Hi, I'm Croquette!
I might seem shy at first, but once I'm comfortable, I'm a total sweetheart. I love mealtime, getting pets, and being close to my favorite humans. I'll follow you around like a little shadow, though I prefer to approach you on my own terms.
I get along well with other cats and enjoy being near my person. Whether you're working or watching TV, I'll happily sit beside you-and if you let me, I'd love to snuggle up next to you at bedtime.
I'm gentle and never scratch or bite, but I do like to nibble on fingers sometimes, so I'd do best with someone who understands cat body language and is patient with my playful quirks.
I'm looking for a loving home where I can feel safe and cherished. I hope that can be you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
A volunteer writes: Shy, quiet Croquette is a young boy who seems bewildered by his new surroundings in the cat adoption room and unsure of how to move forward. This gray tabby with the gentle eyes came from a home situation with several other cats, so his slow adjustment to the Care Center is totally understandable. Since he's been with us, Croquette is showing more comfort and curiosity: he'll poke his head out of his hidey box and allow staffers to treat him to gentle pettings. But he's still stressed by the sudden change in his life, and we keep whispering to him softly that we'll do all we can to find him a real forever home with pet parents who understand that some cats need a go-slow approach. Could that pet parent be you? Croquette is waiting patiently to get to know you on 110th Street today.

221354.name: Ginger
221354.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Ginger!
Ginger is a lovable, playful pup who has had a few changes in her life and is hoping to find her forever home. Through it all, this sweet girl continues to show off her happy personality, her adorable wiggles, and her love for spending time with people.

My Ideal Home
Ginger would do best with a patient adopter who can help her continue building confidence and practicing her manners. She is an energetic girl who enjoys staying busy, so daily walks, enrichment activities, and positive reinforcement training will help her thrive. Ginger's future family should also understand her boundaries around her favorite things and use positive, reward-based training to help her feel comfortable sharing her treasures.

Good with Other Pets?
Ginger has previously lived with another dog and has been described as friendly, playful, and outgoing with other dogs. She has enjoyed meeting canine friends and may do well with slow, thoughtful introductions to new furry companions.

Good with Kids?
Due to Ginger's reported resource guarding behaviors, she would do best in an adult-only home. Her previous family noted that she was playful and excited around children, but her future family should be prepared to manage her favorite toys, treats, and food carefully.

Things to Know
Ginger is a medium-to-high energy pup who loves treats, playtime, and being around her people. She may initially be shy with new friends, but once she feels comfortable, her silly and affectionate personality shines through. Ginger has some skin and ear issues that will need medical attention, and staff will be happy to discuss her care needs when you meet her.


A Volunteer Writes:
Vibes are not everything, of course, but the very first thing I think when I meet Ginger is "wow this dog has excellent vibes." She is all wiggles and waggles and gives the best little play bows you've ever seen. Her previous families describe her as "lovely, adorable and playful," and mention that she "gets the zoomies when she wants treats" and that "all the neighbors know and love her." Glad to know my doggie radar is working perfectly!

Ginger has been through a lot of changes, but she continues to be a happy, playful pup who loves making friends. She has been relaxed when meeting other dogs at the shelter and was described as friendly and playful with both familiar and new dogs in her previous homes. Ginger is ready for a family who will appreciate her big personality, silly moments, and loving heart.

221464.name: Simba
221464.summary:
My foster writes: Simba is a loving and playful cat that basks in attention. Even if you just stand near him, he will brush against your legs and headbutt your hand to ask you to pet him. He has a lot to say and is a very curious cat. When you are unable to give him attention, he often bats his toy mice around and explores his space by climbing carefully to high spaces. He would thrive best in a home that understands his boundaries, as he is easily overwhelmed by too much play. He is very well adjusted, but can get overstimulated if you pet him too much or stay in his space for too long. He would be okay in a home with a dog! 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Simba tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

222035.name: Seaweed
222035.summary:
My foster writes: Seaweed is a shy, quiet soul that is also curious. He loves scratches under the chin, behind the ears and the lower back. He has a beautiful coat of fur and spends his days taking it easy. His nights are spent curiously exploring his surroundings. No zoomies from this guy. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
 Seaweed has blossomed in the foster home and went from being a nervous cat to a friendly cat! He enjoys petting now, he likes play, has a nice appetite and can be picked up and held. He may enjoy another cat in his life, and very young children should probably be avoided. He can be nervous around strangers but has warmed up to the foster and her teenage son very well! 
I have lived with cats in my previous home.

222110.name: Marble
222110.summary:
My foster writes: Meet little Miss Marble! A girl with an adorable smile and sweet sounding meow! I get excited by food and treats. That's when my mouth curls up super cute as though I'm smiling. I love hopping and jumping playing with my wand toys.  Chasing and playing with my mice and balls. I love my scratcher boards. Mainly, I love being chill sitting or laying near my human in the same room. I'm also a kitty who loves classical music. I've been known to curl up in ball near the radio playing QXR FM classical station. The simple and important things in life make me happy. Love, affection, attention, safety, feeling comfortable and cared about in a safe home with safe people is where I want to be. Will you be my new Cat Mom, Cat Dad or both? My new cat parents? Meows of love. I'm waiting for you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

222398.name: Jam
222398.summary:
Jammy Jam! While her past is a mystery it doesn't matter, Jam lives in the moment and has a pure zest for life. She's a senior gal but that doesn't slow her down. Jam's number one request is to be with her human. She'll wake up on your schedule and wait patiently for her favorite time of day, her morning walk! She does the most adorable tippy taps to show her excitement! On our walks Jam is excellent on a leash and polite with people and other dogs. She's been playful with dogs on leash so she may even do well with a doggy sibling! After our walk, it's time to play with toys or snooze in the sun in the yard. This loving and affection girl will wiggle her way into your heart as soon as you meet her and her unique look will make you fall in love!

My foster writes: Jam is truly man's best friend. Everywhere you go she wants to come with you radiating joy and gratitude that she's invited. She has the biggest smile and softest eyes. Walks will take 15 minutes longer because everyone will stop to tell you how cute your dog is. She can be a little impatient because she just wants to go from one adventure right into the next and she can struggle with separation anxiety when left alone. But it's all because she loves you and just wants to be with you 24/7. If you want a fiercely loyal companion who never takes for granted all that you do for her then Jam is the dog for you.

🏠 My Ideal Home
Jam would thrive with an adopter who appreciates her zest for life and can support her with enrichment, exercise, and structure. She's energetic for her age and loves to learn, so a home that can offer mental stimulation and force-free training will help her shine. Jam has some special medical needs, so a compassionate adopter willing to provide ongoing care is essential. A quieter home where she can be your one-and-only-or carefully introduced to other respectful dogs-would be ideal.

🐶 Good with Other Dogs?
Jam has had a variety of playgroup experiences at the shelter-sometimes playful and bouncy, other times overstimulated or reactive depending on the dog. She's been used as a greeter dog and shown appropriate social skills, but also needs space when she's had enough. With the right match and slow intros, she may do well with a mellow companion.

🐾 Leash Manners
Jam walks with mild to moderate pulling and can become reactive to other dogs on leash, especially in high-traffic areas. A front-clip harness and reward-based redirection are recommended. She's been working hard with our behavior team and shows great progress when engaged in training games like the "123" or "Take A Breath" exercises.

222421.name: Poker
222421.summary:
Poker we noted to be a Spirit Cat in the shelter, but has blossomed in his foster home! The foster indicates that he is a very affectionate social and loving cat now. He is actually pretty outgoing and confident.


My Foster Writes:
Meet this gentle, peaceful soul who may be shy and fearful at first, but never defensive or aggressive. He's a quiet companion who enjoys soft chin rubs and will lean in and roll over when he feels safe-but he needs a delicate, patient approach. Due to limited socialization early in life, he takes time to adjust and is best suited for a calm, understanding home where he's not expected to be cuddly or outgoing. If you're looking for a low-maintenance, serene presence and are willing to let him come out of his shell on his own terms, he could be the perfect match.

A volunteer writes: Having been with us for over two months, Poker's still trying to find his way. He's determined though and wants to do his best, so he waits for a chance even though he doesn't always know what to do when it comes his way. Passing the day all curled up in his little bed is progress for Poker because he used to be curled up in his den. He's comparatively out and about now, but still a quiet kitty who politely asks others to make the first move. This isn't entirely unusual, especially for someone like Poker who came to us from a home with many other cats, but it does bring a bit of a challenge when it comes to making new friends. Though Poker may not have had as many opportunities to meet new people as other cats have had, he's committed to learning and trusting more, which is why he's started to very sweetly welcome pets. Shelter life can be a lot on our gentle hearted friends, but we know there's a family out there for Poker and hope you will come in and meet him soon.

223022.name: Angelo
223022.summary:
My foster writes:
I'm Angelo, a sweet 11 year old gentleman looking for a special someone to share my days with. I consider myself low-maintenance and take pride in my image. My wardrobe is often compared to Men's Style Pro, thanks to my penguin-like coat.
I prioritize my well-being and channel my energy into my corrugated scratch board. I'm a bit on the shy side, but don't let that fool you-once I feel a connection, I'll strut over to your feet and give you a chirp of approval. I love being pampered with Temptations and Delectable treats, served straight from your hand.
When I'm not busy fending off the neighborhood ladies sneaking past my window, I retreat to my cozy cardboard villa to recharge. It's my personal hideaway, but don't worry-I'll come to you when I'm ready.
Secure your cabinets! I consider myself an explorer at heart and enjoy uncovering closed spaces. I'm currently employed as a personal towel warmer, though I must admit, I'm often caught napping on the job.
I'm searching for someone who will patiently help me blossom and build my confidence. Could you be the purrfect Hooman to earn my trust and fill my heart with joy? I'll reward you with a lifetime of love and companionship.


A volunteer writes: It's unlikely that, at 11 years old, Angelo pictured himself here. With years of creativity and love behind him, he has only more ahead but since Angelo takes a little while to warm up to new people, shelter life hasn't been the easiest transition. While Angelo has spent an inordinate amount of time in his den as of late, he's made lots of progress. We also know that he's a playful and imaginative guy with a bright and playful spirit. We've heard that Angelo loves to play with toilet paper and is particularly captivated by scratching posts. Anyway, though Angelo's said to be one who generally prefers to watch from afar, he likes to be around the action, except when it comes to Care Center action. Angelo made many efforts to make himself invisible when he was brought here and he still seems to be on a mission to do just that. That's not what we want for him though and we don't think it's what he really wants for himself. He's begun popping his head out for cuddles and will eat treats right from my hand.

When I'm not busy fending off the neighborhood ladies sneaking past my window, I retreat to my cozy cardboard villa to recharge. It's my personal hideaway, but don't worry-I'll come to you when I'm ready.
Secure your cabinets! I consider myself an explorer at heart and enjoy uncovering closed spaces. I'm currently employed as a personal towel warmer, though I must admit, I'm often caught napping on the job.
I'm searching for someone who will patiently help me blossom and build my confidence. Could you be the purrfect Hooman to earn my trust and fill my heart with joy? I'll reward you with a lifetime of love and companionship.


A volunteer writes: It's unlikely that, at 11 years old, Angelo pictured himself here. With years of creativity and love behind him, he has only more ahead but since Angelo takes a little while to warm up to new people, shelter life hasn't been the easiest transition. While Angelo has spent an inordinate amount of time in his den as of late, he's made lots of progress. We also know that he's a playful and imaginative guy with a bright and playful spirit. We've heard that Angelo loves to play with toilet paper and is particularly captivated by scratching posts. Anyway, though Angelo's said to be one who generally prefers to watch from afar, he likes to be around the action, except when it comes to Care Center action. Angelo made many efforts to make himself invisible when he was brought here and he still seems to be on a mission to do just that. That's not what we want for him though and we don't think it's what he really wants for himself. He's begun popping his head out for cuddles and will eat treats right from my hand.

223086.name: Bebe
223086.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Bebe is a middle aged dame you will spot right away as you enter our adoption ward. She is an all ebony kitty, quiet, gentle and sweet who welcomes caresses, leans into pets and even purrs after a while. She is well mannered and within our walls, is using her litter box. She was noted to be constipated and was placed on miralax. Bebe's former owner told us that she was a very lovable cat who likes to play(gently) all the time. She would have some litter box issues(could it be connected to a then untreated constipation) and prefers not to share her life with male cats and dogs(she lived with 2 or 3 of them).Bebe is apparently healthy(she even has good teeth)beside having a slow gut, is already spayed and did very well on her behavior evaluation. She would love to go home with you, for many years to come!



Bebe is laying in the back of her kennel in a loaf position; front paws tucked under her chest and pupils slightly dilated as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and she is softly spoken to, she begins making soft eye contact and slow blinking at the assessor. She is a bit tense on initial contact but leans into all petting after a few seconds, closing her eyes when she is pet on the head and cheeks. Bebe is unable to be coaxed to the front of the kennel (she is being treated for a medical condition and may be a bit tired) but is tolerant of being maneuvered to the front of the kennel and allows pickup, slightly tense but without issue. When she is placed back, she returns to her loafed position at the back of the kennel, continuing to allow all petting without issue.  

Bebe interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience and demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

223274.name: Jinkx
223274.summary:
My foster writes: Hello! My name is Jinkx! I am a sweet girl who can't wait to find my forever home! I would do best in a home with patient parents who are willing to give me the time and space to open up and show my affection on my own terms. I enjoy sleeping in the sun on the windowsill, playing with all sorts of toys in my foster home (hair ties are my absolute favorite!), taking naps on freshly washed towels, purring when getting pets from my foster mama, and meowing excitedly at my foster mama when I want to eat!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Jinkx tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.
A volunteer writes: Don't be put off by Jinkx's hard stare in her photos. This pretty cat is a good, sweet girl still adjusting to the Care Center after being in a real home shared with many cat friends. Her previous person had awesome things to say about her: Jinkx is quiet, shy around strangers, outgoing with other felines, and a litterbox champion. She liked to hang out in the kitchen, played gently, and enjoyed having her coat brushed. In the cat adoption room, Jinkx has been social with humans, soliciting pettings and leaning in for cheek rubs. But she's also showing some stress from suddenly finding herself in unfamiliar surroundings. We'd love to find a forever family for this marshmallow fudge lady that welcomes her into their household and gives her time to decompress. Meet beautiful Miss Jinkx on 110th Street today!

223431.name: Demas
223431.summary:
My foster writes:

Meet Demas (aka Fantasma), the curious, affectionate, sweet boy for you! He loves to be pet and will head bonk you for your attention. Other than pets, he is very food motivated - a classic NYC foodie. His calm demeanor could suit any cat owner. How could anyone resist this goofy boy. Help him find his cozy, forever home!

Demas can be shy at first; he just needs time to feel secure and at ease. When he's feeling especially happy and relaxed, he may give "love bites" but he does not always realize his own strength so let him know early on that you don't like it and he'll back off. He's also sensitive to the sound of dry food moving in an empty bowl, so he prefers wet food, a full bowl, or dry food placed quietly on the floor. This stubborn guy will starve himself before dealing with the noise.   

Once he comes out of his shell, he's a calm, curious companion who likes to nap in the same room as you, ask for pets as you pass by, and play in the evenings. He loves chasing treats slid or tossed across the floor and enjoys simple toys like a shoestring with a small object tied to the end. Because his eyesight and sense of smell aren't very strong, he appreciates when treats are placed or thrown to where he can easily see them. He'll probably warm up more quickly when other cats or dogs are present, as he seems to enjoy having animal friends around.

223473.name: Ladybird
223473.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

🐾 Meet Ladybird
Ladybird came to us in the middle of the night, after her owner was unexpectedly arrested and there was no one left to care for her. Officers brought her to ACC, and she arrived trembling, unsure, and completely alone. At just 3 years old, this medium-sized sweetheart is trying her best to navigate an overwhelming world-and she's looking for a patient, loving adopter who can help her rediscover safety and trust.

🏡 My Ideal Home
Ladybird is searching for a calm, quiet home where she can take her time settling in. A routine, peaceful environment without a lot of hustle and bustle will help her feel safe. She'd do best with someone who understands that the best relationships are built slowly-and that every small win is worth celebrating.

👶 Good with Kids?
Ladybird should not live with very young children. She may be open to older, respectful kids who can give her space and allow her to approach on her own terms.

🐕 Good with Other Dogs?
Ladybird has shown fearful body language around other dogs in the care center and may be uncomfortable in social settings with them. She'd likely thrive as the only pet.

🦮 Leash Manners
She walks gently on leash but may dart away from loud noises or unfamiliar sights. With a secure harness and lots of reassurance, she'll build confidence over time.

🧠 Behavior Determination: Level 2
Ladybird is shy and anxious in the shelter environment. While she allows gentle handling, she often keeps her distance and watches the world with wide, uncertain eyes. With time and positive reinforcement, we believe she can blossom into a devoted companion.

Ladybird is ready to trade in her uncertainty for comfort. If you're someone who believes in second chances and quiet triumphs, come meet this tender-hearted girl. She may be timid now, but with your help, she could learn to fly. 🐞


My Foster wrote:This young pittie girl is bursting with love, energy, and personality! Whether she's tossing her toys in the air or trotting happily on long walks. Ladybird lives for playtime and time with her favorite humans.
Ladybird didn't get the socialization or training she deserved in her early days, but she's a fast learner with the right person and plenty of structure. She's working hard on her manners and gaining confidence every day! At the moment, she's reactive to other dogs and needs to be the only pup in your home, but with the right support we are hopeful that she may be able to have dog friends in the future. For now, she wants you all to herself!
What Ladybird needs:
* A dog- and cat-free home
* A committed, patient human to continue her training
* Daily exercise + playtime
* Couch privileges (non-negotiable)

In return, you'll get unconditional love, soulful eyes staring up at
you, and the best snuggle buddy in the five boroughs.

223631.name: Zazu
223631.summary:
My Adoption Fee is Sponsored!

My foster writes: I've had a lot of foster pups and Zazu truly is something special. I don't think I've met a sweeter soul. Zazu is very easy going and knows all the basic commands. She is SO happy when it's time for a walk but equally loves being a couch potato while you binge watch. Zazu doesn't ask for much and is very low maintenance. She sleeps soundly through the night, is crate trained, housetrained, a professional cuddler and big lap dog. Zazu gets along well with our medium sized dog. She is a little weary of small dogs, especially when they yap at her. Zazu walks beautifully on a leash. She may pull for a second if she sees another dog but quickly gets back on track with her walker (especially if they have a treat)! Zazu is an easy going, well behaved pup that would be ideal for any family, even new dog owners! She is very gentle and doesn't jump, making her a wonderful family pup for kids. I truly can't believe she hasn't found her forever home yet. 

Bonus: She is estimated to be 7yrs but this spring chicken recently had a full glow up at the vet and came back with a clean bill of health!

Meet Zazu - Your New Cuddle Companion!
Zazu was brought to us by officers at the 116th precinct after she was found abandoned in Queens. Despite her rough start, Zazu has been nothing but gentle, wiggly, and ready for love.

My ideal home:
Zazu is a senior sweetheart looking for a calm, loving home where she can snooze in sunny spots, enjoy leisurely strolls, and be spoiled with affection. 

Good with Kids?
Zazu is gentle, social, and tolerant of handling-traits that could make her a great match for a family with respectful kids. As always, a meet-and-greet is recommended.

Good with other dogs?
Zazu has shown mixed responses with other dogs in shelter playgroups and seems more comfortable avoiding confrontation. A solo-pet household or slow introductions at home would be best.

Leash Manners:
She walks politely with minimal pulling and happily follows her handler's lead. Just bring the leash and some treats-Zazu's ready to go!

223905.name: Doug
223905.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Doug is curious and enjoys long walk. At home, he loves snuggle, naps and dog tv. He is calm, potty-trained and never barks. He is a sweet boy and a very good company.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

A volunteer writes: If there's one thing we hate to see it's seniors in the shelter. 10 year old Doug deserves all the luxuries that come with a life long lived: warm beds, delicious treats, and naps in the sunshine, amongst many other things. Each time we pass his kennel, Doug is laying on his bed, a humble guy, not too noisy, not too pushy. He's a leisurely walker, a gentle treat taker, and a cuddly boy in an unassuming way. His giant ears may not be as in tune as they have in the past, his gait a little slower, his muzzle a bit whiter. He's walkable by our newest volunteers which means he's a very good and easy boy. Our behavior team has even deemed him adoptable by even novice families. Doug has been mostly aloof and avoidant of other dogs. If there's one thing we love to see, it's seniors leaving the shelter. So come to Queens ACC to meet him today!

224183.name: Picnic Basket
224183.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Picnic Basket must have gone to lots of picnics in the one year he spent with his past adopter! He gained nine pounds!! Time to trim down a little....Picnic Basket is with us for no fault of his own. His family is moving far away and is unable to take him along. Picnic Basket is said to be a friendly and affectionate kitty who loves to play. At the care center, he follows his visitor everywhere(he resides in our community/playground room which he enjoys tremendously). He loves petting, makes biscuits and rolls on the ground, his four legs and belly up, waiting for scratchies..Does he think he is a doggie? Picnic Basket is a big fluffy Baloo dreaming to be home again as your forever best friend. Come and meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
Picnic Basket is at the front of the kennel, meowing softly with a relaxed body as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he leans forward to head bunt their hand, allowing and leaning into all petting. He calmly walks out of the kennel, appearing curious and wanting to explore. Picnic Basket is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting without issue. 

Picnic Basket has been a big, sweet, friendly boy during interactions at the care center. He interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. Due to reported history in his previous home, we recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in petting induced aggression, overstimulation, and decompression/new home adustment.

He interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. Due to reported history in his previous home, we recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in petting induced aggression, overstimulation, and decompression/new home adustment.

224778.name: Major
224778.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I need a home where there are no other dogs.
I need a home without cats or small animals.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
Not only do I pull at heart strings, but I also pull on leash! I will need someone to help me with my leash manners.

A volunteer writes: Major is fitting name for this boy. He is majorly handsome, majorly huge, and majorly amazing. At 110 pounds, Major plops his giant self down right at our feet, gently requesting unlimited pets (and dont worry he did say please and thank you!) His giant jowls flop around as a smile grows on his face. His tongue is no less huge than any other part of him and it eventually makes its way down and out of his mouth, flopping to the side. He prefers toys more for dogs about 1/5th of his size rather than any big stuffies. 

Major came to us after an eviction. In his home, he lived with 3 adults, 2 children, and 2 other dogs. He was said to sometimes hide at first when visitors came over, but after a bit of time he warms up and is playful and tolerant. He had always been outgoing and friendly with the children and dogs he lived with, and novel dogs on and off leash. He was described as a gentle giant, and he loved kongs, car rides, and cuddles! Staff have noted this big boy appreciates baby talk as well to help him feel more confident.

My foster writes: Sundae is a gentle giant with a heart as big as his 75lb frame. This handsome 6-year-old is a master of transformation, moving from a frightened soul to a loving companion ready to melt your heart. He's as well-mannered as they come, with perfect house-training skills and a polite demeanor on walks. While his curiosity might lead to a slight pull on the leash, Sundae always looks to his human for guidance and quickly adapts to new experiences with a bit of reassurance.
Sundae is searching for a forever home where he can feel safe, loved, and part of the family. Open your heart to Sundae, and be rewarded with endless love and loyalty. Are you ready to give Sundae the sweet life he deserves? Adopt him today!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

225640.name: Marley
225640.summary:
My foster writes:
Marley is bonded to her brother Alex and they make quite the dynamic duo. They enjoy play wrestling and relaxing together for very funny and entertaining viewing. Marley can be more nervous around new people and new surroundings, but the way to her heart is crunchy treats and playtime.
Marley is a bit more independent and gives you your space during the day to get work done. However, she remains a good supervisor kitty and likes to check in by doing the very important task of taking a nap behind you. Her favorite sleeping positions are to be fully stretched out on the bed, sleeping with one paw covering her face, or staring at you upside down with her very adorable little face. Ideally, Marley should be going to an adult only home that is quiet and patient.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Marley is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appreciates some attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people, we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans.  Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I came in with multiple cats and am currently housed with my sibling, Alex 226461 who I am bonded with! (as seen in photo)

A volunteer writes: Visiting with Alex (226461) and Marley makes me feel like I've walked into a play. Except both of these adorable cats seem to patiently and adorably look to us for their entertainment. With one paw delicately perched on the ledge of his bed, Alex waited for me to introduce myself before presenting his neck for some scritches. Marley, meanwhile, prefers her perch to being downstairs when there are guests but she really, really loves pets. The circumstances need to be just right (i.e., calm and quiet) and when they are, she very sweetly leans in. They loved watching me try to play with them and every so often, Alex would stretch a paw up for the pipe cleaner feather. Alex and Marley came to us from a home with many other cats. Settling into any new environment comes with challenges and we're grateful that Alex and Marley have found so much comfort in each other.

225820.name: Kali
225820.summary:
Meet Kali!
Kali is an owner surrender who is now looking for a fresh start and a home where she can settle in and feel secure. She has a calm, easy presence and does best when life feels predictable and kind of low-key, which helps her confidence really shine through.

Personality
Kali is a steady, people-oriented girl who likes being part of whatever her humans are doing. She's not pushy for attention, but she enjoys staying close, checking in, and quietly taking in her surroundings. Her foster describes her as an easy dog in the home who settles well once she understands the routine and enjoys just being included in daily life.

She responds really well to calm energy and kind handling. Nothing overly complicated, just a consistent, relaxed environment where she knows what to expect.

Out and About
Kali is a super nice leash walker with no pulling and no reactivity toward people. She moves along at an easy pace and stays soft even when passing other dogs, often with a loose body and a friendly, wagging tail. Walks with her feel pretty straightforward and relaxed, like she's just happy to be out and about with you.

Social Behavior
Kali is moderately social when meeting new people and will usually approach when called. She tends to stay nearby and then drift around the room a bit before coming back to check in. She's comfortable with gentle handling and does best when interactions stay calm and unforced.

At the shelter she greeted another dog with a loose, wiggly body, then casually disengaged and went back to focusing on her handler, showing a nice ability to take things in stride.

Home Life
Kali would do really well in a home that has a steady routine and a calm vibe. Her foster describes her as an easy companion who enjoys being part of everyday life without needing constant stimulation. She's happiest when things feel balanced and predictable and she can just hang out with her people.

Things to Know
Kali is comfortable with normal handling and day to day environments, and she does best when people are gentle and not overly intense with her. She's the kind of dog who settles in nicely once she understands the rhythm of a home.

Fun Fact
Kali is a quiet "stick by your side" kind of dog. She doesn't ask for much, she just likes being near her people, keeping things calm, and being part of the moment. 🐾

226092.name: Cherry Waves
226092.summary:
My foster writes: Hi! I'm Cherry wave (my foster family calls me Jasper, because my foster sister thinks that name fits me better), and my foster mom tells me I am the best boy ever. I always hear her say I am going to make a special future family very happy. I am a sophisticated red headed little man who is well trained on my litter box and scratching post skills. I know where I am supposed to do my business and where I am not. No training is needed whatsoever. I purr loudly, and my family says I sound so cute. I love to be brushed, even more than getting pets. Do not get me wrong, I still like pets and will let you know when I have had enough. I don't think I ever get tired of being brushed. I prefer to sit next to you than on your lap, but I am a lover. My foster sister even gets to carry me around the house, without me getting upset. Please consider adopting me so I can live out life with a furever family. I will greet you at the door and brighten your day every time you look at me.
From my foster mom: Cherry wave has been such a joy to be around. I am amazed at how quickly he adapted to his surroundings. He is patient and loving. He follows us around and has the best behavior ever. He is not a big fan of toys, but he cannot get enough of being combed. I have never seen a cat or animal loving grooming so much. Whoever adopts Cherry Wave is going to be very lucky.

My foster also writes: Greetings human friends.  It is your favorite orange feline, Cherry Wave (Jasper to my close human companions), live from East Harlem. It has been a few weeks since I checked in last and thought all of you deserved some updates. I continue to bond with my foster mom, sister and even the resident hamster (AKA purrrster).  I like to wake them up every morning with a little song of meows and head nudges to get everyone's day started on the right track.  I like to think of myself as their personal alarm clock.  After my foster mom and sister get back from a day of work and other activities, I like to follow them around the house and bat at their legs for hugs and attention.  I have even started to play with a couple toys. Don't get me wrong, I still love my naps and am a sprinter, not a marathon runner when it comes to playing.  My foster mom always tells me that I could adapt to any situation and be incorporated into any type of family. I love to go out on the balcony for a little sunbathing, but my favorite thing to do is probably eat!!!!!!  I LOVE FOOD.  I continue to be awesome with my potty routines and scratching (I have a favorite small rug that you can get from Target for cheap that I love more than a scratching post).  I have not had one accident and have NOT scratched furniture.  I am always on my best behavior.  My foster home has been awesome, but I would love to have one of you out there become my furever family so I can prove to you what has been missing from your home until you found me.

226118.name: Jill
226118.summary:
Jill is a beautiful 3-year-old pup with striking good looks. Recently found as a stray, she's still settling in and figuring out the world-but she's already shown us she's a fantastic walking buddy with a nose for adventure.
Jill enjoys affection on her own terms-think "respectful roommate" more than "clingy bestie." She'd do best in a calm home with no young children under 13, where she can take her time to decompress and feel safe. She's eager to learn and would love a patient person to help her grow in confidence through training and consistency.
Come meet this snow-kissed sweetheart and help her write her next chapter-one with plenty of walks, quiet moments, and a soft place to land.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

My foster writes: Very sweet girl, who is starting to come around to people. Loves treats and pets, but likes her space respected. A true New Yorker who asserts her boundaries.

My foster writes: Tannenbaum is a shy girl, who keeps late hours. You make catch her scurrying around after midnight, but by the time the sun is up she is safely hidden away. She has a healthy appetite and a playful nature, but only when she's not being watched!

Tannenbaum is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appears wary of human contact. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Visiting with Alex and Marley (225640) makes me feel like I've walked into a play. Except both of these adorable cats seem to patiently and adorably look to us for their entertainment. With one paw delicately perched on the ledge of his bed, Alex waited for me to introduce myself before presenting his neck for some scritches. Marley, meanwhile, prefers her perch to being downstairs when there are guests but she really, really loves pets. The circumstances need to be just right (i.e., calm and quiet) and when they are, she very sweetly leans in. They loved watching me try to play with them and every so often, Alex would stretch a paw up for the pipe cleaner feather. Alex and Marley came to us from a home with many other cats. Settling into any new environment comes with challenges and we're grateful that Alex and Marley have found so much comfort in each other.

226765.name: Oreo Krispies
226765.summary:
My foster writes:
Say hello to Snickolas and Oreo Krispies, a bonded brother-and-sister duo with complementary personalities and plenty of charm. Oreo is the brave big sister who likes to investigate anything interesting, while Snickolas is a little more cautious and prefers to hide first and decide later whether something is safe. Give him a little time, though, and he'll be out and ready for attention!
Oreo is endlessly curious and has a adorable habit of resting her front paws on anything within reach-whether it's a toy, the laundry rack, the water bowl, or even her favorite person. If you're sitting in bed, don't be surprised to find two little paws resting on your hip. She's also a fantastic self-entertainer who especially loves kickers and small toys she can bat around.
Snickolas, meanwhile, is the cuddle bug of the pair. Once he's comfortable, he can never get enough pets, and at night he likes to sleep with his back pressed against your leg. Oreo is a little more independent, but she'll sometimes curl up next to you in bed, too, when she's in the mood
Both siblings are happy to let you know when they want attention with a well-timed meow, and they share a serious appreciation for "cat TV"-especially a good window with something interesting happening outside.
They have their own sibling dynamic, too: Snickolas is often the instigator, occasionally starting a playful tussle by simply sitting on Oreo. They'll sometimes try to spook each other for fun, but they're generally very friendly with one another and are perfectly content to share a windowsill while they supervise the neighborhood.
Together, Snickolas and Oreo are a wonderful balance: a curious, confident little explorer and her affectionate, slightly more cautious brother. They may take a little time to settle into a new environment, but once they do, they'll reward their person with plenty of personality, companionship, and adorable quirks. 🐱🐱

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am bonded to Snickolas. We must go home together and our adoption fee includes both of us!
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I am bonded to Snickolas. We must go home together and our adoption fee includes both of us!

A volunteer writes: Oreo Krispies and Snickolas may have a notably limited grasp of personal space as an applied concept, but if personal space with cats isn't a concern or you just get a kick out of watching adult cats barrel into each other with the grace of kittens, they're probably the pair you want to meet. Appearing to be joined at the hip (or the foot, or the ear, or whatever is closest at the moment) they're genuinely thrilled at the prospect of adding more to this party. They sit at the front of their condo like little bookends and excitedly confer with each other after any movement in the room like nosy little pigeons as they wait for someone to join in. Patience may not be one of their interests, specifically Oreo Krispies who dutifully intercepted each pet I tried to share with her brother by nuzzling underneath my hand. He eventually got his turn for cuddles but one thing is for certain, this lovely duo would love to have their turn together and we hope you'll come in and meet them soon.

227016.name: Princess Shelly
227016.summary:
My foster writes: Hi! I'm Princess Shelly, the sweetest, sleepiest girl who loves treats. I adapt to new environments quickly and love to explore and follow you around, getting involved in what you're doing. I am super athletic, jumping like LeBron James. I use my litter box like a princess and do not knock things off tables and counters🙅‍♀️❌ I can't wait for you to become my favorite pillow!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

 My foster wrote: I am a super playful cat that's curious about everything and anything around me! I love chasing toys or pointers and am really interested in what's going on outside the window. I love being in the same room as you if not on top of you as much as I can!

A volunteer writes: Princess Shelly has her own style and has been forging her own path. Only Princess Shelly is Princess Shelly but I thought I would talk through some ideas with her and she asked me to please keep my ideas and my hands to myself. Fair enough. She's going to do this and she's going to do it her way, thank you very much. I appreciate her heart and her independence more than I can say and was grateful when Princess Shelly gave me some alternatives as we built a friendship. Princess Shelly loves to play and spiritedly ran into her cubby to reach her paws out for her toy. Pretending I couldn't see her, I bought into her game and watched in awe as she waved her paws around to catch it. We've heard that Princess Shelly isn't often a fan of new people, which adds a bit of a challenge to shelter life. She just has her style and is hoping you'll come in and give her a chance soon.

227499.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

King H is at risk due to behavioral concerns. King H recently returned to our care as a stray. During his previous stay, King H was surrendered due to a bite incident in the home which left one puncture. In the care center King H is noted to have a tense body and will head whip when unfamiliar handlers interact with him. With familiar handlers, King H has been noted to be social with handlers, approaching with a soft body and wagging tail. Medically, King H has dental disease and is overweight

King H previously arrived at MACC following a bite incident. It was reported that he bit the owner's partner on the finger. This bite was a bite and release that resulted in a puncture wound. Recently King has returned to the care center. He has been observed to head whip during contact and become tense when toys are in his possession. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

227670.name: Rosie
227670.summary:
Meet Juniper, a sweet and affectionate cat who's as graceful as she is friendly. With a lively spirit and curious nature, Juniper loves to explore her surroundings and engage with people. She's social, people-oriented, and enjoys head scratches, gentle petting, and even being picked up-purring and trilling with delight.

Juniper has shown herself to be calm, easygoing, and incredibly loving. She greets visitors at her kennel with soft eyes and a raised tail, eager for interaction and attention. Her affectionate and adaptable personality makes her an excellent match for adopters of all experience levels.

While she may need a brief adjustment period in a new home, Juniper's confident and cuddly nature suggests she'll settle in quickly. Whether you're a first-time cat adopter or a seasoned feline fan, Juniper is ready to bring joy and companionship into your life.

227706.name: Penne
227706.summary:
As a part of OG's Starting Five, I will receive a year of free pet food from Royal Canin. VCA will also provide one free year of unlimited exams with a CareClub Access Plan.


A volunteer writes: The one cat who will love you unconditionally and be your soulmate. The perfect lapcat!
Penne came to us with nine housemates and a dog as they were left behind in an empty apartment. Penne is quiet and relaxed. She seems to have a degree in perfect pethood and does all the right things to charm me or any other visitors to her den. She comes right away for a meet and greet, purrs softly, makes little biscuits and leans non stop into pets. Penne is a great cat sure to make a new owner happy to have chosen her as a forever best friend. Come and meet her ASAP!


What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
My purr motor is always running!
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!

I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Horizon was at the back, looking slightly tense, lying on his side. He sniffed treats and allowed petting, but gave a quick hiss, then relaxed slightly and continued to allow petting on his head, cheek, and along his back. Pick-up was not attempted due to his medical condition, but he's a sweet cat who may need some adjustment time in his new home.

Horizon interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or who demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

228190.name: Sable
228190.summary:
My foster writes: Hi! I'm Sable! I'm a beautiful, very shy girl but becoming sweeter and sweeter by the day! My history is a mystery, but I don't seem to have had a lot of human contact prior to my being fostered! I at first was too scared to be around humans, but now when my foster parents are in bed but not asleep yet, I immediately jump up for pets! I love chin scratches and head scratches! I occasionally give love bites but never bit down! I love "making biscuits" on my foster parents too and especially cute doing this when I start chewing on the comforter a little! My foster parents are very impressed with the progress I've made in just a few months, and with more patience and understanding, am getting more comfortable and happy to be with humans every day!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
Sable interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience, demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

228511.name: Nina
228511.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Nina is at risk due to behavior concerns. These concerns are from a previous reported bite. Nina has demonstrated consistently a low threshold for arousal while in care and in foster. Nina became aroused while on walk and started jumping and mouthing which ended with a wound on handler's arm. While she was previously in foster she was returned due to her behavior concerns. Nina allows handling, is social with her handlers, and very affectionate. Medically, Nina is apparently healthy.

Nina came into the center as a stray but has spent time in foster during her previous stay. She is noted to have a bite history in the foster home and has shown a history of arousal while on a walk and began jumping up, mouthing, and tugging on her handlers sleeve. A period of decompression is recommended to allow Nina to acclimate comfortably to her new environment; force-free, reward based training only is advised when introducing Nina to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Nina presents with outside of the care centers.

My foster writes: Nina is a 4-year-old, 64-lb sweetheart who strikes the perfect balance between playful and cozy. She enjoys her walks and will happily trot along, but her true passion is curling up on the couch for a good nap or snuggle session. She's also a big fan of people-watching-give her a balcony or a window and she'll happily hang out, watching the world go by like it's her favorite show.
She's been known to fall asleep flat on her back with her paws in the air and snore like she owns the place! On walks, Nina lies down when she sees other dogs because she really wants to say hello. She's non-reactive and has shown nothing but friendliness so far, though her foster home hasn't officially tested her with other pets. She's also learned to communicate when she needs to go out and is making great progress with potty training as she adjusts to home life.
Nina isn't a fan of the crate-but she doesn't need one! She's quiet, gentle, and non-destructive when left to relax freely. One of her sweetest quirks is "corncobbing" and gently sucking on her blanket or stuffed animal to self-soothe-she never destroys them, just cuddles and comforts herself.
She's a smart girl who already knows sit, stay, come, off, and leave it. Nina would thrive in a home that gives her affection (but gives her space until she's ready for it!), daily walks, a comfy spot to snooze, and a good window or balcony to supervise her neighborhood. If you're looking for a loving, goofy, low-maintenance companion with a heart of gold, Nina might just be your perfect match.

Nina is a bright and determined pup enrolled in our Shelter Scholars program, where she's working on managing on-leash reactivity and developing more calm, confident walking habits. Through positive reinforcement training, focused leash work, and enrichment activities, Nina is learning how to stay connected with her handlers.

228889.name: Blanket
228889.summary:
My foster writes: Blanket is an absolutely gorgeous torti girl, she adores other cats! and dogs (with socialization time and a very calm environment) and can open up to be such a sweetheart. 
Her favorite scratch spots are her head, neck and top of her back, but most of all she ADORES it when you scratch her cheeks (like brushing her teeth, but with her cheeks 😂) 
She had high confidence and will greet you at the door, but can get quite scared at certain things. She's great with loud sounds but can get Skittish with fast movements and uncommonsounds. She'd do best in a home with one or multiple cats, she usually runs away from children as they can be too much for her (i get it) and a calm residential.

Blanket is such a unique sweetheart and ADORES any and any peice of trash! Wrappers, STICKS anything she can bop around WILL be bopped, she loves to come cuddle up right on top of you, nugget, and fall asleep on you, thats probably why her name is blanket!

Some of her hobbies include window watching, trying to get love from the resident cat, morning snuggles, staring at the automatic feeder 20 minutes before it goes off, climbing anything she can, and getting into bags! 


My foster writes: Blanket is a beautiful tortoiseshell who was given glowing reviews from her former owner. She is accustomed to living with many cats, as well as adult humans and older children. In the foster home, Blanket is friendly and enjoys gentle pets. She is moderately energetic and loves chasing after toys. She is food motivated and is an excellent candidate for clicker training. Blanket likely has a food allergy which causes hair loss, but is doing well on a poultry-based diet. While she does have a nearly permanent grouchy expression, she is actually very sweet, with a bit of attitude (standard tortitude level). Blanket is a good candidate for an adopter with previous cat experience.

My foster writes: Meet Blanket, yes Blanket! Shes as warm and cuddly as her name sake! A beautiful and small medium torti girl. She LOVES other cats and while she can be pretty shy and scared at first but especially with another cat around is VERY quick to warm up. She's a quirky girl who will play with ANYTHING you try with, paper? Any stick? Your pinkies finger? She will gently play with it XD anything is a toy if you try hard enough! She has slight issues like allergies and but overall is an extremely good kitty.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

229617.name: Laguardia
229617.summary:
Meet **LaGuardia** ✈️-no delays, just naps! 

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

This sweet, low-maintenance girl is a professional snoozer who happily supervises the home or office from the comfort of her dog bed. She greets every human like an old friend, belly up and ready for head scratches, and has zero interest in chewing, barking, jumping on people or causing trouble.
Her quirks? She's still learning that walks are for strolling, not shouting at other animals. She's also not the biggest fan of peanut butter or stairs (though she'll put up with both if she has to). Give her a crunchy snack, preferably plant-based-watermelon cubes, green beans, cabbage, cucumber, you name it-and she'll be your biggest fan.
LaGuardia's motto: **nap hard, snack often, love everyone.** 🐾💤

My ideal home

A calm, adult-only home that will give LGA time to decompress and continue positive-reinforcement training. She's easy-going inside, enjoys meeting new people, and thrives with a predictable routine, enrichment (sniffy walks, food puzzles), and lots of cuddle breaks. Adult-only (no children under 13). LGA is working on her confidence and can be uncomfortable around high-energy environments. LGA can become tense around other dogs on leash and has shown kennel reactivity. She may do best as the only pet while she builds skills.(Cats: unknown.)

Leash Manners: Polite walker at your side once she settles in. When she sees other dogs, she may get stiff and focused; treats, distance, and a front-clip harness help her reset. She's learning check-ins and responds to patient, reward-based guidance.

 LGA is affectionate and leans in for pets-she simply needs consistent, kind coaching to feel secure. Her foster calls her a "sweet, loving mush" who will lounge near you all day.

My foster writes: Let little LaGuardia love you! This perfect-sized munchkin wants nothing more than to snuggle and give kisses. A chill, low-energy dog, LGA doesn't need much in her golden years. While she does ask everyone to pay the cheese tax, really all that she wants is a quiet home, a comfy couch to lie on, and someone to be her favorite person to make her a happy girl!

229621.name: Nipsey
229621.summary:
My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! 

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Nipsey is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Nipsey is a social dog with staff and actively participates in training. Recently, however, he has been showing signs of increased anxiety and arousal. He has been panting heavily and repeatedly jumping on staff, at times reaching up toward their heads. During walks, he appears to stay focused only when treats are consistently provided. Once the treats stop, he immediately returns to jumping on the staff. Medically, Nipsey is apparently healthy.

Meet Nipsey!
Nipsey was found tied up and alone and is now ready for a fresh start. He is a social, affectionate boy who enjoys being around people and happily accepts pets and attention. He has a friendly, easygoing demeanor in interactions and is quick to engage, especially when treats or snuggles are involved.

My Ideal Home
Nipsey would do best in a home that can provide structure, routine, and regular activity. He thrives on companionship and would benefit from someone who can spend time with him and help him feel secure when home alone. An adopter committed to continued training will help him build confidence and good habits.

Good with Other Pets?
Nipsey has shown neutral, appropriate behavior toward other dogs in care, including calm greetings and the ability to disengage. With proper introductions, he may do well with a compatible canine companion.

Good with Kids?
Nipsey is recommended for an adult-only home due to on-leash reactivity and the potential for becoming overly aroused in social situations.

Things to Know
Nipsey pulls moderately on leash and will benefit from continued work on leash manners. He may bark when he hears knocks or unfamiliar people approaching and can feel anxious when left alone, so gradual alone-time training will be helpful. He is comfortable with handling and enjoys physical affection.

Fun Fact
Nipsey is always ready for some quality cuddle time, if you sit down, don't be surprised if he's right there soaking up the love.

229786.name: Nivens
229786.summary:
**Meet Nivens**

---

**My Ideal Home**
Nivens is an active, social bunny who will thrive in a home where she can explore and interact with her people daily. A spacious, bunny-proofed setup is a must-she's constantly on the move and loves climbing, zooming, and investigating everything (especially your shoes!). She'd do well with an adopter ready to provide enrichment, time outside of her pen, and plenty of love as she grows into a confident adult rabbit.

---

**Good with Kids?**
Yes! Nivens is very friendly and has no concept of personal space-in the best way. Her playful nature makes her a fun companion for older, respectful children who understand how to safely interact with a young rabbit.

---

**Litter Box Trained?**
Nivens is still a baby and learning, but she's well on her way! Rabbits generally become more consistent with litter habits after spay/neuter surgery, which she'll be ready for soon. With time and patience, she'll be a clean little house bunny.

---

**Behavior Determination: Other**
In a word: delightful. Nivens loves people, attention, and especially your shoelaces. She's inquisitive, playful, and always the first to run over when someone enters the room. Her affectionate, bold nature makes her a great match for someone looking for an interactive rabbit buddy.

---

**Fun Facts**

* Nivens has a shoe obsession-you've been warned!
* She'll happily hop right into your lap...or your face. She's still working on boundaries.

---

**Before You Adopt a Rabbit...**
Rabbits aren't low-maintenance pets-they need daily cleaning, enrichment, time out of their pens, and a special diet rich in hay and fresh greens. Nivens may be small now, but she's growing fast and needs a home ready for the long-term commitment rabbits require. With the right care, she'll reward you with binkies, snuggles, and endless laughs.

If you're ready for a curious, comical companion, Nivens is ready to hop into your heart! 🐰❤️

My foster writes: Meet Nivens, the ultimate people-loving bunny!
If you've ever dreamed of a rabbit who's friendly, curious, and endlessly charming, Nivens might just be your perfect match. She greets you at the front of her pen the moment you walk in, happily eats treats right out of your hand, and warms up to people almost instantly.
Nivens adores affection, follows her humans around during free roam, enjoys pets and snuggles, and even gives nose kisses when you lean in close. She's brave, playful, and loves to explore, but she's just as happy taking cozy midday naps complete with the cutest bunny flops.
She would thrive in a home where she gets plenty of love, enrichment, and time to play and explore. Whether you're a first-time rabbit parent or an experienced bunny lover, Nivens is truly a dream rabbit who makes everyone fall in love with rabbits a little more.

229787.name: McTwisp
229787.summary:
My foster writes:
McTwisp came to our home at the recommendation of the ACC foster team after he spent 4 months in the shelter, and we are so grateful for that! Honestly, we have no idea how he hasn't been adopted yet; a bunny with this demeanor is rare (and he actually reminds us of a previous foster we had!).
For the first 2 days, he was very shy and stayed mostly in his hidey. However, he gently took treats from us while in his safe space. From day 1, his litter box skills were impeccable!
On the third day with us, he spent more and more time outside of the hidey, and engaged with us when we sat in his pen. He started booping our feet and legs, which was so cute! Within another day, we let him out of the pen and he was so happy!
McTwisp really enjoys enrichment - digging activities, eating cardboard, running through a tunnel, chew toys, climbing on the couch, the snuffle mat for foraging, and more! He is food motivated, making bonding extra easy - also, he is super gentle when he takes food from us. He is a very clean boy and is too cute as he washes his little face and ears. His binkies and zoomies are just delightful to watch. He has even started climbing on the bed when he is hoping his human shows up for company.
After several months with us, and changes as college kids come and go, I'm pleased to share that McTwisp remains such a delightful boy. He is the best work pal - happy to hang next to me in the mornings as I settle into the day, and take a nap at my feet in the afternoon, sometimes even flopping and exposing his belly. If he ever hears the treat bag open, he perks up and comes for a visit. He is always up for snuggles, and once he's comfortable with his humans, he is open to the closest snuggles possible - he's very tolerant and sweet. He remains food motivated and excited for both breakfast of pellets and dinner of fresh greens (lettuce, parsley, basil, mint, etc.). We typically change his litterbox during dinnertime as he sometimes looks nervous when we remove his litterbox when he's not otherwise occupied.
We still think that McTwisp would be a wonderful bunny for a new or experienced bunny family, or even as a partner bun if there's a good fit. He is an absolute angel.
We want him to find his perfect forever home (though we will continue to love fostering him)!

Meet McTwisp
Surrendered due to an unmanageable number of rabbits-this dapper gentleman is ready to hop into your heart!

McTwisp may not carry a pocket watch like the White Rabbit from Alice in Wonderland, but he is a punctual little fellow when it comes to snack time. He's a handsome white bunny with a calm presence, a healthy frame, and the beginnings of a sweet, gentle personality. McTwisp was surrendered with several other rabbits after his previous home became overwhelmed with accidental litters, and now he's ready to start fresh in a place where he can finally settle down.

My Ideal Home
McTwisp would do well in a peaceful home that lets him bloom at his own pace. He appreciates a safe, quiet space and gentle interactions. A home with adults or respectful older kids would suit him best, especially if they're patient and understanding of a bunny's unique needs.

Good with Kids?
He's a bit reserved, so we recommend a home without very young children. Older kids who can be calm, quiet, and gentle will likely earn his trust over time.

Good with Other Pets?
McTwisp hasn't lived with other pets, but may be a good candidate for bonding with another bunny after he's neutered. As always, any introductions should be slow and supervised.

Litter Box Trained?
Not yet-but McTwisp is just the right age to learn. With a consistent setup and a clean space, neutering will help reinforce good litter habits.

His binkies and zoomies are just delightful to watch. He has even started climbing on the bed when he is hoping his human shows up for company.
After several months with us, and changes as college kids come and go, I'm pleased to share that McTwisp remains such a delightful boy. He is the best work pal - happy to hang next to me in the mornings as I settle into the day, and take a nap at my feet in the afternoon, sometimes even flopping and exposing his belly. If he ever hears the treat bag open, he perks up and comes for a visit. He is always up for snuggles, and once he's comfortable with his humans, he is open to the closest snuggles possible - he's very tolerant and sweet. He remains food motivated and excited for both breakfast of pellets and dinner of fresh greens (lettuce, parsley, basil, mint, etc.). We typically change his litterbox during dinnertime as he sometimes looks nervous when we remove his litterbox when he's not otherwise occupied.
We still think that McTwisp would be a wonderful bunny for a new or experienced bunny family, or even as a partner bun if there's a good fit. He is an absolute angel.
We want him to find his perfect forever home (though we will continue to love fostering him)!

Meet McTwisp
Surrendered due to an unmanageable number of rabbits-this dapper gentleman is ready to hop into your heart!

McTwisp may not carry a pocket watch like the White Rabbit from Alice in Wonderland, but he is a punctual little fellow when it comes to snack time. He's a handsome white bunny with a calm presence, a healthy frame, and the beginnings of a sweet, gentle personality. McTwisp was surrendered with several other rabbits after his previous home became overwhelmed with accidental litters, and now he's ready to start fresh in a place where he can finally settle down.

My Ideal Home
McTwisp would do well in a peaceful home that lets him bloom at his own pace. He appreciates a safe, quiet space and gentle interactions. A home with adults or respectful older kids would suit him best, especially if they're patient and understanding of a bunny's unique needs.

Good with Kids?
He's a bit reserved, so we recommend a home without very young children. Older kids who can be calm, quiet, and gentle will likely earn his trust over time.

Good with Other Pets?
McTwisp hasn't lived with other pets, but may be a good candidate for bonding with another bunny after he's neutered. As always, any introductions should be slow and supervised.

Litter Box Trained?
Not yet-but McTwisp is just the right age to learn. With a consistent setup and a clean space, neutering will help reinforce good litter habits.

229904.name: Tom Tom
229904.summary:
My foster writes: Tom tom is really the sweetest, most playful cat in the world. He showed no apprehension about a new environment and immediately wanted to explore when he arrived in my apartment. He loves pets and kisses, and he even lets me rub his little belly. He's quite a sleep boy during the day, but likes to take breaks from his nap to plop himself on my laptop and drink from the kitchen sink. He loves to play with his toys, especially at night. He is the most lovable little cat ever!

My foster writes:
Hi! I'm Tom Tom (or so I'm told; I absolutely do not know my name). I'll come over if you make kissy sounds, though, because I love people! I may look a little grumpy, but I'm as sweet as can be. I'm a curious, playful, and affectionate boy. I'll even let you pick me up! Will I interrupt your work because I want to play? Maybe, but you probably need to take more breaks away. Scratch my neck and I'm yours forever. I'm also super soft with stripes on my back and spots on my belly. I'm still making up my mind about being brushed, but I think I like it so far. I'm always up for a good play season and if you can tire me out then I'll be ready to hang out on the sofa or hop into your lap. I'm always on the look out for toys to chase and sunny spots to nap in.
I'm a good (if slightly messy) eater and I always use my litter box. I'm also good at drinking my water, which makes my foster fam very happy.
Speaking of my foster fam, did you see the bakery they made me? I call it Tom Tom's Treat Treats and I'm told that, if you want, you can bring it home with me to help support kitty employment.
Likes: things on strings, attention, doing a big stretch. Dislikes: being ignored, closed doors

Another foster writes: Tom Tom has been an amazing fit to my family, he's sweet and very gentle with kids. He's very playful and is always willing to be pet. He's very vocal with his needs and loves to be around humans. Tom Tom would be an amazing fit into a family with playful and energetic humans.
