229951.name: Blizzard
229951.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Blizzard (aka "Lizzie") 🤍
Blizzard is a stunning REW (red-eyed white) bunny with a gentle soul and a delightfully sassy streak. She first came to the shelter in July 2025 and, after a short adoption that didn't quite work out, she's now thriving in foster care where she's been able to decompress and truly show her personality.
Lizzie is currently free-roaming 24/7 in a bunny-proofed apartment and has proven herself to be an exceptionally polite house guest. She's well behaved overnight and while left alone during the workday, with excellent litter box habits and a very healthy appetite for hay. (Her poops are top tier, according to her foster.)
While she's still learning that pets and snuggles are a good thing, Blizzard is incredibly curious and brave. She approaches new people right away-especially if treats might be involved-and will happily accept snacks from your hand, making bonding easy and rewarding. With patience and time, she's expected to grow even more relaxed and affectionate.
Blizzard is an active bunny who loves space to hop, binky, and fully sploot out. She enjoys enrichment, playtime, and especially her chew toys, so a tidy, rabbit-savvy home where tempting human items are kept out of reach would be ideal. She also loves to burrow under blankets and will occasionally hop onto the couch to hang out nearby.
One of her most endearing traits? Blizzard greets her people with 3-5 rapid-fire nose boops to the ankles. If attention isn't immediate, she may add a dramatic back-leg stomp to make her feelings known. She lounges comfortably out in the open near her foster while they work or read, naps close by, and even gives sweet little kisses to her stuffed animals-especially her favorite stuffed seal.
Blizzard would do best in a calm, patient home with someone who understands rabbits and is willing to let her confidence and affection continue to blossom. With time, she's sure to become an incredibly loving and entertaining companion.

230137.name: Bonnie

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bonnie was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Bonnie has been highly fearful during her stay in care, staying at the back of his kennel with a tense body and trembling, avoiding interaction with the handlers and seeking exit. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Bonnie be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can allow her the time and space to acclimate and decompress on her own terms.

230214.name: Lizzy
230214.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Lizzy is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Lizzy was returned to the Care Center due to her previous adopter no longer being able to care for her. Her previous adopter reported that Lizzy is playful, social, and affectionate. Unfortunately, Lizzy is showing signs of deterioration. At times has been observed to be pacing the perimeter of her kennel, spinning, barking, and vocalizing. When outside of the kennel environment Lizzy remains an easy walk, is soft bodied during contact, and is treat receptive. Medically, Lizzy is noted be overweight and has otitis chronic.

Lizzy arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. Lizzy's previous owner states that she has handling sensitivity and will escalate to biting when her paws are touched. During her assessment Lizzy began to mouth the handler when they grabbed her collar. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.
 
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I am really treat motivated. You can use treats to teach me new things!

A Volunteer Wrote: Lizzy quickly became a volunteer and staff favorite because she is the most delightful, perfect company! She is cheerful and funny and affectionate; she loves lying on a park bench next to her walker and checking out the scene, and all the better if we both pet her at the same time. Lizzy showed no reaction to dogs in the park. When I told a staff member I loved her she said, "Who doesn't love Lizzy?" So will you!!

230500.name: Lindt
230500.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

A volunteer writes: Lindt's nine years young and being asked to start anew. It's hardly ideal and for someone as gentle hearted as Lindt, well it's just easier said than done. He was brought to us when his guardian passed away and all of these big changes and heartbreaks seem to have really done an understandable number on his confidence. Lindt was huddled in the back of his cubby when I visited and looked like he'd been hoping I would forget he's there. Except, we can't forget he's there. Lindt may not be able to show us all his best sides under the day to day hustle and bustle of the shelter, but he'd still like the chance to show you. He could use a little patience and a whole lot of love as he becomes the cat he's meant to be.

230978.name: Bolton
230978.summary:
My foster writes: Bolton is very shy, he's quiet and well behaved. He loves to be in your company once he become adjusted to his new surroundings.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!
Bolton was in the den, appearing slightly fearful, staring out past the assessor with large pupils. He sniffed treats and accepted petting without visibly reacting to it, and he remained focused on the world outside the kennel.

Bolton tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

232213.name: Ice T
232213.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Iced T is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the prior home, Iced T was reported to become over aroused with his finders and accidentally bit a person's hand, resulting in a bite-and-release that broke skin. In the care center, Iced T has also been reported to snap during a medical examination when being handled. Iced T in the care center is exuberant but is social with staff and loves to go on walks. Medically, Iced T is apparently healthy.

Ice T came into the care center as a stray; due to this, his behavioral history in the prior home is unknown. Ice T is reported to have a bite incident when with the finder. The behavior department recommends  Ice T be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow  Ice T to acclimate comfortably to his new environment; force-free, reward based training only is advised when introducing Ice T to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Ice T presents with outside of the care centers.\

A volunteer writes: Ice T was initially a little scared, but very quickly he became his wiggly, friendly self. Overall, he is a playful, high energy boy who loves to be around people. He is known to press his body into you, asking for pets.
Ice T displayed neutral body language during one gate greet with another dog at the shelter.
Last summer, Ice T was brought in by police after a landlord called them for help with a tenant who continued to tie up Ice T in the hallway. Ultimately, Ice T was reunited with his family. This year, Ice T was found with a harness and leash walking around a construction site. The workers there worked slowly to gain his trust, since he was initially a little nervous, and eventually were able to catch him and bring him to ACC. He benefits from a slow approach, but once he is comfortable he is a bundle of joy and energy. Ice T is available for rescue partners.

232450.name: Max
232450.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Max is at risk for behavior reasons. Max is dog reactive and was kept in a pop-up crate initially for space. When moved to the dog room, he began to deteriorate, jumping up and biting at the leash, persistently making him a handling risk in care. We have been better able to manage him in a crate in an office, which is not an ideal living situation in the shelter. Medically, he is overweight. 

Max is a social, affectionate, and playful male dog who loves being part of the family. He enjoys spending his time wherever his people are, especially relaxing in the living room, and has a wonderful balance of playful energy and laid-back couch potato moments. Max loves car rides and is always happy to join you on your next adventure. He also enjoys playing tug-of-war, spending time with his toys, and earning treats-he isn't picky and appreciates just about any snack!

Max walks 3-4 times a day and has mild to moderate leash pulling. His walks are kept short, usually around 10 minutes, because he tires easily and often enjoys taking a break by lying in the grass before heading home. He is crate trained and is comfortable relaxing in a large crate for up to eight hours when needed. Max also knows basic cues such as "sit" and "stay."

His previous owner described him as a sweet, gentle dog who may look intimidating at first but is truly a big teddy bear. He can be a little clingy at times, but that's usually his way of letting you know he's bored and ready for a toy or some playtime. After getting his exercise and having some fun, Max is happiest curling up for a long nap by your side. If you're looking for a loyal, affectionate companion who enjoys both playtime and relaxation, Max could be the perfect addition to your family.

232710.name: Diotima
232710.summary:
My foster writes:
Here's Diomita, or Lady Di. She's a super sweet little lady who certainly does things on her own timeline! She's very loving and will come up for attention, but she will also hide for hours at a time. Diomita is curious and loves to look out the window and play. She will jump on your lap and purr when she's comfortable. Diomita does give little love bites, so it may be best for her to be in a home free of young children. Due to her need for play, she would probably be good in a home with another pet, but it may take a moment for her to acclimate.

A volunteer writes:
Diotima is a cute little lady who is with us as her owner passed away. She lived with fourteen other cats and we were told that she was fine with them. Diotoma was a bit nervous when she arrived at the care center, giving a little growl and a little hiss, here and there. She is still a bit skittish, worries that someone might snatch her food, something she is very much in need of(she is quite on the thin side). Diotima is a social kitty but she nevertheless likes a gentle approach and a soft voice. She pops out right away of her bedroom to meet her visitor and very much enjoys petting without ever seeming annoyed. She peeks sometimes in the adjacent kennel and does not appear bothered at all by the other cat looking intensely at her. Diotima has alopecia(hairloss) on her belly and inner legs. This is why for now, she wears a collar and is on a special diet. This condition and its potential causes/management can be discussed with the adoption counselors. Diotima is a sweet gal known to be calm, gentle and affectionate, very much in need of TLC as well as a quiet and loving home. Ask to meet this young and lovely kitty when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

233021.name: Mr. Fluffy Garfield

What my friends at ACC say about me:

233101.name: Lovely Lody
233101.summary:
Meet Load O' Potatoes!
Found as a stray and brought to the 90th Precinct before coming to ACC, this affectionate city walker is ready to trade kennel noise for cozy naps and neighborhood strolls. Volunteers rave about her sweet manners and cuddle game on BoroughBreaks.

My Ideal Home
An experienced, adult-only home that offers calm structure, patience, and a thoughtful decompression plan. Routine sniffy walks, enrichment (food puzzles, long-lasting chews), and reward-based training will help her shine. A front-clip harness and clear, consistent cues set her up for success.

Good with Kids?
Recommended adult-only (no children under 13) based on shelter observations and behavior team guidance.

Good with Other Pets?
Best as the only dog for now. In the busy kennel room she can be reactive (barking/lunging), but outdoors-with space and support-she often passes dogs without fuss. No dog parks. If you have a resident dog, plan slow, structured introductions with professional guidance. Potatoes needs a home without cats or small animals.

Leash Manners
Often a loose, thoughtful walker who checks in with her handler. If excited, she may briefly grab the leash; this has been easy to redirect with treats or a squeaker. She's tolerant of gentle petting during walk breaks and navigates sidewalks well when supported.

Overall Health
Spayed. Vet team notes dental tartar; regular dental care, balanced diet, and everyday exercise will help her feel her best. Previously had a shelter cough that resolved. (Your vet can personalize her wellness plan once home.)

Behavior Determination & Other
ACC Behavior Level: 3
Recommendations: Adult-only; no dog parks; front-clip harness; reward-based training to build focus around other dogs. In kennel/play-yard settings she may react toward neighboring dogs; on the street, distance and support help her stay composed.

Fun Facts
Her BoroughBreak buddies called her "an absolute angel" with "paw-tastic manners." Car-ride comfy, picnic-ready, generous with kisses, and a champion at settling after a good walk.

Ready to meet Load O' Potatoes?
If you love training, structure, and cuddly couch time-and you're ready to be her safe landing-Lo's your girl.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Lo was an absolute angel and pawtastic! She was very well-behaved and had great manners. She is very sweet and gave loads of kisses! She was never hesitant and was always ready for the next adventure!

A Volunteer Wrote: I first met her flat on her back. She had thrown herself down, in a fit of pleasure, on the sidewalk, and was scratching her back on the cement and wriggling around and wagging her tail, while her borough break buddy looked equally delighted. "She's just the best!" she reported in on her morning with our girl. She's endlessly affectionate, has fantastic manners, and is adored by all of us because she's been here long enough for us all to fall in love. Please--come break her out, once and for all, and let the back scratches begin!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Sandy is a great girl: very smart, quiet, and doesn't bark at all. She'll approach you when she wants to play. Sandy loves to bring you ropes and toys, always eager for a spirited game of tug-of-war.
She's an exceptional companion: intelligent, gentle, and remarkably quiet-she never barks. When she's in the mood to play, she'll come right over and let you know. To me, she is the perfect dog-adorable in every way and a joy to have around.

I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

233230.name: Bunny Holiday
233230.summary:
My foster writes:
Bunny Holiday is a sweet girl with a cute habit of sleeping on her side so you'll see plenty of adorable flops once she feels safe and comfortable.
She would do best with an experienced rabbit owner who understands that trust takes time, and in a calm home where she can adjust at her own pace. Bunny Holiday is shy and fearful when meeting new people. It is normal for her to run away, hide or thump when approached.
It took a couple of weeks for her to warm up in foster care. Consistency and positive reinforcement makes all the difference to reward her with a small treat when she allows pets and social time.
Bunny Holiday's future adopter should be prepared to earn her trust slowly and celebrate the small wins along the way. With patience and a predictable routine, she continues to make progress and show her gentle personality. Watching her gain confidence is incredibly rewarding.

My foster writes: Bunny is looking for the right calm and patient home that will foster the right environment for her to open up. She is sweet and gentle, but is still learning to love people. She lays on her side to sleep and sploots when she is relaxed, she loves her veggies and to eat out of stacking cups. She loves burrowing in hay and is for the most part a lower maintenance girl.

233434.summary:
My foster writes:
Guava is a shy girl who adores being pet on her terms and in her time. She is curious and adventurous and loves a window! While climbing around in exploration, she is dainty and careful, never knocking things over or making a mess. She can't wait to settle into a quiet and loving home where she can finally come out of her shell and give all her love and cuddles to her forever family.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming.  
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

233442.name: Dr. Mouse
233442.summary:
My foster writes: Mouse is such a curious little fellow. Despite his history and lack of socialization, he consistently shows signs of wanting to get closer to me. He often assigns himself the role of bathroom-guard and makes sure I am never alone when I'm in there. He loves to explore and is always seeking to discover his newest, comfiest hangout spot. Mouse is always showing his playful and lively side when he gets his daily zoomies, but he is also very content to just lay beside you while you're working at your desk. He loves to accompany you to the kitchen just in case you might have any treats to share. I see him at his most content when he lays next to my screened-in window, simply enjoying the fresh air and watching the bugs and birds. If you want a professional fly swatter, Mouse is the man for your job. Sometimes I forget that he's not just a baby because he always exhibits such youthful and curious behavior. Getting to know this guy is such a rewarding process.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.

233706.name: Starlight Twilight
233706.summary:
My foster writes: I am Starlight Twilight, a big boy with the soul of a little kitten. My foster parents love that I am a curious and playful kitty, yet also a calm companion who enjoys being near you. I thrive in a peaceful environment because I can be a bit nervous and easily startled, but I've been growing more confident every day. The presence of another cat at home has been really soothing for me and reassuring of safety. Having him around has been an important boost of my trust in humans.
I get along very well with my resident cat brother, I like to follow his lead and see the world the way he shows it to me. I constantly seek to play and hang out with him. I also love chasing toys, playing with feather wands, racing for my favorite treats, and I am an exceptional fly's hunter.
Most of the time, I am a silent boy, but I can get vocal if I'm worried. Sometimes, I also vocalize when I get excited to see my cat brother or when I want some pets, because yes, I ask for them. I am a sweet and affectionate kitty, always ready to melt into your hands. I don't mind you rubbing all of my body, but my favorites are scratches on my chin, cheeks, and the base of my tail. I can also allow belly rubs, which turns me into a cuddling baby. I especially love when people talk to me softly, it makes me feel safe, loved, and cherished. I'm still a little unsure about kisses and not to fond of being carried on hands, but I'm slowly learning to tolerate it. And I have even allowed my nails to be clipped three times already!
I am a master at finding cozy, hidden spots for naps during the day, and if I hear something fun happening, I'll want to be included and will run to join in immediately. But don't get me wrong, I also love to nap on the bed near you while you watch TV.
I appreciate your patience in getting to know me since I need time to trust people. With time, my foster parents believe I'll grow into a big cuddler.
If you're seeking the ideal mix of curiosity, playfulness, quietness, and independent companionship, I hope to find a loving forever home with you.

Starlight Twilight tolerates some attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

233894.name: Coco Mango Cherry
233894.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Coco Mango Cherry is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Coco MC was returned to shelter due to behaviors in the home; her previous adopter reported that Coco MC would bark and snap towards a new child in the home.  During her current stay, Coco MC was initially fearful but allows easy leashing for walks, tolerates petting from select staff, and is treat receptive. Unfortunately, Coco MC has still shown defensive behaviors. Recently she was observe to growl and lip-curl toward a staff member when attempting to remove her from a crate.  Medically, Coco MC is noted to have undermined allergies, alopecia, otitis chronic, and pyoderma.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

233975.name: Aurora
233975.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
Meet Aurora, a beautiful and affectionate grey land seal who is as smart as she is loving. She's food motivated, quick to learn, and lights up when it's time for training. Aurora thrives on enrichment and loves anything that keeps her mind busy, from puzzle feeders and lick mats to her favorite food toys.
At home, she's a mix of curiosity and sweetness. She sleeps through the night in her crate, loves belly rubs, and has the most endearing habit of nursing on soft things like her bed or toys when she's settling down. She's fully house trained now and even lets you know when she needs to go outside.
Aurora is still learning how to stay calm during exciting moments, especially around other dogs, and she's been working closely with a trainer. She does best with a steady routine, gentle guidance, and someone who enjoys helping her learn.
She would thrive with an experienced adopter who can offer structure, exercise, and plenty of love. In return, Aurora will bring warmth, goofiness, and endless affection to your home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

My foster writes: Litchi is a sweet and gentle cat who adores human company. She might seem a little shy at first, but within moments she'll be purring and asking for cuddles. Her favorite things include face rubs, naps in sunny spots, and showing off her belly when she's happy. Litchi would be the perfect companion for anyone looking for a calm, affectionate friend.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Litchi appreciates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed at times in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
My purr motor is always running!
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!

I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

234010.name: Leonard
234010.summary:
My foster writes: Leonard is an extremely people-oriented cat who loves companionship, brushing, and soothing interaction. He would likely thrive in a home where someone has plenty of time to give him the closeness and grooming he craves. Leonard is so good, so sweet that he deserves to be celebrated for his rebellious wild side! He's the perfect cat for a peaceful clean home. Leonard needs lots of attention and love.

Leonard is a once-in-a-lifetime kind of cat - a sweet, gentle
soul wrapped in kitten energy and curiosity. From the
moment he first meets you, he's all heart. Leonard shows his
love in unforgettable ways: he gives the softest, sweetest
kisses that will melt you completely. He's never aggressive
- just a playful, affectionate boy who thrives on closeness
and trust.
⸻
Leonard's Favorite Things
• Kisses & Cuddles: His special way of saying
"you're my person."
• Brushing Sessions: Leonard adores being brushed
- especially his face and head. He'll happily guide you
to the spots he loves most, rewarding you with purrs and
snuggles.
• Playtime: Lightning-fast zoomies, tunnels, and
crunchy foil toys make him come alive. He's a kitten at
heart - rambunctious but never mean-spirited.
• Velcro Cat Moments: Leonard loves to be close.
He'll curl up on your lap, sit by your side, or even
gently perch at your feet, keeping you company with
devotion.
⸻
What Leonard Needs in a Family
• Lots of Time Together: Leonard bonds deeply. A
retired person or someone home often would be ideal -
he's happiest when he has his people nearby.
• Understanding His Mischief: Like any cat,
Leonard has playful, silly, "naughty" moments -
especially when human food is involved. He's smart
enough to know the rules, but still cheeky enough to test
them now and then. His new family must be dedicated
to keeping him safe from foods that could harm him.
• Gentle & Patient Love: Leonard thrives with
people who celebrate him - who see his kisses,
zoomies, and quirks as proof of his amazing personality,
not as problems.
⸻
How to Love Leonard 💜
1. Brush him daily, always finishing with his
favorite head and face strokes.
2. Keep him safe by protecting him from human
food temptations.
3. Celebrate his playful energy - tunnels, foil balls,
and toys keep him happy.
4. Accept his kisses, cuddles, and constant closeness
- he's a Velcro cat through and through.
5. Above all, treasure him as the extraordinary
companion he is.
⸻
✨ Leonard isn't "just a cat." He's affectionate, funny, loyal,
and deeply loving - the kind of companion who fills a
home with warmth and joy. Whoever adopts Leonard will be
gaining a best friend who gives back 1000 percent in kisses,
purrs, and unwavering love. 

A volunteer writes:
Leonard, a young ginger was found hurt in the street and brought to us to mend his wound. His past is a total mystery opening the path to a whole new life. Sweet Leonard has a booboo at the base of his tail and we are working at getting him all better. He is a sweet guy, quite friendly, trusting and eager to lean into pets, purr and be loved. Cute Leonard will for sure be quite a catch once 100% back on his feet  and in plain sight in our adoption quarters. Keep him in your thoughts and be ready to meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center.

234236.name: Sushi
234236.summary:
My foster writes: Sushi is a beautiful and extremely well-behaved tabico. Independent and self-sufficient, she prefers to watch you with her large green eyes but also enjoys the occasional enthusiastic game of chase the laser pointer.

My foster writes: Meet Sushi 🍣
Sweet, soft, and a little shy-Sushi is a gentle beauty who just needs time to feel safe in her new home. Once she warms up, her quiet charm and adorable looks will melt your heart. Give her patience, and you'll gain a loyal little friend for life. 💖

Sushi is a beautiful Tabico or Caliby (Tabby + Calico) - a quiet, modest beauty, like a tiny flower on a sidewalk, undisturbed, blending into the ordinary landscapes that is usually overlooked in our busy lives.
She appreciates admiration from the distance, slow blinking sessions with soft spoken voices. She lounges and naps on her favorite spots with no frills (cat lotus branch laid down near the floor, behind the cushy cat bed that sits under the chair, and a carrier). Being low energy (no climber or a zoomies from her), she can be a chill cat with the human who leads the Zen lifestyle, being just present nearby and calm in the same room.
She is still learning to trust human - it will be baby steps when she lets her guards down. She waits for the understanding family who will find her charms, appreciate how worth she is, and find her inseparable for life.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A volunteer writes: Sushi tries everyday to start on the right paw and like any of us, her best looks different each day. She was left behind with other cats in an apartment and while we don't know much else about her life before the shelter, we can understand that she's been asked to sort through several big changes and that's quite an ask for a soft and gentle girl such as herself. Snuggled up in her den with paws stretched out wide, Sushi looked at me with a bit of confusion but was trying her best to be open and she's hoping you'll come in and meet her soon.

234708.name: Bay Laurel
234708.summary:
My foster writes: Bay Laurel may be very shy to start (yes, very!) but with patience, play and treats, she is energetic and ready to chase that feather toy until everyone is panting. She is tiny and cute and very friendly (once she gets to know you) - an energetic ball of fluff.

Bay Laurel is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with strangers/humans from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appears wary of human contact. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Innovative and enterprising, Bay Laurel's doing her best to make shelter life work for her. This is no small feat, nor does it look particularly comfortable, but it's right for Bay Laurel and that's what counts. Bay Laurel has a big fluffy bed that she chooses to sleep underneath, nuzzling around to do what she needs like a little ball of fluff. While this sounds adorable and admittedly it is, Bay Laurel definitely isn't loving the Care Center and tends to freeze in place when we try to offer our range of fun toys and delicious treats. She came to us from a home with many other cats. So, when you peek in Bay Laurel's condo, you might just see a fluffy bed but please take a moment to meet her because she just might be the cat for you.

234740.name: Zeus
234740.summary:
Meet Zeus!
Zeus is a sweet older gentleman who found himself at ACC after being found as a stray. He can be a little cautious at first, but once he's comfortable, he's happy to approach his people, sniff around, and accept some treats and affection. We're hoping his next stop is a forever home where he can finally feel safe and settled.

My Ideal Home
Zeus would do best with someone patient who can give him time to adjust to his new surroundings. A calm home, predictable routine, and positive-reinforcement training will help him build confidence while keeping his curious mind busy.

Good with Other Pets?
Zeus' history with other dogs is unknown. He has shown interest in dogs at the shelter, but some interactions have become overly enthusiastic, so slow introductions and careful supervision will be important.

Good with Kids?
Because of Zeus' resource guarding and mouthiness, ACC recommends an adult-only home at this time.

Things to Know
Zeus can be sensitive when he's feeling unsure and will need to be allowed to approach new people and situations at his own pace. He's also working on polite treat-taking and learning to share space around his favorite toys. With patience, positive training, and a little time to decompress, Zeus has a wonderful opportunity to become a confident companion.

234741.name: Biggs
234741.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Biggs!
Biggs was found abandoned with three other dogs and is now looking for a fresh start with a family who will help him settle into the good life he deserves. He's social, people oriented, and has a big personality that comes out once he feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Biggs would do best with an adopter who can provide structure, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training to help guide his enthusiasm. He enjoys attention and engagement from people and will thrive with daily physical and mental exercise like walks, puzzle toys, and interactive play. A home that can continue working on leash manners and impulse control will help him really shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Biggs has shown some interest in other dogs at the care center, but also tends to pull strongly toward smaller dogs on leash. His history with other animals is unknown, so slow, controlled introductions would be important if living with another pet.

Good with Kids?
Due to potential resource guarding tendencies and his strength and enthusiasm, Biggs is recommended for a home without young children at this time.

Things to Know
Biggs is a social and affectionate boy who enjoys being around people and seeks out attention readily. He can be strong on leash and may redirect his energy toward other dogs or exciting stimuli, so he'll do best with continued training and management. He has shown possible interest in guarding valued items, so ongoing trade up games and positive reinforcement around handling and resources will be important. With consistency and structure, Biggs has all the makings of a loyal, fun, and engaging companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Biggs is giving main character energy from the moment you meet him. He's a social, handsome guy who leans in for attention and happily accepts treats like he's starring in his own feel good rom com. Out in the yard, he's engaged and people focused, soaking up interaction and showing off his affectionate side. You might say he's looking for someone to be his "Mr. Biggs," the steady presence who matches his charm, guides his enthusiasm, and takes him on all the best adventures the city has to offer. With the right home, this boy is ready for his happily ever after.

Fun Fact
Biggs is the kind of dog who believes every walk should come with a little drama, a lot of heart, and maybe a snack break on a park bench.

234744.name: Lulu
234744.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Lulu is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In her previous home, Lulu was reported to leash bite, become mouthy, and lunge and hard bark at certain individuals. In the Care Centers, Lulu has shown behavioral deterioration despite receiving daily enrichment. She is noted to be highly anxious, frequently ping-ponging off her kennel walls and barking excessively. In the pens and training room, Lulu is social with staff and receptive to treats. Medically, Lulu is apparently healthy.	

Meet Lulu!
Lulu was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and she is now hoping for a fresh start with someone who understands her big personality, big feelings, and big heart. She's social, playful, and full of energy, with a clear love for people and engagement.

My Ideal Home
Lulu would do best with a patient, experienced adopter who can help her work through anxiety, build confidence, and provide structure. She benefits from a calm, predictable environment, consistent routines, and reward-based training. Enrichment like sniffy walks, chew toys, and mental games will help her channel her energy in positive ways.

Good with Other Pets?
Lulu has shown mixed signals around other dogs, including both interest and uncertainty. Because of this, slow and careful introductions are recommended, and she may do best as the only pet or with structured introductions to compatible dogs. She is not recommended for dog parks.

Good with Kids?
Due to her anxiety, mouthiness, and occasional conflict around handling, Lulu would do best in a home without young children.

Things to Know
Lulu is an active, affectionate girl who can be both enthusiastic and sensitive. She may become anxious or vocal in new situations and benefits from slow introductions and positive reinforcement. She has some house soiling and leash challenges that will improve with consistency and routine. She loves car rides, toys, water play, and spending time with people she trusts. With patience, Lulu's loving and playful personality really shines through.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Lulu is a girl that quickly steals my heart. We met her about a month or so ago for the first time. She had been high energy and a little unsure of her surroundings. Since then, she had been adopted and returned, went to adoption events, and became a volunteer favorite. In the yard, Lulu easily leans into pets, even getting a bit of belly rubs in! Lulu came to us for the first time last year when her owner was arrested. She was quickly reclaimed by her family. This year, when her family was moving out of state, Lulu was surrendered with the hopes of finding a new family for her. Lulu has been stressed at the shelter, as many dogs are. She is high energy, but seeks comfort in people. She can be conflicted with getting pet - she leans in but sometimes jumps away. Lulu does not like going back into her kennel, and often lays down when approaching her room. Our volunteers have accompanied her to events, and they said Lulu was "beyond perfect." Lulu was adopted, but returned when her adopter was uncomfortable with Lulu's mouthy behavior. Lulu is described as social, active, and playful. She loves car rides, braided toys, and cuddling. She had been crate trained for up to 5 hours, loves water and bath times, and had been playful with familiar and unfamiliar dogs.

234762.name: Casentino
234762.summary:
Meet Casentino!
Casentino is the longest stay dog at Queens ACC and a truly special boy who has already come so far. He was found as a stray and arrived very overwhelmed and stressed, but with time, care, and consistency he has slowly started to show his  brighter personality. His adoption fee has been sponsored, and he is more than ready for a patient home to help him continue his journey. Bushwick Bark has generously donated a goodie bag of treats and toys to get him started in his new home! Come to Queens to meet him and help him explore his gifts!

Personality
Casentino is a thoughtful, sensitive dog who does best when given time and space to feel comfortable. In the past, he struggled with stress and found it hard to focus, but now he is showing steady progress and a growing sense of confidence. He is beginning to reveal a more relaxed, affectionate side, especially with people he trusts.

When he feels safe, Casentino enjoys gentle attention and even gets wiggly with soft voices and familiar people. He knows "sit," enjoys treats, and is starting to show interest in toys, which is a big milestone for him. He still prefers affection on his own terms, but with patience he continues to open up more and more.

Out and About
Casentino walks better and more calmly than when he first arrived. He is able to stay engaged with his handler. He does not focus on other dogs on walks and generally moves through the environment without fixation, especially when supported with structure and reassurance.

He is also part of the Shelter Scholars program, where he is actively working on staying focused during walks and building confidence around distractions using positive reinforcement. He is making big progress!

Social Behavior
Casentino is learning to trust and relax in new environments. In his kennel, he now shows a soft, wiggly greeting style, often stretching and approaching with a loose body and wagging tail. br />


Home Life
Casentino will thrive in an adult only home that can offer patience, structure, and time to continue building his confidence. He has made incredible progress in a shelter environment, and there is strong potential for him to blossom even more once he is in a stable home setting.

Things to Know
Casentino is housebroken, enjoys quiet rest periods, and is continuing to grow in comfort with handling and daily routines. A volunteer describes how he has gone from highly stressed to much more settled, now able to relax, enjoy treats, and engage in simple enrichment. He will benefit greatly from continued positive reinforcement training and a patient adopter who understands sensitive dogs.

Fun Fact
Casentino is a perfect example of a dog who just needs time to shine. From a stressed stray to a pup who now stretches, wags, and leans into gentle affection, he's quietly writing his own comeback story and is ready for someone to help him finish it. 🐾

My foster writes: Don't let his appearance fool you, this guy is a sweetheart. When he isn't curled up on his bed, he loves a good game of tug of war or rolling around on his back getting pets. Casentino has been the best foster dog. He is perfectly house trained, doesn't beg for food, and has no destructive behaviors. He does get a little over excited sometimes around new people or other animals, but is very food motivated and will do great with a little patience and TLC.
234762.summaryHtml:
Meet Casentino!
Casentino is the longest stay dog at Queens ACC and a truly special boy who has already come so far. He was found as a stray and arrived very overwhelmed and stressed, but with time, care, and consistency he has slowly started to show his brighter personality. His adoption fee has been sponsored, and he is more than ready for a patient home to help him continue his journey. Bushwick Bark has generously donated a goodie bag of treats and toys to get him started in his new home! Come to Queens to meet him and help him explore his gifts!

Personality
Casentino is a thoughtful, sensitive dog who does best when given time and space to feel comfortable. In the past, he struggled with stress and found it hard to focus, but now he is showing steady progress and a growing sense of confidence. He is beginning to reveal a more relaxed, affectionate side, especially with people he trusts.

When he feels safe, Casentino enjoys gentle attention and even gets wiggly with soft voices and familiar people. He knows "sit," enjoys treats, and is starting to show interest in toys, which is a big milestone for him. He still prefers affection on his own terms, but with patience he continues to open up more and more.

Out and About
Casentino walks better and more calmly than when he first arrived. He is able to stay engaged with his handler. He does not focus on other dogs on walks and generally moves through the environment without fixation, especially when supported with structure and reassurance.

He is also part of the Shelter Scholars program, where he is actively working on staying focused during walks and building confidence around distractions using positive reinforcement. He is making big progress!

Social Behavior
Casentino is learning to trust and relax in new environments. In his kennel, he now shows a soft, wiggly greeting style, often stretching and approaching with a loose body and wagging tail. br />
Home Life
Casentino will thrive in an adult only home that can offer patience, structure, and time to continue building his confidence. He has made incredible progress in a shelter environment, and there is strong potential for him to blossom even more once he is in a stable home setting.

Things to Know
Casentino is housebroken, enjoys quiet rest periods, and is continuing to grow in comfort with handling and daily routines. A volunteer describes how he has gone from highly stressed to much more settled, now able to relax, enjoy treats, and engage in simple enrichment. He will benefit greatly from continued positive reinforcement training and a patient adopter who understands sensitive dogs.

Fun Fact
Casentino is a perfect example of a dog who just needs time to shine. From a stressed stray to a pup who now stretches, wags, and leans into gentle affection, he's quietly writing his own comeback story and is ready for someone to help him finish it. 🐾

234827.name: Pear
234827.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Pear is on the at risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers. Medically Pear is apparently healthy.

Meet Pear!
Pear has had quite the journey. After originally arriving as a stray, he found himself back in our care after spending time surviving outdoors on his own. While all of these changes have left him feeling understandably unsure, Pear has been steadily gaining confidence with the help of patient staff. Beneath his shy exterior is a gentle cat who is beginning to realize that people can be trusted again.

My Ideal Home
Pear is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with experienced cat guardians who will give him the time and space he needs to adjust. He'll appreciate a calm environment, cozy hiding spots, and adopters who let him take the lead when it comes to interaction. With patience, routine, and plenty of tasty treats, Pear is likely to continue blossoming into a wonderful companion.

Good with Kids?
Adult-only home. Pear is a sensitive cat who needs a calm environment where he can build confidence at his own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
There is no known history of Pear living with other cats or dogs. Slow, gradual introductions would be recommended if resident pets are present.

Overall Health
Pear has been treated for Giardia. Our staff can discuss any follow-up care or recommendations with his adopter.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Experienced Adopters. Pear has shown fearful behavior in the shelter but has made encouraging progress over time. While he initially became overwhelmed by touch, he has gradually learned to accept gentle interactions without escalating. He will do best with adopters who understand feline body language, respect his boundaries, and allow him to continue building trust at his own pace in a quiet home.

Other Fun Facts
Pear has a soft spot for squeeze-up treats! They have helped him build positive associations with people, and he'll happily come forward for a tasty snack. Staff have loved watching him grow more curious and confident, from cautiously peeking out of his hidey box to gently taking treats from their hands. Every small victory has shown just how much potential this sweet boy has once he feels safe.

A volunteer writes: Before we get into everything that happened before, I'd like to please focus on the absolutely charming little cat Pear is now with the caveat that he has no interest in being charming right now. Pear seems to be on a mission to explain that he doesn't love the shelter even if there are some things here that he really does love, which are toys that can be left for him in his beloved box (which, coincidentally, is another thing he loves here). Pear so adorably did not want to play with me, even though I really tried and he didn't even want me to watch him play, which is ok too but also unintentionally very cute. Most recently, Pear walked into someone's backyard and he was pretty happy to be noticed. Though I'm sure he'd say otherwise right now, Pear would love to be noticed once again.

234865.name: Chase
234865.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Chase is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Chase a high level of kennel stress behaviors including repeatedly launching to the top of his kennel, springing off kennel walls, persistent jumping, heavy panting, and pulling so intensely on walks that he vomited multiple times. He has also shown fixation toward birds and small dogs while outside. Chase is social and affectionate with staff and volunteers, but struggling to acclimate. Medically, Chase is slightly underweight.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

235075.name: Fizz
235075.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Fizz is both a great speed walking companion and a snuggly couch potato! He loves giving kisses and cuddling with you in bed at night. Fizz is sweet and endearing, and so patient while you prepare his food! Fizz is very food/treat motivated. Fizz loves having plenty of options to get comfy and lounge around in - chairs, couches, beds. And to top it off, he loves to sleep in!

My foster writes: Fizz is a VERY physical, athletic guy and super devoted LOVEBUG at 1+ year old! He is by nature a extremely happy fellow and the true definition of JOY! Adores high-energy activities like flying zoomies and retrieving his stuffed animals and anything else he can carry... but chills out well on the sofa with you, preferably with his head in your lap. Will absolutely make you laugh! Has an infectious smile and bubbliness, adores people and children of all ages (doesn't even bat an eye at screaming kids on skateboards). Still dog-reactive but has made amazing improvement in this area.

235429.name: Max
235429.summary:
My foster writes: Max is a young, energetic bundle of joy who might start off a little skittish but will quickly learn to trust and hop up to you for attention, head scratches, and treats. She shows off her impressive zoomies and binkies whenever she can and will make sure to find the coziest spot around to lounge after all her exercise. Her litter box skills aren't perfect yet, but with a bit more time and training, she will surely get the hang of it. Max will be most comfortable in a quiet space where she can comfortable and will get lots of attention and love.

A Volunteer writes: Max is an absolute love. She happily snuggles during floor time, enjoying pets quietly and calmly. One volunteer spent over half an hour petting Max, and Max never moved away. She is a sweet-natured, gentle rabbit who seems to love gentle human affection.

235650.name: Apollo
235650.summary:
Meet Apollo!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Apollo came to us as a stray and is full of energy and curiosity! He loves attention on his own terms and is eager to explore new environments. He is playful and wiggly, enjoys treats and pets, and responds well to positive interactions. Apollo is ready to learn, but he needs a patient adopter who can work with him on manners and training.

Apollo is a strong and spirited dog participating in our Shelter Scholars program, where he's developing calmer leash skills and practicing thoughtful responses to triggers. With consistent redirection and focus-building exercises, Apollo is learning that walks can be structured, predictable, and successful. His determination is fueling real progress.

My Ideal Home
Apollo would do best in a calm, adult-only home with an adopter experienced with dogs who require structure and guidance. He needs daily physical and mental enrichment, including long walks, food puzzles, and games. Slow introductions to new people and places will help him feel safe and confident.

Good with Other Pets?
Apollo can be selective around other dogs. In shelter observations, he showed tension and reactivity during interactions with some dogs. No history with cats is known.

Leash Manners
Apollo is a strong puller and needs consistent training to improve loose-leash walking. He responds well to structured walks, positive reinforcement, and proper equipment like a front-clip harness or head halter. Short, frequent walks and training sessions are recommended to help manage his energy and strength.

Overall Health
Healthy overall.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - New Hope/Experienced Adopters. Apollo is energetic and social but has challenges with impulse control, handling sensitivity, and leash manners. He needs a patient adopter willing to provide guidance, enrichment, and structure.

Other Fun Facts
Apollo loves toys, treats, and attention on his own terms. He is playful, curious, and enjoys learning new skills. He thrives when he can explore, play, and engage with his humans, rewarding patience and consistency with loyalty and affection.

235795.name: Brittany
235795.summary:
My foster writes: Hi! This is Brittany, a very sweet cat who loves getting attention and having a nice soft blanket to lay on. She also loves being able to burry into blankets. She's quick to warm up to new people and situations and loves playing with whatever cat toys are provided to her. She's definitely a quiet cat but every one of her little meow chirps are just too adorable. She of course loves getting her food and will be following your every step whenever she deems it to be meal time! Sadly, not as often as she would hope but it does earn her lots of affection.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

A volunteer writes: Brittany was brought to us when her owner had too many cats and gave Brittany to us to care for her. Our sweet tiger is about 4 years old and my interaction with her was very gentle and sweet. It is reported in her last home she was playful with a good amount of energy and at times may play a bit rough. As she begins to get more comfortable we hope her personality begins to shine a bit more and we can indulge in some play time! For now, she enjoys taking things at her own pace, relaxing in her penthouse top kennel suite, eating treats, getting pet, and napping.

236019.name: Serge
236019.summary:
My foster writes: Serge, or Mr.Cookie is a sweet, shy and observant kitty! He loves to play and roll around on carpets. He will never turn down a tube treat or a minnow and wants to hang out and watch what you are doing. Serge loves having his own safe space and will hide when he is overwhelmed but always comes back out when he's ready. Anyone would be lucky to have Mr. Cookie in their home!

My foster writes: Serge has been lovingly nicknamed Cookie! Cookie is getting braver ever day and getting used to being around people. He still hides when anyone approaches him and does not tolerate being touched but he loves to watch you! Cookie loves his tube treats and is starting to be more playful at night! He needs someone who is patient and will give him lots of space and time to come to you.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

236413.name: Sage
236413.summary:
My foster writes: My name is Sage. I'm a sweet and occasionally energetic, lovely little girl. I know my name and will come when called out. I also know "no" and its many variations, though the only time I am told no is when when nails accidentally stick to the couch when I am trying to secure a close spot next to my person. It's not my fault and as soon as I'm reminded, I become very soft and gentle. I am curious about my surroundings and my foster tells the shelter I am a very quick adaptor. I'm good with the other foster cat in my home and I've been slowly introduced to a large dog and have shown no signs of aggression. If you go slow, I will warm up to you extremely quickly. I love all kinds of pets-head scratches, soft strokes, nose kisses, and I will even let you pick me up without any protest.
There's a good chance I might think I'm part dog, as my tail wags constantly, and I chirp softly to let you know I would like some attention please (though I'm not pushy, if you need your space to get some work done, I'll understand, and keep my distance waiting patiently for some love). I occasionalllllllyyyyyy snore in my sleep but I'm told it's veryyyy quietly. And I LOVE the chicken squeeze tubes that my foster gives me.
THE PROS:
-gentle
-easy going
-quiet except for purrs and soft chirps
-knows my name, will come when called and understands gentle "nos"
-once I'm comfortable (which doesn't take long) I will love the hell out of you
-good with strangers, cats, and dog curious and no signs of dog reactivity
-playful but not destructive
-stunning green eyes, a beautiful and soft coat, and an overall really beautiful girl (so I'm told)
-extremely well behaved and looking to love you for you
-my foster is really going to miss me, she says I'm the best girl
THE CONS:
I shed a little, but will let you brush me softly to help mitigate. And honestly what's a home without the occasional tuft of fur to remind you someone is there who loves you.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Sage was lying in her litter box, alert with ears forward and average eyes, and gave a little hiss when first approached, but this then converted into some gentle meowing, and she sniffed treats. She then allowed petting on her head, cheek, and along her back while remaining calm. She sniffed Squeeze Up and then began eating it. She allowed more petting while eating the Squeeze Up and remained calm and sweet.

Sage interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

THE PROS: -gentle -easy going -quiet except for purrs and soft chirps -knows my name, will come when called and understands gentle "nos" -once I'm comfortable (which doesn't take long) I will love the hell out of you -good with strangers, cats, and dog curious and no signs of dog reactivity -playful but not destructive -stunning green eyes, a beautiful and soft coat, and an overall really beautiful girl (so I'm told) -extremely well behaved and looking to love you for you -my foster is really going to miss me, she says I'm the best girl THE CONS: I shed a little, but will let you brush me softly to help mitigate. And honestly what's a home without the occasional tuft of fur to remind you someone is there who loves you.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

I have lived with cats in my previous home.

Sage was lying in her litter box, alert with ears forward and average eyes, and gave a little hiss when first approached, but this then converted into some gentle meowing, and she sniffed treats. She then allowed petting on her head, cheek, and along her back while remaining calm. She sniffed Squeeze Up and then began eating it. She allowed more petting while eating the Squeeze Up and remained calm and sweet.

Sage interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

236486.summary: A Volunteer writes: Binklesworth is a volunteer favorite. She is friendly and outgoing, and clearly loves interacting with everyone who stops by her space. Binklesworth loves being petted and talked to, and she snuggles in whenever humans give her attention. She happily binkies and hops around during floor time. She has a "Golden Retriever" personality, which makes her especially lovable.

236597.name: Missy
236597.summary:
My foster writes: Missy is a beautiful, calm, independent tortie girl. She loves lickable treats! After a little bonding, she'll let me scratch her cheek if I have one of these in hand.  She recently had some teeth pulled (everyone at the vet said she was an angel)  so wet food and treats for the future. She has been doing her own thing while in foster but, with time, I'm sure she'll be seeking out attention.  I imagine she would do best in a home with another friendly cat, as she seems to meow looking for friends. She tolerates a calm dog, one that wouldn't be interested in playing with her.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

236732.name: Fara
236732.summary:
My Borough Breaker writes:
Walked through two different types of park, took her to the dog store and she was the most happy smelling all the treats, had brunch with her and she was able to decompress and sat with her and gave all the rubs and love. I notice when walking her and came across another dog she wanted to come up and play with them. At the park she came across another dog, and you can tell that she was happy the way she had the zoomies and body language. Also loves to rub her cute self on the ground while is very wholesome to watch

Meet Fara!
Fara was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and she's now looking for a home where she can feel secure, loved, and part of the family again. She is a very affectionate girl who truly enjoys being near her people and staying involved in whatever is happening around her. She already knows cues like sit, stay, and down, and is especially motivated by tasty treats like salmon.

My Ideal Home
Fara would do best with a patient adopter who can give her time to settle in and feel comfortable in new environments. She thrives in a home that offers structure, gentle guidance, and calm introductions to new people and situations. Because she can become overwhelmed in busy or overstimulating settings, a more relaxed home environment will help her shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Fara has lived with other dogs before and can enjoy canine company, though she can get overstimulated in group settings and may need help with space and boundaries. With thoughtful management and slow introductions, she may do best with compatible dog friends or as the only dog depending on the home.

Good with Kids?
Fara is recommended for a home without young children under 5 due to her sensitivity, anxiety, and need for a calm environment.

Things to Know
Fara is a gentle, people-focused dog who loves being close to her humans and prefers spending time in shared spaces like the living room. She walks nicely on leash, enjoys car rides, and is comfortable with bathing and basic handling. While she can become anxious or overstimulated at times, she responds well to calm redirection and benefits from a steady routine.

Fun Fact
Fara is the kind of dog who just wants to be your shadow in the sweetest way, happiest when she's included and part of your everyday life.

A volunteer writes: Last weekend I met Fara for the second time since she arrived a month ago. Weeks living in a small crate in an overflow room would get to any of us, and Fara is 65lbs - too big to be so confined. So I gave her as long a break as I could. We started with a walk to let her stretch her legs, and then settled in the yard. She zoomed some stress out, each time settling back at my feet. I pet her big head and she rolled dramatically away, only to return and show me her trick again. The third time she returned she dropped her torso and head against my legs, butt in the air and panted while I loved on her. I loved it.

Fara's guardian surrendered her saying she was overstimulated around too many other dogs (they had several). The shelter has noted hind limb stiffness and perhaps a torn CCL, which may contribute to her discomfort and zoomies. Her guardian also said that she loves attention and affection and being involved with everything that's going on.

Fara is ready to get all that attention and affection back, in a new home.

237110.name: One Bunzy
237110.summary:
Meet Bunzy!
One Bunzy is a 3-year-old long stay pup who came in as a stray and is now waiting patiently for her chance at a forever home. She is a longstay and her adoption fee has been reduced!

Personality
One Bunzy is a sweet, friendly, and affectionate girl who truly enjoys being close to people. Her foster describes her as calm, loving, and very people oriented, often happily resting her head on your lap for attention and cuddles. She is gentle in her interactions and seems to enjoy forming quiet, steady bonds with those she trusts.

She is also smart and eager to please, with a natural willingness to learn. Her foster notes she seems easy to train and responsive to positive attention, especially when she feels safe and included.

Out and About
One Bunzy is an easy leash walker with no pulling and no reactivity toward people or other dogs. She moves calmly through her environment and tends to stay close to her handler. She enjoys steady, relaxed walks and benefits from continued positive experiences outside the home.

Social Behavior
In the shelter, One Bunzy is highly social and approaches handlers readily with a soft body and gentle wagging tail. She accepts both soft and more active handling and remains neutral and relaxed during interaction. She enjoys being near people and shows a calm, steady interest in connection.

In a dog interaction on 09/23/25, One Bunzy showed a soft body and wagging tail but chose not to approach the gate, suggesting a polite and observational style when meeting other dogs.

Home Life
One Bunzy will thrive in a home that can offer love, consistency, and gentle structure. She enjoys being part of daily life, whether that means going for walks or simply relaxing at home beside her person. She will benefit from positive outlets for her energy, such as toys and enrichment activities, even though she is not highly toy motivated right now. Bunzy is a Level 1 dog, meaning she is suitable for the majority of households.

Things to Know
One Bunzy has medical needs that staff will discuss with adopters. She enjoys social interaction, but her history with other animals and children is unknown, so slow introductions will be important. 

Fun Fact
One Bunzy is kind of dog who doesn't ask for much, just a little love, a soft place to rest her head, and someone to walk through life with by her side. 🐾

My foster writes: If you are looking for a loyal, people-loving shadow, meet Bunzy! She is an incredibly sweet, even-tempered girl who absolutely adores human company. Bunzy is the ultimate "velcro puppy"her favorite place in the world is right next to you (or literally on you!). Whether she's squeezing herself into your office chair to "help" you work, or adjusting her sleeping position at night to make sure her body is glued right next to your head, Bunzy just wants to be close.
Not only is she a total sweetheart, but she's also a dream to train! Bunzy is highly food-driven and incredibly eager to please, making her a star student who loves following commands. With just a little bit of basic puppy training, this well-balanced girl is ready to become an absolute angel in her forever home. She's ready to fill your life with chin rests, cuddles, and endless love!

237198.name: Juniper
237198.summary:
My foster writes: If you want a cat that keeps a polite distance, doesn't rub fur on your clothes or try to climb on your bed or lap, but gently witnesses you with a warm presence and imbues your day to day with a magical quality, Juniper is the one. She is polite, tidy, and moves respectfully out of the way with a chirp. Any time there is a string waved her way she will engage enthusiastically, playing is a sure way to bond with her and stave off any built up anxiety. If you speak to her lovingly, she will roll around on the carpet and mew back, stretch her little paws towards you as if she knows you're speaking love to her. She loves calm and silence, that is the environment where her true powers can come to be. If you have a home that is all about peacefulness, she will fit right in. 
She doesn't love to be pet or snuggled but she will give you a chin bump by her own initiative. She will check on you and sit by your side in a protective stance as you do your work. She has been a gem to us and has made our home warmer and cuter than we ever expected. 


What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

237461.name: Logan
237461.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Logan!
Logan came to us as an owner surrender. He is very sweet and friendly, initially hyperactive but quickly settles into a calm and affectionate demeanor. He enjoys attention and handles being examined or brushed well, making him a gentle companion for the right home.

My Ideal Home
Logan would thrive in a home with only adults. He benefits from a calm, structured environment where his anxiety and resource guarding can be managed. Consistent routines, positive reinforcement, and patience with his leash manners will help him succeed.

Good with Kids?
No - He is recommended for adult-only homes due to sensitivity, resource guarding, and general anxiety.

Good with Other Pets?
Dogs: Friendly with familiar dogs, tolerant of unfamiliar dogs, but may not pick up on social cues and can be sexually motivated around some dogs. Introductions should be carefully managed.
Cats: Unknown.

Leash Manners
Logan pulls hard on the leash and may react to other dogs and strangers. He will need consistent, reward-based training to improve loose-leash walking and manage on-leash reactivity.

Overall Health
Healthy overall, recovering from minor skin irritation and dental concerns (gingival mass observed).

Behavior Determination
Level 3 / Experienced Adopters - Logan requires an adult-only home and adopters who can manage resource guarding, leash pulling, anxiety, and on-leash reactivity with structured training.

Other Fun Facts
Logan is playful, energetic, and affectionate once comfortable. He loves treats, interactive play, and being petted on his own terms. He tolerates handling well and enjoys walks, though he may alert bark at strangers or other dogs. He responds best to a calm, consistent approach and rewards-based training.

237718.name: Elma
237718.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Elma is a loving, cuddle bug, with a ton of strength and energy for frequent playimes. She loves any adventure, whether it's a walk around the block, a few hours in the park or a car ride, she's always interested and curious about everything. She also loves a good rest and cuddle. So you might find her sprawled out across your lap snoring away while binge watching your favorite TV show or YouTube series.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

A Volunteer Wrote: We could learn so much from the resilience of dogs. Take our beloved Elma, who arrived at the shelter absolutely terrified by whatever awful things has happened to her before she got here. But within days, the volunteers were chattering: "She's so endlessly loving!" "What an energetic, sweet girl!" And "what a fun, exuberant, affectionate girl!" Elma also adores treats and she's been learning to sit in return for them...we were thinking maybe you could take over the training from here on out? You'd be in for such a treat yourself!
