237833.name: Mickey
237833.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Mickey! He's a gentle, kind, unbothered little guy. He likes to do his own thing most of the time, but will come out to question what on earth just happened if you drop something in the kitchen, or if you come to him with snacks. His heart is in his stomach, and he will eat treats right out of your hands. He's a lover of ear scritches, and if you hit just the right spot, he'll lean in. During the day, Mickey just wants a cozy place to hang out and snooze. In the evening, his playful and curious side comes out, and he loves to chase a spring toy, ball or a string. Mickey is a discerning little guy, and will make you work for his love, but is incredibly kind and is so rewarding when he accepts you as his.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
 A volunteer writes:
 Mickey, Mickey, he's so fine.
 His history is mostly a mystery. In the shelter, he is quiet and shy,
spending most of his free time in his cozy den. He calmly accepts petting, and likes to be approached slowly. He is also a very handsome- looking guy. He is waiting patiently to meet you at our Queens center.

237849.name: Peppina
237849.summary:
My foster writes: Peppina is a gentle, wide-eyed kitty who enjoys the simple things in life: yummy treats, cozy naps, and watching the world go by from a safe window perch. At night, she loves to sit by the window and quietly observe cars and people passing.
While she may be shy at first, Peppina's curiosity shines through. Once she feels comfortable, she'll sit nearby to keep you company, especially if she knows a Churu stick treat is available. She always devours them as an evening treat! She also adores curling up in her homemade cave or hiding in cozy boxes around the house.
Peppina would thrive in a calm, patient, adult home where routines are gentle and predictable. She came from a multi-cat household, so she may enjoy having another friendly feline around, though she's still figuring out what she prefers. Left on her own, she spends her days exploring, playing with toys, and snoozing peacefully on the couch.
If you're looking for a tender, curious kitty who will blossom with time, kindness, and quiet companionship, Peppina might be the perfect match. She will likely be shy during the initial meetup, but will warm up!

What my friends at ACC say about me:

Peppina was in the den, appearing slightly stressed with fairly large pupils and a watchful stare. She was slightly hand-shy, but allowed petting on her cheek and head after pulling back slightly. 237849.summaryHtml:
My foster writes: Peppina is a gentle, wide-eyed kitty who enjoys the simple things in life: yummy treats, cozy naps, and watching the world go by from a safe window perch. At night, she loves to sit by the window and quietly observe cars and people passing. While she may be shy at first, Peppina's curiosity shines through. Once she feels comfortable, she'll sit nearby to keep you company, especially if she knows a Churu stick treat is available. She always devours them as an evening treat! She also adores curling up in her homemade cave or hiding in cozy boxes around the house. Peppina would thrive in a calm, patient, adult home where routines are gentle and predictable. She came from a multi-cat household, so she may enjoy having another friendly feline around, though she's still figuring out what she prefers. Left on her own, she spends her days exploring, playing with toys, and snoozing peacefully on the couch. If you're looking for a tender, curious kitty who will blossom with time, kindness, and quiet companionship, Peppina might be the perfect match. She will likely be shy during the initial meetup, but will warm up!

238134.name: Hop Scotch
238134.summary:
Meet Hop Scotch!
Hop Scotch is a born-and-raised ACC bunny currently living it up in foster care - which means his foster family knows him better than anyone. Here's what they have to say:


"Cutest friendliest bunny who would win your heart by his playful tricks - peekaboo, grab the string, stand up on two feet, spin, circle you to show his love if you sit at his level, binkies. Amazing with children and adults and responds so well to your love."

My Ideal Home
Hop Scotch is friendly, interactive, and people-oriented - he'll do well in a wide range of homes. His foster confirms he's great with both children and adults, making him one of the more versatile rabbit placements we have. He needs the usual rabbit essentials: unlimited timothy hay, fresh greens, space to roam, and enrichment to keep that busy brain occupied.

Handling & Socialization
This bun has tricks. Peekaboo, spinning, standing on two feet, circling his people - Hop Scotch is engaged, curious, and genuinely interactive in a way that surprises people who think of rabbits as hands-off pets. He responds enthusiastically to attention and affection.

Good with Kids?
Yes - his foster specifically notes he is amazing with children. Still recommend teaching kids gentle handling, but this is a rabbit who can genuinely thrive in a family home.

Good with Other Pets? Unknown beyond his shelter siblings. Homes with dogs or cats need a solid plan for safe, permanent separation.

Overall Health
Hop Scotch is in great shape - healthy since birth, with clean exams throughout his time at ACC. He was neutered in February and recovered uneventfully. He is fully up to date on care and ready to go home.

Behavior Determination
General Adoption. Hop Scotch is neutered, healthy, people-loving, and foster-tested with kids. He is about as adoption-ready as a rabbit gets.

238137.name: Twixiehop
238137.summary: My foster writes: Twixihop (white ears) and Bunny Bear (grey ears) are an adorable bonded pair of sisters. They might act skittish at first, but are excellent explorers. They enjoy playing with toys, especially when they include hay and treats. They are well on their way to being fully litterbox trained, but might leave some droppings to mark their space. They are very social with each other and once they trust their human, enjoy head scratches galore. Make sure you have both hands free as thy like to cuddle up together and get scratches together. The pair will make an excellent addition to a household that can give them plenty of space and attention. In return, they will be a wonderfully adorable addition to their forever home.

I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

238477.name: Nubi
238477.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Meet Nubi: The Left-Turning Legend! 💃
This smart cookie knows a bunch of commands and is a master of the spin-as long as we're going counter-clockwise. She's a "lefties only" dancer who's still figuring out the right side, but she makes up for it with 10/10 enthusiasm!
When she's not showing off her moves for a treat (she's very food motivated!), you can find her winning a game of tug or burrowing into your lap. Nubi is a world-class snuggle bug who would fit perfectly into just about any home.

My foster writes: Nubi (or Nubby as I call her) is a sweet gem of a dog. She is quick to trust her person and full of love and kisses for them. She is fully potty trained and is well behaved in the apartment. She has a favorite blanket and a favorite spot on the couch that I have had to fully surrender to her. Nubby loves to play with her stuffies, she loves to shake them into submission, and enjoys our training sessions, showing that she is quick to learn. Nubby is working on her leash skills and she needs someone who is willing to go slowly with her and help her to build her confidence in new situations and when outside.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A Volunteer Wrote: We love, love, love this dog with all of our hearts. So many of us have praised her sweetness (she offers kisses even through the bars of her pop up crate), her adoration of scratches when she leans into you, and her gratitude at being given treats.  Her former owner reports she's lived with kids, is fine with other dogs, and loves to play. We hate that she's not getting a chance to do that in an overcrowded shelter when she should be playing tug of war (her favorite) or sleeping on a couch. This is a girl with so much love to offer, and it's a privilege to do for such a gentle soul. Please come meet her!

238738.name: Buns
238738.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

Meet Buns!

What she lacks in a tail she makes up for in personality! Buns is a gorgeous calico who seems like she's got a tough exterior but, once you've gained her trust, is really a huge mush. Her previous owner mentioned that she is a friendly, talkative, lap cat and that she loves being where the people are, playing with toys, and is the ultimate alarm clock, gently tapping you with her paws and letting you know that it's breakfast time while you're snoozing the day away. She's not a fan of other cats but wouldn't mind a small canine sibling. What she'd really love, though, is to curl up in your lap and get tons of chin scratches. Come say hi to Buns at SIACC!

238855.name: Kriss
238855.summary:
My foster writes: Kriss is ready for the Olympics: although she took a while to warm up, once she did, she vaulted over our baby gate and never looked back. A champion jumper, Kriss is a beautiful gray kitty with buff undertones and green eyes. Although she is initially shy and needs time to get to know you, once she comes out of her shell she is ready to roam and play! Kriss also enjoys pets and being near her people. Her purr motor is always running. She loves to collect and arrange her soft toys on her bed, explore, and scratch cardboard and she is curious about her foster cat siblings.

Kriss has made incredible progress in her time with us. After spending her first three weeks cowering under our couch, she is now the queen of the castle (or apartment)--following us everywhere, giving us heat bunts and purring, batting around her toys, and engaging in her favorite pastime: chewing on cardboard boxes (she will help you with your recycling goals!) Once extremely skittish, she now allows us to pick her up and cuddle her. Kriss does need a cat-competent family as she sometimes gets a bit exuberant with her love bites (though never too hard) and her paws. She loves all toys and other cats and would likely benefit from another energetic cat in the household who likes to play. She is a character who will bring a smile to your face every day.

My foster writes: Kriss is an adorable cat who loves independent play time and lots of pets once she gets to know you. She loves to curl up on the bed and watch the world go by perched on the windowsill

My foster writes: Kriss is an adorable, shy cat who might need some time to warm up to you, but its the best feeling when she does! Enjoy watching her play with her favorite ball + fish toys and perch up on your windowsill

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

238868.name: Marsala
238868.summary:
My foster writes: Meows of love from me Marsala! If a low maintenance, mellow, sweet, chill kitty companion is what you seek -then I'm your boy!! Your gentle pets and chin and head scratches make me happy. Listening to your sweet soft voice talking to me and singing to me relaxes me and strengthens our bond and connection. Will you be my new mommy, daddy or both? Will you bring me home and give me the chance to be your favorite little fur family member? Meows of loving thanks!!

"Meet Marsala, a distinguished 6-year-old grey gentleman whose striking green eyes tell a story of recent change. Along with his companion Marmalade, Marsala came to us after losing his beloved owner, facing a whole new chapter in life. His soft grey coat and expressive face hint at his gentle nature, though he's still finding his footing in his temporary home.
In our care, Marsala has shown himself to be incredibly gentle, if reserved. While he accepts affection with perfect manners, he's still processing his new surroundings - like many cats who've known only one home, big changes take time to adjust to. During his stay in our community room, we witnessed a touching moment when he chose to stay close to a female cat, finding comfort in her presence. This sweet interaction showed us that beneath his careful exterior lies a social soul.
Though Marsala may seem a bit 'frozen' at first, he never shows an ounce of aggression - just the careful consideration of a cat who needs time to warm up. His civil nature with other cats and gentle acceptance of human attention suggest that, with patience and understanding, this handsome boy will blossom in a loving home.
Looking for a gentle soul to cherish? Come meet Marsala - sometimes the quietest hearts have the most love to give.

"What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Marsala tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

239243.name: Sal
239243.summary:
Sal is a sweet, independent rabbit with a gentle personality and a playful side. Having come from an active household with children, Sal is already familiar with the sounds and routines of daily family life. He's a well-socialized companion who enjoys being part of a home environment, looking for his fur-ever home!

Having also lived with other rabbits in the past and already being altered, Sal may do well with another bunny friend after proper introductions.

Sal has experience living both indoors and outdoors when the weather is seasonally appropriate, and he adapts well as long as he has a safe, comfortable space to relax. He loves tasty treats like dark leafy greens, snap peas, and blueberries.

While Sal enjoys affection, he prefers attention on his own terms. He loves being pet and cuddled when he's in the mood, but he also appreciates having time to himself to play, explore, or simply rest quietly nearby. His balanced personality makes him a wonderful match for a family or individual who understands and respects rabbit behavior.

If you're ready for a sweet companion to hop into your life, come to SIACC to meet Sal today!

239246.name: Chubs
239246.summary:
Meet Chubs!

Chubs is a young, active rabbit ready to hop into your heart, and possibly even your lap! He previously lived with adults, children, and other rabbits and was described as friendly and playful with all residents in the previous home. This energizer bunny needs lots of activity so make sure to give him plenty of opportunity to play. He is used to living indoors but having frequent adventures outside (in an appropriately secured enclosure) and is said to have loved running around with his brother Junior and snacking on timothy hay.

In the Care Center, his favorite activities are hopping into people's laps for attention, minding the other rabbits' business, redecorating his kennel, and enjoying a wide variety of veggies like cilantro. He especially enjoys having his picture taken, and will shove his nose right into the camera lens.

If you're interested in adding Chubs to your family, reach out to SIACC to learn more about the rabbit adoption process!

239414.name: Cider
239414.summary:
My foster writes: 
Meet Cider: Part-Time Window Watcher, Full-Time Newspaper Editor!
Are you looking for a calm, sophisticated companion with just a touch of "artist" in him? Meet Cider! This handsome fellow has been perfecting his craft in his foster home for a month now and is ready to find his forever workspace.
Cider is a quiet soul who appreciates the finer things in life: watching "Bird TV" through the window, napping in the quiet comfort of a closet, and "helping" you read the news by occasionally shredding the edges of your newspaper. He's a polite roommate who waits patiently for his meals and stays quiet through the night-perfect for anyone who values their beauty sleep!
Cider's Favorites:
The "Sweet Spots": Scratches under the chin and on his cheeks are the way to his heart.
Playtime: He's a pro at hunting his favorite mouse-on-a-string!
Independence: He's been great home alone for 3-4 hours, usually spending that time catching up on his naps.
Note: Cider is a sensitive soul who prefers "quality over quantity" when it comes to pets. He'll let you know when he's had enough love, making him a great match for someone who understands feline body language. Though he loves people and is not afraid of visitors.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
My purr motor is always running!
Cider solicits attention and accepts petting but may be assertively demanding of attention or may play roughly.  
Due to his potential to get overstimulated, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced cat parent home with older, more mature children.

239421.name: Gepetto
239421.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My Foster writes: Looking for a best friend who will absolutely adore you? Gepetto is your girl. 💜 She's the sweetest mix of playful and cuddly-always up for a walk or play, but equally happy curled up beside you. She's house-trained, gentle, knows sit and how to give both paws, respects furniture boundaries, and is incredibly loving and trusting. She forms such a special bond with her person and is looking for someone who will give her the consistency and reassurance she deserves. She's still building confidence around other dogs on walks, but with her person by her side, this sweet girl has so much love to give and is ready to finally find her forever home.

My foster writes: Gepetto is an angel amongst us. She's the type of dog you fall in love with immediately (and she returns the affection tenfold). This girl loves hugs and kisses, and just wants to be in the same room as you. Well, that and as many stuffed toys she can find.
She is a great walker, good in her crate, and an excellent treat taker. She's understandably still a little anxious, so on walks she's wary of other dogs and people. But we just walk right by them no fuss no muss.
Gepetto I think would like another dog in the household to help with her confidence and loneliness. She would also be very happy being solo and the center of your world.
I can't say enough good things about Gepetto. Snap her up, she's a keeper, no lie!

My foster writes: Geppeto is a sweet girl who loves to give kisses and enjoy snuggling up next to you. She's great with children and doesn't chew on furniture. She has separation anxiety and is a little skittish sometimes when she is being walked- but with a little time and effort she will be ok in no time.
Although she pulls on a leash a little when being walked (because she's so curious of the world!) she comes right back to your side if called. Gepetto also knows sit, paw and up. She's an amazing dog and will be anyone's best friend !

My foster writes: Gepetto is super friendly and sweet! She gives so many kisses and loves to cuddle! Shes perfectly potty trained and doesn't bite on things in the house. Gepetto is great around children and will be your best friend!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

239429.name: Leo
239429.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

A volunteer writes: "Leo is a sweetheart who displays a lot of kindness, consideration for others, and affection," and honestly, that's all you need to know to understand why everyone here adores him. But there's even more to love. "He is very friendly. He tends to like to be around people, involved in whatever you're doing, and loves to sleep on our laps or at our feet."

His previous family shared that Leo has always loved meeting new people, greeting visitors with enthusiastic head bunts, cuddles, and plenty of charm. That affectionate, social spirit shines through every day at the shelter. The moment someone walks by, Leo stretches his chunky paws up on his door, eager to say hello and hopeful that today might be his day. He rolls onto his back, reaches for attention, and greets each new visitor like an old friend. Leo is one of those cats who simply wants to be part of your world. Whether he's supervising your chores, soaking up affection, or flopping over for belly-up stretches, he brings a special mix of sweetness, goofiness, and companionship that has made him a staff and volunteer favorite.

Leo is looking for the right home where his behavioral needs can be understood and managed. Beneath it all is a big-hearted, affectionate cat who has never stopped believing that his people are out there. We can't wait for the day this lovable boy finally gets the happy ending he's been waiting so patiently for.

239483.name: June
239483.summary:
My foster writes; Hi, I'm June, and I proudly wear the crown of Miss Independent. At 7 years young, I haven't spent a ton of time around hoomans, but I'm ready to find my person - someone patient, gentle, and willing to let me settle in at my own pace. I love exploring every nook and cranny of the home so I can choose the perfect nap spot (and map out a few escape routes... just in case). I'll gladly accept short, calm petting sessions as long as you approach me slowly and respectfully - boundaries are important to a girl like me! If you're looking for a low-maintenance companion who doesn't need constant attention and is happy to coexist peacefully, I'm your gal. Give me time, space, and kindness, and I'll reward you with quiet companionship.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

June tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

I can go home today!

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

239789.name: Piglet
239789.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Piglet is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Piglet has shown fearful behavior, including trembling, avoiding the leash, growling, barking, and remaining tense around handlers and in his previous home noted to have separation anxiety. Piglet has shown improvement once out of his kennel, approaching handlers for attention, leaning into petting, and soliciting play with other dogs during playgroup, but still shows some reluctance with select staff when being removed in kennel and is generally still fearful. Medically, Piglet is apparently healthy.

Piglet was surrendered by his previous owner due to destructive behaviors in the home. His family described him as a vocal, active, and playful dog who prefers contact on his own terms. He would spend the majority of his time in the living room of the home or wherever his people were; he is said to love car rides, running, going to the park, playing tug of war, and all forms of squeaky toys. Piglet allowed his family to bathe and brush him but does not have much experience on a leash because he previously had access to a yard. He is not picky with food or treats and will eat both wet and dry food diets. His previous owner reported that he has hard barked and growled at strangers, does resource guard items like toys, bones, and random objects, and becomes destructive when left alone in the home. During his intake, Piglet began growling at staff and thrashed lightly while on leash being walked to his kennel. He has allowed handling from Select Staff but has dodged leashing attempts when trying to remove him from the kennel. In calmer settings, Piglet has shown the potential to warm up and show sociable behaviors when approached slowly, allowing interaction at his own pace, with a slower approach and reward-based interactions. Due to the behavior concerns reported in the previous home and observed during his staying care, we recommend that Piglet be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope Rescue partner that can address his potential challenges with the use of a certified professional trainer that uses positive reinforcement methods only.

239847.name: Louise
239847.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Louise is at the front of the kennel, body and eyes relaxed with his tail held high as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he softly head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting. He does crane his neck to look at the kennels near him when he hears sounds but is easily refocused with petting and attention. He calmly walks out of the kennel and is easily picked up, remaining calm when held. When he is placed back into his kennel, Louise remains at the front and continues to allow and lean into all further petting and attention.

Louise enjoys attention and petting and has warmed up to staff in the shelter but has displayed some challenging behaviors previously in a home environment. He may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to his behavioral history, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

239965.name: Charlotte
239965.summary:
My foster writes: Charlotte is an adorable, shy, and fearful cat who would do well in a low traffic home with a gentle, patient and experienced cat lover who would give her time to build confidence and trust with her/him/they. She is independent and enjoys time by herself to explore her surroundings and play. Her boundaries must be respected and she would be better off in a home without young kids. She will spend most of the day hiding/sleeping and is most active at nighttime- this could change as she opens up to you and learns to trust you.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Zoey tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with younger children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

239967.name: Jordan
239967.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Jordan! In just a short time frame with his foster, he opens up more and more each day. This Halloween cat, with his black coat and yellow eyes, is definitely a night owl. You can hear him playing with multiple toys, running around, munching on food, and climbing all over. He's very hesitant around new people, and takes his time warming up, but who doesn't? He loves his space, but tolerates chin scratches, cheek scratches, and head pets. If you're patient with Jordan, he'll be patient and appreciative of you :)

Meet Jordan!
Jordan came to ACC from a home with more than 40 cats after his owner became ill. With so many animals and so little individual interaction, he didn't have many opportunities to build confidence around people. Here at the shelter, Jordan is a very shy, quiet boy who prefers to stay tucked into his cubby. He tolerates gentle petting and is beginning to relax during calm interactions, sometimes closing his eyes softly as he adjusts to attention.

My Ideal Home
Jordan will thrive in a calm, patient home with adults who understand shy or under-socialized cats. He needs a quiet environment, predictable routines, and a safe space to retreat to while he slowly acclimates. Treats, soft voices, and low-pressure interactions will help him build trust over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Likely yes. Jordan previously lived with many cats and may benefit from a calm, well-socialized resident cat who can model positive interactions with people. Slow introductions are important so he doesn't feel pressured.

Other Fun Facts
Jordan is a thoughtful little observer who watches quietly from his safe spot. As he warms up, he leans gently into cheek rubs and shows moments of comfort that hint at the companionship he could offer once he feels safe. For adopters who enjoy helping a shy cat blossom, Jordan is a rewarding, heartfelt project and a sweet soul waiting for his first true home.

240256.name: Caramel Toffee
240256.summary:
My foster writes: Caramel Toffee is, as her name suggests, the absolute sweetest! This polite, petite girl will steal your heart (and your lap) at first sight. I have had the pleasure of fostering her for a month and can see her finding her forever home with a family who wants genuine companionship. Toffee is a total couch potato, but also enjoys a round of tug-of-war during playtime. During walks, she'll do all of her business right away so that you can focus on enjoying a nice loose-leash stroll with her. Toffee rarely barks, making her perfect for NYC apartment living! She's extremely food-motivated, so it's easy to get her attention when there are distractions nearby and to teach her new things. So far, she knows "sit", "stay", "paw", and "go to bed" (go to her crate). Toffee is fully crate-trained and stays by herself for up to 8 hours on the days I am at the office. When I come home, she'll wait patiently for me to open the crate so that she can greet me with the cutest wiggles ever! She's happiest when I'm sitting on the couch, so she can have a spot to rest her house hippo head. If you choose to partake in a nap on the couch, Toffee will join you and shower you in snuggles.

My foster writes: Hi, I'm Caramel Toffee. I'm a calm, affectionate girl who loves being close to my people, and I'm looking for someone who enjoys energetic walks, cozy evenings, and a loyal companion who quietly follows them from room to room just to feel connected. I settle beautifully into a rhythm once I know my human, my home, and my neighborhood. Routines make me feel safe, and because I'm a reward‑based queen who's motivated by treats, attention, and all things comfy, I learn expectations quickly. After my first week with my foster human, he said - and I quote - "You're a level-1, zero‑accident superstar!"
I have lots of sweet quirks that make people smile: I lean my full weight against you for "supportive hugs," let out a soft, satisfied huff when I curl up for a nap, and I absolutely melt for head rubs and belly massages. I also have just a little habit of falling asleep quietly and then suddenly breaking into a spontaneous snore like a tiny engine starting up. Sometimes I even sit in funny, yoga‑like positions that make my foster humans laugh. I'm house‑trained, treat‑motivated, and fully convinced I'm the perfect size for a lap dog (I'm definitely not - but please don't tell me).
If you're looking for a gentle, loving companion with a big heart and an even bigger desire to bond, I just might be your girl.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
 
Due to a scratch incident I require a little extra paperwork to be filled out and a few extra vet visits this year).

240264.name: Sophie
240264.summary:
My foster writes: Sophie is a very calm, gentle, and adorable cat. She enjoys staying close to her family and will quietly follow us to the living room, dining room, working room, bedroom, and even the bathroom. She is also very sweet and patient with young children. Her litter box habits are excellent. Once we installed a baby gate at the kitchen entrance, she learned not to enter the kitchen.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!
Sophie interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience. 

A volunteer writes: Sometimes Sophie puts her paws up on the door when people walk by. It's her most heartfelt request that they please remember her. Rolling over to show her belly for good measure, I recognize and celebrate her efforts but am at a loss as to why this sweet marshmallow of a cat has to work so hard to make a friend. All she wants to do is cuddle and will elaborately roll herself in a number of directions to prove it. She has the softest fur I've ever felt and cuddling with her is an absolute joy. Sophie was left behind after her guardian moved away and has been spending her days making new friends as she tries to convince everyone she's the cat for them. I'd like to help her out and ask if maybe she's the cat for you?
240264.summaryHtml:
My foster writes: Sophie is a very calm, gentle, and adorable cat. She enjoys staying close to her family and will quietly follow us to the living room, dining room, working room, bedroom, and even the bathroom. She is also very sweet and patient with young children. Her litter box habits are excellent. Once we installed a baby gate at the kitchen entrance, she learned not to enter the kitchen.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

My purr motor is always running!

Sophie interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

A volunteer writes: Sometimes Sophie puts her paws up on the door when people walk by. It's her most heartfelt request that they please remember her. Rolling over to show her belly for good measure, I recognize and celebrate her efforts but am at a loss as to why this sweet marshmallow of a cat has to work so hard to make a friend. All she wants to do is cuddle and will elaborately roll herself in a number of directions to prove it. She has the softest fur I've ever felt and cuddling with her is an absolute joy. Sophie was left behind after her guardian moved away and has been spending her days making new friends as she tries to convince everyone she's the cat for them. I'd like to help her out and ask if maybe she's the cat for you?

240397.name: Meowy Dearest
240397.summary:
My foster writes: Meowy is a sweet but shy girl that loves to take her time to explore. She would do great with another cat playmate - especially one that's on the calmer side. She loves chin scratches and to play with her wand toy. Churros are her favorite treats! If you're looking for a long lasting love, Meowy is the right girl! With a dedicated pet parent, she will thrive.

My foster writes: Meowy Dearest is a shy but curious sweetheart who loves enrichment toys and relaxing on her cat tree. She takes her time warming up, but once she does, she'll quietly hang out nearby and make herself right at home. This cute little void needs someone who's patient, but the bond is worth the wait.

This petite little kitty has a quiet charm that wins hearts quickly. Meowy Dearest is naturally curious and observant-she likes to take in her surroundings carefully before deciding the best place to explore next. Once she feels comfortable, her playful side comes out and she'll happily chase toys, investigate every corner, and show off her gentle kitten energy.
Though she can be a little cautious in new situations and with new people, she's incredibly sweet and affectionate once she settles in. She loves calm company and approaches once she feels secure. Her gentle personality makes her a peaceful companion.
Meowy Dearest is quite confident with other cats and enjoys feline friends, making her a wonderful addition to a multi-cat household. 💛

Meet Meowy Dearest!
Pulled from a hoarding situation and understandably overwhelmed, Meowy Dearest arrived wary but watchful. With calm voices and a gentle approach, she'll tolerate brief petting and is starting to relax on her perch. She's an independent, curious girl who'll do best with a patient person willing to let trust grow at her pace.

My Ideal Home
An experienced, low-traffic home that understands shy cats. Start her in a quiet "decompression" room with hiding spots and vertical perches; keep interactions short and choice-based, and pair your presence with tasty treats. Coming from a hoarding environment, predictable routines will help her feel safe and blossom over time.

Good with Kids?
Best with adults only or older, cat-savvy teens who can move slowly and respect her boundaries.

Good with Other Pets?
History with pets is unknown. A very calm resident cat may help model confidence if introductions are extra slow, but she could also thrive as a solo cat while she settles in.

240452.name: Hercules
240452.summary:
My foster writes: Hercules was a great house guest. He's housebroken and slept peacefully in the basement overnight. He didn't bark, whine or chew on anything. We saw no destructive tendencies. He is affectionate and snuggly. He's also pretty good on the leash. He pulled a bit at the start but then settled into a nice pace. He seems interested in meeting other dogs with bouncy, happy energy. But he's easily redirected with a treat. He shows no reactivity to dogs. He enjoyed being in the car. Hercules could be a running buddy or a couch potato. And at 4 years old, he's the perfect age. The puppy stage is behind him and he's ready to join a home. You won't regret taking a chance on this good, good boy.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Really wonderful dog-- very responsive to our commands, didn't notice any jumpiness, destructiveness, or fearfulness. Very trusting-- was comfortable with us handling him and let us clean his paws after our first walk. He was exciting for whatever activity we presented him with-- whether a walk outside or hanging out on the couch inside. Showed no reactivity to other dogs we walked past, though seemed pretty interested in them. Showed no fearfulness to new people approaching him. Very cuddly, excitable, and attached at the hip to whoever is spending time with him!

Meet Hercules!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Hercules is a friendly and social dog who was abandoned by his previous owner and later surrendered to the shelter. He is a laid-back and affectionate dog once he feels comfortable but can be nervous in new situations. Hercules enjoys being around people and can be playful and wiggly when he bonds with someone.

My Ideal Home
Hercules would do best in an adult-only home with a calm, predictable environment. He needs a family that is patient and experienced with fearful or anxious dogs. He may display some nervousness or fear-based behaviors, so a home where he can adjust at his own pace will be ideal. His new family should be prepared to provide enrichment, structure, and positive reinforcement to help him manage his impulsivity and destructive tendencies.

Good with Kids?
No. Due to his fearfulness, especially around strangers, Hercules is better suited to a home without children under 13.

Good with Other Pets?
No. Hercules has not been tested with other animals but has shown fear-based behaviors (barking, growling, hiding) around cats. He would do best in a home with no cats or other pets.

Leash Manners
Hercules walks on a loose leash but can pull moderately. While he is generally easy to leash, he may be hesitant about collaring, and desensitization could help him feel more comfortable during walks.

Behavior Determination
Level 4. Hercules is recommended for an experienced adopter. His fearfulness and destructive behaviors, along with his poor impulse control, make him best suited for someone with experience working with anxious dogs. He will need a patient and dedicated adopter who can provide consistent training and care.

Other Fun Facts
Hercules is a sweet, affectionate dog who enjoys attention once he feels comfortable. He can be playful and social with those he bonds with, but he's also independent. He loves being near his humans, especially when treats are involved, and he seeks out attention on his own terms. Hercules is generally a calm dog but may need some extra time to adjust to his new home.

240561.name: Wemby
240561.summary:
My foster writes: Wemby is an affectionate, calm gentleman that is happy to be with you while you are working from home, cooking, or watching Netflix. His happy little meows and chirps will welcome you home and alert you to any birds outside your window :) He's a relaxing guy who is happy to snuggle and also loves his treats. He's a pleasure to have around!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am playful and cute!
I absolutely love catnip! It's my favorite treat!
Wemby was sitting in his litter box with dilated eyes and forward ears. He slowly approached and began sniffing the treats offered to him before cautiously eating. He allowed pets along his head and body, his eyes softening in the process. When transitioning to adding pressure to his chest to lift him up, his eyes dilated again as his body tensed up, stiff but tolerant. He soon moved back and repositioned himself on top of his den. 

Wemby interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting, however, he has a history of rough play outside of the shelter. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior. 

A volunteer writes: Wemby is a funny, 5 year old tuxedo. I struggled to get good content of this handsome gent because he was so all over the place, in the best way possible! He was curious to see what was going on in the room, so if I let him he likely would have explored the room and walked along the cat walk (aka the tops of the kennels). It was also his meal time and he is not a patient customer, he urged me to let him go pick up his food himself instead of waiting for his DoorDash to arrive (aka staff bringing him his food). Overall I found him to be a friendly, fun, and curious guy.
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

240565.name: Caramel
240565.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Caramel is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. Carmel has displayed periods of arousal, including heightened anxiety and inconsistent leash biting. At times she has refused to walk, while at other times she pulls on leash and fixates on people. She is social with staff, engages in weekly training to help with her anxiety, and has played with multiple other dogs in care; however, she is currently struggling in the care center environment. Medically, Caramel is apparently healthy.

Meet Caramel! As a long-stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out how you can take me home!

Caramel came in as a stray with an unknown history. She's a timid, sensitive dog who is still learning to trust. She may show signs of fear like trembling, a tucked tail, and whale eyes when stressed, and needs a quiet, calm environment where she can build confidence at her own pace.

My Ideal Home Caramel needs an adult-only home with a patient, experienced adopter who understands fearful dogs. She thrives with gentle handling, predictable routines, and gradual introductions. Enriching activities like scent work and puzzle toys will help her feel secure.

Good with Kids? No. Caramel is not suitable for homes with children under 13 and needs a calm, structured adult household.

Good with Other Pets? Caramel has shown to be very social with dogs in the care center.

Leash Manners Caramel is still developing her leash skills and can be nervous on walks. Quiet routes and positive reinforcement will help her build confidence.

Behavior Level: 4 Caramel requires an experienced adopter to help her work through her anxieties in a low-stress, adult-only home.

Other Fun Facts Caramel is a sweet, shy girl who enjoys connecting with her humans on her own terms.

Caramel is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is making wonderful progress every single day. She is working through resource guarding around food, and with every training session she is learning that mealtime is a safe and happy experience. Through positive reinforcement and a whole lot of encouragement, Caramel is building the trust and confidence she needs to relax and thrive.

240591.name: Orion
240591.summary:
My foster writes: Orion is a gentle, shy little gentleman with a big heart. He may be a bit hesitant at first, but with a little patience and his bonded sister by his side, he quickly blossoms into a loving and devoted companion. Once he feels safe, Orion becomes your loyal shadow He will follow you from room to room, chat with you, and keep up with his daily "patrol" of the home.
He enjoys affection on his terms and loves relaxing with you on the couch or bed. Calm, sweet, and quietly affectionate. Orion would thrive in a peaceful home where he can continue to build confidence and show his true, loving personality. He shares a special bond with his sister Caramelo and would love to find a home where they can stay together.

My Foster writes: If you're looking for a sweet, big boy who loves pets, look no further. Orion is the sweetest boy who seeks out pets and then purrs like a machine. He has some tabby stripes but he also has some spots that look like a cow's. So sometimes I call him Cowboy. He loves to play with toys, tossing them around and then running after them.

My Foster Writes:
Orion is a big mellow boy who needs a quiet home to show his big, goofy self. He is curious and brave in inspecting his surroundings. He uses his scratching post like a champ and loves to eat.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Orion was on top of the Kuranda bed, a bit hunched and appearing slightly apprehensive with fairly large pupils and giving occasional lip licks. He slightly sniffed the treats and then allowed petting on his cheek and head along his back while remaining slightly wary. He also gave slow blinks while remaining in place.

Orion interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

240592.name: Caramelo
240592.summary:
My foster writes: Caramelo is a sweet, confident girl with a gentle and affectionate nature. She settled in right away and quickly made herself at home, exploring her surroundings with curiosity and ease. A true purr machine, she loves attention, makes the best biscuits, and enjoys being near her people. She's also playful and loves watching the world go by from the window.
Caramelo shares a special bond with her brother Orion and helps him feel safe and confident. Together, they make a wonderful pair and would love to find a home where they can stay side by side.

My other foster writes:
Caramelo is a sweet girl who would love a quiet home where she is the queen. She is an expert biscuit maker and uses her scratching post like a champ. She loves pets and leans into your hand and purrs like a motor expressing how happy she is.

Caramelo is a playful, sweet girl who has a lot of love to give! She plays like a kitten by herself and with you. She'll carry a toy in her mouth which is so adorable. When you pet her, she'll move her head in your hand and purr really loudly. Her fur is so soft. She is just a lovely girl.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Caramelo is laying on her side at the front of the kennel, body and eyes soft. As The kennel door is opened, she head bunts the assessor's hands, leaning into all petting. She is able to be easily picked up and purrs as she is held, leaning against the assessor's body and remaining relaxed. When placed back down she continues to be receptive to attention, soliciting petting by leaning her body against and head bunting the assessor's hands. 

Caramelo interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

A volunteer writes: Caramelo is as sweet as caramel candy. She is a very full bodied girl who would love to join your family for Thanksgiving and maybe get a little turkey for treats. She loves turkey and gravy kitty treats and is practicing for the holidays and getting into the spirit. Whenever I walked by she waited at the front of her kennel hoping I would visit... naturally I had to. She graciously accepted pets, leaning her had into my hand. I really enjoyed my interaction with her and found her to be extremely sweet.

240769.name: Woody
240769.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My Borough Breaker writes:
Woody's vibe is relaxed, and unbothered. He'll let you pet him if you'd like, but he won't pressure you to. He's curious and will stop to sniff and eat plants along your walk, and he will take a lot of breaks to relax and lay in the shade with you. He's in no rush, he's just happy wherever he's at.
He does have a bit of a limp, but he doesn't let that stop him from enjoying his day; He'll even do some short prances and hops when he has a burst of energy! I think that if Woody were a person, he would be a very go with the flow, positive kind of guy with an independent nature. He's just content with life!
On our walk, SO many people stopped to admire and compliment him; He has a gorgeous coat of brindle fur and just a beautiful look that makes people talk. But he's unphased- he's used to all the attention!


Meet Woody!

Woody arrived at our care center as a stray, and his history is mostly a mystery. He's a very sweet, playful, and energetic dog who enjoys bouncing around and interacting with people he trusts. Woody loves interactive play, especially chasing and retrieving toys. He appreciates slow introductions to new people and places and prefers to approach on his own terms for pets and attention.


My Ideal Home
Woody would do best in a calm, adult-only household where he can set the pace for interactions. He benefits from consistent routines, gentle guidance, and positive reinforcement. Woody needs adopters who are patient and experienced with dogs that have touch sensitivities and mild resource guarding. A home that can provide cooperative handling and safe enrichment will help him thrive.


Good with Kids?
No - Woody is recommended for homes without children under 13. He prefers calm interactions and can become stressed in high-energy environments.


Good with Other Pets?
Woody has limited dog-to-dog experience. When properly introduced, he can be playful and gentle, but he may be pushy around treats. He is not recommended for homes with cats or smaller pets due to his size and energy.


Leash Manners
Woody walks well on leash with experienced handlers. He can be excitable when first leaving his kennel but quickly focuses on exploring once outside. Pulling is minimal with calm, consistent leadership.



Behavior Determination
Level 3 / Experienced Adopters - Woody requires a knowledgeable and patient home due to his touch sensitivities, mild resource guarding, and medical considerations. He responds best to calm, predictable, and positive interactions.


Other Fun Facts
Woody has a joyful, bouncy personality and loves games of chase and fetch. He enjoys bonding with people who respect his boundaries and allows him to approach for attention. While he likes to assert independence, he is very affectionate with those he trusts and thrives in a patient, structured environment.

More like jiggling by my side than walking, really, as his whole jello body quakes with joy with each step.  I adore his cartoon face, the way his teefies sometimes get stuck in his lips and his freakishly large milk chocolate eyes. He loves to play with toys, loves attention and loves to be out of his kennel.
240769.summaryHtml:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! My Borough Breaker writes: Woody's vibe is relaxed, and unbothered. He'll let you pet him if you'd like, but he won't pressure you to. He's curious and will stop to sniff and eat plants along your walk, and he will take a lot of breaks to relax and lay in the shade with you. He's in no rush, he's just happy wherever he's at. He does have a bit of a limp, but he doesn't let that stop him from enjoying his day; He'll even do some short prances and hops when he has a burst of energy! I think that if Woody were a person, he would be a very go with the flow, positive kind of guy with an independent nature. He's just content with life! On our walk, SO many people stopped to admire and compliment him; He has a gorgeous coat of brindle fur and just a beautiful look that makes people talk. But he's unphased- he's used to all the attention! Meet Woody!
Woody arrived at our care center as a stray, and his history is mostly a mystery. He's a very sweet, playful, and energetic dog who enjoys bouncing around and interacting with people he trusts. Woody loves interactive play, especially chasing and retrieving toys. He appreciates slow introductions to new people and places and prefers to approach on his own terms for pets and attention.

My Ideal Home
Woody would do best in a calm, adult-only household where he can set the pace for interactions. He benefits from consistent routines, gentle guidance, and positive reinforcement. Woody needs adopters who are patient and experienced with dogs that have touch sensitivities and mild resource guarding. A home that can provide cooperative handling and safe enrichment will help him thrive.

Good with Kids?
No - Woody is recommended for homes without children under 13. He prefers calm interactions and can become stressed in high-energy environments.

Good with Other Pets?
Woody has limited dog-to-dog experience. When properly introduced, he can be playful and gentle, but he may be pushy around treats. He is not recommended for homes with cats or smaller pets due to his size and energy.

Leash Manners
Woody walks well on leash with experienced handlers. He can be excitable when first leaving his kennel but quickly focuses on exploring once outside. Pulling is minimal with calm, consistent leadership.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 / Experienced Adopters - Woody requires a knowledgeable and patient home due to his touch sensitivities, mild resource guarding, and medical considerations. He responds best to calm, predictable, and positive interactions.

240801.name: Bonsai
240801.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

This lovable boy is incredibly smart, obedient, and eager to please. We can't believe he's not been adopted. His manners are impeccable!! He is such a good boy, incredibly happy and has so much love to give!! He is crate trained, house broken, and loves to do movement puzzles and play fetch. He can also catch treats in mid air!

I had the pleasure of hanging out with Bonsai at the recent ACC adoption event sponsored by Best Friends Animal Society. The weather was a bit chilly and overcast. Bonsai behaved well throughout the entire event. Bonsai happily greeted everyone (adults and kids) who then reciprocated with lots of pets and loves. Bonsai was eager to show off his skills - perfect sit, treat catching and waiting patiently for a treat left a short distance away until I said "ok, go get it". Between meeting the people, Bonsai and I took nice leisurely walks and spent time cuddling up under the blankets.

Bonsai is a playful, active, sweet and loving boy. He can be chilled when needed. Bonsai walks nicely on leash. He can pull a little when he is interested in something, but he can be easily redirected and continues his walk. Bonsai definitely loves to play and to spend time with his person.

My Boroughbreaker writes: We had such a fun day together. He's down for anything. He LOVES meeting people, and is so cuddly and friendly. He is a huge teddy bear and goofball. He's also very treat motivated! He checked in with me a lot on walks and was redirected easily. He is a strong boy, so he needs to work on his leash manners but that shouldn't be any trouble with only a little training. When he sees other dogs on walks, he whines, growls, and lunges, but to me it seems like excitement/frustration rather than aggression. We didn't actually meet any dogs obviously but I definitely wouldn't categorize him as dog aggressive. He just needs to be properly socialized. The good thing is that he is so treat motivated he should be easy to work with. He has such a good heart and so much love to give, he will be anyone's best friend.

240872.name: Hank
240872.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Hank is at risk for behavior reasons. Hank was escalating towards his owners in the home when they attempted to crate him. He began to display similar behavior, hard barking and growling when being returned to the kennel. During socialization sessions, he has been tolerant of handling but remains highly anxious. Medically, he has mild - moderate dental disease. 

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Hank is a people-oriented dog who loves being close to his family and spending time wherever his favorite humans are. One of his former owner's favorite things about him was his love of nighttime snuggles, and he's happiest when he can be near the people he cares about. Hank enjoys playing with balls, knows the cues sit, stay, and paw, and is always eager for a tasty snack-he isn't picky when it comes to treats!

Hank allows handling for grooming, including bathing and brushing, and he enjoys companionship and attention. He can be vocal at times and would likely do best in a home that understands his need for interaction and structure. He does not enjoy car rides and prefers not to be confined. While he has experience with crate training, he struggled when placed in a crate in his previous home. Since arriving at the shelter, Hank has shown similar behavior, reacting to staff when being returned to his kennel. Adopters should be prepared to work with him on building positive associations with confinement and transitions.

241043.name: Indiana Blue
241043.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Indiana Blue is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Indiana Blue has shown high arousal in his kennel, including jumping and barking at the kennel door, and has needed treats or toys to help with leashing. Indiana Blue is also reported to leash bite intensely in his kennel needing toys and treats to remove him from kennel. Outside of his kennel, Indiana Blue generally walks with a neutral body, approaches handlers for treats, and has been able to pass dogs and people without reacting. Medically, Indiana Blue is underweight, has distal limb laxity, a tear to tip of tongue and holding small portion out of mouth and mild pododermatitis.

Indiana Blue came into the QUACC after being brought in as a stray. In the care centers, Indiana Blue has displayed persistent leash biting, which can be difficult to redirect with treats, toys, or other distractions while he is in his kennel. He has otherwise been social and affectionate with staff, often leaning into contact and soliciting attention. As a result, we recommend Indiana Blue is placed with one of our New Hope Partners.

241061.name: Cunningham
241061.summary:
My foster writes: 

Meet Cunningham, the Little Prince in cat form. He's a gentle, affectionate boy who loves people and has the sweetest habit of softly patting your hand when he wants attention. He may be a little shy at first, but warms up within 2-3 days and quickly becomes very friendly. He enjoys playing with his favorite sheep toy, loves being brushed, and is a super clean little gentleman who's always ready to explore. If you're looking for a charming companion to treat like royalty, Cunningham is your prince.

Cunningham is not your typical cuddle bug, He's a thoughtful, observant cat who prefers to take his time getting to know people and his surroundings. Loud environments and lots of activity can make him a little anxious, so he'd do best in a calm home with someone who understands that trust takes time.
Once he's comfortable, though, Cunningham shows off his sweet and funny side. He enjoys doing his own thing nearby, and will occasionally have moments of affection.
Cunningham would thrive with a patient human who appreciates an independent cat who loves from a distance. For the right person, he'll be a wonderfully unique companion.

He enjoys doing his own thing during the day and comes alive at night with playful energy and curiosity. A perfect match for a home that loves a laid-back companion with a fun side!

241083.name: Charcoal
241083.summary:
Meet Charcoal!
Charcoal's foster writes "He also goes by Muñeco or Buddy and he is a gentle sweet boy who really just wants to be close to his person. He is the best companion who will happily follow you around all day looking for belly rubs, treats, and company. He enjoys exploring outside but his favorite place is right next to you especially if it means a cozy nap nearby."

Personality
Charcoal is calm affectionate and people oriented. His boroughbreaker writes that he is very relaxed and calm and tends to guide you toward the things he enjoys. He is gentle and patient when interacting with people and likes to stay close to his handler. He has a soft easygoing presence and is happiest when he is near someone he trusts.

Out and About
On leash Charcoal walks nicely with mild pulling and does not show concern toward people or other dogs. He is focused on his handler and keeps a relaxed steady pace. Volunteers describe him as attentive and charming and say he often gives his full attention to his person rather than his surroundings. He responds well to guidance and redirection.

Social Behavior
Charcoal is moderately social and will approach when called. He enjoys being near people and often stays close while quietly observing. He is not reactive toward dogs and typically walks past them without concern.

My Ideal Home
Charcoal would do best in a calm home where he can feel safe and included. He enjoys companionship and will thrive with someone who appreciates a gentle dog who wants to be part of everyday life. He may take a little time to fully settle but once he does he becomes a loyal and steady presence.

Living with Kids
Because Charcoal can be sensitive he would do best in a home without very young children. He may be open to older respectful kids once he has had time to meet them and feel comfortable.

Things to Know
Charcoal is a Level 2 dog who will benefit from continued confidence building and positive reinforcement training. He enjoys affection but prefers to engage at his own pace and on his own terms. He does well with gentle structure and clear guidance.

Fun Fact
Charcoal is a loyal shadow who is happiest following his person around the home getting belly rubs and then settling in nearby for a nap. He has a quiet charm that makes him easy to fall in love with.

241187.name: Beauty
241187.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Beauty is at risk for behavior reasons. Beauty is reported to have separation anxiety in her previous home, escalating to biting when the owner was leaving. Beauty has bitten over resources as well. Beauty does show bite inhibition, as no bites have broken the skin. In the care center, she is fearful, often shaking in her kennel. During socialization, she warms up to handlers quickly but can be wary when handlers reach towards her. Medically, she is apparently healthy. 

Beauty is looking for an experienced, patient adopter who understands canine behavior and is committed to helping her succeed. She has a history of resource guarding and separation anxiety, and in the home these behaviors have escalated to biting when she is uncomfortable or guarding valued items. While the bites did not break the skin, they demonstrate that Beauty needs careful management, consistent training, and an owner who can recognize and respond appropriately to her body language and behavior. A calm, structured home that can provide positive reinforcement training, predictable routines, and ongoing support will give Beauty the best opportunity to thrive.

Beauty is a loving, affectionate companion who thrives on being close to her people. She enjoys spending her days wherever her family is and is happiest when she can be part of the action. Beauty loves playing catch, carrying around balls and stuffed animals, and earning biscuits for being a good girl. She also enjoys going on three to four 30-minute walks each day and knows several cues, including sit, down, stay, lay down, quiet, go, and up.

With the right experienced family, Beauty has the potential to be a deeply devoted and comforting companion who forms strong bonds with the people she trusts.

241237.name: Burrata
241237.summary:
Burrata is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans/strangers from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appears wary of human contact. It is difficult to predict exactly how socialized she is and if she will respond to further socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
As described in her previous home, Burrata is a friendly, quiet, and independent cat. She enjoys being where people are in the home. Burrata has never had interactive playtime before. Burrata enjoys scratching on rough rope and cardboard. 

My foster writes: Burrata and Basil are two young sister cats who bring a calm, gentle presence to the home. Since arriving, we've learned that they love observing everything around them. They have the sweetest, most curious little expressions, sometimes it genuinely feels like they're quietly "commenting" on whatever we're doing, and it always makes us smile.
During the day, they relax in their favorite cozy spots where they feel safe and comfortable. And when nighttime comes, they open up a bit more: they come out to explore, walk around the home with quiet curiosity, and show small signs of growing confidence. Watching these little moments has been incredibly rewarding.
They are very clean, peaceful, and easygoing. While they aren't seeking direct contact yet, their progress is clear, they're spending more time out in the open, moving around more confidently, and showing a stronger interest in their surroundings. With patience and a stable, loving environment, they continue to take meaningful steps forward.
Burrata and Basil are looking for a calm and understanding home where they can continue growing at their own pace. They're perfect for someone who appreciates a peaceful home and finds beauty in watching shy cats slowly blossom. With the right environment, these two sweet sisters have the potential to become very special companions.

With the right environment, these two sweet sisters have the potential to become very special companions.

241271.name: Ryder
241271.summary:
Meet Ryder!
Ryder was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and now this fun, affectionate girl is ready to bring her big personality to a new home. She's social, playful, and loves being around people, basically your built-in best friend with a goofy streak.

My Ideal Home
Ryder would do best in an active home that can give her plenty of attention, exercise, and structure. She thrives when she has outlets for her energy and people to interact with, and would benefit from a routine that helps her feel secure when left alone.

Good with Other Pets?
Ryder is playful and social with other dogs and has shown friendly greetings at the shelter. However, she may chase or lunge at cats and small animals, so a home without them would be best.

Good with Kids?
Ryder has previously lived with children and was described as friendly and outgoing with them, but due to her sensitivity when startled and her energetic play style, a home without very young children (under 5) is recommended.

Things to Know
Ryder is a high-energy, affectionate dog who loves to play, learn, and be close to her people. She walks with a loose, social demeanor and enjoys greeting both people and dogs, sometimes with a bit of enthusiastic jumping. She already knows cues like sit, down, paw, and spin, and loves games like fetch and snuggling up after playtime. Ryder can feel anxious when left alone and will need a patient home to help her build confidence and comfort with independence. With consistency, enrichment, and positive reinforcement, she has all the tools to thrive.

A Volunteer Writes
"This girl has it all: so funny, so friendly, and so smart! She walks beautifully to the back where she play bows to dogs on either side until she realizes I'm the only one who is going to play with her-lucky me! Ryder is not only a great fetcher, she knows sit, down, paw, and spin, and she has mastered the art of snuggling. We are in love and you will be, too!"

Fun Fact
Ryder is basically a professional goofball with a soft side, equal parts zoomies and snuggles.

241322.name: Mr. Jay
241322.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Mr. Jay is laying in his litterbox in his cubby, paws tucked under his chest, body tense, eyes wide and pupils dilated as the assessor approaches and opens the cubby door. He is spoken to softly and a squeeze up is offered. He briefly leans forward to sniff it before pulling his head back, not eating it. Mr. Jay is tolerant of petting on the head and cheeks with the tool but does not engage with the attention. When he is pet down his shoulders and back, he begins flinching and leans away to avoid contact. Pickup is not attempted due to observed behavior.

Mr. Jay tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

241614.name: Sugar
241614.summary:
Meet Sugar!

Sugar is a sweet, quiet girl who enjoys relaxing. She enjoys short walks, loves car rides, and knows commands like "sit," "lay down," and "go in the cage."

Sugar has a playful side and loves chasing a ball or playing with an empty plastic bottle. According to her previous owner, she is friendly with people and enjoys playing. She eats both wet and dry food but has a chicken allergy, so she will need to stay on a chicken-free diet.

Sugar is currently being treated for a skin condition and is on a special diet to help it clear up. Because of this, she isn't comfortable with much handling at the care center right now, and she also finds bathing and brushing stressful. She'll do best with a patient adopter who will give her time to settle in and build trust.

If you're looking for a calm, loyal companion who enjoys quiet time, leisurely walks, and the occasional car ride or game of fetch, Sugar could be the perfect addition to your family.

241644.name: Ellie
241644.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Ellie is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns in her previous home and in the care center. In Ellie's previous home, Ellie had an incident where she lunged at a small dog and pinned it to the ground, requiring intervention to get away from the small dog. Ellie was able to disengage from the situation when redirected with a treat after several attempts. Ellie also in the care center has been starting to kennel fighting leaving the kennel room, making it difficult to walk her safely at times. Ellie is in the care center and social and affectionate with staff. Medically, Ellie is apparently healthy.

Meet Ellie!
Ellie was found as a stray, tied to a fence on Liberty Ave & Sackman St. She was friendly and easy to transport to the shelter, and from the start has shown herself to be a social, affectionate girl who is eager to connect with people.

Personality
Ellie is a wiggly, loving, high-energy girl who truly enjoys people. She seeks attention, especially butt scratches, and is very food motivated, which makes her a great candidate for continued training. She can get very excited and may be jumpy when she's happy to see you, but it all comes from a place of enthusiasm and affection.

A previous foster describes her as 60 lbs of pure love, the perfect companion for both long walks and lazy sofa time. At home, she loves to snuggle close and will happily try to fit right into your lap if you let her. She also handles alone time well, staying calm and quiet until her people return.

Training & Needs
Ellie is still working on some basic manners and impulse control. She will benefit from structure, consistency, and continued positive reinforcement training. Because she is energetic and easily excited, she does best with an adopter who can guide her with patience and help her channel her enthusiasm in positive ways.

Ideal Home
Ellie would thrive in an active, experienced home that can provide both physical exercise and mental enrichment like walks, chews, and food puzzles. A calmer home environment without young children will help her feel more settled and allow her to continue building confidence and manners at her own pace.
