241679.name: Tennessee
241679.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Tennessee and housemate Lizzie Girl were brought to us as their owner was going through a very rough patch. Tennessee is a handsome long hair gentlecat, said to be shy but very active, affectionate and playful when he is comfortable. He has a tendency to go for cover when he feels insecure like he is at the care center. Tennessee tries to make friends, though but it sometimes takes time for other cats in the community room(Tennessee shares the room with 3 other kitties)to want to mingle and even play. So, right now, Tennessee opted for a nice and open hide out from where he can watch the playroom. He enjoys petting and ...brushing which is very much needed for a long hair cat. Tennesse is three year old, already neutered, apparently healthy and did well on his behavior evaluation that let us know, though that his new owner needs to be understanding of his timid personality and the difficult times he went through and give him time and space to adjust to his new life. Tennessee would love to meet you at the Manhattan Care Center.






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

A volunteer writes: The Community Room crew!!! There are currently 4 cats (mixed gender) in our community cat room. When I was in there, there were all very relaxed and peacefully coexisting. They had relaxed body language and accepted all pets. They were all sweet a bit reserved at first but gentle souls.

241803.name: Onix
241803.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Onix is at risk due to behavioral concerns. During his multiple stays in care, Onix has shown arousal concerns, handling sensitivity, and kennel stress. When touched, Onix has a head whipped with a tense body, and would pant heavily. During his previous assessment, Onix began to become aroused and jump onto the handler, mouthing their clothing, and an interrupter was used to get him to stop. During a walk, he became aroused after a moped sped by and bit a handler on their hand, leaving red teeth marks around the base of their thumb; the bite did not break skin or draw blood. In his kennel, Onix wails for an extended period of time during his multiple stays. He readily accepts treats, is easy to remove from the kennel, and readily engages with relaxation games. Medically, Onix is overweight.

Onix came into the care center as a stray during his prior stay in care he is described by his prior owners as an affectionate and friendly dog who is very active and playful. He spends most of his time in the living room of his home where he enjoys playing with plushies and chew toys. He is accustomed to going on 1-2 walks a day during which he pulls on his leash. He allows his family to bathe, brush, and trim his nails and loves going for a car ride. He knows the cues sit, paw, and stay in both English and Spanish and is not picky with food or treats. In the care cneter Onix allows leashing and is able to move through the care center, he displays clear stress signals including avoidance, head whipping, and discomfort with touch, particularly during more hands-on interactions. Onix has displayed high levels of anxiety and is noted to jump on handlers and leash bite. Onix s would benefit from a New Hope placement that can provide a calm, predictable environment and low-pressure handling. Onix is available for rescue through one of our new hope partners. 

A volunteer writes: Onix is a frequent flier at Queens ACC and in shelter speak, that isn't necessarily a good thing. By no fault of his own, he has been found stray and reclaimed numerous times. But each time he resurfaces with us, once for each of the last three seasons, fall, winter and spring, I recognize his endearing face immediately. Mr. Congeniality with that big smile and each time I learn something new about him. On this visit, we discover his LOVE for the water. Running through the stream, having the time of his life.

Onix's guardian noted that he's friendly with kids (he lived with 3), and hasn't had much experience with cats or dogs. He rarely has accidents in the home. He's described as a friendly and affectionate dog who is outgoing and playful. He loves going for car rides and is bilingual when it comes to cues. Due to some handling sensitivity shown in the care center and stress seen inside of the kennel, Onix is at risk for euthanasia and available to foster through a New Hope Rescue Partner.

241862.name: Mist
241862.summary:
Meet Mist!
 
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Mist came to the shelter after her family was evicted from their home, and her world was suddenly turned upside down. While this transition has been stressful, Mist has shown herself to be a friendly, curious, and food-motivated dog who enjoys enrichment and engagement with her handlers. She can be nervous in new situations but is eager to connect once she feels safe and understood.

My Ideal Home
Mist would thrive in a calm, adult-only home with an experienced, patient adopter who understands fearful or sensitive dogs. A predictable routine, positive reinforcement training, and respecting her boundaries will help her build confidence. She benefits from mental enrichment, sniffing activities, and guidance around impulse control and polite greetings.

Good with Kids?
No. Mist is recommended for a home without children due to her sensitivity to handling and need for a slow, thoughtful approach to touch and interaction.

Good with Other Pets?
Unknown with dogs and cats. In shelter observations, Mist has been avoidant and aloof with other dogs, preferring space rather than social interaction. She may be best as the only pet or with very careful, slow introductions.

Leash Manners
Mist generally walks on a loose leash but can pull at times, especially when excited or exploring. She enjoys sniffing and outdoor time and benefits from calm, structured walks to help her stay focused.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Mist needs an experienced adopter who can help her work through fearfulness, touch sensitivity, and impulse control using patience and positive reinforcement.

Other Fun Facts
Mist loves snuffle mats, searching for hidden treats, and enrichment games that let her use her nose. She's very food motivated, enjoys exploring new spaces, and has a playful, energetic side once she feels comfortable. With the right person, Mist has the potential to blossom into a deeply loyal companion.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Mist was great on our walks! She does not pull on the leash and she listens to basic commands. She did not reach to other dogs or people passing by. She was very good in the house especially after tiring her out after our long walk. She was very curious and always following us around the house no matter where we went! She was great overall

A volunteer writes: Mist is just the most darling little girl. She sits quietly and patiently in her crate in the overflow room, waiting for her turn to get some fresh air. Outside Mist is friendly and social, but prefers food over anything else we can provide her. She is about 4 years old and was found left in an apartment after he family was evicted. She is clearly a gem of a girl, although needs some time to adjust to new people and places.

My foster writes: Meet the sweetest girl Ramona! Once Ramona warms up, she loves to love on her people. Ramona eagerly waits by the door for you to get home and immediately flops over for snuggles and belly rubs. Ramona loves to greet guests the same way and is not afraid of new people in her home. She loves to rub up against you and even adorably jumps up to get kisses and rub her face on yours. Ramona spends time napping and playing with springs or a mouse toy. She loves to lay by the window and watch the birds fly around. Sometimes Ramona even likes to lay under the covers against your legs for extra warmth! She is such a sweet cat and can't wait to love on her forever family!

My previous foster writes:
Ramona is five years old and 15lbs. Her coat is a silky dark grey and her eyes shift orange to green. She may at first dodge or hide but once she feels at home, all humans are welcome visitors to her queendom. Ramona will greet you by running towards you and rubbing against your legs, ask to bonk her head against yours, then flop at your feet and stretch out to show her belly. She loves belly pets!
Ramona is a large cat, and some large cats need help with grooming. Ramona can clean herself after using the litter box but she needs help on her back. She adores brush time and asks for help grooming after her meals.

Ramona is regal. She wears a dark grey coat and has tiny ivory fangs. Ramona wants churu for dinner and is slow to eat most other wet foods even with churu mixed in. 
Ramona is curious and wants to be involved, but she is not exactly food motivated. She enjoys sitting and dozing quite near her person. She is mildly interested in the house and considers the bedroom her HQ between short explorations. Ramona enjoys string toys, feathered balls, and springs. She plays by herself and asks to play an equal amount. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Ramona tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home.  We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children.

241898.name: Maya
241898.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Maya accepts attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home. She will likely require an appropriate decompression period and slow start in her new home to allow her to build her confidence as she adjusts, and build a relationship with her new family using treats and positive reinforcement.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I am playful and cute!

A volunteer writes: Maya knows it's so important to show your friends you care, which is why she was always comforting her previous guardian whenever they felt sad. If she could only find someone to comfort her. Admittedly Maya doesn't always know how to put herself out there to tell us what she'd like. In a sea of sparkly kittens with kneading paws and happy purrs, it could potentially put dear Maya at a disadvantage but since we certainly don't want that to happen, please let me share with you what we know about this wonderful cat. Firstly, Maya really needs a chance. Snuggled up in the back of her cubby, things were a little different in her home before where she was affectionate and playful, chasing after bugs and joyfully playing with her water. She's hoping to find a family who will welcome her, so please come and give her a little chance.

242187.name: Sterling
242187.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Sterling is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns in care and in his previous home. He was reported to have bitten a resident cat after escaping his crate. During the incident, he bit the cat on the leg and bit the foster on the hand while they attempted to separate them. Sterling was also reported to display significant separation anxiety when left alone, including eliminating indoors, attempting to escape and flip his crate, chewing baseboards and door frames, counter surfing, destroying household items, and accessing human food. While in the care center, Sterling has also been observed to hesitate in certain areas during walks, requiring coaxing or a change in direction to continue walking. In his previous foster homes, Sterling was described as friendly, affectionate, and eager to cuddle. Sterling in care has done well in dog playgroups and loves hanging out with his favorite staff members. Medically, Sterling has anemia, cryptorchidism, and dental disease.

My previous foster writes: Meet Sterling the giant with a heart of gold. This gentle giant is a professional snuggler who believes personal space is highly overrated. If you're on the couch or If you're working being next to you is his favorite place to be. If he could fit in your lap, he absolutely would (he tries!). Sterling is fully house trained, loves car rides, and walks beautifully on leash. He's extremely food-motivated, which makes training fun and rewarding. He already knows to sit and wait politely for his food and getting in and out of doors. He loves tug-of-war, ball toys, and matching your energy during playtime, but at heart, he's a couch potato who just wants to be near his person.
Sterling is sweet, affectionate, and happy to be handled (even tolerates baths for the right peanut butter bribe).
If you're looking for a loyal best friend who will adore you endlessly and makes the best couch buddy, Sterling is ready to move in and claim his permanent cuddle spot.

My foster writes: Sterling is such a sweet gentle soul! He's so friendly and calm, he just wants to be by his humans (or any human) at all times. He's lazy & loves to snuggle - he'll play a little but then he'll be ready to curl up for a nap right after. He's great on the leash & looks at everyone like they're his long lost love! He's a really special dog who just needs someone who can give him the attention he deserves. Anyone will be lucky to welcome him into their home!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I need a home without cats or small animals.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I really enjoy toys! I'll let you know my favorite one when we meet!

242246.name: Atreus
242246.summary:
Meet Atreus!
Atreus, also lovingly known as "Girlfriend," is a wiggly, affectionate girl who truly just wants to be your best friend. She's happiest right by your side-whether that's curled up on the couch, hanging out while you work, or joining you throughout your daily routine. She's the ultimate work-from-home companion and will gladly spend her day cuddling as close as possible.

Personality
Atreus is loving, goofy, and full of personality. She has absolutely no concept of personal space (which earned her the nickname "Elbows") and will happily climb into your lap or snuggle right up against you. She's also a champion burrower-if you're under a blanket, expect her to politely request access so she can tuck herself underneath. She can be a little chatty when she wants a walk or attention, but at heart she's eager to please.

Training & Behavior
Atreus is incredibly treat-motivated and loves to learn. She already knows many commands, including Sit, Down, Paw (her favorite), Stay, Come, Off, Bed, Crate, Place, and Kiss. She has great house manners and will relax in her bed during mealtime instead of begging. She's familiar with structured training (including the "123 game") and thrives with consistency and positive reinforcement.

Atreus is a natural city dog. She's comfortable with street noise, crowds, and busy environments. Thanks to her petite 40 lb frame, she has even learned to travel on the subway in an XL tote bag. She has experience as an office dog and adjusted quickly. She doesn't scavenge or eat food off the ground during walks and handles everyday distractions well. Atreus also rides nicely in the car-she may get excited at first, then settles in for a nap within minutes.

Daily Routine & Energy
Atreus is a medium-energy dog who is just as happy napping beside you as she is joining you on a long walk or hike. She currently enjoys four walks a day, including one longer 40-60 minute outing. She does have a strong prey drive and loves chasing squirrels and rats, so she may pull in park settings-but she tends to walk more calmly in the city. When she gets excited, she may jump or bark, but it's all out of love. To burn off extra energy, she loves a good game of tug-of-war. She enjoys bully sticks and puzzle feeders, but isn't very interested in squeaky toys.

Social Behavior
Atreus loves people and has no fear of strangers. She's very comfortable with handling, including having her paws touched. She walks calmly past other dogs and may enjoy canine friends with proper introductions. Due to her prey drive, she is not a fit for homes with cats or small animals. Because she can be a bit jumpy, she's not the best match for homes with small children.

My Ideal Home
Atreus would thrive with someone who wants a constant companion and is ready to give her the time, structure, and affection she deserves. If you're looking for a loving, cuddly, slightly goofy best friend-she's your girl.

242422.name: Snoopy
242422.summary:
My foster writes: Snoopy has completely transformed in his foster home! After taking a few weeks to settle in, Snoopy burst out of his shy shell with so much love to give. He now takes his role as a companion very seriously; he will greet you at the front door and dutifully follow you from room to room. He doesn't quite meow, but he has developed a very cute chirp that he uses to let you know when he wants attention. His foster guardian works from home, and Snoopy prefers to spend his afternoons snoozing on her lap or on one of his favorite soft spots very nearby. When nap time is over, Snoopy is very serious about play! He has a lot of energy and prefers to get his exercise in with you and one of his beloved wand toys. Once he's tuckered himself out, he'll happily sleep through the entire night at the foot of your bed or on his own on the couch, where he'll wait patiently for you to get up. Snoopy is a dream come true. Whoever adopts this gentle boy will be lucky indeed.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
Snoopy somewhat tolerates some attention and petting but displays a high level of FAS an may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Snoopy sat quietly alone in an empty apartment bathroom. Waiting for someone to remember him or maybe hoping they wouldn't, he was brought to us when a construction company doing work in the apartment found him. Settling into shelter life has put Snoopy on a steep learning curve. He's a gentle hearted guy and still seems to be hoping for the possibility of flying under the radar. Since that won't be happening, we'd been trying our best to meet Snoopy halfway by finding the things he likes most. Though our offers of pets, treats, and toys haven't gotten us very far yet, it seems what brightens Snoopy's day most is curling up on his Kuranda bed as he tries to find the sun spot and remember the bright one, which is that he's one step closer to finding you.

242512.name: Kemuri
242512.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

A volunteer writes: When I met Kemuri at the Care Center the other day, this gray and white charmer was sitting at the front of his cat condo, welcoming my attention by sniffing my hand softly. He remained relaxed during our time together, never showing any aggression or discomfort. So it surprised me to look into his backstory and find that his previous person noted that although Kemuri was affectionate, he could occasionally play rough. My hunch is that Kemuri is a well-behaved boy who perhaps was overstimulated in his former household or not given the appropriate playtime and space every cat needs. Our behavior team found him to be social and loving, as well as a huge fan of toys and squeeze-up treats. Looking for a good boy who deserves a second chance and new pet parents who know how to read cats? Then you must meet Kemuri today!

242642.name: Bellajae
242642.summary:
Meet Bellajae!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My Ideal Home
Bellajae would do best in a home with a patient, experienced owner who can help her work through her anxiety and teach her basic manners. She needs a structured environment with plenty of physical activity and mental stimulation to keep her happy. A home without young children (under 13) is recommended, as Bellajae can be a bit mouthy and excitable. She is a strong candidate for an adopter who is dedicated to training and managing her energy levels.

Good with Kids?
No. Bellajae would do best in a home without young children. She tends to be mouthy and has a high energy level that may be overwhelming for kids.

Good with Other Pets?
Bellajae has not been tested with other dogs or cats, so it's unclear how she would react. Given her high energy and potential for reactivity, she may be best as the only pet in the home or with an experienced adopter who can manage introductions carefully.

Leash Manners
Bellajae pulls mildly on leash, and she is still working on her leash manners. She has no notable reactions to other animals or people while walking, but she will need continued training to improve her walking behavior.

Behavior Determination
Level 3. Bellajae is an energetic and excitable dog who may require extra attention for training, especially to work on her anxiety, destructive behaviors, and poor impulse control. She will do best with an experienced adopter who is prepared to handle her anxiety, jumpiness, and mouthiness. Some work on house training and chew behavior will also be needed.

Other Fun Facts
Bellajae is playful and loves water-bath time is one of her favorite things! She enjoys spending time with her humans, playing with toys, and getting attention. Bellajae is crate trained, but she does not enjoy being in the car. She knows basic commands like "sit," "stay," and "down," and she's always ready for some fun or snuggles when she's feeling comfortable.

Bellajae's energy level is a 10 but when she meets Santa it somehow manages to escalate to 100! Her tail never stops wagging as she engages Santa in a number of games, even using her as an obstacle course as she zooms under her legs. One of Bella's legs looks a bit atrophied and as hard as we try to slow her down so as not to injure herself, she has other plans in mind and speeds across the yard numerous times in glee. After an extended play time we get her to sit for a few treats in front of Santa but it's not before long that she's off to whiz across the yard again.

Bellajae was surrendered when her owner became hospitalized and she was reportedly without care for many days. When the field officer picked her up, if she stopped petting her, Bella would lick her hands to get her to continue. Her guardian's favorite thing about her was how affectionate she is. She likes bath time and playing with her toys. She knows sit, stay and down. Due to some destructiveness in the home, she is available to a Level 3 adopter.

She likes bath time and playing with her toys. She knows sit, stay and down. Due to some destructiveness in the home, she is available to a Level 3 adopter.

242675.name: Ace
242675.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ace is at risk due to behavior concerns. In the Care Centers, Ace is highly fearful and can be difficult to remove from his kennel. Staff often need to use multiple high-value treats to encourage him to approach the front of the kennel so they can place their slip lead on him. He has been observed snarling on one occasion and thrashing while on leash. Although Ace readily accepts treats, he does not actively seek attention and prefers limited interaction, though he will tolerate gentle petting. Medically, Ace is on treatment for CIRDC.

Ace came into the care center due to his owner not having time for him anymore, and due to his large size and they are expecting a child. The prior owners say Ace is a big, energetic lovebug! He is social and affectionate, and is vocal about telling you he wants to play. In the home Ace can be found where the people are, asking for love and playtime. The things he loves most are rubs and cuddles! In the care center Ace has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes:  Ace 💙 this shy guy won my whole heart, and I hope he wins yours too. The softness in his eyes as he delivers his paw into our palms, licks peanut butter from a cup, or just watches us as we get to know one another melts me. Once upon a time Ace lived with parents and a cat. Changing circumstances led them to surrender him, and now Ace, who once had a home and family, calls the shelter his home - and he doesn't like it. As I look at a handful of photos from his original home, I can't blame him one bit.

Ace's guardian said he is a Labrador x Doberman who lived well with a cat, is an energetic lovebug, and loves rubs and cuddles. We don't see any of that in the shelter, but it's easy to believe it's just behind there, and that with some decompression in a home he will be right back to cuddling and playing like the young dog he is.

242683.name: Clove
242683.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! 

Meet Clove!
Clove arrived to us as a stray with no ID. He's a sensitive, shy sweetheart who prefers to take his time connecting - he often approaches on his own terms and enjoys coming for pets when he feels ready. Clove is thoughtful and steady, and he's participating in our Shelter Scholars mat work program to help him decompress and build confidence in busy or new settings.

My Ideal Home
A calm, predictable adult-only home where a patient adopter can continue confidence-building work with slow, gentle handling. Clove does best with predictable routines, gentle enrichment, and gradual introductions to new people and situations. Training that focuses on cooperative care, impulse control, and loose-leash skills (and use of appropriate equipment like a front‑clip harness) will help him thrive.

Good with Kids?
No - Clove would do best in a home with only adults. He can be fearful and has nipped when frightened, so we recommend no children (under 13) while he continues to build confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Unknown history with household pets. In shelter assessments he has ignored dogs in crates and remained calm during some introductions, though he can hold a tense frame during new encounters. Slow, controlled, supervised introductions are recommended and may help him feel comfortable around other dogs.

Leash Manners
Clove can be strong on leash and is known to mouth or leash-bite at times. He would benefit from loose-leash training, impulse-control exercises, and redirection with high-value treats or toys. Techniques like stop-and-go, direction changes, and a front‑clip harness will be useful while his handler builds engagement and focus.

Overall Health
Healthy overall; neutered and microchipped, and receiving routine veterinary care while in our care.

Behavior Determination
Experienced Adopters - Clove is sensitive and can show fearful or anxious reactions when stressed. He needs an adopter who understands fear-based behavior, can move slowly, avoid sudden approaches, and follow a behavior plan that includes desensitization, enrichment, and cooperative handling. This approach will help reduce anxiety and build his confidence over time.

Other Fun Facts
Clove is soft-bodied and affectionate once he trusts you - he often leans into gentle touch and takes treats nicely. He enjoys mat work to settle his body and mind, and he can be playful with toys (he sometimes grabs a toy and keeps it). Because he prefers to call the shots, many of his best moments come when you let him come to you for attention. His adoption fee has been reduced to help him find the home he deserves.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Clove was a super silly and sweet boy! Clove was happy to lay on the couch and nap for a few hours. He was cuddly and loved getting pets. After some rest he was ready to play and got a burst of energy, he loved chewing his toy and playing tug! Clove was also excited to go on a long walk - he pulled on the leash and was intrigued but dogs and squirrels, but didn't bark or react to people. Clove was a great fun affectionate boy!!

My foster writes: Clove is so ready to be a full time loyal, dedicated companion!
As a five year old gent he is in that sweet spot of calm shadow buddy around the house but has energetic puppy bursts at playtime! He also loves attention but not needy and can go full couch potato after a long walk!
Easy breezy on the leash while walking, can go long distance without issue and still curious when out & about, he even checks in with you for a pet while on longer walks!
He's so silent around the apartment; the only noises you hear are of him readjusting his lying down position!
Friendly to new people; open to petting saying hi!
Clove's personality is really engaged & enthusiastic while being chill the majority of the time; he can really match the energy of the room so I could see him being suited to a variety of different types of house holds.
Despite being in the shelter long term he is so bright, interested and full of affection.
Clove will bring so much to a home and make someone fantastically happy as you companion.

242794.name: Otis
242794.summary:
Meet Otis!
Otis came to ACC after his owner sadly passed away, and he's been adjusting to all the sudden changes in his world. Despite feeling unsure, he's shown a gentle, tolerant nature - allowing handling, leaning in for pets once he feels safe, and slowly exploring his surroundings. Otis is a sensitive, soft-spoken cat who just needs a quiet moment and a calm presence to let his sweetness show.

My foster writes:
Otis is very friendly once familiar with the person. He is very talkative and active cat! He love to follow people around. He is suitable in a home that someone can be with him for long extended periods of time and a lot of playtime and stimulation.

My Ideal Home
Otis will thrive in a patient, cat-experienced home where introductions are slow and predictable. He may start out timid, but with consistency and gentle encouragement, he warms up and accepts affection beautifully. Offering him cozy hiding spots and time to decompress will help him settle into a new routine and feel secure.

Good with Kids?
Older, respectful children may be okay, but Otis is easily startled and would do best in a calm home. Young children may overwhelm him.

Good with Other Pets?
His history with other pets is unknown. Based on his shy, gentle nature, he may do best as the only cat or with a calm, well-mannered feline companion introduced very slowly.

Overall Health
Otis is generally healthy. He is being treated for ear mites and has a healed corneal scar in one eye that does not require intervention. Otherwise, he is stable and doing well in care.

Behavior Determination
Experienced Adopters Preferred - Level 2. Otis tolerates petting and handling but is nervous with sudden movements and will need time to build trust. Adopters should be comfortable supporting a shy cat during his adjustment period.

Other Fun Facts
Otis has a quiet, observant personality and enjoys gentle head rubs once he feels safe. He gives little "thank you tail lifts" as he warms up, and his sweet, thoughtful nature shines through during calm one-on-one interactions. With patience, he'll become a loyal, comforting presence in his new home.

242852.name: Treble
242852.summary:
Meet Treble!
Treble was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and is now looking for a new home where his sweet, affectionate personality can shine. He is described by his previous owner as friendly, cuddly, and very people oriented. At home, he enjoyed being a couch companion, spending time near his people, and showing off his gentle, easygoing side. He knows cues like come here and sit, enjoys meat treats, and has a history of being crate-trained and comfortable with grooming, including baths and nail trims.

My Ideal Home
Treble will do best in a calm, structured adult home that can continue reinforcing his manners and provide clear guidance in higher arousal situations. He thrives in environments where he can be close to his people, relax, and enjoy predictable routines with consistent outlets for enrichment and exercise.

Good with Other Pets?
Treble has shown mixed behavior around other dogs. He may be social and playful with familiar dogs, but can bark, become overly excited, or show intense interest in unfamiliar dogs, including marked arousal during greetings. He is also noted to have a history of lunging at cats, so a home without cats is recommended. Any dog introductions should be slow, structured, and closely supervised.

Good with Kids?
Treble's behavior in care and his history of arousal around other animals suggest he would do best in an adult-only home at this time to help set him up for success.

Things to Know
Treble is a loving, food motivated dog who enjoys attention and staying close to his people. While he walks nicely on leash once out, he can be avoidant when first being leashed and may attempt to flee the kennel. He is social and vocal, sometimes barking at other dogs. He'll succeed with structure, calm guidance, and positive reinforcement.

Fun Fact
Treble's favorite "key" in life is simple, people, couch time, and cuddles. Once he's comfortable, he really hits the right note as a loyal little shadow who just wants to be where his person is.

242958.name: Callie
242958.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Callie is on the at-risk list due to medical and behavior concerns. Callie has had intermittent diarrhea, vomiting, and decreased appetite while in our care. It has been determined that Callie has infiltrative bowel disease, but the underlying cause is unknown at this time. Callie will need follow up diagnostics with an outside veterinarian to help determine the cause of her bowel disease, and will likely need medication long term to manage it. Callie has allowed all handling during their exams and did well in her previous foster home in terms of her behavior, however, she is shut down in the shelter environment. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

My foster writes: Callie is one of the sweetest cats we've had the pleasure of caring for. We as fosters are always saying that she is going to be some lucky person's BEST friend. She loves attention from her favorite humans so much; she loves to cuddle, get pets and forehead kisses, and have little conversations (she has a very cute and funny range of meows!)
Her purr is so quiet but you will definitely feel it while she relaxes in your lap for hours each day. When she's happy or excited, her tail puffs up. She loves churu treats and playing with wand toys too, but not nearly as much as she loves just hanging out with you on your lap or as a neat little loaf nearby.
She is shy at first and sensitive, but she always pushes herself out of her comfort zone to show and receive affection. It's very heartwarming! At first she was ALWAYS in my lap but as she's gotten more confident she's been exploring our apartment and wanting to play more (that being said, she still wants to sit in my lap for hours each day!)
She's also fine with getting her nails trimmed, which is great, because she loves to make powerful grippy biscuits on whatever surface she's blissing out on, including your lap.
She would be a fantastic cat for someone seeking a little best friend who will give your love back to you tenfold. Reach out to learn more about this special girl!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

243059.name: Meloni
243059.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Meloni is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Meloni was returned to the shelter due to anxiety-related behaviors, including destructiveness and house-soiling when left alone. Her owner also reported that she would hard bark at other dogs. In the Care Centers, Meloni has displayed fearful behavior, particularly during walks. She has been observed with a tucked tail, pinned ears, a tense body posture, and heightened vigilance. On one occasion, she sought refuge by hiding under a desk. With staff, she has warmed up slowly, accepting gentle pets, and treats. According to her owner, Meloni enjoys playing fetch with her family and likes stuffed toys. Medically, Meloni is currently healthy.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

243160.name: Mistletoe
243160.summary:
When we first received Mistletoe, she was a wee bit 3 month old baby. She was incredibly soft like fluffy cotton, shy, and easily startled. We quickly adjusted her peeing habits into the litter but she was a poop machine for the most part. With much love, affection, snacks, and play, she slowly began to grow into a confident young lady. Her litter habits are impeccably confined only to her litter box. She's very particular about where and how to have her hay and just wild about her daily salad. She is the most affectionate bunny we've fostered, gives you many, many, many kisses, and will circle you for a half hour to tell you she loves you. She's the only foster we let free roam because she's so well behaved. Her fur is softer than ever and she loves pets and brushes from everyone. 9pm is her bed time and she will go back into the cage until the next morning. She's quiet as a mouse at night, and when she gets out, she popcorns all over the place, then will run up to whoever opened up the cage to say, "good morning!"


Her personality is hilarious, we believe she knows she's funny and acts like a dog most of the time. She loves attention and will come get it from you. She will chase her snack ball in circles or chew her sticks in content.


This is the first time we've thought about adopting a foster, but we did such a great job, we feel like it's time for her to find a forever family who deserves such a funny, smart, sweet sweet girl.


When we say she's smart, we mean it. If the cage door did not have a second latch, she would get herself out because she observed how the lock works and actually pulled it up a few times.


We are very satisfied with the job we've done fostering and training her and it's time for us to get a new foster.


So if you want a fully trained sweetheart of a girl, Mistletoe is for you. She's still a baby, a really well fed baby.

243276.name: Sundae
243276.summary:
My foster writes: Hello, I'm Sundae! If you appreciate understated beauty and quiet companionship, we might be a perfect match.
I'm a beautiful, gentle cat with a very serene personality. I form connections in my own unique way: I enjoy sharing a space with you peacefully and keeping a soft, watchful eye on things from a comfortable spot. I'm still learning to trust fully, so I can be shy and prefer to observe from a distance that feels safe for me. I'm not yet comfortable being held or petted frequently.

243364.name: Jefe
243364.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
Jefe is truly the best boy around! How this handsome and lovable guy has not been adopted yet blows my mind. With his big, sweet eyes, he'll steal your heart instantly and shower you with snuggles and love. He does great staying home alone during the day and gets so excited to greet you when you walk through the door. Jefe is well-behaved, house-trained, and an all-around wonderful companion. He does not bark and is a lovely house guest. He can be a little nervous at first, but with a bit of patience and love, he quickly opens up and becomes part of the family. Once he feels comfortable, his affectionate and loyal personality really shines. Jefe is warming up to the outdoors because its a little scary for him. He is looking for a loving family and will fill your heart!

Meet Jefe!
Jefe arrived as an owner surrender to the Manhattan Animal Care Center on December 22, 2025. He is a friendly, attentive companion who is looking for a calm, patient person to help him settle into a new routine. Staff describe him as having some behavior challenges to work through, but he quickly shows that he wants to connect and learn when given consistent, gentle guidance.

My Ideal Home
Jefe will thrive in a quiet, predictable home with a patient adopter who can provide daily interaction and consistent training. He does best without other animals in the household and would do well in a single-adult home where he can get focused attention while he adjusts to life outside the shelter.

Good with Kids?
No - Jefe was surrendered for not being good with kids, so he should be placed in a home without children. He does best with experienced adults who understand his needs and boundaries.

Good with Other Pets?
No - Jefe needs a home with no other dogs, and he should not live with cats or small animals. Staff observations indicate he does not do well in multi-pet homes.

Leash Manners
Jefe is making progress but will need ongoing training and practice on leash. He benefits from a calm handler and clear, consistent cues; patience and positive reinforcement will help him become more comfortable and confident on walks.

Overall Health
Healthy overall and neutered. He is receiving routine care at the shelter and is comfortable now that he's been settled in.

Behavior Determination
Experienced Adopters - Jefe has some behavior needs that staff will discuss with you. He's best suited to someone prepared to work patiently with him, follow shelter guidance, and provide consistent structure and training.

Other Fun Facts
Jefe loves interaction and responds well to calm, consistent attention. He enjoys spending time close to his people and will do best in a home where he gets regular companionship and gentle, positive training to build his confidence.

243366.name: Mufasa
243366.summary:
Mufasa tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: For all the cats who make settling into the shelter look effortless, there are others like Mufasa who wear the effort it takes them all over their faces. Mufasa puts real work into each day he spends at the shelter and rightfully so as he knows it will bring him one step closer to finding his forever family. Greeting people at the front of his condo and coming as forward as he can when people are in Adoptions, Mufasa isn't entirely sure what he should do next. I can practically see the ideas floating across his mind - should he allow pets, try to look out the window, or maybe even try to hop out of his condo? We know that Mufasa tends to prefer contact on his own terms when it comes to children, cats, and strangers, but can be a friendly, cheerful, and curious guy when given the chance.  
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

243383.name: Adam
243383.summary:
My foster writes: Adam is a quiet cat who enjoys spending most of his time lounging and will come over for pets when he feels comfortable. He likes to observe his surroundings and often watches what is going on around him while keeping some distance. Loud sounds and bright lights can startle him, and he may hide at first, but he usually relaxes again after some time.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
Adam tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

243404.name: Blue Bonnet
243404.summary:
My foster writes:
Blue Bonnet is a sweet, playful cat who loves to chase his toys, snooze, and spend time with his human companions. Equally happy chasing crinkle balls, long strings, or his own tail, he is a delight to watch when he's in an energetic and excitable mood! Blue Bonnet doesn't enjoy sitting in laps right now, but he does like to curl up like a shrimp to keep me company on the couch or under my desk while I'm working. He has a charming personality that he expresses through funny stretches, little chirps, and many sweet and gentle headbutts. It takes him time to get used to new people, but it's well worth the wait!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

243412.name: Silk Siren
243412.summary:
My adoption fee has been sponsored by my previous foster parent! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Silk Siren is a smart and sweet girl who would love to live in a quiet home with an active family. She absolutely loves walking -- and will get you to 10k steps in no time! She is past her adolescent phase, so she is fine to chill out with you while you work, and will let you know when she needs to go out. She is housetrained, know basic commands like sit, down and paw, and is eager to learn more. She has a big fluffy fox tail and loves butt scratches. She is highly trainable and loves routine, so I can see her doing really well with someone dedicated to consistent training.

Things Silky (Silk Siren) loves, in no particular order: Bedtime, Broccoli and Apples, Walks, TV Time (cuddled with us on the couch), Sniffing Other Dogs, Watching Us Cook. Hold on tight to the leash if she spots a squirrel. She is a sweetheart!

My foster writes: Silk Siren, who we call Silky, is a bundle of sweetness and energy. She wants to be around us all the time, whether we are going out for a walk or watching TV. She must have had a nice home at some point, because she is well trained with "sit" and "down" and "heal." We tell her it's bedtime, and she rushes and jumps on the bed, curls up, and stays with us all night. Being left alone makes her anxious. She barks and howls, but we are working on that with her and with some training, we think she'll be fine. With a little patience, she will be a great addition to someone's home.

My previous foster writes:
If you want the sweetest dog on earth, you've come to the right girl. Silk Siren (or Silky), is a pup that is full of love. She loves to go on walks, and she'll make sure you know it. She's still working on some leash manners (we're working on getting her to ignore squirrels), but other than that she is a great walking buddy. When she is not on a walk, she usually takes on of two forms: curled into a ball or staring at you for food. She loves her people and sometimes has a hard time leaving their side, she just wants to be part of the fun! She is able to be left at home alone for a bit, but it makes her a bit anxious. Don't worry, because she would never even consider being destructive. If you have a heart that is ready to be stolen, look no further than Silky!

My previous foster writes: Meet Miss Silly (aka Silk Siren!) 💖
Looking for a joyful, wiggly, professionally cuddly best friend? Miss Silly is your girl! This happy pup lives up to her name-when she's not trotting along on a sniff-filled walk, she's expertly folding herself into the nearest pile of pillows and blankets in the most impressively silly positions. Walks are one of her favorite things, especially when there are exciting new scents to investigate! She's also very treat-motivated and lights up for pattern games, enrichment toys, and anything she can proudly carry around in her paws.
If you're searching for a sweet, playful, affectionate pup who will keep you smiling and never let you feel lonely, Silly is ready to curl up right next to you and steal your heart.

243448.name: Freybug
243448.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Freybug is at risk due to behavior concerns. Freybug is a social dog who enjoys affection and treats. Unfortunately, he is having difficulty adjusting to the shelter environment. He has been observed repeatedly jumping, chewing on his kennel walls, and hypersalivating while in his kennel, despite receiving daily enrichment and socialization. Medically, Freybug has dental disease and a wound.

Meet Freybug!
Freybug was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and is now looking for a fresh start. He is a social, energetic boy who approaches readily and enjoys attention from people. He leans in for pets, explores his environment confidently, and shows a playful side once he is comfortable, though he can become very aroused and excitable in new situations.

My Ideal Home
Freybug will do best in an adult only home that can provide structure, consistency, and ongoing support for impulse control. He needs a calm, predictable environment and a family committed to positive reinforcement training to help him channel his enthusiasm in a productive way.

Good with Other Pets?
Freybug has shown mixed responses to other dogs, including tense body language and forward, reactive behavior when on leash. Because of this, he is recommended as the only pet in the home and should not visit dog parks. He will need continued work on leash reactivity and controlled, structured environments.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to high arousal, poor impulse control, and leash reactivity observed in care.

Things to Know
Freybug is a playful, food motivated dog who enjoys interaction but can struggle to settle once excited. He may jump up on handlers, explore counters and doors when stimulated, and becomes very aroused during activity. He responds best to high value rewards like spray cheese and benefits from clear structure, consistent training, and enrichment to help manage his energy.

Fun Fact
Freybug is one of those dogs who is always "on the move," and when he's happy, he really shows it. Think of him as a little bug of enthusiasm who just needs the right garden to help him grow into his best self.

243470.name: Royalty
243470.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Meet Royalty (Ro)! An absolutely dream of a dog. Ro is big on snuggling but is also happy to spend her time sleeping away on her bed. She is fully potty trained and a pro at giving signals when she would like a trip outside. As an older pup she definitely enjoys her rest and sleeps completely through the night. Once she's up for the day she loves a walk around the neighborhood where she'll be asking for pets from strangers and sniffing along the buildings every step of the way. She spends most of her day resting but can always keep up on walks and loves the occasional game of tug a war! She loves to be apart of your day whether that's sitting at your feet while you work from home or laying near by as you catch up on a show. She's also always ready to cheer you up with as many kisses as you want!! She fits perfectly into your everyday routine, is such a happy dog, and is just glad to be along for the ride. If you are looking for the sweetest bestie, Ro is definitely your girl!!

My boroughbreaker writes: Royalty and I took a nice walk around the neighborhood and spent a little time sniffing around the park. While she's a little shy at first, she warms up, and let me handle her to put a little puffer coat on to keep her warm! She has so much energy for an 8-year-old pupper, I thought we might have a chill, cozy day to nap, but she really wanted to explore and go for a much more rigorous walk than I thought she would have preferred! She is an absolute dream to walk, no pulling, lots of sniffs, stops at the corner, and walks at your side. She's a little nervous about larger dogs, but otherwise was unbothered by anything or anyone else. We did spend a little time inside - after she thoroughly examined the apartment, she enjoyed some chew time on the big bully sticks. She does not like squeakers! Or snuffle toys (why would you hide her treats???), but if you give her something tasty and sturdy to chew on she'll settle for a bit.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

243518.name: Marley
243518.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Cutest big baby boi with the best manner. So well-behaved! So loving! Cuddle on four legs with the cutest squishy face. Meet him today to squeeze that face :)))

My foster writes: This sweet pup is basically a walking cuddle with four legs. Always gentle, always well-mannered, and always ready to love, he follows the rules like a pro and steal hearts without even trying. Whether it's a soft nuzzle, a wagging tail, or calmly sitting by your side, this dog's superpower is spreading warmth and happiness everywhere they go. Truly the goodest, snuggliest soul around.

Meet Marley!
Marley was found roaming the streets and brought to us by police officers, who described him as friendly and easygoing on arrival. He's a social, affectionate boy who seeks out human attention and enjoys pets and snuggles. Shelter life has been a big adjustment, and while he's enthusiastic and wiggly, he's also gentle and eager to connect with people who give him a little guidance.

My Ideal Home
Marley would do best with an adopter who enjoys an active routine and is excited to help him build some basic manners. He's still learning how to channel his enthusiasm, so consistency, positive-reinforcement training, and daily mental and physical enrichment will help him thrive. A calm, structured environment will support his continued progress as he gains confidence and strength.

Good with Other Pets?
Marley has limited history with other animals. In the shelter, he has shown difficulty during close dog greetings and may react strongly at first. He may do best as the only dog, or with slow, carefully managed introductions guided by an experienced adopter or trainer.

Leash Manners
Walks with moderate pulling and lots of curiosity. He benefits from guidance, treats, and practice to help him stay focused and polite while out and about.

Overall Health
Arrived significantly underweight and is currently on a refeeding plan. Otherwise healthy and expected to continue improving with proper nutrition and care.

Behavior Determination
Level 3. Marley is friendly and social but lacks basic manners and impulse control. He will benefit from training focused on calm greetings, attention, and basic cues using force-free, reward-based methods.

Other Fun Facts
• Big fan of snuggles and human attention
• Highly social and loves being near his people

243518.summaryHtml:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! My foster writes: Cutest big baby boi with the best manner. So well-behaved! So loving! Cuddle on four legs with the cutest squishy face. Meet him today to squeeze that face :))) My foster writes: This sweet pup is basically a walking cuddle with four legs. Always gentle, always well-mannered, and always ready to love, he follows the rules like a pro and steal hearts without even trying. Whether it's a soft nuzzle, a wagging tail, or calmly sitting by your side, this dog's superpower is spreading warmth and happiness everywhere they go. Truly the goodest, snuggliest soul around. Meet Marley!
Marley was found roaming the streets and brought to us by police officers, who described him as friendly and easygoing on arrival. He's a social, affectionate boy who seeks out human attention and enjoys pets and snuggles. Shelter life has been a big adjustment, and while he's enthusiastic and wiggly, he's also gentle and eager to connect with people who give him a little guidance.

My Ideal Home
Marley would do best with an adopter who enjoys an active routine and is excited to help him build some basic manners. He's still learning how to channel his enthusiasm, so consistency, positive-reinforcement training, and daily mental and physical enrichment will help him thrive. A calm, structured environment will support his continued progress as he gains confidence and strength.

Good with Other Pets?
Marley has limited history with other animals. In the shelter, he has shown difficulty during close dog greetings and may react strongly at first. He may do best as the only dog, or with slow, carefully managed introductions guided by an experienced adopter or trainer.

Leash Manners
Walks with moderate pulling and lots of curiosity. He benefits from guidance, treats, and practice to help him stay focused and polite while out and about.

Overall Health
Arrived significantly underweight and is currently on a refeeding plan. Otherwise healthy and expected to continue improving with proper nutrition and care.

Behavior Determination
Level 3. Marley is friendly and social but lacks basic manners and impulse control. He will benefit from training focused on calm greetings, attention, and basic cues using force-free, reward-based methods.

Other Fun Facts
• Big fan of snuggles and human attention
• Highly social and loves being near his people
• Enjoys toys and treats and is motivated to learn
• Ready for a fresh start with someone who'll help him shine Marley is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is working hard to become a calmer, more confident pup on the leash.

243526.name: Rollie
243526.summary:
My foster writes: Rollie is a spirited, healthy bunny who started exploring from the minute she first arrived. She has not once hidden from anyone. Rollie is incredibly brave and curious, happily exploring and asking for treats. Rollie is well-adjusted to household noises, including occasional dog barks. She is an enthusiastic eater who will run around her enclosure when she hears the sound of her pellet bag opening or sees her greens. She is also intelligent and loves staying busy by figuring out new, creative ways to forage for her food. Once you meet her, you won't be able to resist how cute she is, and her incredibly soft coat.

My other foster writes: Rollie is an adventurous, curious bunny who wants to be part of everything you're doing. Whether she's hopping room to room, checking out every corner of the house, or lounging nearby while you work, she approaches life with confidence and charm.
One of her most special qualities is how calm and comfortable she is around other animals. She currently lives peacefully with two cats and two dogs and handles their presence like a pro. She's confident without being demanding and loves having the freedom to explore alongside her furry housemates.
Despite her independent spirit, she also has a very sweet and affectionate side. Offer her a snack and she'll happily climb into your lap to sit with you while she munches away. She's the perfect mix of curious adventurer and calm companion.
She would thrive in a home that will let her roam, explore, and be included as part of the family.

My foster writes: Rollie is a shy girl who just needs a little time to blossom. Once she feels safe, she absolutely melts for pets and quickly turns into a snuggly cuddle bunny. She has good litter box habits and is a smart little explorer. She already knows exactly where the fridge is and will hop over whenever the fridge door is open hoping for her favorite treats like celery, tomatoes and bananas. During playtime, Rollie shows her happy side with adorable binkies that will instantly make you smile.

Meet Rollie!
Rollie is a stunning young rabbit who was found abandoned and brought into our care. While the shelter environment has been overwhelming at times, Rollie has shown herself to be a gentle, sweet soul with a calm demeanor and absolutely magnificent ears. With a little patience and the right environment, she has so much potential to blossom.

My Ideal Home
Rollie would do best in a calm, quiet home that can give her time to feel safe and build confidence. She enjoys having space to hop, zoom, and explore, and then happily settles in for pets once she feels comfortable. She prefers interacting on her own terms and does not enjoy being picked up, so a home that respects rabbit boundaries and allows her to engage at floor level will help her thrive.

Good with Kids?
Rollie may do well with older, respectful children who understand that rabbits are prey animals and don't always like to be handled. A quieter household would be ideal for her sensitive nature.

Good with Other Pets?
Rollie has shown no signs of aggression and may be a good candidate for bonding with another calm rabbit with proper introductions. Her gentle personality suggests she could enjoy a companion once she's settled.

Overall Health
Rollie is healthy overall and has been treated preventatively for parasites. She has maintained a good appetite and normal activity levels in care, with no ongoing medical concerns noted at this time.

Behavior Determination
Level 1 - Rollie is a gentle rabbit suitable for adopters of any experience level who can provide a calm environment, patience, and appropriate rabbit enrichment.

Other Fun Facts
Rollie is known as a "gentle giant" who loves to binky and zoom before immediately pancaking for pets. Her ears are truly spectacular, and once she trusts you, she melts into affection. With a peaceful home and a little time, Rollie is ready to show just how special she is.


A volunteer writes: I found Rollie easy to handle. She was active in the pen running through the tunnel, hopping all around with lots of energy. Did I just see her do a binky? Yes I did. She was chinning and scoping all around. She came on my lap, enjoying my  pets. She appreciated my company and I loved hers. Come check out this sweet girl.

243561.name: Hercules
243561.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
I'm a super snuggly pup who loves nothing more than being close to my favorite humans. I'm very food motivated (treats are definitely the way to my heart!), which can make training a fun and rewarding experience for both of us.
I'll be honest, I sometimes have accidents and I'm not a fan of being alone, so I'll need a patient, understanding home that can help me continue learning and building confidence. I do best as the only pet, since I'm reactive around other dogs and I'm not comfortable with cats or other animals. Right now, it's unknown how I do with children, so a calmer household may be the best fit while we figure that out. What I really need is someone with a big heart and lots of patience who's willing to help me grow at my own pace. In return, I promise endless snuggles, loyalty, and love. 💛

Meet Hercules!
Hercules came to us as an owner surrender after his family member became unable to care for him. This young, energetic pup may be small in stature, but he has a big personality and a lot of curiosity about the world around him. In the shelter, Hercules can feel overwhelmed at first, but once he settles in, he enjoys walks, treats, and spending time with people he trusts.

My Ideal Home
Hercules would thrive in a calm, adult-only home with an experienced adopter who understands fearful or sensitive dogs. He benefits from routine, patience, and positive reinforcement to help him build confidence and feel secure. A home that can provide daily mental and physical enrichment will help him channel his energy in a healthy way.

Good with Kids?
No. Due to his sensitivity and mouthiness with treats, Hercules is best suited for a home without children.

Good with Other Pets?
Hercules has lived with another dog in the past, but he can be reactive toward unfamiliar dogs, especially on leash. Slow, thoughtful introductions and guidance from an experienced handler will be important if there are other pets in the home.

Leash Manners
Hercules can walk nicely and enjoys sniffing along the way, though he may pull at times and react to dogs or busy surroundings. He does best with steady handling, distance from triggers, and reward-based training to help him stay focused and calm.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Hercules needs an experienced, adult-only home that can support him as he works through fear-based behaviors and builds confidence using force-free training.

Other Fun Facts
Hercules enjoys exploring on walks, accepts treats eagerly (sometimes a little too eagerly!), and has shown that with patience and consistency, he can relax and show his sweet side.

243589.name: Surf
243589.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced!

My foster writes: When Surf first walked into our apartment and seemed to recognize that he was back in a home environment, he picked up his toy and shook it furiously with delight. That moment was classic Surf -- his default reactions are joy and play. This is such a sweet, very good boy who is eager to please and will take his cues from you. If you're relaxing, expect him to rest his head on your lap. Going on a walk? He'd love nothing more than to tag along, wagging his tail the entire time. Surf knows how to sit, give you his paw and lay down on command, and he's well (but not perfectly) house-trained. He's still working on his manners while walking on leash and greeting new humans -- his excitement can be hard to contain! However, he's polite and waits to be invited before hopping on a couch or bed, listens promptly when he's told no, takes treats gently from human hands, and overall does his best.

Surf isn't much of a barker. He whines softly once or twice when his humans leave, but otherwise is happy-go-lucky. He's exuberant but gentle with children and appears to yearn for interactions with other dogs. He's brought so much fun, zest and laughter into our lives and will surely be a devoted, entertaining and loving addition to his forever home.

244039.summary:

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.

I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

244129.name: Bueller
244129.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bueller is at risk due to behavioral reasons. With familiar handlers, Bueller has been observed to have a loose and wiggly body. However, he has shown a pattern of hard barking and baring teeth when unfamiliar handlers approach him while in kennel. While on leash, recently Bueller has been noted to hard bark, fixate, and lunge towards other people even when the handler created distance. Medically, Bueller is apparently healthy.

My Borough Breaker writes:
We had a lovely, relaxed day off with Bueller. His favorite things were
sniffing, snacking, leaning in, and napping. Bueller got into the car like a pro, and once the car rolled, he laid down and took a nap. Bueller would probably love a home where he can get his relaxed sniffing
and exploring time, learn some new things that get him snacks, and enjoy
structure and cuddly downtime.

So, life moves pretty fast. If you don't stop and look around once in a
while, you could miss Bueller.


Meet Bueller!

My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Bueller arrived as a stray with no known history, so his past is a bit of a mystery. He's curious but cautious - he appreciates slow, gentle introductions to new people and places and really shines when given space and patience. Bueller loves attention, but on his own terms, and he's ready to work on training with someone who can read his cues and help him feel confident.

My Ideal Home
Bueller will do best in a home where his person has time for consistent, positive training and can offer predictable routines. A calm, patient household that can provide slow introductions to new people and situations will help him thrive. Because he can be particular about his things, a home where he can have his own safe space and belongings is ideal.

Good with Other Pets?
Bueller has shown that he doesn't always like to share food, toys, or bedding, so he may do best as the only pet or in a home with very carefully managed, gradual introductions and supervision. Household-by-household meet-and-greets and a slow, structured introduction plan would be important.

Leash Manners
Bueller is ready to learn leash skills and would benefit from continued practice and positive reinforcement. He may be uncertain in new environments at first, so short, calm walks and a patient handler will help build his confidence and walking manners.

Overall Health
Healthy overall. He arrived safe at the shelter and is comfortable while he continues to settle in. Routine veterinary care and standard preventive care will be needed as recommended by your veterinarian.

Behavior Determination
Experienced Adopters / Patient Trainers - Bueller would benefit from someone with experience reading canine body language, working through resource-guarding tendencies, and providing consistent, positive training. He's eager to learn but needs a calm, confident handler to help him succeed.

Other Fun Facts
Bueller is a sweet, affectionate dog once he feels safe - he loves attention when he's ready for it and responds well to gentle encouragement. He's curious about the world and shows real potential with training and structure. If you're looking for a loyal companion who will blossom with patience and love, Bueller could be a great match.

A Volunteer Wrote: He's gorgeous! He's charming! He's affectionate! And he needs more stimulation and a chance to stretch his legs than this over-crowded shelter can provide. I found a staff member talking baby talk to him; it took all of three seconds to join in because he has such a dear heart, and he wears his good looks with a hint of goofiness.

Bueller's shelter behavior is very different to how he is out on the streets of New York City. He is an angel on the leash, not pulling too hard. He pulls mildy/moderately when he sees a doggy friend because he would love to say hi. Otherwise, he is content sniff the street and checking his pee mails. He knows some trikcs and is willing to work for treats. He is extremely laid back and will happy accept back pets from all that he bonds with. On our walk, he foun a nice dead end with some ind and just sat on the street to enjoy it. I sat with him and he promptly rolled over onto my legs for some belly scratches and to live in the moment. Bueller is a sweetheart and wants to love you as much as you love him.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Bueller is a strong sweet boy . His size is intimidating at first but he snuggles on the couch like a champ . He rolls over for belly rubs and scratches all the time . He loves to sniff and walk , knows sit , and loves his treats . This 60lb derp didn't want to leave my side .

This poor guy needs to be out of the loud crazy shelter and on someone's couch ASAP ! Once he got the lay of my apartment, he just wanted to snuggle on the couch and take a nap . He's been through a lot and Bueller would make a great pet . He's a strong boy who is treat and food motivated but was never reactive on leash and is potty trained and knows "sit " .
Let's adopt Bueller !

244252.name: Chai
244252.summary:
Meet Chai!
Chai is a happy, playful pittie whose whole body starts wagging the moment she sees her favorite people. She loves attention and will happily lean in for pets, cuddles, scratches, or even try to climb into your lap if you'll let her. Smart, treat-motivated, and eager to learn, Chai enjoys training just as much as she enjoys spending time with her humans. She's looking for someone who will be patient, understand that she can feel anxious around other dogs, and help her build confidence because she's absolutely worth it.

My Ideal Home
Chai would thrive with an experienced adopter who can provide structure, consistency, and plenty of positive reinforcement. She has lots of energy and will enjoy daily exercise, enrichment, and opportunities to continue learning new skills. A fenced yard would be a bonus, but most of all she's looking for someone committed to helping her succeed.

Good with Other Pets?
Chai has shown interest in other dogs but can be anxious and reactive while on leash. Slow, thoughtful introductions will be important if she'll be living with another dog. Her history with other pets is unknown.

Good with Kids?
Chai would do best with older, dog-savvy children (around 12 and up) who can comfortably handle her enthusiastic personality and help reinforce her training.

Things to Know
Chai is healthy, spayed, and ready for her next adventure. She's still working on her leash manners and impulse control, but she's incredibly smart, food-motivated, and loves to learn. With patience, guidance, and lots of love, Chai has all the makings of an amazing lifelong companion.
