Chai is a happy, playful pittie whose whole body starts wagging the moment she sees her favorite people. She loves attention and will happily lean in for pets, cuddles, scratches, or even try to climb into your lap if you'll let her. Smart, treat-motivated, and eager to learn, Chai enjoys training just as much as she enjoys spending time with her humans. She's looking for someone who will be patient, understand that she can feel anxious around other dogs, and help her build confidence because she's absolutely worth it.

My Ideal Home
Chai would thrive with an experienced adopter who can provide structure, consistency, and plenty of positive reinforcement. She has lots of energy and will enjoy daily exercise, enrichment, and opportunities to continue learning new skills. A fenced yard would be a bonus, but most of all she's looking for someone committed to helping her succeed.

Good with Other Pets?
Chai has shown interest in other dogs but can be anxious and reactive while on leash. Slow, thoughtful introductions will be important if she'll be living with another dog. Her history with other pets is unknown.

Good with Kids?
Chai would do best with older, dog-savvy children (around 12 and up) who can comfortably handle her enthusiastic personality and help reinforce her training.

Things to Know
Chai is healthy, spayed, and ready for her next adventure. She's still working on her leash manners and impulse control, but she's incredibly smart, food-motivated, and loves to learn. With patience, guidance, and lots of love, Chai has all the makings of an amazing lifelong companion.

244296.name: Big Bubba
244296.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Big Bubba is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Big Bubba has been social with handlers in care after warming up, enjoys splashing in the pool, and playing with toys. Despite this, he has been displaying high levels of kennel stress, despite best efforts to keep him comfortable. He screeches and barks at other dogs when they pass his kennel, persistently jumping to the top of his kennel, causing him to hit his head, and crashing into his water bowl. Attempts to reduce visual stressors by covering his kennel have been attempted, but he tears them down. Medically, Big Bubba has alopecia.

Meet Big Bubba!
Big Bubba arrived as a stray on 12/30/25, and while his past is unknown, he's been steadily showing staff what a gentle, thoughtful boy he is as he recovered from some prior injuries. He's grateful for care, moves at his own pace, and is now hoping to find a calm forever home where he can truly settle in.

Personality
Big Bubba is a soft, polite boy who tends to keep a neutral, calm presence in the room. He often stays close to his handlers, sitting beside them and choosing quiet companionship over chaos. When he's comfortable, he gently accepts treats and offers sweet, subtle affection like lip licks and staying nearby.

Craves affection, leans into your legs for pets, and stretches his neck out for throat scratches. Absolutely loves the water! He happily hops into plastic pools to splash and play around. Rolls around on his back in the grass like a "funny little sea creature" when he is happy. Loves chasing tossed toys and will shred them with "utter glee" once he catches them.

Out and About
Big Bubba walks with a loose leash and generally explores at an easy, unhurried pace. He is more focused on sniffing and taking in his surroundings than reacting to distractions, making him a steady walking companion in calm environments.

Social Behavior
Big Bubba is neutral to social in new spaces and tends to stay near his people once he feels settled. He sits calmly for treats and accepts gentle handling, though he can be sensitive in certain areas, especially where he has had previous injuries.

Home Life
Big Bubba will do best in an adult only home that can respect his need for space, patience, and gentle handling. He's not a pushy dog and thrives when allowed to approach on his own terms and adjust at his own pace.

Things to Know
Big Bubba is recovering from prior wounds and has some sensitivity around handling, so a calm, understanding home is important for his continued healing and confidence building. He also benefits from slow introductions and a predictable environment.

Fun Fact
Big Bubba may be a quiet observer at first, but once he decides you're his person, he'll quietly choose your side and stick with you like a loyal little shadow.

244389.name: Benji
244389.summary:
Meet Benji, an adorable little stumpy-legged guy with a big personality and an even bigger heart! His owner describes him as loving, caring, very friendly, and absolutely full of energy. Benji loves spending time with his people and is always ready for fun, whether it's a game of tug-of-war or an exciting car ride-one of his favorite activities. He's a smart pup who already knows several commands, including sit, stay, lay down, and paw. With his sweet nature, playful spirit, and charming looks, Benji is sure to bring plenty of joy and laughter to his future family.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:

We had a great time with Benji on his first borough break! He jumped right into the car and seemed so happy watching the world go by. When we got out, he played out in the backyard for a bit but seemed happiest sitting on the porch just watching things. We took a long walk (probably close to 2 miles!) and by the end he was dragging haha. But he never pulled, never ate anything off the street, and never pulled toward people- he was perfect. When we got home, we thought we would sit on the couch with him and watch a movie but he got activated watching the talking sheep- it was very funny! All in all, Benji is a great dog!!

244525.name: Liberty
244525.summary:
Libby (nickname) has been my favorite foster. I've fallen in love with her - she's goofy, sweet, and deeply loving. She entertains me with her little routines, habits, and antics. She makes the funniest faces, and intuitively knows all the comfiest positions for long-lasting cuddles. She does great in a studio apartment and has been relatively easy to work from home with. I'd consider adopting her myself if I didn't have external plans coming. She deserves the best family who can bring out all her best sides (ideally with prior dog experience). Plus, she's a small girl with a puppy face - I constantly get asked if she's a puppy!

My foster writes: The sweetest girl looking for anyone who's willing to cuddle all hours of the day. She loves kicking her head back so you could scratch her tummy and loves looking and asking for affection in the cutest ways. She's a loyal & smart girl

Eager to cuddle couch potato who is sweet but silly and melts into your lap like she got jelly legs

My foster writes: This sweet girl is all love, she adores being close to her people and will happily curl up right next to you for snuggles. She's incredibly gentle, affectionate, and has the most adorable smile that lights up the room. If you're looking for a loyal companion who just wants to love and be loved, she's your girl.




My fee has been sponsored by a generous donor!

244531.name: Sun
244531.summary:
My foster writes: Sun is a soft and affectionate little guy who took a bit of time to come out of his shell. He was separated from his mom and grandma early on, so he started off pretty unsure of everything, but after some patience and time Sun showed his loving personality. Now he's really into the quiet, cozy life. He likes wand toys, but he's even more into curling up on a lap and just being near you. He's the kind of cat who keeps you company without asking for much, and shows his affection in a steady and gentle way.

A volunteer writes:
SUM is a 6-year-old neutered gentleman who arrived at the Manhattan Care Center alongside his companions Shadow and Mamacat when their owner was displaced. Though initially shy with strangers, SUM quickly warms up and reveals his truly affectionate nature-he adores cuddles, lap time, and being carried in loving arms. Sum was at first shy with me, hesitating to leave his den  but when he did after my coaxing, he really was a very sweet and loving kitty. This sweet boy is friendly and playful with other cats, making him a wonderful companion. While SUM may have a heart murmur, cardiac testing (proBNP) shows his heart is functioning well. With his gentle disposition and capacity for love, SUM is ready to bring joy and companionship to his forever family. Ask to meet him when you visit us at the care center!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I can go home today!

244552.name: Flint
244552.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Flint is an absolute sweetheart and joy to be around. He's a professional snoozer, looking for love between naps. Even though he's a senior, he's got a puppy-like energy when it comes to getting excited for walks. It's very clear he looks to please, and may just need a little patience when it comes to his loss of hearing and figuring out how to communicate with him.

My foster writes:
Meet Flint! (Flintstone for long)
Flint is a sweet, easygoing boy who's happiest when he's being pet or snoozing the day away. He loves affection and will always lean in for extra scratches and cuddles. When he's not soaking up love, Flint spends most of his day sleeping and relaxing, making him a wonderful match for a calm, laid-back home. He's friendly and loving to everyone he meets!
Flint is crate trained, house trained, and does great settling in on his own, which makes transitions and daily routines nice and easy. He's a low-key companion who would thrive with someone looking for a gentle, affectionate dog that fits seamlessly into your life.
If you're searching for a mellow best friend with a big heart and a talent for naps, Flint might be the perfect addition to your family.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

244560.name: Oreo
244560.summary:
Meet Oreo - a very round, very handsome, and extremely dapper black-and-white boy 🖤🤍
This delightfully plump gentleman is basically a walking cookie with legs, and he knows how to make an impression. Oreo is shy but curious, preferring a calm, quiet home where he can feel safe and comfortable showing off his soft side. He may take a little time to warm up, but his curiosity always peeks through, especially when his favorite people (or snacks) are nearby. Oreo happily accepts treats and absolutely loves playtime, where his round physique only adds to his charm. He would thrive with patient, kind adopters who understand that trust takes time and who will appreciate him for the lovable, rotund treasure he is. With a peaceful home and lots of gentle encouragement, Oreo is ready to roll his way right into your heart 💕

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

244591.name: Pee Wee
244591.summary:
My foster writes: If I didn't know that Pee-Wee was a mom, I would have thought she was a kitten herself! She's teeny tiny, as her name might suggest. And although she's very shy at first, she's super sweet and a careful, agile climber. She's quiet but she definitely has her playful time. And her fur is so, so soft! She loves pets and small, cozy spots.

After a few weeks, Pee Wee is not just sweet, but also super affectionate! She's a very easy kitty. She purrs and loves full-body pets, and she gets super excited for food! She has an excellent appetite for such a little girl. She came from a home with many cats and is currently in foster with her brother Eyes. They don't fight, but they're definitely territorial; Pee Wee spends most of her time in the bathroom (where she loves batting mice around in the tub). She might prefer to be a single kitty or find a home with another lower energy cat. She's looking forward to meeting her furever person!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

A volunteer writes: Pee Wee's approach to shelter life may be slightly unconventional and reliant on us seeing the potential that's there, but please believe me it is. Since she really makes a case for herself contrary to the generally held belief to not form relationships based on potential, it's impossible not to give her a chance. Snuggled up in the back of her cubby, Pee Wee crunched herself up against the wall to create space only to later stretch her neck into my hand. Well, let me back up a bit. Pee Wee was brought to us with her kittens (who have since been placed) from a home with many other cats. Shelter life has been a learning experience for her and, because no one really learns on an empty stomach, treats definitely help her to expand her thinking on possibilities. After a squeeze up treat, Pee Wee allowed me to pet her, albeit cautiously. She slowly slinked out of her cubby where we had been and into the main part, but mostly to poke her head back through and nuzzle around for some extra pets. Pee Wee's a fantastic girl who is really banking on someone seeing her potential and if she sounds like the girl for you, maybe come in and meet her?

244805.name: Tutor
244805.summary:
Meet Tutor!
Tutor is a wise and affectionate senior who is ready to start his next chapter. At 10 years old, he brings a nice mix of playful energy and relaxed companionship. He was surrendered when his previous owner could no longer care for him, and he is now looking for a patient, understanding home where he can feel safe and settled. Tutor is part of our Shelter Scholar program, where he is working on his leash manners and building confidence with each outing. He enjoys being close to his people, whether that means following you around or curling up in his crate for a cozy nap.

Personality
Tutor is social, affectionate, and still playful for his age. He enjoys attention but prefers it on his own terms. He can be sensitive to handling in certain areas, especially his paws. His previous owner said Tutor is also easily startled by loud noises such as storms or fireworks and may need extra support during those moments.

My Ideal Home
Tutor would thrive in a calm, adult-only home with someone who can give him time to decompress and build trust.  A predictable routine and a quiet environment will help him feel secure. Tutor is used to frequent walks and enjoys getting out multiple times a day, so an adopter who can meet his exercise needs is important.

Good with Other Pets?
Tutor should be the only pet in the home. A pet-free environment will help him feel most comfortable and secure.

Good with Kids?
Tutor would do best in an adult-only home. He may become uncomfortable with certain handling and will need a home where his space and boundaries are respected.

Things to Know
Tutor is crate trained and finds comfort resting in his crate. He enjoys car rides and already knows cues like sit and paw. He does pull strongly on leash but is actively working on improving this through his training. Tutor may become anxious when left alone and can be vocal when strangers approach the home. He will need support with grooming, as he is sensitive to paw handling. With patience and positive reinforcement, he is continuing to build confidence and trust every day.

Fun Fact
Tutor may be a senior, but he still has a playful side and a big appetite for both food and fun. He is ready to be your loyal study buddy for life.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Drove home to introduce Tutor to everyone in my family, including my 2 sisters and my parents. Then, after roaming around in the yard for a while, we took a trip to Petsmart! Of course, everyone there thought he was so handsome and sweet. Finally, we went back home to chill in the yard some more before taking a nice drive back to ACC to end our hangout. I think he likes car rides. He was always more eager to get in my car than go for a walk.

244836.name: Marble Cake
244836.summary:
My foster writes: This tortietude senior would like to spend the afternoon with you investigating new adventures.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Marble Cake was lying quietly in the den and accepted all petting on her head, cheek, and along her body while remaining quiet and slightly reserved. She sniffed treats but didn't eat them and continued to allow petting. She was calm during a partial pick-up and remained in place.

244953.name: Peanut
244953.summary:
My foster writes:
Lindsey is a sweet, gentle boy with a calm and lovable personality. He enjoys being around people and will happily keep you company, just in his own unique way.
He has very strong feelings about flooring and prefers soft surfaces only. You will often find him standing right at the edge of the carpet or carefully navigating across cozy pathways, making his way over to be near you while staying true to his standards.
He loves having a comfy home base to relax in, but he also has a playful side. Give him a cardboard scratcher and he is in his element, happily chewing away and entertaining himself.
Lindsey is also very smart. He once figured out how to get extra pellets from an automatic feeder, so he will definitely keep you on your toes in the most adorable way.
The fastest way to his heart is treats, especially banana!!
Overall, Lindsey is a gentle, funny, and easygoing bunny with a quiet charm and just the right amount of personality. He would make a wonderful companion for both first time rabbit owners and experienced bunny lovers.

244959.name: Morty
244959.summary:
My foster writes: Morty is kind of a strange little guy - in the best way.
He's a bit awkward and mysterious, spending much of his time tucked under the sofa, emerging on his own terms with his signature big, stompy steps (you'll always hear him coming).
He's low-key suspicious of the TV, and while he's not especially food motivated, he'll gladly accept a Churu as a peace offering. Morty loves playing hide and seek, chasing wand and string toys, zooming through his tunnel, and occasionally batting at your feet from beneath the couch.
He isn't needy, but he is affectionate once you earn his trust. He'll wander out to check on you, meow politely for back/butt scratches, and sometimes curl up next to you or in your lap.
When he's really comfortable, he'll dramatically flop over for pets, roll around showing his belly, and gently paw at you if you stop petting him too soon. He purrs loudly and even drools a little when he's extra happy.
He'll check on you in the bathroom to make sure you're okay, and somehow always needs attention the second you're on a meeting. He tolerates being picked up (while looking mildly confused), then may casually scamper off once you put him down.
Laid back, independent, sweet, and a little goofy - Morty just does things on his own time, and it makes it special when he chooses you. 🐾

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Morty tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. 

Meet Morty!
Morty came to ACC after living with adults in a home environment. He is a shy, timid cat who prefers to take things slowly, especially in new surroundings. In the shelter, Morty can appear cautious or stressed at first, but with gentle handling and time, he shows tolerance for petting and curiosity about his caregivers. He enjoys calm interactions and prefers affection on his own terms.

My Ideal Home
Morty would thrive in a quiet, low-traffic home with experienced cat parents who understand shy or sensitive cats. He needs time to acclimate, patience, and a predictable routine. Allowing him space to settle in, approach voluntarily, and build trust gradually will help him feel secure and confident.

Good with Kids?
No young children. ACC recommends Morty be placed in a home without children under 5, as he needs extra time to warm up and may become stressed in busy or unpredictable environments.

244997.name: Mr. Grey
244997.summary:
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.

My foster writes: 
Are you looking for a new best friend who is a cute snuggle bug and a playful sidekick? Mr Grey is the purr-fect match ! This beautiful, spirited young cat is ready for a forever home filled with patience and love.
He enjoys chasing toys, napping and snuggling up to you. He is very curious about everything. He waits at the door when we come home and follows us whenever we leave a room. He really should be named Shadow! You'll never feel lonely again with this guy.
He is super low maintenance as he only eats kibble and loves to drink water. He never tries to steal your food and has never jumped on the kitchen counter.
Mr Grey is litter trained and ready to move in!

245130.name: Stormy
245130.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Stormy is a beautiful big girl who is looking for a patient adopter willing to let her move at her own pace. The shelter environment has been overwhelming for her, and she has shown significant fear in her kennel, including the potential for defensive behavior when she feels threatened.

Once she's out of her kennel, Stormy is still cautious but begins to relax. One of the quickest ways to her heart is through treats-she's very food motivated and enjoys earning tasty rewards. With time, consistency, and positive interactions, she has started to build trust with a small group of staff members and is slowly showing her softer side.

Stormy will thrive with someone who understands that trust isn't built overnight. She'll benefit from a calm, predictable home, gentle handling, and plenty of positive reinforcement as she continues to gain confidence. Watching her make progress has been incredibly rewarding, and we believe that, with the right person, Stormy has the potential to continue blossoming into a loyal and devoted companion.

If you have experience with shy or fearful dogs and are ready to give Stormy the time and understanding she deserves, she may be the perfect match for you.

245216.name: Sheela
245216.summary:
Meet Sheela!
Sheela is a playful, affectionate girl who loves being around people. Found as a stray, she has quickly shown her cuddly side and will happily climb into your lap before bouncing off to chase a toy. Sheela is a long stay dog with a reduced adoption fee, ready to find a home of her own.

Personality
Sheela is social, wiggly, and full of energy. She loves attention, leans into affection, and often rolls over for belly rubs. She can be jumpy and playful when excited but settles with time.

My Ideal Home
Sheela would do best in an adult-only home with an experienced adopter. She will benefit from structure, routine, and continued positive reinforcement training. An active home that can give her outlets for her energy will help her thrive.

Good with Other Pets?
Sheela is not a candidate for dog parks and may become overwhelmed by other dogs, especially in high-energy situations. At this time, she would do best as the only pet. Continued training can help her build more positive associations over time.

Good with Kids?
Sheela would do best in an adult-only home. Her size, strength, and enthusiastic greetings may be too much for younger children.

Things to Know
Sheela pulls strongly on leash and will need continued work on her walking skills. She is very food and toy motivated, which will help with training. She is high energy and benefits from longer walks and playtime.

Fun Fact
Sheela loves to catch toys mid air and will proudly show off her skills during playtime.

Sheela is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is making impressive progress on her training journey. She is working on muzzle conditioning and leave it, two skills that are helping her build trust, focus, and self-control. With patience and positive reinforcement, Sheela is growing into a more confident and adaptable pup with every session.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
Sheela being at risk is breaking my heart. She has been my favorite dog for the past six months of her being in shelter. I walk her every single day on my break and have only seen improvement in her behavior ever since she got here and I hope she can get another chance or more time to stay and improve even more before finding her forever home.

245245.name: Hershey Kiss
245245.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
Meet Hershey Kiss 🍫🐾 - the perfect mix of sweet, silly, and smart.
After spending the past few months in the shelter, Hershey Kiss is learning that the world can be a safe and loving place - and watching his confidence grow has been incredibly special. Even while he's still coming out of his shell, he remains one of the sweetest dogs you could meet. He warms up quickly to new people, proudly shows off his toys to visitors, and absolutely loves snuggling up with his humans.
Hershey Kiss is the kind of dog who's happy joining you for a walk and equally happy spending the rest of the day lounging inside. He loves going on adventures, rides amazingly in the car, and then happily curls up on the couch or in his crate for a nap (yes - he genuinely loves his crate!). One of his cutest habits? Sometimes he gets so cozy chewing on a toy that he literally falls asleep mid-chew.
During his straycation, Hershey Kiss showed just how smart and eager to please he is. He quickly learned "high five" and "down," and he made huge improvements with his leash manners. He can still get excited and pull a little on walks, but he's already learning how to slow down, check in with his person, and redirect himself - especially with treats and encouragement since he's very food motivated.
He's also got a playful side: occasional zoomies, toy parades, and joyful runs around the roof with his favorite toys are some of his specialties. Around other dogs, he's shown friendly interest with a loose, wiggly body.
Everywhere we went, people fell in love with Hershey Kiss - and it's easy to see why. He's a loving, goofy boy with so much potential and such a good heart. His future family is absolutely out there, and whoever finds him is going to be very lucky 💛


What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

Hershey Kiss is a Shelter Scholar who is putting in the work to become a calmer, more confident pup on the leash. Like many dogs, he can get overwhelmed when he spots other dogs or distractions during walks, but through his training he's learning to refocus and look to his handler for guidance. With consistent practice and plenty of positive reinforcement, Hershey Kiss is making real strides one walk at a time.

My Boroughbreaker writes: We were informed about his fearfullness, hard pulling, and resource guarding and I want to highlight that Hershey Kiss is a FAST learner. We spent a few hours together and by the end, he was already checking in with me during the walks and ignored the other dogs. He was definitely curious about other dogs, but based on his body language (loose, wiggly, tail) he just wanted to say hi and play more than being fearful. He would get nervous when we were in big group settings like the farmers market but we quickly redirected and prioritized his comfort. In my apartment, he immediately went straight into his crate and knocked out which makes me think he's okay being on his own once he gets used to it!

245258.name: Thumper
245258.summary:
My foster writes:
Thumper is a sweet boy that loves his churu. He is very friendly and though he doesn't love traditional petting, he will show his affection by following you around and lying next to you. He is super curious and likes to explore the house. He is very comfortable with people and doesn't get scared easily. Thumper is generally a calm cat that tolerates handling very well and sleeps in the sweetest and funniest position. His split nose with a heart around and his big eyes will make you fall in love with him


What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
Thumper is laying in his den, ears forward and body relaxed as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he gets up, tail held high as he comes forward and approaches the assessor at the front of the kennel. He leans forward to sniff their hand before softly head bunting, allowing and leaning into all petting. Thumper is able to be easily picked up and remains calm when he is held for several seconds. When placed back into the kennel he remains calm, standing at the front of the kennel and continuing to lean into all petting. Thumper is able to be easily lifted and placed into a carrier to be transported to a new kennel.

Thumper interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Thumper go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in overstimulation, new home adjustment and decompression, and high energy. Due to history reported by his previous owner an adult only home is recommended.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

245355.name: Lennard
245355.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Lennard is at risk due to behavioral concerns in a home environment. In care, Lennard has been easy to remove from the kennel, but was noted to become conflicted with handling during his assessment - head whipping, pinned ears, but moves closer by backing into the handler. While in his previous foster homes, Lennard was reported to enjoy enrichment games and was treat-motivated. They did report he did experience separation anxiety, mouthiness/nipping with hard pressure, on one occasion escalated to growling and lunging at a young child, and on another occasion snapping at the foster and a stranger when they had a conversation during a walk. Medically, Lennard recently recovered from CIRDC.

Place with a New Hope partner: Lennard came into the care center as a stray but has spent time in foster. His foster parent writes"Lennard is so sweet and playful. He throws his toys up in the air and catches them. We giggle at his constant snoring and have taught him to play "go find it". He's incredibly curious and loves to stick his adorably large head into everything you are doing." Due to all noted concerns displayed in the home environment, the behavior department recommends Lennard be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. Lennard would benefit from a New Hope placement with experienced handlers who can provide structure, management, and behavior modification, particularly around impulse control.

245382.name: Bowie
245382.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Bowie is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Bowie has been showing signs of deterioration as his stay in care has progressed, despite best efforts to keep him comfortable. Bowie has been highly social and readily engages in training sessions, but he has intermittently been leash biting, grabbing and/or tugging at clothing, treat pouches, and one one occasion, tugging on gloves that were clipped to a handler's belt. He also has been mouthing at hands and arms even during training sessions. At times he can be difficult to redirect with treats or toys, once over his threshold. Medically, Bowie has a mass and dental disease.

Meet Bowie!
Bowie is a sweet, thoughtful boy who was found as a stray and is still learning to feel comfortable in new situations. He is very treat-motivated and shines brightest when he feels safe and understands what is being asked of him. Bowie is part of our Shelter Scholar program, where he is working on resource guarding and building confidence through positive reinforcement and structured support. He is just waiting for the right home to help him hit all the right notes.

Personality
Bowie is affectionate and people-oriented, but can be cautious in unfamiliar environments. Once he warms up, he enjoys treats, gentle interaction, and showing off his sit and paw for snacks. He does best when he can approach at his own pace and have a calm, predictable routine.

My Ideal Home
Bowie would thrive in a quiet, adult-only home with patient adopters who can move at his pace. He will benefit from structure, consistency, and continued positive reinforcement training. A low-traffic home where he can relax and feel secure will help him do his best.

Good with Other Pets?
Bowie has shown discomfort around other dogs in some introductions and may become overwhelmed in close or high-energy interactions. He also prefers not to share valued items like food, toys, or bedding. At this time, he may do best as the only pet in the home.

Good with Kids?
Bowie would do best in a home without children under 13. He is most comfortable in a calm environment where his space is respected.

Things to Know
Bowie walks nicely on leash and is generally calm in low-distraction environments. He is very food-motivated and responds well to treats and gentle guidance during training. He is actively working on resource guarding in our Shelter Scholar program and is making steady progress with support and positive reinforcement.

Fun Fact
Bowie is a clever, treat-loving boy who loves showing off his sit and paw, especially when snacks are involved. Once he feels at home, he has a soft, snuggly side that really shines. He's ready to become your new favorite record on repeat.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Bowie is a happy, loving dog that is eager to show you his sit and paw commands. Three different people stopped us to comment on how handsome he is! Bowie wanted to say hi to everyone we passed and let a group of tourists gently pet him. Even though I could see he wanted to take one woman's bracelet, he received my "uh uh" and redirected to a hand licking. Bowie had zero issues with resource guarding and not only did he leave the chicken bones be, but he also listened through some tough tests like a full muffin left on the sidewalk. To my surprise, he had no reactions to birds or dogs (just flies lol). Bowie is a special dog and I would love to spend more time with him in the future!

245386.name: Lily
245386.summary:
My foster writes: Head bumps are Lily's love language. She is affectionate but seems sensitive to some touch-while she is lovely company, she needs someone willing to read her cues with utmost care. Slow movement, light, gentle touch, and patience have begun to draw her personality out into the sunshine. She is a decent conversationalist and oddly adept at articulating what she wants. She follows her foster around the house (readily bumping against their legs while they prepare her dinner) and likes to settle in close, often pressed against her foster at bedtime. She loves to chase string and watch birds out the window. She makes fresh biscuits every morning and sometimes before bed. She is calm and stately, only getting excited when the strings come out. She is a lovely little sidekick and absolutely beautiful. Last but not least, she is a purr machine! She made the recent snow storms and rainy days delightful being curled up and rumbling at her foster's side. Lily with a cup of hot tea: 14/10. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Lily was facing forward in the loaf position, appearing slightly tense with somewhat enlarged pupils. She didn't sniff treats, but allowed petting while remaining slightly tense, and became more vigilant when petted along her back, with her head following my hand slightly. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home.

Lily tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior and a potential dislike of being picked up.

245501.name: Bianca
245501.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: 

This sweet mush of a mama dog will be your new best friend. She is a velcro dog and happiest snuggled up next to you. She's highly observant and aware of her surroundings. She'll gladly curl up by your side to watch some Animal Planet. She is very well house-trained and takes her treats with excellent manners. She also did very well riding in the Lyft. She'd be perfect for someone who can help her work on her leash skills and give her all the love and care she deserves!

Bianca is a perfect pup, a heat sealing, house trained cuddle buddy. She wants nothing more than to be by your side or play fetch with her plushy. She knows how to sit, give her paw and takes her sweet potato and treats very politely. She's alert and observant and rode in the Lyft with excellent manners. With a little peanut butter she's happy to enjoy her bath spa time like the princess she is.

245530.name: Goldie-Barks
245530.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Goldie is the sweetest girl with the biggest smile and a true talent for cuddling. She loves naps, bedtime, and any moment that involves being close to her people. Goldie firmly believes she's a lap dog and will happily climb right in (all 43 pounds of her) if invited. She's potty trained, walks nicely on leash, and is perfectly content relaxing on her own - but will be ready with immediate snuggles the second you return. If you're looking for a loving, affectionate companion, Goldie is your girl.

My foster writes:  Goldie Barks was an absolute delight to short-term foster over the holidays. She quickly acclimated to our apartment, and almost instantly wanted to snuggle and receive belly/neck rubs. She is fully housetrained and does not have separation anxiety (can be alone for a long time by herself without being destructive or getting restless). She is the perfect apartment dog, and doesn't ever bark or whine. If she hears other dogs in the hallway, she'll go up to the door to listen but won't bark or whine. She will sometimes be curious about other dogs and stare, but can be easily redirected to continue the walk. Goldie is a very easy-going and loving dog that deserves an equally loving family who can give her all the snuggles!

My boroughbreaker writes: Goldie is an absolute treasure. She is so precious and lovable, and I feel so grateful that we got paired to be buddies for the day. She is cool, calm, and collected.Goldie is really such a sweetheart, she was affectionate toward us when we showed affection toward her, but she also was fine doing her own thing. She is the perfect snuggle buddy, and she loved back scratches and gentle pets. She also slept for a really long time, and she is the most adorable sleeper. It was really so heart warming to watch her snuggle up on the blanket and take a good rest. I wish it was warmer out so that we could do more exploring outside, because she was really wonderful on the leash and very intuitive. She is a great walking buddy, she is aware of her surroundings and stayed in my rhythm of walking. Goldie passed a few dogs, and while she is curious about them and tries to go say hi, we kept our distance today. But strangers loved her, and she was so friendly and warm to everyone we came in contact with. This was just the most amazing day and most incredible experience, and I am so so glad to have shared it with Goldie. To anyone looking for a forever best friend, Goldie is your gal. I have no doubt that her gentle and pure energy, along with her curious and joyful nature, will truly light up someone's life.

245540.name: Goku
245540.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Goku is at risk for behavior concerns of shelter deterioration. Goku has been noted to lick the kennel walls and glass and to bark and jump at the kennel door. Handlers have also needed to use distractions when leashing Goku due to leash biting. Goku allows handling and is social with handlers. Goku is apparently healthy.

Meet Goku!
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Goku was dropped off at a police precinct without any background information and is now looking for a patient home where he can continue to build confidence and feel safe. He has been slowly coming out of his shell and shows a thoughtful, attentive personality once he warms up.

My Ideal Home
Goku will do best in an adult-only home with experience handling sensitive or fearful dogs. He benefits from slow introductions, predictable routines, and a calm environment where he is given time to decompress and choose interaction at his own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
Goku is recommended as a single pet at this time and should not attend dog parks. He has shown strong reactions to unfamiliar dogs during shelter introductions and will need continued support and management in environments where other dogs are present.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to fear-based reactivity and need for a calm, controlled environment.

Things to Know
Goku is treat-motivated and enjoys learning, already showing a cute habit of consistently offering his paw once he realizes it gets rewarded. He responds best to gentle handling and can be distracted and redirected with food. While he may bark or tense around unfamiliar people or situations, he can begin to settle with patience and slow introductions.

Volunteer Writes
A volunteer describes Goku as quietly endearing, especially noting his soft, expressive "puppy dog eyes" that immediately draw people in. One of his standout behaviors is how clearly he learns routines, particularly offering his paw with precision to the first person who rewards him. Despite arriving scared and overwhelmed from multiple transitions, he has started to show moments of trust and connection with familiar handlers. Volunteers note that beneath his initial worry, there is a sweet, observant dog who is beginning to enjoy human interaction and is ready to continue blossoming in a stable home.

245587.name: Panettone
245587.summary:
My foster writes: Panettone is a sweet, sometimes shy, mostly playful cat. She is good with her litter box and doesn't have accidents. She likes to spend time in the kitchen while I cook and sits on the couch with me and my roommates when we work. She loves people-watching from our window, playing with yarn, and has had good interactions with strangers. After a long and busy day of being adorable, she will come into one of my roommates rooms, burrows under her little blanket and sleep peacefully through the night. Very sweet but a little skittish. She was able to adjust to the apartment well and deserves a beautiful home.

A volunteer writes:
Panettone was found wandering the streets by a compassionate Good Samaritan and arrived at our care center frightened and uncertain about her future.
Her first days in the kennel were understandably difficult. Panettone alternated between seeking comfort through cuddling and expressing her stress with hissing, swatting, and anxious meowing. But with patience and care, she's blossomed into a much calmer cat who's now ready to find her permanent family.
Today, Panettone enjoys gentle petting and absolutely loves her treats. No surprise for a petite girl who weighs just six pounds and could use a little fattening up! While she's made wonderful progress, she remains somewhat skittish around sudden noises or quick movements, which may send her scurrying to a safe hiding spot.
We know nothing about Panettone's past or what she may have experienced before her rescue, but it's clear she deserves a patient, understanding home. Her ideal family will provide a quiet, peaceful environment without children, giving her the time and space she needs to fully adjust and trust again. With love, consistency, and a calm atmosphere, this sweet calico will reward her adopters with the affection she's already beginning to show.
If you're ready to give Panettone the safe, loving home she deserves, come meet her today.


What my friends at ACC say about me:
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

245633.name: Hockey
245633.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Hockey is at risk due to behavioral reasons. In his previous home, Hockey bit a family member during an attempt to place a leash on him. His teeth made contact with the person's hand, resulting in broken skin. While in care, Hockey has been observed displaying reactivity toward other dogs and has occasionally kennel fights. He has also been reported to exhibit resource-guarding behaviors around food and toys. Hockey actively engages in training and is highly motivated by treats, which can be a valuable tool in supporting his continued learning and behavior development. Medically, Hockey is healthy.

Meet Hockey!
Hockey arrived as an owner surrender when his family was moving and couldn't keep pets. He appreciates slow introductions to new people and places and loves to be loved - on his own terms. He's ready to learn and would thrive with a patient person who has time to work on training and help him build confidence.

My Ideal Home
Hockey would do best in a calm, adult-only home with someone who can provide consistent, positive reinforcement training and predictable routines. A household without other animals (or one willing to manage very gradual, supervised introductions) and an adopter experienced with canine body language will help him feel safe and successful.

Good with Other Pets?
Not recommended as an automatic match. Staff have observed that Hockey does not always like to share food, toys, or bedding, so he's likely to do best as the only pet or with carefully managed introductions and ongoing supervision around other animals.

Other Fun Facts
Hockey is affectionate when comfortable and truly enjoys learning - brush up on your training skills with him! He can form a strong bond with the right person and loves attention on his own terms.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I really enjoy toys! I'll let you know my favorite one when we meet!
I am playful and cute!
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.

A volunteer writes: Cookie is a sweet girl only about two years old. I would describe her as sweet as a sugar cookie. Her family was no longer able to care for her so she is now with us and settling in nicely. 245686.name: Keanu
245686.summary:
My foster writes: Keanu means "cool breeze over the mountains," a fitting name for her shy yet quietly captivating presence. She has a calm, slightly mysterious personality, paired with wonderfully balanced cat behavior that makes her an ideal companion. Her distinctive yin-yang face carries a unique charm that makes you fall in love with her at first sight.
Keanu is an independent young girl with a strong love for food and an excellent appetite. She is energetic and playful, especially enjoying cat trees, feather toys, and balls. While she may need about two months to fully warm up to a new environment, she is ultimately a deeply affectionate cat who longs for a stable, loving home.
With her gentle nature and playful spirit, Keanu is ready to become a sweet and lasting member of your family through the summer and all the seasons to come.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Keanu tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home.  We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children.

245752.name: Monet
245752.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Monet is just an angel. He is the perfect gentleman at home--crate trained, potty trained, and an excellent listener, he is such an easygoing dog. He loves to cuddle up next to you on the couch, or chill in his crate and watch you do errands around the house. And because he is comfortable being alone for up to six hours, he's the perfect companion for anyone who likes to both chill at home and go to the office/social events. He doesn't beg for food, chew your things, or bark/whine excessively--all he does is give you love and sweetness! Anyone would be lucky to have this gentle sweetheart in their lives!!

My foster writes: Meet Monet! A loving, playful, silly, energetic 8 year old male. He is potty trained, crate trained, knows tricks, and is a very good listener. He loves his tug toys, playing fetch, is extremely treat driven, and a very good listener. Whether you are looking for someone to cuddle with on the couch or burn some energy with, Monet loves it all! He really is the best dog!

My foster writes: Monet is a joyful, cuddle‑powered sweetheart who loves nothing more than showing off his snuggling skills to anyone willing to receive them. He greets his people with an adorable prance, carries his toys over for gentle tug‑of‑war, and takes treats with the softest mouth. Monet learns quickly, adapts easily, and is eager to please, making him a great fit for many types of homes. On walks he may pull or get excited when he sees other dogs, but his enthusiasm is all wiggles - never teeth, growls, or snaps. If you're looking for a loving, loyal companion with endless charm, Monet is ready to brighten your life.

Another foster writes:
I started off with Monet as a Straycation and quickly realized I would try long-term fostering him as my first foster because of how well behaved he is and of course he has the cutest face !!! I began fostering Monet, who is 8 years old, since 7/21/26 so far and he is the sweetest, happiest boy who is always excited to greet me with wiggles when I return from work. He is a quick learner, adapts easily, and has nothing but love and sweetness to give. Monet is house-trained, crate-trained, and enjoys going for walks. Monet is able to walk on a slacked leash, although he does pull on the leash - he is able to be redirected; moreover, he allows me to clean his paws after walks. He enjoys playing tug-of-war, followed up by fetch. Monet will try bringing a toy/ball to you to get you involved when he's feeling playful. He LOVES treats and will take them with the softest mouth. He is truly easy to love!

This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

245930.name: Origami
245930.summary:
My foster writes: Origami is sweet, curious, and super friendly! She loves to chase little toy mice and bring them to you as a present. She's a perfect cuddle buddy in the mornings and after a long day. She's very responsive to pets and has the cutest squeaky meow. She's an attentive companion who wants nothing more than to receive your love and attention. Her loaf form is a 10/10!

A volunteer writes:
Origami has come a long way since her arrival at the care center, relinquished as she was allegedly scratching her owner(no details provided).Origami is curious and welcoming when a visitor shows up at her door. She does not stay in hiding and it is a must for her to say "hi" and "what's the sccoop?" She is still a little wary of loud noises and sudden moves but clearly enjoys sweet talks and petting. She likes treats but prefers cuddling over eating even the best offerings. I like the way she closes her eyes showing how much she appreciates the attention. Origami does have a right eye issue that might or not need further care. She will need her outside veterinarian to follow her for that matter in addition to the usual yearly health care maintenance. A quiet and experienced home without boisterous children will be the ideal destination for our lovely Origami. Origami is I guess a special need kitty and those so deserve our love and care too. Origami is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Origami was at the front of the kennel eating from her wet food bowl. When spoken to and opening the door, she hovers over the front entrance, rubs her face on the wall, and leans in for cheek rubs. She ignores treats offered and welcomes petting on the head. When stroking her body, she raises her hips and tail in the air. During pick up, she remains calm, tenses up a little, and allows petting all over when held and hugged for 10 seconds. After placing her back down, she continues to appreciate more petting and cheek rubs.

245974.summary:
My foster writes:
Avocado is a sweet, shy cat at first but she warms up to be very loving and vocal about it! She is active in the morning and will want you to wake up and pet her. She likes to sleep on a chair at the table while we sit next to her. She's been good about using the litterbox and will work out great

My foster writes: Avo is a sweet girl who needs time to adjust! She is very smart and very curious but also likes her space. She will let you know if she wants pets

A volunteer writes: 
Avocado is a beautiful 14 year old senior who was found and brought in by a Good Samaritan from the cold. We are so happy she is here and warm with us. She loves treats and gently ate them out of my hand. She is trying her best to adjust so isn't outwardly seeking out pets but does accept them and I know she is trying to build her confidence and accept love. This gentle senior needs a comfy, warm couch to spend her golden years and get a nice nap in a sun puddle.

245975.name: Toast
245975.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Toast, your future shadow with whiskers! He's the kind of cat who believes life is best lived side-by-side: hop onto the bed while you're answering emails, curl up on the couch during a movie, and if you so much as stand up, he'll politely rise to escort you to your next destination. The moment you sit back down, he's right there again, settling in like he was always meant to be part of the furniture (and your life). Sweet, well-behaved, and a champion napper, Toast is the perfect warm presence to make any house feel like home.


A volunteer writes:
Seniors Toast and Avocado were discarded in a carrier among piles of trash waiting to be picked up by the sanitary truck. Luckily, an astute and concerned citizen spotted them and brought them to the Manhattan Care Center. Toast is a ten year old gentleman, a tabby who likely and understandably can not fathom "what just hit him"... He had a cold to make things even harder. How is a former pet supposed to handle himself in the face of such an unexpected and frightening hardship? Toast was a little cranky and fearful when his behavior was tested but, a few days down the line, he welcomed petting, even head bunted my hand with his neck and purred(see his video). I did not hear a hiss, I did not see a swat, just some reservation, some shyness.  Toast needs better than a cage. True, nothing is known about him(except that he lived with a thirteen year old dame, Avocado). Is he a good guy/or not. I would go for the latter... Feeling safe and loved (in a quiet and experienced home) is what will bring warmth and life to this abandoned elderly pet. We hope that Toast will pull at your heart strings and be your forever thankful four-legged companion!


Toast is not open to interaction at this time and does not currently tolerate petting or handling. Because his previous owner reports he is a friendly and well-behaved cat in a home environment, we believe the behavior seen in the care center is shelter-specific and this cat would make a great pet but is really struggling in the shelter environment. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, home with adopters who are willing to work with a cat who needs time and patience to help him adjust to their new home.

246069.name: Buddy
246069.summary:
My foster writes: Buddy is a sweet and curious kitty who loves to head scratches and loves to explore and play! Her favorite toys are pompoms and spiral ponytail holders. Once she warms up to you, she likes napping in the same room as you to keep an eye on what you've got going on. She is friendly with new people and likes knowing what's on the TV or who's on the phone if you're making a call. Her favorite spots tend to be near the radiator or somewhere dark like under the couch. She also loves to sit in the window and watch cars drive by. She can be a little funny to watch when she plays as she jumps onto her hind legs more than I've most cats do!

My foster writes: Buddy is a sweet and curious kitty who loves to explore and play! Despite her small size, she has plenty of energy for play. Her favorite toys are pompoms and spring toys. She especially loves playing right after meals. She also loves to sit in the window and watch cars drive by. She's very small and loves to find a quiet spot to rest such as under the couch. Once she warms up to you, she wants to know what you are watching if the TV is on and will get on her hind legs to take a look.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would like a home where there is another cat that I can play with!
Buddy is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she does attempt to flee and avoid human contact. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

246086.name: Allie
246086.summary:
My foster writes: Hi! My name is Allie. I am a very small, shy girl, but I open up after a couple of days. I like to sit by my person and will chirp when I want your attention. I love head rubs so much. I'm all black except for my belly and neck. I get along well with other cats so I will make a good addition to someone's feline family. I'm looking for my forever home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
Hi, my name is Allie and the shelter has been a little overwhelming for me. I came from a home with many cats, who I've gotten along with well. Because I've lived in this home my entire life and have only been around one person, I have little experience with people and am hesitant of new experiences. I would enjoy living in a quiet home, preferably one with lots of vertical space so I have a place to perch and observe the room. I would also appreciate having experienced, patient adopter(s) who are willing to take things slow with me. I would benefit from socialization, using rewards whenever I make a small positive step like making eye contact, allowing petting, or sniffing your hand. I'd prefer to take things at my own pace and would appreciate some good old fashion TLC. If you can open your heart to adopt a cat like me, I'll hopefully have the confidence to come around to my new people, like you!

246103.name: Luna
246103.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Luna is at risk due to behavioral concerns. She is a young, energetic dog who can become quickly over-aroused during socialization sessions, resulting in behaviors such as mouthing or biting at staff members' shoes, air snapping, and jumping on people. Luna is highly food-motivated and has demonstrated significant potential for training and behavior modification. Luna also appears highly stressed in her kennel and is often heard vocalizing for extended periods. Medically, she is a healthy dog. 

Meet Luna!
Luna is an owner surrender who is looking for a home where she can finally settle in, feel secure, and stay close to her people. She has a bright, affectionate personality and really comes alive when she has company and a bit of playtime in her day.

Personality
Luna is social, loving, and full of personality. She bonds quickly with people and enjoys being involved in whatever is going on around her. Whether she's playing on her own for a bit or following you from room to room, she really just wants to be included. She can be enthusiastic in her greetings and may jump up when excited, but it's all friendly energy and excitement to connect.

She already knows some basic cues and enjoys working for treats, especially when things are upbeat and encouraging. She responds best to gentle structure and consistency rather than anything too strict or overwhelming.

Out and About
Luna enjoys her walks and moves with moderate pulling, more from excitement than anything else. She doesn't react to people or other dogs she passes and is generally focused on getting out and exploring. With continued guidance, she should keep improving her leash skills, especially as she learns to settle into a routine.

Social Behavior
In new spaces, Luna is moderately social and may be a little distracted at first, but she warms up with encouragement and engagement. She likes to approach when called and can be playful once she's comfortable. She tends to feel better when interactions are calm and not overly restrictive, and she enjoys having space to move and engage at her own pace.

Home Life
Luna would thrive in a home that offers structure, companionship, and positive reinforcement. She enjoys being around people and does best when she isn't left alone for long periods without support. She is crate trained for short stretches and will benefit from continued routines that help her feel secure and relaxed.

Things to Know
Luna may need a little extra patience with things like grooming, nail trims, and car rides, as these can make her a bit uneasy. With calm reassurance and consistency, she continues to show how affectionate, smart, and people-focused she really is.

Fun Fact
Luna is happiest when she's right in the middle of the action, playing, exploring, or just sticking close to her favorite humans 🐾

Luna is social, loving, and full of personality. She bonds quickly with people and enjoys being involved in whatever is going on around her. Whether she's playing on her own for a bit or following you from room to room, she really just wants to be included. She can be enthusiastic in her greetings and may jump up when excited, but it's all friendly energy and excitement to connect.

She already knows some basic cues and enjoys working for treats, especially when things are upbeat and encouraging. She responds best to gentle structure and consistency rather than anything too strict or overwhelming.

Out and About
Luna enjoys her walks and moves with moderate pulling, more from excitement than anything else. She doesn't react to people or other dogs she passes and is generally focused on getting out and exploring. With continued guidance, she should keep improving her leash skills, especially as she learns to settle into a routine.

Social Behavior
In new spaces, Luna is moderately social and may be a little distracted at first, but she warms up with encouragement and engagement. She likes to approach when called and can be playful once she's comfortable. She tends to feel better when interactions are calm and not overly restrictive, and she enjoys having space to move and engage at her own pace.

Home Life
Luna would thrive in a home that offers structure, companionship, and positive reinforcement. She enjoys being around people and does best when she isn't left alone for long periods without support. She is crate trained for short stretches and will benefit from continued routines that help her feel secure and relaxed.

Things to Know
Luna may need a little extra patience with things like grooming, nail trims, and car rides, as these can make her a bit uneasy. With calm reassurance and consistency, she continues to show how affectionate, smart, and people-focused she really is.

Fun Fact
Luna is happiest when she's right in the middle of the action, playing, exploring, or just sticking close to her favorite humans 🐾

246150.name: Orange Yogurt
246150.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Orange Yogurt!
Orange Yogurt is a 3-year-old sweetheart with a soft personality and a name that fits her perfectly. Her past is unknown, and she is the kind of dog who opens up slowly. Once she does, she has a gentle charm that really shines through.

Personality
Orange Yogurt can be a little unsure when meeting new people or exploring new places. At first, she may hang back and observe, but with patience and a calm approach, she begins to warm up. Treats tossed her way help her feel more comfortable, and once she trusts you, she will allow gentle petting and start to engage more.

Getting to Know Her
Orange Yogurt does best when she is given time to adjust. A soft and patient approach helps her relax. She is learning that people are kind and predictable, and that is helping her come out of her shell little by little.

Out and About
On leash, Orange Yogurt walks with mild pulling and does not show reactivity for people. She does show sensitivity around other dogs and may fixate or react when they get close, so she will need continued support and redirection on walks. Sometimes she gets a little excited and may jump up softly on her handler, but it comes from a place of seeking connection.

My Ideal Home
Orange Yogurt would love a calm and patient home where she can take her time settling in. She will thrive with someone who understands shy dogs. She does best when she is not rushed and when her boundaries are respected. Once she feels safe, she has so much potential to blossom.

Living with Kids
Orange Yogurt would do best in a home without very young children (under 5). She may be open to older, gentle kids who understand how to give her space and let her come to them when she is ready.

Things to Know
Orange Yogurt is a Level 2 dog who is still building confidence in new situations. She will benefit from ongoing positive reinforcement training and a predictable routine.

246374.name: Banana Cream Pie
246374.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Banana Cream Pie is at risk due to behavior concerns. Banana has show increasing shelter stress and dog reactivity while in care. In kennel, she has been observed to jump up and down and heavily pant. She fixates on dogs on the street as well as in the shelter, hard staring, pulling hard, and barking towards other dogs. She is sometimes able to be redirected with squeakers while outside at a distance from other dogs, but is not able to be redirected with treats or a squeaker in close proximity. Banana's previous owner states that she will growl and hard bark when seeing dogs and moving objects while on leash. Banana has also shown signs of fearfulness while in care. Banana's previous owner notes that she will become tense and hover over food and random objects, and has frequent accidents in the home. She was described to be very playful and hyperactive in the home. Medically, Banana Cream Pie is slightly underweight but otherwise apparently healthy.

Meet Banana Cream Pie!
Banana Cream Pie is as sweet as her name suggests! She was originally found tied up outside a building as a stray and is now searching for a patient, loving family to help her leave her past behind. This playful girl has been spending time in foster care, where she's shown just how loyal and fun she can be once she settles in.

My Ideal Home
Banana Cream Pie would thrive with an experienced owner who can provide structure, consistency, and plenty of exercise. She loves staying active and will enjoy enrichment like puzzle toys, long-lasting chews, sniffy walks, and training sessions that keep her busy. A calm home where she can settle in at her own pace will help her feel her best.

Good with Other Pets?
Banana Cream Pie prefers to have her favorite food and treasures all to herself. She can also be reactive toward dogs while on leash, so slow introductions and thoughtful management around other pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to her resource guarding, leash reactivity, and need for a calm environment, ACC recommends an adult only home.

Things to Know
Banana Cream Pie is an energetic girl who's still working on a few life skills. She'll benefit from continued positive reinforcement training for leash manners, polite greetings, and house training, as she's had occasional accidents indoors. She can be cautious in new environments and appreciates slow introductions, giving her the choice to approach people and new experiences at her own pace. With patience, consistency, and lots of encouragement, she's sure to blossom into an incredible companion.

What My Foster Says
"My foster writes: BCP is a sweetheart. She is very energetic and loves to play with her fluffy toys. She stays calm in her crate, stays by your side during walks, and with a bit of structure and training could become your bestie! Movie nights, binge watching, hikes, or runs... she'll be that loyal, no-drama companion."

Fun Fact
Whether it's chasing after fluffy toys, heading out on an adventure, or curling up for a movie marathon, Banana Cream Pie is happiest simply spending time with her favorite person.

246399.name: Ushi
246399.summary:
My foster writes: Ushi is a truly distinguished NYC boroughbred. He's done his time on the NYC streets serving his community and keeping the peace. Oh the stories he could tell! And now he's looking for a retirement home where he can let his guard down and enjoy some comfort and TLC in his golden years.
Ushi got this far in life by watching his back and keeping to himself. His heroes are those hardboiled movie detectives, keeping their collar up and their hat brim down, sniffing out corruption in the shadows and searching for truth in the seedy city. And old habits die hard, so at first Ushi seems aloof and withdrawn. But there's a real softie inside his stoic exterior. Once Ushi is feeling safe and happy he will literally melt into pets and cuddles. It's very rewarding to watch this big guy learn to trust humans and accept the delights of apartment living. "Oh, this soft comfy bed is for *me*? Don't mind if I do...!"
Ushi is a creature of habit and routine. He'll stake out one or two favourite tucked-away nap spots that he'll return to day in, day out. And he takes mealtimes very seriously - he'll quietly sit by his food bowl until you get the message...! While he will sometimes scamper away to stay out of trouble, he's wise enough to know never to pick a fight - he is not aggressive.
Ushi will be happiest in a quiet, chill, low-traffic home where the humans will respect his need for alone time - but also lavish him with the care and affection he deserves in the golden years of his remarkable, colorful life.

My foster writes: Ushi is a shy cat who needs a little time to feel safe in a new home.
At first he may keep some distance, but with patience and quiet companionship he slowly starts coming closer on his own.
He has a few small imperfections.
One ear looks a bit different, there are some spots on his legs without much fur, and sometimes he gets a little eye discharge.
He loves canned food and squeeze treats.
They make it much easier to win his trust.
He also has some very funny habits.
If you pet his lower back his butt pops right up, and if you touch his cheeks he immediately flops onto the floor and melts there to enjoy the attention.
Ushi just needs someone patient and gentle.
Once he feels comfortable, he becomes a very sweet and quietly affectionate companion.

A volunteer writes: We're so glad Ushi is currently warm and safe at the Care Center, and we think he seems pretty pleased as well! Ever since he's come through our doors he's been sweet, calm, curious, and easy to handle, enjoying petting sessions and scarfing down lots of treats. He can sometimes be shy as he sizes up new human faces, but after a quick warm-up he's ready to make friends and enjoy the affection and interaction. Our behavior team can vouch for his comfort with people and generally chill demeanor, deeming Ushi to be a good fit for almost all types of households. We don't know what kind of life he had before he came to us, but it's a good bet that this wonderful guy was well socialized with people in a home. Now, he's ready to make the move to yours.

Another volunteer writes:
Ushi(Little Bear in German) was brought to us by the Good Samaritan who was taking care of him for years as an outdoor cat. He had a cold(now resolved)and was quite underweight and being a senior, it was about time for Ushi to find a safe haven for his golden years. Ushi likes to shelter in his cubby but say his name, bring some tasty treats and he will be out in nano seconds.. Ushi is a bit handshy but being a smart kitty, he is slowly easing himself into being an indoor pet. Ushi so deserves a new page in his life, filled with warmth, safety and love.

246619.name: Coco Montrese
246619.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Coco is a very handsome kitty with a lovely chocolate head(and tail) and adorable baby blue eyes. He was surrendered with the arrival of a new baby, his owners being worried he could be a safety concern for the child. Coco indeed, although a sweet and affectionate pet can get quite excited/rough with play and prolonged petting. Coco did not take well being relinquished to the care center. He was a well cared for pet and now, a cage. No, no, no... Time and enrichment did their job and Coco is quite a pleasant cat to spend time with(see video). He enjoys being petted, even comes on the lap, tolerating to be put back in his kennel and playing nicely with a feather wand. He does show overexcitement after a while and will give a little swat. Time to relax, stop the game and reset which he seems capable to do. In short, Coco is a beautiful already neutered cat, friendly, social and playful who needs a quiet home without young children and an experienced new owner who will provide love, care and interactive playtime knowing his behavioral challenges. Coco deserves a second chance!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I am not one to sit still and will love interactive playtime in my new home!
I am really treat motivated. You can use treats to teach me new things!
