246625.name: Mercy
246625.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Mercy is a spunky and loving dog that will melt your heart the minute she enters your home. She loves cuddles, belly scratches, and when you call her with kissing sounds. Be ready to have your heart stolen with this precious girl. Mercy has a lot of energy, that stems from her being home alone while I'm at work, so she needs to go on several walks through out the day. If you can squeeze a long walk than even better! At home she takes long naps, plays with her toys, or goes back and forth with the puzzles I leave her. She's a sucker for Greek yogurt and peanut butter, so make sure to have extra jars on hand! She's indifferent to cars and bikes, which is great when going on walks, but can get excited when spotting another dog and/or bird. Mercy is a curious pup, so make sure you have a good grip on her leash or your walk will turn into a spontaneous run. She loves to sniff around and occasionally will sit and enjoy the view while on walks.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
Not only do I pull at heart strings, but I also pull on leash! I will need someone to help me with my leash manners.

246662.name: Pigeon
246662.summary:
My foster writes: Pigeon is a shy but sweet girl who's still figuring out that people can be safe. She's doing great in her foster home-using the litter box perfectly, eating well, and exploring her space when things are calm and quiet.

246732.name: Lily
246732.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Lily, a pretty young tiger with lovely markings, came to us with housemate Luna as their home was overloaded with cats, many of them we already met and adopted out as they were may be shy but really sweet and well cared for kitties. Lily is no exception. She is a timid little princess who likes to take refuge in her cubby. Nothing much is known about her past but very often, cats who live in packs get well along with each other while they are reserved with humans. Lily is a bit subdued but slow blinks as I "sweet talk" her and accepts caresses, very slightly leaning into pets. Lily needs a little more time to show what she likely truly is, a lovely cat who in caring, understanding and loving hands will bloom into a wonderful and affectionate pet. Come and meet Lily at the Manhattan Care Center!
UPDATE: Lily came out of her shell! I knew it! Lily has all the qualities of a sweet and loving cat. She is smart and understood that all what we wanted for her is to be happy and find a wonderful and loving family. Come for cuddles and love to the Manhattan Care Center and ask to meet lovely Lily!


Lily has made lovely improvements since her last assessment and was now fully coaxed out of the cubby onto the main shelf with the promise of treats. She was a little bit chatty, giving sweet little chirps, and she enjoyed all petting on her cheek, head, and along her back. She remained out on the shelf to eat squeeze-up treats and enjoy more petting. She was calm during a partial pick-up and remained so afterward.

Lily interacts with the assessor, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.


	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

246777.name: Lavendar
246777.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Lavendar!
Lavendar was found wandering alone in a sweater with no owner present. She is a young, bright, and expressive girl. She enjoys human interaction and exploring her environment, and she tends to engage with people with confidence and curiosity.

My Ideal Home
Lavendar would do best in home with older children who can understand and respect her boundaries and independent nature. She appreciates interaction on her terms. A calm, consistent environment will help her continue to build confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Lavendar has shown selective responses to other dogs and can escalate in social interactions. Because of this, she is recommended as the only pet in the home and should not attend dog parks. She will do best in a setting where her interactions are carefully managed and controlled.

Good with Kids?
Lavendar is recommended for a home without children under 13 due to her sensitivity and tendency to become overstimulated in certain situations.

Things to Know
Lavendar is social and engaging with people but can be selective about physical affection and may prefer space at times. She is attentive, intelligent, and responsive, and benefits from clear communication and respect for her boundaries. She will thrive with structure and consistency.

Fun Fact
Lavendar loves water, whether splashing in the wading pool or drinking from the hose. She enjoys chasing tennis balls and pouncing on them like a cat. 💜

246786.name: Kody
246786.summary:
My foster writes: If you have a gentle hand and a quiet home and are not expecting a lap cat, Kody will be a wonderful companion. He's clever, has the eyes of an eagle and loves lounging. when he's not playing with his banana. Watching him gives me enormous pleasure.

Meet Kody!
Kody came to us with limited information about his life in a home, though we do know he previously lived with other cats. He is a quiet, shy, and independent boy who tends to observe the world carefully before deciding how he feels about it. In the shelter, he has appeared timid and skittish, often staying tucked inside his den. While he tolerates gentle petting, he may freeze or appear nervous during interactions, showing that he's still adjusting to the busy environment around him.

My Ideal Home
Kody would do best in a calm, adult-only home with experienced cat guardians who understand that he will need time and patience to settle in. A quiet environment with predictable routines will help him feel safe. He may be more independent in nature and will likely benefit from having safe hiding spaces and the freedom to approach people on his own terms. Giving him space, going slow, and allowing him to build trust gradually will be key to helping him blossom.

Good with Kids?
An adult-only home is recommended. Due to his timid and fearful behavior in the shelter, a quieter environment without children will help him feel more secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Kody previously lived with other cats, though we do not have details about those interactions. Slow, careful introductions to any resident pets would be recommended.

Overall Health
Healthy overall at this time.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Kody is a shy and fearful cat who requires an experienced, patient adopter and a calm home environment to support his adjustment period.

Other Fun Facts
Though he may be reserved at first, Kody is also curious and observant. With time and trust, this quiet boy has the potential to show his softer side and become a loyal, steady companion.

246836.name: Ramen
246836.summary:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
My favorite pastime is being visually admired! Pet me with your eyes!

My foster writes:
Ramen is a curious, outgoing, funny little guy! He loves to be around people and always wants to be where the action is. You can surely find him upside down lying on his back nearby wherever you are. He is also a vocal boy with an adorable high-pitched meow and a propensity for chirping. He will squeak out a "hello" whenever you come home, or when he just wants to chat. Ramen is also remarkably handsome, and like any fine piece of art, his policy is similar to "please look but don't touch". More specifically, he can become overwhelmed by petting, so he'd love a home that respects his space and is able to watch for his cues that he needs a break. Fortunately, there are other ways he'd love to hang out with you. He loves to play laser, and if you're feeling too tired he's also happy to join you in bed for a cat nap! If you have space in your home and heart for a devilishly handsome quirky little man, Ramen would love to be your new best friend!

My foster writes: Ramen is a wonderful baby, he is protective and very playful of his humans. Loves his wet food and can tolerate dry food! He is adorable when he is playing and will also watch the door if you leave him for a few hours.

246897.summary:
My foster writes: Panther is a sweet, relaxed guy who seems like he's had wilder days behind him and is ready to settle down. He is pretty content on his own but likes some pets on his head when he's relaxing. In the evening, he knows how to entertain himself with toys when he wants to.
He is a litter box champion and a very deep sleeper whose favorite sleeping position is "perfect black ball," although sometimes on closer inspection you'll notice that his head is actually facing up! He's got sweet round green eyes. Overall, Panther is a gentle soul who just wants to take it easy. He doesn't require much other that a comfy place to lay his head! He loves all food and treats.

With more time in the foster home, Panther has shown himself to be a sometimes-chatty cat who loves human companionship and affection. He takes all cheek scratches as invitations to lay down belly up and roll over a couple times, and he will follow you around at times! Panther is a bit dog-like - he even tolerates belly rubs, although cheek scratches are his favorite.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

246929.name: Ivy
246929.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! 

Meet Ivy!
Ivy came to us after a frightening experience: she and a companion were left behind in an apartment and suffered bite wounds before being rescued and brought into our care. Despite that rough start, she has been quietly and steadily proving she is one of the most resilient pups around. She takes her time warming up, and when she does, the payoff is real: wagging tails, leaning into pets, and the occasional unsolicited hug.

My Ideal Home
Ivy does best with patient, experienced adopters who understand that trust is earned, not assumed. An adult-only household is strongly recommended. She thrives with folks who move slowly, keep the treat supply well-stocked, and let her set the pace for affection.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for homes with children under 13. Ivy's fearful tendencies make her vulnerable to being startled, and an adult-only home gives her the best shot at success.

Good with Other Pets?
Ivy has shown tension with dogs at the shelter, so dog parks are not recommended. Calm, controlled introductions with a resident dog are possible, though a single-pet home would suit her best. No known history with cats.

Leash Manners
Ivy has become a sweet leash walker. She once needed a treat trail just to get out the door; now she often trots downstairs and outside on her own steam. Fair warning: she will spot a pigeon, lock on, and commit. Keep treats handy.

Overall Health
Ivy arrived with bite wounds that have fully healed and recovered from a mild respiratory infection while in our care. She is not yet spayed but will be before placement. She is up to date on core vaccines, microchipped, and parasite-treated.

Behavior Determination
Level 3. Best suited for adopters with experience with shy or fearful dogs.

Other Fun Facts
Those short legs give her the most endearing bouncy trot. She will wiggle between your legs, lean into a belly rub, play fetch, and jog alongside you once she trusts you. Her volunteers are absolutely smitten, and it is easy to see why.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Investigator Ivy is a sweet dog who is the embodiment of resilience. Despite her difficult upbringing, she has blossomed into a sweet, dog who is ready to give and receive the love. She is almost always on the trail, sniffing the streets and house for any clues to the unknown mystery she is solving. Luckily she doesn't eat the evidence. She accepts treats beautifully and politely. She did great with the affection of an older child on our break and even performed her tricks for her. She does not pull hard on the leash. It says in her paperwork that she was bird reactive, but I didn't see that at all despite the numerous pigeons we had on our walk. She is very curious of the other dogs and wants to play, but was able to be redirected every time. Don't let her short stature fool you! She has energy for long walks. Once she has a chance to do her investigation on you, she will open up within hours and become your other half.

246948.name: George
246948.summary:
My current foster writes:
George is an absolute dream of cat. After just two days of being in his new foster home, he started coming out of his shell and it has been so fun to see his personality come to life ever since. He is very interested in what I'm up to and if he's not sunbathing on the windowsill or loafing in his kitty cave, he's likely sitting right beside me purring his little heart out. He does this adorable thing where he comes to find me, headbutts me, and then plops himself down right next to me ensuring part of his body is touching mine. He frequently asks for tummy rubs and is one of those kitties you can pick up and cradle like a baby or gently dance around with. He's a gentleman about using his litterbox and he likes playing with his toys. He also likes going under the blankets and is a great nap buddy. Without a doubt, this handsome boy is something special and so ready to be someone's bestie ❤️

My foster previous writes:
This sweet boy has the most adorable personality. He loves rolling onto his back and showing his belly, basically asking for pets the second you walk by. With his big, beautiful green eyes, he always looks up at you like he's trying to start a conversation.
He's also a professional cuddler. His favorite place to sleep is completely underneath the blanket, all tucked in like a tiny burrito. At night, he loves to curl up cozily right between my legs, making himself the warmest (and cutest) little bed companion.
If you're looking for a loving, affectionate kitty who enjoys belly rubs and cozy snuggles, this little guy might just steal your heart

246953.name: Honey Jr.
246953.summary:
My foster writes: Honey Jr. is a lovely, gentle 10-year-old lady with kitten's soul. She's so sweet that she doesn't even know how to hiss! She silently follows you around, always hoping for pets and scratches. She's perfectly fine playing with her toys by herself or sleeping all day when you are not around.

A volunteer writes: Honey Jr is an attractive tabby who does not look her age of ten, a gentle dame who is with us as her family moved to a no pet- policy housing. Honey Jr is reserved but intuitive too. She is quiet at the back of her cubby, moves cautiously forward for treats and with gentle words, she slowly head bunts and leans into pets. Her coat is lush, silky, her eyes a tiny bit wary... What could she be doing in this kennel....Honey Jr  lived with adults only and liked to stay around people(family or visitors) when she felt comfortable. She seemed to prefer a calm life as well as people or circumstances respecting feline etiquette. Honey Jr behaved well upon arrival at the care center, put up quite properly with her medical examination and did well on her behavioral evaluation. She is already spayed, has a quasi normal senior blood panel and is ready to go home with you! This very private lady is waiting for you to discover her inner warm feelings. Come and meet Honey Jr very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Honey Jr. is a very sweet and slightly shy cat, who was inside her den, not looking out of the door. She did start to lean her head out to sniff treats, but only ate them when they were dropped inside her den. My foster writes: Honey Jr. is a lovely, gentle 10-year-old lady with kitten's soul. She's so sweet that she doesn't even know how to hiss! She silently follows you around, always hoping for pets and scratches. She's perfectly fine playing with her toys by herself or sleeping all day when you are not around. A volunteer writes: Honey Jr is an attractive tabby who does not look her age of ten, a gentle dame who is with us as her family moved to a no pet- policy housing. Honey Jr is reserved but intuitive too. She is quiet at the back of her cubby, moves cautiously forward for treats and with gentle words, she slowly head bunts and leans into pets. Her coat is lush, silky, her eyes a tiny bit wary... What could she be doing in this kennel....Honey Jr lived with adults only and liked to stay around people(family or visitors) when she felt comfortable. She seemed to prefer a calm life as well as people or circumstances respecting feline etiquette. Honey Jr behaved well upon arrival at the care center, put up quite properly with her medical examination and did well on her behavioral evaluation. She is already spayed, has a quasi normal senior blood panel and is ready to go home with you! This very private lady is waiting for you to discover her inner warm feelings. 247027.name: Tigre
247027.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Tigre!Tigre came to us as a stray with unknown history. Since arriving, she has shown herself to be a highly energetic and very anxious girl who is still adjusting to the shelter environment. In new spaces, Tigre becomes overwhelmed and seeks an exit, often pacing, bouncing between handlers, and struggling to settle. Despite her stress, she is food motivated and does seek interaction, showing that she is interested in people even when she's feeling unsure.

My Ideal Home
Tigre is looking for a calm, structured, adult-only home with experienced adopters who are prepared to work on anxiety and impulse control using positive, reward-based training. She will need predictable routines, clear boundaries, and gradual exposure to new environments to help her build confidence. Enrichment activities, food-based training, and patience will be key to helping her learn to settle and focus. Tigre will do best with someone committed to helping her decompress and providing steady guidance as she adjusts to home life.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for homes with children under 13. Due to Tigre's high anxiety levels, poor impulse control, and difficulty settling, an adult-only home is recommended at this time.

Good with Other Pets?
History with other pets is unknown. During assessment, results around dogs were inconclusive due to her elevated stress levels. Careful, slow introductions to any resident pets would be essential.


Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Tigre has displayed high anxiety, difficulty settling, and poor impulse control in the shelter. She requires an experienced, adult-only home prepared to provide structure, decompression time, and ongoing positive reinforcement training.

Other Fun Facts
Tigre is very food motivated, which will be a helpful tool in her training journey. With patience and consistency, this bright, energetic girl has the potential to learn new skills and build confidence with the right support.

A volunteer writes: Meet Tigre, the "Branch Manager of Queens ACC". (You'll see why). This sweet, adorable brindle girl has been overwhelmed in a shelter environment, and living in a pop-up crate since her arrival over two months ago (due to shelter overcrowding); but that doesn't stop her from having a good time. She greets me with a waggy tail and the sweetest puppy-dog face; and I love watching her happiness level go from 1 to 10 as she spots the plush toy in my hand and excitedly takes it before I've even fully opened her crate door. She carries it for her entire walk, then lies down with it when returned to her crate.

Tigre really enjoys playing in the yard - galloping around with her toy like a little horse and playing a gentle game of tug with her humans. And if she finds herself toyless? Well, she'll just pick up a tree branch if one happens to be lying around and carry it with her as she did on a recent walk - despite it being twice the length of her body! There she went briskly down the street with her oversized and lopsided branch dragging along the sidewalk.

We don't know Tigre's history, but she's really sweet, seems to be housebroken, is highly treat-motivated, and responsive to squeakers. With time to decompress and acclimate to her new life, I think Tigre will make a wonderful member of the family.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Tigre was great! she is very active and loved a long walk. she was also active in the house and played with toys a lot, but she calmed down after a little bit. she loves being around people. tigre is a great, fun, energetic girl!

247079.name: Nikki
247079.summary:
My Adoption Fee is Sponsored!

My foster writes:
Nikki is longing to be someone's baby! If you're her main human, she will ride for you immediately, being the most affectionate and loyal companion you'll ever come across. She's also very smart, picking up on new commands fast and loves a puzzle or mentally stimulating game! Of course, she's also always down for a long walk, splash in a puddle or tug of war. But mainly, she wants to do what you're doing! Though active, she is always down for a snuggle session or just laying around if it's with her human.
She does struggle with separation anxiety and fear of abandonment, but with time trust and the right human, she can for sure conquer this! 

Meet Nikki!
Nikki followed her finder home to ask for help and has been showing what a social, affectionate girl she is beneath her worries. She's active, playful, and very people oriented, often choosing to stay close to her humans and follow them from room to room. She enjoys cuddles, gentle attention, and has a soft, couch-potato side once she feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Nikki would do best in an adult-only home that can help her feel secure and supported. She needs a calm, structured environment where she can decompress and work through her anxiety at her own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
Nikki has shown mixed interactions with other dogs and can become overwhelmed during greetings, so she will need slow, carefully managed introductions and continued guidance.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to handling sensitivity, fearfulness, and difficulty with overstimulation.

Things to Know
Nikki is a loving and engaged dog who can struggle with anxiety, separation stress, and reactivity in stimulating environments. She may be sensitive to fast movements or handling around her collar, but she also recovers quickly and responds well to calm reassurance. She thrives with routine, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training that helps her feel safe and understood.

Fun Fact
Once Nikki feels safe, she's all about her people, think cuddles, kisses, and following you around like your very own little shadow.

A volunteer writes: There's something about little Nikki that just draws me to her. Maybe it's those big, brown, expressive eyes that always makes me wonder what she's thinking. Or maybe it's the way she stays so hopeful - happily greeting anyone who stops by her kennel - even as another season passes without finding her forever home. Or it could be the way she makes me smile as I watch her happily carrying her toy on our walks, occasionally stopping to playfully toss it around. Then there's the adorable way she asks for another treat by gently resting her paw on my wrist after she's finished the first (or second) one.

Nikki's previous family describes her as a social, affectionate couch potato who loves cuddles and spending time with her people. And true to form, Nikki spent her BoroughBreak snuggling up to her humans, lounging across their bed while soaking up pets, and handing out plenty of kisses. (To get the full heart-tugging effects, see the video in her profile). This sweet little baby with the big bunny ears has so much love to give and is just waiting for someone to see what the rest of us already do. Nikki is ready to charm you, so come and meet her today at the Queens ACC shelter


My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Nikki was such a good girl!! She doesn't bark, and though she was excited in the beginning and pulled a lot on her leash, throughout the afternoon she was walking easier and was less and less jumpy when she saw other dogs. When we went to eat at cafes, she didn't beg or try to eat the food- she was very patient and sweet. I noticed that she preferred to eat the treats in little bite sized pieces and often spit up the whole treats we gave her. She also likes to paw and spill her water dish so we found it easier to hold it while she drank. She loved water- anytime we were near a sprinkler or a stream of water she was so happy and playful. Nikki likes to jump up, but she is light and not aggressive at all. She likes to give kisses and likes lots of pets. She didn't mind us touching either her neck or paws, which was something noted on the original doc. I totally fell in love with Nikki- if my current lifestyle had room for a dog, I would totally consider adopting her.

247179.name: Faith
247179.summary:
Don't let Faith's age fool you, she loves a game of fetch, long walks around the park, and some water fun. Faith is perfectly house trained and a great communicator when she needs to go to the bathroom. Can be left at home for 4-6 hours. Faith LOVES her treats and thrives best with treat toys and other treat enrichment games. She is a very easy going dog and just looking for someone who can continue to boost her confidence and show her some TLC.

My foster writes:
My time with Faith has been so wonderfully sweet. She has the most adorable underbite; she sleeps so deeply all night, having happy dreams. She snores and purrs. She is a world class snuggler- the snuggling is my favorite. She rests her head on my head or lap or stomach and settles in for a relaxing evening. She is chill and waits for me on each staircase landing waiting for the go ahead to keep walking. We are constantly stopped for comments on her cuteness and joyful personality. Faith loves to walk too. She happily wags her tail, stopping to sniff along the way. She prefers A/C to bright sunlight.

Another foster writes:
Meet Faith, the ultimate cuddly potato puff! I've been fostering this sweet girl for 6 weeks, and she is an absolute delight to be around. Faith is the perfect blend of playful and relaxed; she loves trotting around the neighborhood to collect pets and snacks from the neigborhood "Aunties," but she is always happy to chill out in the park listening to jazz. She has zero prey drive, rarely barks, and greets house guests with perfect manners. She comfortably settles at home alone for 4 hours at a time, though would gladly spend every minute at my side. I have to head back to HI in a couple of weeks to my own dogs, and I miss her already. My biggest wish is that Faith finds the loving, stable home she so richly deserves!!

My foster writes: Faith is a sweetheart. She loves walks and sitting in parks and getting treats from her neighborhood aunties. Solid gold.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: On my borough break, Faith gave me the sweetest Sunday I could've asked for. It's impossible not to smile around her - her joy is completely contagious. We started with a trip to the pet store where she politely picked out toys and bones like a seasoned regular. Then we headed to Central Park, where she showed off her great leash manners, checked in constantly on walks, and happily worked for treats and basic commands. She was calm around food while I ate lunch, content to curl up under the bench or lean her whole weight against me for pets and scratches (her favorite thing in the world). The highlight of the day was watching her cautiously approach a shallow fountain... only to fully commit and splash around like it was the best day of her life. Everyone nearby was laughing and smiling at her happiness. Afterward, we found a quiet patch of grass where she stretched out for the deepest nap, and it was so easy to picture her in a loving home, snoozing beside her person on a comfy couch. When she woke up, she lazily rested her chin in my hand. We finished the day with a pup cup, which she enjoyed with impressive enthusiasm. Faith is truly such a special dog - sweet, gentle, goofy, and unbelievably affectionate. Between her giant ears, golden eyes, and adorable gummy underbite, she's impossible not to fall for. I genuinely cannot believe she's still waiting for a home. If I didn't already have a resident dog, I would've gone home with her that day. Whoever adopts Faith is getting a best friend who will wedge herself straight into your heart.

A Volunteer Wrote: If you think you're a people pleaser, wait until you meet Faith! This happy go lucky, mellow girl is all about pleasing, and will look sweetly into your eyes every other moment of your walk to make sure she's being a good girl! She's SUCH a good girl! She walks beautifully on a leash, and passes all dogs without a second glance during our time together; when it's time to stop for a rest, she hopped into my lap ever so gently and leaned in for comfort. Faith's former owner says she's playful with kids, and we are so hoping she'll have the chance to show that joyful side of herself again as soon as possible.

247375.name: Onyx
247375.summary:
My foster writes: Onyx is a very curious cat! Once she becomes comfortable with her environment, she likes to sniff around and investigate new spaces that she is not familiar with. Onyx is also a HUGE fan of tube cat treats such as Churu! Any flavour floats her boat!
With that being said, Onyx is also a spirit cat that is mostly nocturnal and comes out at night. She is VERY quiet even when she occasionally has zoomies chasing her toys, so she is perfect for anyone who is a light sleeper. During the day, you can expect her to be hiding in her cat house. During the night, she slowly comes out to explore. Her favourite activities are sitting by the window to enjoy the night breeze, and lying on a soft cushion. She currently still does not tolerate pets and becomes afraid when I get close to her, but she does tolerate me coming close when I have a tube of cat treat in my hands.
If you're someone with little time to play to allocate to play with a cat, but still prefers to have a cat companion at home, Onyx would be a great addition to your home!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Onyx tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.
247375.summaryHtml:

Onyx is also a HUGE fan of tube cat treats such as Churu! Any flavour floats her boat! With that being said, Onyx is also a spirit cat that is mostly nocturnal and comes out at night. She is VERY quiet even when she occasionally has zoomies chasing her toys, so she is perfect for anyone who is a light sleeper. During the day, you can expect her to be hiding in her cat house. If you're someone with little time to play to allocate to play with a cat, but still prefers to have a cat companion at home, Onyx would be a great addition to your home!

247382.name: Marbles
247382.summary:
Another foster writes:
Meet Marbles, an incredibly kind, loving, and playful companion with a sweet and gentle soul! From the moment you meet him, you will see just how smart and adaptable this precious boy truly is. Marbles thrives on love and affection, and he is happiest when he is just hanging out near his people, quietly keeping you company and soaking up all the attention he can get.
He has the most adorable way of communicating, using soft purrs and the cutest little chirps you have ever heard to let you know exactly what he wants. When he is feeling extra happy, Marbles loves to make biscuits and will stretch out right on the floor to politely ask for pets, especially his absolute favorite booty scratches, which will get him purring instantly.
His daily routine is a perfect balance for any household. If you keep him active during the day with interaction, he is wonderfully calm and relaxed all night long. If you are looking for a sweet, affectionate best friend who will fill your home with happy chirps and cozy snuggles, Marbles is ready and waiting to meet you!

My foster writes:
Marbles is a sweet, gentle soul. Very shy and slow to trust, but a sucker for head scratches and treats. We have never seen him exhibit any aggressive behavior. He loves his hiding spot and takes his time warming up to people. Surprisingly tolerant of vacuum cleaners compared to most pets. Largely prefers interacting with people from within a confined space or hiding space, rather than out in the open.

Notes from Foster Home:
Marbles is an incredibly kind, loving, and playful companion. From the moment he arrived, he showed how smart and adaptable he is. On his first day, he spent most of the time quietly observing the house from under our son's bed, taking everything in. By the very next day, he was confidently exploring and quickly became part of our daily routine.

He has such a sweet personality and a gentle way of communicating with us through his soft purrs and adorable little sounds. Marbles definitely knows what he wants, and he always finds the cutest way to let us know.

He loves his meals, especially wet food. We usually mix a little dry food into his wet food during the day, and he eats three times daily - at 8 AM, 5 PM, and 10 PM. His late-night meal is wet food only, which helps him stay full and sleep comfortably through the night without waking us up early. He was under nourished when we received him but with his new food schedule he has gained some weight and he looks very healthy. 

Marbles also loves attention, playtime, and affection. We keep him active during the day with lots of toys and interaction, so he's usually very calm and relaxed at night. After every meal, he enjoys either being brushed, playing with his toys, or sometimes both.

Most of all, Marbles loves kids and being around people. During the day, he'll come sit near us or quietly hang out wherever we are, just happy to be part of the family.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.
Marbles tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

247560.name: Puppy
247560.summary:
My foster writes: Puppy is one of those dogs who quietly steals your heart.
She's a sweet, gentle girl who can be a little shy when meeting new people or exploring new places. She appreciates slow introductions and a little patience, but once she knows you're safe, her personality shines. She'll greet you with full-body wiggles, happily curl up beside you for a cuddle, and look at you with the sweetest puppy eyes you've ever seen. (We're pretty sure that's how she got her name.)
Puppy previously lived with children and other dogs and has done wonderfully with both. She loves playing with canine friends. At home, she's just as happy chewing on a favorite toy, going for a nice walk, or settling in for a movie night. If you sing to her, she'll gladly listen. Belly rubs and forehead kisses are always appreciated.
She's crate trained, potty trained, and making great progress on leash walking. She does need daily exercise, about 45 minutes or more, along with chew toys to help keep her happy and engaged.
Like many dogs, Puppy gets excited when she spots a squirrel and may try to chase it, so she'll need someone who can confidently handle her on walks and continue working on her leash skills.
Puppy isn't the kind of dog who loves everyone the moment they meet. She's the kind who builds a real bond. If you're willing to give her a little time to settle in, she'll reward you with unwavering loyalty, endless affection, and a best friend for life

Puppy is a wonderful dog. At 2 years old, she is mature but still has a very nice energy about her. She needs a moment to warm up but once she does, she will bond quickly. This dog has had a lot of change and she has handled it beautifully; it certainly can't be easy being shuffled around to different homes. Gets along amazingly with my dog and my boyfriend. When I get her from her crate each morning, her tail is wagging and she can't wait to start her day. She would make a nice addition to any family. Loves to be outside but is also able to settle easily inside. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

247634.name: Starfire
247634.summary:
My foster writes: Starfire is a sweet, affectionate girl who just needs a little time to shine. But once she does, she's all love! She's talkative, loyal, and loves to stay close, happily keeping you company as you go about your day.
Her signature move? Flopping belly-up and purring to ask for pets.
Starfire consistently uses her litter box and has been easygoing in her foster home. She may be a bit shy at first, but with a calm environment and a little patience, she warms up into a loving, devoted companion.
She'd thrive as the only cat in a quiet home where she can be your one-and-only.
Looking for a cuddly, loyal shadow? Starfire might be your perfect match.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

247681.name: Spot
247681.summary:
My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! 

My foster writes:
Spot is looking for his perfect forever home. He loves pets and cannot get enough of belly rubs once he warms up to you, which doesn't take much time at all. Though he is not the most toy driven, he has a playful personality that shines when he is taken on walks and interacting with the outside world.
Outside, Spot is wonderfully curious and observant, always paying attention to the acute details and his surroundings. Inside, this docile boy loves a snuggle session and craves a good nap. Spot's cuddles have healing powers. Don't take our word for it, try it out yourself!
He is very treat/food motivated and loves to play with his enrichment mat and puzzles, and then wind down with a peanut butter Kong at the end of the day. If you are looking for the perfect cuddle companion to binge all your favorite shows with, look no further! 

Another foster writes: Spot completely stole our hearts while we were fostering him, and saying goodbye was incredibly hard. He is such a sweet, mellow, loving, and smart boy who truly just wants to be close to his people. Spot thrives on love, cuddles, and companionship, and he quickly becomes your little shadow, happily following you around no matter what you're doing. He loves deeply and forms strong bonds with his humans, always checking to make sure you're nearby even when he wanders off to explore. Around new people, he's incredibly gentle and affectionate-if someone offers a hand, he's more than happy to return it with kisses and cuddles. Spot gets excited when he sees other dogs and would wag his tail and pull a little on the leash in hopes of making a new friend, but he never showed any aggression. He also enjoys watching squirrels and rats, though with a moment and a small treat he's easily redirected. Spot does experience a bit of separation anxiety because he loves his people so much, but that devotion is part of what makes him such a special companion. We truly can't say enough wonderful things about him-he's the sweetest boy who will bring so much love to the lucky home that adopts him. 🐾💛

247682.summary:
My foster writes: Mr Mao is truly one of a kind! He is very sweet and social and will soak up all the love and attention that given to him. But at the same time, he doesn't need to be the center of attention. He is happy to be happy and will make a perfect family member! I believe he would thrive in any home! He is friendly around strangers including children! He does well when left alone. He is such a chill cat who wants to be loved, but does not need to be tended to at all times.He's such a special boy. He's just happy to be happy and loved.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

247724.name: Spice
247724.summary:
My foster writes: SPICE - SWEET BABY BOY LOOKING FOR HIS FOREVER HOME
Backstory/Journey

Spice has spent nearly 25% of his life in the shelter after being brought in stray/abandoned. He is such a sweet boy who has persevered despite his hard past. His demeanor is that of a puppy younger than his stated two years as is typical of puppies who find themselves living the shelter life.  Despite those obstacles, he possesses a stoicism and intelligence - as if his past has rendered him simply grateful for love and support. In foster, Spice continues working very well on his puppy manners with commands - sit, come, leave-it/no. He makes such a loyal companion; he is an affectionate (touch is his love language!), obedient, funny boy - patiently waiting for his forever home. 

Potty Trained/House Broken?...Yes. 
Crate Trained?...Sort-of.
Toy and/or Resource Guarding?...No.

Personality & Energy Level
Spice is goofy, playful and very smart. He has high emotional intelligence and a moderate energy level. Belly rubs are his standard and he LOVES to cuddle. He does get a case of the zoomies from time to time. Spice can be slightly fearful/skittish while he acclimates to new environments. He also is alert to sounds in close proximity to the home's front door. Supporting puppy development with enrichment serves Spice well. Spice loves the car, he loves looking out the window and sleeping!

Social Skills: Kids & Dogs
It is unknown if Spice previously lived with children; introductions should be careful/thoughtful. He has shown good demeanor with elementary aged children who had previous dog experience and moved slowly with him while playing catch in the park. Spice is "mouthy" defined as: a natural way for puppies to explore their environment and relieve teething pain. As an Adult dog, this usually stems from a lack of exercise, never learning appropriate play boundaries as a new puppy, and/or excessive stress (i.e. abandonment/shelter life). This is addressed with a consistent environment/routine - daily walks, affection and no-fear training.
With dogs, Spice is reactive particularly in crowded, busy environments. Spice is easily redirected with command of his short leash and verbal commands like "no Spice", let's go" and/or "leave it". We keep distance to ensure plenty of space for him. In foster, he did very well in suburban environments. He walks well on his leash, with zero to mild pulling. 

Home Time & Separation
Spice is housebroken and quiet. 
Like most puppies, he does best being with his human(s). His separation anxiety manifests as laying at the front door, whimpering & wandering- but with time he grows more trusting in being alone. A puppy cam would allow for check-ins (perhaps one that releases treats!). He has shown no signs of destructive behavior in foster, but he is very smart and knows how to stand to attempt to open doors. We do not know Spice's past challenges, but he is fearful of (and can escape from) pop-up crates. While he continues training on being home alone, puppy proofing is recommended.

He chooses the couch or his crate as a peaceful spot to nap and he sleeps peacefully through the night from his semi-covered crate - he prefers to see out a bit. Gentle bath time was good (doesn't love the dryer but what pup does!). He was also non-reactive to the washer/dryer and vacuum! 


Diet, Health, Exercise & Wellness
Spice's diet is currently GI focused. He is treat driven but won't hesitate to spit out something he doesn't like! He loves water (& really appreciates his water bottle on hot days)! Spice loves going on walks however he is being assessed for a healing hind leg(s) so walks (after he goes potty) are limited to 10-15 minutes and stairs avoided - current information can be discussed with his ACC team. 

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Spice!
This lively, affectionate boy is full of personality and love, and he's ready for a home that can keep up with him and help him feel secure.

My Ideal Home
Spice would do best in an active, adult-only home that can give him plenty of exercise, structure, and companionship. He prefers not to be alone for long and thrives when he has his people nearby.

Good with Other Pets?
Spice's interactions with other dogs have been mixed and can be a bit overwhelming for him. He would do best with slow, structured introductions or as the only pet while he continues to build confidence.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13, as Spice can become overexcited and benefits from an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Spice is a high-energy, affectionate dog who loves attention and will happily jump in for pets, playtime, or even a cuddle in your lap. He can get a little overexcited at times and will benefit from continued training to build calm behaviors and impulse control. He prefers company and may struggle when left alone for long periods, so enrichment, routine, and companionship are key. He also enjoys his toys and does best with positive "trade" games to keep things fun and safe.

247811.name: Fork
247811.summary:
My foster writes: Think of Fork as a curious girl who wants to be your friend, who just needs to feel safe first. Right now she is still shy and spends most of her time hiding away, but we often see her popping her head out the door to observe us. At night or when we are not looking, she comes alive doing zoomies, playing with her toys, and watching birds by the window.
Fork will benefit from a quiet and chill adult-only household with someone who has some experience with cats and understands their boundaries. She is very independent, so she would be a great fit for a working household.

Another foster writes:
Fork is a little, shy gal who is still learning to trust humans. She prefers quiet locations that are enclosed, like a cave-style bed, underneath cabinets, or litter boxes with a top. 247815.name: Jonah
247815.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Jonah interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience, demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

My foster writes:
Jonah 247815 is a soft, quiet soul with the gentlest heart you'll ever meet. He's never growled, hissed, scratched, or bitten- just a shy boy still figuring out the world at his own pace. He is a tiny, mysterious shadow who prefers to observe first... and trust later.
He's a bit timid and will sometimes hide when people are around, but with patience, he allows gentle handling and even enjoys soft head, chin, and neck scratches. There's a sweetness in him that feels earned - and that's what makes it so special.
At night is when he comes alive. He turns into a playful little hunter, zooming around, chasing teaser toys, and getting "locked in" on his imaginary prey like a mini panther. He loves rolling around with his silvervine/catnip stick, crunchy sounding toys, and watching the outside world from the window. He also has a hilarious sneaky side, especially when it comes to food - and some wonderfully goofy, expressive eyes.
Jonah would do best in a calm, quiet home where he can build confidence at his own pace. He hasn't met children and may feel overwhelmed in a busy environment. He's currently coexisting with another cat who growls/hisses at him, but Jonah himself remains completely non-reactive and gentle.

247819.name: Hilly
247819.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Hilly tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. 

My foster writes:
Cake and Hilly are the sweetest sisters who are ready for their forever home! These spunky, curious, playful, sweet girls have come so far from when they first came to our foster home. They are brave every day, exploring every nook and cranny, and have discovered how much they absolutely love to play.
Cake will do anything for a churu treat, and is learning how wonderful chin scratches are! Hilly is still a bit skeptical of human touch, but will be your best friend if you'll play games with her consistently. Seeing their growth is incredibly rewarding, and I'm positive there's much more learning and trust in their future.
They would do best in a home where they can sit next to windows and have dedicated play time most days, and though they may become comfortable around kids in time, they're still learning that humans aren't scary, so quick and unpredictable movements from kids might be too scary for now. They will likely hide when strangers come over, but will poke their heads in and out to investigate if people are calm enough.
No spicy behavior to report, except a few dust ups with each other when they have too much pent up energy. No aggression towards humans at all, and barely any vocalizing (except when they're trying to find each other).

My foster writes: Hi, we're Cake and Hilly! Over the last few months, we've been at a foster home where we've learned all about living with humans, and we love it!! Our very favorite activities are play time, and pet time. Any kind of toy is fun, but especially cardboard boxes, paper bags, and wand toys - we can't get enough of them. Before we came to foster, we didn't understand petting, it felt a little scary. But now, we know that this is the best way for humans to show their love, and it feels soooo good (especially on our chins!). We're not always in the mood to be pet, but can't wait for it when our humans wake up, and around dinner time.
Now its time to find a forever home. We'd love to find a forever human who can love us always and be patient as we continue to learn, and play with us consistently. If they're not always home thats perfectly fine, as long as theres a window open where we can hear the birds, and a comfy cozy nap spot. We can't wait to meet our human!

247898.name: Keto
247898.summary:
My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! 


Meet Keto!
He can be shy at first and appreciates slow, calm introductions to new people and places. Keto enjoys attention on his own terms - he seeks contact when he's comfortable, leans into people he trusts, and shows a soft, neutral wag when relaxed. Because he can be wary, moving at his pace and using treats and praise to build trust will help him settle in.

My Ideal Home
A calm, patient home where introductions to people and new routines are done slowly and respectfully. Keto would benefit from a family or adopter who understands canine body language and can give him predictable structure, consistent positive reinforcement, and daily mental and physical enrichment (long-lasting chews, food puzzles, games, and regular walks). A quieter household or one with older, respectful children will help him thrive.

Good with Kids?
No (not with very young children). Keto would do best without very young children under 5 due to his fearful/defensive tendencies. He may be open to meeting older children once he's had calm, supervised introductions.

Good with Other Pets?
Keto has greeted other dogs with some tension and vocalizing at the gate, so dog introductions should be slow and supervised. He's not strongly reactive on leash during assessments but would benefit from careful, controlled meet-and-greets. No reliable information about cats - assume unknown and introduce cautiously if considered.

Leash Manners
Keto shows mild pulling at times but follows a handler readily and responds well to movement and guidance. He can be distracted when loose in a new space, so short, positive training sessions on the leash and reward-based walks will help his confidence and focus.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 / Experienced or Patient Adopters - Keto has shown fearful or defensive behavior in some situations (barking/growling when first approached by officers). He needs adopters who will move slowly, use positive association techniques, and allow him to initiate interactions when he feels safe. No young children recommended.

Other Fun Facts
Keto loves to sniff and explore, follows his handler on short jogs, and will often lean in for contact once he trusts you. He responds well to calm encouragement and treats, and with a little patience he shows a sweet, affectionate side.

My foster writes: Keto is a great dog who deserves a loving home where he will feel safe and happy. He has been in ACC for about 100 days 😔 but it did not break his spirit. He is completely housebroken! He becomes affectionate when the mood strikes and may lick your leg or arm. He does not interrupt you when you eat. He may patiently sit politely and watch you eat but will not move to grab or sniff your food. He will gladly accept it if you decide to give him a piece. He speaks when you ask him if he wants to go outside by a couple of low barks. Very cute and impressive-he communicates! When you tell him to go lay down he will walk over to his bed and lay down and stay in his bed and not bother you. He will get excited to go outside and run around the apartment with joy a bit and will stick his neck out for you to put a collar on. Very cute. He will relieve himself as soon as you take him out. He knows going outside is for going to the bathroom. Please consider giving Keto a great home he deserves and has been waiting for. He is also very skinny and I would love for him to finally be home where he is love and spoiled.

247921.name: Koda
247921.summary:
My foster writes:
Koda is a very independent cat who values personal space. She can be selective with affection, greatly prefers quiet environments, and will take time to warm up. Sudden noises startle her, and she dislikes being handled. With patience, she'll coexist peacefully, though not particularly interactively, with her new owner.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

Koda may be a spirit cat!

Spirit Cats are very shy with people. They live in your home, but are rarely seen.
Visitors will probably never see them. They are cats who live with you, and who may
sometimes grant you the opportunity to touch them. Or, they may not.

Here's what to expect with these special cats:

· They're great with other cats! They are used to living with many cats, and are excellent
companions for other cats
· Over time, they will most likely get used to one or two people who will be allowed to
touch them. They may choose to hang out near you, or sleep on the bed with you at
night
· They are a great choice for people with a quiet household, who want to make a
difference for an individual cat. Spirit Cats require patience and understanding
· They are a fine choice for situations where you don't have a lot of time to devote to a
pet - most of these kitties do not need or want much attention from people

They won't magically turn into normal acting cats; what you see is what they will be
like for a long time, maybe always. Some will change more than others, but be prepared
for what you see now.

248018.name: Cookie
248018.summary:
Another foster writes:
Meet Cookie & Serena, two sweet besties looking for their forever home together!
Cookie is a calm, sweet, and noble boy with a quiet confidence. He's very independent and enjoys having his own space, but he'll happily follow you from room to room just to keep you company. He loves being near his people on his own terms and thrives with gentle affection and a calm environment where he won't feel overwhelmed.
Serena is his playful counterpart. She's quick on her paws, loves leaping onto the windowsill to bird-watch, and never passes up the chance to stretch out in a sunny spot for a cozy sunbath. She's curious, athletic, and brings a fun, lighthearted energy wherever she goes.
Together, they're the perfect balance. Cookie brings the calm, Serena brings the fun, and they absolutely adore each other. Whether they're relaxing nearby, quietly keeping each other company, or sharing a cozy nap, their bond is truly special. If you're looking for two built-in best friends who will fill your home with love, companionship, and plenty of adorable moments, Cookie and Serena are ready to meet you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am bonded to Serena 257062. We must go home together and our adoption fee includes both of us!

My foster writes:
Hi there! My name is Cookie but my foster parents call me Cookie Monster because I looooove food. Nom nom nom. Meal times are my favorite times. I'm also pretty clever and have mastered 3 different puzzle feeders so far (see my video). "That's one smart cookie!" they say. Next I'm going to learn how to fist bump like a pro (because I'll get treats for it). I also love to play, either on my own or with you! I had so much fun with my favorite toy (a catnip carrot) that there are pieces of orange fluff all over the floor ... oops. I came from a home with many other cats so I'm still not too sure about human attention, but with enough bribery and patience I'll probably get there. I enjoy playing chase with the resident cat and I make an adorable squeaky noise when I'm really interested in something or exploring something new. If you are ready to accept a squeaky Cookie into your home, I'm ready to move in!

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

My foster writes: Cake and Hilly are the sweetest sisters who are ready for their forever home! These spunky, curious, playful, sweet girls have come so far from when they first came to our foster home. They are brave every day, exploring every nook and cranny, and have discovered how much they absolutely love to play. Cake will do anything for a churu treat, and is learning how wonderful chin scratches are! Hilly is still a bit skeptical of human touch, but will be your best friend if you'll play games with her consistently. Seeing their growth is incredibly rewarding, and I'm positive there's much more learning and trust in their future. They would do best in a home where they can sit next to windows and have dedicated play time most days, and though they may become comfortable around kids in time, they're still learning that humans aren't scary, so quick and unpredictable movements from kids might be too scary for now. They will likely hide when strangers come over, but will poke their heads in and out to investigate if people are calm enough. No spicy behavior to report, except a few dust ups with each other when they have too much pent up energy. No aggression towards humans at all, and barely any vocalizing (except when they're trying to find each other). My foster writes: Hi, we're Cake and Hilly! Over the last few months, we've been at a foster home where we've learned all about living with humans, and we love it!! Our very favorite activities are play time, and pet time. Any kind of toy is fun, but especially cardboard boxes, paper bags, and wand toys - we can't get enough of them. Before we came to foster, we didn't understand petting, it felt a little scary. But now, we know that this is the best way for humans to show their love, and it feels soooo good (especially on our chins!). We're not always in the mood to be pet, but can't wait for it when our humans wake up, and around dinner time. Now its time to find a forever home. We'd love to find a forever human who can love us always and be patient as we continue to learn, and play with us consistently. If they're not always home thats perfectly fine, as long as theres a window open where we can hear the birds, and a comfy cozy nap spot. We can't wait to meet our human!

248029.name: Hamlet
248029.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Hamlet is at risk for behavior reasons. Hamlet is deteriorating in care. He was brought into the care center as a stray in February. Lately, Hamlet is becoming easily over-aroused during socialization sessions, jumping up and mouthing handlers with mild pressure. He can be difficult to interrupt in these moments. Medically, he has some dental disease.  

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Hamlet!
Hamlet is a young stray who was found running alone in a park, and he's now ready to find a place where he can finally settle into a loving home. He's affectionate, social, and full of big feelings and even bigger enthusiasm.

Personality
Hamlet is a friendly, attention-seeking guy who really enjoys people and interaction. He tends to "stage center" himself in new environments, happily approaching for attention and leaning into whoever is willing to give him some love. With guidance, he absolutely has the heart of a loyal companion in the making.

Out and About
On walks, Hamlet can pull with enthusiasm, especially when he's excited to explore. He's not bothered by people or other dogs passing by and generally keeps his focus forward, but he will benefit from continued leash training so his story doesn't turn into a tug-of-war drama.

Social Behavior
Hamlet is very social and loves engaging with people right away. He is affectionate, leans into contact, and enjoys being part of the action. He's comfortable with handling and tends to stay engaged once he's interacting, especially when he knows the spotlight is on him.

My Ideal Home
Hamlet will do best in an adult only home that can give him structure, consistency, and plenty of enrichment. He's still working on impulse control and manners, so he'll need a patient adopter who can direct him on how to turn his main character energy into calm, happy routines. He's smart, eager, and very trainable when given the right support.

Things to Know
Hamlet is still learning how to manage his excitement, especially around greetings and play. With positive reinforcement and steady guidance, he has all the ingredients to become a well-mannered and very loving companion, a true superstar.

Fun Fact
Hamlet doesn't believe in "to be or not to be" energy... he believes in "to zoom, to love, and to follow you everywhere." With the right home, he's ready to turn his story into a happy ending worth applauding for.

248097.name: Foxy
248097.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
Foxy tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: Foxy was given away at a deli and brought home to a family who really welcomed her. Recognizing her as a kitty who likes to do her own sparkly thing, they learned she can be friendly, affectionate, and playful when she's given the chance. We've also tried to welcome Foxy as best we can, but as we well know, the shelter isn't the same as a home. Foxy hasn't taken the shift to Care Center life as smoothly as we'd hoped and seems to be feeling a little shut down by all the big changes. Snuggled up in her cozy bed, Foxy seems to be trying to wish the day away but she accepts pets and has so much potential. She only needs a family to notice.

My foster writes:
Foxy is a cute and affectionate cat! While she is somewhat skittish and likes to come up to you when she is ready, she LOVES to be pet non-stop and play with strings. Her purr motor is always running, even when she is gazing out the window. She can get spooked if you make very sudden movements and run to hide, but she comes out of her hiding place a minute or two later ready to hang out again. Listen out for her tiny quiet little meows when she's ready to hang!

248218.name: Theo
248218.summary:
My foster writes: Theo is an engaged, people-oriented cat who loves to chase his toys, daydream while watching the world through the window, play catch with a stream of water from a sink or bathtub faucet and curl up purring on a pillow in the early morning. His strong build, markings and beautiful light yellow eyes look a bit like a sleek Turkish van - maybe his roots are far from here? So glad he came!

My foster writes: Theo is a friendly and playful guy! He will greet you with meows in the morning and when you come home. He loves pets and head scratches and will turn into a purr machine when he gets them, and may curl up for naps next to his favorite people. Theo likes to chase and jump after toys on a wand but also plays by himself with balls and his favorite catnip mouse.

A volunteer writes:
THEO is a 3 year old  gent I felt immediately a connection with as he was dropped hastily at the care center with just one word:his owner died. He looked so lost and I named him Theo after my dad who passed away. Theo was easy going as he was admitted to the shelter, became a little antsy with the veterinary team and a bit conflicted once in a kennel, appreciating petting but then hissing softly too. Overtime, Theo got accustomed to his new reality and is now quite a friendly and outgoing cat, really cute too in his pristine cow-print coat. Theo loves to exit his kennel to explore a little but is quite easy to put back in his kennel, accepting more petting and treats. He enjoys catnip toys and feather wands. Handsome Theo is an apparently healthy cat who is already neutered and so ready to go home with his new family. Come and meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Theo interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and allows all petting. We recommend that Theo go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression periods, and overstimulation.

248250.name: King Georgie
248250.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet King Georgie!
King Georgie is a big-hearted boy who came to us when his owner could no longer care for him, and he's now looking for a calm, patient home where he can feel secure and understood. He may start out a little unsure in new situations, but once he warms up, he shows a soft, affectionate side and enjoys leaning in for attention from people he trusts.

My Ideal Home
King Georgie would do best in an adult-only home or one with older, respectful children. He thrives with routine, patience, and gentle structure, especially while he continues building confidence in new environments. A calm home where he can decompress at his own pace will help him shine.

Good with Other Pets?
He has lived with small dogs and a cat in the past and has shown both interest and cautious behavior toward other dogs in the shelter. He may do well with slow, careful introductions and continued guidance as he settles into a new home.

Good with Kids?
While he has lived with children before, he can initially be unsure or vocal around them, so a home with adults or older, dog-savvy kids is recommended.

Things to Know
King Georgie is a playful, affectionate "couch potato" who enjoys toys, treats, and being part of the household routine. He can be sensitive to handling, especially around restraint and paw touch, and may bark or growl when uncomfortable. He also values his food and toys, so structure and positive reinforcement are important to help him feel secure. Once comfortable, he enjoys walks, cuddle time, and being near his people. With patience and consistency, he has a lot of love to give.

Fun Fact
Despite his royal name, King Georgie is really just a giant "baked potato" with a tippy-tap happy dance who melts once he knows you.

248284.name: Buddy
248284.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Buddy is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the prior home and in the care center, Buddy has displayed significant dog reactivity, including barking, lunging, growling, and fixation toward other dogs. During a fake dog assessment, Buddy approached with a tense body and briefly sniffed before escalating to growling, snarling, biting, holding, and shaking the fake dog. In his previous home, Buddy was described as a highly active dog who likes to spend time with people. Buddy did live with a cat and small mixed breed dog in his previous home, he was reportedly tolerant around both and friendly with the dog.  Around staff, Buddy is friendly, affectionate and loves to play in the yard. Medically, Buddy has moderate dental disease.

In the Care Centers, Buddy has been social with staff and engages well in training and pattern games, picking them up quickly. During his time with his previous owner, Buddy was involved in an altercation with another dog, which reportedly contributed to his reactivity toward other dogs. His owner stated that he believes Buddy may attempt to go after another dog while off leash. He did live with a small dog successfully. In Playgroup, Buddy displayed offensive behavior toward a fake dog, immediately becoming aroused before snarling and biting at the fake dog. Buddy should go to an adult-only home that can appropriately manage his behavior around other dogs using positive reinforcement training methods.

Meet Buddy!
Buddy was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and he's now looking for a stable, structured home where he can feel secure and understood. He's a high-energy, people-focused boy who loves being near his humans and enjoys toys, treats, and an active routine once he's comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Buddy would do best in an adult-only, single-pet home where he can fully relax without the stress of unfamiliar dogs. He thrives with structure, consistency, and calm guidance, especially in environments where he can focus on his handler and feel safe during transitions.

Good with Other Pets?
Buddy previously lived with a small dog, but he is highly reactive to most other dogs, especially medium to large ones. For this reason, he should be the only pet in the home and avoid dog parks or uncontrolled dog interactions.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children due to sensitivity around handling, restraint, and unfamiliar things. He will do best in a calm, adult-only environment.

Things to Know
Buddy is an active, affectionate dog who bonds strongly with his people and enjoys being part of daily life. He walks with a loose leash at times but can become highly reactive around other dogs, especially after a past negative experience. He is crate trained, knows basic cues like "sit" and "down," and is motivated by food and toys. He may become tense when restrained or startled, so slow introductions and force-free, reward-based training will be important for his success. With the right structure and support, Buddy has great potential as a loyal companion.

Fun Fact
Buddy's favorite things are simple: his people, a good baseball toy, and snacks, basically the perfect recipe for a ride-or-die best friend.

My straycation buddy writes: I would LOVE Buddy to find a permanent home; he would make any person or family happy, the affection he showed me on a short Straycation would be multiplied endlessly as a lifelong companion! From our very first Uber ride from the adoption centre he wanted belly rubs in the car! When we got to my apartment he made himself at home with ease; was excited and delighted to find I had tennis balls ready for him. He slept in his own bed all night with no whining or anxiety, went to his bed while I did chores, watched me wfh then indoor cycle, never touched my plants and didn't bother me once while I ate a ham sandwich as he sat beside me on the sofa - a perfect house guest! Speaking of the sofa: this guy LOVES to saddle up beside you, tuck in under your arm like a warm snuggly arm rest, he really gets his naps in! When I cam back from my 10x minute coffee run, he greeted me like I had been away for 10x years - he bounced around the room and ran over for more pets. This is an affection motivated boy, he loves chest rubs even more than snacks or toys. Buddy was the perfect Straycation guest, everything went well - this was my first time doing it and definitely will again.
Buddy is the ideal dog for someone who would love a dedicated and loving pet companion in their lives that doesn't need house training or any puppy madness, Buddy is a sweet, mature and independent guy but will follow you to the end of the earth (or just to the kitchen for a snack run). Buddy has the puppy energy when playing, follows you like a guard dog and his goal in life is just to hang out with you and be best friends!

248338.name: Buttermilk Biscuit
248338.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Buttermilk Biscuit!
Buttermilk Biscuit was found abandoned, but you'd never guess it from how much love he has to give. This sweet, slightly silly boy is affectionate, people-oriented, and always ready to lean in for pets once he feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Buttermilk Biscuit would do best in a patient, understanding home that can help him settle and feel secure. A calm environment with structure and routine will help him relax and show his best self.

Good with Other Pets?
Buttermilk Biscuit shows interest in other dogs but can become overwhelmed and frustrated in high-energy or barrier situations. He would benefit from slow, structured introductions and guidance to help him feel more comfortable.

Good with Kids?
No young children under 5, as he can become anxious and jumpy when overstimulated.

Things to Know
Buttermilk Biscuit is an affectionate dog who enjoys attention and will happily lean into pets. He can feel a bit anxious in new or busy environments, which may show up as pacing, panting, or extra excitement like jumping and grabbing treats a little enthusiastically. With time, patience, and positive reinforcement, he will learn to settle and feel more at ease. He's a soft, loving dog underneath it all, just looking for a place where he can finally relax and feel safe.

Fun Fact
Despite his name, Buttermilk Biscuit isn't just a snack, he's the whole comfort meal, warm, a little fluffy, and guaranteed to make you feel better.

My purr motor is always running!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
248352.summaryHtml:
