248376.name: Lucy-Belle
248376.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Lucy-Belle, the low maintenance companion with a world class wiggle while she politely carries her own toys. She is a chill soul famous for her side saddle sit where she flops her legs to the side to make sure her belly is fully exposed for rubs. Whether she is snoring through her signature deep naps or people watching at a restaurant, she is a master of the quiet life.
She is very respectful of other dogs and adjusts beautifully to their energy. If a dog wants to play, she goes right into a play bow, but she is just as happy to coexist peacefully if they aren't interested. She is a total dream on leash (although a but zig-zaggy lol) walking alongside her humans with a nice slack leash, making her a very calm and easy walking partner.
Lucy-Belle gives actual hugs and loves carrying a favorite toy in her mouth while her whole body moves in happy S curves around the apartment. She is a gentle, low to medium energy girl who is gaining confidence every day. Her cute cleft lip makes her uniquely charming and all she needs is a quick face wipe after her meals to stay looking her best. If you are looking for a sweet, soulful best friend, with positive energy, Lucy-Belle is ready to meet you!
See more on Instagram @nycacc_foster

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

248399.name: Dutch
248399.summary:
My foster writes: Dutch is a shy sweetheart with a playful side! Once he warms up, he is all about the love. He'll happily flop onto his back for belly rubs and always leans in for head scratches. He's got the best of both worlds - you'll catch him doing zoomies and chasing his toys, then later lounging like royalty on the cat tree. He's also very inquisitive with the resident cat and always comes running the second he hears the treat bag (Churus included, of course). If you're looking for a gentle, affectionate cat who needs a bit of patience to blossom, Dutch is your guy!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would like a home where there is another cat that I can play with!
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Dutch is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, he does attempt to flee and avoid human contact. It is difficult to predict if he will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
"Spirit cats" in a shelter context refer to cats who are very shy with people, preferring to live in a quiet environment and interacting with other cats rather than humans. They are often a good choice for patient, kind individuals who can create a safe and comfortable space for them to thrive. We cannot be certain whether or not Dutch will warm up to socialization in shelter or in a home environment and clients should be counseled on the potential of  Dutch being a Spirit Cat.

248418.name: Truffle
248418.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:

Truffle is the happiest and most loving dog! He is amazing with all humans and would make a great family dog. He loves to give kisses, enjoys belly scratches, playing tug-of-war and fetch while also being able to lay and watch a movie with you. He's great in his crate during the day and very polite at home. He will follow you around like he's your shadow. With a routine and consistent positive reinforcement he will thrive!


Truffle is a super loving and happy dog. He wants nothing more than to be by your side. He loves attention and lots of belly rubs. He's happiest even being in the same room with you while he plays with his toys. He's your perfect work from home companion. He would do best in a home with an outdoor space to let out some of his energy, but can also do well with someone who has an active lifestyle and can give him the exercise and stimulation he needs. He gets very excited when heading for a walk and is on full alert of his surroundings when outside. When he sees another dog he gets excited, but a quick tug will get his attention again. He needs structure and consistency, but with positive reinforcement and training he'll continue to learn and do great. His sweet face will completely steal your heart!

248419.name: Pan Keki
248419.summary:
My foster writes: Meet this adorable 1-year-old kitty with a playful personality and beautiful tabby coat. She's incredibly friendly, curious, smart and eager to get to know new humans in her life. Besides being your right hand pal, she enjoys playing fetch with her favorite red toy and laying in a sunny spot. She loves to explore her surroundings and be involved in whatever you're doing, but responds well when gently told to hop off the counter or leave things alone. In the morning, she asks permission to curl up in bed with you and chat about her night. Although she doesn't like being picked up she loves affection and closeness and has never been known to hiss or hide.
If you're looking for a playful, loyal companion, she might be your perfect match! 🐾

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
Pan Keki tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Pan Keki is a beautiful young girl a little over 1 year old. She was found in a carrier left in the lobby of an apartment building and a Good Samaritan brought her to us. I found her to be very sweet but she is reported to get a bit overstimulated at times, although I do no experience this. In my opinion she needs a home with individuals that can respect her space, give her adequate play time, perhaps with a wand toy (she loves feathers!), and is willing to let her set the pace. She is and amazing girl who loves to be pet and play!

248480.name: Guppy
248480.summary:
Guppy is the sweetest, prettiest, softest girl! She has been through a lot and still gets nervous, but her curiosity and love of love keeps her coming out and getting more and more comfortable in the world every day. She will continue to blossom in a safe, loving home!

My foster writes: Guppy is a sweet and beautiful, but shy, cat. She is still decompressing and learning to trust humans, so spends most of her time hiding. But every so often, she is open to a cuddle. In these moments, Guppy loves being pet! She rubs her face and body into your hand, rolls on her back to expose her fluffy tummy, and is comfortable being touched on her head, back, and feet. With time and patience, Guppy will surely come out of her shell and be a true cuddle queen.

248481.name: Happy
248481.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Happy tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

My foster writes:
Happy is very affectionate, friendly, curious and very charming cat. She is easy to get along. She loves snuggling, being petting, very active cat she wants to play all the time.
She follows you all over, very close to your feet as you walk. (be careful to not kick her accidently!)
She got along with my cat quite quickly, (even he may little annoyed of her..lol) she loves to go around, snuggle with him or me all the time. After 2 weeks of staying with us, she already has started to sleep in my bed with me and my cat. But watch out she bites sometimes.... I don't know the reason..
She loves to play! She loves to chase stringed toys and catch, she brings it to her favorite toy box and she gives big meows like she is proud herself. (or asking to play more.)
She also like to play with crumpled shiny ball.
She is chatty cat. She has different voices. It's funny and cute how she talks or meows.
She is very lovely cat. but she has bit issue about using litter box and biting habit I need to mention. She use litter box, but her pee goes out side of the litter box. (she stands up as she pees... ) I just ordered high-wall litter box. I can tell you how it goes later.
And she may not be good for house with little kids.
Because she bites sometimes. She is very happy cat, but then suddenly she bites. It happens at blushing time, or in the bed. (mostly in the morning)
I think it sometimes it meant to "stop" during the blushing, but other time, I am not sure why.
Happy is very sweet and very cute kitten. I am hoping she finds forever loving family who doesn't mind her little issue and work with, also who can spend time with her playing a lot. Because she loves it!!

248484.name: Sneezy
248484.summary:
My foster writes: Sneezy is an 11 month old, male cat with an adorable lop-sided white mustache. He started off his foster journey as a very fearful boy, but slowly became more trusting. He doesn't have an aggressive bone in his body! However, he does prefer to observe humans from a distance, and quick movements scare him easily. Sneezy loves to eat tube treats, watch birds from the window sill, chase his ball, and pounce on his feather toys. Sneezy is okay being left alone for long periods of time and is not a very destructive cat. He would be perfect for an owner looking for an independent, quiet cat (he NEVER meows!) and for someone who can respect his boundaries. An adult-only home with another cat or kitten is preferred. Over time, Sneezy has the potential to become less fearful and more trusting in the home of a kind and patient human!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Sneezy tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will likely need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

248591.name: Princess
248591.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Princess!
Princess was found as a stray and is now looking for a calm, patient home where she can feel safe enough to show her affectionate side. She starts off a bit unsure of new people and environments, but once she trusts you, she leans in for comfort and even seeks out lap time and gentle affection.

My Ideal Home
Princess would do best in an adult-only home that can give her space to decompress and allow her to build trust at her own pace. She needs a gentle, predictable environment where she is never rushed into interaction and can choose when to engage.

Good with Other Pets?
Princess has shown neutral to avoidant behavior toward other dogs in the shelter setting, but she should have slow, controlled introductions as she adjusts to a new home.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children due to fearfulness and the need for a calm, low-pressure environment where she can initiate contact on her own terms.

Things to Know
Princess is a sensitive girl who can be fearful at first, often observing from a distance before slowly warming up. Once comfortable, she becomes very affectionate and may even jump into your lap for attention. She benefits from patience, soft handling, and allowing her to set the pace for all interactions. With time and consistency, she reveals a very sweet and loving personality.

Fun Fact
True to her name, Princess prefers to choose her royal audience carefully, but once she does, you're officially in her inner circle of cuddle privileges.

A Volunteer Wrote: If Princess had a theme song, it would be "All I Wanna Do Is Have Some Fun!" She's a riot to be with, and has a contagious joy--she's like a child in the playground when she gets into the back with a ball, amusing herself to the point where I swear she was laughing as she chased it and ran around. She circles back for hugs and affection, and whatever fearfulness when she arrived as a stray has been replaced by wonderful exuberance. Come meet your wonderful playmate!

Princess would do best in an adult-only home that can give her space to decompress and allow her to build trust at her own pace. She needs a gentle, predictable environment where she is never rushed into interaction and can choose when to engage.

Good with Other Pets?
Princess has shown neutral to avoidant behavior toward other dogs in the shelter setting, but she should have slow, controlled introductions as she adjusts to a new home.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children due to fearfulness and the need for a calm, low-pressure environment where she can initiate contact on her own terms.

Things to Know
Princess is a sensitive girl who can be fearful at first, often observing from a distance before slowly warming up. Once comfortable, she becomes very affectionate and may even jump into your lap for attention. She benefits from patience, soft handling, and allowing her to set the pace for all interactions. With time and consistency, she reveals a very sweet and loving personality.

Fun Fact
True to her name, Princess prefers to choose her royal audience carefully, but once she does, you're officially in her inner circle of cuddle privileges. A Volunteer Wrote: If Princess had a theme song, it would be "All I Wanna Do Is Have Some Fun!" She's a riot to be with, and has a contagious joy--she's like a child in the playground when she gets into the back with a ball, amusing herself to the point where I swear she was laughing as she chased it and ran around. She circles back for hugs and affection, and whatever fearfulness when she arrived as a stray has been replaced by wonderful exuberance. Come meet your wonderful playmate!

248594.name: Deuce
248594.summary:
My adoption fee has been generously sponsored by an anonymous donor*! 

Another foster writes: Meet Deuce - a sweet, wiggly, and affectionate little guy with a big personality packed into a small body! Deuce loves people and greets everyone like a friend he's been waiting to meet, often with his signature full-body wiggle (especially his happy little butt shake).
He's a smart, well-mannered boy who already knows "sit" and "stay," walks beautifully on leash, and is both house trained and crate trained. Deuce is very easy to care for and quickly settles into a calm, cozy routine at home.
He does best in a cat-free home and enjoys being around other friendly dogs. While he may sometimes get excited and alert to hallway noises like a little "guard dog," he's sensitive, loving, and eager to relax once he feels safe.
If you're looking for a fun, affectionate companion who will keep you smiling every day, Deuce is your guy!

My foster writes: Deuce is a super wiggly and cute little guy who just wants to be your bff! He loves his walks, he loves to cuddle and he wants to learn from you exactly how to be the perfect gentleman. He's smart and tuned in and just wants to do the right thing. Any home (without cats!) would be even more complete with this super compact, smart and lovie little guy!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I would prefer someone who can be home with me most of the time.

A Volunteer Wrote: We didn't need to know that Deuce likes other dogs to fall head over heels with this little guy, but it doesn't hurt to know how sweetly he would reside again with other animals! He's overwhelmed by the hustle in the shelter but get him on the street, or in the back, and he's all about affection, walking perfectly on a leash and, once he's done his business, leaning in to get as close as he possibly can. What this boy really wants to get back to is a home, and any home would be so very lucky to have him.

*Please note that this does not include the dog license fee for NYC residents.

248776.name: Rugrat
248776.summary:
My #Borough breaker writes:
Rugrat is the sweetest boy, and so polite, mild mannered, and well-behaved! He smiles as he trots along, and so many people smile back at him. He sits attentively and loves gently taking treats from your hand. He is very mindful of people's personal space and listens well - When I asked him to pull over to the side of a busy sidewalk he did so immediately so the elderly could pass by. Then when I said "ok!" he would start walking again. He walks SO nicely on leash. He loves being pet and getting ear scratches and getting fawned over and admired by passersby, and he loves belly rubs and chewing on tennis balls. We went inside a dog-friendly cafe and he was so well-mannered, he sat and then laid down and was very relaxed.  His only odd quirk is that he wants to drink every possible water source so I tried to keep him away from running faucets, fountains and puddles, and just gave him clean drinking water in a water bowl. He decided to go up multiple sets of stairs in Central Park so he definitely likes stairs. He didn't display any resource guarding behavior throughout our 3+ hours together. He also didn't pull on the leash and didn't care for squirrels or birds. He wasn't reactive when spotting other dogs from a distance. He just likes strolling around the city and being in parks with people. I can see him being a perfect family dog for a family with kids 5 years old and up!!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

. I can't wait to meet you!

248787.name: Will
248787.summary:
Meet Will!
Will is a long-stay resident who arrived through NYPD after his owner experienced housing insecurity, and he's been waiting patiently for his chance at a fresh start. He's an energetic, social boy with a big personality who's ready for someone who can help channel all that enthusiasm into positive outlets.

My Ideal Home
Will would do best in an active home that can keep up with his energy and help him continue building impulse control through structure and enrichment. He thrives with mental stimulation like food puzzles, long-lasting chews, sniff games, and consistent daily exercise. He'll shine with a patient adopter who enjoys training and can help him turn his excitement into good manners.

Good with Other Pets?
Will should be the only pet in the home. He has shown strong interest in small animals at the shelter and has a reported history of conflict with other dogs, so a dog-free home is recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his exuberance and tendency to jump up, ACC recommends a home without very young children. He may be open to older, dog-savvy kids with proper introductions.

Things to Know
Will is a bright, affectionate dog who sometimes struggles with impulse control when he's excited. He may jump up, counter-surf, or become overly focused on food, but he is also responsive to handlers and enjoys engagement and training. On leash, he can pull moderately and occasionally fixate on treats, so continued practice with leash manners and structure will help him succeed. With consistency, enrichment, and positive reinforcement, Will has so much potential to thrive in a home environment.

Fun Fact
If you've got treats, Will already thinks you're his favorite person-and he'll happily prove it with all his goofy enthusiasm and nonstop charm.

248790.name: Pinto Bean
248790.summary:
My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! 

Meet Pinto Bean!
Pinto Bean was found tied to a bench in a park and has been showing us ever since that she's got a big heart and plenty of energy to match. She is social, people-oriented, and happiest when she has someone to engage with. With a little guidance, she really starts to shine.

Personality
Pinto Bean is a lively, affectionate girl who enjoys attention and connection. She may bounce between exploring and checking in with her person, especially when she's feeling excited. Once she settles, she enjoys affection and can be very sweet and engaging one-on-one.

My Ideal Home
Pinto Bean would do best in an adult-only home that can match her energy and provide structure. She's a great fit for someone who enjoys an active, interactive companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Pinto Bean has shown neutral, appropriate greetings with other dogs and is able to disengage and re-approach calmly. With thoughtful introductions, she may enjoy polite canine companions.

Good with Kids?
Pinto Bean is recommended for an adult-only home due to her high energy and excitement level.

Things to Know
Pinto Bean is strong on leash and will benefit from continued leash training and structure. She is very responsive training, especially when treats are involved. 

Fun Fact
Pinto Bean is always ready to "refry" your expectations of a shelter dog with her big personality and even bigger heart. She's got the kind of energy that makes every day a little more seasoned.

248807.name: Lady
248807.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Lady is at risk for behavior reasons. Lady is beginning to deteriorate in care, throwing herself at the kennel door. While out in the yard she can be evasive to return and may escalate to biting at the leash. She was surrendered due to not getting along with resident dog and is reactive to other dogs on leash. Medically, she has been treated for otitis externa. She is otherwise healthy.

Meet Lady!

Lady is a stunning young female dog with captivating eyes and a unique merle coat that's impossible to ignore. She's affectionate and social, thriving on human companionship and making every moment spent with her full of joy.

Lady loves car rides and is always ready for an adventure by your side. She's also impressively well-mannered, knowing basic cues such as sit, stay, paw, and get the leash.

Lady would do best as the only pet in the home, so she can receive all the love and attention she deserves. If you're looking for a loyal, loving companion who will brighten your days, Lady is ready to meet you!

249008.name: Snoopy
249008.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Snoopy!
Snoopy is a young, sweet, and social dog who came to us after being found tied to a gate. Despite that difficult start, he has shown himself to be very people oriented. He really enjoys attention and companionship.

Personality
Snoopy is affectionate, playful, and full of curiosity about the world around him. He enjoys meeting new people and tends to warm up quickly, becoming more and more affectionate as he feels comfortable. 

Out and About
Snoopy is energetic on leash and can pull moderately, especially when entering or exiting buildings. He does not show reactivity toward people or other dogs while walking, but he is very engaged with his environment and benefits from continued leash training to help him build consistency and manners.

Social Behavior
Snoopy is very social and enjoys being around people. In new environments he may be a bit distracted at first, often sniffing and taking in his surroundings, but he approaches handlers readily and seeks engagement. He accepts both soft and more active handling, though he may arch his back during contact as part of his excited response. He is affectionate and enjoys interaction, sometimes becoming very animated when he is engaged.

Play and Enrichment
Snoopy enjoys toys and play but can become tense and freeze when introduced to certain items, so he will benefit from gentle, positive exposure and guidance around play. He thrives with enrichment activities and enjoys interactive experiences like tug and exploring new environments.

My Ideal Home
Snoopy would do best in an active home that can provide daily physical exercise along with mental stimulation. He will benefit from continued leash training and structure to help him channel his enthusiasm in a positive way. He enjoys being involved in daily life and will thrive with adopters who appreciate an energetic and social companion.

Fun Fact
Snoopy is a social butterfly who loves being out in the world. On his borough break he enjoyed exploring parks, watching boats, playing tug, and soaking up attention from everyone he met. He is happiest when he is part of the action and close to his people. 🐾


My foster writes: SNOOPY 🐾
6-year-old Pitbull | "puppy playful" energy | Lover, not a fighter
Snoopy is the kind of dog who wants to be part of everything you do. He's incredibly smart, eager to please, social with dogs and children, and has a goofy, affectionate personality that still feels very puppy-like.
He would thrive with an active person or family - especially a runner, hiker, outdoorsy person, or someone who works from home and wants a loyal companion beside them all day. Snoopy LOVES movement, stimulation, and being included.
🐶 Personality:
• Playful, loving, social
• Very food motivated (but not food aggressive)
• Smart and trainable
• Loves praise and interaction
• Great potential with continued training
🍎 Favorite healthy snacks:
Apples, frozen blueberries, bananas, carrots, green beans, watermelon
Snoopy responds really well to praise and guidance.
Snoopy has all the ingredients of making someone willing to give him structure, exercise, and love very happy. ❤️
A Volunteer Wrote: Volunteers and his lucky Boroughbreak buddy agree that this dog is SO MUCH FUN! He's the sweetest, most hilarious guy, who adores his toys (if you let him walk with one in his mouth he thinks he's the luckiest dog in the world), loves treats, and worships people who will show him any attention. He showed zero interest in the dogs around us in the park, and just wanted to hop up on a park bench and lean in for some love. Someone will get so lucky when they offer up their heart space to Snoopy!

249010.name: Handsome
249010.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Handsome!
Handsome is an 8-year-old boy who was found wandering in a park, and now he's ready for a fresh start with someone who can give him the stability he's been missing. Despite everything, he's a bright, engaging dog who clearly enjoys being around people and soaking up attention.

Personality
Handsome is social, enthusiastic, and full of energy. He likes being involved and will readily approach people, often with a bit of extra excitement like jumping up to say hello. He's the kind of dog who wears his heart on his sleeve, sometimes getting a little carried away in the moment, but it all comes from a place of wanting to connect.

He can get a bit overstimulated during handling, especially when things get busy or fast-paced, so he does best with people who can keep things calm and help him settle when he gets worked up.

Out and About
Handsome walks with a mild pull and enjoys being out and moving. He does not react to people or other dogs on walks, and when greeting another dog at the shelter, he showed a soft body and a friendly wagging tail. With some structure, he has the potential to be a really nice walking companion.

Social Behavior
In new spaces, Handsome likes to explore and check things out, but he keeps coming back to his handler for interaction. He takes treats enthusiastically and can get a bit jumpy when excited, so he'll benefit from guidance around polite ways to ask for attention.

Home Life
Handsome will do best in an adult only home with someone who can provide structure, patience, and outlets for his energy. He's ready to learn and would really benefit from continued training to help him channel his excitement into calmer behaviors.

Things to Know
Handsome responds well to engagement and will benefit from consistent, reward-based training to build his skills and confidence.

Fun Fact
Handsome lives up to his name not just in looks, but in personality too he's got a big, expressive way of connecting with people that makes him hard to forget. 🐾

A Volunteer Wrote: A volunteer favorite and if we may say so, we are not wrong! Many, many volunteer notes on Handsome's walking log attest to how lovely it is to hang out with him, noting that we have seen nothing but impeccable manners and easy-going sweetness on his walks. On a stroll to the park, this sweetheart didn't even look at the dogs we passed, even as we headed out of the shelter which is filled with 'em. He's so smart, knowing his basic commands and always checking in, acting like such a good boy. His favorite thing? Of course treats, but mostly it's allll about affection for this sweetheart. Handsome is just fantastic in every way.

He can get a bit overstimulated during handling, especially when things get busy or fast-paced, so he does best with people who can keep things calm and help him settle when he gets worked up.

Out and About
Handsome walks with a mild pull and enjoys being out and moving. He does not react to people or other dogs on walks, and when greeting another dog at the shelter, he showed a soft body and a friendly wagging tail. With some structure, he has the potential to be a really nice walking companion.

Social Behavior
In new spaces, Handsome likes to explore and check things out, but he keeps coming back to his handler for interaction. He takes treats enthusiastically and can get a bit jumpy when excited, so he'll benefit from guidance around polite ways to ask for attention.

Home Life
Handsome will do best in an adult only home with someone who can provide structure, patience, and outlets for his energy. He's ready to learn and would really benefit from continued training to help him channel his excitement into calmer behaviors.

Things to Know
Handsome responds well to engagement and will benefit from consistent, reward-based training to build his skills and confidence.

Fun Fact
Handsome lives up to his name not just in looks, but in personality too he's got a big, expressive way of connecting with people that makes him hard to forget. 🐾

A Volunteer Wrote: A volunteer favorite and if we may say so, we are not wrong! Many, many volunteer notes on Handsome's walking log attest to how lovely it is to hang out with him, noting that we have seen nothing but impeccable manners and easy-going sweetness on his walks. On a stroll to the park, this sweetheart didn't even look at the dogs we passed, even as we headed out of the shelter which is filled with 'em. He's so smart, knowing his basic commands and always checking in, acting like such a good boy. His favorite thing? Of course treats, but mostly it's allll about affection for this sweetheart. Handsome is just fantastic in every way.

249190.name: Lenny
249190.summary:
Meet Lenny!
Lenny is a 5-year-old girl who was found running loose on the street and is now at ACC looking for a calm, patient home where she can finally feel safe and settle in. She can be shy in new situations, but once she relaxes, her gentle, affectionate personality starts to come through.

Personality
Lenny is a sensitive, quiet girl who takes her time getting comfortable with new people and places. At first she may seem unsure, but with patience she begins to settle, seek reassurance, and lean into gentle contact. Once she trusts you, she enjoys affection and often shows her softer side by resting her head on people for comfort.

Out and About
Lenny walks with a loose leash and a steady pace. She does not react to people or other dogs she passes and generally follows her handler calmly. She benefits from predictable routines and gentle guidance, especially in busier environments where she may initially feel overwhelmed.

Social Behavior
In new environments, Lenny may be hesitant at first, but she softens with time and reassurance. She allows petting once comfortable and often responds to calm interaction by settling into a seated position and leaning into touch. Her comfort grows best when she is given space to approach things at her own pace.

Home Life
Lenny will do best in an adult only, single pet home that can offer patience, consistency, and a calm environment. Slow introductions to new people and places will help her continue building confidence. She has strong potential to become a loyal, steady companion once she feels secure.

Things to Know
Lenny has medical needs that staff will discuss with adopters. She thrives with gentle, force-free handling and will do best in a home that understands shy dogs and allows her to progress at her own pace.

Fun Fact
Lenny may be reserved at first, but once she feels safe, she becomes a quiet, comforting companion who just wants to stay close and lean in for affection. 🐾

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

249207.name: Numo
249207.summary:
Another foster writes:
Meet Numo! This handsome gray boy is the quintessential cat: curious, independent, and laidback. He's a clever kitty who adjusts well to new routines and will make himself at home in all the best hiding spots he can find, and whenever he's a little overwhelmed by a new experience, he'll self-soothe by retreating to one of his safe spaces. He loves playtime with people equipped with feathery wand toys, and is just as happy to amuse himself hunting toy mice and springs and scratch pads. Numo is used to living with people and thus accustomed to human voices (he likes if you narrate your day to him) and typical household noises (TVs, neighboring apartment doors slamming, even the vacuum!), and he doesn't mind visitors. He keeps a tidy litterbox, doesn't make a mess at mealtimes, doesn't bite or scratch at people, and can be left alone to hold down the fort while his humans are at work or school; no worries about him making a mess, he's very polite. And while he's not a big cuddler, Numo shows his love by lounging around near his people and offering leisurely slow blinks - but he makes an exception when he's offered a Churu squeeze-up, which will bring him right into your lap at snack time.

My foster writes:
Big head. Bigger heart. Takes a little while to show it.
Numo had a rough start: abandoned, then shelter life, then a brand new home with a stranger. Understandably, he was not immediately thrilled.
He spent his first few days under the bathroom sink giving everyone his best scary face. It did not work because he is very plush and his head is extremely round.
Slowly but surely, Numo decided that maybe humans were okay actually. Then he discovered toys. Then zoomies. Then cuddles. Now he is simply a big soft boy who loves to play and wants you to know he was never scared. He was just being cautious. Please respect his privacy on this matter.
Numo is looking for a home that will appreciate his dramatic backstory, his chonky head, and his very important opinions about blanket arrangement.
He is worth the wait!

A volunteer writes: Right now, Numo should be hanging with his people in his home, lazing around the couch and chasing the occasional bug. But this gorgeous gray boy's family recently moved and didn't take him with them. Ever since, he's been down in the dumps--preferring to hide in the den in his cat condo rather than engage with humans and make friends. It's a tough blow to get over, but we just know Numo has what it takes to come out of his shell and find a real forever home where he'll never again be left behind. If you're the kind of cat parent who has a soft spot for shy guys and knows how to help them blossom, Numo would love to meet you.

249220.name: Leon
249220.summary:
My foster writes; Léon is still a shy young boy but is becoming braver and has come closer to me lately because I have TREATS! He is a great conversationalist and chirps and talks to me. He has a cute little face, a very handsome longish fur coat and a fluffy tail- all in all a beautiful boy. He loves to play with his fishing rod-and-feather toy and with balls with bells inside.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Leon tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

A volunteer writes: Leon puts on his bravest face for as long as he can when he tries to convince himself to join in. Sitting right by the front, he really wants to try, but as many of us know, it's often easier said than done. Brought to us from a home with other cats, Leon's known to play gently and be friendly and outgoing with them. Perhaps a bit of a social butterfly at heart, but with a teeny tiny caveat. Leon isn't always sure about new people, which adds a bit of a wrench to shelter life. With wide eyes and puffed cheeks, Leon kind of scrunched himself from me when I opened his cubby door but since we know the results don't always match the efforts, I also knew to explain that all he needs to do is keep trying and his forever family will see.

249221.name: Jackson
249221.summary:
Meet Jackson!
Jackson was found tied up behind a building and is now looking for a calm, stable home where he can feel safe and understood. He is a sensitive boy who is still learning to trust new environments, but he shows curiosity about people and other dogs once he has time to adjust. 

My Ideal Home
Jackson would do best in a quiet, adult-only home that can offer consistency and a low-pressure environment. A calm routine will help him build confidence over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Jackson has shown soft, appropriate behavior when greeting other dogs, including loose body language and interest through the gate. He may benefit from slow, structured introductions to compatible dogs in a calm setting.

Good with Kids?
Jackson is recommended for a home without children under 13 due to his fearful nature and need for a quiet, predictable environment.

Things to Know
Jackson is still building confidence in new spaces and may show hesitation in unfamiliar areas. He responds best to patience, consistency, and a calm approach.

Fun Fact
Jackson may start off a little unsure, but he has a sweet, soft energy that comes through once he feels safe. With the right home, he has all the makings of a loyal, steady companion.

249270.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I am FIV+ and am enjoying a healthy, full life!
Cherry tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to his/her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

My foster writes:
Cherry is the kind of cat who chooses you and then never leaves your side.
She is incredibly affectionate and will follow you through your entire day, quietly keeping you company whether you are working, eating, reading, or resting.
She loves to curl up right next to you or on your blanket, often falling asleep with a soft purr that feels instantly calming.
Her fur is very soft, and she enjoys gentle head rubs and even belly pets when she feels safe.
Cherry is playful and lively, with a cute "cow cat" pattern that makes her extra memorable.
She loves making biscuits, showing how much she trusts and feels at home with you.
If you are looking for a sweet, loyal companion who truly wants to share your everyday life, Cherry will be right there with you. 🐾

249278.name: Mama
249278.summary:
My foster writes: Mama is the sweetest little soul you could ever meet. She has an adorably soft voice, a calm gentle personality, and the cutest way of quietly coming over to rub her head against your leg. She starts purring before you even pet her, as if she's already grateful for the love.
Mama is easygoing, low-energy, and wonderfully peaceful. She can be picked up, have her nails clipped, and handled with ease. She has never shown any aggression-just quiet trust, soft purrs, and lots of gentle affection. If you're looking for a cozy, loving companion who feels like a warm little cushion for your heart, Mama is your girl.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
Mama appreciates attention and petting with a slow approach but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to an adult-only home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

249362.name: Big Foot
249362.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Big Foot is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Big Foot was returned to the shelter due to behavior reported by his recent adopter. Big Foot was reported to be highly reactive to people when on leash; noted to growl, bark, and lunge when seeing people on walks. In shelter, Big Foot is noted to have inconsistent, reactivity towards unfamiliar people on walks and visually fixate on dogs.  During his previous and current stay, Big Foot is often described as 'easy walk' for the majority of his interactions.  He continues to be very social with staff, and allows all contact with a soft body, including medical exams. Medically, Big Foot is noted to have otitis externa due to suspected allergies but is otherwise healthy.

Big Foot was returned to the shelter due to behavior reported by his recent adopter.  Big Foot was reported to be highly reactive to people when on leash; noted to growl, bark, and lunge when seeing people on walks.  In shelter, Big Foot is noted to have brief, low level reactivity towards unfamiliar people and visually fixate on dogs.  During his previous and current stay, Big Foot is often described as 'easy walk', very social with staff, and allows all contact with a soft body.  We recommend placement with an experienced New Hope Partner that can carefully manage his behaviors. 

My foster writes: He is very calm, gentle, and affectionate. He just wants to be near you and spend time together. He is very good companion. He is a truly great dog.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Big Foot is the ultimate 'leaner' he has this precious habit of leaning his weight against your legs when he's standing next to you just to be close. He is incredibly well-behaved; he walks beautifully on a leash and is a total pro at 'sit' and 'down' on command. He's a gentle soul who perfectly balances being an active walking partner with being a world-class cuddler. Safe to say if i was in a position to adopt, I would have submitted my application then and there.

My Boroughbreak buddy writes:
Big Foot is the sweetest, most well-behaved, goofy pup!
 I was so impressed with his manners! He was so polite while waiting for breakfast and dinner, sitting and watching, waiting to eat until I gave him the go ahead. Potty-trained and did not even attempt to chew on anything that wasn't his toy. He did not jump on any counters or scratch any doors. He knew how to sit and lay down. He did great sleeping in his crate at night. He walked great on a leash and was happy and excited to meet new people, greeting them with a wagging tail!
He was the most flexible and loving guy. He was so excited to go for walks and play, but also more than happy to chill and take some naps in his crate. He enjoyed tug of war and chasing after his squeaky ball. He also liked to chew on his bone before he got too sleepy and would fall asleep. If I sat on the floor, he would come over and either sit in my lap or lay down with his head in my lap. He just wants to cuddle up and be with you. He was overall just a happy boy and just wanted to be around you, regardless of whether that was on a walk, cuddling, or just in your presence. He's got the biggest heart and is so easy to love!

My Boroughbreaker writes : Walked over to Central Park and spent some time sniffing around the grass while waiting for a friend to arrive. Big Foot enjoyed all of the smells and getting to observe the birds and dogs, but he never once lunged or jumped at any of them. We practiced redirecting attention from other dogs with treats and he did very well. He knows how to sit and lay down and I guarantee he would become a star with commands if he had a consistent person around! He loves treats as a reward! We did not have toys but he eyed all the soccer balls at the park so I'm sure he would love some of his own! After our ~10 block walk through upper Central Park we stopped at a cafe and sat outside. He did well standing/sitting or laying down next to our table and would either watch people walking by or watch for food crumbs. But he never begged for food but enjoyed getting some treats tossed. He also needed a couple water breaks. He was great at walking on a leash and loved to get cuddles and belly rubs when we sat down. He truly was the calmest most UNreactive dog ever!

My Boroughbreaker writes: We walked around Central Park and went for a treat at Petco! He is such a sweetheart and is truly a gentle giant! He was happy exploring and walking around and loved to plop down on some soft grass for belly rubs. This pup is a true gem and shouldn't be spending his time in a shelter! If anyone has been thinking of getting a pup, Big foot is ready for his forever home and would make an amazing addition to a loving household!

Volunteers Note: Big Foot is a wonderful, 74-pound gentle giant who is incredibly affectionate, confident, and a breeze to walk on a loose leash. He is highly responsive to handlers, loves treats, and shows plenty of potential with training. Big Foot is a happy boy and full of life. He will make a fantastic, loving companion for an active family with older children.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I will need daily physical activity to

In shelter, Big Foot is noted to have inconsistent, reactivity towards unfamiliar people on walks and visually fixate on dogs. During his previous and current stay, Big Foot is often described as 'easy walk' for the majority of his interactions. He continues to be very social with staff, and allows all contact with a soft body, including medical exams. Medically, Big Foot is noted to have otitis externa due to suspected allergies but is otherwise healthy. Big Foot was returned to the shelter due to behavior reported by his recent adopter. Big Foot was reported to be highly reactive to people when on leash; noted to growl, bark, and lunge when seeing people on walks. In shelter, Big Foot is noted to have brief, low level reactivity towards unfamiliar people and visually fixate on dogs. During his previous and current stay, Big Foot is often described as 'easy walk', very social with staff, and allows all contact with a soft body. We recommend placement with an experienced New Hope Partner that can carefully manage his behaviors. My foster writes: He is very calm, gentle, and affectionate. He just wants to be near you and spend time together. He is very good companion. He is a truly great dog. My Boroughbreaker writes: Big Foot is the ultimate 'leaner' he has this precious habit of leaning his weight against your legs when he's standing next to you just to be close. He is incredibly well-behaved; he walks beautifully on a leash and is a total pro at 'sit' and 'down' on command. He's a gentle soul who perfectly balances being an active walking partner with being a world-class cuddler. Safe to say if i was in a position to adopt, I would have submitted my application then and there. My Boroughbreak buddy writes: Big Foot is the sweetest, most well-behaved, goofy pup! I was so impressed with his manners! He was so polite while waiting for breakfast and dinner, sitting and watching, waiting to eat until I gave him the go ahead. Potty-trained and did not even attempt to chew on anything that wasn't his toy. He did not jump on any counters or scratch any doors. He knew how to sit and lay down. He did great sleeping in his crate at night. He walked great on a leash and was happy and excited to meet new people, greeting them with a wagging tail! He was the most flexible and loving guy. He was so excited to go for walks and play, but also more than happy to chill and take some naps in his crate. He enjoyed tug of war and chasing after his squeaky ball. He also liked to chew on his bone before he got too sleepy and would fall asleep. If I sat on the floor, he would come over and either sit in my lap or lay down with his head in my lap. He just wants to cuddle up and be with you. He was overall just a happy boy and just wanted to be around you, regardless of whether that was on a walk, cuddling, or just in your presence. He's got the biggest heart and is so easy to love! My Boroughbreaker writes : Walked over to Central Park and spent some time sniffing around the grass while waiting for a friend to arrive. Big Foot enjoyed all of the smells and getting to observe the birds and dogs, but he never once lunged or jumped at any of them. We practiced redirecting attention from other dogs with treats and he did very well. He knows how to sit and lay down and I guarantee he would become a star with commands if he had a consistent person around! He loves treats as a reward! We did not have toys but he eyed all the soccer balls at the park so I'm sure he would love some of his own! After our ~10 block walk through upper Central Park we stopped at a cafe and sat outside. He did well standing/sitting or laying down next to our table and would either watch people walking by or watch for food crumbs. But he never begged for food but enjoyed getting some treats tossed. He also needed a couple water breaks. He was great at walking on a leash and loved to get cuddles and belly rubs when we sat down. He truly was the calmest most UNreactive dog ever! My Boroughbreaker writes: We walked around Central Park and went for a treat at Petco! He is such a sweetheart and is truly a gentle giant! He was happy exploring and walking around and loved to plop down on some soft grass for belly rubs. This pup is a true gem and shouldn't be spending his time in a shelter! If anyone has been thinking of getting a pup, Big foot is ready for his forever home and would make an amazing addition to a loving household! Volunteers Note: Big Foot is a wonderful, 74-pound gentle giant who is incredibly affectionate, confident, and a breeze to walk on a loose leash. He is highly responsive to handlers, loves treats, and shows plenty of potential with training. Big Foot is a happy boy and full of life. He will make a fantastic, loving companion for an active family with older children.

249366.name: Bella Noche
249366.summary:
My foster writes: Bella Noche is a gentle, sweet-natured cat who's just waiting for the right home to feel safe. At first she may be a bit shy, but give her a little time and you'll discover a sweet companion. She'll happily greet you throughout the day for meals, playtime, and quiet company.
Bella Noche enjoys chasing balls and her favorite stuffed mouse-but she'll also delight you with a game of fetch when you join in! While she's not a lap cat, she shows her affection in her own special way, coming up to you for pets and occasionally stopping by for a quick couch visit.
She prefers a calm, peaceful home where she can feel safe and move at her own pace. Loud noises and fast movements can startle her, but with patient, loving people, Bella blossoms into a truly wonderful companion.
If you're looking for a low-key, playful, and quietly affectionate kitty, Bella Noche might just be your perfect match.

Bella Noche is laying in her den, head up, ears forward, eyes wide, and pupils dilated, poking her head out of the portal exit as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she ducks back into the den, poking her head out of the portal exit when she is softly spoken to. Crunchy treats are offered and she hesitantly leans forward to sniff at them before beginning to eat one. When the assessor offers their hand, she leans forward and softly head bunts it, leaning in and closing her eyes when she is pet on the head, cheeks, and under her chin. It takes a few minutes of petting and soft talk but she is able to be coaxed to the front of the kennel. She cranes her head to look out towards the hallway when noises occur outside of the room, tensing, but continues to allow all petting. She periodically is startled by loud sounds and runs back into the den but continues to be able to be coaxed back out to the front of the kennel where she allows and leans into all petting. She is able to be easily picked up but does squirm to be placed back down when she is held. When placed back into the kennel, Bella Noche walks back into her den, continuing to poke her head out of the portal exit and lean in and close her eyes when pet on the head and cheeks.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Bella Noche is a very sweet but shy lady, who enjoys attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful and stressed in the shelter. She may need time to warm up to her new home and appears to respond well to soft talk, crunchy treats, and a slow approach. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

249415.name: Fluffy
249415.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Fluffy is on the at-risk list for medical concerns. Fluffy is a 10 year old cat with diabetes and obesity. He will need insulin administration twice daily and regular veterinary visits for diabetes follow-up. Behaviorally, Fluffy has been very interaction and loves petting.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
My purr motor is always running!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

A volunteer writes: Embracing his unconventional living arrangements and unique designation of resident cat seal, Fluffy stretches out on his giant bed in his enormous dog crate to half roll over and show us his belly. He's currently staying in our medical wing because of some medical needs, hence the crate and bed, but Fluffy seems to emphatically say with every chirp, nuzzle and headbunt that these are just things and what he really wants are friends. A terrifically social senior gentleman, he bounced around a little bit before arriving at his most recent guardian where he was a friendly and quiet couch potato, playing when interested but with a sweet gentleness. Fluffy's now with us looking for a forever home and he's hoping that you'll come in and visit him soon.

249431.name: Kobe
249431.summary:
Meet Kobe!
Kobe is a social and affectionate dog who was surrendered when his owners could no longer care for him due to housing insecurity. He loves being near people and enjoys simple pleasures like car rides, water, and chew time with his favorite toys and bones.

My Ideal Home
Kobe would do best in a calm, structured adult-only home where he can feel secure and understood. He is house trained, enjoys a routine of daily walks, and already knows cues like his name and "stay." He will thrive with patient, force free training that helps him build confidence and reinforce calm behaviors.

Good with Other Pets?
He is recommended as a single pet home and should not visit dog parks. He will do best as the only animal in the home.

Good with Kids?
Due to fear responses and sensitivities observed in care, Kobe is recommended for an adult-only home at this time.

Things to Know
Kobe is a medium energy dog who enjoys walks and engagement with his people, but he can become fearful in unfamiliar or stressful situations. He may pull on leash and can react to other dogs, so he will need supportive equipment like a front clip harness and ongoing positive reinforcement training. He also shows strong interest in toys and can become protective of them, so trade up games and teaching a "drop" cue will be important. Kobe is sensitive to handling at times, especially around restraint or touch of his paws and collar, so a slow, choice based approach will help him feel safe. With structure, patience, and consistency, Kobe has a lot of potential to be a loving and loyal companion.

Fun Fact
Kobe's favorite thing in the world might be a good chew toy followed closely by a car ride adventure with his favorite person.

249438.name: Slips
249438.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Slips is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

A volunteer writes: I spent some time with Mr. Slips today, and now that he's more adjusted to the Care Center, he seems like a totally different cat than his earlier notes state: I found him to be playful, gentle, and a lover of any and all human interaction. This handsome youngster waited patiently for me to approach his kennel, and when I did he greeted me with some hearty meows and an invitation to bat around a feather toy. He took a break to munch some chow, then lay down on his side and rolled around to reveal his belly, a sign of trust. Slips really is a fan of humans, and the perfect new pet parent for him is someone who keeps a pile of toys on hand and gives him one-on-one time. He's the kind of cat who will cheer you up when you're feeling blue, listen to you when you talk about your day, and never turn down the opportunity to just hang and enjoy your company. Meet this handsome boy at the Manhattan Care Center today!

249510.name: Stoney
249510.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Meet Stoney! While he has a serious-sounding name, this pup's affectionate, playful, and gentle personality shines bright. Stoney loves his people, wanting to be close to you when you're home, and always game for a pat or snuggle. While he's often snoozing on the couch, when he is awake and active he's got a playful side that makes him interactive and fun - he adores every kind of toy (squeaky tennis balls are his fave), and will happily toss and pounce on his toys to entertain himself. He loves to play with people and get attention, and will often initiate play, but can be redirected with a Kong or other toy when you're busy. He's also a smart cookie who relishes the challenge of finding food in a complex puzzle toy or Kong. Stoney LOVES food, and his treat motivation and fondness for people make him highly trainable! He already knows "sit" and "paw", and would probably love to learn more tricks. Stoney is generally calm and well-behaved on walks, passing people and other dogs without incident. He does get excited and pulls when he encounters a squirrel or rat nearby, but on the flip side he'll happily help keep vermin out of your neighborhood! Stoney is housetrained and is polite and friendly when meeting new people. He can sometimes need a reminder to keep "four-on-the-floor" when meeting a new person or when near the kitchen counter, but he's a good listener and responds well to redirection. Stoney's past may be a mystery, but with such a playful and loving personality, his future is bright! If you're looking for a dog with lots of love to give and whom you can spoil with all the toys, Stoney just might be your guy!

Meet Stoney!
Stoney is a striking, sensitive boy who was found tied near a warehouse and is now looking for a calm home where he can build confidence at his own pace. He can be a little cautious in new situations but shows curiosity, engagement, and a softer side once he feels comfortable. He enjoys exploring and responds well to patient, gentle handling.

My Ideal Home
Stoney will do best in a quiet, adult-only home that can provide structure, predictability, and a slow introduction to new experiences. He benefits from a calm environment where he is not rushed and can choose when to engage.

Good with Other Pets?
Stoney shows interest in his surroundings and can be curious around other dogs, but he is sensitive and benefits from slow, controlled introductions. A calm, well-matched dog may work, or he may also do well as the only pet, depending on management and fit.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to sensitivity during handling and need for a low-stimulation home environment.

Things to Know
Stoney is observant, food-motivated, and already shows interest in learning cues like sit. He can be flinchy around neck handling and needs a gentle, patient approach that allows him to build trust over time. He enjoys sniffing, exploring, and settles best when given space and reassurance.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer notes that Stoney immediately stands out for his striking eyes and gentle energy once he is out of his kennel. While he may show signs of a difficult past, he quickly reveals a sweet, intelligent dog who is eager to learn and connect. He responds beautifully to food rewards and already shows off a reliable sit, offering his attention in exchange for praise and treats. On walks, he can be initially nervous around unfamiliar sights, but he settles into a calmer rhythm with reassurance and shows moments of curiosity and softness as he gains confidence.

249530.name: Cold Foam
249530.summary:
Meet Cold Foam!
Cold Foam came to us as part of a group of three rabbits surrendered by their owner, who no longer had time for them. She's a petite all-white bunny with a clean bill of health and a cooperative, easygoing temperament - she allowed all handling during her intake exam without fuss. She was bred by her previous owner and has a litter record on file, which is worth knowing for any adopter.

My Ideal Home
Cold Foam will do well with an adopter who understands rabbit care - unlimited timothy hay, fresh greens, space to roam, and enrichment to keep her engaged. She's young and still developing her personality, so a patient, attentive home will get to watch her really bloom. She may enjoy a bonded companion rabbit with proper introductions, but can thrive solo with enough interaction.

Handling & Socialization
Cold Foam was calm and cooperative throughout her intake exam - a great baseline for a young rabbit. She's not a hands-off pet; with consistent gentle interaction she should continue to build comfort and confidence with her people.

Good with Other Pets?
Unknown. Any home with dogs or cats will need a solid plan for safe, permanent separation.

Good with Kids?
Unknown. Older children who understand gentle rabbit handling are the best fit - rabbits are easily injured if dropped or handled roughly.

Overall Health
Apparently healthy at intake - clear eyes, clean ears, healthy coat, good gut sounds, and moving well. She received a routine anti-parasitic treatment (Ponazuril) at intake. She is intact and has a temporary spay/neuter waiver as she is still under 6 months - her spay (OHE) is planned once she reaches that milestone, which is important for long-term health.

Behavior Determination
General Adoption. Cold Foam is a healthy, easygoing young rabbit with no behavioral concerns. A great match for anyone ready to commit to proper rabbit care and enjoy watching a young bun grow into herself.

A volunteer writes: Cold Foam is an energetic young rabbit. When I let her out for play time she always does lots of binkies and zoomies around the pen. I've found she's a bit of an introvert who can take some time to warm up to people, but once you've earned her trust she's a very loyal companion. The last time I had her out for playtime, she jumped right in my lap! Cold Foam is looking for a home with a patient human where she can run and binky every day.

Unknown. Older children who understand gentle rabbit handling are the best fit - rabbits are easily injured if dropped or handled roughly.

Overall Health
Apparently healthy at intake - clear eyes, clean ears, healthy coat, good gut sounds, and moving well. She received a routine anti-parasitic treatment (Ponazuril) at intake. She is intact and has a temporary spay/neuter waiver as she is still under 6 months - her spay (OHE) is planned once she reaches that milestone, which is important for long-term health.

Behavior Determination
General Adoption. Cold Foam is a healthy, easygoing young rabbit with no behavioral concerns. A great match for anyone ready to commit to proper rabbit care and enjoy watching a young bun grow into herself.

A volunteer writes: Cold Foam is an energetic young rabbit. When I let her out for play time she always does lots of binkies and zoomies around the pen. I've found she's a bit of an introvert who can take some time to warm up to people, but once you've earned her trust she's a very loyal companion. The last time I had her out for playtime, she jumped right in my lap! Cold Foam is looking for a home with a patient human where she can run and binky every day.

249577.name: Bean
249577.summary:
My foster writes:

Mr. Bean, or Beanie Baby, is the sweetest and most affectionate cat you will meet! He is calm, gentle, and extremely friendly. Bean can get along with anyone, big or small, furry or human. Bean loves his Churus and crunchy treats, but LOVES being around his friends & family even more! He will greet anyone in the room with soft purrs, head rubs, and by kneading your legs, arms, or clothes. He is content just chilling all day with his people and napping peacefully next to them. When he does get little bursts of energy, he enjoys gently playing with spring toys and scratching rope posts/cat trees. Bean is truly the sweetest little guy, and deserves a loving forever home. Bean is cat, dog, and kid friendly, and would love to meet you! The luckiest, loving black cat!

249603.name: Stark
249603.summary: My foster writes: Stark is a sweet, energetic, vocal boy! Don't let his cuteness fool you - he takes playtime very seriously and quickly earned the nickname "shark." If Stark could play 24/7, he absolutely would, and he makes catching wand toys look like an olympic sport with all his flips and jumps. He's not shy about telling you when he wants to play, and he's looking for a home where someone can match his energy and give him lots of play time. Stark can be slow to warm up to new people, but once he trusts you he will follow you around everywhere (it's hard to walk because he's always standing between your legs)! While he loves being near his people, he's still figuring out how he feels about pets and cuddles. He's also still learning that hands, arms, and legs are not toys, so he's looking for a patient person who can help redirect his playful energy. Stark will make a perfect companion for someone who needs some adorable energy in their life!

249613.name: Sadie
249613.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Sadie Baby is the absolute sweetest soul you'll ever have the pleasure of knowing! She is a total lovebug who craves nothing more than your affection and attention. I've been genuinely amazed by how quickly she masters complicated puzzle games, proving just how bright she really is. Sadie is highly motivated by praise and snacks, and if you have anything peanut butter flavored, I'd say you've officially won her heart.
Because she's such a sensitive and gentle spirit, she can be nervous around loud noises, so she'll need a patient family to help her settle into her new home at her own pace. But she's absolutely ready to be someone's new best friend.

My foster wites:

Sadie Girl aka The Baby is one of the sweetest, most loving dogs we've ever met. From day one of bringing her home she wowed us with her trust and love - she just wants to be near her people and it takes so little to make her happy. If you're settled, she's settled. She'll jump up on the bed or couch next to you, put her little head on your knee, and snuggle in with a big sigh and probably some snoring. She is an extremely polite and friendly girl- trying to say hi to every human and dog we pass on the street- always with an excited but calm body and lots of kisses. Sadie is really still a baby herself - even though she's already had puppies- which maybe explains some of her patience and tolerance getting kisses and bear hugs and baths and paw cleanings. Whoever brings Sadie home forever will get to watch this girl grow into an adult dog and her best self.
Since she is still young, someone with patience, time, and readiness to work on training with her is needed. Someone ready to meet her energy when she's excited and then help her calm her body down after. She is a FAST learner, so eager to please, very smart and treat-responsive. An energetic, patient home with people who are ready to snuggle and laugh (she is so silly) will be perfect for Sadie girl.
Sadie continues to melt our hearts everyday by showing us how much love and gentleness she has in her heart. We are excited for her to find her people and for them to find her 🧡

249634.name: Ground Ginger
249634.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Ground Ginger is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Ground Ginger tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He/she may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his/her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.
Ground Ginger is a sleek little mini panther with silky black fur, soulful eyes, and the quiet elegance of a cat who knows she's fabulous. 🖤✨

This demure lady prefers to keep things low-key. She'll politely accept treats (without ever mussing up her perfect paws, of course) and can often be tempted out of hiding with a little catnip and gentle patience. Ground Ginger came from a hoarding situation and may never become a super social cat - but that doesn't make her any less special.

She's looking for a calm home with someone who appreciates the beauty of simply sharing space with a quiet companion. Ground Ginger may not demand attention, but her soft presence and mysterious charm make her the perfect roommate for a fellow introvert.

If your dream pet is a peaceful, low-maintenance little shadow with movie-star eyes, Ground Ginger is waiting to meet you. 🐾

249635.summary:
My foster writes:
Paprika thinks he's a tough guy, but once he warms up to you, he's a sweetie that will steal your heart! He wasn't dealt the best cards in the first part of his life - but he's ready to learn true love and gain confidence along the way! He's incredibly respectful, clean, and private - making him an amazing apartment companion. He loves watching life through a window, lounging out on couches, playing with his feather toy, cuddling up to his stuffy, and Churu. LOTS of Churu. Paprika is looking for a forever home that will extend him patience and love so he can enjoy all that life has to offer.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Paprika tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will likely need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

249640.name: Mullien
249640.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Mullien, a sweet, soft boy with a gentle soul. His early years were in a home that had a lot of cats and very little humans, so he is a little shy with humans at first, but around other cats his personality absolutely shines. He gains confidence from feline friends and would thrive in a home with another cat to show him the ropes. When he feels safe, his adorable, playful side comes out in full force.
Mullien is obsessed with feather toys and can happily play for hours chasing around a feather or running after a mouse toy. After playtime, you'll often find him curled up in a cozy dark corner catching up on sleep or quietly perched nearby, observing everything you're doing like a tiny furry supervisor. He is not afraid to vocalize his emotions in any given moment.
Affection with Mullien happens on his terms, but if you leave space on the couch or bed, don't be surprised if he decides to snuggle up beside you. He appreciates the reminders that you are his friend so if you simply outstretch your hand he will curl right into it for pets and loving. Those moments feel extra special because they're earned. He's incredibly soft, very food motivated, and full of quiet charm.
Because sudden movements can make him nervous, Mullien would do best in a calmer home without very young children. With patience, another cat companion, and someone willing to let him move at his own pace, he'll reward you with his loving and sometimes silly personality.
If you're looking for a gentle, playful companion who blossoms with feline friendship, Mullien may be your perfect match.
Interested in two cats? Mullien is currently fostered with his best friend Nettle, who is also looking for a home. They would love to be adopted together!

The Feline Behavior team has decided to identify Nettle and Mullien as a Bonded Pair.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Mullien tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He/she may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home.  We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children.

A volunteer writes: A fluffy grey fellow with a penchant for snuggling himself in the corner, Mullien's concerted efforts to recede from view will only take him so far. A path to the center of his condo and into a forever family's heart may seem a bit in the distance at the moment, but things can change and actually, Mullien knows a lot about changes. It's worth looking a little in the past as we celebrate his very promising future. Mullien came to us from a home with many other cats and may not have a lot of experience meeting new people. He does, however, want to try and he demonstrates glimpses of openness when he accepts the treats we leave him and allows pets. Mullien would love a second chance to become the cat he's meant to.
