249644.name: Lemonade
249644.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Lemonade, a 7-year-old orange gentleman who will steal your heart and immediately pretend you have never fed him in his entire life.
Lemonade serves as the household's dedicated live correspondent and his beat is very specific: meal times and litter box visits are breaking news, announced to the entire home with great enthusiasm and zero filter.
He is a true connoisseur of boxes and hideouts. If it fits, he sits. Boxes, bags, cosy nooks - every tucked-away corner becomes a five-star suite. Lemonade adores affection and will soak up every pet and head scratch you offer, right from the comfort of his chosen spot. The best way to bond with him is to come sit beside him he will reward your patience with the warmest, most devoted companionship a cat can give.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
Lemonade is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, he tolerates attention and appreciates some petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people, we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans.  Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

249647.name: Nettle
249647.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Nettle, don't let the stern face fool you - he is the kind of cat who believes every person is a potential best friend. He's incredibly social, outgoing, and eager to be part of whatever you're doing. Nettle would do well in a home with another cat, but he'd also be perfectly happy as the center of attention in a single-cat home because humans are truly his favorite company.
When Nettle first settles in, he may ask for a lot of reassurance and affection, but once he realizes you're sticking around, he relaxes into a more independent rhythm. "Independent," however, still means he'll happily curl up next to you for snuggles and follow you from room to room as your loyal little shadow.
Nettle is playful and can entertain himself (or you!) for hours with feather toys, balls, and toy mice. He's a remarkably good independent player, so if you're busy, he'll happily keep himself occupied. On the flip side, if the day's vibe is lounging around and napping, Nettle is equally content spending hours snoozing nearby.
One of Nettle's most special qualities is how smart and trainable he is. He learns routines quickly and responds well to gentle reinforcement. For example, after only a handful of redirects from a work desk to a nearby chair, he decided on his own that the chair was his spot. He's curious, confident, and seemingly fearless-always ready to explore every corner of your home and introduce himself to every visitor.
Nettle would do wonderfully in a home with children of any age thanks to his easygoing, tolerant nature. He's also exceptionally cooperative during care routines; even medication and eye drops have been met without aggression or fuss.
If you're looking for a confident, affectionate companion who will play hard, nap hard, learn quickly, and make himself part of your everyday life, Nettle is ready to be your new best friend.
Interested in two cats? Nettle is currently fostered with his best friend Mullien, who is also looking for a home. They would love to be adopted together!

The Feline Behavior team has decided to identify Nettle and Mullien as a Bonded Pair.

What my friends at ACC say about me:


I can go home today!
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

On the flip side, if the day's vibe is lounging around and napping, Nettle is equally content spending hours snoozing nearby. One of Nettle's most special qualities is how smart and trainable he is. He learns routines quickly and responds well to gentle reinforcement. For example, after only a handful of redirects from a work desk to a nearby chair, he decided on his own that the chair was his spot. He's curious, confident, and seemingly fearless-always ready to explore every corner of your home and introduce himself to every visitor. Nettle would do wonderfully in a home with children of any age thanks to his easygoing, tolerant nature. He's also exceptionally cooperative during care routines; even medication and eye drops have been met without aggression or fuss. If you're looking for a confident, affectionate companion who will play hard, nap hard, learn quickly, and make himself part of your everyday life, Nettle is ready to be your new best friend. Interested in two cats? Nettle is currently fostered with his best friend Mullien, who is also looking for a home. They would love to be adopted together! The Feline Behavior team has decided to identify Nettle and Mullien as a Bonded Pair.

249691.name: Mars
249691.summary:
Mars is a loving rabbit ready to hop into his forever home! 

Mars is a gentle soul with a heart just waiting to bloom. This handsome rabbit may be very shy and nervous when you first meet him, but with a little patience and a calm environment, his true personality begins to shine. Once Mars feels safe, he absolutely loves being pet and will happily settle in to enjoy your company. Unlike most rabbits, he doesn't mind being picked up, and he knows that a beckoning hand gesture means "come over here and get petted". He's also comfortable being photographed, which is good, because he's extremely cute.

In his previous home, he was said to have lived with a puppy, so he has had some exposure to other animals. He doesn't seem to enjoy hearing barking dogs, though, and would do best in a peaceful setting where he can build confidence at his own pace.

When he's comfortable, Mars enjoys free roaming and showing off his playful side, happily running around and exploring his space. Watching him gain confidence and come out of his shell is incredibly rewarding.

He's still working on a few rabbit manners and learning to enjoy a healthy diet full of hay, and will benefit from a bit of continued training and guidance from his adopter. Because of this, Mars may do best with someone who already has some rabbit experience and understands bunny behavior. However, the fact that he's so friendly with humans and comes when beckoned suggests that he'll probably learn pretty quickly.

Mars is looking for a calm home where he can roam, play, and continue building confidence with a patient adopter. If you're a rabbit lover ready to give this active little explorer the peaceful home he deserves, Mars might just be the perfect match!

249723.summary:
My foster writes: Hi! My name is Drax and I'm a cute little fellow who is looking for my fur-ever home! My favorite activities include watching bird cat-tv (or live ones if a pigeon sits outside my window) and chasing laser toys. I may take some time to warm up to you, but am curious about people and want to engage with them. When we meet at first I can be shy, but come out of my shell more and more each day, and am slowly learning to enjoy chin scratches and pets. I'm also one of the chattiest cats you'll ever meet and like having long conversations with whoever will listen!

Drax tolerates some attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

249798.name: Lilypad
249798.summary:
My foster writes:
If you're looking for a sweet and gentle companion with big soulful eyes, look no further than Lilypad. Lilypad's favorite place to be is curled up right next to you. Lilypad warmed up quickly to her foster home and with each day wanted more love and affection. She likes lots of pets, chin scratches, and being brushed. The more you get to know Lilypad, the louder her purr will become. Her big eyes make her look a little sad sometimes, but Lilypad is very content spending her day curled up snoozing on the couch. She is very quiet, and her 'meow' that she greets you with when you come home is really more of a little squeak.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Lilypad is laying in the back of her cubby in a loaf position as the assessor approaches, front paws tucked under her chest. When the cubby door is opened, she observed the assessor with wide eyes and dilated pupils, body slightly tense. Lilypad is tolerant of all petting, leaning in slightly and closing her eyes when she is pet on the head and cheeks. Lilypad is unable to be coaxed forward from the back of her cubby, so she is unable to be fully picked up. She is tolerant of light, upward pressure under her chest and on her sides without issue. 

Lilypad tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: Peering out at Adoptions with her deeply soulful eyes, Lilypad seems to just be waiting for things to happen to her, embodying Eeyore and breaking my heart in the process. Lilypad was brought to us with another cat when her guardian couldn't bring them along and Lilypad seems to be diligently searching for some optimism to carry her through the long shelter days. When I opened her condo door, Lilypad quietly hopped into the cubby, likely hoping that I wouldn't notice her except that Lilypad really needs someone to do just that. Though she wasn't looking for pets from me, her previous guardian shared that she's friendly and likes to be kissed and given treats. All she needs now is a little chance, so please if you could share one with her.

249817.name: Dimitri
249817.summary:
My foster writes: Dimitri is the softest, sweetest teddy bear you could ever meet. This gentle giant is calm, easygoing, and wonderfully relaxed no matter what's going on around him. He's happy to be handled, easy to pick up, and even lets you clip his nails like a champ-just remember, he's a big boy! But bring out a teaser toy, and Dimitri's playful side shines. He becomes interactive, curious, and so much fun to watch. Whether you're looking for a cozy cuddle buddy or a playful companion, Dimitri is the perfect big-hearted pillow to hug.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am playful and cute!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Dimitri appreciates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will likely need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Dimitri may be intimidated by small children, any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

249827.name: Yuro
249827.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Yuro is at-risk list due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Yuro has displayed concerning resource-guarding behaviors. During his first stay, he grabbed the Assess-a-Hand multiple times, and during his current stay he has been observed gripping, tensing, and grumbling. Yuro was also observed biting his leash in the kennel and only responding to high-value treats. More recently, he was noted to engage in kennel fighting while exiting the room. Outside of the kennel environment, Yuro is social with staff. Medically, Yuro is apparently healthy.

Yuro arrived at MACC as a stray with a history. During his previous stay in the care center, Yuro was reported to leash bite and guard resources. When being removed from kennel, Yuro was noted to jump up and bite the leash. During his assessment, Yuro was observed to fixate on the assess-a-hand, grabbing, pulling, and whipping his head around. During his current stay in the care center, Yuro has been observed to be highly kennel reactive. Noted to pull hard towards the neighboring dogs and intensely cage fight with them. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an exerienced adult only home.

249872.name: Luna
249872.summary:
Luna arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. Her previous owner states that she is fearful of loud arguments and will escalate to growling, barking, and snapping. While in care, Luna has also been observed to be fearful. Noted to be at the back of the kennel and will begin to lip lift when handlers attempt to coax her out of kennel. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

A staff member writes: Luna is a happy, affectionate girl whose whole body wiggles when she's excited to see her people! She loves getting out for walks, sniffing around, and soaking up attention from familiar faces. While she can be enthusiastic and pull a bit on leash at first, she's easy to handle, enjoys learning new things, and has already shown off her smarts by mastering "leave it" with her trainer. Luna has made wonderful progress during her stay and has become increasingly social with both people and dogs. She has participated in dog introductions and playgroups, and while slow introductions are always recommended, she's ready to bring her joyful personality and endless tail wags to her forever home.

249891.name: Zuessey
249891.summary:
Meet Zuessey!

My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! 

Zuessey is a 7-year-old boy who came to us as an owner surrender when his family could no longer care for him. He's a sweet, social guy who is now looking for a steady, understanding home where he can feel secure and supported as he settles into a new routine.

Personality
Zuessey is an affectionate, people focused dog who enjoys being near his handlers and staying involved in whatever is going on. He is social in the room, often staying close, exploring calmly, and coming over readily for attention and treats. Once comfortable, he shows a friendly, engaged side and enjoys interaction with people.

He can be a bit mouthy when taking treats and may become anxious at times, especially in situations that are unfamiliar or when left alone, so he benefits from structure and reassurance in his environment.

Leash Walks
Zuessey walks with mild pulling on leash and generally stays manageable with guidance. He is not reactive to people and tends to focus more on moving forward with his handler than on distractions.

Social Behavior
Zuessey is friendly and comfortable with handling, accepting pets and treats with a neutral, easygoing posture. He tends to stay near people and checks in frequently, showing a desire for connection and reassurance.

With other dogs, he has shown interest and playful behaviors, but interactions can become overexcited, so structured introductions and supervision are important.

Home Life
Zuessey has some anxiety when left alone and may benefit from a consistent routine and gradual alone-time training. He does best in a home that can provide patience, structure, and positive outlets for his energy and stress.

Fun Fact
Zuessey is the kind of dog who wants to be part of everything. If you're there, he's there too, quietly keeping you company and waiting for the next treat or moment of attention.

249909.name: Racer
249909.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Racer is a cute sepia tabby who is with us for no fault of his own. A lively puppy entered his life and it was not to Racer's like. The puppy stayed but Racer had to go. Racer comes with excellent recommendations from his former family who took very good care of him: friendly and affectionate with all, a talkative lap cat, a playful and well mannered pet! Racer is a lovely cat, a little shy starting an encounter but very quickly engaging, trusting, friendly, sweet, playful and making "air" biscuits...I had a really great time petting him, talking to him and playing with him. Handsome Racer did very well on his behavior evaluation, is already neutered and could go home today with you for many happy years to come. Racer is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!

249992.name: Darling
249992.summary:
My foster writes: Darling is a gentle, loving cat that will blossom in a caring home. She is a sweet girl that doesn't have an aggressive bone in her body and has never hissed or batted in over four months (a real rarity in any cat!). Darling loves to sit on the lap of her favorite human and cuddle on the couch and in bed. She can be sensitive to new situations but has made huge strides in becoming comfortable in her foster home. Patience and kindness will be rewarded with many requests to snuggle and play.

My foster writes:
Darling is a very shy cat with great potential for warming up to her forever home. She will need a lot of time to decompress and appreciates quiet and patience from her humans. With enough care and space she will seek out pets and affection.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Darling tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

250011.name: Bell Pepper
250011.summary:
My foster writes:
Bell Pepper likes to go outside. As soon as i grab a leash, she would wag her tail and hit everything around her with her tail, ready and happy for a walk.
She loves her naps. She would sleep next to my foot while I'm working or in the balcony but her favorite spot is her bed in the crate.
When it's time to wipe her paws after a walk, this super smart girl knows and tries to go to her safe spot, which is her crate, and hides there.

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Bell Pepper!
Bell Pepper is an 11-year-old sweetheart who came to us as an owner surrender. She has lived with adults and is described as friendly, outgoing, and playful with new people. She enjoys attention but prefers to engage on her own terms. She is the kind of dog who likes to be near her people and soak up the calm moments of the day.

Personality
Bell Pepper enjoys being part of whatever her people are doing. She loves a good cuddle session and is happiest when she can relax close to someone she trusts. She is more of a couch potato than a toy player and enjoys fuzzy blankets. She can be a little anxious at times, so she will benefit from structure and supervision in a home.

Daily Life
Bell Pepper walks nicely on leash with no pulling and does not react to people or other dogs while out. She enjoys a calm, steady routine and tends to keep to herself in new environments until she feels comfortable. Once settled, she is easygoing and enjoys simply being near her person. She is partially crate trained and can stay in a crate for up to several hours as long as it is large enough for her to move comfortably.

Training and Manners
Bell Pepper knows several cues including sit, stay, paw, and go. She is treat motivated and will happily take most foods offered to her. She is not reactive toward people on walks and handles gentle and more active handling well, standing still and tolerating contact. She may be a bit more reserved in unfamiliar situations but recovers quickly once she feels safe.

Social Behavior
Bell Pepper is generally soft and low key in new environments. She may take a moment to warm up and will approach when coaxed. She enjoys calm interaction and prefers gentle engagement over high energy play.

My Ideal Home
Bell Pepper would do best in a calm home with adults who can provide structure, routine, and gentle guidance. She would love a cozy environment where she can relax, enjoy couch time, and be included in daily life. She may benefit from continued support around her anxiety and supervision to prevent unwanted behaviors like counter surfing or getting into the garbage.

Living with Kids
She would do best in a home without young children due to her anxiety. She may be open to older, respectful teens who understand her need for space and calm interactions.

Fun Fact
Bell Pepper is a professional snuggler. Once she trusts you, she is happiest just being your quiet little shadow. 

A volunteer writes: Bell Pepper 🫑 if a girl could be more my type, then I haven't met her yet. She is 11 years old, but none the wiser to that fact. Age is just a number, and Bell is the definition of young at heart. She bounds towards us, confident and happy. Jumps around for treats, trying to impress us with her sassy sit (and succeeding). She is so full of life and fun that it lifts our spirits and fills us with laughter. I joke that I'd keep her name and call her Bell when she's sweet and Pepper when she's spicy.

250021.summary:
Meet Coco! 🐾

Coco is a sweet, social, and absolutely lovable girl looking for her forever home! She's lived with older kids (ages 8 and 13) and was reported to be friendly, outgoing, and playful. Coco loves to play, enjoys her treats, and has a big heart full of affection. Super soft and squishy, she's the perfect cuddle buddy after a fun day of activity.

If you're looking for a playful, loving companion who's ready to fill your home with joy and snuggles, Coco is the one! Come meet her and fall in love. 💛

My Boroughbreaker writes: A little anxious in the car but settled down and laid on my lap I sat in the back seat with her She gives tons of kisses and wanted to be next to me all the time for pets if I stopped petting her she would look back at me as if saying why are you stopping She was a pleasure to spend time with Walked nice on leash enjoyed exploring her surroundings She will make a wonderful companion for some lucky person

My Boroughbreaker writes: On my boroughbresk we took a walk around my neighborhood. It was a very hot day so we brought Coco back to our house. She loved to play fetch in the yard. She seemed to always want to be pet and to be showed affection. She was very sweet. Very quiet dog. She didn't bark at all. She sat on command and gave her paw too.

250088.name: Bayne
250088.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Bayne is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Bayne is reported to be fearful and has escalated to displaying hard barking and baring his teeth when people approach his kennel. Recently, his behavior has deteriorated, and he has been observed spinning in his kennel and jumping toward the top of the kennel. Outside of the kennel, Bayne displays a neutral body posture and readily accepts treats offered to him. Medically, Bayne is apparently healthy.

Meet Bayne!
Bayne was found as a stray and spent some time in a home before coming to the shelter. He is a sensitive boy who can be cautious at first, but with a little reassurance, he will approach for gentle pets and connection. He is still adjusting to new environments and benefits from a calm, low-pressure approach.

My Ideal Home
Bayne would do best in a quiet home with a predictable routine and a patient adopter. He needs time to build confidence and will thrive with someone who allows him to go at his own pace. A low-traffic environment will help him feel more secure as he settles in.

Good with Other Pets?
Bayne has shown no reactivity toward other dogs in care, though he has been noted to pull toward animals and moving stimuli on walks. Slow introductions and continued training will be important to support calm behavior around other pets.

Good with Kids?
Bayne is recommended for a home without children under 13 due to his fearful nature and sensitivity to new environments.

Things to Know
Bayne may become startled by outside stressors like cars or sudden movement and can show signs of stress such as yawning, lip licking, or a low body posture. He walks with a zig-zag pattern and will benefit from confidence-building and loose-leash training. With patience, structure, and positive reinforcement, he can continue to grow more comfortable and confident.

A volunteer writes: Meet Bayne! Bayne is the type  of dog who could change the English language. Picture it: you adopt Bayne and decide, as many people do, to keep his shelter name. You then, easily and joyfully, spend the rest of his life saying "you're the Bayne of my existence!" and he says "what does that mean?" and you say "it means you're amazing and wonderful and a reason to smile when I wake up in the morning" and you both laugh and eventually Merriam Webster agrees that a Bayne/bane is indeed a really, really good thing.

This wonderful, shy little Oreo cookie was found February during a snowstorm. At the shelter and on a recent borough break he was  timid at first but warms up once he feels comfortable, something I can certainly attest to during our walks where a few treats and a gentle approach score me lots of points. 

Bayne has not shown reactivity to other dogs at the shelter or on his borough break. He is available to a Level 4 adopter and recommended for a home without children under 13 due to his fearful nature and sensitivity to new environments.

250111.name: Milky Way
250111.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! 

Meet Milky Way!
Milky Way was found walking alone on the street. She is a sensitive, gentle girl who is trying her best in a very new environment. She shows small but meaningful moments of trust with people she begins to know. With calm handling and patience, she can settle and seek comfort from her handler.

My Ideal Home
Milky Way would do best in a quiet, adult-only home with experience or willingness to work with fearful dogs. She will need a patient adopter who allows her to adjust at her own pace without pressure. 

Good with Other Pets?
Milky Way has shown mixed responses to other dogs and can become tense in close or high-energy interactions. Careful, structured introductions and ongoing management would be important in a home with other animals.

Good with Kids?
Milky Way is recommended for a home without children under 13 due to her fearful and sensitive nature. She will do best in a calm, low-stimulation environment.

Things to Know
Milky Way walks nicely on leash but may freeze or hesitate in unfamiliar environments. She is very sensitive to handling and does best with slow introductions and gentle encouragement. With time and consistency, she shows the ability to relax and connect with her person.

Fun Fact
Milky Way may start out a little starry-eyed and unsure, but once she trusts you, she shines brightly!🌌

Milky Way is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is making wonderful progress on her leash manners. Encounters with other dogs or unexpected distractions can be overwhelming for her during walks, but through her training she is learning to settle, refocus, and trust her handler. With patience and positive reinforcement guiding the way, Milky Way is growing more confident and composed with every outing.

250119.name: Winter
250119.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Winter is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers. Winter is now beginning to accept treats and she has responded positively to gabapentin.

In shelter care, Winter has presented with distance increasing fear-based behaviors before progressing/improving through work with behavior staff. She has a history of a fear-based behavior incident that occurred in her previous home, which should be discussed with an adoption counsellor and taken into account when considering adopting Winter. A fearful cat will feel more relaxed when given options, she will likely require allowing her to lead interactions, and providing her with the chance to move closer, investigate, or interact with you. Winter would do best in a single-pet, Adult-Only home.

A volunteer writes: Please see Winter with any questions, comments, and concerns regarding scheduling, policy, and programming. She's been here since March but that's not why she's been fast tracked to upper management. It's her skills! For consideration and approval, Winter utilizes a rigorous process that only she understands and because task delegation hasn't been a priority (please don't tell her I said that) we've been left trying to parse out the details. Winter knows who she is and we celebrate her confident stride, but just because she's a picture of self assuredness and leadership, doesn't mean shelter life has been exactly easy for her. We know Winter likes to be the one to make decisions but the Care Center doesn't always have a lot of opportunities for that. We don't know that much about her life before, but Winter isn't a fan of other cats and is hoping her next role will be supervising a family.

250127.name: Lady Bug
250127.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Ladybug? More like Cuddle-bug! Meet Ladybug, a really special girl with an endless amount of love to give. Once you start petting her and she looks up at you with her beautiful brown eyes, and starts purring as she melts into your arms, you'll never want to stop! She might be a little hesitant at first, but with just a little love and reassurance, Ladybug blossoms into the sweetest, cuddliest, adorably playful dog. Most of time, Ladybug is a sleepy, docile couch potato, and is impressively gentle taking treats, pawing, and giving affection, but she also has a fun, silly, energetic streak! Don't be surprised to catch her zooming around the room to celebrate a particularly good cuddle session or meal, or to initiate play mid-day! And if you're looking for a new running partner, don't count Ladybug out! She is quite the athlete and will also be an excellent exercise companion. She's still working on getting all of the basic commands down, but she is responsive and highly engaged during training sessions. While we don't know too much about Ladybug's past, her almost magnetic pull to the couch (no invite needed!) and stellar potty training suggest that she may have once had a home.

My other foster writes: Ladybug is a brindle queen waiting for her forever home!
She is beaming with love, and is as energy fueled as she is a master in cuddling (naps with her are sure to improve your life). While she loves a lazy day, Ladybug loves a long walk and much needed playtime (she will let you know!) She is great at fetch and LOVES a puzzle toy.
Ladybug will do best in a consistently social environment without prolonged alone time. cannot be left alone for long periods of time due to her anxiety. She is a true velcro pittie, and will follow you around desperate to be part of the action.
Ladybug needs a patient owner who can continue to work through her anxieties, helping build her confidence and trust around strangers.

My Borough Breaker writes:
When I brought Ladybug home for a short foster stint, she literally started jumping for joy! She gave me her belly and zoomed around the room grabbing toys before snuggling in for a solo nap.

Meet Ladybug!
Ladybug was found roaming the streets alone and is still learning that the world can be a safe place. She is a sensitive, thoughtful girl who takes her time to warm up, but with patience and kindness, she starts to show a quiet curiosity about her surroundings. She does best with people who let her come forward at her own pace.

Personality
Ladybug is cautious at first and can feel overwhelmed in new situations. She may prefer to observe from a distance before engaging, but she is gentle and non-reactive, and she benefits from calm, steady companionship. Once she feels secure, her softer personality starts to come through.

My Ideal Home
Ladybug would thrive in a quiet, low-traffic home with patient adopters who understand the value of letting her set the pace. She will do best with a calm routine and gentle encouragement rather than pressure. A peaceful environment will help her confidence grow over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Ladybug has not been comfortable passing other dogs closely and may feel overwhelmed in busy or high-energy interactions. With slow, thoughtful introductions and proper management, she may be able to adjust, but she will need space and patience while she builds confidence.

Good with Kids?
Ladybug would do best in a home without young children under 5. She is sensitive to her environment and will thrive best in a calm, predictable household.

Things to Know
Ladybug walks nicely on leash without pulling but is still building confidence outside the shelter. She benefits from slow introductions, consistency, and a gentle approach that allows her to explore the world at her own pace. Small moments of trust go a long way with her.

Fun Fact
Ladybug may be a little shy at first, but once she starts to feel safe, she really starts to "bug" for attention in the sweetest way. With time, she's the kind of lucky charm who quietly lands in your heart. 🐞
250127.summaryHtml:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! My foster writes: Ladybug? More like Cuddle-bug! Meet Ladybug, a really special girl with an endless amount of love to give. Once you start petting her and she looks up at you with her beautiful brown eyes, and starts purring as she melts into your arms, you'll never want to stop! She might be a little hesitant at first, but with just a little love and reassurance, Ladybug blossoms into the sweetest, cuddliest, adorably playful dog. Most of time, Ladybug is a sleepy, docile couch potato, and is impressively gentle taking treats, pawing, and giving affection, but she also has a fun, silly, energetic streak! Don't be surprised to catch her zooming around the room to celebrate a particularly good cuddle session or meal, or to initiate play mid-day! And if you're looking for a new running partner, don't count Ladybug out! She is quite the athlete and will also be an excellent exercise companion. She's still working on getting all of the basic commands down, but she is responsive and highly engaged during training sessions. While we don't know too much about Ladybug's past, her almost magnetic pull to the couch (no invite needed!) and stellar potty training suggest that she may have once had a home. My other foster writes: Ladybug is a brindle queen waiting for her forever home! She is beaming with love, and is as energy fueled as she is a master in cuddling (naps with her are sure to improve your life). While she loves a lazy day, Ladybug loves a long walk and much needed playtime (she will let you know!) She is great at fetch and LOVES a puzzle toy. Ladybug will do best in a consistently social environment without prolonged alone time. cannot be left alone for long periods of time due to her anxiety. She is a true velcro pittie, and will follow you around desperate to be part of the action. Ladybug needs a patient owner who can continue to work through her anxieties, helping build her confidence and trust around strangers. My Borough Breaker writes: When I brought Ladybug home for a short foster stint, she literally started jumping for joy! She gave me her belly and zoomed around the room grabbing toys before snuggling in for a solo nap. Meet Ladybug!
Ladybug was found roaming the streets alone and is still learning that the world can be a safe place. She is a sensitive, thoughtful girl who takes her time to warm up, but with patience and kindness, she starts to show a quiet curiosity about her surroundings. She does best with people who let her come forward at her own pace.

Personality
Ladybug is cautious at first and can feel overwhelmed in new situations. She may prefer to observe from a distance before engaging, but she is gentle and non-reactive, and she benefits from calm, steady companionship. Once she feels secure, her softer personality starts to come through.

My Ideal Home
Ladybug would thrive in a quiet, low-traffic home with patient adopters who understand the value of letting her set the pace. She will do best with a calm routine and gentle encouragement rather than pressure. A peaceful environment will help her confidence grow over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Ladybug has not been comfortable passing other dogs closely and may feel overwhelmed in busy or high-energy interactions. With slow, thoughtful introductions and proper management, she may be able to adjust, but she will need space and patience while she builds confidence.

Good with Kids?
Ladybug would do best in a home without young children under 5. She is sensitive to her environment and will thrive best in a calm, predictable household.

Things to Know
Ladybug walks nicely on leash without pulling but is still building confidence outside the shelter. She benefits from slow introductions, consistency, and a gentle approach that allows her to explore the world at her own pace. Small moments of trust go a long way with her.

Fun Fact
Ladybug may be a little shy at first, but once she starts to feel safe, she really starts to "bug" for attention in the sweetest way. With time, she's the kind of lucky charm who quietly lands in your heart. 🐞

250148.name: Spot
250148.summary:
My foster writes: Spot is an affectionate goofball! He is loving, trusting, playful, curious, and sweet. He leans his head and body into pets and scritches and will flop on the floor by your feet to request them. Spot is brave and very curious - he likes supervising the roomba, exploring, and climbing. He will hunt a wiggled piece of twine like it's his job or bat and chase a ball toy all over the apartment. He uses the scratching post instead of furniture and does not demand food in the morning. Spot would be an excellent companion or family cat! He would thrive in a home where he gets the pets and attention he craves.

A volunteer writes:
Spot came to us with two of his housemates as his home counted too many pets.This handsome and elegant cow print young gentleman arrived with lovely comments from his former owners-friendly, well mannered, outgoing, active and playful with all, something we love to hear when we want to add a new four legged member to our family! Spot might be a tinsy winsy shy in his kennel but he warms up to gentle words, is tempted by a feather wand and likes his cuddles, purring very softly and leaning into pets(see video).Spot is apparently healthy, did very well on his behavior evaluation, is  100% ready to meet you and be your beloved pet for many years to com. Spot is at the Manhattan Care Center!




What my friends at ACC say about me:
Spot was in the cubby and appeared slightly shy but curious at the same time. He sniffed treats and appeared reasonably calm, if slightly unsure. He was slightly hunched and behind the litter box, and while he didn't eat treats, he did warm up to petting, leaning in gently for cheek rubs and allowing petting on his head and along his back. He didn't come forward, but he seemed reasonably calm, if a little bit unsure about being approached and about his surroundings. After the door was shut in a little while later, he came out into the main part of the kennel and ate the treats and squeeze up. When the assessor went to open the door again for another interaction, he quietly went back into the cubby and behind the litter box.

Spot interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.  	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

250164.name: Jack R.
250164.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Jack R. is At Risk due to behavioral concerns. While in the Care Centers, Jack was observed becoming tense and pulling toward other dogs. On one occasion, he was seen pushing off the room walls in an attempt to engage in kennel fighting behavior. Jack has also been reported to display signs of fear while outside and will sometimes immediately pull back toward the shelter after relieving himself. Staff currently use treat trails to help manage him during walks. He was seen licking his kennel walls and spinning outside but he hasnt engage in those behaviors often. In the pens, Jack is playful with staff and enjoys engaging in zoomies. Medically, Jack R is apparently healthy.

Jack arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. His previous owner describes Jack as a social and affectionate dog! He loves to play but is just as happy cozying up on the couch. He can usually be found where the people are. Jack allows for bathing and brushing but not nail trims. He is used to going on 10-15 minute walks 3 times per day and pulls hard on the leash. He has experience in crates and enjoys car rides. Jack is a smart guy and knows sit, shake, and go to crate. He loves hard chew toys and according to a prior owner, is "very loyal and loveable."

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Not only do I pull at heart strings, but I also pull on leash! I will need someone to help me with my leash manners.

250300.name: Casanova
250300.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.Pre-Screener Form

Casanova is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Casanova arrived at the Care Center as a stray. Upon intake Casanova was reported to be fearful by police however allowed handling by ACC staff. During his handling assessment Casanova approached handlers readily and allowed contact. Casanova has shown intense resource guarding tendencies while in care. Casanova was reported to hover over his food while in kennel, growl, and muzzle punch the kennel door when staff approach. Additionally Casanova has shown a decreasing threshold for arousal, when a handler attempted do refocus Casanova away from a dog by pressing a squeaker toy (the toy was in a treat pouch), Casanova jumped and grabbed hold of the handler's treat pouch, hard leash pressure had to be used to get him to let go. When on walks and not over threshold Casanova continues to be treat receptive and allow contact. Medically, Casanova is noted to have dental disease and undetermined allergies.

Since arriving at the care centers Casanova has displayed concerning behaviors, displaying fearful aggression toward police during intake (growling), reactivity on leash toward dogs as well and a low threshold for arousal manifesting in mounting and biting and holding a handlers treat pouch at one point. We recommend placement with a New Hope rescue partner who is able to provide an experienced, adult-only foster home. Force-free, reward based training and/or consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Earl Grey is on the at-risk list for medical concerns. Earl Grey has lost a significant amount of weight and has had a poor appetite for a prolonged amount of time. I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
My purr motor is always running!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!

250351.name: Teriyaki
250351.summary:
Meet Teriyaki!
Teriyaki was found hiding under a truck and has been taking everything in stride while he waits for a calm, loving home. The shelter can feel like a lot for him, but when things quiet down, his sweet and affectionate personality really shines.

Personality
Teriyaki is a gentle, loving boy who truly enjoys being close to his people. He's the kind of dog who will lean into you for comfort, rest his head on your lap, and quietly soak up affection. Even while still adjusting, he shows how social and people-focused he is, greeting with a soft, wiggly body and a desire to connect.

He may feel a bit overwhelmed in busy environments, but in a calm setting, he relaxes and shows just how much of a love bug he really is.

Out and About
Teriyaki walks nicely on leash with a mild pull and no reactivity toward people or other dogs. He moves along calmly and follows his handler with a relaxed, easy pace, making him a lovely companion for quieter walks.

Social Behavior
Teriyaki is highly social and approaches people readily, often leaning in for pets and staying close by. He enjoys gentle interaction and shows his affection by pressing into his handler or resting his head against them. He may briefly explore, but always comes back for connection.

Home Life
Teriyaki would do best in a calm, adult only home with a low-traffic environment where he can feel safe and settled. Slow introductions to new people and places will help him continue building confidence and feeling secure.

Things to Know
Teriyaki is still adjusting and can feel overwhelmed in busy settings, so he will thrive with patience, routine, and a peaceful space. He responds beautifully to gentle handling and connection and will blossom as he becomes more comfortable.

Fun Fact
Teriyaki loves to be close, he's happiest when he can lean into you, rest his head on your lap, and just quietly enjoy being together. 🐾

My foster writes: Teriyaki is a beautiful (white and brindle - with beautiful ears that stand up with pretty black spots/dots in the back of those ears - he also has white eyelashes!!😍), kind, loving and affectionate dog. He is not dog or bird or people reactive, easy on a leash and is housebroken. He has no prey drive! He loves when you pet him and give him love and he gives you love/affection back. He loves being petted. He will show you how happy he is to see you and make you feel great. He will stand still next to you while you pet him and soak up all your love. He will lick/kiss you to show his love and appreciation if you put your face next to his. You know that song by Ozzy Osborn "I just want you" I think Teriyaki wrote it.😄He will choose his person over anything and really enjoys being close to his human. He would choose you over any toy, food or treat even though he loves to eat and play, he would love you much more. Some people say their dog would trade them for a treat in a heart beat- not this dog. Someone would be very lucky to have this beautiful and loyal sweetheart.

250379.name: Springtime
250379.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Springtime tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: Springtime came to us courtesy of the NYPD. His crime? Simply finding himself all alone, with no human home to go to anymore. While he's waiting for new pet parents to fall in love with him, he's adjusting well at the Care Center. Springtime is a shy, calm, quiet youngster who shows interest in the humans who drop by to coax him out of his shell. When I met him last night, he was sitting on top of his cat den, observing me with soft blinks and seemingly unbothered by the sights and sounds of the cat adoption room. Springtime has been enjoying his treats and accepting some pettings, but what he really needs is a new person to come by and declare, "you're going home with me!" Make it happen for this good boy by introducing yourself to him at the Care Center today!

250408.name: Prince
250408.summary:
Meet Prince - Handsome, Playful, and Full of Love!

Prince is a strikingly handsome, active, and playful mixed breed who loves being where the people are. He thrives on attention and enjoys every moment spent with his favorite humans. Grooming is a breeze with Prince-he loves bath time and water, making it a fun experience for both of you.

On leash, Prince walks nicely with minimal pulling and enjoys one to two 30-minute walks each day. He's crate trained, comfortably spending up to six hours in an XL crate, and also loves car rides, eagerly joining any adventure.

Smart and responsive, Prince knows "sit," "lay down," and "paw," and he's always ready for playtime. He adores peanut butter treats and loves games, making him the perfect mix of funny, loving, and playful. With Prince, every day is full of joy and companionship.

250411.name: Cricket
250411.summary:
Meet Cricket - a gentle, quiet soul looking for a patient and understanding home.

Cricket is a shy and timid adult cat who prefers a calm environment where she can feel safe at her own pace. She's still learning to trust people and may be a bit fearful at first, but with time, consistency, and kindness, she can begin to open up. She tolerates gentle pets and shows curiosity in small moments, especially when given space and reassurance.

Cricket would do best in an adult-only home with someone experienced or willing to go slow and let her set the pace. Offering treats, soft voices, and a predictable routine will help her build confidence and feel more secure.

If you have a quiet home and a big heart for a cat who just needs a little extra time, Cricket could be the perfect companion to grow alongside you.

A volunteer writes: Cricket's gently curious about new things and will allow small pets with the teeny tiny caveat that everything goes at her pace. This is more than ok but not always the most conducive to making new friends at a busy shelter. Cricket was brought to us from a home with many other cats back in April and making sense of all the changes and new people she's facing has been very much a work in progress. For someone who may not have a lot of experience with new people, the daily hustle and bustle of Adoptions often leads Cricket to snuggle up in the back of her cubby. With her tail determinedly wrapped and her paws tightly tucked, Cricket finishes the look by putting her ears all the way back so that her perfect kitty head looks round. This isn't so much fashion as it is an attempt to understand just exactly what she needs to be doing to skip this middle part and get into a forever home. The glimpses of promises Cricket continues to show also demonstrate that she's just getting ready to shine.

I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

Meet Grayson!

Grayson came to SIACC from a home where cats outnumbered people 40-to-1, so being in the shelter environment surrounded by humans has made him justifiably nervous. Still, he very bravely allows staff to interact with him, and through positive reinforcement, has made significant progress. Grayson is looking for an adopter who can continue working on socialization for an adult cat, someone compassionate, patient, and understanding. He'd do best in an adult-only, low traffic home that can give him both support and space. If you think that sounds like you, come down to SIACC to meet Grayson today!
250412.summaryHtml:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

Meet Grayson! Grayson came to SIACC from a home where cats outnumbered people 40-to-1, so being in the shelter environment surrounded by humans has made him justifiably nervous. Still, he very bravely allows staff to interact with him, and through positive reinforcement, has made significant progress. Grayson is looking for an adopter who can continue working on socialization for an adult cat, someone compassionate, patient, and understanding. He'd do best in an adult-only, low traffic home that can give him both support and space. If you think that sounds like you, come down to SIACC to meet Grayson today!

250413.name: Flint
250413.summary:
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.

Meet Flint!

His pictures may give the impression that he's a rough-and-tumble kind of guy, but we like to think that in the right environment, Flint can show off his sweet, sensitive side. He came to SIACC from a home where he had very little interaction with people, so he was not so keen on interacting with staff at first. However, with time, patience, and a LOT of treats, Flint has shown interest in human contact (even some petting!). Flint will need a patient and compassionate adopter, an adult-only low-traffic home, and continued positive reinforcement through treats and toys. If that person is you, come meet Flint at SIACC!

I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.

Meet Dusty!

Dusty is a handsome three-year-old grey tabby who came to us from a home with too many cats and not enough interaction with humans. Understandably this has made him  a bit fearful while in our care. Dusty's ideal home would be adult only, with an adopter who understands feline body language and can respect his boundaries, someone willing to be as patient as he needs them to be and with a heart big enough to care for a slightly scared, slightly grumpy, adult cat. If that person is you, come to SIACC and say hi to Dusty!

250419.summary:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

He will likely need time to warm up to his new home before he shows off his his social, sweet, and cuddly personality. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior and/or appropriate decompression periods.

250430.name: Mona
250430.summary:
My foster writes: Mona is a sweet, chunky girl who honestly reminds me of a little cow. When I first brought her into my room, she hid for about an hour, just quietly adjusting. But the second I put food in her bowl, she came right out from under the bed to eat. After that, she even came up to me for pets it was so adorable. Later that same day, she started exploring the rest of her new temporary home. She's also really talkative, which makes everything even cuter.

A volunteer writes:
Mona is a young gal surrendered by her recent owner as a child in the house became allergic to her dander. Mona was a bit nervous around her arrival at the care center but she is more relaxed now, welcoming petting, gentle words and treats of course. I love the way she rolls on her side or back, legs up and making air biscuits. Mona is a sweet gal who just needs time to warm up before she shows her friendly nature. Her former owner describe her as a sweet, outgoing and playful young cat who would be very good with children. Mona is right now recovering from a cold  but being already spayed, she could go home today as your new forever best friend and for many years to come!

 What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I lived with children in my previous home.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

250436.name: Royale
250436.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Royale is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Royale was returned to the shelter due to a bite incident in the home with resident dog. When the dogs were being separated Royale did bit the adopter which broke skin. Royale's previous owner stated that he would lunge at small animals while on leash. During his previous stay in care, Roayle was noted to be tense and trembling during intake and sought exit during his assessment. He was also reported to jump up and snap at handlers. Royale's previous adopter describes him as a couch potato that loves squeaky balls. Medically, Royale is underweight.

Royale arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. Royale was returned to the shelter due to a bite incident in the home. Royale's previous owner stated that he would also lunge at small animals while on leash. During his previous stay in care, Roayle was noted to be tense and trembling during intake and sought exit during his assessment. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only, single pet home with no trips to the dog park. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

A Volunteer Wrote: If you're looking for a little love in your life, don't consider Royale--this amazing dog is a LOT of love! The kisses start on my hands as I go to leash him, and then he ever so gently stands to lean in for a hug. He's affection on four legs (or two, when he's hugging), and just the happiest, gentlest boy who walks sweetly beside me, happy to be on an adventure. Volunteers shout out his gentleness and sweetness, and we are shouting it to the rooftops!

250451.name: Diamond
250451.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Diamond is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Diamond has displayed significant dog-directed reactivity and escalation during dog greetings. Due to previous concerning behaviors noted, a fake dog assessment was conducted, Diamond immediately charged forward and pinned the fake dog to the ground. Diamond increasingly beoming more vocal and aroused. Diamond required an air can to disengage. In the Care Center, Diamond remains highly aroused and hypervigilant when returning to kennel, lunging and high-pitch vocalizing towards dogs being walked nearby. Diamond is very social with staff and volunteers, and loves to play fetch. Medically, Diamond is healthy at this time.

Diamond arrived to QACC as a stray after her owner passed away. While she was previously housed with other pets, her past behavior with them is unknown. At intake and during her stay, she has been social and friendly with people but pulls strongly on leash. Recently, she has shown escalating reactivity toward other dogs, including screeching, lunging, and fixating. During introductions, she displayed intense charging a gate, barking and growling, and later repeatedly pinning a fake dog, requiring intervention to stop. She remained highly aroused and reactive afterward. Due to her quick escalation, inability to disengage, and ongoing dog reactivity, placement through one of our new hope partners is recommended.

250459.name: Mazie
250459.summary:
My foster writes: 
Mazie's world changed forever when her owner passed away, and she was brought to ACC. Since then, she has to rebuild her world from scratch and learn how to trust again. Could you be the person to give Mazie the second chance she deserves? She is looking for a loving, permanent home where she can finally feel safe again. 

Mazie struggled to adjust to shelter life, so she came to stay with me at the end of April. While she still doesn't trust me enough for direct interaction, she quietly watches me from a distance in open spaces, and that distance has been getting smaller and smaller over time. Mazie is a brave girl who is trying in her own way. 

Although Mazie hasn't shown her playful side when I'm in the room, her camera footage tells another story. When she feels safe and alone, she reveals an energetic, entertaining personality. One of her favorite things is sitting by the window (even when I'm nearby) soaking up the sunshine, fresh breeze, and the world outside. 

Mazie is making progress every day. What she needs now is someone patient and compassionate enough to let her continue healing at her own pace.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I am bonded to Max. We must go home together and our adoption fee includes both of us!

250461.name: Max
250461.summary:
My foster writes: Max is a quiet and timid boy waiting to find a home filled with love, kindness, and patience. He is trying his best to face his fears and is the cutest little thing. He loves to sit by windows and take in the fresh air. On a rainy day he'll try to sit by an open window to feel the cool breeze and water droplets! Even though he has no teeth, he loves dental chicken greenies, and you can hear him smacking on kibble in the middle of the night. He's starting to learn to use his voice, so, if you ever have the pleasure of hearing his meow, it sounds like a squeak!

My foster writes: Max is a very sweet but scared kitty. He has no teeth and is the cutest when he yawns. He's most active at night and loves a quiet fluffy blanket to himself.

250486.name: Brandee
250486.summary:
My foster writes: As you can see, Benson is a very cute and lovable boy! Benson looks to be a wire terrier mix and his previous owner reported he lived with kids and two other cats. He is very affectionate and a velcro dog - he wants to be cuddled and kissed! He also loves some soothing music (think Appalachian folk) and his eyes will start to close. Benson appreciates his own space and is still learning boundaries and handling. He is very treat motivated and a quick learner. I should mention too that Benson is a great walker and has phenomenal leash skills! During our walks, he has been non-reactive to other dogs and small animals. Benson is very cat savvy and gets along well with my cat; I also think he would do great with a dog sibling. Benson is looking for any calm home with a confident, experienced dog owner who loves to be affectionate and cuddle as much as he does, and can continue to grow his confidence inside the home and on outside adventures.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

250519.name: Knock Knock
250519.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Knock Knock is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Knock Knock arrived at the Care Center as an owner surrender. Knock Knock's previous owner reported that he is fearful of unfamiliar people. Knock Knock has remained selective with people and been observed to escalate to defensive behaviors at times. In a recent handling assessment Knock Knock escalated to growling and lunging at a staff member, however was reported to be social in his first assessment. With familiar staff Knock Knock remains social, allows contact with a wiggly body, and is treat receptive. Medically, Knock Knock is apparently healthy.

Knock Knock arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. He has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to bare teeth, growl, lunge, and dodge the leash when handlers approach him in kennel. Recently, Knock Knock has been observed to warm up to handlers. However, during his reassessment, Knock Knock growled and lunged at the handler when they approached him. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home. 

Meet Knock Knock!
Knock Knock came into the shelter after his owner was no longer able to care for him. He is a social, people-oriented boy who approaches quickly and is eager to interact with handlers. He enjoys attention and play, but can become very excited in social situations and may have trouble settling once he is engaged.

My Ideal Home
Knock Knock will do best in an adult-only home that can provide structure, consistency, and guidance around impulse control. He will benefit from calm routines and reward-based training to help him learn how to settle and channel his enthusiasm in appropriate ways.

Good with Other Pets?
Knock Knock has shown playful and tolerant behavior with other dogs, including loose and wiggly greetings and play bows. He may enjoy social dogs in a structured setting, but his excitement level means introductions should still be supervised and gradual.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to reactivity in stimulating situations.

Things to Know
Knock Knock is a friendly, energetic boy who pulls mildly on leash and stays engaged with his handler. He enjoys play with toys and interaction with people but needs help learning calm behaviors and impulse control. With consistency, structure, and positive reinforcement, he has strong potential to channel his enthusiasm in a more focused way.

Fun Fact
Knock Knock lives up to his name because when he is excited, he is basically "knocking" at life with his whole body, ready to play, ready to greet, and always ready to say hello first.

250530.name: Sadie
250530.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!


A volunteer writes: With a smile bright enough to light up not just a room but the entire shelter, Sadie's personality can best be described as capital-F FUN. A moment with her is enough to whisk your blues away, and yet another reminder of why we simply don't deserve dogs. On walks, she delights us with her happy trot as she looks up at us - almost as if she's skipping with glee.

She's a spirited, happy girl, passing other humans and dogs without a care in the world. With slightly oversized ears always at attention and a permanent grin, she's quickly become a volunteer favorite; everyone can't say enough about how much they love her, and how lovely she is to walk. We can't imagine her future adopters will ever have a bad day that can't be comforted by being in her presence.

Sadie was found tied to a pole in Coney Island on a cold day in March, and brought to the shelter by police, so we don't know much about her past. Sadly she's been living in a crate in an overflow room since she arrived. She is already spayed and ready to go home today!

A volunteer writes: With a smile bright enough to light up not just a room but the entire shelter, Sadie's personality can best be described as capital-F FUN. A moment with her is enough to whisk your blues away, and yet another reminder of why we simply don't deserve dogs. On walks, she delights us with her happy trot as she looks up at us - almost as if she's skipping with glee. She's a spirited, happy girl, passing other humans and dogs without a care in the world. With slightly oversized ears always at attention and a permanent grin, she's quickly become a volunteer favorite; everyone can't say enough about how much they love her, and how lovely she is to walk. We can't imagine her future adopters will ever have a bad day that can't be comforted by being in her presence. Sadie was found tied to a pole in Coney Island on a cold day in March, and brought to the shelter by police, so we don't know much about her past. Sadly she's been living in a crate in an overflow room since she arrived. She is already spayed and ready to go home today!

250552.name: Garfield
250552.summary:
My foster writes: Garfield was found as a stray with part of his ear missing, but I think it only adds to his charm. (How many dogs do you know who sleep with one ear forever up?!) It also says a lot that he's been through so much, yet is still so loving and trusting of people. He loves playing with toys, especially the squeaky one, but is happy to share them w/ you and will drop them directly into your lap if you let him.
He's great with essential training commands-sit, stay, and lie down-and is easy to walk, even for someone who isn't very experienced w/ dogs. If you're cooking or doing chores, he is happy to simply sit nearby while you're busy. On the other hand, if you want to snuggle or feel like playing, he's thrilled to oblige! He has great manners-despite all his energy, he focuses that energy on chewing or chasing toys, but completely ignores shoes, socks, furniture, and cushions.
Garfield is an incredibly sweet boy who radiates sweetness and loves to be around people!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am playful and cute!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.

A volunteer writes: This Garfield could cure anyone's case of the Mondays. Although not as plump as his feline namesake, I would almost bet this boy loves lasagna as much as anyone would expect. Garfield is a year old and only 42 pounds, perfect for lap sitting and wearing PJs. He has been social, silly, and easy going. He walks with a loose leash, checking in for snacks as often as you can provide them!

Garfield was found alone and loose on Flatbush Avenue, skinny and bleeding from his ear, the bit of it that remains! Loosing half an ear can't break this boys spirit, it just makes him all the more special. Garfield is rated for beginner adopters.

250584.name: Mousse
250584.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other pets.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
Mousse tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and displays consistent signs of overstimulation. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, single-pet, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Mousse reached her paw out from her cubby to pick up her toy for about five seconds, told me it was her best and then asked if it was good enough. Of course it is, but for someone like Mousse who has been trying to figure out exactly what kitty work is expected of her, her efforts and progress are adorably heartening but also illustrate that shelter life can be a bit confusing without a road map. Brought to us in March without many details about her life before, we have to give Mousse some credit. Shelter life can be overwhelming at times but still she's consistently shown glimpses of promise. Trying to play in her own way and sometimes enthusiastically allowing pets, we know that Mousse could go a whole lot further in life if only someone would give her a little chance.

250608.name: Luna
250608.summary:
Meet Luna!
Luna is a sweet, soft-hearted girl who was found tied up on the street before coming into our care. Despite her past, she's shown a gentle, affectionate nature and is quickly learning that people can be a source of comfort and safety.

Personality
Luna can be a little shy at first, but she warms up quickly and leans into attention once she feels safe. She often greets handlers with a soft body, wagging tail, and gentle affection, and she especially enjoys staying close for reassurance. Once comfortable, she becomes a very loving "leaner," happily pressing into people for pets and affection like a 60lb cuddle companion.

Leash Walks
Luna walks nicely on leash with only mild pulling and is generally easygoing outdoors. She tends to ignore both people and other dogs while walking, staying focused on her handler.

Social Behavior
In new environments, Luna may appear a bit cautious and head shy, but she responds well to gentle interaction. She accepts handling, enjoys soft petting, and shows her comfort through wagging, leaning in, and relaxed body language once she trusts you.

Home Notes
Because she can be sensitive around her head and needs a calm approach, Luna would do best in a home without very young children. She also benefits from continued positive reinforcement and gentle confidence building, especially around other dogs, as busy environments can feel overwhelming for her.

Fun Fact
Luna is known for becoming a full-body "leaner" when she bonds with you, happily pressing in for comfort like she's giving hugs back. Once she trusts you, she really commits to being your shadow and your snuggle buddy. 🐾

250609.name: Liba
250609.summary:
Meet Liba!
Liba is a 1-year-old sweetheart who's still figuring out the world after coming in as a stray. New places can feel a little overwhelming for her, but through it all, she keeps coming back to people for comfort and connection. She's a soft, sensitive girl with a playful side just waiting to shine once she feels safe.

There is an adorable video of me on a boroughbreak.  Click here to experience the cuteness! 

My Ideal Home
Liba would love a calm, patient home where she can settle in at her own pace. She's still young and ready to learn, so a family that can help guide her with positive reinforcement and gentle structure will be perfect. Daily walks and playtime will help her feel her best, and a predictable routine will go a long way in helping her relax.

Living with Other Animals
Since Liba came in as a stray, we don't know much about her past with other dogs. So far, she's shown that she can feel a bit unsure around them and may need slow, thoughtful introductions. She might be happiest as your one-and-only for now while she builds confidence. Dog parks aren't her thing at this time.

Good with Kids?
Because Liba can be a little nervous and still has some puppy-like habits, she'd likely do best with older, dog-savvy kids or an adult home that can help her learn and feel secure.

Things to Know
Liba walks pretty nicely on leash with just a little pulling and tends to mind her business around people and other dogs outside. In the shelter, she can seem a bit stressed (lots of pacing and panting), but she stays very tolerant during handling and leans on people for comfort. She's a Level 2 pup who will really benefit from continued training, confidence-building, and lots of patience. She also has some medical needs that staff can go over with you.

Fun Fact
Liba is equal parts wiggly, worried, and wonderful-and once she feels safe, her playful, adorable side really starts to peek through. She's just waiting for someone to help her feel at home. 🐾
