250625.name: Walter
250625.summary:
My Foster Writes: 
Walter is a very handsome, vocal and sweet boy. He previously lived with human adults and several cats. He loves the company of other cats, particularly his sister. While initially shy in a new home, he will open up and enjoy petting and flopping on the floor for attention. Being a long hair, he benefits from the occasional brushing to help prevent mats. While he is going through alot of scary life changes, Walter has been reported to be very affectionate and playful. A home without small children is recommended, but older children familiar with cat body language will do great.

Every cat is the best and most handsome and Walter is no exception. Walter is a charismatic med/long-haired tabby with a graceful bottle-brush tail. He's a chatty young man who communicates his needs and reports his position in the house. He eats well, especially with a little variety, and he looks forward to his nighttime treat. Since he's a social eater, Walter can be petted while he eats.
Walter loves life - other cats, familiar people, and just about any quiet toy make him so excited that he has to flip and roll! Bouncy balls are his favorite for playing by himself. Since he is so energetic and curious, Walter is an excellent candidate for leash and harness training, clicker training, and adventure trials. Once he remembers that he's tired, he prefers to curl up near his person or fellow cat so that he can cuddle and hold paws in his sleep.
While Walter is undecided about brushes, he enjoys and benefits from thorough pets and face scritches. Pumpkin powder mixed into his nighttime treat helps with hairballs.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

250662.name: Doe
250662.summary:
Doe is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appears wary of human contact. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

Doe is a tiny snow-kissed beauty with the gentlest soul. 🤍✨

This dainty little lady spends most of her time tucked safely inside her cozy hidey box, quietly watching the world from where she feels secure. The shelter has been a bit too overwhelming for her sensitive heart, but she remains tolerant of gentle touch and patient kindness.

Doe is the kind of cat who will need a calm home, soft voices, and someone who understands that love doesn't always arrive loudly - sometimes it arrives in tiny, brave moments. Beneath her shy exterior is a lovely little cat just waiting to feel safe enough to bloom.

If you have a quiet home and a gentle heart, Doe may be the delicate companion you've been waiting for. 🕊️🐾

250663.name: Poe
250663.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Poe is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is an under socialized adult cat and is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful and under socialized adult cat adjust to strangers.

Poe is a tiny cream-and-white sweetheart with a pink heart-shaped nose, delicate little freckles, and the gentlest soul you could imagine. 🤍✨

Right now, the world feels a bit too big for this sensitive boy, so he spends most of his time tucked safely inside his cozy cat den. But his caretakers have caught glimpses of his curiosity - especially when treats are involved. He'll cautiously peek out, investigate his snack offerings, and then scamper back to safety like the tiny, brave creature he is.

Poe does not currently feel comfortable with petting or handling, and he'll need a patient, understanding home willing to let him warm up on his own timeline. In his previous home, he lived peacefully with other cats, and in shelter he has been respectful and tolerant of his feline sibling's space.

This little guy may never be the life of the party, but for someone who appreciates shy, tender-hearted cats, Poe's quiet trust will feel incredibly special. 🐾

250664.name: Joe
250664.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form


A volunteer writes: We may not always see Joe at his best, but we try to see Joe for he is and that can mean a whole lot when trying to make a new friend. Joe's a cat who needs to work a little harder than most to fit in largely because things don't come as easily to him as they do to others. Joe was brought to us from a home with many cats and hasn't been particularly open to many of the things we have to offer. Often choosing to curl up in the safety of his den as he waits for the day to pass, there are a number of things we know aren't going to speak to Joe, namely pets and scritches. There are, however, a number of things that do. For example, when I slowed down and read to Joe, he shared some very sweet slow blinks before tucking himself in to listen. He's hoping to find a calm and patient family where he can learn to be the best cat he can be.

250701.name: Chop
250701.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Chop!
Chop was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and is ready to find a fresh start with a family of his own. This handsome boy has a medium energy level and loves spending time with his people, whether it's heading out for a walk, playing with his favorite rope toys, or hopping in the car for an adventure. He's ready to chop his way right into your heart!

My Ideal Home
Chop would love an adopter who can provide daily walks, enrichment, and plenty of positive reinforcement. He enjoys staying active but also appreciates a predictable routine to help him feel confident. Puzzle toys, appropriate chew toys, and fun training sessions will keep both his mind and body happy.

Good with Other Pets?
Chop's previous family shared that he was friendly with unfamiliar dogs on leash, but he has shown that he can be uncomfortable around some dogs in the shelter environment. Slow introductions to dog friends are recommended, and dog parks are not the best fit for him. He also chased cats on walks with his previous owner, so a home without cats or small animals is recommended.

Good with Kids?
An adult only home is recommended for Chop. He can be sensitive about having his paws handled, especially during nail trims, and will do best with adopters who can respect his boundaries while helping him build positive associations through reward based training.

Things to Know
Chop is housetrained, enjoys car rides, and isn't picky when it comes to treats, making training extra rewarding. His previous family shared that he sometimes chewed on shoes, so providing plenty of appropriate chew toys and enrichment will help keep him on the right paw. He may need a little time to settle into new situations, but with patience and kindness, this sweet boy is sure to shine.

Chop is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is blossoming with every training session. He is working on learning to relax on a mat, which is helping him find his calm and feel settled no matter the environment. With patience and positive reinforcement, Chop is developing the confidence and composure he needs to truly thrive.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Went to Astoria park for a long walk where Chop decided to stop unexpectedly to roll around on the grass. Walked around the park with no bother. Then went to small beach area in Astoria as well where it look like it was his first time in a beach and was very curious about the waves. He very quickly decided that he liked the water and showed me he knows how to swim. After when to my private backyard area where we played fetch then he was rinsed and dried from the salt water. Very well behaved. Did not pull on the leash whatsoever. Really enjoys car rides.

He very quickly decided that he liked the water and showed me he knows how to swim. After when to my private backyard area where we played fetch then he was rinsed and dried from the salt water. Very well behaved. Did not pull on the leash whatsoever. Really enjoys car rides.

250752.name: Yosemite
250752.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Yosemite is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.
A volunteer writes: Yosemite was found sitting stiff frozen on a blanket with friend Everglades in a park. Their past life is a total mystery. A GS scooped them up and brought them over  almost four months ago to the MACC. Time and enrichment from staff and volunteers very slowly got him out of his hide out. Yosemite started to sit more and more on his balcony or rest in his "living room". He became curious, observing people, his surroundings and even extended his arms to get treats(when he realized that other cats were getting squeeze ups or temptations).  Yosemite has still a very hard time to trust us, even those he has seen the faces countless times over so many months. Yosemite likes to play though as you can see on his photos. He enjoys catnip toys and feather wands. He occasionally will accept a brief pet on his head when he samples treats or eats(see videos). Recently, Yosemite was reunited with his former housemate. Did they recognize each other? Who really knows? The two "brothers" coexist pretty nicely and although both kitties are still in a cage(double), their lives have tremendously changed for the better! I think that Everglades is a little bossy and protective but  Yosemite, in a very diplomatic way, lets him know. It is pretty cute. It is pretty endearing too to see them both laying next to each other in a cubby. Like Yosemite, Everglades has trust issues with humans but he might be one or two steps ahead of Yosemite. For sure, both cats need an experienced and patient adopter or foster. May be (of course, this is only my thought, the one of a volunteer), the duo could be part of an indoor caterie for a start and stay together while mingling with other felines? I do not know...May be just a silly thought? We all wish for both brothers to stay together because we ALL can see that they support each other and  look happier. That is what love is all about! 

What my friends at ACC say about me:]
I came in with my friend Everglades 250751 and would love to find a home with them!

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

250780.name: Lila
250780.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Pop-Up Event on:

Saturday, May 23 | 12PM - 4PM
Life Time One Wall Street Gym
29 New St, New York, NY 10005

adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!


What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Lila appreciates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter and may generally be sensitive to her environment. She will likely a full decompression period in a smaller area when brought home and need time to warm up to the rest of her new home and new family. We recommend that she go to an adult-only home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: Lila was found wandering around on her own and I imagine her confidently explaining over her shoulder that she had it all under control as she walked on by concerned passersby. Did she really though? People noticed Lila and called the police who brought her to us where she kind of seemed to start with a self contained approach. I admit it might feel safer in the moment, but over time we've been able to show Lila that there is simply no burden she needs to shoulder alone. We'll be right beside her as we help find just the perfect fit of a family. We don't know much else about Lila's life before, but we know that shelter life can feel like a lot for our gentle hearted friends. The first few times I met Lila, she stayed happily ensconced in her little bed and though she was totally ok with me hanging out with her, she didn't really make moves to come say hello. I'm thrilled that she's started to show us more of her personality and she sure can't wait to show you.

250784.name: Goofy Goober
250784.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Goofy Goober is At risk due to behavioral concerns. While in the Care Centers, Goofy Goober was reported to grab staff members' leashes while being returned to his kennel. On one occasion, he chewed through a staff member's slip lead. He has also, occasionally, displayed signs of kennel deterioration, including banging on his transfer door, vocalizing loudly, and repeatedly jumping up and down in his kennel. Outside of the kennel, Goofy Goober is social and friendly with staff and readily accepts treats offered to him. Medically, Goofy Goober has dermatitis and dental disease.

Meet Goofy Goober!
Goofy Goober was found as a stray and is now looking for a home that can match his big personality with calm structure and guidance. He's a friendly, people-oriented boy who is always ready to say hello and be part of whatever's going on.

My Ideal Home
Goofy Goober would do best in an experienced adult-only home that can help him build impulse control and support him in managing his excitement. He'll thrive with consistent routines, positive reinforcement, and clear expectations.

Good with Other Pets?
Goofy Goober has shown neutral behavior around other dogs in the shelter, including calm greetings and appropriate disengagement. Slow, structured introductions are recommended as he continues to build focus and manners.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 due to a low threshold for arousal and his tendency to become very jumpy and overstimulated during interactions.

Things to Know
Goofy Goober is an affectionate, energetic dog who gets very excited around people and shows his enthusiasm with jumping, panting, and close contact seeking. While he is friendly and social, he benefits from help learning calmer greetings and more controlled engagement. With structure, training, and appropriate outlets for his energy, he has strong potential to become a well-mannered and joyful companion.

Fun Fact
True to his name, Goofy Goober is all heart, big feelings, big wiggles, and even bigger love to give.

250790.name: Ranch Dressin
250790.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ranch Dressin is at risk due to behavioral concerns. He has been involved in several bite incidents that did not break the skin, though most resulted in red marks. These incidents primarily occurred during handling procedures, such as collaring, leashing, or putting on a coat. He has also been reported to escalate to lunging in some situations. Recently, he was observed to lick his kennel walls. On walks, Ranch Dressin is social with staff and enjoys treats while being petted. Medically, Ranch Dressin has diarrhea.

Ranch Dressin came to ACC as a stray, so we don't have any information on how he is in a home environment.  Ranch has been timid with a low body when interacting with most staff.  Over time, Ranch Dressin has warmed up slightly to familiar handlers, taking treats when approached slowly.  Ranch Dressin would do best in a quiet, low-traffic environment where he can decompress and show off his true colors.

Feedback from my favorite volunteers - Once he warms up, he loves to snuggle on the steps, climbing up close for ear scratches, belly rubs, and chin massages. He completely lights up and forgets his worries when given a toy, happily carrying it on walks and playing fetch. He has lovely leash manners and is highly motivated by tasty biscuit treats. Ranch Dressing is currently dealing with shelter-related stress (FAS), which makes him eager to return to the security of his kennel at the end of a walk. Underneath his initial nervousness lies an incredibly tender, loving dog who is ready to thrive with a new family!

Ranch Dressin came into the care center as an owner surrender after being returned due to behavioral concerns in the home. The prior owner says he loves any kind of treat and is a good eater loves pup cup Greek yogurt and pumpkin and steak.  A period of decompression is recommended to allow Ranch Dressin to acclimate comfortably to his new environment; force-free, reward based training only is advised when introducing Ranch Dressin to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Ranch Dressin presents with outside of the care centers.

250820.name: Charm
250820.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Charm is at risk due to behavioral concerns. While Charm has been highly social with handlers and engaged in play with other select dogs during playgroup sessions, he is displaying a concerning level of arousal and kennel stress as his length of stay progresses. In his kennel, he is jumping up and spinning. Charm has intermittently been leash biting and thrashing when taken out of the kennel, kennel fighting as he exits the kennel room, and mouthing at handlers/staffs hands, has nipped at handlers' chests, leaving red marks. Due to these concerns, it has become increasingly difficult to walk Charm. Medically, Charm is apparently healthy.

Charm was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is mostly unknown. Charm initially was fearful with leashing but tolerated having his collar clipped. Once out of the kennel, he is loose and wiggly during interactions, engaging in play with toys and readily soliciting attention. Charm was returned by a trial adopter due to being mouthy and reactive to other dogs. He has been observed to jump up and mouth handlers/staff's hands and has recently begun to leash bite and occasionally thrash. He is now jumping up and grabbing onto clothing or onto a handler's person. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Charm be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.


Meet Charm!
Charm was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and is now looking for a fresh start. He is a social, affectionate, and very people oriented dog who enjoys being where his humans are. In the shelter, he comes forward readily, leans into attention, and shows a playful, engaged personality. He can get very excited during interaction and tends to jump up often, but he remains friendly and eager to connect.

My Ideal Home
Charm will do best in an adult home that can provide consistency, daily activity, and structure around impulse control. He is active and thrives with a routine that includes exercise, training, and enrichment to keep his mind and body busy.

Good with Other Pets?
Charm shows strong reactivity on leash toward dogs and other outdoor triggers including bikes, cars, and small animals. He can lunge and bark when overstimulated, so he will need managed walks and a controlled environment. At this time, he is best suited as the only pet or with very careful, structured introductions if appropriate.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children due to high excitement levels, leash reactivity, and difficulty settling in stimulating environments.

Things to Know
Charm is an affectionate and energetic dog who enjoys companionship and being involved in daily life. He can be a strong puller on leash and becomes easily overstimulated outdoors. He is also sensitive to loud noises and may show destructive behaviors when anxious or under stimulated. On the positive side, he is comfortable with handling, grooming, and routine care, and he responds well to attention and engagement. With structure and consistent training, he has strong potential to improve his impulse control and settle into a stable routine.

Fun Fact
When Charm is comfortable, his name fits perfectly. He turns into a goofy, affectionate shadow who just wants to be near his person and soak up all the attention he can get.

Charm is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is working hard to become a calmer, more confident pup on the leash. He can get overwhelmed when he encounters other dogs or distractions during walks, but through his training he is learning to refocus and look to his handler for guidance. With consistent practice and positive reinforcement, Charm is making real strides one walk at a time.

250836.summary:
Dino is a sweet, affectionate boy who loves attention and isn't shy about asking for it. He'll greet you with a soft meow, stretch out, and happily roll over for pets. Once you're close, he leans right in-rubbing against your hands and soaking up all the love he can get. Dino enjoys gentle affection and will make sure you know just how much he appreciates it. This charming little guy is ready to find a home where he can share his cuddly, loving personality every day.


What my friends at ACC say about me:
Dino is a super sweet cat who was on top of the shelf and gave a sweet, slightly chirping greeting meow, ate a treat immediately, and then jumped down for more treats. He loves treats, but he seems to love petting even more because he would pause in his eating while getting pet. He leaned in nicely for cheek rubs and enjoyed petting all over his body. He then came gently into the assessor's arms, where he sat quietly, curious, looking around the room and enjoying his time outside the kennel. He then gently went back into the kennel, devoured a Squeeze Up tube, and remained curious, sweet, and slightly energetic.

Dino interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Cobra Kai was surrendered by his previous owner due to moving to a new home that does not allow pets. Cobra was described as a very active, playful, and independent dog who enjoys spending his time where people are, in the basement or in his wire crate. During his stay in care, Cobra Kai has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

250878.name: Dr. Zeus
250878.summary:
Meet Dr. Zeus!
Dr. Zeus was surrendered when his owner was no longer able to care for him. He has lived with both cats and dogs before and is described as an affectionate, playful companion who enjoys staying close to his people. He likes being involved in whatever his humans are doing, especially if it involves walks or play.

Personality
Dr. Zeus is friendly and people-oriented, and he often seeks out attention once he feels comfortable. He can show signs of anxiety in new environments, but he is also capable of engaging with handlers and leaning in for affection. 

My Ideal Home
Dr. Zeus would do best in an adult-only home that can offer structure, patience, and a predictable routine. He will benefit from continued support with confidence-building and calm exposure to new environments. br />

Good with Other Pets?
Dr. Zeus has lived with both dogs and cats previously. He has shown neutral behavior on leash with other dogs in care, though careful introductions are still recommended to set him up for success in a new home.

Good with Kids?
Dr. Zeus is recommended for an adult-only home at this time due to his anxiety in new environments and need for a calm, predictable setting.

Things to Know
Dr. Zeus enjoys walks, play, and interactive toys, and has a generally social nature with his people. He may show initial hesitation when leashed or in unfamiliar situations, but he warms up with patience. He will thrive with structure, gentle guidance, and regular enrichment.

Fun Fact
Dr. Zeus can't wait to becomes your everyday sidekick. ⚡️

250907.name: Rocky Road
250907.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Rocky Road. A two-year old lover boy with a light-hearted, goofy, and curious personality. This little man is ready to move into his forever home and become a part of a loving family. He is is quick to bond and become loyal to his people. You will quickly fall in love with this puppy eyed ball of energy.
He loves to snuggle, play with his toys, and learn new tricks. He still has plenty of youthful energy so enjoys long walks, play time, and a good treat. He likes to be pampered and doesn't mind being bathed or cleaned - he is very gentle.
Rocky Road felt at home with us in first few hours. And we're sure he'll also quickly warm up to you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I need a home without cats or small animals.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

250925.name: Cody
250925.summary:
Meet Cody, a smart, playful, and personality-packed dog who is ready to find his next adventure! This active boy loves being with his people and thrives on companionship, whether he's showing off his impressive list of tricks, playing fetch, riding in the car, or relaxing in the sunshine. Cody is highly intelligent and knows a variety of commands, making him a fun and engaging companion for a family that enjoys interacting with their dog.

His previous owner described him as incredibly clever with a larger-than-life personality, saying he sometimes seems more human than dog. While he's the perfect size for indoor living, he also has plenty of energy and enthusiasm for outdoor activities.

In addition to his many talents, Cody has experience being around horses, making him a great candidate for a home with an equestrian lifestyle. If you're looking for an affectionate, intelligent, and active companion who will keep you smiling every day, Cody may be the perfect match for you.

250929.name: Mr. Mustard
250929.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Mr Mustard!
Mr. Mustard arrived as a stray, and right now he's still figuring out that the world isn't such a scary place. He's a sensitive boy who's looking for a calm, patient home where he can take life at his own "slow and steady" pace and build confidence in his own time.

Personality
Mr. Mustard is a quiet, cautious guy who prefers to hang back and observe rather than jump into new situations. Right now, he's more of a watch and wait kind of pup, sticking close to familiar handlers and showing that he feels safest when things stay predictable and gentle.

He isn't quite ready to take treats or seek out attention yet in new settings, but he does best when given space and allowed to come around at his own pace. Think of him as a little mustard seed of potential who just needs time to grow. 🌱

Leash Walks
Mr. Mustard keeps things simple on leash with a calm, no-fuss walking style. No pulling, no drama, just a quiet stroll through the world while he takes everything in at his own speed.

Social Behavior
Right now, Mr. Mustard is more comfortable in the background than the spotlight. He is still learning to trust new people and environments and does best when interactions are gentle, slow, and on his terms. With time, patience, and consistency, he has room to blossom.

Home Life
Mr. Mustard will thrive in a calm, adult-only home where life moves at a softer pace. He needs someone who understands that confidence takes time and that the best relationships are built one small step at a time.

Fun Fact
He may be a little shy now, but once he feels safe, Mr. Mustard might just turn into someone's sweetest little condiment of comfort.

Mack has been placed on the at risk list for medical reasons. He has a painful left front leg and is reluctant to place weight on it. I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am playful and cute!

A Volunteer Wrote: We didn't need the lavish praise heaped on this sweetest boy from his former owner to fall in love: He's playful with dogs, friendly with strangers and children, loves car rides, and knows his basic commands. At the shelter, where he's been living in a pop up crate with great stoicism, he seems to be applying for most popular resident, beloved by all: He's a hugger, a lover, a lap dog who offers kisses to his walker's hands, and is as gentle on the leash as he is with everyone he meets. The one thing that scares him is people with hoodies, but summer is upon us so who needs to wear one while he remembers that the world is safe and ready to return his love and enthusiasm? Please come fetch this boy and let him live out his days walking loyally by your side.

250999.name: Sage
250999.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Sage is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. Due to concerning dog behavior Sage displayed in playgroup with a novel dog, she was tested with a fake dog. Sage when greeting the fake dog escalated when the fake dog was moved, biting onto the stomach area, readjusting his grip multiple times, and then holding and shaking. Sage continued to bite, hold, shake, and readjust onto the fake dog while moving around the yard, requiring an air can to disengage as she could not be refocused which may create a serious safety risk around other dogs in the future. Sage in the care center is very affectionate with staff, and loves to pet in there laps. Medically, Sage is apparently healthy.

Sage arrived at QACC as a stray with another dog and was initially social with staff but showed kennel reactivity and reluctance to return to his crate. During dog introductions, he displayed tense, stalking behavior toward a female dog, preventing direct interaction. In a controlled test with a fake dog, he initially appeared neutral but quickly escalated-charging, then repeatedly biting, holding, and shaking the fake dog. Although friendly with people,  we recommend he be placed in a home through one of our new hope partners.

A volunteer writes:  I often like to imagine what adult dogs at the shelter looked like as puppies, and the thought of Sage as one - with his gorgeous auburn coat, truly exceptional forehead wrinkles, and big pink splotch on his nose - makes my heart nearly explode. He's a beautiful pup, but I quickly realize he's much more than just his good looks.

Like many extraordinary dogs at the shelter right now, Sage is making the most of a less-than-ideal situation. Although he's been living in a crate in an overflow room since he arrived in late March, he hasn't let it break his spirit: He's always ready to go on long walks (he's been militantly housebroken), to play in the yard, and enjoy the small respites from his small living quarters. He's a happy soul with a vibrant personality, eager to connect with us and rest his paws on our lap. He seems to be curious when passing other dogs, and in fact was found wandering loose in the Brownsville area of Brooklyn alongside another dog, Cedar, who has since been placed with rescue. They were reported to be friendly with the police who picked them up and escorted them to the shelter.

251023.name: Juniper
251023.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Juniper is at risk for behavior reasons. He was initially highly fearful and avoidant during his first few weeks. With a slow approach, and lots of treats, he warmed up to staff and volunteers. Juniper is highly stressed in the kennel, constantly barking and jumping. He has escalated to lunging at staff when exiting. Medically, he is apparently healthy. 

Meet Juniper, this handsome boy was found as a stray and is still learning that the world can be a safe and kind place. Because of his past, Juniper may be a bit unsure when meeting new people-he can be avoidant of touch at first and prefers to take things at his own pace.

With patience, understanding, and a considerate approach, Juniper is already beginning to show his softer side. Juniper would do best in a calm, predictable home with someone who respects his boundaries and is willing to let him come out of his shell on his own terms. For the right person, watching Juniper build confidence and form a bond is an incredibly rewarding experience. Juniper was found along with other dogs.

If you're someone who believes in giving a dog the time and space they need to thrive, Juniper may be the perfect match for you.

251035.name: Jellybean
251035.summary:
🐾 Meet Jellybean!

Jellybean is a gentle, sweet-natured girl who's ready to find a loving home of her own. She was found as a stray, so her past is a bit of a mystery-but what we do know is that she has a soft heart and a kind spirit.

She can be a little shy at first, especially in new situations, but with a calm and considerate approach, Jellybean begins to relax and show her affectionate side. Once she feels safe, she enjoys quiet companionship and will happily stay close to her person.

Jellybean would do best with someone patient and understanding who can give her the time she needs to build confidence and trust. In return, you'll gain a loyal, loving companion who just wants to feel secure and cherished.

If you're looking for a sweet, sensitive dog to grow with, Jellybean might be the perfect match. 💕

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Jellybean is the most lovable happiest girl! She walks great on a leash and is so well behaved (no pulling as long as you hold the leash firmly, no leash biting, no barking, walks right next to you and just wants the occasional pet) She is everything you'd want in a dog! We have gone on little hikes, to the park, and to the beach and she loves sniffing and exploring her surroundings. She especially loves running around the sand at the beach and watching squirrels in the park. Also in 3 borough breaks with her I don't think I've ever heard her bark.

251043.name: Hamburglar
251043.summary:
Meet Hamburglar!
Hamburglar is a stray with a big personality and an even bigger heart. He is still figuring out the world around him and can feel unsure in new situations, but with patience and time he begins to show his playful, affectionate side. Once he feels safe, he really enjoys being around people and being part of whatever is going on.

Personality
Hamburglar can be a little reserved when first meeting new people, but he warms up with gentle encouragement and treats. Once he feels comfortable, his personality comes out in a big way. He becomes very affectionate and excited to interact, often seeking attention and wanting to be close to his handler.

Out and About
Hamburglar has a lot of energy and walks strongly on leash, especially when he is excited. He does not show concern toward people or other dogs while out, but he will need continued leash training to help him learn calmer walking habits. 

Social Behavior
Hamburglar enjoys contact and can be very expressive in how he seeks connection. He benefits from gentle guidance to help him learn calmer ways to greet and interact.

Training and Behavior
Hamburglar is a very enthusiastic dog who is still learning impulse control. He will benefit from continued positive reinforcement training to help him develop skills like sit, stay, and leave it. He also needs support around resource guarding, especially with toys, and should always be given space and safe trade options when working with valued items. He responds best to kind, reward based training and clear structure.


My Ideal Home
Hamburglar would do best with an experienced adopter who understands energetic and sensitive dogs. He will thrive in a home that can give him daily mental and physical enrichment along with calm guidance.

251078.name: Twilight Sparkle
251078.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

A volunteer writes: If we could get Twilight Sparkle to show the shelter the same openness she shows treats, it would probably go a long way. In the meantime, however, she seems pretty set on getting through the days from the comfort of her den. She'll accept some pets from our scratcher tool, but mostly what she comes out for are treats. What we know of Twilight Sparkle's life before the shelter began in a Park Ranger's garage where she was definitely trying her best to make things work for herself. Initially completely uninterested in their attempts of assistance, Twilight Sparkle eventually agreed that a forever home might be a better fit and so she's here with us hoping that someone will notice her in her den and give her a little chance.

251079.name: Sheera
251079.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Sheera is at risk due to medical concerns and behavior concerns. Sheera presented to the shelter with severe generalized skin ulcerations, which have markedly improved with treatment. She recently developed a swelling in her left forelimbs digits with a non-weight bearing lameness due to an unknown cause. Sheera needs continued veterinary care and possible diagnostics (such as a skin biopsy) to determine an underlying diagnosis for her skin concerns, though we are suspicious of an immune-mediated disease. Behaviorally, Sheera allows all medical handling and responds well to a slow approach. She recently has begun displaying kennel stress behaviors - wailing for extended periods of time throughout the day while sticking her snout or paws out from her food slot while still vocalizing. 

Meet Sheera!
Sheera is a beautiful husky who was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and now she's looking for a home that understands her sensitive side and her big heart. She is a social, affectionate girl who can also be a bit of a couch potato once she feels comfortable, and she has a playful streak that shines through with toys and people she trusts.

My Ideal Home
Sheera would do best in an adult-only home that can give her a calm, predictable environment. She benefits from slow introductions, gentle handling, and a patient approach that helps her feel secure as she builds confidence in new situations.

Good with Other Pets?
Sheera has lived with dogs before and is generally social with familiar dogs and tolerant of unfamiliar dogs in both home and shelter settings. As always, slow introductions are recommended to set her up for success.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 are recommended at this time due to Sheera's fearfulness and sensitivity to touch.

Things to Know
Sheera can be an anxious girl who may react to strangers or small dogs on walks by growling or barking, and she does best when given space and time to feel safe. She may also feel nervous in handling situations, especially when startled or touched unexpectedly, but she is unbothered by everyday handling like being moved or resting nearby people. Once comfortable, she shows a softer side, enjoys toys, knows several cues like sit and paw, and has a playful, intelligent personality. She is also very loyal to her people and forms strong bonds once she trusts her environment.

Fun Fact
Sheera may start out cautious, but once she knows you, she's all about playtime, treats, and sticking close to her favorite humans like a true husky sidekick.

251101.name: Crown
251101.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

My foster writes: Crown is a handsome, energetic dog looking for an active home to match his adventurous spirit! He loves walks, attention, and all the pets he can get. Despite his playful energy, he's very respectful in the home and has great house manners. Crown already knows cues like "sit" and "look at me," and he's eager to learn more every day. He enjoys being outside, exploring, and taking in the world around him. Crown is incredibly affectionate, friendly with the people he meets, and happiest when he's close to his person. With his sweet personality, smart mind, and loving nature, this really good boy is going to make an amazing companion.

Crown is a cute energetic loving dog. He loves to play fetch and getting pet, if you work from home, he will not leave your side. His favorite thing is going out for walks and exploring the neighborhood. Crown would love to get adopted by someone who can take him to the park and get lots of exercise

251134.name: Fogwhisker
251134.summary:
Meet Fogwhisker!

Fogwhisker came to SIACC from a home with 30+ other cats and very little socialization, so it's understandable that she's been a bit shy around us humans. Still, Fogwhisker braves the shelter environment like a champ, taking things one day at a time. Ideally, she would be able to open up in a calm, low-traffic environment, with lots of positive reinforcement (especially with treats!) to help her feel comfortable. Come say hi to Fogwhisker today!

A volunteer writes: It takes Fogwhisker a little minute to assemble all the courage she can muster in those tiny paws of hers, but we know that when she's given the time and space to do so, she'll really get it. This brings us to our next point that a quiet moment at the Care Center can be hard to come by so even though Fogwhisker spends a good part of the day collecting her confidence only to start back at square one, a patient, understanding, and loving forever home will likely go a long way in helping her become the cat she's meant to be. We don't have a lot of information about Fogwhisker's life before as she was brought to us from a home with many other cats and not a whole lot of experience with people. She still gets up each day to hope for a better one and she's really hoping today will include you.

251136.name: Shadowpaw
251136.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Shadowpaw is at risk due to ongoing, distance increasing behaviors displayed in care. He is an under socialized cat who may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is currently quick to lunge, hiss, and swat with nails extended during interactions. These behaviors have made cleaning tasks more difficult for staff to complete as he is much quicker to escalate. Due to these behaviors, Shadowpaw had to be moved into a lower traffic room. Staff have reported that in this room, he still continues to escalate. He would benefit from being placed into a stable home where he can be given the appropriate space to decompress. Medically, he has stage III dental disease.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

Meet Shadowpaw!

Shadowpaw is a bit of a wallflower here at the shelter. He prefers to keep things more low-key, hanging in the shadows or cuddling up in a nice hiding spot. He's in need of more socialization as an adult cat so he's best suited for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who have lots of love and patience to give. Think you're the one who can give this little guy the TLC he needs? Stop by and say hi to Shadowpaw at SIACC!

A volunteer writes: Shadowpaw kind of knows that patience is a big ask, especially when he's surrounded by so many bright and playful kitties. He would like to be included too, just at a pace that's a bit slower than some of the other cats you might meet. We don't know a lot about his life before the shelter as he came to us from a home with many other cats and not nearly as many opportunities to meet new people. Thus, he doesn't always know what to make of us. Shadowpaw enjoys having a little space and time to make his own decisions. If that's something you can spare with him, he'll be just the right fit.

251164.name: Lady G
251164.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

There is an adorable video of me on social media!  Click here to experience the cuteness! 

Meet Lady G!
Lady G came to us after being found living in difficult conditions with several other dogs, and she is now ready for a fresh start. Despite her past, she is a gentle, social girl who enjoys being around people. She comes over for attention, leans into pets, and shows her sweet nature in soft, quiet ways.

My Ideal Home
Lady G would do best in a calm, adult-only home that can give her structure, patience, and time to fully settle in. A peaceful environment will help her feel safe and build confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Lady G has lived with multiple dogs before, but her interactions can be a bit mixed. She may feel unsure in new situations and can become overwhelmed, so slow introductions and a thoughtful approach will be important. A lower traffic, more controlled environment is recommended.

Good with Kids?
Recommended for a home without children under 13 due to her sensitivity and need for a calm environment.

Things to Know
Lady G can be a bit anxious, especially in busy or high energy settings, and may pant or feel overwhelmed at times. She benefits from gentle handling, predictable routines, and positive reinforcement training. With consistency and kindness, she has a lot of potential to relax and grow more confident.

Fun Fact
Lady G lives up to her name, she's a soft, gentle girl who carries herself with a quiet, regal charm once she feels comfortable.

251180.name: Sky
251180.summary: Sky is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans other than her owners from an early age and likely had limited handling experience. She is very apprehensive of people and may begin to grumble or growl when touch is attempted. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

Blue is a petite tabby with the tiniest meow. She previously lived with human adults and several cats. She seems to get along with her brother in the foster home, and may do well in a home with another calm and friendly cat. Blue is rather shy in unfamiliar environments and around new people, but will open up with time. She is reported to be playful and independent. In the foster home, she has started to accept limited petting and treats. A home without small children is recommended, but older children respectful of her space may be fine.

251198.summary:

I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Symba has made excellent progress since his first assessment. When approached, he did move from the main kennel into the cubby, but then when offered squeeze up treats, he ate them repeatedly off the assessor's finger, coming forward slightly for more. He allowed and seemed to appreciate petting on his cheek and head and was even able to get chin scratches while eating squeeze up off the assessor's hand. As hoped and predicted, he has made nice progress.

Symba interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in previous nervousness.

251205.name: Quinn
251205.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Quinn!
Quinn was found abandoned on the street and has shown himself to be a social, energetic, and affectionate young dog who loves play, enrichment, and spending time with people. He is especially people-oriented and quickly bonds with handlers, often greeting them with enthusiasm and playful behavior.

My Ideal Home
Quinn would do best in an active, structured home that helps him channel his energy into positive outlets such as training, enrichment, and exercise. He benefits from consistency, patience, and continued work on impulse control, confidence building, and calm handling.

Good with Other Pets?
Quinn has shown interest in other dogs during introductions and is generally social, but interactions should always be supervised and carefully managed to ensure comfort for all dogs involved.

Good with Kids?
Due to his exuberance, impulse control needs, and handling sensitivity, Quinn is recommended for an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Quinn is a playful and affectionate dog who loves toys, attention, and interactive time with people. He can be easily spooked by loud noises and may become overly excited during handling or play, so continued positive reinforcement training is important. He is working on skills like settling on a mat and polite exchange, and he responds very well to food motivation and structure. He is a social and engaged walker, though he can be strong on leash at times. With consistency and support, Quinn continues to grow more confident and focused each day.

Volunteer Note
A volunteer writes: As I sit with Quinn in the play yard, watching him retrieve balls or joyously tossing a soft toy into the air for himself, I marvel at how trusting and open he remains after 70 days in confinement. All I can offer is a 15-minute walk, Pupperoni and cuddles, yet he greets me like I'm his BFF. When I call out to him, he runs to me like I'm a long-lost friend, then hops into my lap, happily accepting pets. This young, energetic boy loves carefree playtime, but is also food motivated, which is great for learning. He is similarly noted by the shelter's canine behavior team to be social (and even playbowing to them!) & engage with enrichment as he works on impulse control, a skill that would be understandably easier for an adolescent to develop in a consistent home environment. Bonus: he comes pre-housebroken! In shelter assessments, he's been found to ignore dogs on walks, and take positive interest in another dog during a supervised introduction. Quinn is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is putting in great work each and every day. He is developing two important skills, polite exchange and relaxing on a mat, both of which are helping him become a more grounded and easygoing companion. With positive reinforcement guiding the way, Quinn is growing more confident and composed with every training session.

251209.name: Luna
251209.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Luna is displaying behaviors that preclude placement in the adoptions room and/or may require further investigation before placement in a home.  She has tried to swat and scratch and is very fearful in the shelter environment and does not currently tolerate petting or handling. The behavior department feels that placement with a New Hope Partner is the best option at this time. She was owner surrendered but other than saying she is aggressive the former owner gave us no additional information. 

A volunteer writes: We're determined to meet Luna halfway as working through the shelter days stretching before her seems to be written all across her face. She could be charmingly indifferent to our efforts, but it could also be that we haven't quite been able to catch her interest just yet. We don't really have much to go by as Luna was abandoned in the shelter vestibule with no information. Loafing on top of her den, she may be considering the stream of variables or perhaps her current and unenviable job of telling us everything about who she is now. It's a big job and we'd love to be helpful, but each time we've tried to get started on the right foot with her, we've promptly been told it isn't the right time. I imagine her sighing to herself as she returns to her thoughts. Luna may not be sure how to ask for the second chance she needs, which may be where meeting her halfway comes in, because we're asking you to please give her one.

251226.name: Gandalf
251226.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Gandalf is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A volunteer writes: Gandalf's previous family forgot one very important family member when they moved out and that would be Gandalf. Gandalf was found wandering around an apartment building, looking as lost as he probably felt. While the Good Samaritan who found him was able to scoop him up in a towel, he hasn't been as amenable when it comes to acclimating to shelter life. Uninterested in our offers of treats and toys, Gandalf mostly prefers to stay in his den to pass the seemingly endless shelter days and we think that, in spite of his efforts to say otherwise, he'd really love a little chance to be seen and known. 
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.

251238.name: Cloud Milkyway Galaxy
251238.summary:
My foster writes: Hi, I'm Cloud, sometimes comes with a thunderstorm. I am a small pittie who loves to snuggle my way into your hearts. My foster parents say I have the biggest pittie smile and the wettest kisses they have ever received, my entire neighborhood loves me and says the same thing also! I love a long walk to the bodega, nice hike on the mountains, and going for a swim on the beach. If you are looking for a buddy on the couch and a buddy for a run, I'm your gal!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

251241.name: Garfield Theodore
251241.summary: A volunteer writes: Garfield Theodore sees the bigger picture, so if you see him sitting pressed up against the door with his fur going in every direction, please just know it's part of a plan. He's an extraordinarily smart guy who feels compelled to manage several projects concurrently, so Garfield Theodore has taken on shelter life with that type of understanding exuberance. He knows he has to work a little harder to stand out so he's always trying out some new moves that he hopes might impress you. Garfield Theodore's latest is a bouncy leap onto my shoulders. Making himself big and tall, he gave me a hug and then nuzzled so emphatically I couldn't help but fall in love. He did this several times with slight variations, one time putting his whole nose into my ear but I think he was just trying to ask which one I think his forever family will most like. A life of the party cat who loves to be in the mix, Garfield Theodore's looking to find an experienced cat family who will provide cat projects for him to preside over and a forever family to love.

251281.name: Mini Cooper
251281.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Mini Cooper is standing upright in his den, lip licking and slightly tense as the assessor approaches. When he is spoken to softly, he pokes his head out and observes the assessor with wide eyes before approaching the front. He leans forward and sniffs their finger before softly head bunting it, allowing and leaning into all petting with his tail held high. He does occasionally stop and look around the room towards the top of the kennels as if contemplating a place to jump, but his attention is easily refocused with petting, soft talk, and crunchy treats. Mini Cooper is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm and purring when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all petting and allowing the assessor to hand feed him a squeeze up.

Mini Cooper interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Mini Cooper go to an adult only home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression, and overstimulation. 
A volunteer writes:
Mini Cooper appeared a little shy when I first met him but few days down the line, he revealed himself to be a very welcoming host. What a cutie! Head bunting, making biscuits, purring and trying his best to soak all the love he could get. Mini Cooper is a cute and petite gent, a bit on the thin side and with a worn coat that begs good nutrition and TLC. He was owned it seems since kittenhood and surrendered for allergies that developed in a family member. Mini Cooper is said to be a very active kitty who can sometimes play a little too excitingly, very affectionate, shy(and hiding) at first with strangers and kids(something he did at first upon arrival at the care center). Mini Cooper never met with any cat or dog. I love Mini Cooper at first sight as he looks adorable, engaging, endearing and so in need of a loving and caring new owner or family. Mini Cooper is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!

251306.name: Kwik
251306.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Kwik is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Upon his arrival Kwik was noted to be highly social with staff during his handling assessment.  Unfortunately, Kwik has been observed to be highly dog reactive. Noted to snarl, pull hard and fixate on other dogs while in the yard. In one instance when handlers attempt to switch Kwik to a slip lead he is noted to jump up with an open mouth and snap. In the kennel room, is observed to pull hard towards the other dogs while barking. With handlers, Kwik has a loose body and climbs up next to them on the bench, soliciting contact. Medically Kwik is apparently healthy.

Meet Kwik!
Kwik came into the shelter when his owner was no longer able to care for him. He is a social, treat-motivated boy who enjoys interacting with people once he feels comfortable. With familiar handlers, he comes forward readily and shows a friendly, engaging personality.

Personality
Kwik is outgoing and people-focused, often approaching for attention and responding well to treats. He can show some tension in certain situations, especially around toys or when unsure, but overall he enjoys being handled and included once he settles in.

My Ideal Home
Kwik would do best in an adult-only home with a calm, structured environment. He will benefit from adopters who can give him consistency and time to build confidence. Positive reinforcement and routine will help him feel more secure and succeed long term.

Good with Other Pets?
Kwik has shown no issues with dogs while on leash, though slow introductions are still recommended. He will do best with thoughtful management as he adjusts to a new home environment.

Good with Kids?
Kwik is recommended for an adult-only home at this time due to fearful responses in new or overwhelming situations.

Things to Know
Kwik walks nicely on leash and stays engaged with his handler. He enjoys interaction and treats, and while he can be a bit unsure at times, he responds well to gentle guidance. He benefits from clear structure and a predictable routine.

Fun Fact
Kwik may take a minute to warm up, but once he does, he's all in for attention and snacks. Kwik just needs little time to click.

251357.name: Caffery
251357.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Caffery is a calm, affectionate foster dog who is quickly stealing hearts. He loves being close to his people and is happiest when he's getting gentle rubs and attention. On walks, he really enjoys himself-taking his time to sniff, explore, and soak in his morning strolls and evening park visits.
He thrives with structure, responds well to positive reinforcement, and is very food-motivated, which makes training easy and rewarding.
Caffery has also been building strength in his legs after past mobility discomfort. With medication and consistent care, he's made great progress and is steadily increasing his endurance, now enjoying more movement, play, and confidence each day.
He's a loving, easygoing companion who is ready to continue growing in a patient, caring home.

Meet Caffery!
Caffery is a soft-hearted boy who was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. He is still learning to feel comfortable in new environments, but he shows a gentle, sweet nature once he settles in. Caffery does best with patient adopters who give him time to take in the world at his own pace.

Personality
Caffery is calm, observant, and tends to take a step back in new situations before engaging. He enjoys quiet, gentle interaction and accepts handling well when he feels safe. Once comfortable, he can relax and show a soft, easygoing side.

My Ideal Home
Caffery would thrive in a quiet, low-traffic home with a steady routine. He will do best with patient adopters who use positive reinforcement and allow him to build confidence gradually. A calm environment will help him continue to come out of his shell over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Caffery has shown a soft, friendly approach toward other dogs but can become overwhelmed if interactions are too forward or energetic. He does best with calm, respectful dogs and slow introductions. Careful matches and supervision will help set him up for success.

Good with Kids?
Caffery would do best in a home without young children under 5. He is most comfortable in calm environments where interactions are gentle and predictable.

Things to Know
Caffery is still gaining confidence on leash and may hesitate in unfamiliar settings. He benefits from slow introductions, routine, and enrichment like puzzle toys to help him stay engaged and relaxed. With consistency and patience, he continues to build trust in new experiences.

Fun Fact
Caffery has a quiet, endearing presence and a soft charm that comes out once he feels at ease. He's the kind of companion who forms a deep, steady bond with his people over time.

251389.name: Daba
251389.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Daba is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

A volunteer writes: Daba makes an adorable first impression, if not an entirely welcoming one and that's ok. I admired how he stretched his little paw out on his box like he was in mid-knead and he decided to leave it as is. Really, so cute. I said songs could be written about that paw and Daba surreptitiously rolled his eyes and tried to explain that he was busy by pretending to nap. I know very well that snuggles (and compliments) aren't always the way to someone's heart, so I quietly closed Daba's condo door to sit and read for a little bit. The Daba I met before reading and the Daba I met afterwards are almost two different cats. The next time I held my hand out, he nuzzled into me and looked for more pets. This makes a little sense because in his previous home Daba was friendly and outgoing with people and other cats. There are times he likes to take a moment or so to warm up, which we see at the shelter, but we're so sure that after a little time, a lot of patience and love, Daba will become the sparkly young cat he's meant to become.

251444.name: London
251444.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
London is the sweetest girl who absolutely adores affection and human connection. She thrives with people who approach her slowly and kindly, and once she feels comfortable, her loving personality shines through. She's a total cuddle bug who wants nothing more than to be close to people and soak up all the love and attention she can get.
One of London's best qualities is how calm and easygoing she is. She is non-reactive around other dogs, walks beautifully on a leash, and does not bark. She recently spent a gorgeous day relaxing in the grass, peacefully taking in the beautiful view, and showed just how content she is simply being near someone who cares for her.
London has a gentle presence that makes people instantly fall in love with her. She would do wonderfully in a patient and loving home where she can continue building confidence and feeling safe. While she can be a little nervous getting into the car right now, with patience, encouragement, and love, we know she'll learn that adventures can be fun too.
She's the kind of dog who doesn't ask for much, just kindness, comfort, and someone to love her forever. In return, she'll give you loyalty, companionship, peaceful walks, endless cuddles, and a heart that's truly grateful.
London is ready to leave shelter life behind and finally find the family she deserves. 💕

251445.name: Patootie
251445.summary:
Meet Patootie!
Patootie was found tied to a gate on the sidewalk and is now looking for a calm, patient home where he can finally feel safe and understood. He's a sensitive, high energy boy who can be a bit overwhelmed in new situations, but he's also very people oriented and shows interest in connection once he has a little reassurance. With the right support, his sweet side starts to peek through between all that nervous energy.

My Ideal Home
Patootie would do best in an adult only home that can offer structure, consistency, and plenty of calm enrichment. He'll thrive with an adopter who understands anxiety and can help him channel his energy into positive outlets like games, puzzles, and steady routines. He needs a home that moves at his pace and helps him feel secure without pressure.

Good with Other Pets?
Patootie has shown mild interest in other dogs but can become tense when overstimulated, so slow and careful introductions are important if he lives with another dog.

Good with Kids?
Patootie is recommended for an adult only home due to high anxiety and guarding behaviors when stressed.

Things to Know
Patootie is an anxious but bright boy who needs daily mental and physical enrichment to help him feel balanced. He benefits from calm handling, predictable routines, and positive reinforcement training to help him build confidence and better coping skills. Once comfortable, he shows a playful, curious side that enjoys engaging with people he trusts.

Fun Fact
Even when he's feeling unsure, Patootie still tries his best to connect, and with time he has all the makings of a truly loyal little "patootie pie" companion.

251492.name: Apollo
251492.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Apollo is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. While in the care center, Apollo has consistently displayed dog reactivity, including growling, hard barking, lunging, and hard staring at other dogs in the kennel, yard, and on walks. He has also shown reactivity toward small dogs and has bitten kennel bars while attempting to reach another dog and has also barked at novel staff members in the hallway. Despite these behaviors, Apollo is social and affectionate with handlers, readily accepting petting, leaning into people for attention, and responding well to treats but is struggling to acclimate despite best efforts to keep him comfortable. Medically, Apollo is apparently healthy.

Meet Apollo!
Apollo is a playful pup looking for a family ready to join him on his next adventure. After being surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, Apollo is hoping to find a forever home where he can keep learning, playing, and soaking up all the love. This energetic guy has a big personality and is ready to become someone's out-of-this-world companion!

My Ideal Home
Apollo would thrive with an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He is a smart pup who enjoys engaging with his people and will benefit from continued practice with polite greetings and impulse control. With the right guidance, Apollo is ready to rocket into his best life!

Good with Other Pets?
Apollo's previous family shared that he can bark and growl at dogs and small animals on walks as a way of trying to initiate play. He would benefit from continued leash training and positive reinforcement to help him learn calmer ways to interact with the world around him. Slow introductions would be recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Apollo's fearful behaviors and leash reactivity, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. He would do best with people who can help him build confidence while continuing to practice his manners.

Things to Know
Apollo is an energetic and playful dog who loves staying busy! He enjoys attention from his people and is comfortable with handling, including having his paws and collar touched. His previous family shared that he enjoys using wee-wee pads indoors and can be a bit of a curious explorer, so providing appropriate chew toys and enrichment will help keep his busy brain and playful paws occupied. Apollo is ready to find a family who will help him shine!

251494.name: Eduardo
251494.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
Eduardo tolerates some attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter and displays some avoidant behaviors. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home with an appropriate decompression period, and positive reinforcement for social behaviors with high value treats. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

A volunteer writes: Eduardo's beloved box may be two sizes too small, but it was a gift. More than the sentimental value, his box is something he can count on and call his own in a life that's rather suddenly become an everchanging landscape. Eduardo came to us from a home with many other cats and is said to play gently with them. His endearing playful streak brings him even further with his penchant for mouse plushies, bottle caps, and crinkle balls. Eduardo was always a very friendly presence as he benevolently roamed around in his prior home, but he generally preferred to make contact on his own terms. This is a fair preference, if a challenging one in a shelter setting. I saw his little paws sticking out of his box and took that as my cue to tell Eduardo how cute he is, but it wasn't quite the invitation I had assumed it to be. Eduardo does allow pets at the shelter, but is really hoping for someone to extend a hand and an invitation his way. He has so much to offer a family who will share their love and patience with him in return.
