251504.name: Billygoat
251504.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
A volunteer writes: Billygoat might look a little rough around the edges in his Care Center photo. But it's just because this young creamsicle guy and his siblings were found abandoned in a basement. No wonder Billygoat has been shy and standoffish since coming to the Care Center, accepting some pettings but then other times preferring to hang back on his own. We get it, trusting new humans isn't easy after a rough start in life. The encouraging thing is, Billygoat shows no aggression or bad behavior, and we have a strong feeling that he'll come out of his shell when he's in the hands of the right patient new pet parent--someone who understands cats like this one need time and space to blossom. Looking to give a helping hand to this timid good boy? Billygoat is waiting to meet you on 110th Street today!

251512.name: Silque
251512.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, June 7 from 11AM - 4PM at Petco Love Adoption Event, Union Square Park, 201 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

My foster writes:
Silque is a perfect sweet but low key cat. She'll greet you at the door and follow you from room to room. She loves cheek scratches and will bow her little head so scratch the top of it. She's not a cuddler (not interested in laps) but she does want to be near you at all times - the couch cushion next to you, at the foot of the bed. And if you're not petting her she'll stare at you and slow blink when you talk to her. She's pretty quiet, just some grunts and chirps when you wake her up.

251541.name: Lucy
251541.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Lucy is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.

251577.name: Broccoli
251577.summary:
My foster writes:
This sweet and gentle dog loves to be in your presence. When you're chill, he's happy to lay around. When youre up and about, he's happy to go for a walk. He'll gently place his head on your lap. But, he's also very adaptable and goes with the flow. He learns new behaviors very quickly and is very intelligent. Oh boy, does he love to people watch and just take in his surroundings. He reminds me to stop and smell the roses. You honestly can't ask for a better dog!

251581.name: Autumn
251581.summary:
My Boroughbreaker writes: Autumn was a JOY to take on a BoroughBreak. She was very fearful leaving the shelter, but I knew she was a gorgeous girl that just needed to warm up a little (with lots of patience and respect for her space)! She was so easy to walk on the leash through central park, with stops for treats because Autumn lovessss treats. We went to brunch, where she was an angel and laid under the table, with occasional nose boops on my hand for some love. We spent the afternoon laying in the park, and Autumn took a well deserved nap after she spent time laying on my lap. She charmed everyone who walked by with her sweet spirit, and seeing her come out of her shell was the best. She is so easy to love and will be a perfect companion.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

251585.name: Funk Master Flash
251585.summary:
My foster writes: This clever little guy is equal parts sweetheart and explorer. He loves giving head bumps, comes over when you call or gesture to him, and is always curious about what you're up to. He's also figured out how to open doors-and once he decides there's something interesting on the other side, he is very committed to his mission. He's affectionate without being needy, respectful of your food and space. He is a very cute, very clever little guy with lots of love (and head bumps) to give.

A volunteer writes: We know Funk Master Flash likes the treats we leave for him. We also know that he prefers we not stare at him while he enjoys them. This is understandable for many reasons but also because Funk Master Flash could use a little extra space to collect his thoughts at the moment. Brought to us with two other cats when their guardian passed away, it must seem like the rug has been pulled from beneath his little paws. Settling into shelter life has been a considerable process and I'm not entirely sure Funk Master Flash knows where to start. Snuggled up in the back of his cubby and ready to air his grievances, we know he's not a fan of the Care Center but he shows bright and starry glimpses of the kitty he can be when he allows pets. We might not be able to see all of Funk Master Flash's best sides at the moment, but we hope that what we see is enough to convince someone that he's the cat for them. 


A staff member writes: Funk Master Flash has finally got his Funk back! Mr Flash has been more outgoing when introduced to some of his siblings and new cats. Funk has gone from being distant to being curious and outgoing in a Flash during his shelter stay and may do best in a home with experienced, patient adopters that may already have a fur friend or two to continue to help him come out of his shell.
251585.summaryHtml:
My foster writes: This clever little guy is equal parts sweetheart and explorer. He loves giving head bumps, comes over when you call or gesture to him, and is always curious about what you're up to. He's also figured out how to open doors-and once he decides there's something interesting on the other side, he is very committed to his mission. He's affectionate without being needy, respectful of your food and space. He is a very cute, very clever little guy with lots of love (and head bumps) to give.

A volunteer writes: We know Funk Master Flash likes the treats we leave for him. We also know that he prefers we not stare at him while he enjoys them. This is understandable for many reasons but also because Funk Master Flash could use a little extra space to collect his thoughts at the moment. Brought to us with two other cats when their guardian passed away, it must seem like the rug has been pulled from beneath his little paws. Settling into shelter life has been a considerable process and I'm not entirely sure Funk Master Flash knows where to start. Snuggled up in the back of his cubby and ready to air his grievances, we know he's not a fan of the Care Center but he shows bright and starry glimpses of the kitty he can be when he allows pets. We might not be able to see all of Funk Master Flash's best sides at the moment, but we hope that what we see is enough to convince someone that he's the cat for them. 


A staff member writes: Funk Master Flash has finally got his Funk back! Mr Flash has been more outgoing when introduced to some of his siblings and new cats. Funk has gone from being distant to being curious and outgoing in a Flash during his shelter stay and may do best in a home with experienced, patient adopters that may already have a fur friend or two to continue to help him come out of his shell.

251599.name: Celine
251599.summary:
Meet Celine!
Celine was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and she's now looking for a patient home where she can feel safe, settle in, and show her affectionate side. She is a cuddly, people-oriented girl who enjoys being near her family, following them from room to room, and curling up for nap time once she's comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Celine would do best in an adult-only home that can help her build confidence at her own pace. She'll thrive in a calm, predictable environment where she can decompress and learn that the world is a safe place.

Good with Other Pets?
Celine has shown neutral behavior toward other dogs in the shelter setting, but as always, slow introductions are recommended as she transitions into a new home.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to anxiety in new environments and sensitivity to handling, though she has a history of being gentle and playful once comfortable.

Things to Know
Celine is an affectionate and intelligent girl who knows several cues and enjoys interactive play like hide and seek and squeaky toys. She can be anxious in new situations and may vocalize or become overstimulated when things feel unpredictable. She prefers gentle handling, especially around her paws, and may become mouthy when excited during play. With structure, reassurance, and positive reinforcement, she blossoms into a very loving companion.

Fun Fact
Once Celine feels at home, she's all about cuddle time, she's basically a professional nap buddy who just wants to be wherever her people are.

251606.name: Luke
251606.summary:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.

I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

Meet Luke!

Luke came to us from a home with lots of cats and very little interaction with humans. This has made living in shelter care, justifiably, a bit tough on him. Luke is looking for an experienced adopter, one who understands the unique needs of a fearful cat who requires help with socialization and has the patience to go however slowly Luke might need. If that adopter is you, come say hi to Luke at SIACC! 

A volunteer writes: Snuggled up and stretched out under his blanket, Luke's approach to shelter life is certainly unique, if not always entirely facilitative to finding a forever family. We can understand if you glance at Luke's condo and, seeing only a little lump of blanket or a pair of wide eyes from inside a cubby, walk on to the next. Except that Luke's progress is very much worth noting. He came to us from a home with many other cats in April and making sense of shelter life has been effortful to say the least. He might not have much experience meeting new people, but he likes to be present right at the front and if you bring some treats, he might even allow some pets. Luke has quickly become a staff and volunteer favorite, but he's really hoping to become part of your forever family.

251607.name: Morrigan
251607.summary:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

Meet Morrigan!

Morrigan came to us from a house that didn't offer her the best start in life. A home overcrowded with cats and little interaction causes a cat to grow up unsocialized, making life in the shelter pretty tough. Morrigan, however, braves every day that she's here, dreaming of a future home that has plenty of space for her to decompress, feather wands for her to play with, low foot traffic, and adult humans only. Wanna make her dreams come true? Then come say hi to Morrigan at SIACC today!

A volunteer writes: Morrigan seems to be in a near constant state of surprise and not really the fun kind. We come prepared with treats, toys, maybe even some pets if she's open to it and she peers up at us each time like she's trying to conceptualize what exactly is going on and what will happen next. Morrigan, who will allow a few pets from time to time, slowly and quietly inched herself toward her cubby when I opened the condo door. This is presumably where she feels a bit more comfortable and in control of a situation that's been out of her paws for quite some time. Morrigan came to us from a home with many other cats and considerably less experience with people. The shelter is full of new experiences that Morrigan does her best to navigate, even if many of them (most of them?) take her by surprise. We know that with a patient and loving forever family that will meet her where she is and go at her pace will be just the thing to get her started.

251608.name: Kylo
251608.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

Meet Kylo!

This kitty has had a rough start in life and is looking for a smooth landing. Kylo came to us from a home where he had little interaction with humans and is still learning that people are friends, not foes. All things considered, the optimal adopter for Kylo is someone patient and willing to go slow as well as someone who is experienced with cats and has a good grasp on feline behavior and body language. Luckily, he responds well to treats (especially crunchy ones like Temptations!) so you've got one route to his heart already. Our hope is, with time and patience, he'll be able to decompress and come further out of his shell. He just needs the opportunity, so if you're interested in being the one to give that to him, come say hi to Kylo at SIACC!

A volunteer writes: Kylo just likes to have options and while we don't believe he's asking too much by any means, shelter life doesn't always provide for so many. We invite him to make choices whenever we can and though Kylo's careful deliberation process may be a bit under wraps at the moment, we can see that he likes having his choice of foods, toys, and space to interact with us when it makes sense to him. Kylo was brought to us from a home with many other cats and while he has a lot of experience doing his own thing, he has much less experience with people. We know there's a forever family who will work with Kylo's timeline and help him to build the confidence he needs with lots of love and lots of choices.

251620.name: Whittakers
251620.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Playtime is essential! I love climbing tall cat trees and having fun with interactive toys!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!

A volunteer writes: Whittakers seems somewhat unjustly jailed behind two barriers which make him almost impossible to see. You'll know him by the paws he shoots through the plastic blockades to get attention. If you do catch a glimpse of him, you'll no doubt find he's worth seeing. Whittakers is a gray and white tabby with big, round, super-cute green eyes. He's engaging and talkative -and perhaps a bit too energetic and even rambunctious, which is why he finds himself in the setting he does. Whittakers needs to expend some energy, so I introduced him to the toy known as the cat dancer, which he approached with the suspicious eye of a detective on a crime scene. After a while, though, he decided this dancing culprit was worth pursuing and we had a rewarding play session.

251652.name: Sammy
251652.summary:
As a part of OG's Starting Five, I will receive a year of free pet food from Royal Canin. VCA will also provide one free year of unlimited exams with a CareClub Access Plan.

Meet Sammy!
Sammy's story began when he was found abandoned in a cardboard box and brought to ACC as a stray. The shelter has been a big adjustment for this sensitive guy, but with patience and kindness he has shown everyone just how sweet he can be. Once he feels safe, Sammy enjoys gentle head scratches, cheek rubs, tasty treats, and quiet companionship. He may not be the first cat to greet you at the door, but he has a soft, affectionate side that shines through when given the chance.



My Ideal Home
Sammy is looking for a calm, patient home where he can settle in at his own pace. He can be startled by sudden noises and fast movements, so he will do best with adopters who understand that trust takes time. Once he feels comfortable, Sammy enjoys attention and has shown that he can be a loving companion. A quieter environment and a predictable routine will help him thrive.



Good with Kids?
Sammy would do best with respectful older children who can understand his need for space and gentle interactions. Because he is easily startled, a home without young children is recommended.



Good with Other Pets?
There is no known history of Sammy living with other pets. Slow, thoughtful introductions would be recommended with any resident animals.



Medical Notes
Sammy is currently in good health. He received treatment for minor ear irritation and a mild eye infection while in our care, both of which have resolved. He is ready to head home and start his next chapter.



Did You Know?
Sammy is one of OG Anunoby's "Starting Five" cats! His adoption comes with a year of free Royal Canin pet food and one year of unlimited exams through VCA's CareClub Access Plan. More importantly, it comes with the chance to give a deserving cat the patient, loving home he's been waiting for.

251679.name: Companion
251679.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Companion!
Companion was found wandering loose on the street and is now safe and looking for a steady, understanding home. He's a calm, independent boy who takes a little time to warm up, but once comfortable, he moves through the world with a gentle, easygoing presence.

My Ideal Home
Companion would do best in an experienced adult-only home that can support him with structure and patience, especially around outdoor distractions. He'll thrive with calm leadership and predictable routines while he builds confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Companion can become stiff, vocal, and tense when seeing other dogs on walks, so he will need slow, controlled introductions and careful management in shared spaces.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for young children due to on-leash reactivity and his need for a calm, structured environment.

Things to Know
Companion is a more reserved dog who prefers to take in his surroundings before engaging. He may appear aloof at first, often focusing on sniffing and observing rather than interacting. While he accepts handling and walks politely without pulling, he can become reactive when he sees other dogs and will need guidance and distance to feel comfortable. With time, patience, and consistent routines, he has the potential to become a steady, loyal companion.

Fun Fact
True to his name, Companion is the kind of dog who quietly grows into your best sidekick once he decides you're his person.

My foster writes:
It is a joy, fostering Companion. He is very social. Well-behaved. Minimum leash pulling, he loves to eat and go on frequent short walks. He is well toilet trained, does not soil the house. He follows simple command stay, sit, no. Sleeps throughout the night. He makes a very good Companion. His name is very becoming and suits him well.

251680.name: Nines
251680.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Nines is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Nines arrived at the Care Center as a stray. Upon arrival Nines was initially fearful but warmed up to staff quickly. During her most recent handling assessment she was noted to be highly social and accept all contact. Unfortunately, Nines has struggled with a decreasing threshold for arousal. In a recent interaction Nines was noted to jump up and persistently tug on a staff member's sleeve and leash; she was difficult to redirect even with use of a pet corrector. When not over-threshold, Nines remains social with staff, solicits contact, and is highly treat receptive. Medically, Nines is noted to have Dental Disease but is otherwise apparently healthy.

Nines arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Nines has been observed to have a low threshold for arousal. Noted to mouth handlers with moderate to hard pressure, jump at them persistently, and leash bite. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

A Volunteer Wrote: We're all smitten with this girl, and for so many good reasons! She's joy on four legs; exuberant, snuggly, and paying no attention to the dogs around her when she can devote all her attention to YOU! If you have two hands with which to pet her and a pocket full of treats, it's safe to bet you will be Nines' most favorite person ever. Please stop the competition between volunteers over which one of us she'll pick and proclaim yourself the winner--you will earn the world title by opening your home to this baby! Energetic, full of beans. She's a happy, exuberant leash walker, a bit jumpy and zig zaggy. Needs a bit of training there. Affectionate, loves treats which she'll readily sit for, but she can be mouthy. So use paper treat- giving technique: flat hand or on the ground. Big girl energy into a small body so make sure you're ready for it. Couch Potatoes need not apply.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
Nines is the absolute best girl! She is so loving and friendly and pays absolutely no attention to other dogs around her! She is well-behaved and loves getting scratches! It was an absolute joy to spend the day with her and she will make a family so happy!

251695.name: Devon Deluxe
251695.summary:
Meet Devon Deluxe - a sleek little house panther with movie-star looks and a heart that's learning to be brave. 🖤✨

When Devon first arrived at the shelter, the world felt a little too big and scary. But with patience, treats, and lots of encouragement, this handsome guy has blossomed beautifully. He's officially graduated from our "Fraidy Cat" program and now proudly shows off his clicker-training skills like the smart little gentleman he is!

Devon especially loves bubbles, visual toys, and cozy enrichment time - you can practically see the curiosity sparkle in his eyes. Once he trusts you, he'll bravely trot over for treats and gentle attention, making every small victory feel extra special.

If you're the kind of person who understands that the sweetest friendships take a little time, Devon Deluxe is ready to be your loyal mini panther companion for life. 🫧🐾
Devon Deluxe is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, he does hiss and avoid human contact. It is difficult to predict if he will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Devon Deluxe has spent over a month in the shelter and so he gave it a good chance only to realize that this is, in fact, not the place for him. A quiet guy who prefers his little cubby to being out and about, he's really putting all of his time and energy into figuring out what he needs to be doing to finally find his forever home. Devon Deluxe was brought to us from a home with many other cats and might not have a lot of experience meeting new people. He has allowed pets, but isn't one to seek them out so he's looking for a calm and patient home that will welcome him for who he is and give him the space to find out who he wants to be.

My foster writes:
Devon may be reserved when you first meet him, but if you give him a little time, you'll start to see his sweet personality peek through in quiet, endearing ways.
He's quite the little conversationalist, with a rich repertoire of different meows, each sounding a little different from the last-though what he's trying to tell you is anyone's guess... unless it's breakfast time, when his message is crystal clear! He's also not the most graceful jumper, which only adds to his charm.
He doesn't demand constant play or attention and brings a peaceful, easygoing presence to the home. One thing he does love is the company of other cats. He follows his foster feline friend around and clearly enjoys having another cat nearby, so we think he'd thrive in a home with a friendly feline companion who can help him continue building confidence.
If you're looking for a calm, gentle companion who's happy to simply share your space, Devon could be the perfect match. One of the most rewarding parts of loving him is watching him grow more comfortable and confident with patience, kindness, and a little TLC. We're incredibly proud of the progress he's already made, and we can't wait to see him continue to blossom in a forever home.
251695.summaryHtml:

But with patience, treats, and lots of encouragement, this handsome guy has blossomed beautifully. He's officially graduated from our "Fraidy Cat" program and now proudly shows off his clicker-training skills like the smart little gentleman he is! Devon especially loves bubbles, visual toys, and cozy enrichment time - you can practically see the curiosity sparkle in his eyes. Once he trusts you, he'll bravely trot over for treats and gentle attention, making every small victory feel extra special. If you're the kind of person who understands that the sweetest friendships take a little time, Devon Deluxe is ready to be your loyal mini panther companion for life. 🫧🐾

Devon Deluxe is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, he does hiss and avoid human contact. 251696.name: Evan Got Rhythm
251696.summary:
Evan Got Rhythm is a dashing little house panther with a brave heart and the cutest comeback story. 🖤✨

This handsome guy started out shy and spooky in the shelter, but thanks to lots of patience, treats, and clicker training, Evan has officially graduated from our "Fraidy Cat" program! He may greet new people with a dramatic little hiss at first - but give him a little time, and suddenly he's chirping, meowing, and chatting away with his favorite humans like an old friend.

Evan absolutely loves treats, enjoys learning through clicker training, and gets braver every single day. And yes - his adorable eyebrows grew back, making his expressive little face even more irresistible.

If you're looking for a sweet, quirky mini panther who will reward your patience with tiny chirps, growing trust, and lots of personality, Evan Got Rhythm is ready to steal your heart. 🐾

Even Got Rhythm is an under socialized adult cat that has made significant levels of improvement in socialization in shelter through working with the behavior team. He appreciates attention and petting and had become very vocal to solicit attention and pets from those he is comfortable with. He remains somewhat sensitive to his environment and will need time to adjust to his new home, likely requiring an extended decompression period. He would do best in an adult-only home with and adopter with a moderate level of experience. They ideal would have some level of experience with under socialized/hoarding cats and helping them adjust to new environments, or will be open to thorough counselling on socialization techniques and positive reinforcement.

A volunteer writes: Evan Got Rhythm has a big story of progress that serves as a helpful reminder to trust someone's looking out for you. In Evan's case, it's his new friend Demas (223431) among others, but let's rewind a bit. Evan Got Rhythm came to us from a home with many other cats and the first few times I met him, he made it very clear that he was just fine on his own, thank you very much except that he wasn't. Evan Got Rhythm entered and has since matriculated from our "Fraidy Cat Program" where he learned extraordinarily helpful skills and gained a new comfort level that has proudly accompanied him to the free roaming room. Enter his new buddy: Demas. When Evan stretched out to greet me, he jazzed it up with some adorable kitten like chirps, which alerted Demas that it was party time. Demas hopped on down to get some cuddles and show off his new friend. They circled and cuddled, elaborately swirling into each other and into me. Both of these truly terrific cats are waiting for their forever families.

251706.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Pebbles is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Pebbles is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she does attempt to flee and avoid human contact. It is difficult to predict if he will respond to socialization, but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

251708.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Freddy is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A volunteer writes: Many of us like to have some input when it comes to shaping our surroundings, but it seems like Freddy hasn't had that opportunity in some time. One of many cats left alone in a room with some food and water to tide them over, they had each other but no clear path for a future until someone brought them to us. We've been trying to show Freddy that we love his ideas, even if the shelter isn't exactly designed to incorporate all of them. Freddy seems to really enjoy his own thoughts from the comfort of his cubby, but the constant stream of visitors peeking in on his me-time can throw him off a bit. I fully understand and celebrate the value of his process but admittedly it isn't the most conducive to finding a forever family. Freddy is hoping to find a patient and loving family who will meet him where he is and give him the space and love to become the cat he wants to be.

251709.name: Wilma
251709.summary:
Wilma is a dreamy orange-and-white gentleman with chubby cheeks, giant amber eyes, and the face of a storybook cat. 🧡🤍

Right now, shelter life feels a little too scary for him, and he isn't comfortable with touch just yet. But beneath those cautious eyes is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and a loving person willing to let him move at his own pace.

Wilma is looking for a calm home where he can slowly learn that the world is safe - and where his future human will celebrate every tiny step forward. With love and understanding, this handsome boy has all the potential to blossom into a devoted companion.

If you believe the quietest cats often have the biggest hearts, Wilma may be waiting just for you. 🐾

Due to the detailed behavior issues, this animal is only available for foster/adoption through one of ACC's New Hope Partners. If you are interested in adopting or fostering, please fill out the pre-screener form. This animal is not directly available for adoption through ACC and is only available by completing the pre-screener form.Adoption inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response. 
Pre-Screener Form

251757.name: Ramona
251757.summary:
My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Ramona was such a sweetheart. She had a lot of commonalities in personality to my own family dog. She is a great companion and wants to socialize with dogs so much, but doesn't know how to. She loves greeting strangers and she was so good at being redirected when a dog was near. Her redirecting skills improved significantly within the few hours I spent with her, demonstrating her remarkable trainability. Ramona's willingness to learn and tender spirit make her undeniably lovable. Ramona would do wonderfully with an active family who can spoil her as an only fur baby. She's such good company and is open and adventurous despite her past being a mystery. I loved the time I spend with her and I hope she's adopted soon.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

A volunteer writes: As Ramona trots besides me in her pocket-sized, tiger-striped body I start imagining all the places she could fit into in a forever home: a tiny slice of a love seat, half a porch swing, perhaps even an IKEA bag on the subway. I imagine her next to her adopter, snugged in close, trying to the answer the age old who rescued who question.

Ramona came to us when her owner was concerned about some "playful lunging" towards the cats in her home. At the shelter she has been sociable and friendly and can be walked by our newest volunteers. We are told this smart, little girly knows the commands "sit, stay, down, paw, and leave it". We are also told she "loves to lay in the sun and enjoys playing fetch" and that her favorite treats are dental sticks and Elk antlers

251812.name: Marbles
251812.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes:
Marbles is an intensely loyal, super-intelligent guy. He's got a lot of energy and is always up for long brisk walks and hikes. He'd make an excellent hiking companion. (He's good in a car if you have a doggie seatbelt or a crate.) He loves chasing balls and he keeps himself busy with chew toys and snuffle mats. He would do well with a strong active owner who can patiently teach him to walk at your pace, not his (he does love his walks and gets very excited about going outside!)

Marbles loves his naps. He loves any spot that has tons of pillows; your favorite chair, your spot on the couch and your bed. He will also sleep in a dog bed in his crate. But mostly he likes to sleep curled up next to you so you can rub his tummy. Cuddle time is his favorite time of the day. 

Meet Marbles!
Marbles was found tied up outside a building and is now looking for a calm, patient home where he can truly settle and feel safe.

My Ideal Home
We call him our "Velcro-dog" because once he has claimed you as his pack, he won't leave your side. Marbles would do well in a calm predictable adult-only home. He needs a patient adopter who will take the time to teach him how to be the best dog ever. Marbles is smart and highly motivated to please you. He just needs consistent positive reinforcement (and lots of exercise) to learn how to be your best buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
When on a leash, Marbles has shown neutral, polite behavior towards other dogs. If introducing him to other dogs in a household, it's highly recommended that you make a slow, thoughtful introduction over an extended period of time. He hasn't been around other pets and can be territorial.

Good with Kids?
He still has toddler tendencies and is a very physical dog. When he loves you, he loves you with his entire 50-pound body! He doesn't know his own strength, so we wouldn't recommend a household with children under 12 or anyone who can be knocked over easily.

Things to Know
Marbles is a tender-hearted boy who can feel overwhelmed in busy or high-stimulation environments, so he does best with calm handling and plenty of space to decompress. Once he feels safe, he enjoys gentle attention and will quietly seek out connection in his own way. He's still learning that the world isn't something to be worried about, and he benefits from slow, reassuring guidance.

Fun Fact
Once Marbles trusts you, he really starts to roll with affection and shows the sweetest little moments of leaning in like he's decided you're his safe place.

251817.name: Casper
251817.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Meet Casper!
Casper was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now this sweet, low energy boy is looking for a soft place to land. His previous family describes him as social, affectionate, house trained, and a big fan of car rides and spending time close to his people.

My Ideal Home
Casper would do best in a calm adult-only home where he can continue healing and settle in at his own pace. He's looking for patient adopters who can give him stability, kindness, and lots of cozy downtime while he regains his confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
According to his previous owner, Casper has been friendly and outgoing with other dogs both on and off leash. At the shelter, he showed interest in greeting another dog through the gate, though interactions have remained limited while he focuses on healing.

Good with Kids?
We recommend an adult-only home for Casper at this time due to his discomfort with novel situations and handling while recovering medically.

Things to Know
Casper is currently recovering from ongoing skin issues and has been unable to complete a full handling assessment while receiving treatment. Even so, he has remained gentle with staff, takes treats softly, and continues to tolerate care and medical handling well. He can become a little timid in unfamiliar situations and may bark or growl at strangers approaching his family on walks, but overall he is described as an affectionate, easygoing companion who enjoys being near his people. Casper also loves car rides and already has great house manners.

Fun Fact
Casper may be named after a friendly ghost, but this Casper prefers cozy naps, car rides, and sticking close to his favorite humans.

A volunteer writes: Casper 🥰 8 year old Casper has spent the last 2 months in the shelter, much of it in a too small kennel in an overflow room. With few breaks from his living space, it's no minor feat that he's maintained his good nature. But he patiently waits for walks, and I think hopes for some butt scratches and affection from his human companions. His skin must be itchy, and it's scabbed over when we meet. His guardian reported that he developed skin issues 2 years ago and interventions from his vet were not successful and abandoned about a year ago.

Regardless, he's a little gentleman. He places his paws in our palms and watches us quietly until we produce his reward. He's got tall pointy ears atop a perfectly round face, with short little leggies adorned in white socks. He plays enthusiastically, and walks on a loose leash while sniffing.

Casper's guardian reports he's good with dogs and cats, and alerts to strangers but is friendly. He also did well with baths. You can meet this lovely boy at Queens ACC 
This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

Meet Casper!
Casper was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now this sweet, low energy boy is looking for a soft place to land. His previous family describes him as social, affectionate, house trained, and a big fan of car rides and spending time close to his people.

My Ideal Home
Casper would do best in a calm adult-only home where he can continue healing and settle in at his own pace. He's looking for patient adopters who can give him stability, kindness, and lots of cozy downtime while he regains his confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
According to his previous owner, Casper has been friendly and outgoing with other dogs both on and off leash. At the shelter, he showed interest in greeting another dog through the gate, though interactions have remained limited while he focuses on healing.

Good with Kids?
We recommend an adult-only home for Casper at this time due to his discomfort with novel situations and handling while recovering medically.

Things to Know
Casper is currently recovering from ongoing skin issues and has been unable to complete a full handling assessment while receiving treatment. Even so, he has remained gentle with staff, takes treats softly, and continues to tolerate care and medical handling well. He can become a little timid in unfamiliar situations and may bark or growl at strangers approaching his family on walks, but overall he is described as an affectionate, easygoing companion who enjoys being near his people. Casper also loves car rides and already has great house manners.

Casper may be named after a friendly ghost, but this Casper prefers cozy naps, car rides, and sticking close to his favorite humans. 251826.name: Dipity
251826.summary:
My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! 

Meet Dipity!
Dipity is a male dog who was found alone in a park and brought to the shelter as a stray. He is still adjusting to new environments and benefits from time and space to feel comfortable. Once settled, he is able to move through his surroundings calmly with a steady, neutral presence.

Personality
Dipity is quiet and observant in new situations. He may not seek attention right away and can appear reserved when first approached. With gentle handling and patience, he is able to relax and tolerate interaction.

My Ideal Home
Dipity would do best in a calm, low-traffic home with a consistent routine. He will need patient adopters who can let him adjust at his own pace without pressure. A quiet environment will help him feel more secure over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Dipity's behavior around other dogs is still unclear. Slow, structured introductions and careful management would be needed in a home with other pets.

Good with Kids?
Dipity is recommended for a home without young children under 5 due to his fearful behavior. Older, respectful children may be considered after slow introductions.

Things to Know
Dipity walks well on leash and follows his handler with a calm, neutral body. He does best with slow introductions and a gentle, consistent approach. He benefits from patience as he continues to build confidence in new environments.

Fun Fact
Dipity is a quiet, thoughtful boy who takes his time to settle in, but shows a steady, calm presence once he feels comfortable.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
Dipity is a very happy boy. He is also the perfect walking buddy. He has great leash manners, is interested and friendly with other dogs without being aggressive, and has a huge smile and a tail that never stops wagging--especially when being offered treats! We walked for hours through the park and he never pulled, never barked, and never chased after any animals. He was so happy to meet other people and soaked up all attention and skritches. After hours of walking, we sat on a bench where he calmly fell asleep for a long time, just happy to have company outside in the shade. He's a very sweet boy.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes: I had such an amazing day with Dipity today. We walked to Central Park, he did a great job on the leash and was completely non reactive towards other dogs (he just looked at them, but never pulled or barked). We then spent some time at my apartment, where he loved playing with a toy and got some good rest. It was also great that he was fully housebroken, after a little bit I didn't even have to worry about him having an accident. We then went to the Barking Dog around lunchtime- and again he kept to himself and I and only interacted with other people when they wanted to say hi. He got plenty of compliments there for his good behavior and relaxed nature. He loved getting scratches and used any surface (usually me) as a scratching post. Dipity is an amazing, lovable dog who will easily adapt to whatever environment he is in.

251833.name: Bunso
251833.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Bunso is a very cute little gal(a Tabby/Tortie), only one year old who came to us with her very good friends as their house counted too many cats. All of them are shy and Bunso is no exception...Bunso is often seen lounging at the back of her kennel. She is a bit worried when she sees me approaching but accepts my hand wandering between her cheek, her neck and her head. She shifts her body, seems a little uncomfortable but relaxes a bit further in our encounter. Bunso is not hissing or swatting at me. She has made progress since her arrival at the care center, a place that she does not recognize as hers. We know very little about her except that she got along very well with her housemates. Bunso has not had many interactions with people and it shows in the way she appears in a shelter environment. Time, patience, compassion and a low traffic environment(no young children) are of essence for her to succeed in new settings and be happy as a pet. Come and meet Bunso at the Manhattan Care Center.

Follow up note: Bunso came out of her shell. Still a little timid and needing some pep talk at the beginning of an encounter but when the engine starts, the little gal goes full speed, leaning into my hands, purring, rolling on her side and showing how happy she is being cared for...I am so proud of Bunso! Ask to meet her when you visit us at the care center, fall in love and take Bunso home!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

251865.name: Mango Lassi
251865.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Mango Lassi is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Mango Lassi is behaviorally deteriorating in the kennel despite receiving daily enrichment. He has been observed repeatedly jumping up and down throughout the day, often with all four paws off the floor. At times, he is reluctant to return to his kennel and requires multiple treats to encourage him back inside. Despite these challenges, Mango Lassi is highly social with staff and enjoys spending time with them during borough breaks. Medically, Mango Lassi is apparently healthy.

Meet Mango Lassi!
Mango Lassi was found running alongside a road and is now looking for a calm, patient home where he can learn that the world isn't so overwhelming. He can be a bit unsure at first, but once he starts to feel safe, his softer side begins to show. You might just be his favorite flavor of comfort!

My Ideal Home
Mango Lassi would do best in a calm adult-only home where he can take things at his own pace. He needs a gentle, predictable environment and people who understand that trust is something he builds slowly but meaningfully. With time, patience, and soft routines, he will really start to blend in and relax.

Good with Other Pets?
Mango Lassi has shown neutral behavior on leash around other dogs and would benefit from slow, careful introductions if living with another dog.

Good with Kids?
Mango Lassi is recommended for a home without children under 13 due to his fearful nature and need for a quiet environment.

Things to Know
Mango Lassi is a sensitive boy who can be nervous in new situations, but he warms up with calm, patient handling and soft encouragement. Once comfortable, he enjoys gentle affection and will lean in for connection in a very sweet, understated way. He does best in a low-stress home where he can build confidence at his own pace.

Fun Fact
Mango Lassi may start off a little shy, but once he trusts you, he's the sweetest companion.

251907.name: Ace Of Hearts
251907.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Meet your new cuddle buddy! This sweet, affectionate boy loves being close to his people and is known for giving actual hugs-he'll wrap his front legs around you and rest his head while soaking up the attention. He gets so excited for mealtime that he jumps and spins, loves car rides and playing in the sprinklers, and will happily curl up next to you on the couch for movie night. He even watches TV and tries to follow the ball during basketball games! With his funny personality and loving nature, he's sure to bring plenty of smiles and snuggles to his future home. 


Meet Ace of Hearts!
Ace of Hearts was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. He previously lived with adults, and is described as a highly social, wiggly, and affectionate dog who loves interacting with people. He comes over readily for attention, leans into touch, and enjoys playtime, often offering play bows and engaging happily with toys.

My Ideal Home
Ace would do best in a calm, patient home that can support him as he settles in and builds confidence. He can be anxious at times and may pace or have trouble settling, especially in new environments, so a consistent routine and a quiet space will help him feel more secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Ace has shown neutral behavior around dogs at the shelter, but he is not a match for homes with cats due to lunging toward them on walks. Continued positive reinforcement training and management will be important when navigating environments with other animals.

Good with Kids?
A home without young children under 5 is recommended due to his sensitivity to handling and tendency to become fearful when startled.

Things to Know
Ace is a sweet and people-oriented dog who enjoys affection and play, but he can be sensitive to loud noises, sudden movements, and handling around his paws. He may also feel anxious when left alone. He responds best to gentle, choice-based interactions and should never be forced into situations that make him uncomfortable. With time, structure, and positive reinforcement, he has great potential to feel more confident and settled in a home.

Fun Fact
Ace of Hearts lives up to his name, he is all heart when it comes to his people and loves being right by your side soaking up attention.

251916.name: Couch Surfer
251916.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Couch Surfer is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Couch Surfer arrived as a stray. Upon arrival he was exuberantly social with staff; this was also noted during his handling assessment. Unfortunately, Couch Surfer has shown increased barrier frustration making it difficult to handle him safely. When being returned to kennel Couch Surfer has been observed to attempt to bite the kennel lock when handlers are securing his kennel. In one instance he caught the hand of a staff member leaving a small wound in their finger. When outside of the shelter environment Couch Surfer remains social with staff, often soliciting contact and is treat receptive. Medically, Couch Surfer is apparently healthy.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I am playful and cute!

251965.name: Rocky Boat
251965.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Rocky Boat is at risk due to behavioral reasons. His previous owner states that he will resource guard and has a bite history pertaining to the resource guarding. The bite occurred when a person in the home attempted to remove his food. No further details were acquired. While in care, Rocky has been observed to be fearful. Initially, Rocky was noted to baulk on leash and required a sling to be returned to kennel, Rocky was noted to growl when the sling was used. Rocky has since shown improvement in returning to kennel.  During one instance of being returned to kennel however, Rocky got tangled in the leash and snapped at a handler, making contact. Rocky's previous owner describes him as social, active, and playful. Medically, Rocky has diarrhea and is emaciated. 

Meet Rocky Boat! This active, playful boy loves being close to his people and is happiest spending time with his family. Affectionate and social with those he knows and trusts, Rocky enjoys companionship and would love a home where he can be included in daily activities.

Rocky can be an anxious dog, especially around unfamiliar people. He may bark or growl when startled or when strangers approach his family, so he is looking for an adopter who can help him feel secure while continuing positive, reward-based training. He can also be uncomfortable with handling such as grooming and may need patience and a gentle approach during care routines.

Like many smart, energetic dogs, Rocky can become destructive when stressed or under-stimulated, so he will benefit from plenty of exercise, enrichment, and structure. With a consistent routine and an understanding home, Rocky has the potential to be a devoted and loving companion.

Rocky Boat is searching for a patient adopter who will appreciate his loyal nature and help him build confidence at his own pace.

Goldie is a gentle, shy girl who is still adjusting to her new surroundings. While her past is unknown, she's currently showing signs of fear and anxiety and can be a bit unsure at first. With a calm, slow approach, Goldie allows staff to handle her and is beginning to show that she can feel more comfortable over time.

Goldie is a rather large dog, so we recommend a home with older children who can respect her space and move calmly around her. She would do best in a patient, understanding home that will give her the time and space she needs to settle in at her own pace. A quieter environment may help her feel more at ease as she builds confidence. With consistency and care, Goldie has the potential to become a devoted companion.

Goldie is a rather large dog, so we recommend a home with older children who can respect her space and move calmly around her. She would do best in a patient, understanding home that will give her the time and space she needs to settle in at her own pace. A quieter environment may help her feel more at ease as she builds confidence. With consistency and care, Goldie has the potential to become a devoted companion.

252017.name: Brooklyn
252017.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Brooklyn is at risk due to behavioral concerns.  Upon arrival Brooklyn was noted to be reactive to other dogs and this has remains consistent during his stay at the Care Center.  Brooklyn has been observed to pull and hard bark at dogs when on walks and moving through the shelter.  Brooklyn has also been showing signs of deterioration in kennel; noted to jump high persistently and bark persistently during active room hours.  Brooklyn was noted to be social, sweet, and enjoys contact with handlers. Brooklyn has remained treat receptive and are used to redirect his attention. Medically, Brooklyn is apparently healthy. 

Meet Brooklyn!
Brooklyn came in as a stray and is still adjusting to shelter life. He is a people-oriented dog who will readily approach his handler and engage, especially when treats are involved. He can be a bit vocal and emotionally expressive during his time in care, often whining or crying, but he remains responsive, social, and willing to connect with his person.

My Ideal Home
Brooklyn will do best in an adult-only home that can offer a calm, steady routine and a low-stress environment. He benefits from gentle handling, predictable structure, and patience as he settles and builds confidence at his own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
Brooklyn has shown moderate reactivity to other dogs on leash, including barking and pulling toward them. He will need slow, structured introductions and supportive leash handling. At this time, he is not suited for off-leash dog socialization or dog park environments.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to on-leash reactivity and anxiety in stimulating environments.

Things to Know
Brooklyn walks with mild pulling and generally stays engaged with his handler, but can become reactive when seeing other dogs. He accepts handling and remains social overall, though he can be emotionally expressive and may need help learning calmer coping skills. With consistency, patience, and positive reinforcement, he has strong potential to settle into a comfortable routine and continue building confidence.

Fun Fact
Brooklyn is a bit of an older gentleman with a soft side. Once he feels comfortable with you, he likes to stay close and check in often like a loyal companion who just wants to make sure you are part of his little world.

252042.name: Marmee
252042.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

Meet Marmee!

Marmee is a bit of a shy girl and for good reason. She came to us from a home crowded with cats and received almost no socialization to humans. Getting picked up and placed in a shelter is stressful for any cat, but a cat who hasn't yet learned that humans are friends can find the shelter a very tough place to live. Our hope is that in the right home and the right hands, Marmee can properly decompress in a safe, comfortable environment. She'll need a very special person to help her slowly unwind and learn that humans aren't half bad (especially when they have lots of toys and treats to go around). We recommend that she go to an adult-only home that has lots of space for her to stretch out and be the cat she never got the chance to be. Open your heart and meet Marmee at SIACC today!

252043.name: Weasley
252043.summary:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

A volunteer writes: Weasley's been trying to keep up with the shelter days that seem to simultaneously come on fast while and stretch out before him. His snout looks like the cutest Rorschach test ever, but he had no interest in entertaining my ideas (for the record, I see a forever home). This is more than fair but we still like to at least try to say hello and offer some treats, maybe some pets if he'd like, but this isn't really Weasley's style. Weasley came to us from a home with many other cats and very limited experience meeting new people. This makes shelter life a considerable challenge and snuggled up in the back of his cubby, the effort it takes for him to decompress is written all over his little kitty face. He'd love the chance to figure out who he is and wants to be in a safe and loving environment, so please come and meet Weasley at the Staten Island Care Center. 

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

252075.name: Philly Cheese
252075.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Philly Cheese!
Philly Cheese arrived at ACC as a stray, but he has quickly become a staff favorite and is currently living it up as a superstar employee in the manager's office! This lovable guy is social, affectionate, and always ready to make new friends. Whether he's going for a walk, playing with toys, or soaking up attention from his favorite people, Philly Cheese brings plenty of personality wherever he goes.

My Ideal Home
Philly Cheese would thrive with an adopter who is ready for an active and enthusiastic companion. He will benefit from daily exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training to help him practice calm greetings and build his impulse control. With patience and consistency, Philly Cheese is ready to be the big cheese in someone's life!

Good with Other Pets?
Philly Cheese's history with other animals is unknown, but he has met several dogs while in our care. He enjoys social interactions and can be very enthusiastic when meeting canine friends, so continued training and slow introductions will help him practice polite play and appropriate greetings.

Good with Kids?
Due to Philly Cheese's high energy, jumping, and tendency to become overexcited, a home without children under 13 is recommended. He would do best with adults who can help him practice good manners and reward his calmer behaviors.

Things to Know
Philly Cheese is a fun-loving pup with a huge personality! He loves walks, toys, treats, and spending time with people. He may get a little carried away when saying hello and sometimes uses his mouth during play or greetings, but he is eager to learn and loves being around his humans. If you're looking for a playful companion with plenty of love to give, Philly Cheese is ready to melt your heart.


My BoroughBreaker says
Philly Cheese is a total sweetheart who loves being out and about! He is a fantastic walking buddy who could happily keep exploring all day long. He gets excited when he sees other dogs but is a quick learner and was able to settle, watch calmly, and earn treats for his good choices. Philly Cheese loves playing with toys, especially ropes and plushies, and enjoys showing off his silly side with plenty of running and jumping. He is a social butterfly who seems to love everyone he meets, and while he may use his mouth during play or greetings, his heart is always in the right place. This affectionate, energetic pup is ready to bring lots of fun, laughter, and love to his forever home!

252101.name: Momo
252101.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Momo is on the At-Risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and is deteriorating in the Adoptions room. He is now displaying more intense distance increasing behaviors, hissing and swatting hard when interaction is attempted. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

A volunteer writes: I'm sure that there are plenty of things that Momo wishes he could tell us. Things that would help us to understand who he is and what he likes, but any variation of communication can be easier said than done when you're all on your own. Momo isn't exactly that, as we're proudly on his team, but he's still left us guessing quite a bit. Mostly what we've been able to deduce are things that Momo doesn't like. When I met him, he tried to politely decline my friendship by folding himself into the corner and flattening his little ears. Though Momo successfully made his point, I also know that he's been through quite a few changes recently through no fault of his own. At the shelter he tends to lean away or freeze in place in response to our outstretched hands and though he does allow some pets from time to time, it hasn't exactly been his thing. We're very sure that a forever family where he can be himself and communicate as freely as he feels will be the perfect fit.  

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

252206.name: Spud
252206.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Spud is at risk due to behavior concerns. Spud is a highly social dog in the Care Centers; however, despite receiving enrichment and training, he has shown signs of behavioral deterioration. Recently, he has been reported to engage in leash-biting behavior and has been observed slamming into his kennel door. During playgroup, Spud attempted to bite another dog. Outside of the shelter environment, Spud has presented differently. During a Borough Break outing, he was reported to be social. Medically, Spud is apparently healthy.
 
Spud was brought to the Care Centers as a stray, so his behavior history in a home environment is unknown. In the Care Centers, Spud has been social with people; however, he has recently displayed a low threshold for arousal, frequently grabbing and biting the leash during handling. He was also observed attempting to bite another dog during playgroup. While Spud is food-motivated and will take treats, his response is often brief before he returns to leash-biting behavior. Spud would do best in an adult-only home with adopters who can safely manage his arousal and continue working on his behavior using positive reinforcement-based training methods.

Meet Spud!
Spud came into our care after being dropped off at a precinct by someone who did not share their information. He is an energetic, expressive boy who shows a big personality and a lot of enthusiasm for life. In calmer moments, he is eager for attention, checks in with his handler, and clearly enjoys being part of what is going on around him.

My Ideal Home
Spud will do best in an adult only home with a very structured, experienced setup that can support his arousal level and help him build better impulse control over time. He needs a calm, consistent environment and a committed adopter willing to work on training and management using positive reinforcement. A single pet home is recommended so he can focus fully on his own progress.

Good with Other Pets?
Spud has shown significant reactivity toward other dogs and becomes highly aroused in their presence. Because of this, he needs to be the only dog in the home and should not visit dog parks. With structured support and training, he can continue learning more appropriate ways to cope around other animals.

Good with Kids?
Spud is recommended for an adult only home due to his high arousal and impulse control needs.

Things to Know
Spud is a strong, active walker who benefits from clear guidance on leash. He is very people interested and food motivated, but can become mouthy or jumpy when excited. With consistency, structure, and enrichment, he has a lot of potential to channel his energy in a more focused way.

Fun Fact
Spud is a big personality kind of dog who is always ready to engage with life at full speed, and with the right outlet, he can turn that enthusiasm into something really fun to work with.

252254.name: Zephyr
252254.summary:
My foster writes: Zephyr is aptly named; when he has the zoomies, he's as fast as the wind! While he is definitely a shy boy, he cannot resist the temptation of a wand toy, or a cozy spot to nap in the breeze. He has the cutest chirps and he loves a good treat now and then.
Zephyr would do really well in a home where he is given a lot of patience and time to make himself feel comfortable. He could really benefit from having another cat around, one that's confident and friendly and can show him the ropes. He'd also do well with a friendly, respectful, cat-friendly dog.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Zephyr is laying in the back of his cubby, curled up behind his litter box. When the cubby door is opened, he opens his eyes and looks up towards the assessor, remaining in his position curled up behind the litter box. He chirps when he is pet on the top of his head and tolerates all petting, leaning in slightly when he is pet on the head and cheeks. He is unable to be coaxed forward, so full pickup is unable to be attempted. Although he tenses slightly, he is tolerant of light, upward pressure on his sides and under his chest.

Zephyr tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

252300.name: Mimong
252300.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Mimong lights up her kennel with her beautiful orange coat. She is quite vocal too but who can blame her. She comes from a house full of cats, with her three babes(already adopted) and now finds herself all alone in a kennel. At first, she was a bit confused and subdued but now, she seems to be asking questions. We do not have answers, we can not discuss with her the why she is here but we can make her feel comfortable until the day she will finally leave us to join her new family. Mimong can be a little skittish with sudden noises and moves but once she feels at ease, she head bunts, leans into pets, rolls on her kennel floor and purrs(see video and photos). A happy cat! Mimong is a real cutie so worth to meet and hopefully adopt as your new best four legged friend for years to come. Mimong is apparently healthy, is spayed and did very well on her behavior evaluation. She is all ready to go home with you!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

252308.name: Oreo Sprinkles
252308.summary:
Meet Oreo Sprinkles! This lovely young lady believes in quality over quantity when it comes to her friendships. While she can be shy at first, she's affectionate with the ones she trusts and enjoys spending quiet time with her favorite humans. She is also known to really appreciate alone time relaxing in her favorite spots. If you are someone who might be out of the house for parts of the day, or are just looking for a gentle, independent little friend to spend calm evenings with, Oreo Sprinkles might just be your girl. 
She has lived with other cats before and may be open to some new feline friends. She just needs to move at her own pace, and is ready for a calm, understanding, adult-only home where can open up and be herself. Her forever person will be rewarded with a lifelong living room companion!

252316.name: Celina
252316.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Celina is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and is deteriorating in the Adoptions room. She is now displaying signs of petting-induced aggression. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

At the time of assessment, Celina did not tolerate petting or handling. Because her previous owner reports she is a friendly and affectionate lap cat, following her family around, and will be very cuddly and hopping on shoulders once she warms up to her people, in a home environment - the behaviors are considered to be shelter specific, and she would make a great pet but struggles in shelter. This cat is suitable for adopters with previous cat experience, willing to work with a cat to help them adjust and settle in.
Celina is a gorgeous tabby girl with a playful spirit, bright personality, and lots of love waiting beneath the surface. ✨🐾

Shelter life has been overwhelming for her, so she's still learning to feel safe here. But according to her previous family, once Celina settles into a home, she transforms into an affectionate cuddle bug who follows her people around, hops onto shoulders, and happily curls up as a lap cat.

This lively girl loves toys, activities, and interactive play, and she's looking for a patient, cat-savvy adopter who will give her the time and understanding she needs to blossom again. With a little patience, Celina promises to reward her future person with companionship, affection, and plenty of personality.

If you're ready to help a sensitive girl rediscover her confidence, Celina could be your perfect match. 🩷
