252342.name: Salem
252342.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Salem needs his Lucky Star to work harder for him....His family twice lost their home, then he got a really bad cold and a loss of appetite so bad that he needed a feeding tube to be placed. Salem is better thanks to the good care of the veterinary team but he still needs a proper environment to recover 100% from his ordeal. He is a good and sweet cat who has been an exemplary patient and very much loved one by all(see his video). He seeks and enjoys company, truly comes in the arms and never seems to have enough of having people caring for him. Salem dreams of a home, a family and by adopting him, you will gain an amazing companion for years to come. 


What my friends at ACC say about me:

Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I am playful and cute!
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!
Salem is sitting upright at the front of the kennel, observing the assessor with relaxed eyes and body as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, he leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand before gently head bunting it, allowing/leaning into all petting, tail held high. After several passes over his body, he exhibits mild overstimulation, turning and nipping lightly at the assessor's hand without applying any pressure. He does allow more petting on the head and cheeks and doesn't display further signs of escalation. Salem is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back in his kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to softly head bunt and leaning into petting on the head and cheeks. 

Salem interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. Due to behaviors reported in the previous home, we recommend that Salem go to a home with cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, rough play, high energy cats and overstimulation.

252350.name: Kj
252350.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

KJ is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns in the care center and the home environment. In the home, KJ bit a person on the finger, resulting in a small puncture wound that broke skin. In the care center, KJ displays avoidant behavior during leashing, including dodging the leash and hesitating during handling, and has escalated to snapping when his collar is clipped but is able to be walked and slowly warming up to select staff. Medically, KJ has presumed CIRDC.

Kj came into the care center as an owner surrender due to his owner losing housing. Kj has a bite history in the prior home. In his prior owners noted that he prefers not to be picked up, if attempted to he will snap immediately. KJ is a couch potato that enjoys lounging all day. He is low maintenance and likes to be independent. Due to these concerns, we recommend that KJ be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

252361.name: Viggy
252361.summary:
Meet Viggy!
Viggy was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and is now looking for a patient home to help him feel safe again. This sensitive boy can be a bit unsure at first, but there's a playful, curious side to him that starts to peek out once he gets more comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Viggy would do best in a calm, experienced adult-only home that can move at his pace. A quiet environment with gentle, consistent handling will help him build confidence over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Viggy has shown mixed signals with other dogs. He may appear tense at first, but has also engaged in playful interactions off leash. He would benefit from slow, structured introductions and continued guidance.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13, as Viggy can be fearful and needs a low-pressure environment to feel secure.

Things to Know
Viggy is a shy, sensitive dog who may show signs of fear such as a tense body, trembling, or uncertainty during handling, especially around collaring. He does best with slow approaches and will come closer with gentle encouragement. While he can feel overwhelmed at times, he also shows moments of curiosity and even playful energy, especially once he begins to relax. With patience, positive reinforcement, and a calm routine, Viggy has the potential to grow into a more confident and comfortable companion.

Fun Fact
Underneath that shy exterior, Viggy has a playful side just waiting for the right person to help it shine.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
Viggy is an adorable, affectionate dog who was very playful and curious from the start. He doesn't know many commands (he seems to know "sit" and sometimes "stop") but he listens and is considerate in certain environments. He enjoys being in the grass and likes to play tug-of-war (plays rough and will playfully bite) and enjoys being rewarded with treats. During our walks through the parks, he seemed to have a particular interest in leaves and tree branches/bark, and would often stop to chew on some but never swallowed it. Despite it raining during our Boroughbreak, he did not seem to mind the rain (despite a bit of sneezing) and was still very loving and playful regardless of the weather. He's a unique dog and deserves a family that will return his affection and treat him with kindness and loyalty. If given the chance, we would love to have a BoroughBreak with Viggy again.

252368.name: Sunny D
252368.summary:
My foster writes: Sunny D is gentle and easy to please. Little chirps in the morning, say hello as I gather her breakfast. And we begin the day together. Sunny immediately made herself at home, very confident, and now functions as a greeter when I have guests over. Sunny mostly follows me room to room, with her little chirps, occasionally head butting my legs or hands asking for pets, offering nice little breaks as I work from home.
Nothing makes her happier than a Delectables treat, she'll climb all over me to finish her snack and rubs herself against me after as if to say thank you. Sunny doesn't love being carried around but tolerates it for a short while, she prefers to sleep pick her spot on your leg or lap to use as a pillow.

252403.name: Suzie
252403.summary:
My foster writes: Suzie is SUCH a special girl. For one thing, she's the smartest kitty in the world, and she's been working very hard to be noticed by her future family. So far she's learned how to play fetch (which she loves), how to ding a bell for treats, and how to high five! She's also very sweet and social and will bond very closely to her person. She likes to greet you when you come home, and while she's not quite a lap cat, she does love to curl up by your side-especially if it's in bed for a nap! Aside from being sweet, she's also a very funny girl and gets zoomies all the time, running around and tossing her toys up in the air. Based on her history, we suspect she might enjoy playing with feline friends too. So, if you want an adorable mini house panther with crazy soft fur and a big personality, Suzie is your girl!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Suzie is laying in a loaf position on top of her den, pupils slightly dilated and looking around the room as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she tenses slightly, remaining in her position on top of the den. Initially when petting is attempted, Suzie backs away to avoid contact. The assessor softly speaks to her and offers a squeeze up treat, and she sniffs the air before quickly coming forward to eat it. Suzie is tolerant of all petting while she eats, not engaging and tail held low. She is unable to be coaxed down from the top of the den, so pickup is unable to be attempted. She is tolerant of light upward pressure applied to her sides and under her chest, remaining slightly tense but without further issue.

252403.summaryHtml:
My foster writes: Suzie is SUCH a special girl. For one thing, she's the smartest kitty in the world, and she's been working very hard to be noticed by her future family. So far she's learned how to play fetch (which she loves), how to ding a bell for treats, and how to high five! She's also very sweet and social and will bond very closely to her person. She likes to greet you when you come home, and while she's not quite a lap cat, she does love to curl up by your side-especially if it's in bed for a nap! Aside from being sweet, she's also a very funny girl and gets zoomies all the time, running around and tossing her toys up in the air. Based on her history, we suspect she might enjoy playing with feline friends too. So, if you want an adorable mini house panther with crazy soft fur and a big personality, Suzie is your girl!

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I have lived with cats in my previous home.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

Suzie is laying in a loaf position on top of her den, pupils slightly dilated and looking around the room as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she tenses slightly, remaining in her position on top of the den. Initially when petting is attempted, Suzie backs away to avoid contact. The assessor softly speaks to her and offers a squeeze up treat, and she sniffs the air before quickly coming forward to eat it. Suzie is tolerant of all petting while she eats, not engaging and tail held low. She is unable to be coaxed down from the top of the den, so pickup is unable to be attempted. She is tolerant of light upward pressure applied to her sides and under her chest, remaining slightly tense but without further issue.

Suzie tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

252439.name: Meryl
252439.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Saturday, June 27 at 12PM - 4PM with Buddy's Dog Den - 429 Graham Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11211  Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!
My foster writes:
The sweetest angel, here on earth for us to pet! Meryl is the friendliest, good-natured, patient pup around. She loves meeting people and is gentle with kids. No one on earth is more excited to go for a walk, and she has become my new running buddy (although what I consider running is a little trot for her!) After her walks, she loves to curl up and nap. Once in a while, she will decide it's time for a some pets and kisses, and then she will go back to sleep. In the time we have had her, we have barely heard her bark, and she doesn't react to street noise at all.She has good manners, and even in her excitement, will sit while her leash is being put on and when you are preparing her food. She know how to sit and come, and and is just as happy working for pets as she is for treats. She is not destructive at all, and can be left alone and then her warm greeting will make you so happy to be home! She is the nicest girl around, a great apartment dog, and a wonderful addition to any family!

Meet Meryl!
Meryl is a 6-year-old girl who was found as a stray and is now ready for her next chapter. She has a calm, steady presence and is generally easygoing when meeting new people. Meryl is social in a relaxed way and enjoys checking in with her handler while exploring her surroundings.

Personality
Meryl is friendly, balanced, and moderately social. She approaches people readily, accepts handling, and tends to stay neutral and composed during interactions. She is past the high-energy puppy phase and has a more settled, even-tempered style.

My Ideal Home
Meryl would do well in a variety of homes, including first-time adopters, thanks to her steady temperament. She will enjoy a home that provides regular walks, gentle structure, and companionship. Overall, she is a flexible, easy companion for many lifestyles.

Good with Other Pets?
Meryl has shown no reactivity toward other dogs on leash or during handling. With slow introductions, she may do well with other respectful dogs. She appears generally neutral and easygoing in social settings.

Good with Kids?
Meryl's gentle and stable demeanor makes her a potential match for many home types, including families. As always, introductions should be done thoughtfully to ensure a good fit for everyone.

Things to Know
Meryl walks with a moderate pull but is responsive and easy to handle. She is social without being overly demanding and adjusts well to new environments. Her level 1 behavioral rating reflects her overall steady, adaptable nature.

Fun Fact
Meryl is a low-drama, good-company kind of dog who's happy to just be part of your day. She's the definition of an easygoing best friend.

252442.name: Swanson
252442.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Swanson is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to the limited information available on admission, it is unknown just how socialized she is, and she has been avoidant of touch and escalates to defensive behaviors during interactions due to her high level of FAS. Due to these consistent elevated stress levels and her length of stay, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who have experience with cats that potentially have limited socialization - and are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust. And those who have experience with positive reinforcement training and adult cat socialization, and helping a potentially under socialized/fearful cat adjust to strangers.

Swanson is a quiet, watchful tabby girl with thoughtful eyes and a gentle spirit. 🩶🐾

Right now, the shelter feels far too overwhelming for her, so she prefers to observe the world from a safe distance rather than join in on playtime or social activities. There's something deeply meaningful and moving in her quiet presence - a soft kind of beauty that reveals itself slowly to those willing to listen.

Swanson is looking for a calm, low-traffic home with patient caretakers who will let her settle in at her own pace. She may never be the loudest or boldest cat in the room, but for the right person, her cautious trust and quiet companionship will feel incredibly special.

If you have a peaceful home and a heart for shy souls, Swanson may be ready to write her next chapter with you. ✨

252444.name: Kaleidoscope
252444.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

p>What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
A Volunteer Wrote: He's so loving and affectionate that on a rainy day we took him out twice just to lift our spirits! Kaleidoscope was so happy to hang out on a stoop showing off his tricks (paw with both paws! Sit! Stay!) and didn't care at all about the other dogs walking by because it was all about us. He showered us with much-deserved love (he's a wonderful hugger) in exchange for treats and pats. We definitely got the better deal! Please, come meet this fabulous pup!

My Foster writes: Kaleidoscope (Scopey, Kai Kai) is the perfect balance of energy and snuggles. Upon meeting him, he immediately greeted us with a smile, wiggly body, and ears back- as he continues to do so. He has the softest fur and has the biggest softest ears that he loves to get scratched- along with head and butt rubs of course. Kaleidoscope loves his daily enrichment such as the lick mat, Kong with peanut butter, playing fetch, practicing commands and learning new ones. He is already a master of sit, paw, other paw, stay, and okay go. While he loves to play, he also loves being a big lug that snuggles into us, spoons, get pets, watches tv with us, and cutely snores lol. He is such a gentleman when we eat dinner (no whining and begging) and when we do chores around the house. When left alone he just chills out and patiently waits on the couch for us to get home. Kaleidoscope is such an intelligent mush-ball that would excel in a calm home environment.

252448.name: Merlot
252448.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Merlot is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns in the care center and in his previous home. In the prior home, Merlot was reported to display resource guarding and attempted to bite by lunging and snapping during one incident, though no contact with skin was made. In the care center, Merlot displays high arousal, including hard pulling, frantic movement in new environments, and significant reluctance to return to his kennel, often pancaking and requiring multiple handlers, treat trails, or coaxing to complete kennel re-entry. Merlot is social with handlers, enjoys training, learns new cues readily, and engages well with toys and food reinforcement. Medically, Merlot is apparently healthy.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I would prefer someone who can be home with me most of the time.

Merlot is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is making great progress every single day. He is working on polite exchange, a skill that is helping him learn to share and interact with confidence and ease. With positive reinforcement and plenty of encouragement, Merlot is building the trust and composure he needs to put his best paw forward.

252463.name: Nina Bobina
252463.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Nina Bobina is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Nina Bobina has been jumping up, leash biting, and flailing/thrashing once removed from the kennel. Nina Bobina can be social with familiar handlers/staff and readily engages in training sessions. But due to her leash biting, she had become more difficult to walk. Medically, Nina Bobina is apparently healthy.

Nina Bobina was surrendered by her previous owner due to her owner urgently moving out of the country and not being able to take her.  Her family described her as a quiet yet active, affectionate, playful dog. She enjoys car rides, is allowed bathing and brushing by her family, and had access to a yard, so she does not venture outside often. She loves peanut butter snacks and playing fetch. During her stay in care, Nina presented as highly fearful, growling when approached in the kennel. Over time, she slowly warmed up and is social and playful with staff/handlers that she is familiar with. But due to her handling sensitivity, Nina has begun leash biting once out of the kennel, which has made her walks more difficult. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Nina Bobina to be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can allow her the time and space to acclimate at her own pace. 

Meet Nina!
Nina was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her and is now looking for a calm, loving home where she can feel safe and settle in at her own pace. She has a sweet, people-oriented nature and truly enjoys being near her humans once she feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Nina would do best in a calm, structured home that can offer patience, routine, and gentle guidance. She has some anxiety in new environments, so a quiet space and slow introductions will help her confidence grow over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Nina has shown neutral behavior around other dogs in the shelter setting. She does not appear reactive, but continued slow and controlled introductions are recommended as she settles into a new home.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 due to her fearfulness. An adult-only home is recommended so she can decompress and build confidence at her own pace.

Things to Know
Nina is a gentle, affectionate dog who enjoys being close to people and leans into attention once she feels secure. She can experience anxiety in new situations and may need time to relax and adjust, but she responds well to calm handling and positive reinforcement. She enjoys familiar routines like walks, crate time, and enrichment activities, and she especially loves cuddles, peanut butter treats, and playtime like fetch. With patience and consistency, Nina's loving personality really begins to shine.

Fun Fact
Once Nina feels at home, she transforms into a cuddle-loving shadow who just wants to be wherever her people are.

A volunteer writes: Nina is the first dog we bring out this weekend, but I really don't even want to take out anyone else after I meet her. She is so delicious and charming I could spend all of my shelter volunteer hours just with her. Her nose has the most perfect pink tip, and her ears are horizontal straight out to the horizon.
Her notes indicate at first she was very scared, unwilling to leave her kennel, but she has been bright, charming and a social butterfly with us! Nina romps, plays, cuddles, and relaxes with us out in the yard.
Nina lived with 3 adults and two children. She was friendly and outgoing with visitors, strangers, and children. She is described as playful and social. She enjoys spending time with her family, has been crate trained, and loves car rides. She knows basic cues and loves peanut butter snacks. Her family's favorite thing about her is how much she loves cuddles.

She enjoys car rides, is allowed bathing and brushing by her family, and had access to a yard, so she does not venture outside often. She loves peanut butter snacks and playing fetch. During her stay in care, Nina presented as highly fearful, growling when approached in the kennel. Over time, she slowly warmed up and is social and playful with staff/handlers that she is familiar with. But due to her handling sensitivity, Nina has begun leash biting once out of the kennel, which has made her walks more difficult. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Nina Bobina to be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can allow her the time and space to acclimate at her own pace. Meet Nina!
Nina was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her and is now looking for a calm, loving home where she can feel safe and settle in at her own pace. She has a sweet, people-oriented nature and truly enjoys being near her humans once she feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Nina would do best in a calm, structured home that can offer patience, routine, and gentle guidance. She has some anxiety in new environments, so a quiet space and slow introductions will help her confidence grow over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Nina has shown neutral behavior around other dogs in the shelter setting. She does not appear reactive, but continued slow and controlled introductions are recommended as she settles into a new home.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 due to her fearfulness. An adult-only home is recommended so she can decompress and build confidence at her own pace.

Things to Know
Nina is a gentle, affectionate dog who enjoys being close to people and leans into attention once she feels secure. She can experience anxiety in new situations and may need time to relax and adjust, but she responds well to calm handling and positive reinforcement. She enjoys familiar routines like walks, crate time, and enrichment activities, and she especially loves cuddles, peanut butter treats, and playtime like fetch. With patience and consistency, Nina's loving personality really begins to shine.

Fun Fact
Once Nina feels at home, she transforms into a cuddle-loving shadow who just wants to be wherever her people are. A volunteer writes: Nina is the first dog we bring out this weekend, but I really don't even want to take out anyone else after I meet her. She is so delicious and charming I could spend all of my shelter volunteer hours just with her. Her nose has the most perfect pink tip, and her ears are horizontal straight out to the horizon. Her notes indicate at first she was very scared, unwilling to leave her kennel, but she has been bright, charming and a social butterfly with us! Nina romps, plays, cuddles, and relaxes with us out in the yard. Nina lived with 3 adults and two children. She was friendly and outgoing with visitors, strangers, and children. She is described as playful and social. She enjoys spending time with her family, has been crate trained, and loves car rides. She knows basic cues and loves peanut butter snacks. Her family's favorite thing about her is how much she loves cuddles.

252466.name: Koda
252466.summary:
Meet Koda!
Koda arrived at the shelter alongside three other dogs after her family lost their housing, and while all of her siblings have already found homes, Koda is still waiting patiently for her turn. This sweet girl can be shy at first and prefers to get to know new people on her own terms, but once she feels safe, her playful and affectionate personality starts to shine.

My Ideal Home
Koda would do best in a patient home that understands she may need a little extra time to settle in and build confidence. Once comfortable, she's an active and loving companion who enjoys walks, toys, car rides, and spending time close to her people.

Good with Other Pets?
Koda previously lived successfully with other dogs and was described as tolerant and playful with both familiar and unfamiliar dogs. At the shelter, she has shown some nervousness during introductions and may become tense when overwhelmed, so slow and thoughtful introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Koda previously lived with children and was described as tolerant and friendly once warmed up. As with any shy dog, respectful interactions and allowing her space to settle in will help her feel most comfortable.

Things to Know
Koda can be fearful in new environments and initially struggled to come out of her kennel or engage with handling at the shelter. As she's decompressed, she's shown more of her social and playful side, happily running over to handlers, leaning into affection, and showing off her loose, goofy energy. She can be a little mouthy with treats, may jump up when excited, and has some playful puppy-like manners she'll continue working on. Koda is also crate trained, enjoys long walks, and already knows cues like sit, stay, wait, and come.

Fun Fact
Koda's siblings may have already left the building, but this playful girl is still holding auditions for her perfect forever family.

252476.name: Karma
252476.summary:
Meet Karma!
Karma was surrendered due to housing insecurity and is now ready for a fresh start with a family who can give her the stability she deserves. This gentle girl is as sweet as her name suggests, a soft, loyal companion who just wants to be close to her people (and collect plenty of belly rubs along the way).

My Ideal Home
Karma would do best in a calm, adult-only home that can give her time to settle in and build confidence at her own pace. She thrives with routine, patience, and a gentle approach, especially when adjusting to new people or environments.

Good with Other Pets?
Karma previously lived with other dogs and cats and has shown neutral, appropriate behavior at the shelter. She may do well with other calm pets with slow, respectful introductions.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for children under 13 due to her sensitive nature.

Things to Know
Karma is an affectionate, loyal girl who enjoys being near her people and loves gentle attention on her own terms. She walks nicely on leash and is used to multiple daily walks. She can be a little shy at first and may feel unsure around loud noises or new situations, but she warms up with a slow, patient approach. She may also alert bark when someone knocks, simply letting you know someone's there. With time, positive reinforcement, and a calm environment, Karma continues to grow more confident every day.

Fun Fact
Karma is a firm believer that what you give is what you get, so if you give her love, patience, and snacks, she'll return it tenfold with loyalty and cuddles.

252487.name: Maxipoo
252487.summary:
My foster writes:
Hi my name is Max, aka Baemax, MaxNCheese, Tuxedo max! My foster parents are so impressed with how quickly I'm learning. My foster mom can't help but love on me all day long because I'm so cuddly and love kisses. She says I'm the prettiest dog in greenpoint, which is why she's allowed to give me belly rubs all the time (although some may say I'm not too picky about who gives me belly rubs). I really love being around my people and I'm working on being more confident when I'm left alone at home or when I'm meeting other dogs. My forever family is ideally one who has the time to give me structure and socialize me with other pups. I do great on the New York City ferry and on car rides when my foster dad takes me in my K9 sports sac. I'm really looking forward to meeting my forever family!


I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

252494.name: Shiny
252494.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Shiny is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the Care Center, Shiny displays high stress deterioration & repetitive behaviors including spinning, pacing, vocalizing, and soiling the kennel while being unable to settle. Shiny was found running loose on the BQE and when emergency services attempted to capture her, she did bite one of them which broke skin. In the Care Center, Shiny is becoming more social outside of kennel with staff and volunteers. Despite this in kennel we are unable to break the harmful kennel syndrome behaviors for any significant amount of time that benefits Shiny. Medically, Shiny recently recovered from CIRDC and is physically healthy at this time.

Shiny came into the care center as a stray found wandering the highway. She is noted to take treats from handlers but will remain avoidant and allow minimal handling. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: The first time I meet Shiny, she's enamored with a ball in her kennel - so much so that she's able to successfully ignore the barking dogs in crates all around her, hopping excitedly in place in response to the rubber toy in front of her. To see a dog still find slivers of joy amid the noise and chaos of a shelter is one of the most beautiful things about these animals; in this environment, many never gain the confidence to embrace their silliness with abandon.

When it's time to go for a walk, she finds another toy in the hallway and is just as happy to entertain herself for a few moments before trotting on her way. While she can be a bit timid and may need some coaxing to make it all the way outside, once in the fresh air she's eager to sniff and intently explore her surroundings. Her striking red coat turns heads more than once.

Despite these small moments of playfulness, the shelter has been stressful for Shiny, and she's been seen pacing and spinning in her kennel, unable to settle. We imagine this petite husky craves much more activity than shelter life affords. Volunteers have given her a lot of attention in the past few weeks: She's been housed in a small kennel in a back room not viewable by the public. And so we make sure to give her a nice walk every chance we can get. 

Shiny was found wandering the BQE, with an injured paw and small abrasions on her body; we don't know how she sustained her injuries or much else about her history.

252500.name: Chloe
252500.summary:
My foster writes: Chloe is the kind of dog who forms a deep bond almost instantly and just wants to be by your side at all times. Sweet, loyal, gentle, and naturally protective, she has the perfect mix of playful energy and calm cuddle bug. Whether she's following you from room to room, resting her head in your lap, or keeping a watchful eye on her people, Chloe's loving personality makes everyone around her feel safe and adored. She would make an incredible companion for someone looking for a true best friend or a family wanting the sweetest addition to their home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

A Volunteer Wrote: Seeing Chloe in the shelter is to imagine the transformation she will be given when she is rescued, and the lifetime of delight it will give you. She cowers in the back of her pop up crate in the middle of a noisy hallway, absolutely stressed, but with patience and delicious treats she takes a leap of faith and allows herself to be leashed. And when I take that leash off of her again in the back, look at our girl go!!!!! She bounces with joy, jumps in a lap for affection, and, as one volunteer insists, actually smiles. She is not happy here, this shy, sensitive girl who deserves the world, a world she will light up with her joy.

252577.name: Joe Schmoe
252577.summary:
My foster writes; 🐾  There is no Schmoe in this Joe.  Joe is an absolute Gem!  At 3 years old he is past his puppy phase, and presents himself like a sweet, smart, playful, loyal boy.  He is a 68lb handsome delight.  Joe is one part protector and 2 parts love bug.  He is extremely smart and knows a lot of commands- 'Sit', 'paw,' 'stay' (he will stay until you say come), 'down', 'drop it', 'come',  'find your ball'.  Joe likes to go on walks and only pulls a tiny bit.  Joe is well behaved on walks, does not react to wildlife, other dogs, or people, which makes him the perfect outdoor companion.  Unlike most dogs who are treat-motivated, Joe is very trainable because he is both treat-motivated and very eager to please his owner.  And is the gentlest treat-taker I have ever fostered. He will also wait very patiently for his food with a simple 'sit - wait' command. He is also terrific in a car. Just an all around good boy. 
He did great staying home alone for a few hours in a room.  Joe is very sweet with new people as long as he is introduced with some distance. 

❤️ Well-behaved and eager to please
🐕 Good on a leash
🧠 Smart and knows his commands
🎾 Playful, goofy, and very sweet


Joe is someone's soul dog. He deserves the absolute best.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

252605.name: Tony
252605.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Tony is at risk due to behavioral concerns in his previous home. Tony's previous owner reported a multiple bite history, a history of guarding toys, food, any stolen or random objects, and destructive tendencies. Tony is reported to have bitten multiple household members. The bites are reported to have broken skin during the incidents. Medically, Tony is apparently healthy.

Tony came into the care center as an owner surrender due to moving. Tony is noted to have a bite history in the prior home.  Tony is noted to have handling sensitivity in the prior home, resulting in bites towards family members. In the prior home Tony prefers contact on their own terms and likes to spend most of his time in Living room or his crate for up to 6 hours. He loves to run. He loves to run, cuddle (he will let you know it's ok), go on walks, play fetch with his favorite toys, he loves treats in the shape of bones, he loves toys that squeak and are easily able to bite on and run with and he previously was both wet and dry food diet his favorite brand is Purina. Though the bites have not typically caused serious injury, they happen consistently and indicate a high level of stress for Tony when he is in these situations that escalate to biting. This is a behavior that has been rehearsed over his long lifetime and will require careful environmental management and likely significant lifestyle adaptations to prevent injury to his future humans and to increase Tony quality of life. We highly recommend consultation with a veterinary behaviorist and/or highly qualified behavior modification trainer. Tony is available for rescue through one of our new home partners.

My Foster Wrires: 
Leonardo is a little miracle of healing. His shelter pictures show him when his poor tail was still raw from his nervous habit of pulling out his own fur to deal with a situation - he can't tell me what it was but I hear it included animal, situational and human stressors - that was just too much for him. Now, finally, for the first time in his kitty life, he has space and quiet to himself, and has been able to show me and my friends what a real jewel he is. He starts purring halfway down the hall and will push his furry face into your hand in anticipation of pets. He runs after a ping pong ball as joyously as a little kitten. He's thrilled by the sights and sounds outside the window but is just as happy keeping company on a desktop or next to a good book. He can be content all by himself if that's what is called for, too. It's incredibly rewarding to offer him a place where he can be his best self, and that best self is everything a wonderful cat could ever offer.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
Leonardo tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: We've heard Leonardo is playful and sweet when no one else is around, but as you can imagine that doesn't happen with much frequency in the busy shelter. Leonardo's a quiet guy who doesn't ask for much and he could use a little reassurance that this last point is indeed the case. Like a lot of cats, he prefers a calm and predictable place to call his own and though he hasn't found that just yet, he's hopeful and we are too. Brought to us from a home with other cats and dogs, Leonardo has tried and tried to make the shelter work. He came forward to say hello to me but wasn't sure about everything else happening in Adoptions, but still I admire his openness. His little tail bears the brunt of his confusion, but Leonardo wants the chance to be better or at least the chance for someone to take their time and learn more about him.

252639.name: Junie B. Jones
252639.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Junie B. Jones!
Junie B. Jones was found as a stray and is still figuring out the world around her. This sweet, sensitive girl may be a little unsure at first, but she's quietly curious and wants to connect, she just needs a little time and patience to get there.

My Ideal Home
Junie B. Jones would do best in a calm, quiet home with a patient adopter who will let her warm up at her own pace. A low-pressure environment will help her feel safe and build confidence over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Her history with other pets is unknown, but she has shown neutral behavior at the shelter. Slow, gentle introductions would be important.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13, as she is still building confidence and can be sensitive to new or overwhelming situations.

Things to Know
Junie B. Jones is a gentle, shy girl who may show a mix of curiosity and hesitation when meeting new people. She'll stay close by, offer small tail wags, and accept light petting once she feels a bit more comfortable. Handling is tolerated but she may appear unsure at first, showing signals like lip licking or a tucked tail. With time, she begins to soften and relax. Giving her space, going at her pace, and using positive reinforcement will help her continue to come out of her shell.

Fun Fact
Just like her namesake, Junie B. Jones has a little bit of sass, a little bit of sweetness, and a whole lot of personality waiting to shine once she feels safe.

A volunteer writes: Junie B. Jones 💕 Junie made her way to the shelter via a field rescue. She had been left behind after an eviction and was in a room when the shelter's team arrived. Soft kind voices was all it took for Junie to approach and sniff, and be off to the safety of the shelter.

You can imagine that these circumstances were scary for her, and Junie was timid and scared for a bit. But within weeks she's become not only brave and social, but a sassy girl! And I LOVE a girl full of sass, bonus points if she's middle aged or senior. And Junie is a perfect 6 years old. She adores toys and makes sure I know I'm meant to throw them for her to fetch by tossing them at my feet and backing up in anticipation. When I'm slow, which is often, she barks hoarsely her complaints at me, honestly one of the cutest scratchy barks I have ever heard. We play and then she goes back to her kennel where she naps in a sun spot.

Junie is looking for a home with some experience, and she's been looking too long in my opinion! Come meet her at Queens ACC.

252686.name: Baby Nyla
252686.summary:
My foster writes:
Baby Nyla is a two year-old playful, cuddly and incredibly friendly princess. She loves to chase her fishing pole toy around and watch birds through the window. Nyla's preferred sleeping position is cuddled up on your pillow next to you. I have never seen a cat so eager to meet and quick to snuggle up with guests of all ages - she reminds us of a dog! She's been a perfect eater, litter box user and cuddler appropriate for an adopter with any level of experience. We also think she'd be great with kids!

A volunteer writes: Stretched out on her enormous bed in very princess and the pea style, Baby Nyla got right up to say that she's more of a people's princess and proceeded to welcome me like she's never met a stranger. This is likely true, but only part of the story as Baby Nyla went right on to the next order of business, which was how she was going to climb onto my lap. A charmingly busy cat who situated herself right at the front when she realized she couldn't, Baby Nyla was completely content to cuddle. She's looking for a home where she can play to her heart's content and become the best little kitty she can be.

252687.name: Melow
252687.summary:
Melow is a sweet, easygoing boy who's ready to find a loving home to relax in. This handsome couch potato enjoys the simple things in life - lounging in the sun room, short leisurely walks, and spending time with his people. He walks wonderfully on a leash with no pulling, loves bath time and water, and is always happy to hop in the car for a ride.

Melow already knows several commands, including sit, come, and walking cues, and his previous owner described him as an especially loving dog. When he's not napping, Melow enjoys playing with rope toys and soaking up affection.

If you're looking for a calm, loyal companion who will happily curl up beside you and enjoy life's quiet moments, Melow may be the perfect match.

252737.name: Big Mama
252737.summary:
Meet Big Mama!
Big Mama was brought in by the NYPD after being found with multiple puncture wounds, likely from another animal. Despite everything she's been through, she has remained incredibly affectionate, social, and resilient. Her bite wounds have fully healed, and she's now ready to leave shelter life behind for a loving forever home.

My Ideal Home
Big Mama would do best in a loving home that can continue supporting her recovery while giving her the stability and affection she clearly craves. She enjoys being around people and would thrive with a family that appreciates a sweet, attention seeking companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Big Mama has shown neutral behavior around other dogs in the shelter setting. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended as she settles into a new environment.

Good with Kids?
No young children under 5 are recommended due to some resource guarding around toys.

Things to Know
Big Mama is a soft, wiggly girl who loves attention and happily leans into affection from handlers. She walks nicely on leash, greets people warmly, and has shown a very social personality despite her difficult past. She does appear to value certain toys and may hover over them, so continued positive reinforcement training around sharing and trading items will help her succeed. Because one of her injuries was likely a bite wound, her future adopter will need to complete a little extra paperwork and continue with a few follow up vet visits this year, but she has been recovering wonderfully and her wounds are fully healed.

Fun Fact
Big Mama may have had a rough start, but her favorite thing now seems to be soaking up love and giving full body wiggles to everyone she meets.

A volunteer writes: At 80 pounds, Big Mama has earned her adorable name. Found stray with 11 punctures from bites of an unknown origin, Big Mama has recovered well at the shelter. In spite of whatever happened before she arrived, her notes and interactions with staff all indicate she's an affectionate, social and resilient girl. She's also a toy loving girl, and once we give her one, it doesn't leave her side. Or more specifically her paws, as she perfectly positions and holds it to chew and squeak at us. Big Mama attempts to roll over onto her side a few times, and maybe it's her mobility or the heat, but she abandons her attempts to give us that glorious belly to rub.

Because of those bites, Big Mama will need a little extra paperwork to take home, but the process isn't daunting and shouldn't deter anyone. Big Mama is ready to go home today and is available to level 2 homes - so ones with just a bit of experience.

252738.name: Moss
252738.summary:
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am looking for a home with a patient person who is very generous with treats.

A volunteer writes: Moss will kind of tuck his head into the corner in his version of hello and he knows that his best might not reflect all the effort he puts into it, but Moss is hoping that someone will still take the time to get to know him. Making friends is a process for someone like Moss, who came to us from a home with many other cats and limited experience with people, and it might be a process that takes some time. In the back of his cubby when I opened the door, Moss seemed to sort of shrink even further into the corner before making his entrance... to his other cubby. We haven't been able to learn too much about his likes but can say with some confidence that the Care Center isn't amongst them. He's hoping to find a patient and loving home where he can be himself, figure things out, and become the best cat he can be.

Meet Parsley!

Life has not been easy for Parsley. He came to us from a house crowded with cats and little to no interaction with humans. Now he's starting from scratch in the shelter (and that's not an easy place for a cat to be). He's looking for an adopter who can meet him where he's at. It's also recommended that he go to an adult-only home as children could easily overwhelm him and hinder any socialization progress. Our hope is that in a calm, stable, environment, Parsley can properly decompress and finally just be a cat. He may be a bit of a project, but earning his love and trust would be worth all the effort. Come to SIACC to meet Parsley today!

252789.name: King Julian
252789.summary:
Meet King Julian!
King Julian is a fun-loving, people-oriented dog who enjoys spending time with his favorite humans. He previously lived in a home with adults, children, and other dogs, where he was described as friendly, playful, and outgoing. He loves attention, enjoys playtime, and is always ready to join in on the next adventure.

My Ideal Home
King Julian is looking for an experienced, adult-only home that can provide him with structure, consistency, and continued positive reinforcement training. He is an active dog who will thrive with daily exercise, enrichment, and opportunities to work on his leash skills and impulse control. A predictable routine and patient guidance will help him build confidence and succeed in his new home.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 years old. Due to his resource guarding, mouthiness, and reactivity, an adult-only home is recommended.

Good with Other Pets?
King Julian should be the only pet in his new home. He has a history of reactivity toward unfamiliar dogs and small animals and is not recommended for homes with cats or visits to dog parks.

Overall Health
Healthy overall.

Level 4 - Experienced Adopters. King Julian has shown resource guarding, leash reactivity, anxiety, and strong leash pulling both in his previous home and in the shelter. He will do best with adopters who are committed to continuing reward-based training, providing clear structure, and helping him build confidence while managing his triggers.

King Julian has a playful, goofy side and loves engaging with toys and spending time with his people. He's eager for affection, happily leans into pets, and enjoys interactive play. With the right guidance and an experienced family, King Julian has the potential to become a loyal and entertaining companion who will keep life full of fun.

252790.name: Confetti
252790.summary:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

Meet Confetti!

She may not be the life of the party, but Confetti still brings joy to those who take the time to get to know her. This reserved and demure kitty needs a patient, understanding adopter who understands feline behavior & body language as she came to us from a home with too many cats and not enough humans. With treats, toys, and positive reinforcement, she can grow to learn that people are worth being around. She has already shown signs in shelter that she could be open to making friends, so why not come to SIACC and say hi to Confetti?

A volunteer writes: Confetti has been waiting months for someone to notice her, even if she doesn't know what to make of them when they do. Coming to us from a home with many other cats, her confusion at finding herself here seems to have extended to the day to day of shelter life. Confetti notices the treats and toys we leave her and then stretches out in response. She sometimes sees us trying to win her favor and will accept pets from our scratcher tool and engage with a feather want. We don't have much information about her life before, but Confetti's determination to live her life on her own terms is admirable, if not always the perfect opening for making a new friend. She's hoping to find a family who will meet her where she is and love her for who she is.

252812.name: Sugar
252812.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Sugar is at risk due to behavior concerns. She was returned to the care centers, as an owner surrender, after being adopted. Her previous owner reported house training challenges, displayed separation anxiety, was fearful of loud noises, and would resource guard high value items. Sugar was noted to escalate to snapping or attempting to bite if approached with food. On leash, she was described as shy and prefers contact on her own terms, as she will escalate to hard barking and growling. In the care center she was noted to kennel fight and become tense, hard bark, and growl at another dog during playgroup. Sugar has tolerated handling, has been able to be redirected with treats, and engages with handlers on her walks. Medically, Sugar is overweight but otherwise healthy.

Sugar was surrendered by her previous owner due to landlord issues, behavior concerns, and not having time to provide care. Her previous owner described her as a social and active dog who can be very quiet. She spends her time where people are, in the bedroom of the home, or in the living room. Sugar allowed her family to bathe and brush her, and only pulls moderately on her leash during her usual 20min walks she goes on twice a day. She loves to cuddle and is not picky with food or treats. Her owner did report behavior concerns including resource guarding of food, barking and growling at strangers, hard barking and growling at unfamiliar dogs, house soiling, and more. During her stay in care, she has been loose and wiggly with handlers but is reactive to dogs in her kennel. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Sugar be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

252844.name: Miu Miu
252844.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
This sweet, high-energy, affectionate and silly boy is waiting for his second chance at a home. Miu Miu has been at the care center since April 2026. With his dashing good looks and his love for play with wand and feather toys, he is beloved by staff and volunteers. He can typically be found lounging on his favorite bed and waiting patiently for his turn at snuggles and games with whoever has come to visit. He is looking for an adult-only home who is familiar with feline body language. He can sometimes become overstimulated and he needs positive outlets for his energy. He is incredibly smart and loving, all he needs is to build that special bond with his person who will understand his boundaries. He is trusting of people, patient and his purr motor is constantly running. If you are looking for a very handsome boy who will keep you laughing and be your very best friend, come and meet Miu Miu.

A volunteer writes: Miu Miu looks like he's admiring his own paws when he splays them out on the wall. A momentary distraction from his rolls, he has a unique coordination that is somehow even cuter than it sounds. Miu Miu's known as a friendly and outgoing superstar with some pretty clear and defined interests, mainly playtime. He's a smart cat who would love nothing more than to go and do, to play and to pounce, he only needs someone to invite him. Since they haven't just yet, Miu Miu has taken it upon himself to invite himself. Rolling around and stretching his paws like it's the best thing ever, we all know that it's only second to meeting you. He will do best in a home with adults who are familiar with feline body language and signs of overstimulation. He is a sweet, high-energy, affectionate and silly boy who is just waiting for his chance at a home.

252869.name: Riley
252869.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Riley is on the At Risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display challenging behavior during interactions and touch sensitivity. She is extremely intelligent and high energy, and needs to expend energy constructively with interactive play sessions 3-4X/day. In addition to playtime, this cat would also benefit from mental exercise from activities such as puzzle toys/games, lick mats, or clicker training. Without providing activity for her mind and body, the cat may react with rough play, potentially resulting in bite/scratch incidents. It is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with feline body language, overstimulation, rough play, and who have the time to invest in managing these behaviors on a consistent basis to avoid bite/scratch incidents.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
Riley appreciates some attention and petting but has been highly fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents and would do best in an adult-only and single-pet home, unless potential adopters are significantly experienced in cat-to-cat interactions and appropriate decompression periods.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!

A volunteer writes: Tilly has the love of ten cats! Maybe even twenty cats! But he wants to be your only cat. Tilly is a calm and loving senior gentleman who finds himself in the shelter looking for a fresh start with a forever family. Tilly has approached shelter life with an open mind and heartfelt hope that someone will notice his dreams and his efforts and then be inclined to offer him a little chance. The Care Center is notably different from a home and we know that we may not get to see all the sides of his sparkly personality, but we heard that in his previous home Tilly enjoyed being held and was generally curious about others. He was feeling a bit under the weather when I went to visit him, but still he poked his head up to say hi and offer his friendship, his heart, and hope that his forever family will come and see him soon.

252905.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Motif is on the at risk list for medical concerns. Motif is a senior cat with dental disease, masses, and significant polydipsia reported by staff. An underlying disease process is suspected, but bloodwork was unremarkable. Clinically, Motif is stable and has a good appetite. Behaviorally, Motif can be a bit spicy during medical handling.

I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am playful and cute!
Motiff tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

I have lived with cats in my previous home.

A volunteer writes: Motif was brought to us when his guardian passed away and while that's enough to break my heart, so is the thoughtful way he continues to put on his brightest face for anyone who happens to be in the room. Motif knows there's a good chance shelter visitors are here looking for kittens, but he knows just as well that seniors like him still have so much love to share. Calling out to me when I walked by his condo, I was instantly charmed by Motif's completely accurate insistence that I had some time for him. I must also commend him for his spirited approach to hosting guests as he tried several times to invite me on a little tour of Adoptions. We've heard that in his previous home, Motif enjoyed wandering around the house and watching TV. He's only waiting for another little chance to do that and love again.

252909.name: Soline
252909.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Soline is on the At Risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center due to requiring more space to stretch his legs and get his energy out. Due to his pent up energy he continues to display challenging behavior during interactions. He is extremely intelligent and high energy, and needs to expend energy constructively with interactive play sessions 3-4X/day. In addition to playtime, this cat would also benefit from mental exercise from activities such as puzzle toys/games, lick mats, or clicker training. Without providing activity for his mind and body, the cat may react with rough play, potentially resulting in bite/scratch incidents. It is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment as quickly as possible and into a stable home, where he can expel his excess energy and ideally settle down some. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with feline body language, overstimulation, rough play, and who have the time to invest in managing these behaviors on a consistent basis to avoid (further) bite/scratch incidents.

Due to prior owner history, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced cat parent home with adults only who are committed to following the behavior modification plan outlined in the GAN as well as the suggestions listed in the recommended behavior flyers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I love to play and will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.

A volunteer writes: We don't know if Soline is a cat or a prairie dog, but we do know he doesn't want to be in his condo and tries everything he can to say as much. His protests are duly noted, but we've been trying to explain that it's merely a step in the process of finding a forever home. Soline was brought to us with notes detailing an independent kitty who likes to have as many options as possible when it comes to activities. This is why we see him sometimes trying to look out the window like a little prairie dog and sometimes why he politely tried to push past my arm and out to the Adoptions floor. While Soline's a fellow who could really use options and choices, he's also known to happily greet his loved ones at the door and lean in for pets.

252914.name: Lil Leo
252914.summary:
As a part of OG's Starting Five, I will receive a year of free pet food from Royal Canin. VCA will also provide one free year of unlimited exams with a CareClub Access Plan.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
My purr motor is always running!
Lil Leo interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience. Adopters should be counseled on large cats and limiting handling in order to make sure they remain comfortable.

A volunteer writes: Lil Leo says if you're going to do it, do it big and do it well. Whatever that means to you, he says it's totally up to interpretation. To Lil Leo this means sleeping like he's on an actual cloud and playing with his toys as innovatively as he can. Standing up on his back legs to hold a pipecleaner feather in his front paws, he kind of looked like an adorable giant prairie dog. This is style though. When he isn't playing with us or entertaining himself Lil Leo stretches out on his bed like he's completely oblivious to everything going on in Adoptions. Lil Leo was brought to us when his guardian passed away, so we don't know much about his life before. We're with him every step of the way as he finds the forever family he's been searching for.

When he isn't playing with us or entertaining himself Lil Leo stretches out on his bed like he's completely oblivious to everything going on in Adoptions. Lil Leo was brought to us when his guardian passed away, so we don't know much about his life before. We're with him every step of the way as he finds the forever family he's been searching for.

252921.name: Flo
252921.summary:
Meet Flo!
Flo came to the shelter after her owner lost housing and could no longer keep her. She was described as friendly and outgoing with people, but also as a sensitive girl who can become anxious and overwhelmed in new or busy environments. Once she feels comfortable, Flo is affectionate, social, and enjoys spending time with her people.

My Ideal Home
Flo is looking for a calm, predictable adult-only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will do best with patient adopters who understand that confidence takes time and who are committed to using positive reinforcement and gentle guidance. A steady routine, quiet environment, and enrichment like sniffy walks and food puzzles will help her feel secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Flo enjoys familiar dog friends but can feel unsure and reactive around unfamiliar dogs. Because of this, she will need slow, careful introductions and is not a candidate for dog parks. With the right match and structure, she may do best as the only pet or with a very compatible, well-managed canine companion.

Good with Kids?
Flo would do best in an adult-only home while she builds confidence and continues working through her anxiety and handling sensitivities.

Things to Know
Flo is a thoughtful, sensitive dog who does best when the world feels predictable and calm. She may need time to warm up in new situations and can become overwhelmed by noise or fast movement. She has shown some anxiety and sensitivity around handling and change, but she also shows many positive qualities once she feels safe, including affection, engagement with her handler, and a willingness to connect. With patience, structure, and reward-based training, Flo has great potential to blossom into a steady and loving companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: I'm taken by Flo the moment I meet her. She has the affect of a reserved wise elder, despite being only 3 years old, and everyone is friend. When she's not quietly snoozing, she's always happy to greet a visitor at her kennel, and on walks she's very engaged: checking in, making eye contact, sitting once she realizes a treat is coming her way, and calmly observing her environment. Her former guardian had wonderful things to say about her too, describing her as friendly and outgoing with people. Flo lived with another dog and is said to be playful around familiar dogs but nervous and reactive toward unfamiliar ones. Flo's story is a heartbreaking one. She arrived at the shelter when her person was fleeing a tumultuous situation and subsequently became homeless; the shelter did not allow pets. While they were hoping to reunite with Flo, ultimately they were unable to. She was clearly very loved by her former guardian, and we hope someone can honor their bond and provide her with the continued loving care she deserves. At the shelter, she's been social and affectionate with handlers. Her former guardian notes that she's scared of loud noises and fast-moving objects like skateboards, but she's shown a brave face in the shelter environment. Due to her anxiety and some handling sensitivities, she is recommended to an adult-only home. Flo is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is making wonderful progress every single day. She is working on leave it, a skill that is helping her build focus and self-control in any situation. With positive reinforcement and consistent practice, Flo is growing into a more attentive and confident pup with every session.

252940.name: Koba
252940.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Koba (formerly Ruffle)! Renamed Koba from Planet of the Apes due to his spicy personality.
Some cats disappear into closets. Some cats observe from afar. Koba has absolutely no interest in any of that.
This boy is the opposite of a spirit cat. If you stand up, he stands up. If you fold laundry, he supervises. If you brush your teeth, he's conducting quality control. If you sit down... congratulations, you have become furniture.
With his striking stripes and spots and a tail that deserves its own SAG card, Koba communicates with his whole body. His tail is expressive, intentional, and occasionally weaponized. Don't take too long scrolling, he has been known to slap phones directly out of hands when he feels neglected, unimpressed, or simply has notes.
He came to the shelter as a stray, but it was obvious pretty quickly that this wasn't a cat who was born for the streets. When he first arrived, he was nervous and unsure of people for a few weeks. These days? Complete reversal. He wants company, closeness, and to know exactly what every member of his household is doing at all times. Maybe life outside taught him that being together is better.
While he's affectionate, sweet, and deeply expressive, he also has a spicy side. He believes in clear communication: if you're doing something he doesn't appreciate, he may deliver a swift "excuse me" bite... or more commonly, a dramatic tail slap to express his concerns.
He currently lives peacefully with a foster dog, and his ideal home is with a person(s) who works from home and needs a supervisor to keep them on task!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

252942.name: Simba
252942.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!


My foster writes: Hakuna Matata! I'm Simba, and while I've spent some time exploring the Pride Lands, I've decided my true kingdom is wherever my humans are.
My dream role? Royal Work-From-Home Companion. I excel at supervising Zoom meetings from a cozy nap spot, providing couch snuggles on demand, and conducting important squeaky-toy inspections during coffee breaks. If you're looking for a loyal member of your pride, I'm your guy.
When I venture beyond Pride Rock, I enjoy greeting humans with a friendly sniff and saving my best kisses for my favorite people. I'm more Rafiki than wildebeest stampede-I prefer calm, peaceful surroundings so I can sleep all day. Sometimes, when I see other dogs that want to play with me, I feel compelled to give them my best lion impression so they know I'd love to play. What can I say? A future king has to make his presence known!

My foster writes:
Hi, I'm Simba, and my favorite place in the world is being by your side. My dream job is a full-time work-from-home coworker, and I take my duties very seriously: napping next to your desk, snuggling next to you on the couch, and proudly squeaking my toys during breaks.
When we're out and about, I love sniffing humans and licking my favorite ones. I'm more of a calm-vibes kind of guy and would love a quieter home (as I am still learning that many humans can live on apartment floors). Sometimes I feel that other dogs on walks want to hear my voice and see me jump so they know I want to play with them.Humans say I am a smarty-paws as I'm crate-trained, already know tricks (sit, down, and paw), and think that bathrooms belong outside. Now all I need is my forever humans. Could that be you?

Searching for a loyal sidekick who never misses a bathroom trip? This sweet boy is happiest being near you and would excel in his dream career as a full-time work-from-home coworker. He is always down to nap next to your desk, snuggle next to you on the couch, or chew on his squeaky toys. Outside, he's friendly with people and incredibly attentive. He thrives in calm. quieter surroundings without too much hustle and bustle and is looking for walks in low dog areas. Simba is also a total smarty-paws, crate-trained and has mastered "sit," "down," and "paw." If you're ready to meet a gentle soul, Simba's your guy!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

252949.name: Sarabi
252949.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older children once I meet them.

Sarabi is standing in the middle of her kennel, immediately approaching the front to greet the assessor with a soft head bunt as they approach. She allows and leans into all petting, raising her back and continuing to head bunt as she is pet. Sarabi calmly walks out of the kennel and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she begins to tail flick. The handler gives her a moment to settle and allows Sarabi to approach before attempting further interaction. She head bunts the assessor's hand and flops over onto her side, initially leaning in firmly to petting on the head and cheeks before turning her head to nip at the assessor's hand without pressure. The interaction is ended to avoid further overstimulation.

Sarabi interacts with the assessor, soliciting and appreciating attention. She may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents familiar with overstimulation. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.
