252963.name: Lebron
252963.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Lebron interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior and be familiar with a new home adjustment period.

A volunteer writes: I must've known Lebron in a different life. He picked his head up from his nap, remembered where he was and thought for a moment. He rolled over to show me his belly and reached his paws out to play through the glass walls. When I went to visit Lebron a little later, he twirled and kneaded, cuddled and purred, so eager for a little love that I nearly cried. While I felt instantly connected to this fluffy cheeked boy, his past is a distressing mystery. He was left in a plastic container in a building lobby with other cats but, after his initial hellos where he takes a second to orient himself, he's taken to shelter life with the enthusiasm of one who fully recognizes the chance he's been handed. He's so lovely and could really just use one more chance.

252968.name: Mikey
252968.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form
 
Mikey is at risk due to behavioral concerns. While Mikey has been sociable during most interactions: loose bodied, leaning into petting along his body after he has chosen to solicit - he has presented with sensitivity around his neck. Mikey had escalated to growling and snapping during attempts to collar him for a handling assessment and intermittently when clipping leads to return him to the kennel. Medically, Mikey has alopecia, dental disease, pyoderma, and an ear infection. 

Mikey came into the care center as a stray. Mikey has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. Mikey will approach for petting but will quickly become overstimulated. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: As I watch back my videos of Mikey, I hear myself saying "Mikey!" And "You're a good boy" over and over again. I say that a lot at the shelter. One, because it's filled with good boys and good girls. And, two, because sometimes dogs come in that make me think they haven't been told this enough or maybe even ever. Though we have no history for Mikey, we can only infer he falls into the latter group: between the lack of physical care he's had and being brought in by police after roaming Brooklyn alone.  Still, Mikey stays optimistic.  He is loose and wiggly and oh so playful.  In fact, it's so hard to get good video of him because he's a blur of happiness.  He loves toys and seems to TREASURE the fish plushy we have to offer him. No matter what path Mikey's trajectory takes, at least he will know that someone thought he is a VERY GOOD BOY! 

Though Mikey was described as very friendly and outgoing by the police who brought him in, he has shown sensitivity around being collared and leashed. For this reason, he is at risk and available through a New Hope Rescue partner. Medically, he has suspected allergies and alopecia around his eyes for which he is being given apoquel.

252992.name: Willow
252992.summary:
Willow appreciates attention and petting but appears somewhat fearful in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to an adult-only home with experienced cat parents.
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

A volunteer writes: Looking like she's only ever known love and rightfully leaning fully into the belief that what she brings to the table is more than enough, shelter life has come as a bit of a shock to dear Willow who was brought to us when her guardian passed away. In truth, we don't know much about her life before. No one stepped up for her when she needed it most but here's where we come in. We've been trying our best to learn about Willow and she's been (I think) unintentionally adorable as she explains her preferences. Willow loves making choices and big fluffy beds, snuggling into hands when she feels ready and snacks whenever they're offered. Her favorite thing at the moment is her beautiful flower blanket. Welcoming me by enthusiastically twirling into my hand and demonstrating her beautiful blanket, Willow is hoping to find a patient and loving forever family who will love and celebrate all she is.

Willow loves making choices and big fluffy beds, snuggling into hands when she feels ready and snacks whenever they're offered. Her favorite thing at the moment is her beautiful flower blanket. Welcoming me by enthusiastically twirling into my hand and demonstrating her beautiful blanket, Willow is hoping to find a patient and loving forever family who will love and celebrate all she is.

253017.name: Eclipse
253017.summary:
My foster writes: Eclipse wears his name well. Wrapped in a sleek black coat, he can seem like nothing more than a pair of green eyes peeking out from the shadows at first. But behind that is a surprisingly bright and affectionate little guy just waiting to emerge. When he first arrived, he was terrified everything and would freeze the moment anyone peered his way. Week by week, he's been blossoming into a bit of a sunflower. Since then, he's learned that pets are actually pretty awesome-and when the room gets really quiet, you can almost always hear his little purr motor go off and the biscuit machine start running.
Eclipse is as gentle as they come-a quiet and mellow soul who likes to take things slowly and cautiously. He's the type of cat who may be too shy to ask for attention, but once it's offered, he's more than happy to soak it all up. Head scratches, chin rubs, full-body pets down his back-Eclipse isn't picky; if it's affection, it's all fair game for Eclipse once he's comfortable. He's also an absolute fiend for Churu and Temptations treats. Occasionally, he'll still pause mid-snack and look up at you with big cautious eyes as if to ask, "Is this okay?" For someone willing to give him a little patience and understanding, Eclipse is proof that some of the sweetest cats just need a little time to come out of the shadows.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Eclipse tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home.  We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children.

253032.name: Baby Beluga
253032.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Baby Beluga is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Baby Beluga was returned by his previous adopter due to a bite incident. Baby Beluga had snapped at the child moments while they attempted to remove a bone from the wrapper. He escalated to biting and holding onto the adopter's hand when they attempted to take the bone that was still partially in the wrapper. In care, Baby Beluga is loose and wiggly with handlers, readily seeking pets and accepting of treats. But he has mounted their legs after becoming aroused with handling. Medically, Baby Beluga is apparently healthy.

Baby Beluga was initially surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Baby Beluga initially presented as easy to remove from the kennel, readily accepted treats, but would become aroused and mount the staff/handler's legs during handling. During interactions, he would readily seek petting from handlers. Baby Beluga was trially adopted, but returned due to a bite incident while in the adopter's care. He was reported to resource guard a bone and escalated to snapping at the adopter's child who attempted to take the bone due to the wrapper not being fully removed. When the previous adopter attempted, Baby Beluga bit and held onto their hand. The bite did break skin and draw blood, leaving a puncture. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Baby Beluga be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

253062.name: Tommy
253062.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Young Tommy comes from a house counting too many cats but(unlike cats coming from overcrowded houses) he is so well groomed, healthy, shy(but not scared) while welcoming and friendly and well known to his former family as an individual pet. He came with Chystery and more friends are still to arrive at the care center. Tommy starts a bit shy but eases into a very sweet, gentle and affectionate kitty who moves forward for petting, head bunts and purrs. No treats needed. Handsome Tommy knows what to do to be loved...Still as he was quite timid when he first was brought to the care center and is known to his former owner to need time to warm up, Tommy's new family will need to take it slower in order for him to succeed in his new environment. Tommy did very well on his behavior evaluation, is awaiting his neuter and is hoping to meet you today at the Manhattan Care Center.









What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

A volunteer writes: Chistery 253065: every so often while I am volunteering, I meet a cat that I have have a special bond with. Today for me, that was Chistery. When I first came into his kennel, I found him in his box and he seemed a bit timid, not really wanting to come out, so I started to speak to him and pet him on the head. Our connection grew from there and as soon as I would stop petting him, he would poke his head out asking for more. After a bit, he decided he wanted to come out and was more confident so he strode forward asking for pets. I had other cats to visit, however something kept me at his kennel. I really love him as he gave me kisses and pushed his head into my face, rubbing himself against me. Anyone who adopts him will be so so lucky because with a little bit of patience he has so much love to give.

A volunteer writes: The secret to Chistery's heart? Slow introductions and yummy treats. This two-year-old tuxie was relinquished to the Care Center through no fault of his own; his former person said they had too many pets in the house. Fearful and uncertain at first, Chistery began poking his head out of his hidey den to scarf down squeeze-ups. In no time he relaxed and began letting his guard down, engaging his human visitors with slow blinks and pettings. We knew Chistery had it in him to come out of his shell, as his previous owner told us he was friendly and respectful of the adults, kids, and other cats in his former household. Chistery comes from a home, and to a loving home is where we want him to go. Make it happen for this fraidy cat today!

253133.name: Lucky
253133.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Lucky is at risk for behavior reasons. Lucky has a history of multiple bites but shows some inhibition, as the bites have not broken the skin. He requires a slow, considerate approach. He has allowed handling to be taken out on walks and enjoys time outside. Medically, he is apparently healthy.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Lucky is a 20-pound doodle-type dog with a playful personality and a love for the outdoors. He enjoys car rides, bath time, and entertaining himself with empty bottles and cardboard boxes. Lucky knows basic commands, walks nicely on a leash, and is crate trained.

Lucky does have a bite history. While the bites were not severe, he can be uncomfortable with certain handling and will need time to build trust with new people. Because of this, Lucky is looking for an adult-only home with an experienced owner who can provide structure, respect his boundaries, and help him continue to succeed. With patience and understanding, Lucky has the potential to be a rewarding companion.

253141.name: Keke
253141.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Keke is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns in her previous home. In the prior home, Keke was reported to display overarousal and mouthy behavior on walks, including multiple bite-and-release incidents toward her adopter. During one incident, Keke bit the back of the adopter's calf, resulting in a small puncture wound that was self-treated at home. In the care center, Keke has also been observed repeatedly licking the walls of her kennel, deteriorating in the care center. Keke is very social with staff and has a positive history with other dogs in playgroup. Medically, Keke is apparently healthy.

Keke was originally surrendered by her previous owner due to her owner being older and not being able to manage her high energy levels and provide adequate care. Keke has been described as a very high-energy dog who is social and affectionate. She was previously adopted and in the home for 3 weeks before being returned. She was returned due to a multiple bite incident. Keke's previous adopter also described her as a social but very energetic dog. She would become aroused on walks and bite the adopter; only one bite broke skin and drew blood on their calf. Due to these concerns, we recomend for Keke be placed in an adult-only home without cats or smaller animals through a New Hope rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes:Meet Keke...a huge bundle of love and energy packed into a little 37-pound body! Here are some things I've learned about her:
First - she's a total lovebug! She runs up to me when I call her, wiggling and jiggling while soaking up all the pets and attention I shower on her. My favorite is when she gently puts her paws on my arms and snuggles in close as I scratch her back.   

Second - she has A LOT of energy. She's thrilled when I take her to the yard - excitedly zooming around; playing with her toys (oh, how she loves carrying them, batting them around with her paws, and tossing them to herself and racing to catch them before hitting the ground); splashing around in the doggie pool; and playing fetch. And if pigeons happen to be hanging around, she'll chase them too. (Or maybe she's trying to herd them).

Third - Keke is a Cattle Dog - a smart, active, herding breed. She'll thrive with adopters who understand CD behaviors and can provide positive, fear-free guidance as she transitions into adulthood and life as a Cattle Dog in a non-cattle and non-herding world.

In her short 10-month life, this sweet, affectionate puppy has already been bounced between homes and the shelter. She deserves stability, understanding, and a family committed to loving her for life. Let's make her next home her forever home!

253142.name: Mila
253142.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

Meet Mila!

Miss Mila is a pretty little lady looking for a home to call her own. Preferably it would be all her own as she doesn't get along with other animals. She's also recommended for an adult-only home with adopters who understand her boundaries as well as feline behavior & body language. One-on-one, Mila is a sweet girl ready to shower you with her love. So, let her! Come say hi to Mila at SIACC!

A volunteer writes: Tucked into her cubby, Mila stretched herself into my hands and for a brief moment, the hustle and bustle of Adoptions fell away. She had a whole life before coming to the shelter which is how we've come to learn some sparkly details that aren't always so easy to see in the shelter. Her loving notes are how we know Mila enjoys being picked up and held. A window cat who enjoys being wherever the people are, Mila likes to chase and pounce on toys, even fetching items like bottle caps and toys. A playful and affectionate kitty, she's hoping for the chance to be your one and only.

253165.name: Nora
253165.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am FIV+ and am enjoying a healthy, full life!
What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!

Meet Nora!

With her all-white coat, Nora is a striking beauty. Her pictures make her look like an elegant queen sitting on her royal throne, but, in reality she's more of a lazy couch potato who once in a while likes to play with crinkle toys and take a nice stretch break on some vertical scratching posts. She's happy to lay on a window sill all day or next to you on the couch while you complete your next Netflix marathon. Her previous owner noted that she wasn't a fan of her feline sibling, so she might enjoy living in a single-cat household. If her chill vibes fit your laid-back lifestyle, come say hey to Nora at SIACC!

A volunteer writes: Nora has one of the most generous interpretations of Care Center life. Sitting at the front of her condo and gazing out at Adoptions like it's merely a favorite window, she looked like she was quietly enjoying the show as she waited her turn for pets and Nora really loves pets. She nuzzles and circles with enthusiastic headbunts in between because Nora knows a forever family is just around the corner and it's best to start with her style. Eventually twirling into my hand and leaning into my arm, she's ready to put her best paw forward and find them. Brought to us with other cats, Nora used to love to be where the people were when she wasn't keeping close watch at her windows. Nora's FIV+ and ready to live a full and happy life with you.

253166.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, June 7 from 11AM - 4PM at Petco Love Adoption Event, Union Square Park, 201 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Meet Rumi!
Rumi is a cheerful little Jack Russell Terrier mix with a zest for life and enough personality to fill a room. This young girl is friendly, social, and always ready to make new friends. Whether she's greeting you with a wagging tail, hopping over for attention, or eagerly joining you on an adventure, Rumi approaches life with enthusiasm and a joyful spirit.

My Ideal Home
Rumi is looking for an active home that can keep up with her bright mind and playful energy. Like many terriers, she enjoys being involved in whatever her people are doing and thrives when given opportunities for exercise, enrichment, and companionship. Daily walks, playtime, training games, and interactive toys will help keep this clever girl happy and engaged.

Personality
Rumi quickly wins people over with her friendly nature. Staff describe her as highly social, loose-bodied, and wiggly when meeting new people. She enjoys affection, happily approaches handlers for attention, and has consistently been easy to interact with throughout her stay. If you're looking for a dog who enjoys being part of the action, Rumi may be your perfect match.

Behavior Notes
Rumi has been assessed as a Behavior Level 1 dog, making her a great fit for many types of homes. She is social, easy to handle, enjoys meeting people, and has shown friendly behavior throughout her time at ACC. While her full history remains unknown, she has demonstrated excellent sociability and adaptability in the shelter environment.

Exercise & Enrichment
As a young terrier mix, Rumi will benefit from regular physical exercise and mental stimulation. She enjoys exploring her surroundings and would likely love activities such as puzzle toys, scent games, training sessions, and neighborhood walks. Keeping her mind busy will help her thrive.

Overall Health
Rumi is spayed, microchipped, vaccinated, and ready to go home. During her spay surgery, a non-reducible umbilical hernia was successfully repaired. She has recovered well and is currently in good health.

Why You'll Love Her
Rumi combines the best qualities of a terrier: smart, affectionate, playful, and endlessly entertaining. She's the kind of dog who will happily join you on adventures during the day and curl up nearby when it's time to relax. If you're looking for a fun-sized companion with a big heart and an even bigger personality, Rumi is ready to meet you.

253170.name: Lucy
253170.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am FIV+ and am enjoying a healthy, full life!
My purr motor is always running!

Meet Lucy!

It only takes a few minutes being in her presence before you find yourself saying "I Love Lucy!" This pretty girl is a sweet, gentle cat who has experience living with other cats and children. She's happy to lay on a windowsill watching the world pass by or snuggle up next to you on the couch for a nice, long nap. She's not crazy about treats, but give her some toys to play with and she'll be pleased as punch. Looking for a new feline companion? Come say hi to Lucy at SIACC today!

A volunteer writes: Carrying her favored paper balls to people and asking to be pet are just part of what makes Lucy so adorable. Shelter life has been a big change for her, but she does her best to stay involved. Sitting proudly at the front of her cubby, Lucy was busy welcoming everyone to Adoptions and directing all subsequent traffic, but her exemplary manners take precedence. Welcoming me by lowering her head just a tiny bit, Lucy's known to enjoy some pets but was a little too busy at the moment to accept any from me. She's said to be friendly and outgoing with children, cats, and dogs. Her previous family explained that she's a smart cat who isn't looking to bother anyone, but she sure hopes you'll give her a little chance. Lucy is FIV+ and ready for a full and happy life with you.

253185.name: Yuki
253185.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Yuki is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Yuki's owner stated, Yuki will lunge, bare his teeth, and snap at small animals. While in the Care Centers, Yuki has generally been a social dog who enjoys attention and petting; however, he has recently begun exhibiting deteriorating behavioral concerns. Staff have observed him spinning repeatedly both inside and outside of his kennel. At times, he will also jump very high, reaching as high as staff members' heads. Despite our best efforts to support him, Yuki appears to be struggling with the kennel environment. Medically, Yuki is apparently healthy.

Yuki arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. His previous owner states that he will lunge, bare teeth, snap, growl, hard bark, or attempt to bite when seeing skateboards or small animals. While in care, Yuki has been observed to be highly rope reactive. This behavior is not easily redirected. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

253202.name: Lowkey  Mischief
253202.summary:
Meet Lowkey Mischief!
Don't let the name fool you. Lowkey Mischief is a sweet, affectionate boy who absolutely loves spending time with his favorite people. Surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, he's now searching for a fresh start with someone who will appreciate his playful spirit and help him continue building confidence. He's eager to learn, loves treats, and is happiest when he's interacting with the people he trusts.

My Ideal Home
Lowkey Mischief is looking for an active, patient adopter who enjoys training and can provide plenty of physical exercise and mental enrichment. He's a smart, energetic dog who responds well to positive reinforcement and is already showing how eager he is to learn. With consistency and encouragement, he'll continue growing into an amazing companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Lowkey's history with other dogs is limited, and he's shown mixed reactions while at the shelter. Slow, carefully managed introductions will be important with any future canine companions. He also enjoys chasing small animals on walks, so adopters should be prepared to continue working on his focus using reward-based training.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful behavior and tendency to become easily overexcited, ACC recommends an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Lowkey Mischief is a very active, playful dog who thrives when he has an outlet for his energy. Puzzle toys, food-dispensing toys, training games, long walks, and enrichment activities will all help keep his mind busy. He is mostly house-trained, may have an occasional excitement pee, and would benefit from a family that can continue helping him build confidence through patience and positive reinforcement.

Staff Notes
A staff member writes:
"Lowkey Mischief is a sweet, affectionate boy who loves spending time with his people. He greets familiar faces with a wagging tail, enjoys treats and pets, and is eager to learn, happily engaging in training games and checking in with his handler on walks. He's looking for a patient adopter who can continue building his confidence and help him blossom into the wonderful companion he's already proving to be."

253211.name: Jake The Dog
253211.summary:
My foster writes: This handsome boy is the perfect mix of affectionate, playful, and well-mannered. He absolutely loves being around people and is always ready to make a new friend wherever he goes. Whether it's cuddle time on the couch or bedtime snuggles, he'll happily curl up right beside you - especially if he gets to share the bed.
He's house trained, walks great on a leash with no pulling, and is very food motivated which makes him eager to learn and easy to bond with. He loves to play and enjoys meeting kids, though doesn't know his own strength supervision with younger children is recommended while he's having fun.
If you're looking for a loyal companion who will shower you with love and happily be your shadow, this sweet boy is ready to find his forever home

Meet Jake the Dog!
Jake the Dog was found in someone's backyard and is now looking for a home where he can settle in and feel secure. He's a friendly, people-focused boy who enjoys attention and leans in for affection once he's comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Jake would do well in a home that can offer gentle structure, patience, and positive reinforcement. He can be a bit neck-shy, so a calm, thoughtful approach to handling will help him feel more comfortable and confident.

Good with Other Pets?
Jake has shown interest in other dogs and can be curious and social in his interactions, though he may become a bit aroused or intense at times. Slow, supervised introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Unknown at this time. Slow introductions and supervision are recommended while Jake continues to settle and show more of his personality.

Things to Know
Jake is a social and affectionate dog who readily approaches handlers and enjoys being near people. He can be enthusiastic and may jump up for attention, but he responds well to gentle redirection and handling. While he enjoys interaction, he may also show some arousal around other dogs and benefits from calm structure and consistent guidance. With time and continued positive reinforcement, Jake has great potential to thrive as a loving companion.

Fun Fact
Like his namesake, Jake the Dog is all heart, friendly, goofy, and always ready to make a new friend.

253212.name: Harlow
253212.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
 Harlow tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: It certainly isn't my intention to judge a book, or in this case a cat, by their cover but I think Harlow might actually prefer it that way. Pretending to sleep under his blanket fort as he's decidedly uninterested in venturing out, Harlow has struggled to find his place here at the shelter and I can't say I really blame him. He's a senior who was brought to us with other cats when they were found alone in an apartment. Since we don't have much information to go by and he hasn't been so interested in our attempts to offer treats and toys, we've tried the blanket fort route in hopes it will bring some comfort. Adding some places to hide may not be the most conducive to making friends, but it gives Harlow the space to make his own decisions on when to interact. He's hoping to find a family who will permit him the same space and is waiting to meet you.

Hillary appreciates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed as she adjust to new environments. Once comfortable she seems to be unstoppable. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home until she is comfortable enough to show off her silly and energetic senior lady personality. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Hillary may be intimidated by children, and would do best in an adult-only home where she can spend her decompression period in a calm and quiet area.

253233.name: Diamond
253233.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

A volunteer writes: Diamond is the ultimate gem. We heard about her through another volunteer before we met her and she lives up to every last bite of the hype. Diamond is loose, wiggly, goofy and a total love. She plops into our lap easily, not wanting much else from us other than a bit of love. When she does take a break from snuggles to play, she puts her whole body into it, flopping around having the most fun.

Diamond was living in a shelter with her owner when she was hospitalized. Her community rallied around her, and the program director and social worker both tried with ACC to reunite Diamond with her owner. Unfortunately the circumstances did not work out, but that means YOU are the lucky one - you can adopt this absolute icon of a girl. Diamond is 5 years old, is available for level 2 adopters.

253244.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Dale is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Upon arrival Dale was highly fearful, observed to be trembling in kennel and reluctant to approach handlers. With time, Dale has shown some improvements. During a recent handling assessment he was noted to approach handlers with coaxing and accept contact with a neutral body. Unfortunately, Dale still remains fearful. When on walks Dale is noted to easily startle with loud sounds or become frantic in hallways of the shelter; darting away. When outside of the shelter environment in a quiet area Dale has been noted to warm up to staff, leaning in for contact with a soft body. Medically, Dale is apparently healthy.

Dale arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. During his stay in the care center Dale has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to have a tense body, tucked tail, and urinated during intake when handlers interacted with him. Recently Dale has warmed up to select handlers and begun taking treats. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

253264.name: Blaze
253264.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Blaze is at risk for behavior reasons. Blaze is a young dog with high energy. He is deteriorating in care, becoming increasingly mouthy with pressure during socialization. Blaze has resource guarding with food and toys. He is food motivated and responds well with treats, loves to play. Medically, he is apparently healthy. 

Meet Blaze! This handsome 10-month-old boy is full of potential and ready to find a family to call his own. Blaze is an alert, intelligent dog who enjoys learning and already knows several basic cues, including sit, stay, wait, slow, and no. His previous owner described him as eager to learn and ready for training, making him a great candidate for someone interested in continuing his education and helping him reach his full potential.

As a young dog, Blaze loves staying active and enjoys running, playing with rope toys, and relaxing with his favorite people after a day of fun. He is looking for an adopter who can provide him with regular exercise, enrichment, and consistent guidance.

Blaze's previous owner reported some resource guarding around food and toys. Because of this, we recommend a home with no children under the age of 13 and adopters who are committed to using positive reinforcement training and appropriate management techniques. With structure, patience, and understanding, Blaze has the potential to be a wonderful companion.

If you're looking for a smart, energetic young dog who is eager to learn and grow alongside you, Blaze may be the perfect match!
253264.summaryHtml:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Blaze is at risk for behavior reasons. Blaze is a young dog with high energy. He is deteriorating in care, becoming increasingly mouthy with pressure during socialization. Blaze has resource guarding with food and toys. He is food motivated and responds well with treats, loves to play. Medically, he is apparently healthy. Meet Blaze! This handsome 10-month-old boy is full of potential and ready to find a family to call his own. Blaze is an alert, intelligent dog who enjoys learning and already knows several basic cues, including sit, stay, wait, slow, and no. His previous owner described him as eager to learn and ready for training, making him a great candidate for someone interested in continuing his education and helping him reach his full potential. As a young dog, Blaze loves staying active and enjoys running, playing with rope toys, and relaxing with his favorite people after a day of fun. He is looking for an adopter who can provide him with regular exercise, enrichment, and consistent guidance. Blaze's previous owner reported some resource guarding around food and toys. Because of this, we recommend a home with no children under the age of 13 and adopters who are committed to using positive reinforcement training and appropriate management techniques. With structure, patience, and understanding, Blaze has the potential to be a wonderful companion. If you're looking for a smart, energetic young dog who is eager to learn and grow alongside you, Blaze may be the perfect match!

253267.name: Puddin Pie
253267.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Puddin Pie interacts with the observer and appreciates attention, but she has consistently shown signs of over stimulation, at this time appearing to show consistent warning signs. Her behavior remains suitable adopters with a significant level of experience, provided the adopter is aware of these behaviors, is given appropriate counseling on over stimulation, and is able to comfortably manage them. She is also known to display carrier aversion and will require further training to become comfortable with getting into a carrier. She would do best in an adult-only home.
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

A volunteer writes: Puddin Pie is very much a places to go, people to meet kind of cat. I opened her condo to learn she keeps a tight schedule and isn't particularly keen on diversions. Well, unless she sees a bird at the window, or hears another kitty chirping, or someone walks by the door. Come to think of it, diversions and distractions are kind of her thing but they never detract from her main purpose, which is finding a forever family. Puddin Pie was initially brought to us due to moving issues and has found herself here a second time. She's still trying to figure out how to make the shelter work for her and, in all fairness, it can be a lot sometimes. Puddin Pie's hoping to find a patient and loving forever family and maybe that's you.

253271.name: Zucchini
253271.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

A volunteer writes: Looking like a picture of confidence, Zucchini was brought to us back in April when he was good naturedly trying to invite himself into a building. Self-rescue may be a choice that doesn't always go as planned, but we commend his efforts and, for what it's worth, Zucchini might have been prepared for that possibility given how he's tried to settle into shelter life. Shelter life isn't for everyone, but curled up in her bed with paws stretched out big and wide, Zucchini looks like he greets the day like it was made for him. This is easier said than done. Zucchini was curious when I extended my hand in friendship and for pets, but hopped onto his condo shelf when he remembered that it wasn't what he wanted at the moment. Zucchini spent some time in a home, which is how we know he'd prefer to be your only pet at the moment. He's waiting for a second chance at the Queens Care Center.

253273.name: Georgie
253273.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?
I am playful and cute!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

253279.name: Bella
253279.summary:
Meet Bella!

Bella is an active, playful, and affectionate German Shepherd who loves tug toys, chasing toys, treats, and spending time with her people. She knows sit, stay, and down, walks well on a leash with very little pulling, and enjoys having access to a yard.

Bella is very anxious in the shelter and often whines, pants, and paces during socialization. Her previous owners describe her as friendly and social, so she may simply need time and patience to adjust to a new home. While she is crate trained, she does not do well when confined and struggles with getting into the car. With a patient adopter and a consistent routine, Bella has the potential to be a loyal and loving companion.

253284.name: Flamenco
253284.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Flamenco is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association and appears likely to be under socialized. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Flamenco tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.
 	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

A volunteer writes: Flamenco was brought to us with a great deal of love and care but without much information. We don't know his favorite treats or toys and we don't know if he prefers watching squirrels or birds from his favorite window perches but in spite of our sincerest efforts, Flamenco hasn't felt much like filling in the gaps. We do know, however, that Flamenco's been picking up the pieces as he tries to navigate the shelter. He was brought to us from a home with many other cats and these substantial changes have left Flamenco a bit confused and unsure on where to put all of his love, but it has to go somewhere. We're thinking with a patient and loving family, he'll explain who he is and become the cat he's meant to be.

253291.name: Milady
253291.summary:
Meet Milady!
Milady came to the shelter after her owner could no longer care for her, and she is now ready to find a loving forever home. She is a sweet, social girl with a medium energy level who enjoys spending time with people and being part of daily life.

My Ideal Home
Milady would do well in a home that can offer gentle structure, consistency, and positive reinforcement. She may be a bit unsure in new environments at first, but she warms up with patience and thrives when given time to adjust at her own pace. Treats, play, and calm guidance help her build confidence and shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Milady has shown generally social behavior with other dogs, including neutral to friendly greetings. As with any new home, introductions to other pets should be slow and thoughtful to ensure everyone feels comfortable.

Good with Kids?
Due to some fearfulness seen in care, Milady would do best in a home without young children.

Things to Know
Milady is an affectionate, people-oriented dog who loves treats, playtime, and being included in everyday activities. She enjoys walks, engages well with her handler, and responds beautifully to positive reinforcement. She may show some nervousness in unfamiliar situations or around fast-moving stimuli, but with reassurance and structure, she settles in well and shows her sweet, social personality. Milady is ready to bring joy, cuddles, and plenty of tail wags to her next home.

253318.name: Nagini
253318.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I am really treat motivated. You can use treats to teach me new things!
My favorite pastime is being visually admired! Pet me with your eyes!

A volunteer writes: Nagini barely wanted to lift his head from his box even though having once been or having once felt unwanted can't possibly define anyone. He has a story that I can't quite seem to wrap my head around, but it explains a little bit about why opening up presents a challenge. Someone admitted to tossing Nagini from a window and readily offered him to the Good Samaritan who found him shivering next to the building. They brought him to us where a safe space has been elusive though not impossible. When he hears kind voices speaking to his neighbors, Nagini cautiously ventures out to see if he can join only to remember that he isn't quite there yet. He will be one day and we hope you'll be the one to give him a chance.

253323.name: Cattleya
253323.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.Pre-Screener Form

Cattleya is at-risk due to behavioral concerns. Cattleya arrived at the Care Center as a stray. Upon arrival Cattleya quickly warmed up to staff, allowing all handling for her medical exam and handling assessment. Unfortunately, Cattleya has been observed to be selective toward dogs and has shown potential for defensive aggression towards people. In one instance Cattleya attempted to lunge and snap at a staff member after initially presenting a social posture. With handlers Cattleya remains an easy walk, is treat receptive, and allows contact. Medically, Cattleya is noted to have Dental Disease and Otitis Chronic.

Cattleya has displayed concerning levels of fearful and defensive aggression during her stay at the care centers. While on a walk Cattleya was approached by a staff member and became tense before lunging and snapping at them. We recommend placement with a New Hope rescue partner who is able to provide an experienced, adult-only foster home. Force-free, reward based training and/or consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended.

253347.name: Oz
253347.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

My temporary foster writes:
Oz is the sweetest boy ever! He needs someone patient for his sweet personality to shine through. He's a lovable boy who loves his treats and pets. He's great walking on his leash and is not very interested in other dogs or people. He would be great in a house with a calm vibe so he can chill and cuddle with you.


A volunteer writes: "He's very affectionate, not aggressive at all" are notes from Oz's guardian, who had only wonderful things to say about him.

If you ask me, Oz is the perfect age of 8. (Though I'm shocked to learn his age: He looks so puppylike!) After spending most of his life in the comforts of a home filled with people who loved him - his guardian noted he liked to be where the people are - Oz understandably is a little unsure about why he's suddenly living in a pop-up crate in a room amongst a dozen other dogs. When I first meet him, he's conflicted about leaving his crate, and hides in the back trying to make himself as small as possible.) With some gentle coaxing, tasty treats and baby talk, I'm able to convince him that I'm safe, and we enjoy a lovely walk together, where he continues to open up and show glimpses of his personality. 

Over the last few weeks, he's gotten noticeably braver, collecting many volunteer fans along the way. One says: "Oz is so incredibly sweet. I sat with him for a bit earning his trust, and it was well worth it. The dog in the back of his crate with big ears and a soulful face opened up beautifully when I leashed him and we went for a walk. He was bouncy, super responsive and focused on me, and showed off his extra floppy tongue. He walked so incredibly well! Matching my pace the whole time, checking in with me - he was such a joy to walk. We went to a play yard and he just wanted cuddles and affection."

Oz was surrendered due to his guardian suffering from health issues. In his previous home he lived with three adults and two children. He's said to be friendly with familiar dogs and to avoid unfamiliar dogs; his guardian also said he was tolerant of cats. He's extremely housetrained, crate-trained, and ready to spend the rest of his years with a forever family.

253370.name: Lucious
253370.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!

A volunteer writes: Rolling herself out of her condo and into my arms is Lucious's polite way of demonstrating that arms are actually little cat hammocks or at least they could be if anyone held theirs out to her. She's a senior kitty who knows she has to work a little harder to stand out, so she's been working on some ideas. Mainly her rolls. Lucious rolls so emphatically and I could be convinced that she's made of jello, but this isn't what's most notable. What stands out to me is the way Lucious looks around and hopes someone is watching her do this, that someone is watching her try because she's so sure that if they do, they'll take a chance on her. Lucious was brought to us after not being denied entry into new housing with her previous guardian. Her previous guardian only had positive things to say about her. She enjoyed playing and sitting at the window when she wasn't following her family around. Lucious is only waiting for another chance.

253371.name: Brown Sugar Pancake
253371.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Brown Sugar Pancake has made excellent improvement since his first assessment. When working with the volunteer, he came forward and enjoyed petting, and when the assessor went to see him again, he was on top of the den, ate squeeze-up treats, and allowed petting on the head, cheek, and along the back. He was then slowly coaxed down and all the way forward, eating more squeeze-up and enjoying more petting. He was then picked up and struggled a bit, but when set back down, remained reasonably calm and came back for more treats and petting.

Brown Sugar Pancake interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior but should be counseled on carrier aversion.

A volunteer writes: Brown Sugar Pancake was wandering around a building hallway for four whole days on his own. No one claimed this sweet and trusting little guy so he was brought to us where he's been figuring things out with his characteristic charm and curiosity. When I first introduced myself to Brown Sugar Pancake, he was napping on top of his den and while he was a little surprised at first, I could practically see the way he gathered up his courage in his little kitty paws and took a big breath, only to swirl himself into my arms. This is kind of his style. He's intrigued by our toys and especially interested in our laser shows but what Brown Sugar Pancake seems to enjoy most are the pets. Stretching out a paw to knead, he snuggled and gently explained that he doesn't always know what to make of the shelter, but he always wants to try because he knows his whole hearted attempts will bring him that much closer to you.

253374.name: Mina
253374.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Mina is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Mina has displayed resource guarding, including snapping at people who approached while she had a long-lasting chew, and during her behavioral assessment she hovered over and repeatedly guarded a toy. Mina also displays high arousal, including jumping, hard barking, and difficulty settling, and has snapped during leash removal. Mina responds well to training and enrichment, is social with familiar handlers, and is able to re-engage with food and toys after redirection. Medically, Mina is apparently healthy.

Meet Mina!
Mina came to us as a stray, so much of her past remains a mystery. What we do know is that outside of her kennel she's an affectionate, people-loving dog who wants nothing more than to be close to her favorite humans. She can be energetic and excitable, but beneath that enthusiasm is a sweet cuddlebug who loves leaning into pets and soaking up attention.

My Ideal Home
Mina is looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who can help her continue building confidence and good manners through positive reinforcement. She thrives with regular exercise, enrichment, and training games that encourage her to focus and settle. A predictable routine and patient guidance will help her channel her energy into becoming the wonderful companion we know she can be.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 years old. Mina can become overstimulated when excited and has shown resource guarding behaviors, making an adult-only home the best fit for her.

Good with Other Pets?
Mina has participated in several dog introductions at the care center and has generally shown appropriate social skills, choosing to disengage when interactions become too intense. Because of her history of resource guarding, any introductions to resident pets should be slow and carefully managed, with resources kept separate.

Overall Health
Healthy overall.

Behavior Determination
Level 4 - Experienced Adopters. Mina has shown resource guarding with high-value items, excitement-related jumping, and barrier frustration in the shelter. She has made excellent progress with training, enjoys learning through positive reinforcement, and responds well to enrichment such as snuffle mats and focus games. She will thrive with adopters who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence and impulse control in a home environment.

Other Fun Facts
Mina is a volunteer favorite for a reason! Outside of her kennel, she's an affectionate "lap dog" who loves cuddling, leaning into people for pets, and exploring the world with her nose. She enjoys sniffy walks, training games, and will happily check in with her person for treats and affection. One volunteer said that if they adopted her, her official name would be "Mina Cuddlebug"-and after spending time with her, it's easy to see why!

A volunteer writes: Mina is SO SO sweet and a total lap dog! In fact, every time I take her out, if we aren't taking a walk, she's plopped herself onto my legs smothering me as best she can. She's a dog that is completely opposite of her kennel presence (at times jumping up and down, even throwing herself against the door) outside.  When you adopt her, her official government name should be Mina Cuddlebug ________ (your last name). 

In the early morning of the last day of April, Mina was tied to the fence of a neighbor that recognized her from the block.  They said her name was Nina. Since, she's been living in a kennel. Due to some general anxiety and handling sensitivity displayed in the shelter, Mina is recommended to a home with kids over the age of 13.  She has done well in multiple dog greets in the shelter.

253377.summary:
My foster writes: If you're looking for a salamander dark chocolate graham cracker in the form of a four legged fur creature that will cuddle you to no end, sit down for treats, signal you when he has to poop and potty, stare at you lovingly no matter what you're doing, lay out in the sun in the park, and sit by the bathroom door until you're done using it, you have found him, his name is Brunson, but I've been calling him Triple B, which stands for Baby Boy Brunson, because he is exactly that, a baby boy. He has gained so much confidence on his walks, so much so the point where he wants to greet every dog, person, and leaf that blows his direction to say hello.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

253378.name: Roxie
253378.summary:
Meet Roxie!
Roxie is a sweet, active girl who is looking for a fresh start after being surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her. She enjoys exploring her surroundings, loves being close to people she trusts, and has a playful spirit that's just waiting to shine in the right home. With patience and encouragement, Roxie has all the makings of a wonderful companion.

My Ideal Home
Roxie would love an active home that can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive, reward-based training. Food puzzles, long-lasting chews, games, and daily adventures will help keep both her body and mind engaged. She'll do best with someone who understands that building confidence takes time and is happy to let her settle in at her own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
Roxie previously lived with other dogs and has been described as friendly and outgoing. At the shelter she's shown that she may feel more comfortable taking introductions slowly and often prefers staying close to familiar people. ACC also recommends a home without cats.

Good with Kids?
Due to her fearful behavior, ACC recommends a home without children under 13 years old.

Things to Know
Roxie is an energetic dog who enjoys staying busy. Her previous owner shared that she can pull on leash and may become anxious when left alone, so continued positive reinforcement training will help her build confidence and good habits. Once she forms a bond, Roxie clearly enjoys being close to her favorite people and will thrive with a patient adopter who can provide consistency, reassurance, and lots of love.

253409.name: Winter
253409.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Winter is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Winter has begun warming up since his arrival in the Care Center, and while a little bit fearful and wary, he now allows petting under some conditions. He hissed when first approached with treats on the scratcher tool, but then sniffed them and began eating them, and then allowed petting with the tool. On a second approach, he hissed again, but this time sniffed the treats in the assessor's hand and began eating them and allowed petting on his head. He needs time to continue warming up.

Winter tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

253411.name: Prince
253411.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Prince and his ten housemates lost their owner.....They were not happy campers when they arrived at the care center. Their lives were up side down.. A roller coaster of untoward changes... Prince and some of his housemates are slowly making peace with their new settings and starting to breathe better. Every single of these kitties are beautiful, majestic with semi long hair and fluffy cheeks. Prince is now trusting and not only comfortable but happy with his encounters with staff and volunteers. I enjoy every bit of my "sessions" with Prince, his beauty, his sweetness and his appreciation to be loved. Prince is a "lover" and he will be a wonderful and loyal friend if you choose to adopt him and take him home. Still, Prince went through hard times and will likely will need some time to warm up to his new life. Time, patience and empathy are the keys to success....

5/26/26 Prince had made excellent improvement since his first assessment and was lying asleep in the kennel. He woke up when the assessor went in, came forward, and allowed and enjoyed all petting on his head, cheek, and along his back. He didn't overstimulate and enjoyed squeeze up treats, and then enjoyed more petting before being picked up, where he was held in the assessor's arms while remaining calm. When set back down, he remained curious, sweet, and calm and ate more treats and allowed more petting.

Prince interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior. Some experience is preferred due to history of being upset when he first came in.

253412.name: Pugee
253412.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Pugee and his ten housemates lost their owner. Their past life is a complete mystery. The little group was quite upset upon arrival at the care center...and for days. We understand...Nothing, no one looked the same...Pugee laid alone in his kennel, frightened by everything and everyone around. Time does its job as well as the care of staff and volunteers who are so familiar with pets ' distress. Pujee is slowly emerging from a deep and scary well. He is quiet in his kennel, lays low but in his main area, returns slow blinks and accepts  caresses on his head and scratches on his neck and gigantic cheeks. He reminds me a little of a chipmunk greedy for nuts...Day after day, Pugee makes progress and we are mighty proud of him. Staff added his still very wary housemate PJ to his large kennel. Hopefully, PJ will follow in Pujee's footsteps. Pujee wants to go home and may be it could be with you! Still, he will need time, patience and understanding to set him for success in his new home. Ask about Pujee when you come to the care center!

253414.name: Summer
253414.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet your dose of Summer sunshine! Summer is a stunning brown tabby with an adorable white necklace, striking green eyes, speckled fur, well done eyeliner, and the cutest pink toe beans. She also makes a perfectly toasted loaf! If you're lucky, you may even see her approach you with the cutest headbutts. She is very independent and loves being admired from afar like the princess she is. Food and safety is the best gift you can give her. Of course, a lady never stoops as low as to beg or dig through the trash; she has standards you know! Summer is moderately vocal, making the most adorable high-pitched chirps, trills, and meows. While initially skeptical, Summer now enjoys hunting her cat wands and puts on a spectacular show. She often does a silly thing where she has a toy in her mouth and still tries to vocalize through it, as if showing off her catch.
Despite her name, Summer isn't the hugest fan of the heat. She has been shedding, but is a total sweetheart tolerating a daily brush of her coat. While Summer can be a bit shy and timid on the outside, but she's a fierce predator inside. She's caught several pesky fruit flies already, so if you need an exterminator look no further! Around other cats, Summer is respectful but otherwise unbothered and mildly interested. She came from a situation with 10 cats, so she has proper kitty manners.
As summertime approaches the end, Summer hopes to find her new home before her season concludes. Will you give her to chance she deserves?

Hi this is Summer! She's a bit shy at first, but a total sweetheart! Food is the key to her heart! Summer might be afraid to ask, but she greatly appreciates pets when given. She's a chatty gal, greeting you with the cutest chirps and trills. Summer likes to spend her day lounging around basking in the sun and her nights curled up on your bed guarding your feet. Speaking of feet, Summer has the cutest speckled paws with pink toes and black paw pads.
Summer is a cat's cat, she loves feline company! She grew up around a lot of other cats and is in foster with another kitty named Midnight (in black, also up for adoption). Wherever one goes, the other is sure to follow. Summer gets along very well with other cats, understanding how to share food and respects boundaries. In fact, they may get along a little too well, scheming some kitty mischief!
Please, can you help Summer find a home this summer?

253415.name: Coco
253415.summary:
My foster writes: Coco is an inquisitive cat who loves exploring, peering out the window, and inspecting all your cardboard boxes. Coco also continues to grow her people skills; she offers the tiniest meow during treat time to request you drop it quickly and she loafs next to you while you're both lounging. Coco enjoys playtime with wand toys but she'll happily sleep when you're working during the day. Coco will do well in a forever home that can continue to socialize her to the wonders of the large hairless cats (a.k.a. humans).

My foster writes: Coco is a shy but curious cat that loves to explore and play! She is also very cute and has inquisitive eyes! Even the first night fostering her, she was already cuddling with me on the bed, while keeping a distance of course. It might take some time for her to get used to you petting her (maybe a week or so) as she is a very independent one, but know that it's just her finding out more about who you are in an unfamiliar environment. I hope she finds a great forever home!!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Coco is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appears somewhat wary of human contact. She has made a small amount of progress with daily interactions with behavior staff in shelter. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

253416.name: Midnight
253416.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Midnight! At first glance, she's a pitch black void but on closer inspection you'll find the smallest patch of white on her chest (3 hairs!). Amidst the void emerges high beams that stare into your soul--a magical mix of yellow, orange, and green. Midnight is a shy girl at first, but when she gets comfortable she'll meow her demands. However, she's a reasonable lady who knows when you're busy, opting instead to perch by the window or loaf on your bed. She expects the same respect from you, sometimes she doesn't want to be bothered! Midnight keeps great care of her fur and has no problem using her litter box. She respects your furniture and prefers her manicure on dedicated scratching boards. She has a distinguished taste, refusing most non-fishy treats; a lady has her standards!
Midnight enjoys catching wand toys with her adorable little paws. She may pretend to not care, but after a little bit her curiosity gets the best of her and she comes running over. She can be lazy, laying on her back and scooting her body instead of the hard work of getting up. Sometimes she's so entranced that she'll slip off the edge, promise her you didn't see! Midnight adores gentle pets, going as far as standing up on her tip toes for more. Go slow and steady, please don't startle her! But even if you do scare her, Midnight prefers to keep her claws to herself and walks away so you can reflect on your actions. Like many cats, she'll occasionally communicate with a gentle nibble for play or a claw-free swat when she's had enough.
Midnight is looking for someone who appreciates both independence and affection. Will you be the light of Midnight's life?

253417.name: China
253417.summary:
My foster writes: China is a tiny 5-pound girl with a lot of personality. She has a little bit of spunk to her and definitely knows what she likes.
She is great about using her litter box and has been really good in the home. She uses her cardboard scratcher and so far has not bothered or scratched anything else. She likes having her own space sometimes and will go off to find a quiet sleeping spot, but she is always very happy to see you when you come into the room.
China loves back scratches in moderation!
She is also very chatty. She loves chirping, vocalizing, and making sure you know she is around. She is not especially food motivated outside of dinner time, but she still likes being near you and keeping you company.
She has been a really cute, funny little companion to have around. She is independent without being too distant, affectionate on her own terms, and has a lot of personality packed into a very small cat.

My Boroughbreaker writes: On my #BoroughBreak we walked to Central Park and made a lot of friends! We walked to the Conservatory Gardens and talked to a lot of people who were interested in meeting Nova Star. They thought she was so sweet and friendly! We took a break in a shady area before walking to a Mr. Softee truck for a scoop of ice cream that me and Nova shared :) It was such a pleasure to spend the day with her and get to introduce her to some friendly people!

A Volunteer Wrote: Our hearts are aching for this beautiful, intelligent, wonderful German Shepherd girl who is stuck in a pop up crate, wondering why she is no longer in a loving home. Her former owner describes her as friendly and outgoing (she's the same with dogs!) but also anxious, and here in the shelter volunteers are seeing that side of her with a dose of sad. Who could blame her? Still, she remains so gentle and sweet, so grateful for a walk and a gentle hand and company. We wish we could give it to her more than a walk here or there, and reassure her that she is loved and will be again, forever. Please, come meet Nova Star!

253449.name: Mr. George
253449.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with older children in my previous home, and most likely would do best at this time in an adult-only home. However I could be open to respectful children over the age of 13-years-old
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.
Mr. George appreciates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will likely be a cat that will require patience, an extended decompression period, and interactions led by him and moving at his pace in order to respect his boundaries, and allow him to fully warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Mr. George may be intimidated by small children and would likely do best in an adult-only home.

253458.name: Korra
253458.summary:
My foster writes:

Korra is a sweet cat who likes to tell you how she's feeling. She'll come nap by your side and will let you know when she wants to cuddle. She'll play with toys and will bring them to you. She likes sitting by the window and seeing what's going on outside.

Another Foster writes:
Art pop is a super cute and cuddly cat, loves attention and all types of cuddles, she enjoys playing with toys a lot as well and will bring toys to your lap to make it obvious. She loves to hangout right next to you when doing anything and doesn't get scared easy even if small groups our around.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Art Pop was in the main kennel, appearing curious with large pupils, walking around and coming forward, and then allowed and enjoyed petting on the cheek and along the back. She tolerated a brief pick-up, though she struggled with the assessor and hissed once and tried to swat once afterward but then recovered. She's reported to have hissed and swatted on other occasions, but we're hopeful that she will improve, especially after she no longer has kittens to attend to.

Art Pop interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in arousal and pick up.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I can go home today!
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!

253468.name: Cypher
253468.summary:
A volunteer writes:
One year old Cypher comes from a house full of countless cats. No wonder he arrived without any information telling us about him. Cypher has his own personality, though and it is for us and his new family to discover who he really is. Right now, like most kitties coming from overcrowded environments, Cypher is very shy and even fearful. He sits at the back of his cubby, behind his litter box in the hope to pass incognito...Until yesterday(5/12), I was not really able to pet him with my hand, he cried and occasionally gave a little hiss, making himself smaller than he already is. Today, although still shy and very hesitant to "let go" of his fears, after quite a bit of time spent with him, Cypher started to slightly leaning into pets, even dropped briefly on his kennel floor, sometimes cried and went back and forth between being scared and a tiny bit bold. I think there is hope for Cypher, in caring, loving and experienced hands and in a low traffic home. Cypher deserves to be all what he can be which is I know, more than being a scared little mouse. Come and meet sweet Cypher at the Manhattan Care Center.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

Cypher has made excellent improvement since his first assessment and, while remaining a little skittish and slightly high-energy, he is curious, treat-motivated, and allows petting on his head and along his back. He can be a little reluctant to be petted, but he loves treats and will allow petting while he is eating. He will also come out from under the main shelf for treats but can't quite be coaxed down, even though he seems to want to come down. He was skittish during a pick-up attempt but is a sweet and friendly cat who is learning to adjust well.

Cypher accepts attention and petting but appears to be slightly nervous in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in nervous cat behavior.
