253945.name: Exabyte
253945.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Exabyte is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

Exabyte is an otherworldly beauty with shimmering silver-blue fur and striking emerald eyes that look like they were carved from a glowing geode. 💚✨ With his angular features and intense gaze, he looks a little bit like an alien visitor - in the very best way possible.

Right now, Exabyte is deeply misunderstood. Shelter life has been overwhelming for him, and he does not yet feel comfortable with petting or handling. But beneath his wary exterior is a sensitive cat who deserves the chance to decompress in a calm, low-traffic environment with a patient and compassionate person.

Exabyte is seeking rescue placement with someone who understands that trust can take time, and that quiet companionship can be just as meaningful as constant affection. With stability, kindness, and space to feel safe, this extraordinary boy has every chance to thrive.

For the right rescue or adopter, Exabyte won't just be a cat - he'll be a once-in-a-lifetime companion. 🛸🐾

A volunteer writes: Exabyte came right out to greet me like we were already so late and on an airtight schedule, but then he very relatably seemed to decide this wasn't the schedule he wanted to be on. We know shelter life isn't his style and Exabyte's progress at the Care Center reflects a hard won team effort, but we also know we've been asking a lot from this little guy. Exabyte's looking for a family who will welcome him for exactly who he is. He's a social fellow who likes to be invited even if he prefers participating on his own terms - think tall scratching posts to observe his world from afar. Pets, scritches, and cuddles haven't been Exabyte's thing at the shelter, and they might not be at all, but he's hopeful that someone will see the other things he likes to do and give him a chance. Exabyte's hoping to be your one and only, so please come and meet him at Queens Care Center.

Meet Kori!

Kori is a handsome three-year-old black and white cat who's looking for the perfect home. Shelter life is no easy thing for a cat and Kori has understandably been fearful while here. With the right environment and the right people, Kori has the potential to decompress and show how he's the loving, affectionate, chatty cat that his previous owners reported him to be. He would appreciate an adopter who is patient and has a good grasp of feline behavior and body language, hopefully a compassionate person who can put themselves in Kori's paws and meet him where he's at, preferably with a tube of tuna squeeze-up in hand. If that person is you, come to SIACC to say hello to Kori!

253984.name: Lucky
253984.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Lucky is such a pleasure to spend time with... A handsome and tall light color tiger he is with oven-mittens paws(additional toes). He comes right away to his door to salute me, head bunts, purrs and leans into pets. He is such a gentle soul, so well mannered and sweet. I would not mind staying longer with him and enjoy his soothing presence. Lucky was surrendered as his owner passed away. A relative took him in but did not really have time for a pet anymore. Lucky is also on on special diet for a sensitive stomach and has a positive result for FIV on a SNAP test(a condition that can be discussed with you with the adoption counselors if you are interested in adopting Lucky). He is said to be a very sweet, affectionate, quiet and kind cat who plays gently with all. I am not too crazy about the name Lucky but it is his name and we should make sure that Lucky's next chapter is true to his name. Lucky is already neutered and aced his behavior evaluation. He could go home today as your forever best friend...

253988.name: Kingston
253988.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Kingston is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Kingston has been highly social with staff and handlers in care, leaning into petting, engaging with toys, snuffle mats, and enrichment games in calmer settings. But he recently has begun to leash bite when being removed from the kennel and is kennel fighting with other dogs as he is walked out of the room, which has made taking him for walks challenging. On one occasion, Kingston did redirect onto a staff member's leg, nipping them. Due to this, he was returned to his kennel, and his walk was not completed due to his behavior. Medically, Kingston has an ear infection.

Kingston was surrendered into care due to his previous owner not having enough time or the financial means to provide care for him. His previous family described him as a social and affectionate dog who can alternate between being very playful or a lazy couch potato. He loves getting into cars but is not a fan of bathtime. Kingston's favorite treats are peanut butter, beef treats, and watermelon. Kingston has been social with handlers and staff during his stay in care but does have a history of guarding toys and treats, separation anxiety, and reactivity to other dogs on and off leash. Kingston has displayed leash biting behaviors when being removed from his kennel and kennel fights with other dogs once he is removed from his kennel. On one occasion, Kingston did redirect onto a staff member's leg, nipping them. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Kingston be placed in an adult-only home where he can be the only dog through a New Hope rescue partner. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Kingston presents with outside of the care centers.

A volunteer writes: Kingston came to the shelter for the same reason as many - a guardian who could no longer afford him. At 6 years old, I'm sure shelter life is a rude awakening, but like many dogs he's taking his new reality in stride.

I'm quickly enamored with him. His pointed ears and good spirits lift mine. He is thrilled to play, but even more thrilled to wiggle about for butt scratches. His former guardian actually reported butt scratches, cuddles, and watermelon among his favorite things! I love his middle aged temperament- just the right amount of energy for most homes.

Kingston is reported to be friendly with familiar dogs but reactive to unfamiliar ones, and friendly with strangers and kids. He's earned a level 2 behavior rating and is available to most homes with a little experience and no very young kids. Meet his perfect guy today at Queens ACC.

253992.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Garlic Knot is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I can go home today!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

Garlic Knot is not open to interaction at this time and does not currently tolerate petting or handling and is really struggling in the shelter environment. Because this cat previously lived in a home for some time even though without a known history, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, home with adopters who are willing to work with a cat who needs time and patience to help him adjust to their new home.  

A volunteer writes: Garlic Knot came to us hungry. Left behind in an apartment with other cats, he had an appetite and we hoped the food, treats, and snacks we happily and readily offered would help us to get started on the right paw. Since that initial meeting, however, we haven't been able to get as far as we would like in getting to know Garlic Knot. Snuggled in the back of his cubby, he isn't one to come out and say hello. In fact, it seems like he often wishes we'd just continue walking by. We don't have much information about Garlic Knot's life before and we don't know who he wants to be in the future but we know he wants to belong to a family who will claim him as their own.

253998.name: Cici
253998.summary: Meet the queen of Queens Free Roaming Room! Through daily visits, lots of treats and respecting her boundaries, the Feline Behavior Team has been able to build a relationship of trust with her that allows her to seek out petting, purr and choose to be near familiar humans. She is still at times cautious, independent and prefers contact on her own terms, however she has proven that in a quiet and patient environment, she can make a gentle, calm and affectionate companion to her person. It will be important for her new family to understand this trust may take time, as it took several weeks of gentle socialization sessions without touch for her to gain that trust and confidence. Once you win her over and are blessed with her affection, it is the most special feeling in the world. She went from a shut down, fearful girl to a social, snuggly and funny resident at ACC who waits by the door for her favorite human friends. She has come so far. Now all she needs is for her family to find her.
253998.summaryHtml: Meet the queen of Queens Free Roaming Room! Through daily visits, lots of treats and respecting her boundaries, the Feline Behavior Team has been able to build a relationship of trust with her that allows her to seek out petting, purr and choose to be near familiar humans. She is still at times cautious, independent and prefers contact on her own terms, however she has proven that in a quiet and patient environment, she can make a gentle, calm and affectionate companion to her person. It will be important for her new family to understand this trust may take time, as it took several weeks of gentle socialization sessions without touch for her to gain that trust and confidence. Once you win her over and are blessed with her affection, it is the most special feeling in the world. She went from a shut down, fearful girl to a social, snuggly and funny resident at ACC who waits by the door for her favorite human friends. She has come so far. Now all she needs is for her family to find her.

254007.name: Ella
254007.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Ella is not open to interaction at this time and does not currently tolerate petting or handling. Because her previous owner reports she interacts on her times but enjoys spending time in the room where people are in a home environment, we believe the behavior seen in the care center is shelter-specific and this cat would make a great pet but is really struggling in the shelter environment. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, home with adopters who are willing to work with a cat who needs time and patience to help her adjust to their new home.

A volunteer writes: Resting a paw on a catnip mouse while eating her snacks is very adorable and also speaks volumes about Ella's communication style which are often as clear as her beautiful stripes. We know shelter life isn't quite the speed Ella prefers, but all of our follow up questions to see what we can do to improve have been met with requests for treats and not much else. Ella was brought to us due to her previous guardian's health and while she hasn't been as forthcoming as we'd hoped, we've heard she's a curious cat who likes to do her own thing except when it comes to being a cat nurse when her loved ones are sick. Following them around in her sincerest attempts to take care of them as best she could, Ella's now looking for someone to maybe take care of her too.

254011.name: Mia
254011.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Mia interacts with the observer and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting, but she has a tendency to play rough, and has a very high energy level. We recommend that she go to a home with adopters with a moderate level of cat experience preferred and be well counseled in her history of sporadic incidents of pouncing on and stalking legs, ankles, and feet. Her behavior remains suitable for an adopter with an average amount of experience, provided the adopter is aware of these behaviors and is able to comfortably manage them- committing to a consistent feeding and play schedule and behavior modification plan to mange her energy levels and play needs. Though we believe this cat is displaying behaviors appropriate for moderately experienced cat parents, she may not be a great fit for young children, and due to her history of stalking legs, feet, and ankles, may be most appropriate for an Adult-Only home. There may be potential for her to do well in a home with respectful older children understanding of her needs and high energy level. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
Playtime is essential! I love climbing tall cat trees and having fun with interactive toys!
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!
I love to play and will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.

254025.name: Sticky Notes
254025.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Sticky Notes is just a little kitten at six months of age. She was left behind with her three housemates in an empty apartment after her owner died. Sticky Notes was quite scared when I first met her, although never aggressive, just "frozen" at the back of her cubby. Time did its work as well as the efforts of staff and volunteers and although still a bit timid to start with, Sticky Notes just behaves now like a silly kitten. She loves her cuddles, stretches and rolls on her cubby floor and takes silly poses. I am so happy that she finally came out of her shell. Still, the little gal went through hard times and her new owner or family should take it slowly with her and give her the time to fall on her four in her new home. Sticky Notes is dreaming to be yours and is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Sticky Notes tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

254033.name: Mateo
254033.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

My foster writes: Mateo has been such a loyal, goofy shadow in the house! He loves to be near his people, whether that means following you to the bathroom, snoozing at your feet while you work, or doing his adorable "army crawl" to say hello first thing in the morning. When he is totally relaxed, he sleeps in a full "galloping horse" pose with occasional paw twitches showing he's running around with you up to new adventures, that is guaranteed to make you smile.
In the home, we've learned that Mateo is a sensitive, smart guy who thrives on routine and structure. Because he can get overstimulated by the hustle and bustle of big city living, he would absolutely love a quieter neighborhood or a home where he can truly decompress. But outside, he takes it all in stride! He is wonderfully non-reactive to the nitty-gritty noises of the city as he stomps down the streets.
Mateo knows his basic cues (sit, down, paw) and is quickly learning many more. He is looking for a patient, dog-savvy leader who will give him clear boundaries, help him practice impulse control, and guide him in finding his "off-switch." If you want a devoted, adventure-ready companion who will reward your patience with endless loyalty, Mateo is waiting for you!

My foster writes: Mateo is such a sweet dog! Ready to be your new best friend, he's always up for a cuddle, a long walk, some play time, or a tasty treat to gnaw on. Mateo does love car rides, watching the world go by with his head out the window, and loves to meet all creatures; dogs, and humans alike, with his tail often wagging, excited to make new friends. Mateo is a great leash walker, with hardly any pulling and knows the commands "sit" and "stay". Mateo also doesn't mind being left alone - although he'd rather be with his humans, he can be alone at home without showing any anxiety issues. Mateo is also well (but not perfectly) house trained. Although he still has the personality of a puppy at times in the way he loves to be playful with humans and dogs, he also can behave like a gentleman, staying in a calm and non-reactive state, even in the hustle and bustle of NYC.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am playful and cute!

A volunteer writes: Meeting Mateo is like a shot of dopamine directly to your veins. It's been awhile since I've been in the presence of such pure, unbridled joy. In the play yard we are delighted by Mateo's tossing of a toy in the air and his impressive leaps back and forth over the bench . 

Little do we know the best is yet to come: we turn on the hose and invite Mateo over to the pool and Mateo goes from happy boy to absolutely ecstatic pupperino.

He dashes in and out of pool and gives the hose stream his best chomps. We are grinning watching him and I wonder why scientists haven't looked into bottling the experience of hanging out with Mateo. It could certainly solve most if not all a person's woes. 

Mateo was dropped at a police precinct by his owner when they said they couldn't care for him anymore. The officer dropping Mateo at the shelter noted he was friendly and easily took a car ride (we guess he might have asked for the sirens on but cannot confirm). At the shelter he has been loose and wiggly with all handling and sociable and excited with other dogs. 

He's waiting for you at Manhattan ACC, joyfullness included.

254045.name: Champion
254045.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Champion is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Champion is intensely fearful in the care center, including retreating from the leash, seeking exits, and attempting to create distance from handlers. He has also been reported to snap toward a handler's hand during leash clipping when being returned. Champion will ignore unfamiliar staff and likes to be pet and seeks comfort at times, but is struggling to acclimate in the care center. Medically, Champion has CIRDC.

Champion entered the care center as an owner surrender due to his owner becoming homeless. His owner described him as social and affectionate, very active and playful, yet also quiet and a bit of a couch potato. Since arriving at the care center, Champion has shown a high level of FAS (fear, anxiety, and stress), allowing only minimal handling and exhibiting thrashing behavior when placed on leash and taken out for walks.We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

254047.name: Rain
254047.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Rain is at-risk due to behavior concerns. She was reportedly found tied up with another dog, and they were fighting one another. The intensity of the delivered bites is unknown. Rain is social with handlers, but easily becomes hyperaroused. She jumps up repeatedly towards handlers with an open mouth. Rain has been observed to grab at staff/handlers' shirts, pants, and treat pouches. On one occasion, she knocked treats out of a handler's pouch, but she did not take them due to her arousal. When passing another hadnler that moves out of the pathway, Rain attempts to jump on them, mouth open. This behavior has continued to intensify throughout her stay. Medically, Rain is recovering from wounds.

Rain was surrendered into care as a stray, so her history in a home environment is unknown. Rain was reported to have been tied up with another dog, and both dogs began an altercation, resulting in several wounds to various parts of Rain's body; the other dog is unknown. Rain has been wiggly and social with handlers and staff throughout her stay. But as her length of stay progressed, she has begun to jump up on handlers, grabbing clothing and treat pouches. Due to these concerns, we recommend that she be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can address these concerns with the use of a certified professional trainer that uses only positive reinforcement methods. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am playful and cute!
I will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.

254052.name: Puma
254052.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Puma is a friendly, affectionate girl with a heart as big as her adorable, pouty face. Found as a stray, she has quickly shown her sweet nature, being gentle and welcoming with everyone she meets-staff, volunteers, and visitors alike. While she can be a little anxious in care, her loving personality shines through once she feels safe and comfortable.

At this time, we recommend Puma be the only dog in her new home so she can settle in confidently and thrive with her human family. Puma is looking for someone patient and kind, ready to give her the love, reassurance, and attention she deserves. She's full of potential to be a loyal, loving companion to the right person.

On my #BoroughBreak, we...
We played in the backyard, watched some tv on the couch, and took a nap on the couch. Puma loved relaxing inside on the comfy couch and loved sniffing around in the backyard. She also loved getting treats and knew exactly where they were.

My Boroughbreaker writes: I'd describe Puma as a diamond in the rough. She is incredibly sweet, loving, and affectionate, and once she gets comfortable with you, her personality really starts to shine. She has a very endearing way about her and clearly enjoys being around people.
Puma is still figuring some things out and would benefit from a little training,, but I don't think that takes away from what a special dog she is. She has so much potential and seems like the kind of dog who will really blossom once she feels secure and knows what to expect.
She also appears to be housebroken, which was a nice surprise. During our time together, she did very well and seemed to understand that outside was the place to go.
One of my favorite things about Puma was how loving she was. After our walk and some time outside, she was happy to relax and spend time together. She seemed just as content hanging out with me as she was exploring, which made our movie time especially sweet.
Overall, Puma was a wonderful companion for the day. She has a lot of love to give and a really sweet personality that I think will only become more apparent as she gets comfortable

254054.name: Mangu
254054.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Mangu is at risk due to behavior concerns. In his previous home, Mangu had a bite incident. Mangu lunged and snapped at the resident child's forearm, grazing his skin, after Mangu growled at the child that was near his bone. Mangu takes treats from staff and has just started to open up. Soliciting attention and showing interest in toys outside. Mangu is apparently healthy.

Mangu came into the queen care center as a stray the finder had him for a week and wanted to keep him but due to a bite incident towards their child in the home he brought him to QACC. Mangu has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: Mangu was found on the lower east side, hiding in fear in the park. Her finder kept him until she could no longer care for him, at which point he was brought to ACC. Mangu has been understandably nervous with all his life changes recently, but is a gentle, sweet boy. He is calm, but doesn't take much interest in treats right now, but when he gets a toy his whole face lights up. Mangu zooms and jumps, and clearly toys are the way to his heart. He is a beautiful dark brindle, and has one light eye and one chocolately brown one. Mangu is about a year old. He is available for rescues only

254060.name: Chickpea
254060.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Chickpea is on the At Risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display challenging behavior during interactions. She is extremely intelligent and high energy, and needs to expend energy constructively with interactive play sessions 3-4X/day. In addition to playtime, this cat would also benefit from mental exercise from activities such as puzzle toys/games, lick mats, or clicker training. 254134.name: Pugsley
254134.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Pugsley is a cat of a luxurious size, a statuesque and beautiful tiger with a tender, quiet and loving personality. Pugsley was found in a Good Samaritan's backyard and brought to the Manhattan Care Center for us to find him a family. He is often seen resting in his den. Open his door and he will come right out and walk majestically toward you. He is not effusive, does not come on the lap but stays very close to his visitor, looking at them, purring softly, head bunting gently their hand and finally laying by their side. Try a feather wand. Pugsley's eyes will light up. He will stand on his hinds and paw the dancing feather. I like the way he sticks his forelegs through his gate to call us back to the interaction room where he resides because of his majestic size. Pugsley was brought to the care center in the arms of his finder. He slipped and while trying to prevent himself to fall, scratched superficially his savior. That could happen with any good and great cat. Pugsley is a lovely big and beautiful feline who dreams to be in a real home. He is already neutered, is apparently healthy, did very well on his behavior evaluation and could go home today with you.








What my friends at ACC say about me:
Pugsley is at the front of the kennel, leaning his body against the kennel bars to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he leans forward to softly head bunt the assessor's hand. Pugsley allows and leans into all petting, raising his back as he is pet. He walks out of the kennel calmly and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm, purring, and leaning against the assessor as he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front and continues to attempt to leave the kennel to be closer to the assessor. He is able to be easily maneuvered back each time, continuing to allow and lean into all petting and purr as he is pet. Pugsley does display some piloerection at the base of his tail throughout the interaction but was not observed to escalate even with extended handling. When the kennel door is closed and the interaction is ended, Pugsley gently paws outside of the kennel to solicit further attention.

Pugsley interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

254135.name: Jack
254135.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!


Meet Jack!
Jack is a handsome, affectionate pup looking for an experienced family who can help him continue building confidence and learning new skills. While Jack has had some big changes in his life recently, he has shown that he is a friendly guy who enjoys spending time with people and exploring the world around him. With patience, structure, and positive reinforcement, Jack is ready to find a home where he can thrive.

My Ideal Home
Jack would do best with an experienced adopter who understands canine body language and is committed to helping him practice calm behaviors. He is an active dog who will benefit from daily exercise, enrichment, and reward-based training. A predictable routine and patient approach will help Jack feel comfortable and set him up for success.

Good with Other Pets?
Jack has shown some interest in other dogs and has had positive moments meeting canine friends. However, he can become tense and fixate on dogs while on leash, so continued training and slow introductions will help him have successful interactions. A front-clip harness and positive reinforcement training can help him focus on his person during walks.

Good with Kids?
Due to Jack's tendency to become over-aroused and mouthy during exciting situations, an adult-only home is recommended. He would do best with someone who can recognize his communication signals and help him stay calm before he becomes overwhelmed.

Things to Know
Jack is a sweet dog who enjoys affection, but he prefers interactions on his own terms and appreciates slow introductions. His previous family reported that he can become overexcited and mouthy, especially during high-stress situations like grooming, so he will need continued work on impulse control and calm handling. Jack has shown that he can be a wonderful companion, and a patient adopter willing to help him succeed will have a loyal friend by their side. 

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Jack is perfect as far as we're concerned! He's gorgeous, kind, and friendly to everyone he meets. During outings, Jack has shown his gentle nature, calmly handling distractions and enjoying time with his people. He walks nicely on leash, appears housetrained, and is even a champion cuddler who loves sharing a bench with his favorite humans. Jack has so much love to give and is hoping someone will give him the chance to show them just how special he is.

My#BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
Jack was a good boy . He's big but well behaved . He pulls on leash a little but quickly adjusts with redirection . Knows sit and gently takes treats out of your hand . A lovable big strong derp .

254138.name: Gabby
254138.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Gabby is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Gabby arrived at the Care Center as a stray with limited history. Upon intake she was noted to be fearful and reluctant to allow leashing. Over time, Gabby has shown some improvement in sociability. During her recent handling assessment, Gabby did approach staff with a softer body posture, allowed brief petting, and accepted treats. Unfortunately when trying to place a collar on Gabby, she would head whip and become slightly tense. During walks Gabby is observed to become highly social with familiar staff. Medically, Gabby has recently recovered from CIRDC.

Gabby arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care Gabby has been observed to be fearful. Noted to be trembling with a tucked tail and showing whale eye. During her medical exam Gabby was observed to snap at the muzzle. When brought into the assessment room, Gabby was observed to be very avoidant of the handler. She was not receptive to treats, and when the handler approached she would retreat quickly. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

254169.name: Hershey
254169.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Hershey is at risk due to behavioral concerns in the care center. He has shown leash reactivity and kennel fighting toward other dogs, He is also noted to react to dogs in nearby kennels and pop-up crates. On walks when seeing other dogs he will hard pull on leash with a tense body, causing himself to choke and salivate. During walks, handlers use treats and toys for redirection, but he does not always respond to them. With handlers, Hershey displays social behavior, maintaining a loose body and leaning into petting. Medically Hershey is apparently healthy. 

Hershey arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. He has shown leash reactivity and kennel fighting toward other dogs, He is also noted to react to dogs in nearby kennels and pop-up crates. On walks when seeing other dogs he will hard pull on leash with a tense body, causing himself to choke and salivate. Recently Hershey was reported to jump at a handler's face with an open mouth. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home. 

Meet Hershey!
Hershey is a handsome boy with a big personality and an even bigger heart. He was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now he's searching for a home that can match his enthusiasm for life. He's happiest when he's active, learning new things, and spending time with the people he loves.

My Ideal Home
Hershey would thrive with an experienced adopter who enjoys training and can help channel his energy in positive ways. He'll love an active lifestyle with plenty of walks, enrichment, and games to keep both his body and mind busy. A consistent routine and reward-based training will help him continue building confidence and good manners.

Good with Other Pets?
Hershey has previously lived with both dogs and cats. At the shelter, he can become excited and tense when meeting unfamiliar dogs, so slow introductions are recommended. ACC also recommends avoiding dog parks for now while he continues working on his dog-to-dog social skills.

Good with Kids?
Due to Hershey's excitement level and tendency to become easily overstimulated, ACC recommends a home with no children under 13.

Things to Know
Hershey is a strong, enthusiastic walker who is still working on his leash manners. He can become excited around other dogs and some distractions on walks, but positive, reward-based training can help him build focus and confidence. He's also known to jump up when excited, so continuing to reinforce polite greetings and calm behaviors will set him up for success. Providing plenty of physical exercise, mental enrichment, and appropriate chew toys will help keep this smart boy happy and fulfilled.

Fun Fact
Hershey has lived with both dogs and cats before, and once he's gotten his energy out, he's ready to soak up attention and be your loyal sidekick for whatever adventure comes next.

A volunteer writes: Like her namesake, Mermaidia is a sight to behold: In lieu of flashy iridescent scales is a beautiful merle coat and eyes that sparkle in the sun. But Mermaidia's vibe is anything but flashy. She's a quiet, timid girl who's sometimes hesitant to leave the safety of the crate she's called home since arriving at the shelter - she often needs some gentle coaxing and baby talk. Once she hits the pavement, though, she's happy to walk nicely alongside us and snack on all the treats we have to offer, and she was even lucky enough to go on a Boroughbreak her first week at the shelter. During her outing, this smart girl demonstrated she knew the commands for "sit," "paw," and "down," and was a model citizen. (Her Boroughbreakers described her as sweet, calm, and adorable, and we can't think of three more accurate adjectives.)

Mermaidia was dropped off by an anonymous person at a police station in Brooklyn, and she's estimated to be just a little over a year old. She's been friendly with all of her new friends at the shelter, but has shown some fearfulness of loud noises (and has been especially brave given that she's in a noisy overflow room with a dozen other dogs in crates), though she's getting a little braver every day.

My foster writes: Gingerale is a sweet and kind dog. She would be a joy to have in the home. She had a staycation at my house for three days and adapted quickly. Gingerale will express her love for her people by leaning her body toward you, showing her belly, following you around the house, and by just looking at you. While in the house she didn't have any accidents and enjoyed laying down and taking naps. She can be a little anxious outside and put her attention to everything in the environment so walks in low traffic areas would be best. However, she loves and is friendly to all people. Gingerale loves to watch squirrels and is reactive (non aggressively) to dogs. I think she can be adopted into a home with adults and children and potentially another dog. She also could be adopted into adult only single dog home.

254205.name: Bennie Baby
254205.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Bennie Baby is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and while she is social, she is prone to overstimulation and will swat hard at handlers when approached for interactions. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who are familiar with signs of behavioral arousal and agitation in cats, so that interactions can be ended before becomes overstimulated.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

Initially when the handler approaches, Bennie Baby vocalizes with wide eyes and dilated pupils and swats hard towards the assessor through the kennel door. She is softly spoken to, and she turns to lay in the middle of the kennel, fur displaying piloerection down her back and laying down facing the back wall, engaging in displacement grooming. The assessor gives her time to settle before returning for further interaction. Bennie Baby is standing at the front of the kennel, pupils dilated. She is softly spoken to, and she leans her body against the kennel bars to solicit attention. When the kennel door is opened, she leans forward to head bunt the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting. Pickup is not attempted to avoid potential overstimulation. 

Bennie Baby is a sensitive, social girl who appreciates attention and interactions on her own terms. She appears a bit stressed in the shelter and may need time to warm up to a new home. Due to behaviors observed in the shelter and an observed tendency to overstimulate, an adult only home is recommended.

254217.name: Bua Loi
254217.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Bua Loi is an adorable and petite gal with additional toes, which is quite cute. She is rather charming and welcoming and her company is quite enjoyable. She has a cold right now but it will be soon history. Bua Loi is with us because of a scratching incident. The house dog bursts into her quarters, ate her food and disturbed her litter box. Something that dogs do....Bua Loi did not like this, got scared and scratched the dog and a nearby child. Bua loi was not a happy camper when she arrived at the care center but time did its job. She is a sweet, friendly and sociable gal who most likely would do better in a quiet and low traffic home with no young children or dogs and with a new owner who understands that pets can have boundaries too while being very loving and loyal to their family. Bua Loi is dreaming to be very soon your forever best friend!








What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

254220.name: Tigerlily
254220.summary:
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

Meet Tigerlily!

Tigerlily is a nine-year old tabby but she doesn't look a day over three! This little beauty is a friendly and affectionate girl who likes to hang out with her people and play with interactive toys. She is not shy about expressing herself as she was described as quite vocal in her previous home (she would make a great conversation partner!). Tigerlily is looking for an adopter who is experienced with feline behavior & body language and would prefer being the only cat in the home. If you're a cat-lover looking to give this senior girl the golden years she deserves, come to SIACC and say hi to Tigerlily!

A volunteer writes: Stretched out with her favorite toys, Tigerlily welcomed me with a quick little nuzzle to her crinkle ball and catnip cucumber before leaning into my hand. Stretched out with confidence, Tigerlily leaned into each pet and neck scritch but also explained that the shelter can be a lot, so taking little breaks when she asks can be helpful. Tigerlily was brought to us with glowing notes detailing a cat who loves to play and pounce after toys and water, chit chat about her daily comings and goings, and snuggle with her family. A smart lady, we've heard she will even learn some new tricks for treats. Tigerlily isn't always a fan of other cats, but this very delightful kitty is hoping to get a chance to be your one and only.

254231.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Blanket is a pretty gal dressed in the timeless "little black dress". She comes at once when someone is at her door. She is gentle and welcoming, head bunting with grace my hand and even softly purring. Blanket was found laying on a blankie with food and water in front of an apartment building, I guess for everyone to see and possibly rescue. A dangerous gamble as so may dangers plague stray cats in the streets... Thankfully, a Good Samaritan saved the day and brought sweet Blanket to the Manhattan Care Center. She was underweight, dehydrated  and in dear need of TLC. Blanket is still working on getting a clean bill of health but being in a caring and loving home would certainly speed up the process. Blanket deserves better than a blankie in the street. Ask to meet this little princess with almond eyes, fall in love and take her home!

254233.name: Milo
254233.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Milo is placed on the at risk list for medical reasons. Milo is a geriatric cat with chronic kidney disease. He is also very underweight and has significant dental disease, but has been eating well in shelter and is friendly. Milo will need continued nursing care and veterinary follow-up for his medical issues.

Milo is a handsome senior gentleman with a friendly personality and plenty of love to give. Affectionate, talkative, and independent, he's the kind of cat who enjoys being part of the household without demanding constant attention. You'll usually find him wherever the people are-lounging in the living room, supervising activity in the kitchen, or watching the world go by from his favorite window perch.

Milo enjoys gentle play and especially likes toys that crinkle. He still has a playful side and loves chasing the occasional bug or moth that wanders indoors. When it comes to scratching, he prefers rope, carpeted surfaces, and cardboard scratchers.

A low-maintenance eater, Milo happily enjoys Friskies wet and dry food. As a senior cat, he's looking for a patient adopter who will appreciate his companionship and understand that he may need some extra support. Milo has been reported to scratch furniture and has had occasional litter box accidents, so he may do best with an adopter willing to help him adjust to a new environment and provide appropriate scratching options and litter box management.

If you're looking for a sweet, conversational companion who enjoys sharing your space and keeping you company throughout the day, Milo may be the perfect match.

A volunteer writes: Milo presses his nose into his door and dutifully shares his best ideas and the way he talks leads me to believe he thinks every idea is the best idea. I noticed Milo's little nose and his very expressive curiosity about anything and everything happening in the room, but also admired his resilience and commitment. Milo's a senior guy with some medical concerns but a brightly shining hope that someone will still welcome him. Loudly purring as soon as I extended my hand, Milo tries hard to join in as best as he can and while shelter life isn't always set up for his kind of fun and snuggles, he knows that a forever home will be.

254237.name: Silvester
254237.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Sylvester was in the kennel, facing forward, looking curious and reasonably calm. He reacted to the sound of the treat bag being shaken and sniffed them when offered. He gave a single hiss when approached with the assessor's hand, but allowed petting on his head, cheek, and along his back. He then began eating squeeze-up treats and continued to allow petting while eating, occasionally grumbling. After the treats were finished, he continued to allow petting, and then the kennel door was shut. He went back on top of the den. A pick-up was not attempted.

Silvester interacts with the observer, accepts attention, is fairly easy to handle and tolerates most petting. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in ramping up unexpectedly, and over handling.

Pre-Screener Form

Angel Cake is described by his owner to be friendly, prefers contact on their own terms, he is quiet, lazy/couch potato, and solitary they also mention he has handling sensitivity and is noted to growl, bark and snap. This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Toose is at risk due to behavior concerns. He arrived at the care centers as an owner surrender. His previous owner stated that he will growl and alert bark at strangers, but with time will warm up. In the care centers Toose has not acclimated well. He tolerated handling during his assessment but remained tense. On occasion, Toose has shown some interest in familiar handlers, approaching them for treats with a soft body. However, he has remained fearful throughout the majority of his stay. Noted to enter the training room with a tucked tail, pinned ears, crouched body with a low head, and growling. He is also observed to fixate on handlers hands when returning to his crate, escalating to snapping, hard barking, and growling as handler locks the crate. When moved to a kennel, he continued displaying similar behavior, lunging towards the door, hard barking, and snarling at handler. Recently, Toose has begun leash biting, being able to be redirected with treats but almost catching a handlers hand at one point. Toose has been medically diagnosed with allergies, dermatitis, otitis externa, and a wound.

Toose was surrendered into care due to his family no longer being able to care for him. Toose was described as a medium-energy dog who enjoyed salmon-flavored food and treats. He was very affectionate with his family but was noted to growl at new people/strangers and needs time to warm up. Toose was intially fearful during his intake, but presented as easy to leash for walks. As his stay progressed, Toose has escalated to defensive behaviors when being returned to the kennel - hard barking, growling, snapping, and lunging at handlers - fixating on their hands as they secure him in his kennel. Toose recently has attempted to redirect onto a staff member after returning him to his kennel after his evening walk. Due to these concerns, we reocmmend for Toose to be placed with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home. 

Meet Toose!
Toose is a sweet and sensitive pup who is looking for a patient family that will help him feel safe and comfortable in his new home. After being surrendered when his owners could no longer care for him, Toose is ready for a fresh start with someone who understands that the best relationships are built with trust and time. While he may be a little shy at first, this gentle guy has so much potential to blossom once he knows he is safe.

My Ideal Home
Toose would thrive in a calm, predictable home with adopters who are willing to let him settle in at his own pace. He prefers to make new friends on his own terms and will appreciate a family who understands canine body language and respects his boundaries. With patience, positive reinforcement, and plenty of encouragement, Toose can continue gaining confidence and learning that the world is a safe place.

Good with Other Pets?
Toose's previous owners reported that he ignores other dogs while on walks. His history with dogs in a home environment is unknown, and during shelter interactions he appeared unsure around unfamiliar dogs. Slow, thoughtful introductions would be recommended to help him feel comfortable and successful around new canine friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Toose's fearful nature and his preference for approaching new people at his own pace, a home with adults only is recommended. He would do best with people who can give him the time, space, and gentle guidance he needs to feel secure.

Things to Know
Toose is a quiet, gentle dog who enjoys taking things slowly. He walks nicely on leash and is happy to explore his surroundings at his own pace. His previous family shared that he can become mouthy during play, so continued practice with appropriate play skills and redirection to toys will help him succeed. Toose may bark or growl when unfamiliar people enter his home, but once he has time to warm up, he can become a friendly and loving companion. This sensitive sweetheart is looking for someone who will give him the patience and understanding he deserves.

254282.name: Remy
254282.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Remy is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Remy is a social dog but presents as highly anxious. He has been observed licking and biting his crate bars and will begin to heavy pant and pace in his crate. Outside of the kennel, he is generally social, affiliative, and easily handled, but can become overly aroused around food, jumping up, mouthing handlers without pressure, and seeking treats. Medically, Remy is Underweight.

A Volunteer Wrote: "Wait, that's a GREAT dog," another volunteer said to me about Remy, after hanging out in the pen next to ours in the back with another dog. She had watched Remy play bow at the fence to her dog, and then snuggle with me, and then sit for me, and then take treats so gently...the only surprise is that it took her a few minutes to see this dog is AMAZING!!!!! Other volunteers agree, praising his extraordinary manners on and off the leash and his wonderful desire to give and get affection. It's hurting our hearts that this star is tucked away in a side room in a pop up crate, far from the eyes of adopters. Please, don't miss out on the chance to meet this fabulous boy.

254286.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Sunflower is at risk due to behavioral reasons. While in care, Sunflower has been observed to be highly dog reactive. Noted to pull hard towards other dogs while hard staring at them. This behavior is not easily redirected. During intake Sunflower was noted to push off the walls while reacting to the other dogs in the kennel room. Sunflower has also been reported to be difficult to leash. The handlers needed spray cheese or treats to leash him. During one instance, Sunflower bit the handler on the finger when they were attempting to leash him. While out with handlers, Sunflower is observed to have a loose body. Medically, Sunflower is apparently healthy.

Sunflower arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Sunflower has been observed to be highly dog reactive. Noted to pull hard towards other dogs while hard staring at them. This behavior is not easily redirected. Sunflower has also been reported to be difficult to leash. The handlers need spray cheese or treats to leash him. During one instance, Sunflower bit the handler on the finger when they were attempting to leash him. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home with no trips to the dog park.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

254311.name: Meow 15
254311.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Meow 15 is laying in her den as the assessor approaches, eyes wide, pupils dilated, and body tense. When the kennel door is opened and the den cover is lifted, she backs up further into the den. She is offered crunchy treats and leans forward to sniff them but does not eat them, pulling away again. Meow 15 is tolerant of all petting but does not engage with the attention. She is unable to be coaxed out of the den, so full pickup is unable to be attempted. She is tolerant of light upward pressure applied to her sides and under her chest, remaining tense but without further issue.

Meow 15 tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

254314.name: Meow 55
254314.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Meow55, a handsome and elegant looking tiger came to us with his female twin Meow15 as their owner became physically unable to care for his pets. Nothing is really known about them except that they are acting very shy at the care center. Meow55 is curious and wants to see who opened his door. Treats and gourmet food...He is interested and samples gladly the offerings. There is some slow blinking with encouraging words, acceptance of my finger caressing his nose but petting on the head was not accepted. No hissing and no swatting, though, just backing off. Meow55 is right now very hand shy and needs a bit more time to come out of his shell. He needs at this point a caring and experienced adopter who will give him time and space in a low traffic and quiet home until he finds his bearings. Meow55 is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.







What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Meow 55 tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

A staff member writes: Rogue is a sweet, affectionate girl who has made wonderful progress during her time at ACC. She enjoys leisurely walks with a loose leash, loves learning new things, and has had fun practicing games like "Touch," "Up/Down," and "1-2-3," showing off just how smart and engaged she is. Once she gets to know you, Rogue happily leans in for affection, flashes her adorable smile, and will even rest her paws on your leg to ask for a few more pets.

Rogue is happiest with patient people who appreciate her gentle nature. She has shown interest in other dogs and enjoys observing them, though slow introductions are recommended. If you're looking for a loyal companion who will reward your kindness with endless affection, Rogue is ready to meet you!

254318.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Smiley is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Smiley has not acclimated well to the shelter environment despite efforts to keep him comfortable. While Smiley has made improvements with being leashed for walks, he remains highly stressed and fearful. Smiley has brief bouts of sociable behaviors with handlers in quiet, calmer settings but quickly reverts to tucked tail, heavy panting, pacing, and exit seeking, becoming increasingly frantic as the session progresses. Medically, Smiley has a mass, a grade 2/6 heart murmur, and dental disease.

While in the Care Centers, Smiley displayed significant fear, often thrashing and pancaking during walks. Over time, he became more comfortable with slip leads and began to tolerate some petting, though he remained visibly stressed. His previous owner reported that Smiley is a fearful dog who requires time to become comfortable around unfamiliar people. On walks, he may bark and growl at strangers and small animals. Smiley should be placed through a New Hope Partner in an adult-only home with adopters who are experienced in managing fearful behavior and are committed to using positive reinforcement-based training methods.

254327.name: Hailey
254327.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Hailey is at risk due to behavioral reasons. While in care, Hailey has been observed to be dog reactive and rope reactive. Noted to pull hard towards other dogs while barking. Recently Hailey has begun biting and tugging the leash into kennel. During one instance when a handler was attempting to leash her using a treat, she bit them on the hand. This bite resulted in a puncture wound. With handlers Hailey is receptive to treats. In kennel, Hailey has been observed to show signs of kennel stress. Such as biting and tugging on the water bucket. Medically, Hailey has CIRDC. 

Meet Hailey!

If you're looking for a fun-loving, energetic companion, Hailey may be your perfect match! This very active and playful girl loves spending time with her family and can often be found hanging out in the living room, ready for her next adventure or play session.

Hailey is a well-mannered dog who knows several cues, including "sit," "stay," "yes," and "no." She enjoys daily walks and walks nicely on a leash with very little pulling, making her a pleasant walking partner. She currently enjoys one to two walks each day to help burn off some of her energy.

One of Hailey's favorite things in the world is greeting her people when they come home. Her previous owner loved how excited and happy she gets when she sees her family, and her joyful welcome is sure to brighten anyone's day.

Hailey enjoys treats and toys and is always ready for some fun. She is also comfortable with routine grooming and allows her family to bathe, brush, and trim her nails.

While Hailey no longer needs a crate, she has experience being crated in the past. She can be a little nervous when getting into or riding in the car, so she will benefit from patience and encouragement during car trips.

With her playful personality, loving nature, and enthusiasm for life, Hailey is ready to bring happiness, laughter, and companionship to her forever home.

A volunteer writes: Star is my kind of girl because even though she's busy with her projects, she always has time for friends. 254376.name: Irish Cream
254376.summary:
My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: On our borough break, Irish Cream was an absolute dream-truly one of those dogs you don't forget. With his soft white coat, perfect black spots, and that little black nose and pink jowls... he is ridiculously cute in person. The kind of cute that makes strangers smile.
It was a rainy day, so we spent most of our time at my apartment, but first-car ride test: A+. He was a little nervous at first, but so trusting. He stayed curled at my feet, quietly checking in with me for reassurance, and calmly peeking out the window to watch the world go by.
Out and about, he was unbelievably well-mannered. No pulling, no reacting-just a gentle, steady walk right at my side. Dogs, kids on scooters, sirens... nothing fazed him. He simply looked up at me like, "Am I doing okay?" (Yes, Irish Cream, you're doing perfect.)
At the pet store, he politely picked out some bones and toys and charmed everyone he met. Back home, he curled up next to me on the couch and slept deeply for hours, clearly catching up on rest from kennel life. It felt like he got to exhale a little bit.
When he woke up, his playful side came out-tail wagging, flopping around with his toys, happily entertaining himself. No destruction, no chaos-just a sweet, silly boy enjoying simple things. He also took his role as "window watcher" very seriously, quietly observing the outside world without a single bark (I didn't hear him bark all day!). We did a few walks in the rain and he didn't seem to mind the weather. We also stopped for a pup cup which he gobbled right up.
He loves treats, knows "sit," and is so eager to learn-his adorable head tilts will melt you instantly.
Irish Cream is a gentle, affectionate soul who just wants a soft place to land and someone to look to for comfort. He is an affection loving teddy bear and after spending the day with him, it's so clear-he's going to make someone incredibly lucky.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bruce is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Bruce arrived at MACC following a bite incident in the home. Bruce was reported to have bitten the resident cat, and the cat passed away due to the bite. While in care, Bruce has been observed to be highly anxious and fearful, noted to often be reluctant to re-enter the kennel however a treat trail is effective to coax Bruce back to kennel.  During interactions with staff, Bruce is highly exuberant, solicits contact, engages with tennis balls, and is highly treat motivated. Medically, Bruce is underweight and has a wound. 

Bruce was surrendered to ACC following a bite incident to a resident cat in his previous home.  Bruce's previous owner describe Bruce as a social, hyper, friendly dog.  He would pull excitedly when seeing other dogs on walks.  In shelter, Bruce has been anxious due to the stressful nature of the shelter setting.  He would do best in an adult-only home where he can get his energy out in healthy ways and decompress.

Pre-Screener Form

Bricks is at risk due to behavioral reasons. When Bricks initially arrived at the care center, he was observed to be fearful and would growl at handlers when they approached him while in his crate. Over time Bricks warmed up to handlers and would be at the front of his kennel with a soft body and wagging tail and would jump up on handlers exuberantly. Despite our best efforts at keeping Bricks comfortable while in care, he has begun to show signs of kennel stress. He has been reported to bite the leash when being returned to the kennel, and this behavior is not easily redirected. He is also observed to jump up high in kennel when the room is active. Medically, Bricks is apparently healthy.

Bricks arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. His previous owner describes him as very lovable. While in care, Bricks has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to growl at handlers when they approach to leash him. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Banana Split is at risk due to behavioral concerns.  Banana Split was returned to shelter following a bite incident in the home.  A child in the home was playing tug-of-war with Banana Split.  Banana Split let go of the toy then proceeded to jump on the child knocking them to the ground and bit the child on the lip;  then redirected and bit the adopter on the hand when being pulled away. The bite to the child broke skin however medical attention was not needed. Outside of this incident Banana Split was described as active and playful. In the Care Center Banana Split has been exuberantly social with staff, treat receptive, and has engaged in pattern games. Medically, Banana Split is currently healthy.

Banana Split was recently returned to the care center due to a bite incident that occurred in the home. Banana Split was playing tug of war with the resident 7 year old. He let go and then jumped towards the rope that they were holding and tackled them down to the ground. Banana Split then bit the child on the lip and broke skin. The adopter pulled him off, and he attempted to bite their hand. They then put him in his crate. While closing the door, he attempted to bite again. No medical treatment was sought, but the bite made a small hole on the child's lip. Recently, Banana Split has been observed to circle around the handler and then bite the leash. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

254409.name: Rubio
254409.summary:
My foster writes:
Come meet Rubio, the sweetest little gentleman! Rubio is a calm, low-energy lap cat who loves curling up on your legs, sleeping beside you, and quietly keeping you company throughout the day. He has a shy, sensitive personality and may take a little time to warm up, but once he feels comfortable, he is incredibly affectionate. He loves head scratches, gentle brushing, and being close to his person. He can also be handled easily and does well with nail trims. With his round face, big round eyes, and adorable expression, Rubio is impossible not to love. He is also a very good water drinker and happily drinks from a regular bowl, so no fountain is needed. Rubio would be a wonderful match for someone looking for a peaceful, loving companion to relax and cuddle with.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Rubio appreciates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

254426.name: Jimmy
254426.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Jimmy!
Jimmy was found wandering alone on the street and brought to a local precinct, where he was described as friendly during intake. This handsome boy has been social and people-oriented in care, and he's now looking for a home that can help him channel his enthusiasm into all the right outlets (especially if cheese is involved).

My Ideal Home
Jimmy would do well with an adopter who enjoys an active, playful dog and is ready to continue his training in a fun, positive way. He can get excited quickly and may grab or mouth the leash when amped up, so a home that can provide structure, enrichment, and reward-based training will help him shine. He'll thrive with consistency, clear boundaries, and plenty of engaging activities to keep his mind busy.

Good with Other Pets?
Jimmy has shown polite, neutral interest in another dog at the care center during a supervised introduction. His overall history with other animals is unknown, so slow, thoughtful introductions would be important if living with another pet.

Good with Kids?
Due to some observed guarding behavior around valued items and his tendency to get excited quickly, Jimmy is recommended for a home without children under 13 at this time.

Things to Know
Jimmy is a bright, affectionate boy who loves engagement with his people and especially enjoys toys, play, and tasty rewards (cheese might be his love language). He'll do best with calm guidance and positive reinforcement training. He has shown potential for guarding high-value items, so ongoing trade-up games and teaching cues like "drop it" will help set him up for success. With structure and patience, Jimmy has a great foundation to become a fun and loyal companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Jimmy is a classically handsome boy with a classic name. He waits patiently in his kennel and greets me with a soft, sweet expression that makes it easy to like him right away. Once outside, he lights up during play, especially with a favorite octopus toy he happily brings back over and over, dropping it into my lap to start the game again. He's social and people oriented, and during his time in care he's shown how much he enjoys interaction and enrichment. He also has a very relatable quirk: a strong appreciation for cheese, which may or may not have made a surprise appearance during his assessment. Jimmy is a fun, engaging dog who will shine in a home that can match his energy and continue helping him build good manners through positive reinforcement.

Fun Fact
Jimmy has a playful streak and a big personality hiding behind those sweet eyes, especially if there's a squeaky toy or a snack involved.

My Boroughbreaker writes: He did great on the boroughbreak! He was a bit anxious in the car and was panting and pacing around but he did eventually settle down, especially so when we gave him a chew which he demolished in the car. Once we got outside he got very excited about all the new sounds and smells. He loved being outside and was happy to explore and run around.

254445.name: Missy
254445.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Missy is an adorable and elegant long hair dame who is with us for no fault of her own. Her ailing owners became unable to care for their pet. It is not easy to take a good photo of Missy and she is soooo pretty! The moment I lay eyes on her, she is on the move toward me(or any other visitor for the matter), at once leaning into pets. She is very sociable, affectionate, gentle  and loves to be petted and talked to. Missy is said to be a very sweet lap cat, friendly to all(she was great upon arrival at the care center and with the veterinary team). She would be well mannered and play gently. Missy passed her behavior evaluation with flying colors, appears healthy although a bit too thin, has a normal senior panel and could go home with you today. Come and meet lovely Missy, fall in love and take her home for many years to come!

254490.name: Spanish Rice
254490.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
Hi, my name is Spanish Rice and the shelter has been a little overwhelming for me. I came from a home with many cats, who I've gotten along with well. Because I've lived in this home my entire life and have only been around one person, I have little experience with people and am hesitant of new experiences. I would enjoy living in a quiet home, preferably one with lots of vertical space so I have a place to perch and observe the room. I would also appreciate having experienced, patient adopter(s) who are willing to take things slow with me. I would benefit from socialization, using rewards whenever I make a small positive step like making eye contact, allowing petting, or sniffing your hand. I'd prefer to take things at my own pace and would appreciate some good old fashion TLC. If you can open your heart to adopt a cat like me, I'll hopefully have the confidence to come around to my new people, like you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am playful and cute!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: We took a short walk up to the park and spent most of our time learning to play fetch! Pepa's a sweet, high-energy baby girl, and is still learning to play and to be patient. After a few repetitions and lots of praise, she started to pick up how fetch works. It went pretty quickly, as she's super treat motivated, and eager to perform for them (still learning to take them gently). We also played a little tug-of-war, which she loved, and she finally took a little nap after spending all of that energy. She didn't care much about any other dogs or people around. She pulls hard on a shorter leash because she's so excited to see everything, but with a little give she walks fine and checks in regularly. Once she warms up to you she's super affectionate, will curl up in your lap and give you all the kisses you'll allow.
