254555.name: Diamond
254555.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Diamond is a little gem! She is a pretty and elegant oreo cookie who might appear timid at first but she is truly not. She likes to stay on her balcony, listening attentively to sweet talks, slow blinks in return and waits patiently for more. A major head bunter she is who pushes her head against my hand quite forcefully, hoping for deep petting in return. Diamond gave birth two months ago, leaving her kitten less(babies were not surrendered with her) and with a uterine prolapse cured by our veterinary team with a spay. Diamond is not only cute, she is also a good girl who aced her behavior evaluation and could go home with you..Today! Diamond is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Diamond is laying in her litter box as the assessor approaches, body slightly tense and lip licking as the kennel door is opened. She allows all petting and after a few seconds she appears to relax, closing her eyes as she leans into petting on the head and cheeks. Due to recovering from medical treatment, she is not fully picked up and removed from the kennel. She is able to be lifted from inside of the kennel with ease, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she flops over onto her side, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting and handling.

Diamond is a bit shy when you first meet her, but when she is given some time to open up, she will show you that she is a very sweet girl! She appreciates attention, is easy to handle, and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

254557.name: Molly
254557.summary:
Meet Molly, a sweet girl with a gentle heart who's looking for a fresh start. Molly was found as a stray, and although she was understandably nervous at first, she chose to follow a kind Good Samaritan who stopped to help her - a sign that she wants to trust and connect with people.

Since arriving with us, Molly has been social and affectionate with staff, often seeking comfort and leaning into pets for reassurance. She enjoys attention and has shown a soft, loving side despite all the recent changes in her life.

Like many dogs in the shelter, Molly is stressed in the kennel environment. Shelters can be overwhelming, loud, and confusing, especially for a dog adjusting to so much uncertainty. Outside of the kennel, Molly's sweet personality shines through much more clearly.

If you're searching for a loyal companion who just needs a chance, come meet Molly and see if she's the missing piece in your family.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Molly was such a joy. She was nervous at first yet quickly warmed up. While driving in the car she looked like she was taking it all in. When she was inside our home, she had the zoomies and I could tell she was feeling so comfortable and happy. To help with her energy, we released her in our closed in yard and played fetch with her tennis balls. She was such a pleasure and I'm still thinking about all her kisses and hugs. Literally the sweetest girl. My husband and I took her out for the day and my parents got to play with her in the yard. She was so warm and friendly to 4 adults - we loved our time with her.

254560.name: Cosmo
254560.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.



Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

My Boroughbreaker writes: Miss Maple is a GOOD GIRL. Miss Maple and I took a slow stroll to Central Park! She was very excited at first, but then settled into having perfect leash manners. We took lots of breaks for water, treats, and we hung out in the grass together. We went home for a little to enjoy the air conditioning, and for Miss Maple to take a nap. She is really a chill hang! She gets so excited when she gets verbal praise, and is an absolute lover. She loves pets and snuggles and really warmed up throughout the day. She has a warm and sweet presence and I would have taken her home forever if I could! She is a medium energy dog who loved the park and meeting new friends.

254591.name: Button Blue
254591.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Button Blue is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Button Blue displays fearful behavior during handling, including growling, hard barking, retreating from the leash, startling at sudden noises, and balking during walks. He also displays on-leash reactivity toward other dogs, particularly small dogs, barking and pulling toward them while moving through the building. Button Blue is able to be leashed with patient handling and food or toy reinforcement, and is slowly acclimating but is still struggling. Medically, Button Blue is recieving treatment for CIRDC.

Button Blue was surrendered by his previous owner due to financial issues. His previous owner describes him as a low-energy, aloof, and mellow dog. Blue was reported to spend most of his time in his crate. He is noted to be allergic to poultry, but his favorite treats were milkbones, and like playing fetch. Button Blue has been highly fearful and defensive when attempts are made to remove him from the kennel. Once out, he avoids interaction, accepting high-value treats when in close proximity to him. Due to these concerns, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can address these concerns with the use of a certified professional trainer who uses only positive reinforcement methods.

254602.name: Gwendalyn
254602.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Gwendalyn is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Gwendalyn is reactive toward other dogs, and the stress of the shelter environment has led to behavioral deterioration. She has been observed vocalizing, engaging in kennel fighting, spinning, and throwing herself against her transfer door. Recently, while a staff member was attempting to remove her from her kennel, Gwendalyn redirected onto the staff member's hand while barking and jumping toward another dog through the upper kennel bars. The contact did not break the skin. Outside of her kennel, Gwendalyn is social and affectionate with staff, readily leaning in for petting and accepting treats. Medically, Gwendalyn is underweight.

Gwendalyn was brought to the Care Centers as a stray, so her behavior history in a home environment is unknown. While in the Care Centers, she has displayed reactivity toward other dogs when they pass by her kennel. On one occasion, following a kennel-fighting incident, Gwendalyn redirected her frustration toward a staff member and made contact with the staff member's leg. No skin was broken during the incident. Outside of her kennel, Gwendalyn is a social and affectionate dog who enjoys attention and leans into petting. Due to her dog reactivity and history of redirected behavior, Gwendalyn should be placed through a New Hope Partner into an adult-only home that can manage her behavior and continue her training using positive reinforcement-based methods.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

254603.name: Argenis
254603.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Argenis is an eight month old ginger, cute as a button who loves to play(he is a very active kitten) and to cuddle. He is quite lively, runs after catnip toys and wrestles feather wands. He rolls on his kennel floor, head bunting and loving his neck and cheeks scratchies and is pretty good at being in the arms. Argenis scratched his owners, something that never happened(totally unexpected for him) in the seven months he lived with his family...The assumption is that he became extremely frightened after smelling on his owner's hand the scents of a stray cat she had just handled and fed. Argenis is fine now, comfortable and happy with his interactions with staff and volunteers. He would love to be home, though, a low traffic one without boisterous children and with an experienced owner who can provide love and plenty of play time. Argenis is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.








What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

254604.name: Mr. Wiggles
254604.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Mr Wiggles is at risk due to behavioral reasons. He has been observed to be rope reactive and dog reactive while in care. During his assessment Mr Wiggles was observed to jump up and bite the leash. This behavior has continued to be observed throughout his stay. Mr Wiggles has also been observed to charge at other dogs while on leash. This behavior is difficult to redirect. While in the kennel room, it is reported that he is jumping off the walls in an attempt to get closer to the other dogs. While on street walks, Mr Wiggles is noted to have a soft body and wagging tail. Medically, Mr Wiggles is apparently healthy.

Mr Wiggles arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Mr Wiggles has been observed to be rope reactive and have handling sensitivity. He has been noted to jump up and bite the leash during the jog portion of the handling assessment. This behavior was not able to be redirected until pet corrector was used. When contact is initiated and when the handler was attempting to place a collar on him Mr Wiggles will head whip. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

254613.name: Poe
254613.summary:
Meet Poe! 🐾

Poe is a charming and affectionate male pup who's always excited to meet new friends! He has done well greeting dogs at a gate. He's full of energy and enthusiasm, which means he can be a little jumpy at first and is still learning basic manners. Despite his playful exuberance, Poe's favorite moments are quiet ones: he loves to cuddle and snuggle up with those he trusts.

Poe would thrive in a home that can provide consistent guidance, plenty of love, and lots of opportunities to play and explore. If you're looking for a joyful companion who will greet you with wagging tail and warm snuggles, Poe might just be your perfect match!

My Boroughbreaker writes: This was Poe's first outing and he walked very well on a leash! He is nervous in unfamiliar environments (loud sounds and unfamiliar visuals seem to be his trigger) and may pull away strongly when startled. He was very friend to meet new people during our time together and seems curious about other dogs. Poe didn't exhibit any interest in small birds or squirrels we may have passed on both our hike and walk.
He had a lot of zoomies when we went into the house, which was great to see! He is a jumper (on both people and tables) when he is excited. To get him to calm down, sitting on the floor seemed to help cause he would come over for human touch and then settle. Again, big dog trying to be a lap dog.
Other random observations: Poe seemed to pick up the "sit" pretty quickly when presented with a treat, but performance of the behavior is inconsistent when excited. He will withhold from food when he is nervous. He has some trouble/confidence with getting in a car - I had to lift him up. When he runs, he does so like a bunny which is quite adorable.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
	Poe did so well on his borough break! We went on a little walk first and he walked so well on a leash- stayed close to me, no pulling /barking /growling/fear of people or animals. Then we went to the beach, where he was the happiest little bug ever! He loved laying in the sand and in my lap asking for belly rubs. He dozed off listening to the waves and was so relaxed! He was a bit timid getting into the car but with some patience he became brave and jumped in by himself. He did like actually riding in the car and looking out the window. We encountered some dogs and people and he seemed friendly and wagged his tail calmly looking to play but because it was a borough break they didn't interact. He was even good at sensing when the other dog was nervous. Poe is really such an amazing dog and anyone would be lucky to have him as an addition to their family!

He will withhold from food when he is nervous. He has some trouble/confidence with getting in a car - I had to lift him up. When he runs, he does so like a bunny which is quite adorable.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
	Poe did so well on his borough break! We went on a little walk first and he walked so well on a leash- stayed close to me, no pulling /barking /growling/fear of people or animals. Then we went to the beach, where he was the happiest little bug ever! He loved laying in the sand and in my lap asking for belly rubs. He dozed off listening to the waves and was so relaxed! He was a bit timid getting into the car but with some patience he became brave and jumped in by himself. He did like actually riding in the car and looking out the window. We encountered some dogs and people and he seemed friendly and wagged his tail calmly looking to play but because it was a borough break they didn't interact. He was even good at sensing when the other dog was nervous. Poe is really such an amazing dog and anyone would be lucky to have him as an addition to their family!

254632.name: Tommie
254632.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Tommie is a cute and very friendly cat who unfortunately got bitten by another animal, likely another unknown cat he met in the street. He is all better now and charming staff and volunteers with his sunny personality. Tommy is not a cat to stay in hiding. He is outgoing and welcomes his visitors with head bunting and purring. He loves to play with catnip toys and feather wands and enjoys a treat at the end of the game(see video). He is really a sweetheart, a fun player and all together a great cat. Tommie is under the supervision of the Department of Health(DOH) that checks bite victims monthly(usually through a phone call or a visit with the ACC veterinarians) for 6 months from the time of the bite(until mid November in Tommie's case). It is really not a big deal and a very good thing for the kitty to be out of a cage, cared for, happy and loved. So, if you are interested and want to bless Tommie with your love and hospitality, come to the Manhattan Care Center, meet Tommie, speak with our adoption counselors and hopefully, take him home. 







Hi there! My name is Tommie and I arrived as a stray so the staff don't know what my life was like before coming to ACC, but I had an injury that I'm recovering from. I only require a little extra paperwork to be filled out and a few extra vet visits this year because one of my injuries was likely a bite wound . I'm thankful for everyone at ACC taking such good care of me, but I think I'd like to find my forever home now. So what are you waiting for? Ask about me today!
Tommie is laying in his den as the assessor approaches, resting his head on his front paws. When the kennel door is opened and he is softly spoken to, he picks his head up, looking at the assessor with soft eyes. He allows all petting, leaning in, head bunting softly, and flopping over onto his side as he is pet. Due to healing from injuries, the assessor does not take him out of the kennel fully to attempt pickup. He is tolerant of pickup from inside of the kennel and remains calm when he is held. When he is placed back, he continues to allow and lean into all petting.

Tommie interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

254648.name: Anpu
254648.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!
Playtime is essential! I love climbing tall cat trees and having fun with interactive toys!
I am not one to sit still and will love interactive playtime in my new home!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.

Anpu tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home. Anpu was surrendered for behavior concerns in his previous home. 

A volunteer writes: Anpu's previous guardian said that their favorite thing about him was "how good of a companion, and how affectionate he is, once he's comfortable." He's been on a mission to demonstrate this at the shelter. Hopping right to the front of his condo when I opened the door, it was like he was saying "Wait, wait, wait, wait..." for his grand introduction. Anpu sat down and tucked his chin into his chest to sweetly nuzzle himself into my hand. Curling into a little kitty circle, Anpu graciously snuggled as he took in the room. A young and joyful cat, he's hoping to find a family with a little extra patience and a lot of love to share.

254683.name: Astrid
254683.summary: A volunteer writes: Astrid was abandoned in a carrier in front of someone's home and she's been trying everyday since then to explain that this doesn't define her. It's just that sometimes her words get jumbled up and her efforts and don't always come out the way she intends. Astrid still tries by doing what she knows best and that is being her friendly self and saying hello! Astrid loves to welcome visitors to Adoptions by rolling around to show her belly and reach her paws. Hellos through the door are great and are usually followed with some kitty conversation, or maybe some pets or some chirps but here's where Astrid gets a little confused on next steps. It's ok because this is where we come in. We've learned that Astrid loves, and I mean loves, our laser shows. Following the dot with hopes of catching it, with some treats to make up for the fact that she probably won't.

254690.name: Vocalist
254690.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Vocalist is the cutest and sweetest little guy, only eight months of age. He was found crying on a fire escape and was brought ASAP by a Good Samaritan to the Manhattan Care Center. Vocalist was a little shy at first, then transformed into the most friendly and adorable kitten, seeking comfort and love with his visitors, even coming into their arms. Beside having a little cold,Vocalist is apparently healthy, did wonderfully well on his behavior evaluation and could go home after his neuter. Come and meet lovely Vocalist at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

254695.name: Chai Latte
254695.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Chai Latte is at risk due to behavior concerns. Chai Latte is reported to growl, hard bark and lunge at staff while being removed or being placed into his kennel. Lately, Chai Latte has been struggling in the kennel environment. He has been observed spinning in circles and attempting to bite his tail, indicating increased stress and difficulty coping in the shelter setting. Outside, Chai Latte takes treats and engages in cue training. Medically, Chai Latte has dental disease.

Chai Latte arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. When he initially arrived, he was observed to be fearful. Noted to growl during his medical exam and was timid with handlers. Recently, Chai has begun to show more defensive behaviors, such as growling and snarling at handlers after being returned to kennel. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

254709.name: Mimi
254709.summary: Mimi interacts with the observer and appreciates attention, but she has a tendency to low growl/grumble while eating treats/food (does not escalate or show signs of resource guarding), hiss when being lifted (does not escalate). Her behavior remains suitable for an adopter with an average amount of experience, provided the adopter is aware of these behaviors and is able to comfortably manage them. Though we believe this cat is displaying behaviors appropriate for new or experienced cat parents, she may not be a great fit for young children. At this time she may be most appropriately matched in an Adult-only home. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

254761.name: Chaschu
254761.summary:
A volunteer writes:
I have a "strong weakness" for blue eyes, mostly baby blue eyes and our Chaschu owns one of the best pairs of eyes on earth. The twist is that he is no Ragdoll or Persian but a handsome dark grey and white American Shorthair. Chaschu is with us for no fault of his own. Someone loved him and cared for him beautifully until they passed away. Chaschu lost his owner and his home and he is blue".... His first few days at the care center were tough to deal with but few days down the live, Chaschu soft blinked at me, purred and stretched his neck in all directions to get the most of my petting. I love this guy, his gentle manners and his beauty. I hope that you will too. Chaschu will likely be a little bit shy when you first met him. Be understanding, patient, give him some time and he will be your loyal and loving forever best friend. Chaschu is waiting to meet you at the Manhattan Care Center.





What my friends at ACC say about me:
Chaschu was in the den, appearing a little concerned and curious at the same time, with somewhat large pupils. He gave a little warning hiss after sniffing treats when approached, but it seemed to be just a warning, and he then allowed petting on his cheek and head and lifted his head for chin rubs. He remained a little guarded, but he's a sweet cat and may just need a little time to warm up. When the front cover of the den was replaced, he gave another very small warning growl but then was quiet.

Chaschu tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. 	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

254765.name: Smoke
254765.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Smoke is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Smoke has displayed fearful behavior toward unfamiliar people during an adoption interaction, including hard barking, backing away, increasing distance from the unfamiliar person, and remaining difficult to refocus away due to his intense reaction. Smoke's discomfort was significant enough that the interaction was discontinued. Smoke is able to be handled by familiar staff slowly, loves to participate in enrichment sessions. Medically, Smoke is apparently healthy.

Smoke came into the care center as a stray with another dog; due to this, his behavior in a home environment is unknown.  Smoke has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has shown fearful defensive behavior towards staff. He is noted to display a tense body, a hard bark, and become avoidant of handlers. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

254766.name: Stack
254766.summary:
Meet Stack!
Stack was found tied up in front of a precinct with another dog. He's an independent guy who is still learning that the world and new people are safe, and he's looking for a calm, patient home to help him come out of his shell.

My Ideal Home
Stack would love a quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace. He enjoys getting out for walks and sniffing around, and he'll do best with a family that gives him time, structure, and lots of positive reinforcement as he builds confidence. Once he feels comfortable, his gentle, curious side starts to shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Stack showed brief, polite interest in another dog at the care center, but became tense during the interaction and was moved away for his comfort. His history with other animals is unknown, so any introductions to resident dogs should be slow and thoughtful. He may be happiest as the only pet in the home.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearfulness and sensitivity in new situations, Stack is recommended for an adult-only home at this time.

Things to Know
Stack is a thoughtful, observant dog who can be a bit anxious in new environments and prefers to take things at his own pace. He is generally tolerant of handling but appreciates gentle, low-pressure interactions and the freedom to step away when he needs space. With patience, consistency, and positive reinforcement, Stack has a great foundation to grow into a trusting and loyal companion.

Fun Fact
Stack has a soft, curious side that comes out more each day. Once he feels safe, he enjoys exploring and quietly taking in the world around him.

254768.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Baby Blu is at risk due o behavioral concerns. Baby Blue's owner reported that he will lunge, hard bark, and snap at strangers, children, and unfamiliar dogs. He was also reported to exhibit resource-guarding behavior and may snap when restrained. He has bitten once, drawing blood. While in the Care Centers, Baby Blue presented as fearful but generally aloof. With a slow approach Baby Blu has warmed up to select staff and will tolerate limited petting and handling. Medically, Baby Blu is healthy.

Baby Blu arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. His previous owner states that he is fearful in the home and will hide or snap when the family tries to put his collar and leash on. During one instance, Baby bit the owner's mother on the hand, drawing blood. This bite was treated at the urgent care. While in care, Baby has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to have a tense body, wide eyes, lip licking, and is reluctant to exit the kennel. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Yuma needs at risk placement for medical and behavioral reasons. Yuma is being treated for CIRDC, he is having difficulty eating due to a slack jaw. Behaviorally, Yuma has displayed concerning over arosual behavior in care results in head whipping, lunging towards staff, and leash biting needing a disruptor to be used to redirect Yuma. Yuma needs support in a home and a neurological consultation to develop a treatment plan for the nerve deficit in his jaw. There is concern of Yuma injuring themselves further due to the persistent leash biting behavior and his medical condition. He would highly benefit from care outside of the shelter environment. 

Yuma arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Yuma has been observed to growl when handlers approach him. Noted to occur during his medical exam and his assessment. During the jog portion of the assessment, Yuma was observed to jump up high and bite the leash. This behavior required pet corrector to be redirected. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

254775.name: Crownie
254775.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Crownie is a petite gal found in a carrier with friend LeBosse at midnight at the Manhattan Care Center's door....Just like that! Both kitties were understandably scared..and for days. Crownie, mostly found in hiding in her den, would come out, seeking petting and then hissing and withdrawing. Time did its job as well as the efforts of staff and volunteers trying to make Crownie feel better. It worked. The pretty gal who is still a bit skittish and watching for signs of "danger" is definitively more relaxed, less interested in food and seeks the attention of her visitor, leaning into pets and even purring under my fingers. She occasionally will let a little stressed cry go while going for more petting. Crownie is a cute and petite gal, a bit underweight, still a little shaky from her past life and her stay in a shelter environment but on her way to become a happy pet in proper and experienced hands and in a low traffic home. Crownie would love to know safety and happiness. You might be the one able to offer her that wonderful gift! Come and meet this little princess at the Manhattan Care Center!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
Crownie has made excellent improvement since her first assessment. She is high-energy, vocal, and demanding, but very sweet and does not overstimulate. She was at the front, rubbing against the bars with large pupils and putting her paw out to get attention. She enjoyed all petting, accepting and leaning in for cheek rubs and head bunts. She ate squeeze-up treats and was calm and quiet when picked up and held in the assessor's arms. She seemed curious about the cat in the kennel behind her and remained active, energetic, and engaged.

Crownie interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in high energy and activity and the possibility that she could go over threshold with too much interaction. 	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

254783.name: Goliath
254783.summary:
Hello, friend, I'm Goliath. I am a professional observer and the owner of one slightly wonky ear. People say it gives me character. As a former stray, I was pretty nervous and unsure when I first arrived at the care center, hiding up in corners. A few weeks of slow interactions, treats and soft blankets suspiciously showing up in my space helped me open up into a whole new man. My friends at ACC have absolutely loved watching me start to open up, now eager to hop right off my ledge as the morning greeter and give TONS of snuggles. All of the snuggles. Seriously, I hope you like snuggles. I sure do. It's somehow even more precious coming from my grumpy face and former street cat aura. All this time, it turns out what I needed was a very cozy high perch, squeeze up treats and a routine I can trust. And someone to give all my cheek rubs.

But my journey is just beginning. I have been waiting for my special person for some time now...I have a good feeling they are coming soon.

A volunteer writes: Goliath doesn't know what imposter syndrome is and he doesn't need to. This fellow searched far and wide for a family and while he didn't quite manage to find one on his own, he did find an approach that worked. It's called fake it 'til you make it and sitting on a porch corner walking himself into a Good Samaritan's house several times was just the thing he needed to do to convince them he belonged somewhere and with someone. Goliath is silly and sociable, greeting me from underneath his little blanket fort and then hopping on top of it to play. A friendly guy, he leaned into my hand as he made his laps around his condo. I'd love to learn more from Goliath and maybe even take a page from his book but what he really needs is to find you.
**Behavior Summary - Goliath**

Goliath is a gentle, shy cat who has shown steady progress in building confidence during his time in the shelter. Initially very cautious and easily startled by unfamiliar sounds and activity, he often preferred to observe from a safe distance and would retreat when feeling uncertain. Despite his nervousness, Goliath consistently demonstrated curiosity about people and was willing to engage when approached calmly and respectfully.

Over time, Goliath has become increasingly comfortable with human interaction. He now readily approaches to sniff offered hands, enjoys chin and cheek rubs, leans into petting, and has shown growing tolerance for handling. While he may still occasionally pull away when feeling unsure, he often re-engages once given a moment to process the interaction. His body language suggests that he wants social contact but benefits from being allowed to set the pace and choose when to participate.

Goliath remains a somewhat sensitive cat who may need time to adjust to new environments and routines. He is likely to thrive in a calm home with patient adopters who can provide him with the space and reassurance needed to build trust. As his confidence grows, he has shown the potential to become a sweet and affectionate companion who enjoys gentle attention and close relationships with his people.

This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

254790.name: Benji Boo
254790.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Benji Boo is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Benji was brought to MACC following a bite incident. The finder stated that Benji will resource guard his food. The finder grabbed Benji's harness while he was eating, and Benji bit them on the hand. His finder noted Benji Boo to be reactive to dogs which we have seen in care as well. Benji Boo was described as social and affectionate by his finder. With handlers Benji is receptive to chicken and has slowly warmed up to staff. Medically, Benji is apparently healthy.

Benji Boo arrived at MACC following a bite incident. The finder stated that he will become tense, hover, growl, and hard bark when food, treats, and toys are in his possession. During one instance, the finder reached to grab Benji's harness. Benji turned his head and bit the finder's left hand. He is also reported to lunge towards unfamiliar dogs while on leash. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

254795.name: Cookie King
254795.summary:
Meet Cookie King!
Cookie King was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him after first arriving at ACC as a stray. This sweet, treat-loving boy has quickly won over volunteers with his happy-go-lucky personality, wiggly greetings, and enthusiasm for making new friends. If you're looking for a dog who's always excited to spend time with you, Cookie King is ready to earn a permanent spot in your heart.

My Ideal Home
Cookie King would love an active home that can give him plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He's an energetic boy who enjoys toys, treats, and staying busy, and he'll thrive with adopters who can help channel all of that excitement into fun adventures.

Good with Other Pets?
Cookie King gets very excited when he sees other dogs and can pull toward them to say hello. While shelter introductions have shown an enthusiastic greeting style, slow introductions to any resident dogs are recommended to help everyone feel comfortable.

Good with Kids?
ACC recommends a home with no children under 13 at this time.

Things to Know
Cookie King is a highly social dog who loves people and isn't shy about showing it. He can become easily excited and may jump around or get a little over aroused during play and handling, but he's eager to engage and enjoys toys, treats, and being part of the action. He's a wonderful candidate for continued reward-based training that helps him learn calm manners while keeping his fun-loving spirit intact.

What Volunteers Say
"What's a wonderful guy like this doing in a pop-up crate in the hallway when there is so much fun to be had in the world?" Volunteers describe Cookie King as an incredibly sweet dog who has everyone rooting for him. He's affectionately known as "treat obsessed," happily accepting just about any snack, and they'd love to see him put on a little healthy weight. One volunteer's wish is simple: come take him for a walk... and then keep walking all the way home.

I'm available for adoption at ACC's Pop-Up Event on:


Saturday, June 20 | 11AM - 4PM
Brooklyn Borough Hall
209 Joralemon Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201


adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

From my Foster Parent:

Coconut is an extremely sweet kitten who loves to explore his environment but also equally loves cuddling. He is extremely curious, and learned very quickly how to play with all of his toys. He was a little nervous around the dog, but I'm sure with time he would get used to one. The one thing he loved the most though was playing with his brother; they were practicing inseparable and followed each other around everywhere. They played, cuddled, and ate together. I believe Coconut will do very well in a home with other cats, and can benefit from having his own place in any home to explore without any hazards. He will be a wonderful addition to any home!

Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

Meet Yin!

Yin and her sister Yang are still a bit of a mystery to staff here at SIACC. We have almost no background information on them so we're still slowly getting to know them. What we can tell so far is that Yin and her sister are both adorable young cats that have lots of potential. Of the two, Yin seems a bit more self-assured and curious about interacting with staff. Our hope is that Yin will find an adopter who can work with her as she decompresses in a new environment (aka your house!). Positive reinforcement and a slow, considerate approach will help her settle in nicely to any new home. All she needs is the right person! Maybe that person is you? If so, come say hi to Yin at SIACC!

254830.name: Mugen
254830.summary:
Mugen appreciates attention and petting but has had a history of being moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will need time to warm up to his new home and new family, preferring contact on his own terms as he adjusts. Once he feels comfortable, he is curious, affectionate and plays gently. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Mugen should go to an adult-only, single-pet home with a new family that is willing to give him time to adjust and open up to them, in order to show his true and sweet personality.

A volunteer writes: For half a very surprising second, I'd left Mugen waiting for pets. He was standing at the front and had presented me with his beautiful forehead. Headbunting into the hand I'd extended as soon as I realized what was happening, this was quite a bit different from a few minutes earlier when Mugen had gracefully hopped on top of his bed upon seeing me at the door. I really thought that space was as far as our friendship would go, which is always ok but after peering over and around my head for several minutes, Mugen had a change of heart. Extending his neck a little and trying to walk forward, I appreciate his thoughtfulness and understand that none of it's magic. Mugen takes his time to come around, but when he's ready, he does. He was brought to us after he followed someone home and since he lived there for a little while, they were able to see his curious and gentle side. Mugen is hoping to find a forever family to give him another chance.

254854.name: Pony
254854.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Pony has made amazing progress since his first assessment, and now all he wants is petting and attention. He was at the front rubbing against the kennel door and then leaned in hard for cheek rubs, almost rolling on his side. He's super sweet and affectionate, and he was reasonably calm when picked up and held and remained so when set back down. He's curious and interactive and just wants to be your friend.

Pony interacts with the assessor,  solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience but should be given a slow introduction to the home.

A volunteer writes : Pony is an adorable 6 year old ginger. He was found by a good Samaritan in a parking garage who brought him into us. When he first came in, he was a bit timid, and it seems as though he is turning a corner. I found him at the back of his cubby and gave him a few gentle pets, and after a few minutes, he came forward and it was endgame from there. He gently pushed his head into my hands, urging me to pet him more. He loves treats and situations like these where I get the opportunity to help an animal gain comfort in a shelter environment and come out of their shell is so rewarding.

Plopper, the little gal was adopted and Aesop is still waiting for his forever. Volunteers love him. He really enjoys catnip toys and feather wands that he likes to wrestle with! Aesop might have been timid for a few days but now, he is at the front of his kennel, asking for attention, petting and play time. He is more than cute. He is super handsome! You get the picture! Aesop is almost perfect except that he was a little wary to be picked up during his behavior testing. He prefers to have his four on the ground or on his kennel floor. Many cats are like that although they could be taught. Aesop is a nice young guy who will make a wonderful pet and for many years to come. Come and meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center, adopt him and take him home!

254861.name: Kenny
254861.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Thirteen year old Kenny and his eight year old female friend Robin were found locked together in a crate in an empty apartment. Nothing, really nothing is known about them. Robin is having a very hard time but Kenny is going with the flow, trying to adapt to his new reality although I can see that he is quite lost. He knows intuitively that he must survive his ordeal and eating well is very much on his check list. Kenny loooves to eat. Of course, some petting here and there helps him a great deal easing into his new life at the care center. He purrs softly after a while spent with his caretaker. Kenny is a handsome cat who in his prime, must have been quite a catch. White and peach color coat, baby blue eyes and a rather big cat at almost sixteen pounds. He is quite well mannered, easy going and trying to make the best of what life threw at him. Let's find him and his friend Robin, may be, a home sweet home for their golden years...Kenny and Robin are at the Manhattan Care Center. Both are spayed and neutered and could go home today!

254891.name: Miles
254891.summary:
My foster writes: Miles is patiently waiting to meet his new best friend! He's a very friendly and loyal guy who just wants to cuddle on the couch or sit with you outside. Or sit with you in the kitchen or bedroom or poke his head in to keep you company in the shower. He's not a barker but you'll know he's there because of the paw or head or tail he has touching you at all times.
He knows sit, down, paw, stay, and come and loves practicing and learning new tricks.
On walks Miles ignores anything and anyone until he senses they want to say hi to him, then he's excited and wags his tail until someone pets him. He is friendly or apathetic around other dogs but really soaks up attention from people.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes... If you're looking for an easygoing, affectionate companion, Miles might just be your perfect match. This sweet boy is as chill as they come - nothing seems to faze him. He showed no signs of reactivity around other dogs or loud noises and took everything in stride with a calm, happy demeanor.
Miles absolutely loves both people and other dogs. He was excited to say hello to everyone he met, from adults to children, and greeted other dogs with friendly curiosity and zero aggression. He's the kind of dog who just wants to make friends wherever he goes.
He seems to have a lower-to-moderate energy level - despite our walk being a fairly relaxed pace, he was perfectly happy to settle in and relax afterward. An affectionate guy, he gave a few gentle hand kisses throughout our time together. The only times Miles does pull on the leash a bit when he needs to go to the bathroom or when someone is giving him attention and he wants to say hello back, but otherwise he's a relaxed, easy companion who is a pleasure to be around.
One of the sweetest moments was taking him to Starbucks for a pup cup - Miles patiently and gently licked the whipped cream right from the cup I was holding for him, showing just how gentle and well-mannered he is.
Miles is truly an angel. Whether you're a single person, a couple, or a family, anyone would be lucky to welcome this lovable boy into their home. He has so much love to give and is ready to be someone's best friend for life.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

254893.name: Rhylee
254893.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Rhylee!
Rhylee is a fun-loving pup who came to ACC when her owner could no longer care for her. This playful girl has a big personality and loves making connections with her favorite people. From car rides to squeaky toys to splashing around in the water, Rhylee knows how to enjoy the good things in life. She is looking for a patient family who can help her channel her enthusiasm and continue learning.

My Ideal Home
Rhylee would thrive with an adopter who enjoys an active and playful companion. She will benefit from daily exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training to help her practice calm greetings, impulse control, and appropriate ways to show her excitement. A predictable home with someone who understands her need to take things at her own pace will help Rhylee feel confident and successful.

Good with Other Pets?
Rhylee's previous owner reported that she has lived with other dogs, but she prefers interactions on her own terms. During her time at ACC, she has been a bit more independent when meeting new dogs, so slow introductions and allowing her time to warm up will be important.

Good with Kids?
Due to Rhylee's high energy, jumping, and moments of feeling overwhelmed during handling, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. She would do best with people who can recognize her body language and help her feel comfortable through gentle, positive interactions.

Things to Know
Rhylee is a silly, affectionate pup who brings plenty of energy and personality wherever she goes! She loves fluffy beds, squeaky toys, water, and spending time with her people. She is still working on keeping all four paws on the floor and learning that leashes are for walking, not playing tug, but she is smart and ready to learn. With patience, structure, and positive reinforcement, Rhylee is ready to be someone's playful adventure buddy.

Meet Itachi!

This handsome little guy is Itachi! He was described by his previous owner as a friendly and affectionate cat who loved playtime. While he's been here, however, he's been on the shy side. He allows staff to give gentle pets but it's obvious that the shelter environment makes him uncomfortable. Due to his fear, we think it's best if he go to an adult only home. We think he'll really appreciate a slow, considerate approach in his new home where he can interact with folks on his own terms. Positive reinforcement through treats and toys will encourage him to come out of his shell and show you the cat he truly is. If you're looking for a new feline companion, come say hi to Itachi at SIACC today!

254908.name: Michu
254908.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Michu is a young and pretty Tabby surrendered to us as his owner moved to a far away state. He has been very well cared for and was clearly loved. Michu started a bit shy in his debuts at the care center but it did not take long for him to find his bearings. He is an adorable little guy, friendly, quite welcoming and who not only loves petting and sweet talks but also playing with catnip toys and feather wands. The great thing is that he enjoys playing without going overboard. Michu is all together a cute, friendly and fun feline who will make a wonderful for ever best friend and for many years to come. Michu is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center. 








Michu is laying in the back of his cubby behind his litter box, resting his head on his front paws with his eyes closed. When the cubby door is opened, he picks his head up and lip licks. He is softly spoken to and after a few seconds he stretches forward, getting up to greet the assessor at the front of the cubby with a soft head bunt. He leans into petting on the head and cheeks but does flinch when petting down his shoulders and back. He is able to be easily coaxed to the main area of the kennel when he is called over, approaching the front and leaning forward to head bunt the assessor's hand. Michu is offered crunchy treats and enthusiastically begins eating them. He allows all petting, leaning in and lifting his back as he is pet. He steps out of the kennel calmly and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front and continues to lean into all petting. He occasionally flinches throughout the interaction but did not escalate. 

Michu interacts with the observer, solicits/ appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that Michu go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods, decompression, and fearful behavior.

The great thing is that he enjoys playing without going overboard. Michu is all together a cute, friendly and fun feline who will make a wonderful for ever best friend and for many years to come. Michu is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.

Michu is laying in the back of his cubby behind his litter box, resting his head on his front paws with his eyes closed. When the cubby door is opened, he picks his head up and lip licks. He is softly spoken to and after a few seconds he stretches forward, getting up to greet the assessor at the front of the cubby with a soft head bunt. He leans into petting on the head and cheeks but does flinch when petting down his shoulders and back. He is able to be easily coaxed to the main area of the kennel when he is called over, approaching the front and leaning forward to head bunt the assessor's hand. Michu is offered crunchy treats and enthusiastically begins eating them. He allows all petting, leaning in and lifting his back as he is pet. He steps out of the kennel calmly and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front and continues to lean into all petting. He occasionally flinches throughout the interaction but did not escalate.

Michu interacts with the observer, solicits/ appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that Michu go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods, decompression, and fearful behavior.

254916.name: Cj Meow
254916.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

CJ Meow is on the at-risk list for medical concerns. CJ Meow is a young cat with ringworm, a suspected congenital deformity affecting his right hindlimb, and a wound on his left hind limb. Because of the wound, we are unable to administer topical ringworm treatment (lyme dips). Recommend alternative topical treatment with placement. Behaviorally, CJ Meow is sweet and has allowed handling.

Cj Meow interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I am playful and cute!

Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

254927.name: Coco
254927.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

A volunteer writes: Dreaming of a better tomorrow, Coco was kneading to himself as he slept. Illustrating how ready he is to find a family, Coco endearingly ensures he won't blend in at the shelter even if he hasn't found it to be the easiest. He's a smart and playful guy who could use a little more than what the shelter provides. Coco came to us in May after he was left behind in an apartment and then brought to someone for safekeeping. Coco's hopeful that a little loving stability will be coming his way, especially given how hard he's been trying for it. As soon as he saw me at his door, he came forward to say hello. Nuzzling for fun and also with purpose, Coco's a social and curious guy just hoping to find his way home.

254928.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Surfer is at risk due to behavioral reasons. When Surfer initially arrived at MACC he was noted to be fearful. During his medical exam, he was observed to thrash when being restrained and escalated to growling and snapping. Recently Surfer has been observed to be highly kennel reactive. Noted to lunge towards the other dogs in the kennel room. In one instance after lunging at a neighboring dog, Surfer spun and lunged with an open mouth at the handler. While out with handlers Surfer is noted to be receptive to treats and allow contact with a neutral body. Medically, Surfer has CIRDC.

Surfer arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. During his medical exam, Surfer was observed to thrash when being restrained and escalated to growling and snapping. Recently, Surfer has been observed to be highly kennel reactive. Noted to lunge towards the other dogs in the kennel room. During one instance after lunging at a neighboring dog, Surfer spun and lunged with an open mouth at the handler. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

254938.summary:
Mila presents with a very high level of fear and appears to be struggling to adjust to the shelter environment. She tolerates very brief attention and a small amount of petting but may be significantly fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

254940.name: Charleston Girl
254940.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!


Charleston Girl has made major improvements since her first assessment. She was at the front, quiet, attentive, and sweet. She sniffed treats and then allowed and enjoyed all petting, leaning in gently for cheek rubs and allowing petting along her back. She was calm when picked up and held and remained calm when set back down. She enjoyed squeeze-up treats very much, and she's a very sweet cat. She's showing Level 1 behavior but making her L2 due to prior behaviors.

Charleston Girl continues to make consistent and lovely improvements and was at the front, extremely affectionate and enjoying being held so much that she didn't really want to leave the assessor's arms. She was set back down and remained curious, sweet, and at the front wanting attention. We believe her earlier stress was pain-induced and not behavioral in nature.

Charleston Girl interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience. 


A volunteer writes: Charleston Girl has been dealt a pretty unfair hand as of late but it seems she'd much rather discuss her outstanding pipe cleaner feather skills. Though she was left behind when her guardian went into care, she wasn't left without love as a family member took care of Charleston Girl as best they could. It wasn't a permanent solution and Charleston Girl was brought to us where she's been trying her best to show us who she is and wants to be. Waltzing right to the front of her cubby and trying to hop onto my lap, Charleston Girl joyfully but still kind of shyly introduced herself like someone who knows something special is just about to happen and it will. Charleston Girl loves to play and was ready to show me everything she knows about games, which turns out is quite a lot and now she's winning hearts as she waits to meet you.

254942.name: Dior
254942.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Dior is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Dior displays fearful and conflicted behavior, including growling when approached, wariness of handling, trembling, and tensing during physical contact. She may become fixated on dogs in the environment and has been observed pulling toward and vocalizing at other dogs during walks. Dior is social with staff when they go slow with her, seeks out proximity to some handlers, and will lean into petting when comfortable but is struggling to acclimate in the care center. Medically, Dior is slightly underweight and has a mass on her tail.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A volunteer writes: Dior is a victim of circumstance. She lost her family when they were deported. A family member took her in and was trying to find her a home, but ultimately she came to us in hopes of a new start.
Dior is just a joy. She is large, jowly, and so very sweet. We quickly learn Dior knows all the tricks - sit, down, paw, and even a crowd favorite, roll over! She easily flops onto her back, waiting for her congratulatory belly rubs. She tips the scale at 85 pounds, but is demure and gentle enough to pass for less. Dior has been reported to be very fearful at the shelter, sometimes just seen shaking. When we meet her, she has had some time to acclimate to her new surroundings and seems very brave, soft, and social. She plays with toys, snuggles, and snacks. Dior is about 2 years old. She spent most of her time in the basement or backyard in her previous home, but we have limited information about that.

254957.summary:
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A volunteer writes: Red came to us from a home with many other cats and considerably less experience with people. Adjusting to Care Center life is a big ask but Red's determined to do so, provided she gets a little help from some new friends. She wasn't particularly interested when I offered my hand in friendship and we had a bit of a Goldilocks situation with treats until Red's favorite volunteer told me which one she likes best. After snacks, Red decided I could now pet her. Gently and very subtly leaning her neck into my hand for some scritches, she allowed herself to make a friend. We fully recognize and respect what a big step this is for her. Shelter life can be a lot and Red tends to feel most comfortable when it's a bit more quiet, but please come and fall in love with Red's potential at the Staten Island Care Center.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Rocky is at risk due to behavioral concerns. He arrived at the Care Center with limited history. Upon arrival Rocky was aloof and allowed petting. However when approached for medical exam Rocky was noted to become defensive and attempt to bite when vaccines were being administered. Similarly, during his handling assessment he was initially neutral bodied but became tense and seek exit when attempting to place a collar on him. Unfortunately, Rocky is difficult to handle safely due to persistently grabbing and tugging leashes into kennel when handlers attempt to take him for walks and is very difficult to refocus with treats or squeaker toys. Medically, Rocky has Brachycephalic Syndrome and unspecified dermatitis.

Rocky arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Rocky has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to growl, snap, and attempt to bite when vaccines were being administered. During his medical exam Rocky began hard barking and lunging towards handlers. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

254974.name: Patty Pie
254974.summary:
A volunteer writes:
I had a patty pie yesterday bought from a fancy bakery. I really liked it! I can see why staff gave our Patty Pie such a name! He is so sweet and seems so comfi in his kennel, laying lavishly sideways, stretching, making biscuits and throwing non stop slow blinks at me... A Zen Cat! He can play too with catnip toys and feather wans and never ever gets carred away!Patty Pie is not orange(like the real pie) but pitch ebony, shiny, silky and such a pleasure to pet. We basically enjoy each other company! I so wish a nice new owner or family could come true for him... Patty Pie tested positive for FIV on a SNAP test(the adoption counselors can walk you through this presumptive diagnosis). FIV is confined to felines only and can only be acquired though a bite and this is why, although FIV+ cats can live with non FIV+ kitties, all the cats(if there are any others) in the household must be spayed and neutered. Patty Pie is a great and loving cat who so deserves a wonderful home. Come and meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center.

254993.name: Ice Age
254993.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ice Age is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Ice Age is deteriorating in the kennel environment and has been observed biting at the kennel bars in an attempt to reach staff members' fingers. In one instance, he made contact with a staff member's nail but did not break the skin. He has also been reported to scale the walls of his kennel, fixate on a corner of the kennel, and engage in leash-biting behavior. Despite receiving daily enrichment, Ice Age is having a difficult time managing his stress and coping with the shelter environment. Outside of the kennel, Ice Age is social with staff, readily engages with people, and takes treats appropriately. Medically, Ice Age recently recovered from pneumonia and is physically healthy at this time. 

Ice Age is a social dog when outside of his kennel. According to his owner, he is friendly and social with children, strangers, and other dogs. However, while in the Care Centers, Ice Age has begun displaying concerning kennel-related behaviors. He has been observed biting at the kennel bars while staff attempt to unlock his kennel, and in one instance, he made contact with a staff member's finger. He has also started grabbing staff members' leashes, making it difficult to safely remove him from his kennel. Due to these behaviors, Ice Age should be placed through a New Hope Partner into an adult-only home with the ability to manage and modify his kennel-related stress and handling concerns using positive reinforcement-based techniques.


Meet Ice Age!

Ice Age is an active, playful dog with a friendly personality and a love for spending time with his people. He enjoys relaxing in the bedroom and living room and is happiest when he has a comfortable space to hang out and be part of the family.

While Ice Age enjoys affection, he prefers interaction on his own terms and appreciates having his boundaries respected. He knows the commands "sit" and "come here," and he's especially motivated by his favorite treat-Slim Jims!

Ice Age can be fearful when it comes to grooming. He does not enjoy baths or brushing, so he will thrive with a patient adopter who can help him build confidence and make grooming a positive experience.

One of Ice Age's best qualities is his social nature. He is friendly, outgoing, playful, and tolerant around dogs, children, and strangers, making him a wonderful companion for a variety of households.

If you're looking for a fun-loving, active dog who enjoys companionship and has a sweet, easygoing personality, Ice Age may be the perfect addition to your family!

254995.name: Oreo Cheesecake
254995.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Oreo Cheesecake is at risk due to behavioral concerns reported in his previous home. Oreo Cheesecake has bitten his previous owner three times in the past and has a history of spinning in circles/chasing his tail while growling since he was a puppy, will growl and bark at strangers if approached too fast, is reactive to other dogs during walks; and he escalates to growling and snapping during any form of grooming.  All three bites were bites and releases. Medically, Oreo Cheesecake is cryptorchid, and there is concern for neurological disease due to his persistently spinning and growling. 

Oreo Cheesecake was surrendered by his previous owner due to behavior concerns that have been worsening over time. His family described him as very playful and very active. But he has bitten one of his owners three times in the past; the two most recent bites broke skin, and the first did not. The first two were due to being dried after a bath and attempting to bathe him; the last and most recent was when the owner opened his crate door, ushering him inside. Oreo Cheesecake is noted to growl and spin in circles/chase his tail and has been doing this since he was a puppy. This behavior was seen during his intake, his medical exam, and during his stay in care. Due to these concerns, we reccommend for Oreo Cheesecake be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can address his concerns after consultation with a professional trainer/ or veterinary behaviorist, as it is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Oreo Cheesecake presents with outside of the care centers.

254998.name: Knight
254998.summary:
Knight is a handsome 5-year-old mixed breed with a big personality and an even bigger heart. His previous family describes him as social, affectionate, playful, and active, while also being happy to relax nearby after a day of fun. He loves car rides, playing with his ball, and spending time with his people, and he's reported to be friendly with strangers, children, and dogs he knows.

Knight is housetrained, enjoys regular walks, and has lived successfully with a child. He can be anxious at times and may jump up when excited. He is uncomfortable around unfamiliar dogs that approach him, especially off leash, so he'll do best with thoughtful introductions and an adopter who can help him feel secure on walks.  He's also reported to have a chicken allergy, so his new family should keep that in mind when choosing treats and food.

If you're looking for an affectionate, fun-loving companion who will happily join you on adventures and then curl up nearby for a well-earned nap, Knight may be your perfect match!

255019.name: Lightning
255019.summary:
A volunteer writes: To some dogs, an RV means an adventure with their family. To Lightning and his friend Thunder, it was the place they were abandoned, who knows for how long, before park rangers discovered them. Upon intake, both were too skinny and understandably fearful, but have started to show their true, loving selves.
Lightning, initially aloof, has an undeniable, scruffy schnauzer charm to him. Even though he initially didn't pay much attention to me, he now readily comes when called and enjoys pets. He is easy to leash and walk with, and seems okay with other dogs. In a brief gate dog intro, he appeared uncertain and disengaged after a greeting. Bonus: he's been very housebroken with us.

255020.name: Thunder
255020.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

A volunteer writes: Thunder wears his heart on his furry sleeve. He loves to drape himself over my lap, put his paws up on my chest so I can massage his sides, and is generous with affection. When introduced to toys, he first wasn't sure what to do, but has since started bouncing after a tennis ball, like the puppy he still is. He's all legs and moves with the endearing grace of a teenager who just shot up six inches overnight. Thunder seems positive towards and interested in other dogs and is non-reactive on walks. What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
Tom interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience, demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: I stand to learn a lot from a cat who puts herself out there like uncertainty is a gift, who shares her trust because she knows it will only ever be returned. Meet Tom, my role model and someone very much in need of a family. Sitting as close as she possibly can to the door with her little paws tucked beneath her, first, she looks adorable, but she also knows that someone has to see her in order to give her the chance she's counting on. Exuberantly rolling herself into my arms and waiting for whatever is happening next, it's easy to fall in love with this little round love of a cat. Tom was brought to us with other cats and though in her previous home she preferred to stand back and watch before making her entrance, she's been trying to put her right in the middle of the action here at the shelter.
