255037.name: Clinton
255037.summary:
**Behavior Summary - Clinton**

Clinton is a sweet and playful cat who has shown significant progress in confidence during his time in the shelter. While he initially presented as quiet, reserved, and somewhat unsure of handling, he has gradually become more comfortable with people and now actively seeks out interaction and attention. He enjoys treats, purrs during social interactions, and has demonstrated an interest in engaging with people, even while still working through some uncertainty in unfamiliar situations.

As Clinton has become more comfortable, his playful and energetic side has emerged. He appears to enjoy interactive engagement and can become highly focused on food, toys, and moving objects. During his most recent evaluation, some swatting behaviors were observed; however, these appeared more consistent with playful or overstimulated behavior rather than fear or aggression. Shelter staff believe that a lack of appropriate outlets for his energy in the shelter environment may be contributing to these responses.

Clinton may need some time to adjust to a new home and build confidence with his adopters. Providing regular play sessions, enrichment activities, climbing opportunities, and interactive toys will likely help him channel his energy appropriately and continue developing positive social behaviors. With patience and understanding, Clinton has the potential to be a fun, affectionate companion who enjoys both attention and playtime with his people.

A volunteer writes: Crosby was found with other cats wandering around a building hallway. Trying to fit in and find a place to go couldn't have been easy for the group, but things turned their way when a Good Samaritan scooped them up and brought them to us. Stretched out at the front of his condo when I visited, Crosby leaped into his cubby when I opened the door. Asking for just a tiny bit of patience so that considering the path of our friendship from there, Crosby sweetly leaned his head out from his cubby a few times before leaning down to snuggle into my hand. Extravagantly kneading his blanket, Crosby made it look like all he wanted to do was come out and cuddle, but we, of course, understand that shelter life can be a lot.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Stella is at the front of the kennel, pupils slightly dilated, leaning her body against the kennel door to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, Stella head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting and raising her back as she is pet. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front and continues to lean into all further petting. Stella cranes her neck to look at the neighboring cats and hisses at them a couple times during the interaction. She is able to be easily maneuvered back into the kennel, and her attention is easily refocused with soft talk and petting.

A sweet and sociable lady who welcomes pets, even if she isn't really one to seek them out, Kiara's been quietly waiting for someone to notice her.

255055.name: Snow White
255055.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Snow White is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display challenging, distance-increasing behaviors. During cleaning hours, she is quick to lunge, hiss, and swat out at staff. These behaviors make successful interactions difficult. Upon arriving at the care center, she tolerated minimal pets and currently does not tolerate any form of handling. It is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. Snow White would benefit from a low-traffic home with an experienced adopter. Medically, she is overweight and has mild dental disease.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

Meet Snow White!

We don't know too much about Snow White's backstory but we're trying to get to know her a little better. As a new addition to the shelter, she is still trying to unwind and get comfortable in a new environment with a lot of stimuli. Our hope is with time and a patient adopter Snow White can fully decompress in an environment where she feels safe and respected. She'd do best in an adult-only home where she's given the choice to interact on her terms. Positive reinforcement through treats and toys will definitely help her along, too. Think you can be her Prince Charming? Some to SIACC and say hello to Snow White today!

255057.name: Milo Bean
255057.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Milo Bean is a real sunshine! He is one of the most pleasant cats we have right now at the care center! He is a great patient and this from Day One and a real socialite who enjoys petting, purrs, head bunts and plays quite nicely with toys despite his broken left humerus(front leg)that he appears to be using better after a few days spent in the medical room. It is possible (as there is some callous formation where the fracture is at) that a month cage rest might save him from an amputation. It is still to be determined. Whatever the outcome, Milo Bean is a great cat and will always be. He will make a wonderful companion to the person who will adopt him and brighten their life with his presence. Milo Bean is waiting for his forever at the Manhattan Care Center.








What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Milo Bean is at the front of the kennel, pupils dilated, rolling around and rubbing his cheeks against the kennel bars to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he gets up, leaning forward to head bunt and lean his body against the assessor's hand. He allows and leans into all petting, raising his back and purring as he is pet, tail held high throughout the interaction. He flops over onto his side, rubbing his cheeks on the floor and the assessor's hands, leaning in and closing his eyes when he is pet on the head and cheeks. Milo Bean is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm, purring, and leaning against the assessor as he is held. When he is placed back into his kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to head bunt to solicit further attention and continuing to lean into all petting.

Milo Bean interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

255061.name: Photon
255061.summary:
Photon arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Photon has been observed to be highly fearful. He has been noted to be reluctant to allow handling. During his assessment Photon was observed to have a tense body, tucked tail, head whipped upon contact, and lip licked. He was also easily startled by very minimal stimuli. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home. 

A Volunteer Wrote: The way this gentle, angelic  dog loves his treats, prancing and dancing for them and then taking them with the most beautiful manners, I would have been happy to stuff him with every one I could get my hands on. But then I would have missed sitting quietly on a park bench with him, his legs on my lap as he calmly took in the beautiful day around him. Photon is the perfect mix of chill--he is unbothered by anyone or anything who approaches him--and fun, lighting up when he's shown attention and love. It would be a joy to live with him, and if you're very lucky, you will be able to experience this in person soon!

255067.name: Elvis Purrsley
255067.summary:
My Foster Writes: Elvis is a sweet, gentle, playful, confident 5 year old who will solicit "touch" attention frequently. He is especially active in the morning and will wake you up with head bunts and kisses. He loves to play -- especially any wand/pole toys with feathers and bells. Elvis is indifferent to catnip toys but will but will lick his favorite Churu treats from your fingers or a spoon. Elvis loves TV (especially Animal Planet cat videos) and will stay on your lap or beside you as long as he can.

A volunteer writes:
Elvis Purrsley is a handsome tall Grey and a very gentle cat. Every single volunteer at the care center enjoys interacting with him as he not only a pleasure for the eyes but also a friendly and welcoming cat who appears right away at his door when he has a visitor. Given a chance, he will come on the lap, not to escape but to get more petting which he is very fond of. Actually, he now appreciates very much being held in the arms(see pictures). Bring a feather wand and Elvis will play his heart out! Elvis does not get carried away when he plays or is being petted. He is a well mannered cat! A Good Samaritan saw Elvis Purrsley struggling in the street for a few weeks and decided that it was about time to find a loving home for him. Elvis was a bit wary and for days after his arrival at the care center but this is history. He is apparently healthy , did very well on his behavior evaluation(LEVEL1) and will be able to go home with you after his neuter. Ask about Elvis when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!



Elvis Purrsley is at the front of the kennel, slow blinking as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he immediately leans forward to head bunt the assessor's hand, allowing all petting and raising his back as he is pet. He is able to be easily picked up and remains calm when he is held, purring, leaning his body against the assessor, and firmly leaning into petting on the head and cheeks. He is able to be held and pet for an extended period and continues to purr throughout the duration of being held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, allowing all further petting. 

Elvis Purrsley interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

255074.name: Uno
255074.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Uno is a calm, thoughtful staple of Kittyfield, one of our Free Roaming Cat Rooms. He is an under-socialized young man from a hoarding case, so while he is still getting used to humans, he thrives around other cats. He can often be found lounging in a window in the sunshine, napping in one of the soft beds, playing with toys or eagerly eating up treats. He is quite happy to sit near us and eat some of his favorite squeeze-up. He welcomes new cats in the room and shows them that there is no need to hide, as being around humans who respect your space isn't all that scary after all. Uno is waiting for his perfect home: adults who love him for the unique, independent boy he is, ideally with some other cats to spend his lazy days with.

A volunteer writes: I could see Uno rethinking his decision to sit at the front of his condo as soon as I opened the door and my heart went out to him in response. I was in the middle of explaining that there's always time to get a re-do and sometimes a few of them if needed, but Uno hopped onto his ledge, or at least halfway hopped up. He considered me as I admired his big gorgeous face and brightly curious eyes.

255075.name: Deuce
255075.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Deuce is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she does attempt to flee and avoid human contact. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Please speak to an adoption counselor to learn more about socialization techniques.

255076.name: Tre
255076.summary:
Tre is an exceptionally friendly, affectionate, and easygoing cat who thrives on human companionship. He is a social butterfly who readily seeks out attention, greets people enthusiastically, and enjoys being involved in daily household activities. In both his previous home and the shelter, Tre has consistently demonstrated a loving and people-oriented personality, often following his family around, cuddling in laps, and soliciting affection whenever the opportunity arises.

Tre is comfortable with handling and enjoys physical affection, including petting, being picked up, held, brushed, and cuddled. He frequently greets people with head bunts, trills, and a raised tail, and readily leans into attention from both familiar and unfamiliar people. While not especially interested in vigorous play, he is content spending time relaxing with his people and observing his surroundings.

His previous home described him as friendly and tolerant with both adults and a young child, and his history of living among many other cats suggests he may also adapt well to a multi-cat household. Throughout his time in the shelter, Tre has remained confident, affectionate, and highly social, even after experiencing major life changes.

Overall, Tre is a gentle, loving companion who is likely to fit seamlessly into many different home environments. His affectionate nature, adaptability, and ease with handling make him an excellent match for adopters of any experience level seeking a devoted and cuddly feline friend.

A volunteer writes: Sei only wants to say hello and be included, or at least she thinks she does. Sitting as close as she possibly can to her door, she waits and waits for someone to take her up on her sincerest offers of friendship only to hop away when they do. This may be Sei's next step because it's her preference or because she doesn't know any differently, but building a friendship with Sei might take some time. She loves bubble shows and is so curious about us and what we have to offer. She usually isn't quite sure what to make of pets as she came to us from a home with many other cats and she also just might have her preferences, but she'd love a chance to become a friend in a way that makes sense to her.

255081.name: Ocho
255081.summary:
Meet Ocho. This girl has come an incredibly long way since arriving at the shelter from a large hoarding situation where she shared her home with more than 50 other cats. With so many feline roommates, it's no surprise that people are still a bit of a mystery to her. But every day she's showing us that she's braver than she was the day before.

The fastest way to Ocho's heart is playtime! Wave a wand toy and watch her transform from a cautious observer into a silly, energetic kitten at heart. She loves chasing feather toys, batting catnip mice across the floor, and pouncing with enthusiasm. Once she's having fun, her curious personality really begins to shine.

Ocho is still learning that human hands are kind and safe. When she feels unsure, she simply asks for a little more space. Ocho is looking for a calm, understanding home with adopters who will celebrate all her little wins and build that special bond with her. Please give her a chance to win you over and bring many giggles and games to your life.

255095.name: Oolong
255095.summary: My foster writes: Oolong came to us as a very spicy feral kitty. With time, patience, and encouragement Oolong's gone from a hissy spitting kitten, to a friendly, energetic, curious kitty who loves head butts and to be pet. That said, he is still warming up and gets spooked if people approach him too fast. But he bounces back quickly. He will chase/follow us in and out of rooms and likes to be within eyesight of us. He will lay on the couch with us at a comfortable distance and if you approach slowly he will welcome pets. He loves to carry his toys around the house with him in his mouth (even the ones twice his size). Oolong will do well with an adopter who is willing to move as slowly as he needs for major payoffs!

255098.name: Day Dream
255098.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Day Dream is the tiniest adult calico I ever saw. She is not even 4 pounds...Day Dream was left behind in a basement with 16 other kitties, all shy or even fearful. She is quiet in her kennel, seemingly asleep but she is not. She wants you to think she does not exist and leave the premises. Day dream accepts petting without a move or a 'word". Will she ever be ready in a shelter environment to interact with us or potential adopters? I do not know. Some of her housemates did, others did not but were given a chance to open up in a home environment anyway. Will that chance happen for beautiful and tiny Day Dream, I very much hope so.. A caring, patient, experienced and understanding adopter is needed who will offer the pretty Calico a quiet and loving adult home(no young children), waking her up to a good and happy life. Day Dream is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center. 




Day Dream is laying curled up at the back of the kennel, appearing asleep as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and she is softly spoken to, she opens her eyes, observing the assessor with dilated pupils and a tense body. She is tolerant of all petting, not engaging with it through most of the interaction but leaning in slightly when she is pet on the head and cheeks. The assessor attempts to pull her forward to attempt pickup, and she is able to be maneuvered close to the front of the kennel before she lets out a hiss, ears back. The assessor stops attempting pickup, allowing her to return to laying curled up at the back of the kennel. Day Dream continues to tolerate all petting but does lip lick when she is pet, not escalating any further. 

Day Dream is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appears wary of human contact. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes:
Laces is a sweet and shy little tiger who comes from a house full of cats. Still, unlike many cats who lived in "tribes", Laces has made progress while at the care center. He is timid, it is a given but he has "worked hard on himself" with the help of staff and volunteers, of course. His body relaxes now with soft words and spreads on his cubby's floor, accepting caresses, leaning into pets and even purring(see videos). Laces is really a gentle soul.  "Landing" in a shelter is not easy for a cat who has not been exposed to what we expect to be a normal pet's life but Laces has shown to us that he is capable to cope with changes. An understanding, patient, caring and loving new owner, working at Laces' pace will make all the difference in his life. Sweet Laces is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.

With select handlers T'challa has been noted to be receptive to treats. Medically, T'Challa is being treated for CIRDC. T'Challa arrived at MACC following a bite incident. The owner reports that there was a dog bite incident in the home. When the owner attempted to break up the fight, T'Challa redirected and bit the owner on the thumb, causing a puncture wound. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

255124.name: Marcy
255124.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
Marcy is laying on her top shelf, observing the assessor with wide eyes, dilated pupils, and a slightly tense body as the kennel door is opened. She is spoken to softly and after a few moments begins making little air biscuits and returning slow blinks. She is still hesitant to get up but leans into petting on the head and cheeks and closes her eyes as she is pet. When pet down her body, she is initially slightly tense, but with more soft talk appears to relax, body loosening up a bit. She is able to be picked up but is a bit tense when held. When placed back down, she moves further back into the shelf. After a minute or two of soft talk she resumes kneading and leans into further petting on the head and cheeks.

Marcy appears to enjoy attention and petting but seems to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

255125.name: Marty
255125.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Marty is laying on top of his den, observing the assessor with wide eyes as they approach. When the kennel door is opened and he is softly spoken to for a few seconds, he begins rolling onto his side on top of his den, rubbing his cheeks against the top of the den door. He is able to be called to the front of the kennel, greeting the assessor with a firm head bunt. When the cats around him begin to shuffle and make noises, he cranes his neck to look at them and around the room, tail flicking but not escalating. He is able to be easily maneuvered back, continuing to allow and lean into petting. Marty is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, head bunting and allowing all further handling.

Marty interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

255132.name: Ozzy
255132.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Ozzy is at risk due to behavior concerns. He arrived at the care centers as a stray with no known history. Upon intake he had a loose wiggly body and was social with staff. However, during his medical intake exam he was reported to be hard barking, growling and lunging at the kennel door. Throughout his stay, Ozzy has remained social with handlers and readily participates in training sessions. In kennel he has been reported to be jumping and barking as handlers approach, but recently, Ozzy has displayed increased kennel stress. His kennel door has been noted to be covered in saliva and he has been observed to lunge, hard bark, and jump on his kennel door, even escalating to snarling and biting when touching his kennel card. Medically, he has otitis externa.

Meet Ozzy!
Ozzy came to the care center as a stray, so we're still getting to know him. While the shelter environment can make him seem loud and intimidating in his kennel, that's only one small part of who he is. Once he's out for a walk or spending one-on-one time with people, Ozzy relaxes into a sweet, affectionate companion who enjoys exploring, leaning in for pets, and building connections with those he trusts.

My Ideal Home
Ozzy is looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who can continue helping him build confidence. He benefits from calm, predictable handling and enjoys enrichment activities, sniffy walks, and interactive toy games. He's a smart dog who has already shown he enjoys training sessions and responds well to positive reinforcement. With consistency, patience, and opportunities to decompress, Ozzy has all the tools to continue thriving.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 years old. Ozzy can become uncomfortable in stressful situations and would do best in an adult-only home where his body language and boundaries are respected.

Good with Other Pets?
Ozzy has generally walked calmly past other dogs in the shelter and has not shown significant reactivity on outings. Because his history is unknown, any introductions to resident pets should be slow and carefully managed.

Overall Health
Healthy overall.

Behavior Determination
Level 4 - Experienced Adopters. Ozzy has displayed fearful and defensive behaviors around his kennel and has shown mild resource guarding during his behavior assessment. Outside of the kennel, however, he is consistently social, enjoys gentle affection, and has made excellent progress through enrichment and training. He will do best with adopters who are committed to continuing positive reinforcement training, respecting his boundaries, and helping him feel safe as he settles into a home.

Other Fun Facts
Ozzy loves to sniff and explore, enjoys interactive toy trades, and has become quite the training student! When he's comfortable, he'll lean into you for pets, happily ask for belly rubs, and gently nudge your hand for more affection. Volunteers and trainers have watched him grow more relaxed over time, showing just how much his sweet personality shines once he's out of the kennel and spending quality time with people.

255142.name: Valentino
255142.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Valentino!
Valentino came to ACC when his owner could no longer care for him. This handsome guy is equal parts couch potato and adventure buddy, happily enjoying a cozy nap at home just as much as a car ride or a game of fetch. While he can be a little independent at first, Valentino is very affectionate once he gets to know his people and is looking for a patient adopter who will let him warm up at his own pace.

My Ideal Home
Valentino would thrive with someone who appreciates his independent streak and is committed to continuing his positive reinforcement training. He already knows several cues, and will benefit from continued work on his leash manners and confidence around some of his triggers. A calm, predictable home will help him settle in and succeed.

Good with Other Pets?
Valentino has lived with small dogs before. Slow introductions would be the best fit for him.

Good with Kids?
An adult-only home is recommended for Valentino. He enjoys affection on his own terms and will do best with people who respect his boundaries and allow him to build trust at his own pace.

Things to Know
Valentino is a smart, easygoing pup who enjoys the simple things in life, whether that's lounging on the couch, riding in the car, or chasing a tennis ball. He takes treats gently, has lovely manners with people he trusts, and is ready to find a forever home that will help him continue building confidence while enjoying all of life's little adventures.

255146.name: Kingsley
255146.summary:
Meet Kingsley!
Kingsley is a handsome senior gentleman who's looking for a calm, understanding home to spend his golden years in. His previous owner described him as anxious when left alone, but also noted that he's easygoing with everyday handling and unbothered by things like being woken up, touched on his paws, or having his collar handled. At the shelter, Kingsley has been more reserved, preferring to sniff around quietly and politely approach for treats.

My Ideal Home
Kingsley would do best in a patient, lower-key home where he can settle in at his own pace and enjoy a predictable routine. He's looking for adopters who understand that sometimes the sweetest companions are the quiet ones.

Good with Other Pets?
Kingsley has shown neutral behavior around other dogs at the shelter, though his previous owner noted that he may guard food or treats around other dogs. Careful management around high value items and slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to Kingsley's reported resource guarding, ACC recommends a home with older, respectful children who can follow his boundaries or an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Kingsley is a more independent guy who enjoys exploring at his own pace and is especially motivated by treats. He can become uncomfortable with prolonged handling and may show subtle signs like lip licking or tensing when unsure, so he'll do best with people who respect his space and communication. Kingsley may also experience some anxiety when left alone and would benefit from patience, enrichment, and a calm environment as he adjusts to home life again.

A volunteer writes: When I look at Kingsley's frost-kissed muzzle, I see a testament to the 9 years he spent loving and being loved, until housing insecurity made him lose everything he knew. The humans, dog, and cats he lived with. The bed he slept on. The car rides he enjoyed. 

Finding himself at a loud shelter with a vision impairment must be incredibly scary, but Kingsley navigates this new world the best he can. He's happy to join me for a walk (he's been housebroken with regular walks) and maintains a puppy-like curiosity, even jumping into the pool without my prodding. He patiently sniffs his way through a treat scatter. When I sit down, he calmly walks up and gently snouts my pouch asking for a snack (he's very food motivated!). Kingsley is reported to be tolerant of cats, friendly with familiar dogs, and was neutral in a dog intro at the shelter. This resilient New Yorker, described by his former guardian as incredibly loyal, is looking for safety and love for his golden years.

255148.name: Jack Jack
255148.summary:
Meet Jack Jack!
Jack Jack was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now he's searching for a patient person to help him start his next chapter. This energetic, affectionate boy loves quality time with his favorite people, whether that's cuddling on the couch, heading out for adventures, or joining you on a car ride.

My Ideal Home
Jack Jack is looking for an adult-only home with someone who will give him the time and guidance he needs to build confidence. He has lots of energy and will thrive with daily exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. Once he's had a chance to burn off some steam, he's more than happy to settle in for snuggles.

Good with Other Pets?
Jack Jack prefers not to share high-value items like food or toys, so careful management and slow introductions are important if there are other pets in the home. Our staff can help determine whether he'd be a good fit for your household.

Good with Kids?
Jack Jack would do best in an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Jack Jack is a loving dog who enjoys affection on his own terms and forms strong bonds with his people. He's smart, food motivated, knows "sit," and enjoys car rides and staying active. He can be sensitive about handling around his neck and during nail trims, and he prefers to eat without interruption. With patience, gentle handling, and reward-based training, Jack Jack has all the ingredients to become an incredible lifelong companion.

255149.name: Mona Lisa
255149.summary:
A volunteer writes:
My heart goes to Mona Lisa I have "followed" since her arrival at the care center. She came with friends Monet and Matisse as they were abandoned in the lobby of an apartment building. Mona Lisa was a bit fidgety for a while as a very uncomfortable and painful dermatitis affected her, even causing a serious neck wound. Mona Lisa was never aggressive, though. She was prescribed and "anti allergic" diet and it did "miracle" on her. Mona Lisa is now feeling better, eating better and her hair is growing back, showing how beautiful she really is...Mona Lisa is a sweetheart, a friendly and welcoming little gal who lives for spending time with people, being loved and love. She is petite and absolutely gorgeous like a painting. Mona Lisa is already spayed, aced her behavior evaluation and could go home today with you. She will likely need to be on a prescription diet for the rest of her life unless indicated otherwise by an outside veterinarian once adopted. Mona Lisa is dreaming to be home ...with you.







Mona Lisa has made wonderful improvement since her first assessment and was at the front of the kennel, rubbing against the door. She's curious, alert, and sweet, and when the door was opened, she rubbed against the assessor, leaning in for cheek rubs. She's affectionate and slightly energetic, highly interactive, and was calm when picked up and held in the assessor's arms, where she stayed for at least a minute before gently going back into the kennel, where she remained interactive and a little bit grabby through the bars.

Mona Lisa interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

255151.name: Matisse
255151.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

A volunteer writes: Matisse came to us with two other cats in a taped cardboard box and not a whole lot of information. Abandoned in a building hallway, the trio was brought to us to help get started on their next step and Matisse has been trying his best to do his part. Stretched out at the front of his cubby like he's without a care in the world, we know that might not be quite the case but we appreciate the efforts to say otherwise. Matisse allows some petting, but isn't one to seek them out himself. He's hoping to find a patient and loving family who will give him the time and space he'd like to come out on his own terms.

255158.name: Nene
255158.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Nene is a cute little tiger found "lost" on a fire escape. A Good Samaritan got hold of him and brought him to safety to the care center. A tinsy winsy shy at first, Nene bloomed into a sweet, friendly and welcoming kitty, happy to have company, love and treats. He plays quite well with a feather wand but is mainly focused on his visitor, soaking all the petting he can get. Nene is rather calm, well mannered and an all together very pleasant pet to be around with. The cute and sweet little tiger is wondering, though why he is still sitting in a kennel when he has so much love to give...I can not even imagine how happy he will be the day he will be home, safe, cared for and loved by a new owner or family, for ever this time. Come and meet lovely Nene at the Manhattan Care Center.







Nene is laying in his cubby, head up and observing the room as the assessor approaches. When the cubby door is opened, he hesitates for a moment, tail held low, before coming forward to greet the assessor at the front of the cubby. He leans forward to softly head bunt the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into petting on the head and cheeks. He is able to be easily coaxed to the main area of the kennel where he slowly comes forward, again head bunting the assessor's hand and allowing and leaning into all petting. He cranes his neck to look around at the other cats in the room, appearing curious and not escalating. He is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all petting. When the kennel door is closed and the interaction is ended, Nene walks over to his tray of wet food and begins eating.

Nene interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all petting. When the kennel door is closed and the interaction is ended, Nene walks over to his tray of wet food and begins eating.

Nene interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

255197.name: Yuki
255197.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Yukiani and Yuki, two six year old siblings, a gal and a gent, are the perfect pair surrendered to us as their owners were going through difficult times. They were beautifully cared for, two sweet and shy souls who will open up fully once in a home they can call their own. Yukiani is said to be a friendly and affectionate lap cat, very playful and particularly fond of her brother Yuki. He would feel the same toward her. Yukiani started as a shy gal when we first met but then, oh surprise, started to play like there is no tomorrow(see photos). We both enjoyed this burst of joy and carefreeness....Yuki is more reserved although his owner describe him as an equally playful cat, something he still has to show us at the care center. All together, both Yuki and Yukiani are awesome cats who yes could be adopted separately but having them both under a same roof again, might be a double pleasure for their new family and such a blessing for them. Both cats are great, beautiful, healthy apparently, did well on their behavior evaluation and are already spayed and neutered, ready to go home with you....TODAY. Come meet Yukiani and Yuki at the Manhattan Care Center!What my friends at ACC say about me:


My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.

255208.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

Ash tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: "Ash loves to be loved," his former person told us, after they relinquished this gray and white boy into our care because they had too many pets in the house. Ash's previous owner also described him as friendly, affectionate, talkative, and a snuggly lap cat who sometimes prefers to watch his people from afar. Ash likes to play with water (hey, who doesn't?), rough rope for scratching is his weakness, and being brushed puts him in kitty bliss. At the Care Center he's been calm, curious, and on the shy side, leaning in for pettings and even allowing a quick pickup while displaying a sense of uncertainty. Ash is a very sweet, well behaved guy who needs an adopter who loves to give love and will make sure Ash receives lots of it. Meet this beauty at the Manhattan Care Center today!

255219.name: Tanner
255219.summary:
```html id="6kgbmu"
Meet Tanner!
Tanner is the total package: handsome, easygoing, affectionate, and ready to find a family of his own. This charming stray arrived at ACC after being found wandering in a Bronx apartment building, and he's quickly become a favorite among staff and volunteers alike. With his sweet personality, calm demeanor, and striking one blue eye, Tanner has a way of making everyone fall in love.

My Ideal Home
Tanner would fit into a variety of homes. He enjoys spending time with people, loves attention, and has shown himself to be a calm and easy companion. Whether you're looking for a walking buddy, a couch companion, or a best friend to share everyday adventures with, Tanner is happy to be by your side.

Good with Kids?
Tanner's history with children is unknown, but he has been friendly and social with everyone he has met at the Care Centers.

Good with Other Pets?
While Tanner's history with other animals is unknown, he has shown excellent manners around dogs in the shelter. Volunteers report that he remains calm and unbothered even when other dogs are barking or getting excited around him.

Leash Manners
Tanner is a dream on leash. He walks calmly beside his handler with little pulling and has shown no reactivity to people or dogs during outings. Volunteers consistently describe him as easy, relaxed, and enjoyable to spend time with.

Overall Health
Tanner is generally healthy and heartworm negative. He is currently being treated for a mild upper respiratory infection and staff will discuss any ongoing care with potential adopters.

A Volunteer Wrote:
"It's no surprise this lunk-headed love is a volunteer favorite; he's incredibly easy (two barking dogs got in his face and he didn't give them the time of day), he's a dream on the leash, and he's got the trifecta of gifts: mellow, affectionate, and with a smile that lights up the room. Pick a compliment and his walking log is filled with them: fantastic, great, a joy to be with, a confusion that he has not yet been scooped up by a loving family. With his one blue eye, he's as easy on the eyes as he is on the heart, and we are so excited to imagine that soon Tanner will be out in the world, shining his light!"
```

255220.name: Roxy
255220.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Roxy is at risk due to behavioral reasons. While in care, Roxy has been observed to be highly dog reactive. Noted to lunge and bark towards other dogs. During one instance when a handler pulls her away, Roxy spins towards the handler and snaps at them. Recently Roxy has been observed to have a low threshold for arousal. Noted to mouth handlers persistently throughout her assessment with moderate to hard pressure. This behavior was not able to be redirected easily. During walks with handlers, Roxy is observed to have a soft body and is receptive to treats. Medically, Roxy is apparently healthy.

Roxy arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. Roxy has been observed to be highly dog reactive. Noted to lunge and bark towards other dogs when seeing them on leash. When a handler pulls her away, Roxy spins towards them and snaps. Recently Roxy has been observed to have a very low threshold for arousal. Noted to mouth handlers persistently throughout her assessment and was not able to be redirected. She would mouth handlers with moderate - hard pressure and left welts on the handler. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home that makes no trips to the dog park.

I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event onSunday, May 31 from 12PM - 4PM with Dash & Lili at Balsley Park, 306 W 57th Street, NY 10019, In front of Sur La Table. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
Peach is laying cuddled up with his siblings, lifting his head up to observe the assessor as they approach. Peach is able to be easily picked up, slightly tense when held but tolerant of it. When placed back into the kennel, he continues to allow further petting and attention. 

Peach interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Peach go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and kitten socialization.

255261.name: Bernie
255261.summary: A volunteer writes: Bernie was abandoned in a carrier but thankfully someone noticed her waiting and worked quickly to bring her to us. Though her history is a bit of a mystery, we're ready to help Bernie obtain the bright future she deserves. Quietly nestled in her little bed, Bernie noticed me outside her condo. She seemed interested in a new friend and rightfully trusted I wanted the same, so Bernie peeked her little head up before swirling herself forward into my arms for some cuddles. A sweet girl who hasn't been particularly inclined to make too much of a fuss, she's hoping to find a forever home where she'll be loved and celebrated just as she is.

255268.name: Raveena
255268.summary:
My foster writes: Raveena is a classy lady!
She a total love bug and velcro-pup. All she wants to do is whatever you want to do! From walking through the park to sitting at home watching movies, Raveena is a true companion. She's a huge fan of naps and pets, always politely asking for you to come join her for a quick snooze or snuggle. She is a little strong on leash but she knows her name and comes when called, making for a smooth yet active walk. Raveena would love a calm home with humans who will give her a lot of love!

My foster writes:
Raveena is an absolute sweetheart and anyone would be lucky to have her. She as happy on a walk as she is curled up in your lap on the couch - her size does not stop her from getting as close to you as possible! She is able to ask for pets by nudging with her hand, and enjoys treats. She enjoys human companionship and comes when called and is house trained. She would do well in a quiet home where she can lounge with her owner and also enjoy long leisurely walks exploring town. An affectionate, quiet girl, she deserves a home to relax in for her older years 💓 

 Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.

This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

On my #BoroughBreak, we... walked around a park, sat at a cafe, and hung out in my backyard. Raveena was an absolute sweetheart. She loves meeting people, is so gentle, and loves affection. She's an older lady so she likes to take it slow. She's great for the busy nyc streets: she has no problem plopping down to rest at a cafe, or in the park, is calm and unbothered. She is so loving and sweet. She deserves a loving home where she can relax and sleep on a comfy bed. In return she will give you endless love and companionship. She bonded very quickly to me and we were fast friends. She's perfect. Walks nicely on a leash, non reactive, perfect girl.

My Boroughbreaker writes: We were made aware that he loves water which was absolutely true! He drank a lot and peed a lot, but he seemed to be housebroken and waited to pee at lunch until we had just left the restaurant. He easily laid down under the table at lunch. He was great during the meal and did not beg. Typically he was great passing by other dogs, birds, people. Knows how to sit and his name. It will be important for him to be in a household where he can be exercised regularly. He was such a sweet guy and we were sad to have to turn him back in, but hope he will find his forever home very soon!

A volunteer writes: Friskie's story breaks my heart, all the more so because she's been so determined to smile through it. Seen being left outside, she soon got injured and was in need of help. Kind neighbors swooped in to get Friskie the medical attention she needed, bringing her to us to get her started on her way. Hopping around on her little lime green bandaged paw, Friskie wants to prove that she can still swirl herself into cuddles as she does everything she can to explain that she's ready to find a forever family. Affectionate and warmly welcoming, all Friskie needs is another little chance because she's truly ready to shine.

255278.name: Zebra
255278.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Zebra is extremely chatty, especially when the door to the kennel is shut. She sometimes even meows her way into a bit of a frenzy, but when the kennel door is open, she mostly quiets down and wants attention. She enjoys all petting and continues to calm down, sometimes eating treats and sometimes not, and was mostly quiet when picked up and held, although she gave the occasional meow while in the assessor's arms. She spent a few minutes in his arms, and they both seemed to enjoy it. When the kennel door was shut, she resumed her chatty ways. She also purred throughout the interaction. In time a few minutes later, she eventually quieted down.

Zebra interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.  	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheddar is a very sweet and very affectionate kitten who was sitting quietly on top of the den watching the assessor. He sniffed treats, and then leaned in for cheek rubs and rolled on his side, inviting petting on his belly, which he enjoyed. He was easy to pick up and lay gently in the assessor's arms, and when set back down, he turned and faced the assessor again, looking at him with sweet and gentle eyes. He's a very sweet and calm kitten who loves human attention.


Cheddar interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

255283.name: Uwu
255283.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Uwu is at risk due to behavior concerns. Uwu is deteriorating behaviorally despite our best efforts to provide him with daily enrichment. He has been observed repeatedly banging on his transfer door and flipping his drain cover, indicating increasing frustration and difficulty coping in the kennel environment. Uwu was noted to have multiple puncture wounds on his face when he first arrived at the Care Centers. Outside of his kennel, Uwu is a social and engaging dog who readily enjoys petting, treats, and toys. He has also been observed in the pens and was not reactive toward other dogs. Medically, Uwu was recently treated for CIRDC and is currently healthy. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I am playful and cute!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

Hi there! My name is Uwu and I've been at the Manhattan ACC since May (yes, you read that right)! I arrived as a stray so the staff don't know what my life was like before coming to ACC, but I had various injuries that I'm recovering from really well. I only require a little extra paperwork to be filled out and a few extra vet visits this year because one of my injuries was likely a bite wound (now fully healed). I'm thankful for everyone at ACC taking such good care of me, but I think I'd like to find my forever home now. So what are you waiting for? Ask about me today!

255298.name: Tyrion Rexford
255298.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Tyrion Rexford is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Despite our best efforts at keeping him comfortable, Tyrion has begun to show signs of stress while in care and arousal concerns. He has been observed to flip and pull the drain cover up and move it into the kennel.Recently, he has been observed attempting to redirect onto handlers during walks following displays of dog reactivity. This redirection involves mouthing the handler's arm, making contact without breaking the skin or causing welts or bruising.. With handlers Tyrion has been observed to be highly social and affectionate. Noted to have a neutral body and soft wagging tail. During these interactions Tyrion has been known to escalated to mounting handlers and needing to be pulled off as he isn't easily redirected. Medically, Tyrion Rexford is currently healthy as he has recently recovered from CIRDC.


This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Tyrion Rexford has not adjusted well to the care center environment and has begun to show signs of stress while in care and arousal concerns. He has been observed to flip and pull the drain cover up and move it into the kennel. With handlers Tyrion has been observed to be highly social and affectionate. Noted to have a neutral body and soft wagging tail. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!

Biscotti interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

255312.name: Xhylo
255312.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Xhylo is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Xhylo has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and remains highly fearful and avoidant despite best efforts to keep her comfortable. She has been easy to remove from the kennel and walks well on a loose leash, but she remains avoidant of interaction, with her tail tucked and body tense. Medically, Xhylo is underweight.

Xhylo was surrendered to the Care Centers due to her previous owner relocating and not having the ability to care for her. Her previous family described her as a social, affectionate, quiet dog who preferred contact on her own terms. She would spend most of her time lounging in her bed, her crate, or in the living room. Getting in /being in a car makes her nervous, but after a while, she will lay down and get comfortable. Her favorite foods are apples and turkey-flavored treats; her favorite toys are made of rope and hard toys she can chew on. During her stay in care, Xhyloh has been highly fearful and avoided interactions with handlers and staff. She has escalated to growling and lunging in the kennel, biting a lead on one occasion when being removed from the kennel. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and reevaluate her behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: She "always remembers her way home" is one of the saddest owner surrender notes I've read in a long time. Many of us have dogs who know which corner to turn and which door belongs to them - their home. Xhylo lost all that a few weeks ago, and at 3 years old her world has been turned upside down. In her original home she was fearful of strangers, and of course that's continued at the shelter. She moves away from us at times, flinches at surprising noises, and watches everything around her quietly and alertly. Her chocolate brown eyes soften when she finds out about our peanut butter, and her former guardian describes her as a cuddle monster 💕 While we don't see her cuddle monster side she relaxes into some head scratches.

Due to her fear, Xhylo is looking for a rescue and an adult home to decompress in

255317.name: Mali
255317.summary:
My foster writes: Mali is a sweet girl who transitioned from the outdoor life to a professional indoor lovebug. She made herself at home instantly, greeting her foster parent with immediate purrs, chin rubs, and a high-tail salute.
Mali is an active explorer who loves to check out high places, track bugs, and watch the birds from the window. She is also an absolute prolific biscuit maker. When she's in a cuddly mood, the kneading just doesn't stop! She is vocal, confident, and completely unbothered by loud noises and moving things around.
Mali prefers playtime and cuddles over spa days. She can be a little sensitive about being brushed on her back, but she's making great progress and can be won over with a post-meal routine! She is comfortable with being picked up and nail-trimming sessions.
Mali has so much love to give and will make the ultimate companion for anyone looking for a sweet friend.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

255319.name: Iceman
255319.summary:
My Borough Breaker writes:
Don't let the name fool you-"Iceman" may have those striking, glacier-blue eyes, but this beautiful girl is pure warmth. She is incredibly sweet, gentle, and calm-truly one of the most well-mannered dogs I've ever spent time with. I still can't get over how good she was. On leash, she was absolute perfection: no pulling, no lunging, no barking-just a steady, relaxed walk right by my side. We took on the full city experience-dogs, kids on scooters, sirens-and nothing phased her. Even when other dogs barked and lunged, she remained completely calm... a total stoic queen. I didn't hear her bark once all day. She politely picked out a few toys at the pet store, then enjoyed a peaceful afternoon in the park-sniffing, strolling, and lounging in the grass, quietly watching the world go by. At lunch, she settled right at my feet at an outdoor table, perfectly content just being near her person. There's something really special about her-she feels like an old soul. The way she moves through the world is calm, steady, and thoughtful. With her stunning looks and incredibly easygoing nature, she would fit beautifully into just about any home. She's the kind of dog who makes life feel a little more peaceful. Please consider giving this gentle girl the home she so deserves.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

255320.name: Kloe
255320.summary:
A volunteer writes:
I met Khloe the day after her arrival at the care center. A cute and petite grey tiger she was, a bit shy while curious and slowly moving out of her den to meet me. An intake staff told me that she was sooo sweet, seeking pets and purring upon arrival. I heard that she was even a good girl with the veterinary team! Yep, Khloe is a sweet young gal, surrenderd with friend Kira because of landlord issues. She comes with wonderful comments from her former family who told us that she is usually a little shy to start with but is great with strangers, other cats(in this case, her housemate) and visiting kids. She would.loved to play, cuddle with her family and enjoyed belly rubs. Khloe is a must to meet. She is apparently healthy, will be spayed on 5/27 and be ready to go home with you! Come and meet Kloe very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!

255328.name: Green Bin
255328.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Green Bin is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give his plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
Green Bin tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

A volunteer writes: I know Green Bin likes to stay committed to his get off my lawn vibes, and I respect it, but I don't think it's the whole story. In fact, I know it isn't. In his previous home, Green Bin was known as a very sweet cat. Situations change and sometimes we have no choice but to change along with them, which could at least partially be why Green Bin has been struggling a bit to settle himself into shelter life. Green Bin responds to a little bit of extra time, patience, and gentleness with slow blinks that could melt anyone's heart.

255339.name: Rock
255339.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am bonded to Stash 255340. We must go home together and our adoption fee includes both of us!
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
My purr motor is always running!
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I love to play and will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

A volunteer writes: Rock and Stash roll over to show their bellies, if not in tandem, then at least in response to pets. Sleeping on two different levels of their condo and neither feeling particularly inclined to fully greet the day, which is ok because their greetings for me were perfect - a little stretch and a flash of belly that I could just imagine snuggling up next to. Rock reached himself out big and enthusiastically stretched a paw out to me while Stash curled his little paws in and his head into my hand. Though Rock and Stash really love each other, as seen by the way they groom and stay close, this pair has experience with dogs and has lived with other cats and children. Above all, however, both are reportedly friendly and outgoing with all. They're particularly playful young cats who enjoy being wherever people are and are hoping to soon be close to you.

255341.name: Rango
255341.summary: Hi there, I'm Rango! I am the sweetest little man looking for my forever family. I grew up in a house with other kitties and young kids, and I've always been known to be gentle, friendly and outgoing. I am affectionate, active, playful and I love to cuddle on my favorite human's lap. When I wake up, I'm ready for play time! I've met dogs and didn't mind them. As long as I feel happy and safe, I love to be everyone's friend. I'm a little nervous here at the shelter, my world has changed pretty quickly. But if you go slow with me (and maybe bring some squeeze up treats with you...) I'll show you what a silly love bug I am. Please come meet me today!

Pre-Screener Form

During her medical exam she was noted to be barking at handlers but warmed up to them. With select handlers Lunabelle has been observed to seek contact. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

255347.name: Phoenix
255347.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Phoenix is laying in her den, head up, ears forward, eyes wide, and pupils dilated as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and she is spoken to softly, she pokes her head out of the portal exit, gently head bunting the side wall of the door. Phoenix leans into petting on the head and cheeks, softly head bunting the assessor's hand before pulling her head back into the den after a few seconds. When a loud noise occurs in the room, Phoenix hisses once. With more soft talk she appears to settle, tolerating more petting on the head, cheeks, and down her shoulders and back. She is unable to be coaxed out of the den, so full pickup is unable to be attempted. She is tolerant of light upward pressure applied under her chest and on her sides.

A volunteer writes: Phoenix  is a super sweet girl only about 1 year old . When I opened her cage, she was perched on her shelf and stayed relaxed. The entire time she did not try and escape did not try and get out. She just laid there and basked and soaked up  all the attention that I had to give.  She was a really sweet girl who seemed to just be waiting for someone to visit her and give her love!  her. She's a petite girl with a super gentle and calm demeanor although as she settles in, I could see her eventually having a playful side.
Phoenix tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

255348.name: Philip
255348.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Philip is a young and handsome ginger found roaming an apartment building with friend Matcha. The finder had already some kitties who did not appreciate the potential new siblings and as a result, Philip and Matcha were brought to the care center. Philip is really cute, a bit shy to start with but very receptive to sweet talks, gentle petting and treats. It did not take long for the ice to be broken. Soon enough, Philip was rolling on his kennel floor, leaning into pets and purring abundantly. Philip is said to be friendly and outgoing with strangers but never was exposed to children. Because he can play a little bit rough(he is a very active cat) in general and with other cats, we do not recommend young kids in the adoptive household. Philip is a very pleasant young cat who would love to belong and be yours for many years to come. Come and meet Philip at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Philip is laying at the back of his cubby, laying on his side behind his litter box as the assessor approaches, pupils slightly dilated. He is initially slightly tense before appearing to settle when softly spoken to, stretching his paws and leaning forward to sniff the assessor's hand. He softly head bunts, allowing and leaning into all petting. He is a bit hesitant to come forward but is able to be lifted inside of the cubby, slightly tense when held but showing no signs of escalation. When he is placed back down, he continues to allow and lean into all further petting.

Philip interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that Philip go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods and cats who rough play.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Matcha is laying in his litter box inside of his bottom cubby, eyes wide, pupils dilated, ears forward and body slightly tense as the assessor approaches. After a bit of soft talk, Matcha leans forward hesitantly to sniff the assessor's hand before softly head bunting it. He is able to be coaxed to the main area of the kennel, greeting the assessor at the front of the kennel with another soft head bunt before allowing and leaning into all petting. He takes a moment to look around the room before calmly walking out of the kennel and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he initially retreats to the back, but after a few seconds he comes forward and continues to lean in for further petting and attention.

We recommend that Matcha go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods and rough play.

255350.name: Jinja
255350.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event onSunday, May 31 from 12PM - 4PM with Dash & Lili at Balsley Park, 306 W 57th Street, NY 10019, In front of Sur La Table. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
My purr motor is always running!
Jinja has settled in well here at the care center and has been flourishing! Upon approach she is at the front of the kennel, head bunting and leaning against the kennel door to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she immediately begins head bunting the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting and raising her back as she is pet. Jinja is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm, purring, and leaning against the assessor as she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to solicit attention by head bunting, purring, and leaning into all further petting. 

Jinja interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

255356.name: Bruno
255356.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bruno is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Bruno displays fearful and defensive behavior during kennel handling, including growling, hard barking, lunging, baring teeth,, retreating from handlers, and is overall very aloof towards unfamiliar people. . Bruno is able to engage with food and enrichment, responds to treats during handling, and has been able to be safely leashed, walked, and returned to kennel by familiar staff members, but will become defensive during interactions with unfamiliar staff when they pass his kennel. Medically, Bruno has CIRDC.

 Bruno came into the care center as a stray; due to this, his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Bruno is noted to take treats from handlers and allow minimal handling from familiar handlers. Due to all noted concerns displayed in the care center, the behavior department recommends Bruno be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow Bruno to acclimate comfortably to his new environment; force-free, reward based training only is advised when introducing Bruno to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Bruno presents with outside of the care centers.

255359.name: Birthday Cake
255359.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Birthday Cake, a young Tuxedo damsel was left loose to ride an elevator all by herself...A kind person found her and brought her to the Manhattan Care Center. Birthday Cake is as cute as a button. She is a lively gal who is curious, friendly and always ready for cuddles and play. She does not see danger anywhere and behaves like an acrobat on her balcony, playing with a feather wand or catnip toys. Of note, she never fell! Birthday Cake is a lot of fun but like a kid, I can see her getting carried away with prolonged or too exiting play. We all love Birthday Cake. She is pretty, petite, very lively and loving too. She likely needs a new home without small children and an owner who loves to actively interact with their pet. Birthday Cake is apparently healthy and did well on her behavior evaluation. She is ready to meet you and be your forever best friend for many years to come!






I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

255362.name: Jester
255362.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Handsome Jester was found limping in a backyard and brought to the Manhattan Care Center. His left front foot was swollen and painful, the result of an abscess that with proper management, time and cage rest has almost subsided. Jester has still a way to go to be 100% out of the bushes. Since arrival and through his long stay, Jester has been a very pleasant patient to deal with. Not that he would not mind to abscond and enjoy wider spaces to roam in but he knows that we will not allow that...Sometimes his tail switches a little, telling us that he would like things to be different but he "deals with it". A good and well mannered cat who enjoys sweet talks and petting, leaning into pets and purring. Jester was found to have a positive SNAP test for FIV, an immunological condition that can only be transmitted through a bite to other cats.These cats can live a long and uneventful life although they might be more subject to infections(the adoption counselors can provide potential adopters with more detailed information about this condition). Jester has been soooo patient and such a trooper. Time to find him a home sweet home! May be it could be with you!









What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I love getting pets!
This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

255369.name: Prince Ali
255369.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Prince Ali is a breathtaking and magnificent silvery semi long hair cat who is with us as his owner sadly passed away. He had been kicked out of his apartment when a neighbor, recognizing him, brought him to safety to the Manhattan Care Center. His debuts at the shelter were a bit scary as his savior opened the bag he was in and Prince Ali escaped in our driveway...No wonder he acted spooked for a few days... Prince Ali is all relaxed now in his kennel, laying lavishly in his "living room", waiting for a "conversation" and petting of course. He really enjoys being with people and  absolutely loves catnip toys and feather wands(see his videos). He can be petted while playing or eating tasty treats without any problem. Prince Ali is apparently healthy, did well on his behavior evaluation and could go home as soon as his neuter is done. Ask for Prince Ali when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!






I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
