255374.name: Mopple
255374.summary:
Meet Mopple!
Mopple arrived at the care center after being found tied to a pole with another dog, and while his past is unknown, he's shown himself to be a social, affectionate, and enthusiastic boy who is eager to connect with people. He has a big personality and an even bigger love for attention once he feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Mopple would do best in an active, structured home that can help him channel his excitement into positive outlets. He benefits from daily exercise, enrichment, and consistent reward-based training to support his impulse control and help him learn calmer ways to interact with the world. He thrives with routine and clear guidance.

Good with Other Pets?
Mopple was found with another dog, but his behavior with other animals in a home setting is still unknown, so slow and thoughtful introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his high arousal level and tendency to jump and mouth when excited, ACC recommends a home without young children.

Things to Know
Mopple is a friendly, treat-motivated dog who can become very excited during interactions, sometimes jumping up and mouthing the leash or treat pouch. Once he settles, he enjoys leaning into handlers for affection and responds well to gentle handling and treats. He is still learning impulse control, so consistency, patience, and positive reinforcement training will be key to helping him succeed. He also benefits from calm introductions and the ability to opt into interactions at his own pace.

Fun Fact
Once Mopple gets his zoomies out, he transforms into a total cuddle-seeker who leans right into you like he's always known you.

My foster writes: If you're looking for a puppy, then you got one. He's one year-old now so he's a puppy with a lot of talent. All he wants to do is say Hi. Some positive reinforcement would go a long and if you're an experienced walker it will all just fall into place as he gets to know you better!

255377.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

 Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Aries is at risk for behavior reasons. Aries is deteriorating in care with a prolonged stay. He has been unable to settle during socialization, panting, pacing with wide eyes. He has a high energy level, and we are unable to meet his needs. He was recently moved to a pop-up crate, and anxiety is continuously increasing. He has been sweet and social with staff and volunteers and does well when greeting other dogs at a gate. Medically, he is apparently healthy. 

My Boroughbreaker writes: Aries & I had a blast! We ran into so many people and he was extremely friendly and excited. We also ran into 2 dogs that I tried to keep him away from, but failed lol. He was friendly with them and calm!!! If I told him to come or stay, most of the time he responded extremely well.

Aries came to the care center as a stray and is now looking for a loving home to call his own. Since arriving, he has been sweet, social, and friendly with staff, enjoying attention and companionship from the people around him.

Like many dogs adjusting to a new environment, Aries does appear a bit anxious at times, which is completely understandable given all the recent changes in his life. Despite this, he continues to show a gentle and affectionate personality. With patience, consistency, and a supportive home, Aries will likely continue to build confidence and settle into a routine.

255390.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Eloise is on the at risk list for medical reasons. Eloise has a fracture at the olecranon process of his right elbow. He has been persistently painful and lame on that limb since arrival, despite rest and pain meds. Eloise would benefit from a consultation with an orthopedic surgeon to discuss options for recovery. Behaviorally, Eloise can get overstimulated and did bite someone when they touched near his fractured elbow.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I might need time to decompress in my new home - but cheek scratches and dry treats are my love language and how we will build our bond!
Eloise appreciates attention and specifically head and cheek pets but appears somewhat fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to an Adult-Only home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: Eloise can stretch, he can twirl, he can ask for pets and he can see perfectly upside down. He can do almost anything now that he's healing and getting his confidence back. Seen limping on his own with a wound outside, Eloise was brought to us to help him get sorted and started on his next step. He introduced himself like he was in a rush to show me everything he knows how to do at the same time while simultaneously seeming bored with it. Eloise plays with just as much whimsy, stacking his toys between his paws while reaching for more. This doesn't quite sum him up, however, as Eloise knows there's more to life than his condo, just like he knows he can do almost anything. There's one pretty big thing he's missing and we think it just might be you.

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

I might need time to decompress in my new home - but cheek scratches and dry treats are my love language and how we will build our bond!

Eloise appreciates attention and specifically head and cheek pets but appears somewhat fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to an Adult-Only home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: Eloise can stretch, he can twirl, he can ask for pets and he can see perfectly upside down. He can do almost anything now that he's healing and getting his confidence back. Seen limping on his own with a wound outside, Eloise was brought to us to help him get sorted and started on his next step. He introduced himself like he was in a rush to show me everything he knows how to do at the same time while simultaneously seeming bored with it. Eloise plays with just as much whimsy, stacking his toys between his paws while reaching for more. This doesn't quite sum him up, however, as Eloise knows there's more to life than his condo, just like he knows he can do almost anything. There's one pretty big thing he's missing and we think it just might be you.

255417.name: Mitsy
255417.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Mitsy is at risk due to behavior concerns. In the care centers she shows signs of being very fearful. She has avoided being leashed and avoidant of handlers. Once she has warmed up to a specific handler she will accept treats and some petting. Despite best efforts she still remains fearful during the leashing and handling aspects of daily care. Mitsy is reported to jump and bite at a handler hand that was standing by unprovoked while returning to her kennel the bite did not break skin. Mitsy is apparently healthy.

Meet Mitsy!
Mitsy is just one year old and has already been through a lot. She was surrendered alongside another dog when her family experienced housing insecurity, and now she's looking for a patient adopter who can help her discover that brighter days are ahead. While she can be shy at first, this young girl has so much love and potential waiting to shine through.

My Ideal Home
Mitsy would thrive in a quiet, patient home that will let her settle in at her own pace. She'll benefit from gentle encouragement, positive reinforcement, and plenty of enrichment like puzzle toys, long-lasting chews, sniffy walks, and games that help build her confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Mitsy previously lived with another dog. While she hasn't shown much interest in interacting with dogs at the shelter, slow introductions to any resident pets are always recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to Mitsy's fearful nature and preference for approaching people on her own terms, ACC recommends a home with no children under 13.

Things to Know
Mitsy can be nervous in new environments and around loud noises, and she prefers to take her time getting to know new people. At the shelter, she's been cautious during handling but continues to make progress with patient, low-pressure interactions. She's an active young dog who will flourish with daily exercise, enrichment, and reward-based training to help build her confidence. With time, consistency, and love, Mitsy has everything she needs to grow into an amazing companion.

Fun Fact
At just one year old, Mitsy has her whole life ahead of her, and she's ready to fill it with new adventures, happy memories, and a family to call her own.

255420.name: Maxwell
255420.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Maxwell is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the prior home, Maxwell was reported to have bitten two people. In both incidents, he bit and immediately released after being approached and touched while asleep. Previous owner noted Maxwell is attentive, empathetic, and playful. Maxwell in the care center has been social and playful with staff. Medically, Maxwell is noted to be overweight and has recently recovered from CIRDC.

Maxwell was surrendered by his previous owner due to them not being able to care for him any longer. His previous owner described him as a social, affectionate, active, playful, vocal, clingy dog. He would spend most of his time where people are, has been to the groomer, loves bath time/water, playing with balls, sitting in chairs, and loves boiled chicken. In his previous home, he would go on two 40-minute walks a day and had access to a patio. He is not crate trained. He sometimes enjoys car rides, and sometimes is very anxious in cars. Maxwell is noted to have a bite history. He escalated to biting his owner when they attempted to kiss him while he was asleep, and a neighbor who attempted to pet him while he was asleep. During his stay in care, Maxwell has been easy to remove from his crate and take on walks. He did show potential resource guarding of the toy during his handling assessment. Due to all noted concerns displayed in a home environment and in care, we recommend for Maxwell be placed with a New Hope placement partner who can provide an experienced adult-only foster home and provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: Some dogs' bios are so packed with glowing owner notes that they basically write themselves, and break our hearts in the process. Such is the case for Maxwell, who was loved - so loved - by his former guardian, who could sadly no longer care for him due to their health.

"He is a very smart baby" is one of the last things Maxwell's former person told the shelter about their beloved dog. They described him as a social, affectionate, and playful dog who spends most of his time where people are, and as very attentive and empathetic. He loves bathtime (we love a water dog) and going on long walks, plus he knows a handful of commands, including "sit," "stay," "paws," and "ball." He even knows to wait to have his paws cleaned after walks! He is said to be tolerant, friendly, outgoing, and playful around both familiar and unfamiliar dogs.

At the shelter, Maxwell has been friendly and social with staff, and though you can usually find him sitting calmly in his crate, he gets excited for walks. On my first walk with him, a passerby commented on how cute he was, and I wasn't surprised. With his floppy ears and chunky beagle-like physique, it's nearly impossible not to fall in love at first glance. He'd make an easygoing companion who appreciates the little things in life; a few of Maxwell's passions include playing with balls, sitting in chairs, and snacking on boiled chicken.

I can be just a little shy, but if you go slow with me, I will quickly show you what an affectionate and pristine lady I am. I'm curious and love snuggles. I've lived with dogs in my previous home, too! At my golden age, I have some medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me. Please give me a chance to join your family so I can live out my years cozy and loved in your lap!

255444.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Suga interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience, demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

A volunteer writes: The first few times I met Suga she was tucked in the corner, curled up in her little box. I quickly learned that though she looked perfectly content, Suga's the type of cat who is only waiting for an invitation because as soon as I opened her condo door, she stretched herself forward and into my arms for some cuddles and pets. In her previous home, Suga was playful and liked to watch things from afar, but she made time for cuddles, especially when she realized her guardian wasn't feeling well. Suga has some medical needs that will require follow up and we know there's a family out there for this very special kitty.

255450.name: Lucky Charms
255450.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Wusa and friend Lucky Charms, two 13 year old seniors came to us as their house counted too many pets. Being elders and having lived in the same home for soooo many years, we are housing them together in order to boost their spirit. Wusa is a handsome bright ginger with gorgeous eyes(the same sparkle can be seen in Lucky Charms'eyes), a bit timid but giving in to sweet talks and petting, head bunting softly my hand and making slowly biscuits(see his video). He is said to be a shy but sweet, calm and lovable pet. Lucky Charms stands behind her door and lays in plain sight, dressed in a peach and vanilla coat. Her shiny green eyes are soft, gentle and all on me. She enjoys the petting, is an excellent biscuit maker and is all together a sweet lovebug(see her video) .She would be a shy kitty who enjoys cuddles and playing gently. Lucky Charms and Wusa aced their behavior evaluation as we expected when they "stepped" into the care center. They are seniors, yes, who like we, humans do, come with their issues but they too deserve a safe, caring and loving home for their golden years. Please, consider Wusa and Lucky Charms as your next beloved four legged friends!What my friends at ACC say about me:


I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!

255455.name: Kisses
255455.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Kisses is the prettiest creamsicle senior gal. She was surrendered into our care as her house counted too many cats....Kisses was pretty shy when I first met her, hiding her head in her chest as I was petting her. She feels now much better and I am not surprised that her name is Kisses. A very sweet and charming twelve year old gal she is, still timid but leaning gently into pets and even purring. Her owner said that although very shy, Kisses was very affectionate. It is very tough for a former pet to be relinquished and be severed from everything and everyone they knew. So, it is no surprise, and even more so for a senior to have a hard time and need time to find some kind of balance. Kisses has started the process but a home sweet home would truly bring warmth and peace to her heart. Kisses does have health issues often found in mature pets and these can be discussed with our adoption counselors. Kisses will be a source of love and joy to the family who will adopt her!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

She feels now much better and I am not surprised that her name is Kisses. A very sweet and charming twelve year old gal she is, still timid but leaning gently into pets and even purring. Her owner said that although very shy, Kisses was very affectionate. It is very tough for a former pet to be relinquished and be severed from everything and everyone they knew. So, it is no surprise, and even more so for a senior to have a hard time and need time to find some kind of balance. Kisses has started the process but a home sweet home would truly bring warmth and peace to her heart. Kisses does have health issues often found in mature pets and these can be discussed with our adoption counselors. Kisses will be a source of love and joy to the family who will adopt her!

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I have lived with cats in my previous home.

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

255456.name: Valor
255456.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Valor is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Valor displays high arousal behaviors including leash biting, hard pulling, jumping, hypersalivation, and lunging or fixating on other dogs while on leash. During one handling interaction, Valor approached an assessor with a stiff body and cornered them until redirected by the handler. Valor is highly food motivated, responds well to reinforcement-based training, engages appropriately with enrichment, and has learned cues such as sit, focus, and breath work. Medically, Valor is apparently healthy.

Valor came into the care center as a stray; his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. in the care center, he takes treats from handlers and allows minimal handling. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: When I first meet Valor, he's just recovered from kennel cough, and is eager to get some fresh air. He looks disarmingly cute, carrying a soft toy through the neighborhood. In the play yard, I admire his epic jowls, bouncing as he hops after the ball I toss. He also engages with stuffed toys, but when I call, he runs back to me for pets. I do a consent check, and he leans back in, so we enjoy some cuddle time in between bouts of play. He's a smart boy, showing off cues and expertly catching treats of different densities as they fly at him through the air (great at physics!). He's food motivated and has been quite housebroken. 

As I admire him splashing and sniffing around the pool, I wonder about his past life. Found tied up in Coney Island, had he been to the beach before? Does he know the feel of warm sand shifting beneath his paws, of salty sea breeze filling his nose with a thousand fascinating scents? I don't know, but I hope that's in his future.

255467.name: Agnes
255467.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Ten month old Agnes, a little guy, was found with friends Angelica and Angela in a nearby park. They were understandably a little bit scared when they arrived at the Manhattan Care Center. Agnes is a cute tabby, a bit timid at the beginning of an encounter(he is also located in our Alley near loud dogs). He warms up with encouraging words and starts slow blinking, head bunting and rolling on his side for petting. He is a good young kitty, a bit thrown off by his abandonment but so willing to believe that soon life will be better with a caring and loving new owner or family. Agnes did well on his behavior evaluation(pointing to his initial shy behavior), is apparently healthy and will be neutered very soon, making him about ready to start a new page in his life with you and for many years to come. 







What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Boogie was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Boogie has been fearful and initially avoidant of interaction with handlers. He has escalated to baring teeth, growling, and nipping at officers when found and began leash biting once on a leash and when removed during his intake. During his medical exam, Boogie continued to escalate and needed to be sedated for his exam to be completed. He has shown some sociable behaviors briefly with select handlers when in a quiet space on his own terms. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Boogie be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

255481.name: Pucci
255481.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Pucci needs at risk placement for medical reasons. He is a sweet cat with severe inflammation of his eyelids and conjunctiva that is not responding to supportive care in shelter. He needs placement in a veterinary clinic and then a peaceful home to recover.

A volunteer writes:
Pucci comes from a house full of cats. No information was attached to them as they arrived at the care center...Pucci is a super handsome tiger, a tabby in white boots and mittens who knows how to pose for the photo shoot. He was sooo shy when he came in and so ready now for meets and greets with his visitors. He enjoys petting, leans against my hand, returns soft blinks and purrs softly. Pucci has become a favorite among volunteers as he is so calm, friendly and easy going..  As he comes from a large family of cats, not very much exposed to people, Pucci will likely need time and patience from his new family and a low traffic home without small children to bloom into a happy and lively pet. Will you give Pucci the chance  to be yours? He is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.

I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

Pucci has made excellent improvement since his first assessment and was lying quietly inside his cubby. He accepted petting on his head, cheek, and along his back. He was treat-motivated and very sweet.

Pucci interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

255483.name: Cardinal
255483.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I am really treat motivated. You can use treats to teach me new things!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

A volunteer writes: I have a new pastime and it's regularly passing Cardinal's crate to see which way he's managed to maneuver his body while sleeping.  My favorite is legs straight up in the air, or body diagonal on his back.  A niche hobby, maybe, but satisfying? Definitely. And being able to sleep in a relaxed way in such a chaotic and loud environment, is a testament to his unique resilience. Cardinal was found running loose in the Bronx and brought to ACC by police.  He was noted to be relaxed and wiggly on intake. But, Cardinal's hobbies have nothing to do with watching another dog sleep and everything to do with PLAYING!  He loves to frolic in the yard, bring back toys and running til his heart's content. He's learning some cues in exchange for treats and even jumps in the pool for them. Cardinal has done well in playgroup and has met both male and female dogs with a loose, wiggly body.  As much as we love watching Cardinal sleep in the shelter, it would be 100x better to see him snoozing in a home!

255497.name: Evander
255497.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Evander is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Evander was initially social with staff and would allow petting and take treats. He had one instance of mounting a staff member but did not repeat the behavior. More recently, while on a walk, Evander lunged at a staff member, biting and holding onto their sweater and tearing the fabric. Medically, Evander has alopecia, dental disease, chronic otitis, and is underweight.

Evander was brought to the Care Centers as a stray, so his behavior history in a home environment is unknown. While in the Care Centers, Evander was noted to be social with staff, though he would occasionally mount them. More recently, Evander lunged at a staff member and grabbed their sweater with his mouth, releasing only after the fabric tore. Evander would do best in an adult-only home through a New Hope Partner that can safely manage his behaviors using positive reinforcement techniques.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I don't always like to share my food, toys or bedding with other animals.

A Volunteer Wrote: Little surprise that Evander is a volunteer favorite: He's got everything going for him! He wants to play with everyone, which sure is fun to watch. Dogs on either side of the fence get play bows and every trick he can think of to entice them to interact with him; humans get the same amount of affection exhibited with his bouncy, playful affection. The comments on his walking log are some of the best we've ever seen because everyone agrees he's phenomenal in every way (he's also an amazing leash walker, calm and steady). Please, come meet him for yourself and be his forever fan!

255500.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Mello is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Mello is highly fearful in the Care Centers. He has been observed pancaking, trembling, refusing to walk, and urinating or defecating when staff When staff attempt to remove him from his kennel, Mello tolerates being lifted. With staff he is comfortable with, Mello will walk slowly alongside them with encouragement. While in the finder's home, Mello also displayed fearful behavior initially, but gradually warmed up. The finder additionally reported that Mello would guard his food and treats. Medically, Mello is apparently healthy.

Mello came into the care center due to his owner passing away. In the prior home Mello is described as a fearful couch potato who spent most of his time in the living room of the home. He enjoys being pet but is fearful, and he will play with toys when he is given them.During Mello stay in the care center he has to be carried when taken to and from kennel due to him not wanting walk. He will display a trembling body, widen eyes and remains shut down. Mello has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: Things don't always change in the direction we would hope. Scott was brought to us after being abandoned and was a bright and happy star with everyone he met. Friendly and trusting, we knew that his open heart would be helpful in his efforts to find forever family. But shelter life can be a lot and even the sweetest kitties can be overwhelmed by the expectations it entails. We're here to try to help, which is Scott has joined our 'Fraidy Cat Club where we've been working with him to maybe get him to come out of his shell a little bit more. He probably won't be the one to ask for it now, but Scott could really use a little chance.

255555.name: Chickpea
255555.summary: Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

255576.name: Eggo Waffles
255576.summary:
Meet Eggo Waffles!
Eggo Waffles is a beautiful orange tabby with a gentle heart who's learning that people can be pretty wonderful. Found as a stray in the Bronx, she spent her first days in the shelter feeling unsure and overwhelmed. But with patience, treats, and kindness, Eggo Waffles has blossomed into an affectionate cat who now seeks out attention and enjoys spending time with her favorite people.

My Ideal Home
Eggo Waffles would love a calm, patient home where she can continue building her confidence at her own pace. While she has made incredible progress in the shelter, she may need a little time to adjust to new surroundings. Once she feels comfortable, her sweet personality shines through, and she happily leans in for pets and affection.

What to Expect
Eggo Waffles loves attention but prefers interactions on her terms. She especially enjoys cheek and chin scratches and will happily roll around and lean into gentle petting. Like many cats, she can become overstimulated if petting continues for too long, particularly along her back. Learning her body language and giving her breaks when she asks will help build a trusting relationship.

Good with Kids?
Eggo Waffles would do best in a home with older, respectful children who can understand when she needs space. Because she can become overstimulated during handling, ACC recommends a home without young children under 13 years old.

Overall Health
Eggo Waffles is an apparently healthy young adult cat with a good prognosis. She tested negative for FeLV/FIV, is up to date on her vaccinations, and her veterinary exam revealed no significant medical concerns. She is ready to find a home of her own.

Personality
While she was initially fearful and withdrawn, Eggo Waffles has shown remarkable growth during her stay. Volunteers describe her as sweet, affectionate, and eager for attention. She now greets visitors, enjoys squeeze-up treats and tuna snacks, and has become increasingly comfortable with handling and petting. Her journey from shy stray to loving companion has been wonderful to watch.

Other Fun Facts
Eggo Waffles is a mellow girl who prefers quality cuddle time over wild adventures. She loves cheek rubs, enjoys being admired, and has mastered the art of looking adorable while lounging in her favorite cozy spot. With a little patience and understanding, Eggo Waffles is ready to become someone's very special breakfast buddy. 🧇🧡🐾

255588.name: Celime
255588.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Celime is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

Celime is a naturally shy, timid, and fearful cat that chooses to hide initially, and prefers contact on his own terms. It is noted that if boundaries are pushed he may escalate to defensive distance-increasing behaviors. He has distinct boundaries, not choosing to escalate immediately and is noted to warm up slowly but shows affectionate behaviors to his person once he warms up. He will need an understanding, quiet, adult-only, single-pet home that will give as long as he needs to adjust and come around.
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.

Although it may take me a long time to warm up to new people and find my people - I have been known to follow and lay next to my favorite people.

A volunteer writes: Celime has been so loved, so so so so loved and he has loved in return. There's one thing he doesn't love, however, and that's the shelter with all the unfamiliar sights and sounds that come with it. Snuggled up in his den, surrounded by his own thoughts, Celime didn't hesitate to remind me, so I closed his condo door and read to him for a little while. His previous guardian brought him to us when Celime was brought to us due to a no pet policy. We know he takes a little bit to warm up to new people but once he does, he's affectionate and enjoys laying with the person he's chosen, and oh, to be that person! Celime loves to play, he chases toys with a particular penchant for things that crinkle. He's hoping you'll choose him at the Queens Care Center.

255598.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Canela is at risk due to behavioral reasons. She has been observed to be highly dog reactive while in care. Noted to jump off the walls while snarling, barking, and lunging towards the other dogs. When the handler pulls her away from the other dogs Canela begins head whipping and snapping. During intake, Canela was observed to have a wiggly body and allowed all contact. Medically, Canela is receiving treatment for CIRDC.

Canela arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care Canela has been observed to be highly kennel reactive. Noted to jump off the walls and snarl at the other dogs in the kennel room. While on leash Canela is noted to be anxious and will walk in a zig zag pattern. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home, that make no trips to the dog park.

255613.name: Lover Boy
255613.summary:
Meet Lover Boy!
His name says it all. Lover Boy is a friendly, affectionate pup who never seems to run out of love to give. Found as a stray, he quickly won over staff with his wiggly body, happy personality, and enthusiasm for making new friends. Whether he's leaning in for pets, accepting treats with a wagging tail, or trying to climb into your lap for extra attention, Lover Boy is happiest when he's spending time with people.

My Ideal Home
Lover Boy would thrive with an adopter who is ready for an active, social dog. He enjoys being part of the action and would love a home where he can join in on walks, playtime, and plenty of adventures. He already has a wonderful foundation and will benefit from continued positive reinforcement training to polish up his manners.

Good with Kids?
Lover Boy's history with children is unknown, but his friendly and social nature suggests he may do well with respectful children. As with all introductions, slow and supervised meetings are recommended.

Good with Other Pets?
Lover Boy's history with other dogs is unknown, but he has shown loose, social body language during introductions with another dog in our care. Any resident dogs should meet him prior to adoption to ensure a good match.

Leash Manners
Lover Boy enjoys getting out and exploring. He can pull strongly on leash when excited, so continued loose-leash training will help him become an even better walking companion.

Overall Health
Lover Boy recently underwent his neuter surgery and is recovering well. He is currently being treated for a mild upper respiratory infection and is expected to make a full recovery.

Behavior Determination
Level 1 - Lover Boy is a friendly, social dog whose main challenges involve excitement-related jumping and leash pulling.

Other Fun Facts
Lover Boy has never met a stranger for long. He loves attention, enjoys treats, and has been known to greet people with full-body wiggles and enthusiastic hugs. If you're looking for a dog who will make you feel loved every day, Lover Boy may be your perfect match.

255617.name: Brownie
255617.summary:
Meet Brownie!
Brownie was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. He is a sensitive, thoughtful dog who can take time to feel comfortable in new situations and prefers to engage with people on his own terms. Once he warms up, he can be friendly and gentle, but he appreciates a slow, respectful approach.

My Ideal Home
Brownie would do best in a calm, patient home that understands he may need time to build trust. He benefits from a predictable routine, gentle handling, and positive reinforcement. Because of his sensitivity, an adult-only home will help him feel safest and most secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Brownie's history with other animals is not fully known, so slow and careful introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his discomfort with new people and touch, Brownie is recommended for a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Brownie has a medium energy level and can experience separation anxiety, often crying or barking when left alone for long periods. He prefers to approach people when he is ready and does best when given space and choice in interactions. With consistency, structure, and gentle encouragement, he has the potential to continue building confidence and comfort in a home setting.

Fun Fact
Brownie may be shy at first, but once he decides you're his person, he enjoys coming over for affection in his own time and on his own terms.

255650.name: Bunsen
255650.summary:
Meet Bunsen!
Bunsen is a handsome, social boy who is ready to leave shelter life behind and start his next adventure. Found as a stray alongside another dog, Bunsen has quickly made friends with staff thanks to his affectionate personality, wagging tail, and eagerness to spend time with people.

My Ideal Home
Bunsen would thrive in an active home that can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and opportunities to continue learning. He's an enthusiastic dog who enjoys being involved in whatever his people are doing and would love a family that can help him channel his energy into fun activities and training.

Good with Kids?
Bunsen's history with children is unknown. As with any new dog, slow introductions and supervision are recommended while everyone gets to know one another.

Good with Other Pets?
Bunsen arrived with another dog and has shown appropriate social behavior when meeting dogs through a barrier. While his full history is unknown, he has displayed friendly curiosity and may do well with a compatible canine companion following a proper introduction.

Leash Manners
Bunsen enjoys getting out and exploring the world, but he can be a strong puller when excited. He's looking for an adopter who can help him continue working on loose-leash skills through positive reinforcement training.

Overall Health
Bunsen is in good health, up to date on vaccinations, heartworm negative, and ready to head home with his new family.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 - Bunsen is a friendly, social dog who would benefit from continued work on leash manners and learning to take treats more gently.

Other Fun Facts
Outside of the shelter, Bunsen is described as a big cuddle bug who enjoys attention from people. He loves treats, enjoys making new friends, and is ready to bring lots of joy to his future home.

255651.name: Beaker
255651.summary:
Meet Beaker!
Beaker is a sweet, gentle girl who may be a little shy at first, but quickly shows her affectionate side once she feels comfortable. Found as a stray wandering the streets of Brooklyn, Beaker has handled all the changes in her life with grace and has been winning over staff with her soft nature, loose leash walks, and quiet charm.

My Ideal Home
Beaker would love a patient home where she can settle in at her own pace. While she enjoys attention and companionship, she appreciates gentle introductions to new people and situations. A calm environment will help her continue building confidence and showing off her loving personality.

Good with Kids?
Beaker would do best in a home with children over the age of five. She can be a little timid when meeting new people and would be most comfortable with kids who understand how to respect her space and let her warm up naturally.

Good with Other Pets?
Beaker's history with other animals is unknown, though she did arrive with another dog. She has shown interest in meeting other dogs but can become overly intense during interactions. Because of this, ACC recommends no dog parks. Any introductions to resident dogs should be slow, thoughtful, and carefully managed.

Leash Manners
Beaker is a dream on leash, walking with little to no pulling and enjoying leisurely strolls with her people. She likes exploring her surroundings and checking in with her handler along the way.

Overall Health
Beaker is in good health, recently spayed, up to date on vaccinations, and ready to head home with her new family.

Behavior Determination
Level 1 (No Young Children) - Beaker is a friendly, social dog who benefits from gentle introductions and a little extra time to feel comfortable in new situations.

Other Fun Facts
Beaker loves attention from her people, enjoys treats, and has a playful side waiting to shine. With her sweet personality and easygoing nature, she's ready to become someone's loyal best friend.

255676.name: Alfred
255676.summary:
A volunteer writes: Sweet Alfred is 6 years young and ended up in our care  with friend Alexia as their owner unfortunately passed away. I will say he is settling in very well at the shelter. He enjoys to sit on his elevated bed. He loves head, neck, and chin pets and started to purr once I pet him, leaning forward to get more love. He tolerates the noise in the shelter, although I feel that he would be better in a home that doesn't have as much action. I can tell this boy would love a couch to lay on and perhaps a window to bring in sun puddles for him to bask in the sun.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Alfred is laying on his kuranda bed as the assessor approaches, eyes wide, pupils dilated, and lip licking. When the kennel door is opened, he leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand before pulling away. Alfred allows all petting, leaning in and closing his eyes when he is pet on the head and cheeks. He is unable to be coaxed down from the top of his kuranda bed, so full pickup is unable to be attempted. He is tolerant of light upward pressure applied under his chest and at his sides without issue, continuing to lean into all further petting afterwards.



Alfred tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

255678.name: Darla
255678.summary:
Darla arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. Darla has been observed to be highly fearful while in care, noted to balk and thrash on leash when handlers attempt to return her to kennel. Due to the high level of fear, stress, and anxiety, we recommend an experienced adult only home. 
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

A Volunteer Wrote: They don't get easier or sweeter than Darla, who is so happy to amble along to the park and just sniff the air, the grass, the world outside of her pop up crate. This girl is so gentle and kind, and she's so happy to get out of her pop up crate in the middle of a noisy hallway; her fans are desperate for her to be lying next to a loving person on a couch somewhere, and not here! Please come meet this gentle girl and consider making her a part of your family.

255687.name: Satsuma
255687.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Hi, my name is Satsuma and the shelter has been a little overwhelming for me. I came from a home with many cats, who I've gotten along with well. Because I've lived in this home my entire life and have only been around one person, I have little experience with people and am hesitant of new experiences. I would enjoy living in a quiet home, preferably one with lots of vertical space so I have a place to perch and observe the room. I would also appreciate having experienced, patient adopter(s) who are willing to take things slow with me. I would benefit from socialization, using rewards whenever I make a small positive step like making eye contact, allowing petting, or sniffing your hand. I'd prefer to take things at my own pace and would appreciate some good old fashion TLC. If you can open your heart to adopt a cat like me, I'll hopefully have the confidence to come around to my new people, like you!

255710.name: Rhino
255710.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, June 7 from 11AM - 4PM at Petco Love Adoption Event, Union Square Park, 201 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Meet Rhino!
Rhino is a young, happy-go-lucky pup who seems to believe every person he meets is a new best friend. This energetic boy arrived at ACC as a stray after being brought to a police precinct by a good Samaritan. While his past remains a mystery, Rhino has wasted no time showing everyone what a fun, affectionate, and social dog he is.

My Ideal Home
Rhino is looking for an active home that can match his enthusiasm for life. He's still learning his manners and can get a little overexcited when meeting people, often expressing his joy by jumping up for attention. A family committed to continuing his training with positive reinforcement will help him channel that excitement into polite greetings. In return, they'll gain a loyal companion who's always ready for fun.

What to Expect
Rhino is affectionate, playful, and eager to interact. He readily approaches people, seeks out pets and attention, and loves being included in whatever is happening around him. He enjoys toys, play sessions, and opportunities to explore. On walks he is easy to handle, and his friendly nature shines through wherever he goes.

Good with Other Dogs?
Rhino has done well in multiple dog-to-dog interactions while in our care. He has shown playful, social behavior with both male and female dogs, offering play bows, engaging in appropriate greetings, and respecting social cues. He may be a good match for another playful dog after a proper introduction.

Overall Health
Rhino appears to be a healthy young dog with a good prognosis. His veterinary exam found no medical concerns, and he recently completed his neuter surgery. He is up to date on his core vaccinations and preventative care and is ready to begin the next chapter of his life.

Personality
Friendly, outgoing, playful, and affectionate, Rhino is the kind of dog who makes friends everywhere he goes. He loves attention, enjoys interacting with people, and approaches life with an upbeat attitude. His joyful personality and eagerness to engage make him a fun companion for an adopter looking for an active, social dog.

Other Fun Facts
Rhino's favorite way to say hello is with a big smile, a wagging tail, and occasionally all four paws leaving the ground. He's always ready for an adventure, a game, or simply some quality time with his people. If you're looking for a dog who will bring energy, laughter, and affection into your life, Rhino may be the perfect fit. 🐾❤️

255711.name: Bilbo Waggins
255711.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Bilbo Waggins is at risk due to behavioral concerns. While Bilbo Waggins has been loose-bodied and social with handlers, he has displayed leash-biting behaviors that have made it increasingly challenging to walk him successfully as his stay in care has progressed. He could intially be redirected with treats or toys, but he has recently begun to take the treats and/or toys but immediately returns to leash biting, also mouthing at hands in the process. In calmer settings, he remains loose-bodied during his interactions with handlers, but he has difficulty settling, as he pants and paces, with a red/flushed face. Medically, Bilbo Waggins has an ear infection.

Meet Bilbo Waggins!
Bilbo Waggins was found neglected in an apartment and has shown himself to be a sweet, goofy, and social young dog who is eager for connection. Despite his difficult start, he is affectionate, people oriented, and enjoys engaging with handlers once he feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Bilbo Waggins would do best in a patient, structured home that can help him build confidence at his own pace. He benefits from calm environments, consistent routines, and positive reinforcement training to support his confidence and leash skills.

Good with Other Pets?
Bilbo Waggins has shown friendly and social behavior with other dogs during controlled introductions, though he can become fearful when passing barking dogs and should have gradual, supported exposure.

Good with Kids?
Due to fearfulness and sensitivity in new environments, Bilbo Waggins is recommended for a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Bilbo Waggins is a social and affectionate dog who enjoys attention, toys, and being close to people. He can show mild leash biting when excited or overstimulated and may become anxious in stressful environments, especially around loud or barking dogs. He has shown some sensitivity around handling his neck area and benefits from gentle, gradual handling and positive associations. With structure, patience, and reassurance, he continues to show his loving, goofy personality and strong desire to bond with people.

Volunteer Note
A volunteer writes: Bilbo was just a delight the second we met him. He is a big, goofy guy, weighing in at 66 pounds. Visually, he's very much a meathead, a jock. But inside he is just a lover boy waiting for the right person to come his way. A hopeless romantic, Bilbo would definitely be the type of guy to bring you flowers on the first date, or at least a stuffed flower toy. His love language is between gift giving and physical touch, because he is known to be a major lap dog too! Bilbo was reported to be left in a vacant apartment with other dogs. He is about 2 years old. He is super soft, social and playful. Walking past kennels, Bilbo can be a little scared, but when greeting a dog outside he displayed loose body language with wagging tail.

Fun Fact
Bilbo Waggins may look like a big goofy jock, but he is really a soft-hearted romantic who just wants to be someone's loyal best friend.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Levian is laying in his den, eyes wide and lip licking as the kennel door is opened. He is softly spoken to and after a few moments he hesitantly pokes his head out of the portal exit before beginning to head bunt the side wall of the door. He allows and leans into all petting and with lots of soft talk he is able to be coaxed out of the den and to the front of the kennel. Levian leans forward to head bunt the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting, raising his back and purring loudly as he is pet. He is able to be easily picked up and remains calm when held, continuing to purr. When he is placed back into his kennel, he remains at the front, allowing and leaning into all further petting. When the interaction is ended and the kennel door is closed, Levian calmly walks to his bowl of dry food and begins eating. 

Levian interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

255714.name: Coco Melon
255714.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Coco Melon was dropped by an unknown person at the precinct in his personal carrier(it wore his name). Coco Melon's world was turned up side down. He tried to flee when he first arrived at the care center and remained in hiding for quite a while. Enough is enough! Coco Melon is not a Bernard L'Hermite. He likes people, he wants to be loved, he enjoys playing..Time to show for himself and find a way to be home and a family to love. Coco Melon did just that! Coming out of his shell, exiting his cubby, saluting visitors and playing. He is such a handsome cat, a ginger with an orange and white ringed tail. Although he has a little cold right now, Coco Melon is apparently healthy, did very well on his behavior evaluation and would love to meet his new owner or family. So, ask about Coco Melon when you visit us at the care center, looking for your forever best friend!





Coco Melon has greatly improved since his first assessment. He woke up from a nap and came forward with a high tail and a gently arched back and was appreciative of attention, allowing and enjoying petting on his head, cheeks, and along his back. He loved squeeze-up treats, and he was calm when picked up and held and remained relaxed and curious when set back down..

Coco Melon interacts with the assessor,  solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience provided they are counseled on her earlier shelter behavior. 	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

255729.name: Oliver
255729.summary:
Oliver is a shy, sweet, curious boy who easily warms up with a little TLC. Oliver spent his first few days here hidden under his bedding, but with a bit more time he has surely come out of his shell. Oliver rolls, purrs and leans in for petting with each interaction. He enjoys music, interaction, compliments and treats. 

Oliver tolerates attention and appreciates petting but took some time to warm up in shelter. He may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to his sensitivity to active environments, he may not be a great fit for young children.

255731.name: Archer
255731.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Archer is on the at-risk list for behavior concerns. Archer was initially very reactive to staff, hard staring and growling in his kennel. He did warm up quickly with select handlers but remains easily over-aroused when playing in the yard. Archer becomes evasive in the yard to avoid being returned to his kennel. Going for walks have been difficult as well due to him pulling hard to the point of fainting while using a harness. Medically, Archer is being treated for mild pyoderma. We completed chest x-rays for Archer and a radiologist consult ruled out several underlying causes, a redundant tracheal membrane or other underlying condition cannot be ruled out at this time. We recommend follow up with a private vet as we are unable to provide further in-depth care in shelter.

Meet Archer

Archer came to us as a stray, and the transition to shelter life has been challenging for him. He was initially reactive toward staff, but with time, patience, and consistency, he has begun to build trust with select individuals and is showing encouraging progress.

Archer can struggle to settle in our busy shelter environment and may become easily aroused during socialization sessions. He will benefit from an adopter who understands that building a relationship with him will take time and who can provide a calm, structured home where he can continue to gain confidence.

255734.name: Chiquita
255734.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Chiquita is on the at-risk for medical concerns. She is an adult cat with a severe upper respiratory infection and is stressed and not eating in shelter. She needs supportive care in a veterinary clinic in order to recover.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Chiquita was on top of the den in the loaf position, appearing calm. She sniffed treats and then allowed all petting, leaning in for cheek rubs and giving gentle head bunts. She arched her back slightly with back petting but could not be coaxed off the top of the den. She was reasonably calm during a partial pick-up and vocalized only very slightly with a little meow. She's a sweet cat who might need a little time to adjust to her new home.

Chiquita interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

255745.name: Hanifa
255745.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Hanifa and Tutu are two petite seniors with saucer eyes, a pair of pretty tabbies, one in the sepia shade and the other, grey. I wonder if Tutu is not Hanifa's mom.....Both sweet kitties are with us as their owner sadly passed away. A relative who could not keep them let us know that they were gentle and affectionate pets, very much missing their owner.  Hanifa is a bit shy. He likes to stay in his little house, his safe place but comes out at the call of his name and tempted by tasty treats. He is sooo cute, almost a replica of Tutu. He appears a little wary but accepts gladly petting and feels more and more comfortable as our encounter goes on. He is just too adorable...Hanifa does have some medical issues that are not uncommon in his age range. The adoption counselors will discuss them with you if you are considering adopting Hanifa. Seniors have a long history of blessing an owner with their presence and love. It is time for us to be there for them at the crepuscule of their life, making sure they are safe, comfortable and loved. Hanifa(and Tutu) are waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center. 






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Hanifa, who was in the den crouched in the loaf position with somewhat dilated pupils and meowing gently, was sweet and allowed petting on the cheek, head, and along his back. He sniffed treats while remaining in place. He might be slightly shy, but we expect he'll warm up in his new home.

Hanifa interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

255748.name: Tutu
255748.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Senior Tutu and friend Hanifa(a senior too) were brought to the Manhattan Care Center as their owner sadly passed away. Both were on their best behavior upon arrival at the shelter and with the veterinary team. Very little is known about their past life except that(according to a relative) they were understandably quite depressed after the loss of their caretaker. Tutu is very quiet in her kennel, a bit "frozen" even, a cute tabby in white boots and mittens, looking at me with giant eyes and letting a little cry out from time to time. A churru seems to her like and she shortly after licking it, leans gently into pets, accepting caresses. Tutu is a quiet and petite tiger with senior teeth, a normal blood panel, did very well on her behavior evaluation and is already spayed. She could go home today with a new owner or family who loves and knows how to care for seniors, giving them the golden years they so deserve....




What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!

255749.name: Neon
255749.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Playtime is essential! I love climbing tall cat trees and having fun with interactive toys!
Neon tolerates attention and petting but appears to be mildly fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will likely need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

A volunteer writes: Neon was sleeping in a little crescent shape but blinked himself awake to meow at me when I visited his neighbor. He didn't get up, but did some light stretching as he chit chatted and ensured he'd be next in line. I appreciated his efforts, however minimal they might've seemed, and expected Neon would shift a bit when I opened the door. Well, he did not. Choosing to continue the conversation from his little crescent shape, he welcomed pets as we chit chatted and I giggled, completely charmed by his seemingly minimal efforts that was really anything but. He loves to play and managed to even play with two toys, also while not really getting up. Neon has been with us since June and while we love spending time and learning more about him each day, we can't wait for you to meet him.

Kittens are not my focus when I am at the care center, unless they are alone or unwell. 255761.name: Prince Khan
255761.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Prince Khan is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Prince Khan initially displayed fearful behavior during kennel exit, including low growling, reluctance to leave the kennel, freezing, laying down, and a tucked tail. He has also displayed high arousal behaviors including jumping on handlers and biting at the leash or harness during walks. Prince Khan also smears his kennel in feces due to his jumping off his walls of his kennel.. Prince Khan seeks out treats and social interaction but is struggling in the care center. Medically, Prince Khan is overweight and has a Grade II heart murmur.

Prince Khan was surrendered into care due to his previous owner's health concerns and his size. He is described as a very active and playful dog who enjoys spending most of his time relaxing in the living room. He loves going for car rides, and his favorite activities include running and playing with sticks. Prince's previous owner did report destructive tendencies to furniture and walls. During his stay in care, Prince Khan was loose and wiggly upon intake. When initially attempting to leash him for walks, Prince Khan would growl at handlers/staff and would not exit his kennel. Over time, with a slow, reward-based approach/interactions, Prince Khan has now been social with handlers and staff. He has become challenging to walk due to his arousal on walks and leash biting. Due to these concerns, we reocmmend for him to be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can address these challenges with a certified professional trainer that utilizes positive reinforcement only methods. 

A volunteer writes: It's hard to appreciate Prince Khan's size until you meet him in real life. He's a solid 86lbs, a big tall boy, but also a young one. Only a year old, he is perhaps unaware he is no longer puppy sized. He plays with reckless abandon, slapping a tennis ball to the watch it roll around the yard and pouncing on it as it does. At one point he loses track of it all together, looking around Tom & Jerry style only to find it beneath him. He takes a rest by putting all 86lbs on our laps, and eventually just laying at our feet reveling in a belly rub.

The obvious thing here is that shelter life is not easy for a large, young, energetic dog. And Prince Khan is proof of this. While he's able to get some energy out with us and relax at our feet, his daily life in the shelter doesn't include regular breaks from his kennel to move his body. He's frustrated and biting the leash and it's led to him only being able to be walked by select staff members.

In his previous home Prince lived with a cat and a child that he was reported to get along with. Due to his size and his guardians health, they could no longer care for him. Now he needs a rescue and a good home to care for him, and provide an enriching and fulfilling life that he deserves.

255774.name: Taurus
255774.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Taurus is a stray Rottweiler who came into our care with very little known about his past. Understandably, he was initially fearful and unsure of his new surroundings. With patience, consistency, and a slow approach, Taurus has begun to warm up and show his softer side to the people he trusts.

Taurus is still learning to navigate the world and can become easily aroused or overstimulated in certain situations. Because of this, he will need an experienced adopter who understands canine body language and is committed to providing structure, training, and ongoing support.

Taurus is looking for a single-pet home where he can be the center of attention and continue building confidence at his own pace. He will do best with an adopter who is willing to take things slowly, respect his boundaries, and help him succeed.

While Taurus may require extra patience and understanding, he has already shown that he is capable of making progress and forming positive connections.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ricardo is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Ricardo displays high arousal during handling and kennel exit, including hard pulling, spinning toward handlers, jumping up, and mouthing at clothing. During a dog-to-dog assessment, Ricardo displayed signs of discomfort and fearfulness, remain aloof during some interactions with staff. Ricardo is able to be leashed with ease, engages with food and enrichment but is struggling in the care center environment. Medically, Ricardo has recently recovered from CIDRC and is currently healthy.

Ricardo was surrendered into care because his owner was unable to care for him due to losing their home. His previous family described him as a very playful and high-energy dog. Ricardo is reported to prefer lounging in the bedroom or, at times, wherever his people are. During his stay in care, Ricardo has been fearful and mostly avoidant of interactions, seeking an exit. Due to these concerns, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can allow him the time and space to decompress and acclimate at his own pace. 

A volunteer writes: I forgot exactly how handsome Ricardo was until I rewatched all his videos. I smiled ear to ear writing this, just as a I did when I met him. If throwing a toy is a reward for Ricardo, watching him amble back, slowed down by the summer heat, and drop his toy before flashing that "smile" is 10x the reward for me.

I'm sad to learn this boy was living in a car with his human, and another dog, before the shelter. They had found him stray a year prior and I imagine they were instantly charmed the way I was. Against his jet black coat are sparse little white speckles, a happy surprise when you finally get over his handsome face to see the rest of him.

Ricardo knows his cues in English and Spanish, and his previous guardian noted that he alert barks to unfamiliar people and dogs approaching. Due to his fear he is only available via a rescue and he's due to go at risk shortly for arousal when leaving his kennel.

255778.name: Butterfly Bat
255778.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Butterfly Bat tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.


A volunteer writes: I would love to be invited to this particular house of friends but Casa and Migos have been here since May and though they've shown wonderful progress, haven't always been particularly keen on adding people friends to their little group. This kitty focused duo was brought to us when their former guardian was no longer able to care for them and they came in a little shut down, but this isn't the whole story. They're known to turn into silly gooses with toys, provided we leave the toys for them to play with and don't interrupt too much. They like to be included in the conversation even if they aren't going to be the ones to start it themselves and will gently close their eyes when being spoken to. We hope you'll consider giving these lovely cats a chance.

255800.name: Maxon
255800.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Middle aged Maxon came with his much younger housemate, Friendship as their owner was going through a very rough patch. Maxon was not a happy camper upon arrival to the care center. What on earth had just happened to him? From one day to another his whole life changed. Everything and everyone vanished. Now, he is all lonely in a cage. Who could "put a smile" on their face after going though this ordeal? Still, Maxon is trying. I opened his cage, called his name, came with "presents and he emerged from his den, slowly, hesitantly but fully in the end, savoring "special" food and temptations and mostly, accepting caresses and leaning into pets. He briefly returned to his den with loud noises and sudden moves but came back for more treats and interaction. Maxon will improve by the day. He is no "spring chick", does not have blue eyes or long hair. Maxon is an all ebony cat, very common in his looks but with a good heart, the type some owners would prefer and cherish over any other kitties. Maxon's owner told us that he was a quiet, sensitive and playful pet who loved his female companion, had no experience with kids , strangers and dogs, was litter box trained and well mannered. Maxon is already neutered and could go home today with you!. Come and meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center.






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

Maxon tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

255803.name: Matthew
255803.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Matthew is on the at risk list for medical reasons. Matthew has severe dental disease and was noted to have lost a pound over the two months she has been in shelter, despite a reportedly good appetite. Her bloodwork showed some abnormalities, but was not diagnostic for any particular disease. An underlying systemic disease is suspected and additional diagnostics including abdominal ultrasound are recommended. Behaviorally, Matthew is fearful and attempts to flee during medical handling. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Matthew tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.
