255817.name: Mishka
255817.summary:
Mishka arrived at MACC as a stray with no history. Mishka's previous owners reported that she was displaying aggressive behavior in the home. Noted to play roughly and growling at the resident children. While in care, Mishka has been observed to be fearful. Noted to growl at handlers and thrash on leash during intake. When handlers approach her kennel, Mishka has been observed to hard bark and lunge at the kennel door. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experieced adult only home. 

A staff member writes: Mishka is a gentle, affectionate girl who loves spending quality time with her people. She walks beautifully on a loose leash, frequently checks in with her handler, happily accepts treats with a gentle mouth, and enjoys leaning in for pets. She's also a smart cookie who already knows "sit" and loves staying engaged during her walks. If you're looking for a sweet, attentive companion who will happily stay by your side, Mishka is ready to meet you!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Jaboti is standing at the front of her kennel, head bunting and leaning her body against the kennel bars as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she immediately leans forward to begin head bunting their hand, tail held high in a question mark position and body relaxed. Jaboti allows and leans into all petting, head bunting, purring, and rolling over onto her side as she is pet. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, Jaboti remains at the front and continues to allow all further petting and handling. When the interaction is ended and the kennel door is closed, Jaboti gently extends her paw outside of the kennel door, pawing towards the assessor to solicit further attention.

Jaboti interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

255831.name: Diane
255831.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Diane is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Diane has been difficult to remove from the kennel safely due to her dodging the lead and her defensive escalations - tense body, growling, baring teeth, and biting the leash. Out of the kennel, Diane has shown sociable behaviors with select staff - pressing herself into their legs or laps for contact. But she recently escalated to growl and lip curl at a handler after soliciting petting. Medically, Diane is apparently healthy.

Diane came into the care center as a stray; due to this, her behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. She has escalated to higher level warnings throughout her care when handlers attempt to remove her from the kennel. Due to all noted concerns displayed in the care center, the behavior department recommends Diane be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow Diane to acclimate comfortably to her new environment; force-free, reward based training only is advised when introducing Diane to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Diane presents with outside of the care centers.

255842.name: Mia
255842.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Mia is a sweet, affectionate lap cat looking for a quiet home. She was surrendered after a stressful incident at home: during a chaotic moment while her owner was cleaning, with her owner's adult daughter and 1-year-old grandchild also present, Mia scratched and bit several people in the commotion. Up until that point, she had always been well-behaved, and her family describes her as normally shy with strangers but otherwise an easygoing, gentle cat.

At home, Mia was litter box trained, low-energy, and quiet - the kind of cat who likes curling up on a lap and being petted. She could play boisterously, especially with kids, so an adult home is best!

Since arriving at the shelter, Mia was initially fearful but has settled in nicely. She now enjoys being petted, has warmed up to staff and volunteers, and loves chasing a feather wand. She appears to be in good health.
Mia would do best in a calm household where she can decompress at her own pace - likely a great fit for a quiet home, possibly without young children, where she can get to know her people gradually and become the devoted lap cat she's shown herself to be.


What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

255842.summaryHtml:
A volunteer writes: Mia is a sweet, affectionate lap cat looking for a quiet home. She was surrendered after a stressful incident at home: during a chaotic moment while her owner was cleaning, with her owner's adult daughter and 1-year-old grandchild also present, Mia scratched and bit several people in the commotion. Up until that point, she had always been well-behaved, and her family describes her as normally shy with strangers but otherwise an easygoing, gentle cat. At home, Mia was litter box trained, low-energy, and quiet - the kind of cat who likes curling up on a lap and being petted. She could play boisterously, especially with kids, so an adult home is best! Since arriving at the shelter, Mia was initially fearful but has settled in nicely. She now enjoys being petted, has warmed up to staff and volunteers, and loves chasing a feather wand. She appears to be in good health. Mia would do best in a calm household where she can decompress at her own pace - likely a great fit for a quiet home, possibly without young children, where she can get to know her people gradually and become the devoted lap cat she's shown herself to be.

She walks so well on leash and doesn't bark back when dogs bark at her. Even though she's shy, she still allows people to come up and pet her. 255869.name: Teddy Minino
255869.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Teddy Minino is a young and handsome tiger brought to us by his short time family(he was found as a stray) as the owner's child asthma got worse. Being an unneutered male, Teddy Minino also sprayed. Teddy Minino appears at first shy, laying quietly at the back of his cubby. He is a handsome and healthy looking feline, well cared for and accepting my petting, leaning and even purring softly after a while. No hissing, no swatting, a nice kitty. As I brought a feather wand, Teddy Minino's eyes lit up. He started teasing the feather gently and allowed me to pet him while I was playing with him. Teddy Minino did not expect another loss in his life when he thought he had a home. He has the potential to be a playful, loving and happy pet but his new family needs to give him time and space to show his lovely self. Come and meet Teddy Minino at the Manhattan Care Center!









What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

255878.name: Ambrosius
255878.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, June 7 from 11AM - 4PM at Petco Love Adoption Event, Union Square Park, 201 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Meet Ambrosius!
At just six months old, Ambrosius has already been through quite an adventure. He was found tied to a pipe with a bag of supplies beside him, left behind through no fault of his own. While the shelter can feel overwhelming for this young pup, he's slowly showing us that beneath his nervous exterior is a sweet dog who wants to connect with people at his own pace.

My Ideal Home
Ambrosius is looking for a calm, patient home that will give him the time he needs to settle in and build confidence. New experiences can be a little scary for him right now, so he'll do best with adopters who understand that trust takes time and are willing to let him move at his own speed. Once he feels safe, he has all the potential to blossom into a wonderful companion.

Good with Kids?
Ambrosius is seeking an adult-only home. Due to his fearful nature, he would be most comfortable in a quieter environment without young children.

Good with Other Pets?
Ambrosius' history with other animals is unknown. He has not shown reactivity toward dogs while in our care, but slow introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Leash Manners
Ambrosius walks politely on leash and does not pull, though he can be hesitant to leave his kennel and may need encouragement when entering new environments. As his confidence grows, his comfort level on walks is likely to improve as well.

Overall Health
Ambrosius is a healthy young dog who has recently been neutered and is recovering well.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Ambrosius is a fearful young dog who would benefit from a patient adopter committed to helping him build confidence through positive experiences and gentle guidance.

Other Fun Facts
Despite being shy, Ambrosius enjoys treats, toys, and exploring at his own pace. With a little patience and a lot of kindness, this young pup is ready to discover that the world can be a safe and happy place.

255891.name: Atlas Axel
255891.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Atlas Axel is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Atlas Axel has not acclimated well to the shelter environment despite the best efforts to help him acclimate and keep him comfortable. While in the kennel, he has escalated to charging handlers, snapping at leads, and lunging during attempts to remove him from the kennel. Upon returning to the kennel, he intermittently becomes reluctant. Once out, he remains aloof but readily explores different scents during his walks. Recently, he has begun to play with toys (balls and plush toys) but has also shown guarding behaviors. He became tense, started to hover, and then growled when a handler walked around him while he was engaged with the toys.  Medically, Atlas Axel is being treated for CIRDC.

Atlas Axel was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. He has escalated to higher-level warnings when handlers attempted to remove him from the kennel. Once out of the kennel, he remains avoidant. Due to all noted concerns displayed in the care center, the behavior department recommends that Atlas be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow Atlas to acclimate comfortably to his new environment; force-free, reward-based training only is advised when introducing him to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Atlas Axel presents with outside of the care centers.

255896.name: Halle
255896.summary:
My Foster Writes: Halle is a friendly, chatty girl who LOVES to play. We've been on a very pleasant rollercoaster with her since she arrived - for the first few days, she was extremely clingy and cuddly. Then, her independent, playful, vocal side came out and she was in hilarious zoomie-mode for half of the day (and night!) when she wasn't napping in her favourite chair.
Now, with regular playtime and pets, she's settled somewhere in between. She spends much of her time snoozing, and when she's awake she follows us from room to room, hopeful for attention (she loves to flop by our feet for pets!) Sometimes she will curl up next to or in a lap. When we wake up in the morning, she wants a proper cuddle in bed with us. She chirps, murmurs, and chats throughout the day (and night!), especially when we interact with her! She loves playtime and will often bring us a spring toy or stuffy to signal that she wants us to get her wand toy out. Sometimes we wake up to find that she's put a toy on our bed in the night as a little gift to us :)
She is very food motivated and may be an excellent candidate for training some treat-motivated tricks like high-five, spin, etc. She allows most handling with no issues. She does get a little overstimulated sometimes and may gently nibble you to let you know to stop petting her. She does best with 3+ short, intense play sessions a day (we've been trying simple food puzzles with her too which she's been loving!)
She prefers a large, open litter box, but may be open to other types with slow, patient training.

When Halle first arrived at the care center, she seemed convinced she was invisible under her blanket, even with the bottom half of her body sticking out. It might not have been the most effective disguise, but it sure was adorable. We don't know much about her story, arriving as a stray who was seen napping in the park garbage can enough times for a kind human to decide to help her out. What we do know is that once she's given some time to warm up, Halle is an affectionate, sweet and people-loving cat. She still greatly appreciates a good hiding place, making a cozy box her very favorite hang out spot. Though as she learns that she's safe, she's becoming much more interested in snuggles than hiding away. She's slowly blossoming and showing her silly side, sometimes spotted during quiet hours dancing back and forth in her kennel and investigating toys.
A gentle little soul with a soft heart. Halle is looking for a patient, calm home where she can keep discovering just how wonderful it is to be pampered and loved.

255903.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ducky is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Ducky has been struggling to acclimate and has began to intensely leash bite, particularly when returning to kennel. Ducky has become difficult to redirect with treats and other reinforcers when returning to kennel. Ducky is social with staff and is exuberant but is struggling in the care center. Medically, Ducky has a Cherry Eye.

Ducky was surrendered as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Ducky has been highly social with staff and handlers during his stay in care. But when attempting to return to the building after walks or to his kennel, Ducky begins balking and then pancaking. He has escalated to lunging at other kennels once in the room and will intermittently follow treats into his kennel. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Ducky to be placed in an adult-only home with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!
I need a home where there are no other dogs.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

255907.name: Oreo
255907.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Oreo is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Oreo has displayed growling, hard barking, and lunging toward staff in hallways, making it difficult to walk him safely. He also displays leash biting when aroused and, during his behavioral assessment, hovered over a toy and snapped at the assessment hand showing significant resource guarding. Oreo loves to engage with treats and cues he knows, but is struggling to acclimate. Medically, Oreo is Underweight.	

Oreo came into the care center as a stray, so his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Oreo is noted to allow petting and interest in treats. Due to all noted concerns displayed in the care center, the behavior department recommends Oreo be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow Oreo to acclimate comfortably to her new environment; force-free, reward based training only is advised when introducing Oreo to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Oreo presents with outside of the care centers.

A volunteer writes: Spending time with Oreo is always a joy. This sweet soul arrived at the shelter scared, very underweight, and hungry, but still ready to make friends with everyone in his path. Oreo was found as stray by police officers, who say he was sweet and friendly and allowed all handling. On walks, he's confident and eager to explore, checking in with us and happily accepting all the treats on offer; he displays no reactivity to passing dogs.

We don't know much about his past, though it seems like life, at least recently, has not treated Oreo kindly, based on how skinny he arrived. But he acts like he knows tomorrow is a new day: He's not letting his past define him, and he's ready for his new chapter! He's been known to lean into us for all the scritches and we think he will thrive in the safety and comfort of a loving home.

255908.name: Thessaly
255908.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, June 7 from 11AM - 4PM at Petco Love Adoption Event, Union Square Park, 201 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Meet Thessaly!
If you're looking for a happy-go-lucky best friend, Thessaly may be your perfect match. This young girl arrived at ACC as a stray and immediately charmed everyone she met with her wagging tail, wiggly body, and friendly personality. She loves meeting new people and seems to believe that everyone is a potential new friend.

My Ideal Home
Thessaly is an affectionate, social dog who would thrive in a home where she can be part of the action. Whether it's neighborhood walks, playtime, or simply hanging out with her people, she's happiest when she's included. Her cheerful personality and easygoing nature make her a wonderful candidate for many different types of homes.

Good with Kids?
Thessaly's history with children is unknown, but she has been consistently friendly, social, and affectionate with people throughout her time at the Care Centers.

Good with Other Pets?
Because Thessaly arrived as a stray, her history with other animals is unknown. However, she has shown no reactivity to dogs while out on walks and has handled shelter life with a relaxed and social attitude.

Leash Manners
Thessaly walks beautifully on leash with little to no pulling. She enjoys getting out and about, greeting new people with her signature wiggly body and happy demeanor, while remaining calm around dogs and passersby.

Overall Health
Thessaly is a healthy young dog who has already been spayed and is ready to head home. She recently recovered well from surgery and is currently doing great in our care.

Personality
Thessaly is the kind of dog who brightens a room the moment she enters it. Friendly, affectionate, playful, and full of joy, she's ready to bring plenty of tail wags and happy adventures to her future family.

My Boroughbreaker writes: What a sweet girl. Such a good walker. I would love to take her on a borough break again.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.Pre-Screener Form

Oley is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. She has been observed retreating to the back of her kennel, alert barking at approaching handlers, and snapping at the leash during leashing attempts. During handling, Oley requires extensive coaxing before she can be safely leashed and removed from her kennel. Oley allows minimal touch from familiar handlers. Medically, Oley has Dental Disease Mild-Moderate.

Since arriving at the care centers Oley has displayed concerning levels of FAS and has allowed minimal handling for leashing or walks. She has shown fearful and defensive aggression in kennel when being leashed and has escalating to leash biting and bearing teeth in kennel. Outside she is tense and avoidant of people and will flinch when her leash is clipped by staff. We recommend placement with a New Hope rescue partner who is able to provide an experienced, adult-only foster home. Force-free, reward based training and/or consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended.

255912.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!

A volunteer writes: It hurts my heart to see the number next to his age, but I don't think Puss-N-Boots is looking for any pity and rightfully so. He's a bright and happy cat who's quick to purr and offer his paw in friendship as that's really all he wants. I tried to stand corrected as Puss-N-Boots nuzzled into my hand while hopping in and out of his box and cuddling like we've known each other forever. Puss-N-Boots was found in a carrier with another cat who has since been adopted. Left outside the shelter gate one morning, his history is a bit of a mystery, but we all want him to have the bright future he deserves.

255913.name: Muffy
255913.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Muffy is on the at-risk list for medical reasons. Muffy is a very sweet old tripod kitty that has been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. She also has several other medical conditions (including dental disease) that will require veterinary follow-up. Behaviorally, Muffy is social, easy to handle, and loves petting.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.

A volunteer writes: Muffy's the kind of cat you have to meet, the kind who stumbles over her paws in her sincerest efforts to hand you her heart and all I want is for her to get the chance she deserves. Subsequently, I'm more than a little worried that I won't be able to do Muffy justice with just words. Muffy was found in a carrier with another cat abandoned in a carrier outside the shelter gate. A diabetic senior with three paws who might have a little idea of all that she's up against to find a forever home, she's working so much harder than she should to stand out. I want to do everything I can to verify that Muffy's a dream. Heartbreakingly happy to be here, she welcomed me by tucking her head into my hand and gazing up with so much love that I felt compelled to offer her the world. She kneads and circles as she cuddles hoping that someone will accept her and offer her the chance she's been so sweetly hoping and asking for.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Rocko is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Rocko is a social dog but presents as highly anxious. He has been observed licking the walls of his kennel, and when placed in a crate, he will bite at the crate bars and pull at his bedding. More recently, Rocko has been grabbing staff leashes and mouthing their clothing when they attempt to remove him. Medically, Rocko has dental disease.
 
Rocko came in the care center as a stray; due to this, his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Rocko has displayed increasing arousal around kennel handling, including leash biting, jumping at the kennel door, and attempts to push out when the kennel is opened. He has reportedly mouthed or grabbed handlers on several occasions, including biting a handler's sleeve and more recently biting and holding a handler's finger. Outside of the kennel, Rocko is social with familiar handlers, enjoys petting, and walks with mild to moderate pulling.  Rocko is available for rescue through one of our new hope partners; we recommend positive reinforcement training to improve his impulse control and handling.

He has reportedly mouthed or grabbed handlers on several occasions, including biting a handler's sleeve and more recently biting and holding a handler's finger. Outside of the kennel, Rocko is social with familiar handlers, enjoys petting, and walks with mild to moderate pulling. Rocko is available for rescue through one of our new hope partners; we recommend positive reinforcement training to improve his impulse control and handling.

255918.name: Horchata Icee
255918.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, June 7 from 11AM - 4PM at Petco Love Adoption Event, Union Square Park, 201 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Meet Horchata Icee!
Sweet, spunky, and full of personality, Horchata Icee is a little dog with a big heart. Found alone near a dog run, she quickly won over staff with her friendly nature, wagging tail, and enthusiasm for making new friends. The Good Samaritan who brought her to ACC reported that she happily jumped into his lap during the car ride and stayed calm the entire trip. Whether she's hopping up to say hello or happily strolling by your side, Horchata Icee is always ready to brighten your day.

My Ideal Home
Horchata Icee would love a patient family that can help her continue building confidence while enjoying all the fun life has to offer. She enjoys spending time with people, loves treats, and is eager to be included in daily adventures. While she can be a little cautious in new situations, she quickly warms up when given time and gentle encouragement.

Good with Kids?
Because Horchata Icee can be sensitive about handling and prefers to approach people on her own terms, ACC recommends a home with children over the age of five. She will thrive with a family that respects her boundaries and allows her to build trust at her own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
Horchata Icee has shown no reactivity toward dogs while out on walks and has remained calm when encountering other dogs in the shelter environment. Since her history with other pets is unknown, slow introductions are recommended.

Leash Manners
Horchata Icee enjoys getting out and exploring. She walks with only mild leash tension and stays close to her handler. Loud or sudden noises can sometimes startle her, but she recovers well with reassurance and support from her person.

Behavior Notes
Horchata Icee has been assessed as a Behavior Level 2 dog. She is a friendly and social dog who enjoys treats, attention, and spending time with people, but she can be a bit cautious with handling and may choose to move away when she's unsure. She has shown some fearful tendencies in new situations and would benefit from a calm home where she can settle in at her own pace. Giving her choices, allowing her to approach voluntarily, and using positive reinforcement will help her build confidence and thrive.

Overall Health
Horchata Icee is in good health and ready to head home. She has a small corneal scar in her right eye that does not currently require treatment and otherwise appears healthy.

Personality
This little lady is equal parts playful and sensitive. She loves treats, enjoys affection, and has an endearing way of sitting in front of people and gazing up at them for attention. Once she feels comfortable, her happy, wiggly personality shines through. With a little patience and a lot of love, Horchata Icee is sure to become a devoted companion and loyal best friend.

255957.name: Max
255957.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Max is on the at risk list for medical reasons. Max is a geriatric dog with comorbidities. Most significantly, his bloodwork is suggestive of hypothyroidism and he has weakness and neurologic deficits in his hindlimbs. With placement, Max will need either palliative care or further veterinary care including diagnostics and long-term treatment plan. Behaviorally, Max has been timid but has allowed most handling and is food motivated.

Meet Max! This friendly boy loves being around people and is happiest when he's spending time with his family. Affectionate and social, Max enjoys companionship and can often be found relaxing nearby or soaking up attention from his favorite humans.

Max enjoys spending time outdoors, especially lounging in the yard and taking in the sights and smells around him. When it's time for a ride, Max is ready to go-he loves car rides and would be thrilled to join you on your next adventure.

Max is comfortable with bathing and brushing, knows the cues "sit" and "stay," and has earned praise from his previous owner for being both friendly and full of enthusiasm. He has been reported to be friendly and outgoing when meeting unfamiliar dogs on leash. While he has no known experience with familiar dogs or off-leash dog interactions, he has also been described as friendly and outgoing around cats and other animals.

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.

255971.name: Pimienta
255971.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Pimienta is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Pimienta has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and is not allowing for handling. She escalates to baring teeth, severe thrashing, alligator rolling, and flailing when attempting to leash and remove her from her kennel for walks or interaction. She has not taken any offered treats from handlers nor been receptive to any coaxing efforts or reinforcers. Medically, Pimienta has dermatitis and an ear infection.

Pimienta was surrendered by her previous owner due to her ongoing allergies. Her previous family described her as a medium-energy dog who could be aloof at times, but was mostly social and affectionate with her people. She would follow her family around the home and enjoyed lounging in the living room. Pimienta was reported to love bath time/water, would go on 2-3 walks a day for about 20 minutes. Her favorite toys to play with were balls. Pimienta has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and has not allowed for removal from her kennel. She remains intensely fearful, begins thrashing, flailing, and/or gator rolling severely in her kennel once leashed, which has caused concern for her potentially injuring herself. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Pimienta to be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner in conjunction with force-free, reward-based training with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Pimienta presents with outside of the care centers.

A volunteer writes: T. Frank has welcomed us as a kind of control group in his experiments to find just the right hello that will win his forever family's heart. This means we get a lot of outstretched paws tapping us through the bars of his condo and spirited tumbles as he tries to get himself out of the condo and into our lap. T. Frank is absolutely here to make friends and find a family, but his easy going fun and gentle heartedness belie a much tougher beginning. Found outside limping with some injuries, T. Frank found a kind person and introduced himself. He stayed around and they patiently waited with him but when they saw that T. Frank was getting bullied by some neighborhood cats, they scooped him up and brought him home where he was a model houseguest who only wanted to catch up on some rest. He's proven again and again that he's willing to take chances and now he just needs someone to take one on him.

255989.summary:
Meet Bello!
Bello arrived at the shelter as a stray, so while his past is a mystery, we know he has a sweet and gentle side that shines through. This handsome boy is learning to trust again and has shown that he loves spending time with people once he feels comfortable. Bello enjoys affection, takes treats nicely, and has a special way of making connections with the humans around him.

My Ideal Home
Bello would do best with a patient adopter who understands that building trust takes time. He will thrive in a calm, predictable environment where he can move at his own pace and continue gaining confidence. Positive reinforcement, enrichment activities, and gentle interactions will help Bello feel safe and supported as he settles into his new life.

Good with Other Pets?
Bello's history with other animals is unknown, but he has had some interactions with other dogs while at the shelter. He has shown the ability to greet and disengage appropriately, though his comfort level can depend on the situation. Due to his body language during dog interactions, a home without dog parks is recommended, and any future dog introductions should be slow and thoughtful.

Good with Kids?
Due to Bello's handling sensitivities and moments when he has felt uncomfortable, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. Bello would do best with people who can respect his boundaries, allow him to make choices, and help him feel secure as he adjusts to his new surroundings.

Things to Know
Bello is a sensitive pup who may need extra time to feel comfortable in new situations. During his time at the shelter, he has shown signs of anxiety and can become overwhelmed, so a calm routine and patient approach will be important. Bello should be allowed to approach new experiences at his own pace and will benefit from force-free training, enrichment, and plenty of positive experiences. Once he trusts you, you may discover the sweet, affectionate dog who loves nothing more than leaning in for attention and being by your side.

Volunteer Love
A volunteer writes: I recently discovered something truly adorable about Bello: he's a hugger! During a walk, Bello politely stood by my side while I chatted with a staff member. After a few minutes, he gently placed his paws on my arms and looked up at me with the sweetest, softest expression. As I gave him some gentle pets, he leaned right in, snuggled his head into my arm, and completely melted my heart.

Volunteer Love
A volunteer writes: As I began slowly rubbing his cheeks and chin, he leaned into me with a dreamy, blissful expression. And as I gently pet along his back, he snuggled his head into the crook of my arm. Bello was more than happy to lean back in and soak up all the affection I showered on him. It's amazing how quickly Bello has warmed up and felt trustful enough to solicit attention and initiate hugs. I honestly don't think it's possible to meet Bello and not fall in love with him. He's so sweet, gentle, and affectionate; and has a way of making you feel that the very best part of his day is being with you.

Considering what sounds like a difficult past, it is incredible how quickly Bello has learned to trust and seek out affection. He is a treat-loving, gentle pup who knows "sit," takes treats nicely, and has shown polite leash manners. Bello has a way of making you feel like being with you is the highlight of his day, and he is ready to find someone who will show him just how loved he can be.

256010.name: Cookie
256010.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Cookie is a sweet "oreo cookie" who really loves people and we heard, cats and kids too. He is said to be quiet and cuddly, a gentle lap cat. Cookie was surrendered though because of some litter box issues, a problem we did not encounter during his stay at the care center. There are many treatable reasons for a cat not using his/her litter box and they could be discussed with our adoption counselors. Cookie is a little gem, a very affectionate, friendly and welcoming senior who lives for the presence of visitors and staff. He is a true lap cat, enjoying every minutes spent in the arms of volunteers(see video). His presence is very soothing and we surely need love, peace and quiet in this tumultuous world... Cookie like any senior cat has some health issues but did excellently on his behavior evaluation. He so dream to spend his golden years with you. Come and meet Cookie very soon at the Manhattan Care Center.






What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!

Hi there! My name is Koala and I've been at the Queens ACC since June (yes, you read that right)! I arrived as a stray so the staff don't know what my life was like before coming to ACC, but I had various injuries that I'm recovering from really well. I only require a little extra paperwork to be filled out and a few extra vet visits this year because one of my injuries was likely a bite wound (now fully healed). I'm thankful for everyone at ACC taking such good care of me, but I think I'd like to find my forever home now. So what are you waiting for? Ask about me today!

256015.name: Baby Boo
256015.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Baby Boo appears to be fearful and may not have had much human interaction up to this point. During the assessment he flinched slightly when picked up and is somewhat fearful of interactions with humans. He would benefit from extra socialization and is at the prime age for being socialized fully. We recommend that this cat go to a home with cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff. Contact with young children should be avoided or done under strict supervision to prevent provoking a fear response, further delaying socialization. He may do well in a home with responsible older children, able to respect his boundaries and understand his needs for a slow approach and quiet environment at this time.
I would benefit from going to a home with a friendly and social older cat that loves people. Maybe they can take me under their wing to teach me the ropes of being a cuddle bug and trusting me new family!
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I am really treat motivated. You can use treats to teach me new things!

256018.name: Uzi
256018.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Uzi is on the at-risk list due to behavior. Although he has been social and friendly with staff, Uzi has a prior bite/scratch history without known triggers and has shown signs of a potential for overstimulation. He is not thriving in the care center, and it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience managing cats with overstimulation.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Uzi is a big "galoot" of a cat! He was at the front, sweet, friendly, and curious, loving treats and leaning in nicely for cheek rubs. He warmed up quickly, leaning in more with a high tail and enjoying all petting. He was curious and interested in possibly coming out of the kennel, and when picked up and held, he remained calm in the assessor's arms. When set back down, he remained at the front, pushing against the assessor's hand as if wanting either more attention or out of the kennel, or both.

Due to prior owner history (see separate notes) and a bite/scratch history we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced cat parent home.

A volunteer writes: Uzi was sleeping so soundly that it was momentarily difficult for me to imagine that he's ever had a care in the world, but then I noticed the note explaining that his blanket and toys help to provide some of the security he's been looking for. We all contain multitudes so though I welcomed the exuberant cheek rubs and enthusiastic cuddles that I was generously gifted upon opening the door, I also know the shelter, and life in general, can be a lot. Uzi has a lot going for him besides his gorgeously fluffed cheeks. He's chatty and affectionate, skilled at choosing the best window seats and we've heard he plays with other cats, but something that will work for Uzi is an experienced and loving family where he will feel understood and welcomed for who he is.

He's chatty and affectionate, skilled at choosing the best window seats and we've heard he plays with other cats, but something that will work for Uzi is an experienced and loving family where he will feel understood and welcomed for who he is.

256027.name: Tiffany
256027.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

Upon being evaluated again, Tiffany appears to be displaying behaviors that indicate a very high level of FAS and quickly escalates to defensive aggression. She is noted to be a somewhat fearful cat in her previous home and takes some time to warm up to strangers and appreciates her boundaries being respected - making a shelter environment one that would be difficult for her to adjust to. While she may have some potential with socialization to be approached and adjust to the shelter, at this time, she displays behaviors that are not appropriate for general adoption or the adoptions floor.  She displays high levels of FAS and during her assessment, and quickly escalated to defensive behaviors. The behavior team feels that she would do best in an adult-only home with experienced adopters that are willing to give her plenty of time to adjust to her new environment, and understand how to work with fearful cats. Her behaviors are likely shelter specific and the behavior team feels that once given time to decompress outside of the shelter, approached slowly and with respect for her boundaries, she will likely return to her previous playful, lap cat, and cuddly behaviors once she is comfortable with her new family and feels safe in her new home.

256030.name: Faith
256030.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Faith is with us as her owner sadly passed away. A relative told us that Faith was a little shy with strangers but was otherwise a very friendly, playful, chatty and affectionate pet. Faith had a hard time in her debuts at the care center. Time often does its job as well as the care and love from staff and volunteers. Faith who still has some timid sides, comes readily  out when a visitor is at her door. She is sooo cute, head bunts, leans into pets and enjoys treats right from my hand. She is still a little worried with loud noises and guests barging into the adoption room but recovers quickly with appeasing words and more treats. Faith would love to be home, one that is welcoming and quiet and with a new owner or family who will understand that she went though hard times. Faith is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center! 







What my friends at ACC say about me:
Faith has made excellent improvement since her first assessment and was in the cubby with somewhat large pupils, but a very sweet demeanor. She enjoyed all petting, leaning in nicely for cheek rubs and coming forward slightly. She made nice eye contact with the assessor and enjoyed all petting and squeeze-up treats.

Faith interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

256034.name: Kaviar
256034.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Kaviar's start in life was a hard one. Found as a stray by a kind-hearted Good Samaritan, he was shuffled between several temporary caretakers in a very short time - enough to make any cat anxious and unsure of who to trust. During one of these transitions, frightened and trying to protect himself, he hid under a bed. When he was scruffed to be moved, panic took over and he bit out of fear, not aggression.
He arrived at our care center frantic and overwhelmed - but given time, patience, and a calm space, Kaviar has shown us who he really is: a gentle, affectionate boy with so much love to give. He now seeks out attention, hops up onto laps, and melts into long petting sessions. He's still a little jumpy around sudden movements, loud voices, or people rushing into his space - understandable, given everything he's been through - but his sweetness always comes back once he feels safe again.
Kaviar is looking for a quiet, stable home where he can finally exhale. A patient adopter who understands that trust takes time, a peaceful household without small children, and a family willing to let him set the pace as he settles in. In return, he offers a whole lot of love, warm cuddles, and the quiet joy of watching a scared cat become a confident one.
If you can offer Kaviar the calm and consistency he needs, he'll reward you with everything he has to give. 



What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

The moment we sat down on the grass in the park she came to lay on top of me and put her head next to mine. She loves to play with her toys and gives a much younger than 7 year old energy! This girl has the most beautiful soul and anyone would be SOO lucky to have her apart of their lives!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.

I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

256045.name: Soursop
256045.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, June 7 from 11AM - 4PM at Petco Love Adoption Event, Union Square Park, 201 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Meet Soursop!
Soursop is a happy, treat-loving puppy who is ready to start the next chapter of his life. Found wandering as a stray, this handsome young dog has quickly charmed staff with his friendly personality, wiggly body, and enthusiasm for snacks. At just six months old, Soursop is still learning about the world and is looking for a family to help him grow into the best dog he can be.

My Ideal Home
Soursop would love a home that can provide plenty of guidance, structure, and positive experiences as he continues to mature. Like many young dogs, he will benefit from training, socialization, and lots of opportunities to play, learn, and explore.

Good with Kids?
Soursop's history with children is unknown, but his friendly and social nature suggests he may enjoy a family environment. As with any newly adopted dog, introductions should be supervised while everyone gets to know each other.

Good with Other Pets?
While Soursop arrived as a stray and his history with other animals is unknown, he has shown appropriate social behavior when meeting another dog in the shelter. He took his time getting comfortable, then happily followed and investigated his canine companion, demonstrating polite and respectful interactions.

Leash Manners
Soursop has been easy to handle during walks and enjoys getting out to explore. He has shown no reactivity toward people or other dogs while moving through the shelter.

Overall Health
Soursop is in good health, recently neutered, up to date on vaccinations, heartworm negative, and ready to head home.

Other Fun Facts
Soursop absolutely loves treats and is highly food motivated, making him a great candidate for reward-based training. He is social, affectionate, and eager to make new friends wherever he goes.

256079.name: Sirios
256079.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Sirios is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Sirios displays signs of kennel-related stress, including prolonged digging under his kennel door to the point of causing abrasions to his front legs. He has also shown reluctance to return to his kennel, including planting himself, refusing to walk, and attempting to push back out after entering. Sirios is social with handlers, and loves to be around staff, but is struggling to acclimate. Medically, Sirios is apparently healthy.

Sirios was surrendered by his previous owner due to his fearfulness of being outside and his fearfulness of strangers. He was kept indoors due to this. His previous family described him as a social, friendly, active, but calm dog with his people. He would spend most of his time in the bedroom portion of the home. When they did attempt to take him for walks, he was noted to pull moderately. During his intake, Sirios was friendly with staff and allowed petting. But when walking him to the kennel, Sirios began thrashing, and a belly band was used by a second handler to assist with getting him into the kennel safely. He has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. Sirios continues to refuse to return to the kennel. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

256081.name: Jirachi
256081.summary:
My foster writes: Jirachi is an absolute angel. I had him for a borough break and needed to take him out for a straycation. He is loyal, docile, playful, and cuddly. His idea of a perfect day is a long walk followed by couch cuddle time, zoomies/rolling around break, followed by playing with one of his toys. Jirachi is adaptable and smart. If you tell him a rule, he will follow it very quickly and consistently. For example, one told he couldn't climb on a piece of furniture in an office, he didn't try again. He shows his love by cuddling, rubbing his body against you, and rolling around in your presence. He seems house trained though had a tiny accident when separated for the first time. Although Jirachi loves his wet food, he is not extremely treat motivated; pleasing his human is his primary goal. He couldn't care less about small animals, screaming children, thunder, vacuums or other typical dog triggers. He is well behaved in cars and on public transportation. He looks keen to play with other dogs, though didn't get a chance due to foster rules. He is a perfect dog looking for his perfect human.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Jirachi is an amazing intro dog. He is amazing on a leash, knows his sit, and becomes loyal to his handler once you give him some time to trust and warm up. Although he was not allowed to play with other dogs, he gave some dogs a play bow outside a fence when he found one he thought could be his friend. He was neutral towards treats, eating only half of his pup cups and accepting only two treats at a time. He loves to sniff the pee-mails, but is easily redirectable. Once child on a passing stroller (approximately 18 months old) reached his hand out to touch him and he didn't even flinch or react. He seemed interested in a dog drinking from a hose, so he may be interested in a nice beach day or playing int he water. He liked to give face kisses when he was thankful but knew when to stop. With Jirachi's temperament and dashing good looks, Jirachi's future family will be very lucky to have him in their lives.

256085.name: Big Jim
256085.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!


A volunteer writes: Want to feel like you're walking around town with an A-list celebrity every day? Allow us to introduce you to Big Jim! This hunky nugget was dropped off with no information at a police station, and has made it his mission to befriend every single person in his path since. When police transported him to the shelter, he didn't seem one bit fazed by this new adventure: Wiggly and loose, he greeted staff with a wagging tail, jumping up for attention, giving kisses, and even rolling over for belly rubs.

He's been a big ham, enjoying yard time with (you guessed it) all of his new best friends, flopping around on his back like it's his job. During play group, he greeted another dog at the gate with a loose and wiggly body and wagging tail. On walks around the shelter, Big Jim makes many neighborhood fans, and it's not hard to see why. His happy trot, chunky physique, and impeccable underbite speak for themselves. He greets fellow volunteers like the whole world exists just to give him attention - and we don't think he's wrong!

256087.name: Apple Fritter
256087.summary:
Meet Apple Fritter!
Apple Fritter was found tied to a gate with Powdered Donut 256088 and, like his friend Powdered Donut, arrived undernourished and very fearful. While he started off quite timid, he has begun to show that with patience and gentle handling, he can slowly warm up and accept interaction.

My Ideal Home
Apple Fritter would do best in a calm, patient home that allows him to adjust at his own pace. He benefits from quiet environments, slow introductions, and positive reinforcement to help him build confidence and feel secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Apple Fritter came in with another dog, but his behavior with other animals is largely unknown, so slow, structured introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearfulness, Apple Fritter is recommended for a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Apple Fritter is a sensitive, shy dog who takes time to warm up to new people and environments. Once comfortable, he allows gentle handling and will take treats softly, but he can be easily overwhelmed by loud noises and unfamiliar situations. He walks with a loose leash but may show fear in stimulating environments. With consistency, patience, and a calm routine, he has strong potential to continue building confidence.

Fun Fact
Just like his name, Apple Fritter is best appreciated warm and gentle. Once he trusts you, his sweet personality really comes through.

A volunteer writes: This sweet little baby needs some extra TLC and if you meet him, you'll quicky see why. Apple Fritter is completely overwhelmed in a noisy, overcrowded shelter environment. Coming out of his cage, he scrambles through the room, trying to makes it past the row of crates of barking dogs as fast as he can. When it's time to go back, he pancakes in the hallway and I end up having to lift him back in.

Outside though, it's a whole different story. In a quieter, calmer environment, Apple Fritter is as sweet as his name. He stands up and softly snuggles into me, like it's the safest, most loving place in the world. As I give him long, gentle back rubs, he snuggles even closer, and I feel like we could both just stay like this all afternoon.  

We don't know anything about Fritter's life other than he probably lived with the dog he arrived with (Powered Donut: 256088) - both fearful, yet affectionate, and considerably underweight. Fritter seems to be housebroken with regular walks, has nice leash manners, and loves treats.

I think when Fritter dreams of his post-shelter life, visions of snuggles and cuddles and a lap to call his own dance through his head. If you have a soft spot for shy, extra-sweet pups and can give him the love and security he's been missing, Apple Fritter would love to meet you.

256088.name: Powdered Donut
256088.summary:
Meet Powdered Donut!
Powdered Donut was found tied to a gate with Apple Fritter 256087 and, despite appearing undernourished and initially fearful, she has been steadily blossoming in care. Underneath her shy start is a truly sweet, affectionate young dog who is beginning to show more confidence each day.

My Ideal Home
Powdered Donut would do best in a patient, gentle home that can help her continue building confidence at her own pace. She enjoys affection, play, and companionship once comfortable, and will thrive with positive reinforcement, calm structure, and time to settle in.

Good with Other Pets?
Powdered Donut has shown playful, social behavior with other dogs and has engaged in friendly play in shelter settings, though introductions should always be gradual.

Good with Kids?
Due to her fearfulness, Powdered Donut is recommended for a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Powdered Donut is a gentle, affectionate dog who is becoming more comfortable with handling and interaction as she gains confidence. She walks well on leash, shows loose and social body language once settled, and enjoys play and affection with familiar people. While she can be initially timid, she warms up beautifully with patience and soft encouragement. 

Volunteer Note
A volunteer writes: I heard that when Powdered Donut came in, she was too scared to walk. So when she stopped midway on the ramp up to the yard, I was happy to see that it was because she needed to be pet STAT! We rubbed her sweet little head and proceeded to the yard where we did more of the same for the remaining time together. This girl is SO sweet, crumpling up like an accordion in my arms so that she fits neatly against my body. Her legs are so bowed out, perhaps from being crated too much as a young dog. It makes for some clumsiness, but like any young dog she's happy to move around freely and chase toys and run into your arms. She's truly precious, and while she looks more like an old fashioned style donut to me, she is in fact sugary sweet.

Fun Fact
True to her name, Powdered Donut is extra sweet once she melts into your arms and realizes she's safe.

256091.name: Marie
256091.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Marie tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

A volunteer writes: Anything we can do to convince Marie that the shelter is only temporary would be worth it but it would be helpful to have a little bit of buy-in on her part and so far we haven't been able to get very much of that. It doesn't mean we'll stop trying, however, so we offer the things we like as best we can. Marie loves to play gently and we have toys, but she doesn't always love the people coming in and out. Her other favorite thing is treats, but each time someone comes in the room, which as you might imagine happens frequently, she bounces back. We can work with this but we're trying to give Marie the time and space she usually likes to come around on her own terms. She's hoping to find a forever family who will open their hearts and homes and do just that.

256092.name: Rollie
256092.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Rollie is a cute little babe who came to us with a number of her housemates as their house counted too many cats. Rollie is quite shy, even skittish, although curious(she is only six month old) and starving for attention and love. She lives in her cubby, coming down only to use her litter box and eat.The adorable little girl comes slowly forward when called(after sampling a few treats), head bunts my hand, even drops on her kennel floor for more petting and suddenly backs off, sometimes with a little hiss or a little peck, worried, may be that her trust went a little too far(see her video). Rollie is an endearing youngster who has the potential to be a lovely pet in the right hands and the right environment. A quiet home without boisterous children and an understanding, patient and caring new owner is what Rollie truly needs.

256093.name: Houdini
256093.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
My purr motor is always running!
Houdini is laying curled up at the front of her top cubby as the assessor approaches, body relaxed and eyes closed. When the kennel door is opened and she is softly spoken to, she gets up, meows and stretches, and approaches the front of the kennel to greet the assessor with soft head bunts. She leans into all petting, raising her back as she is pet, tail held in a question mark position and occasionally tremoring excitedly at the base. Houdini softly meows at the assessor throughout her evaluation. When pickup is attempted, she is able to be picked up but is very tense and loudly stress meows when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she briefly retreats to the back of the kennel and lip licks. After a few seconds, she recovers and returns to the front of the kennel, head bunting and leaning into all further petting and handling.

Houdini interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Houdini go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and discomfort with pickup.

256101.name: Seal
256101.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Seal is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Seal has displayed high reactivity toward other dogs and has been reported to nip at staff members' hands and ankles while redirecting his frustration onto staff.He is also noted to display kennel stress heavy panting in front of his kennel door. During walks, he pulls toward other dogs and can at times be difficult to redirect and refocus. Seal has responded well to treats and is social with staff when not in the presence of other dogs. Medically, Seal is apparently healthy. 

Seal arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Seal has been observed to be on leash reactive and have handling sensitivity. When picked up, Seal is noted to head whip and snap at handers. While on leash Seal is reported to fixate on leash and react to dogs. After reacting to dogs, Seal would turn towards the handler and nip them. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

Meet Daisy!
Daisy is a sweet, affectionate young tabby who's ready to trade shelter life for a loving home. After being left behind by a family member, Daisy found herself raising three kittens while living in a crowded household. Despite all the changes she's experienced, she has remained friendly, social, and eager for human companionship. If you're looking for a cat who wants to be part of the family, Daisy may be your perfect match.

My Ideal Home
Daisy is the definition of a people cat. She loves being where her humans are and enjoys attention, affection, and companionship throughout the day. Whether she's curling up in your lap, chatting about her day, or following you from room to room, Daisy wants to be involved in family life. She would thrive in a home where she can receive plenty of love and interaction.

Good with Kids?
Yes! Daisy previously lived with children, including newborns, and is described as friendly and outgoing with kids. She plays gently and enjoys being part of a busy household.

Good with Other Pets?
Yes! Daisy has lived successfully with multiple cats, including her kittens, as well as a small dog. According to her previous family, she adjusts to new cats and dogs within a couple of weeks and has a history of living peacefully alongside both.

Overall Health
Daisy is a healthy 2-year-old cat with a good prognosis. She tested negative for FeLV/FIV, is up to date on her vaccinations, and was described by veterinary staff as friendly and soliciting attention during her exam. She appears to be intact and is ready for placement into a loving home.

Behavior Determination
Daisy's history and shelter observations paint a clear picture of a social, affectionate cat. She is described as a talkative lap cat who enjoys being held, brushed, and included in family activities. Shelter staff noted that she remained calm, social, and easy to handle throughout intake and medical care.

Other Fun Facts
Daisy loves interactive play, enjoys cardboard scratchers, and happily accepts nail trims and brushing sessions. She's a medium-energy cat who likes to spend her time wherever the people are. Her only complaint? She tends to stress-meow when placed in a carrier-she'd much rather be sitting in your lap instead! 🐾💕

256150.name: Bowie
256150.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Bowie is a very sweet and slightly shy cat who was in the den, curious and becoming slightly active when presented with treats. She then stuck her head out and accepted and enjoyed petting on her cheek and head. She leaned in nicely for cheek rubs and raised her chin for chin scratches. Sometimes she would go back into the den, but then she would pop her head back out and enjoy more petting. She could not be coaxed out of the den while the assessor was present, but when he shut the door, she came halfway out to eat the squeeze-up. She then came fully out and stayed out when the assessor reopened the door. She loved more petting, with a high, quivering (happy-to-see-you) tail, and she was coaxed even farther forward. She was reasonably calm when picked up and held and, when set back down, retreated slightly into the den, gave one single very small growl, and then came out to eat more treats.

Bowie interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.  	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

256162.name: Angel
256162.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Angel was found in the street, flanked by a bunch of kittens(age unknown). They were unfortunately separated and Angel was brought to her finder's home. She was upset and became frantic when a large dog was brought into the room she was in. I guess, trying to escape, she scratched or bit her host and subsequently was brought to the Manhattan Care Center. Poor cat...What an ordeal! What a terrible succession of events. Angel has been a sweet girl within our walls. She is quite thin but wears a lovely coat. A girly little gal, friendly, social(although a bit shy for a start) and enjoying all the attention and love she can get. Angel so deserves a better life with a caring and loving new owner, in a low traffic home(no small children) and no dogs... Angel would love to be yours.....

Angel is at the front of the kennel, sitting upright and meowing softly as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she leans forward to softly head bunt the assessor's hand. She accepts crunchy treats and allows and leans into all petting, raising her back as she is pet. When she is picked up and held, she remains calm, leans in, and purrs. When she is placed back down, she remains at the front, tail held upright in a question mark position and continuing to head bunt and lean into all petting.

Angel interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Angel go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and decompression periods.

256163.name: Jax
256163.summary:
Meet Jax!

Jax is a sweet, social 5-year-old who loves being with his people. Affectionate and loyal, he's happiest by your side and will happily follow you around just to keep you company. He thrives on attention, loves car rides, and enjoys spending time outdoors.

Jax is well-mannered and easy to groom, allowing baths and brushing without any fuss. He's also a smart boy who knows cues like Sit, Down, Stay, Wait, Paw, Come Here, and even "Let's go for a walk!" His favorite rewards? Any kind of treat!

If you're looking for a loving companion who will be your constant sidekick, Jax is ready to meet you.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
Jax clearly loves going for walks! Every time I picked up the leash, he thought it was time for another adventure-even when we were already outside. For most of the day, Jax was content relaxing in the shade while I worked in the garden, with the occasional stroll around the yard to check everything out. If he ever lost sight of me, Jax quickly came looking for me, which was incredibly sweet.
Jax absolutely loves treats and has wonderful manners when taking them. He was always polite and patient, although he did make me laugh when he gently tried to help himself to the treat bag sitting on a chair!
Jax also appears to be house-trained. During his stay, he never made any attempt to go to the bathroom inside the house, which was a great sign of his good manners.

256164.name: Carmelita
256164.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
Carmelita tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Carmelita is blind and, coming from a home to the shelter, does her best to manage the changes she's facing. Tucked in a safe little loaf in the corner of her condo, she leaned forward to meet my outstretched hand and gently sniffed before gliding back. She let me pet her and as I did, I noticed her noticing the little pieces of fluff coming off her and puffing her cheeks as she tried to engage her errant fur in a game. I brought over a pipecleaner feather and she played so sweetly, rolling over and bringing it to her face, reaching her paws out big and with so much heart. I don't have experience playing with cats who are blind but Carmelita showed me that a slower pace and taking her lead allows her to engage in a way that makes sense for her. This is what she's hoping for in a forever home - someone to meet her where she is and love her for who she is.

256174.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Ocelot has been placed on the at risk list for medical reasons. He has a severe URI that has caused several days of poor appetite, lethargy and discomfort. He needs support and a stress free environment.

Ocelot tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: Ocelots in the wild tend to be low-key and shy, and our boy Ocelot has been that way since arriving at the Care Center. Unfamiliar surroundings, lots of new noises and smells--we understand his hesitation. But once this handsome guy has had a little warm-up time, his sweet vibe comes through, and his desire to make friends with humans emerges. Ocelot did nicely on his behavior exam, sniffing treats and leaning in for pettings. We just know there's a wonderful home out there for him where he can come out of his shell and show off his loving and loyal personality. Meet Ocelot at the Manhattan Care Center today!

256175.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Sheba!
Sheba lost her home when her owner could no longer care for her, but she's ready to start her next chapter with a family to call her own. Her previous family described her as sweet, gentle, affectionate, and incredibly loyal. Whether she's soaking up the sunshine, curling up on a cozy blanket, or leaning in for cuddles, Sheba is happiest when she's close to the people she loves.

My Ideal Home
Sheba would thrive in a calm, adult-only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She's already house-trained, walks beautifully on a loose leash, and knows several cues including sit, stay, come, down, and leave it. She responds best to gentle encouragement, praise, treats, and a consistent routine.

Good with Other Pets?

Things to Know
