If you're looking for a loyal best friend who will happily share quiet moments and endless affection, Sheba is ready to come home.

A Volunteer Writes:
It can be heartbreaking to see a dog who once knew the comfort of a loving home adjusting to shelter life, but Sheba's sweet personality still shines through. Despite being a little uncertain in her new surroundings, she has shown just how gentle and affectionate she truly is.

Sheba's favorite things include being close to her people, relaxing in sunny spots, cuddling on soft blankets, and enjoying peaceful walks. When a volunteer met her, Sheba calmly walked out of her kennel despite the busy shelter environment, explored the play yard, and eventually decided that simply being near her person and receiving gentle pets was the best place to be. She may be a little shy at first, but with patience and love, Sheba is ready to be someone's loyal companion again.

My foster writes: Sheba is a wonderful dog. She is the best dog I fostered. She is housebroken, which is important to me because I am a neat freak. Despite being in a shelter for a while 😔 she did not lose her ability to connect people. She made eye contact with me often and licked my feet, legs and hands as if she felt grateful to me for taking her out of the stressful shelter environment, which was very touching. She takes treats very gently and has a calm energy and will just be happy being close to you and laying around in her bed resting or napping or playing with her toys- she will not bother you at all. She did not even want to get on my bed until I picked her up and placed her there. She was calm - I would say medium to low energy for the time she was in my apartment. When I ordered food, she did not bark at all at the delivery man. In fact I never heard her barking at anything or anyone. Not aggressive at all. Low to none prey drive. I think it's very rare to find a dog like Sheba. She checks all the boxes. She knows certain commands. It shows that she had an owner in the past who unfortunately abandoned her. But what happened to Sheba did not break her and she is still an affectionate, loving and appreciative dog who longs to connect to her person. Anyone would be lucky to have her. I would adopt her if I didn't already have a dog that I adopted several years back. Please consider giving Sheba a great and loving home she deserves and is waiting for. She is an amazing dog and will make a great companion.

Pre-Screener Form

Oreo displayed fearful behavior in the Care Centers and was reported to escalate to thrashing, lunging, and snapping at the leash. Once outside, he tolerated some handling but continued to appear uncomfortable. In his previous home, Oreo was described as friendly with strangers, children, and familiar dogs. Due to his behavior in the shelter environment, Oreo should be placed through a New Hope Partner into an adult-only home with caregivers who are experienced in managing fearful behaviors and can utilize positive reinforcement-based training and handling techniques.

256189.name: Peter Rabbit
256189.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
Not only do I pull at heart strings, but I also pull on leash! I will need someone to help me with my leash manners.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

A volunteer writes: Calling all gremlin lovers! We've got an especially adorable one at the shelter right now, and his name is Peter Rabbit. It's a mystery how he hasn't been scooped up yet, but I think it's due to him being housed in an overflow room (a result of overcrowding) with very limited exposure to adopters. So let's change that!

With his low-rider build, big chunky head, and mini white-painted toes, PR is ridiculously cute. But it's his little gremlin-y personality that really captures my heart. He's super-friendly and affectionate, happily wiggling into my legs, arms, lap - whatever part of me happens to be closest - and making the sweetest little grunting sounds when I pet him.  

And you know what else he loves? Balls! Tennis, foam, rubber...the little gremlin doesn't care as long as they bounce, roll, and can be carried around. He gleefully hops after each one I toss and after collecting them all, he stretches out froggy-leg style, utterly enthralled with his little cache. And if one of the balls starts to roll away, he quickly swats it back into the fold. He also loves soft toys, carrying them on his walks and gleefully shaking them around. (Speaking of walks, he seems to be housebroken).

Peter Rabbit won't have any trouble getting people to fall in love with him - they just need the chance to meet him!

I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
Merida has improved nicely since her first assessment and was lying in the cubby, appearing calm. She sniffed treats and began eating them, and while slightly hesitant, allowed petting on her head, cheek, and back. Her back was a little more sensitive, but she tolerated all the petting and was then coaxed onto the main shelf with the promise of more treats. She was partially picked up and gave a little hiss, but she didn't struggle and was reasonably calm after she was set back down and resumed eating. If pushed a little too hard, she will hiss a bit and get upset, but she is not aggressive and is very sweet.


Merida tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

256223.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Pluto is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Pluto's previous owner states that he will resource guard, noted to snap or attempt to bite if his food is touched. During one instance when a person reached out to grab his bowl. Pluto charged and bit them on the arm. This bite did break skin. Initially in care, Pluto was observed to be fearful and would balk or pancake while on leash. Recently, Pluto has been observed to have a soft body, soliciting attention, and is playful with handlers. Medically, Pluto is on treatment for CIRDC. 

Meet Pluto!  Pluto came to ACC via owner surrender.  Pluto is described as a friendly, social dog who enjoys meeting new people and is known to be outgoing with both strangers and familiar visitors. He has lived with a child and is described as playful and affectionate. Pluto also gets along well with other dogs and has been reported to be friendly and playful with both familiar and unfamiliar dogs.

Pluto is house-trained and has a medium energy level. He generally handles routine interactions well, including restraint, collar handling, and paw touching. However, he can become fearful when startled and does best with a predictable environment.

Pluto's future family should be prepared to manage some behavioral challenges. He has a history of resource guarding his food and may snap or attempt to bite if someone tries to take his food bowl while he is eating.

Pluto can be a strong puller on leash and experiences anxiety, which may lead to destructive behaviors when stressed. He will benefit from a patient family who can provide structure, enrichment, and continued training.

With the right home, Pluto has the potential to be a loving, loyal companion who enjoys being part of the family.

256228.name: Kopita
256228.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
Kopita is laying in the back of her cubby, head up and appearing relaxed as she observes the room. When the kennel door is opened and she is spoken to and called over, it takes her a minute or two to exit the cubby, exiting with a big stretch before greeting the assessor at the front of the kennel with a head bunt. Kopita allows and leans into all petting beginning to tail flick shortly after but not escalating with extended petting. She is able to be easily picked up, remains calm when she is held, and continues to be receptive to further petting and attention when she is placed back into her kennel. 

Kopita interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that Kopita go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods and decompression.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bullwinkle is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Bullwinkle has demonstrated a high level of arousal that manifests as intense leash biting during his previous and current stay in care, which has made walking/handling him safely difficult. During his previous stay, Bullwinkle escalated during handling, including leash biting, head whipping, fixating on staff, jumping, lunging toward staff's legs and torso, and thrashing on the leash. Medically, Bullwinkle is being treated for CIRDC.

Bullwinkle arrived at the care centers as a stray. In the care center, Bullwinkle has displayed a low threshold for arousal, escalating to leash biting and then to lunging/growling at staff. As a result, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through one of our New Hope Partners who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

During his previous stay, Bullwinkle escalated during handling, including leash biting, head whipping, fixating on staff, jumping, lunging toward staff's legs and torso, and thrashing on the leash. Medically, Bullwinkle is being treated for CIRDC. Bullwinkle arrived at the care centers as a stray. In the care center, Bullwinkle has displayed a low threshold for arousal, escalating to leash biting and then to lunging/growling at staff. As a result, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through one of our New Hope Partners who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

256296.name: Snickers
256296.summary:
Meet Snickers!
Snickers arrived at Queens ACC as a stray in rough condition, but he's been steadily healing and showing more of his gentle personality each day. Despite limited history, staff have already seen a sweet, soft-natured boy who is tolerant, calm, and beginning to open up as he recovers.

My Ideal Home
Snickers would do best in a patient, low-pressure home that can give him time to fully recover and settle in. He benefits from gentle routines, calm environments, and positive reinforcement as he continues building confidence. As he heals, he will likely thrive with quiet structure and steady encouragement.

Good with Other Pets?
Snickers' history with other animals is unknown, so slow introductions are recommended if there are resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful presentation and need for a calm environment, ACC recommends a home without young children under 5.

Things to Know
Snickers is a gentle, observant dog who can be a bit reserved at first, sometimes choosing to move away from interaction until he feels comfortable. Once leashed, he walks calmly at a steady pace and may pause or resist briefly but responds well to treats and reassurance. He tolerates handling and has shown soft, friendly body language such as tail wagging and relaxed behavior during care. As he continues to heal medically, his full personality is still emerging, but he already shows strong potential to become a loving companion with time and patience.

Fun Fact
Even while recovering, Snickers has been spotted quietly wagging his tail and gently leaning into attention-he's a soft-hearted boy who's just getting started on his second chance.

This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

256298.name: Chillin
256298.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Chillin is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.
Meet Chillin!

Chillin came to ACC from a hoarding situation and is still learning that people can be friends. She is a very shy and independent girl who has become more curious and comfortable around other cats, but she remains cautious and unsure around people. Chillin will need a patient adopter who is willing to let her build trust at her own pace.


My Ideal Home

Chillin would do best in a quiet, adult-only home with an experienced adopter who understands shy cats. She will need consistent, gentle socialization, plenty of hiding spaces, and lots of time to adjust. High-value treats and positive interactions can help her build confidence, but she should never be rushed or forced into contact.

Good with Kids?

No. Due to her fearful nature and discomfort with handling, Chillin would do best in an adult-only home.

Good with Other Pets?

Yes! Chillin came from a home with many other cats and has been spending time successfully in a free-roam room with feline roommates. She has become more comfortable spending time around other cats and may enjoy having a calm feline companion.

Overall Health

Chillin is a healthy adult cat with no major medical concerns noted.

Behavior Determination

Experienced, adult-only home. Chillin is very fearful of people and may attempt to flee or avoid contact. She will need an adopter who is comfortable with slow, consistent socialization and understands that her progress may take time.

Other Fun Facts

Chillin is quiet, curious, and independent. She has made encouraging progress while living with other cats, spending more time down on the floor and engaging with her feline roommates instead of staying exclusively up high. She may not become a lap cat, but with patience, she has the opportunity to continue gaining confidence and discovering the joys of having a safe home.
>

256302.name: Romi
256302.summary:
Another foster writes:
Romi is a sweet, friendly, and very cute little lady looking for her forever home. She warms up quickly and shows lots of affection through hopping into your lap, rubbing against you, and purring. She enjoys playing, napping, and eating.
Romi is an easygoing cat to care for. She uses her little box without any issues and will use a scratching post. Romi tolerates being picked up and held. She will let you cut her nails with the distraction of a Churu!
Romi can jump onto your shoulder and stand there! She's missing some of her front teeth, so her tongue sticks out sometimes. She has a patch on her head that looks almost like a little haircut or heart. Romi loves pets and will fall asleep on your lap.

My foster writes: Romi is a adorably sweet lap cat. Once comfortable, Romi wants nothing more than to cuddle up to her humans, gaze at them adoringly, and occasionally stand on their shoulders. When overexcited, she may mouth at hands, but is easily corrected or redirected. While she finds some new people or experiences to be initially frightening, all she needs is some time in her hiding spots to chill out. Romi has lived with another cat, and may do well in a multi-cat household with proper introductions. She tolerates handling and enjoys being petted. Romi is a vocal cat, with the cutest little meow. She may do well with gentle older children and a home where she has a dedicated safety den.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Romi tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home

256303.name: Michelle
256303.summary:
My foster writes:
Michelle is a very sweet and affectionate kitty! She loves to cuddle and nap together, and if you sit on the bed and call her name she will jump up to join you.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Michelle tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.
**Behavior Summary - Michelle**

Michelle is a sweet, sensitive cat who appears significantly stressed by the shelter environment but has shown steady signs of progress over time. While she may initially respond to unfamiliar people with hissing, retreating, or defensive body language, she has consistently demonstrated that she is capable of forming positive associations when interactions are patient, predictable, and respectful of her boundaries.

Michelle enjoys gentle attention, soft conversation, squeeze-up treats, and enrichment activities such as watching bubbles. Although timid, she has become increasingly comfortable spending time outside of her hiding space to observe her surroundings and people-watch. She has shown interest in social interaction through slow blinking, accepting head and cheek pets, and readily approaching for high-value treats. Importantly, while Michelle may communicate her discomfort through hissing, she generally does not escalate beyond these warnings and has shown the ability to relax when given time and space.

Michelle will likely thrive in a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who can allow her to adjust at her own pace. With continued positive reinforcement, patience, and understanding, she has strong potential to gain confidence and develop into a loving companion.

256308.name: Angel
256308.summary:
Meet Angel!
Angel is a quiet, independent cat who is looking for a patient adopter willing to let him settle in at his own pace. He previously lived in a home with adults and older children, where he preferred gentle interactions on his own terms. While the shelter has been overwhelming for him, Angel has shown wonderful progress as he becomes more comfortable, revealing the sweet cat that's underneath his initial shyness.

My Ideal Home
Angel would thrive in a calm, quiet home with experienced cat guardians who understand that trust takes time. He appreciates slow introductions, predictable routines, and having safe spaces where he can retreat when he needs a break. Giving him the freedom to choose when to interact will help him continue building confidence and settling into his new life.

Good with Kids?
No young children under 13 years old. Angel has lived successfully with older children but prefers gentle interactions on his own terms and would do best in a quieter household.

Good with Other Pets?
Angel has no known history of living with other cats or dogs. If introduced to resident pets, slow and gradual introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health
Healthy overall. Angel recently recovered from an upper respiratory infection and is feeling much better.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Experienced Adopters. Angel has displayed fear and stress in the shelter environment, particularly when the surroundings are busy or unfamiliar. As he has become more comfortable, he has made remarkable progress, allowing gentle petting and choosing to engage with staff in quieter settings. He will do best with adopters who can respect his boundaries, recognize his body language, and allow him to build trust at his own pace.

Other Fun Facts
Angel may be reserved at first, but he's a big fan of tasty treats-especially tuna and squeeze-up treats! Once he feels safe, he enjoys gentle head and shoulder pets, slow-blinking conversations, and even catnip toys. Watching Angel's confidence grow has been one of the highlights for our behavior team, and we know the right home will help him continue to blossom.

A volunteer writes: Collecting his information the best way he knows how, Angel tucks himself into a soft little loaf and tries to piece it all together. I commend him for his efforts and recognize their value, even if, maybe especially if, they fall on the quieter side of the spectrum. In Angel's life before the shelter, he took his time warming up to new people but would lay gently once he did. He looks like a big teddy bear, but please don't let those fluffy cheeks fool you as getting used to shelter life hasn't been easy with all the new sights and sounds. Angel is FIV+ and has some medical needs that will require follow up, but he hopes someone will notice him and share a little chance his way.

Angel is a quiet, independent cat who is looking for a patient adopter willing to let him settle in at his own pace. He previously lived in a home with adults and older children, where he preferred gentle interactions on his own terms. While the shelter has been overwhelming for him, Angel has shown wonderful progress as he becomes more comfortable, revealing the sweet cat that's underneath his initial shyness.

My Ideal Home
Angel would thrive in a calm, quiet home with experienced cat guardians who understand that trust takes time. He appreciates slow introductions, predictable routines, and having safe spaces where he can retreat when he needs a break. Giving him the freedom to choose when to interact will help him continue building confidence and settling into his new life.

Good with Kids?
No young children under 13 years old. Angel has lived successfully with older children but prefers gentle interactions on his own terms and would do best in a quieter household.

Good with Other Pets?
Angel has no known history of living with other cats or dogs. If introduced to resident pets, slow and gradual introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health
Healthy overall. Angel recently recovered from an upper respiratory infection and is feeling much better.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Experienced Adopters. Angel has displayed fear and stress in the shelter environment, particularly when the surroundings are busy or unfamiliar. As he has become more comfortable, he has made remarkable progress, allowing gentle petting and choosing to engage with staff in quieter settings. He will do best with adopters who can respect his boundaries, recognize his body language, and allow him to build trust at his own pace.

Other Fun Facts
Angel may be reserved at first, but he's a big fan of tasty treats-especially tuna and squeeze-up treats! Once he feels safe, he enjoys gentle head and shoulder pets, slow-blinking conversations, and even catnip toys. Watching Angel's confidence grow has been one of the highlights for our behavior team, and we know the right home will help him continue to blossom.

A volunteer writes: Collecting his information the best way he knows how, Angel tucks himself into a soft little loaf and tries to piece it all together. I commend him for his efforts and recognize their value, even if, maybe especially if, they fall on the quieter side of the spectrum. In Angel's life before the shelter, he took his time warming up to new people but would lay gently once he did. He looks like a big teddy bear, but please don't let those fluffy cheeks fool you as getting used to shelter life hasn't been easy with all the new sights and sounds. Angel is FIV+ and has some medical needs that will require follow up, but he hopes someone will notice him and share a little chance his way.

256309.name: French Onion Dip
256309.summary: A volunteer writes: French Onion Dip can be a bit guarded when you first meet him, but if you give him some time, you'll see his true personality shine through. When I sat with him during playtime, he was skeptical at first. After a while, though, he started opening up little by little until he eventually stretched out next to me for some head pats. In addition to being a total sweetheart, French Onion Dip is also a superstar athlete who does the most impressive binkies! He's looking for a home with plenty of space to hop around and a patient human, willing to work to earn his trust.

256330.name: Meechy
256330.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Meechy needs at risk placement for medical reasons. She is a sweet, senior cat with an upper respiratory tract infection and severe dental disease. She is not eating and needs supportive care in a veterinary clinic to clear her infection. Once cleared, she also needs dental extractions to resolve the inflammation in her mouth.

A volunteer writes:
Meechy, a senior gal was left behind when her owners moved away. She might have lived with another kitty but its whereabouts are unknown. A concerned citizen took care of Meechy(qualified as a very friendly cat) until she was picked up by our field officers. Meechy was a bit reserved when I first met her but treats and tuna brought down her guards(same with the veterinary team). Catnip toys and feather wands had an even greater effect on Meechy, sending her playing like there was no tomorrow. No overstimulation, though, just plain good fun(see her video). Meechy is now quite happy to see a visitor. She makes friends quite easily, charming guests with head bunts and purrs. She is a very sweet and cute cat, very girly and petite. Meechy did very well on her behavior evaluation, is apparently healthy but missing most of her teeth(she should be fed soft food)and on the underweight side. It is without say that Meechy needs a home sweet home where she will feel safe, loved and will be well cared for. If you want to help a senior live happily during her golden years, Meechy is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.

256335.name: Chicken Fries
256335.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Chicken Fries is standing at the back of her shelf, observing the assessor with a slightly tense body as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, she is initially hesitant to come forward, but after a few moments of soft talk she leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand before softly head bunting it. Chicken Fries leans into all petting and quietly purrs when she is pet. She is able to be picked up but stress meows and tenses when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she briefly retreats to the back of the kennel. She is able to be coaxed forward with more soft talk and returns to the front of the kennel, continuing to allow and lean into further petting. 

Chicken Fries tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

256356.name: Rocket
256356.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Rocket is at risk due to his behavioral concerns. Rocket was surrendered following a bite incident. While resident child and their friend were playing in the yard Rocket jumped up on the friend twice. The second time Rocket jumped up he bit the friends left arm, which broke skin. Since intake, Rocket has remained shut down, hiding behind or attempting to crawl under his Kuranda bed, refusing to move. Rocket's previous owner reported that he is very affectionate, very active. playful, and never had any other incidents before this. Medically, Rocket is apparently healthy.

Rocket was brought to the care center as an owner surrender due to a bite incident that happened outside the home. In the prior home he is noted by his owners to be social, affectionate, Very active and Playful. Since arriving at the care center, Rocket has displayed significant fear and stress. He has been observed hiding behind and attempting to crawl under his Kuranda bed, refusing to move when approached, and remaining at the back of his kennel with a tense body and whale eyes. During interactions, he has been unable to engage with handlers and has demonstrated a high level of fear. Rocket would benefit from a New Hope placement that can provide a quiet, low-stress environment, allow for decompression, and support him through gradual confidence-building and positive reinforcement. Given his bite history and current fearful presentation, placement with an experienced adopter or foster through one of our rescue partners capable of managing fearful behavior is recommended.

His purr isn't loud but you feel him purring constantly when you pet him! He's a little messy with his litter and would do well with a covered box and isn't a fan of wet food. Plus, he has the cutest overbite and looks like a little vampire!

I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

He ignored squeeze-up treats but was reasonably calm when picked up and held in the assessor's arms and when set back down. He gently moved to the back of the cubby, looked at the assessor, and licked his lips a few times.

256360.name: Slinky Dog
256360.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Slinky Dog(obviously not his real name)behaved like a little sea urchin when he arrived at the care center. He was terrified by what just happened to him:loosing  his owner, his home and his many housemates. Time and enrichment given by staff and volunteers did their job and just look at Slinky's video.. He is feeling so much better, happy to be with his visitor and purring very loudly. He is truly a very dear little guy, only six month old and who dreams to be cared for and loved again. For now, Slinky Dog needs a low traffic home and an understanding new owner who will let him come out of his shell at his own pace and be the lovely, playful and happy little guy he really is. Come to the Manhattan Care Center and ask to meet Slinky Dog!





What my friends at ACC say about me:

Slinky Dog tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

256362.name: Calabunga
256362.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Calabunga is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Calabunga's previous owner states that he will become tense, growl, hard bark, hover, snap, or attempt to bite when in the possession of toys, food, or treats. During intake, Calabunga lunged and bit the trail adopter's partner on the arm when they touched him while he had a toy in his mouth. This bite left a small puncture wound. The previous adopter also reports that he will bark, growl, lunge, snap, and attempt to bite animals and people that he sees while on walks. While in care, Calabunga has been receptive to treats and accepts contact. Medically, Calabunga is underweight.

Calabunga originally came to ACC via NYPD.  Calabunga was in a trial-adopters home, but had an incident with a resident cat and was returned.  Calabunga's original owner describe Calabunga as a social and affectionate dog! He is very active and playful but does prefer contact on his own terms. He can usually be found where the people are. He is used to going on 3 or 4 walks per day for about 30 minutes and pulls hard on the leash. Calabunga has experience in a crate but does not do well. He is also nervous on car rides. Calabunga knows lots of tricks: sit, shake, down, crawl, spin, leave it.

256366.name: Wyona
256366.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Wyona!
Wyona is a sweet, gentle girl who is still getting her bearings here at ACC. She can be a little unsure at first, but with some patience and encouragement, she'll happily come along with you. She's especially sensitive about her back right now, so she's looking for someone who will give her the time and TLC she deserves.

My Ideal Home
Wyona would love a calm home where she can take things at her own pace. She's looking for a patient person who will help her feel safe, spoil her with plenty of enrichment, and show her that good things are ahead.

Good with Other Pets?
Wyona's history with other animals is a mystery. She's met a few dogs at ACC and has been a little unsure, so slow introductions will be important. For now, dog parks aren't her scene, but she may enjoy making some carefully chosen canine friends in the future.

Good with Kids?
Wyona would do best in an adult-only home where she can relax and have her personal space respected while she gets comfortable.

Things to Know
Wyona has some skin irritation that makes her back uncomfortable, and staff will be happy to talk with you about her medical needs when you meet her. She's been through a lot of change, and what she really needs now is someone willing to be patient, gentle, and in her corner. With a little love, Wyona could be one very happy girl!

256369.name: Ares
256369.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Ares tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

Meet Ares!
Ares is looking for a patient adopter who understands that trust takes time. He can be shy and independent when meeting new people, preferring to observe from a distance before deciding to interact. Once he feels comfortable, he's a curious young cat who enjoys exploring, playing, and spending time on his own terms.

My Ideal Home
Ares would do best in a quiet, adult-only home with experienced cat guardians who can respect his boundaries and let him adjust at his own pace. He enjoys interactive play and will benefit from regular play sessions with wand toys, puzzle feeders, and plenty of enrichment to help channel his energy appropriately. His adopter should be prepared to continue working with him on appropriate play and monitor his litter box habits as he settles into his new home.

Good with Kids?
No. Ares should live in an adult-only home due to his history of rough play and previous bite incidents.

Good with Other Pets?
Ares has no known history of living with cats or dogs. If he is introduced to other pets, slow and careful introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health
Reported urinary marking outside the litter box in his previous home. Neutering and a stable indoor environment may help improve this behavior. Our staff can discuss recommendations for a successful transition.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Experienced Adopters. Ares has a history of rough play and previous bite incidents and has displayed fearful behavior in the shelter. He will do best with experienced adopters who understand feline body language, respect his boundaries, and can provide him with the time, patience, and enrichment he needs to succeed.

Other Fun Facts
Ares is an insect hunter at heart! He loves chasing bugs, pouncing on crinkly toys and random objects, relaxing on windowsills, and enjoying tasty Churu treats. While he's more of an independent companion than a constant cuddle bug, he'll reward patient adopters with his quiet curiosity and unique personality.

256370.name: Gotham
256370.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Young Gotham came to us with housemate Arkham as their home counted way too many kitties. More of their friends are expected....Nothing much is known about his past like it is often the case with these cats. Gotham is very shy and wary within our walls. It is no surprise. He has the potential to bloom in understanding and loving hands. Why do I say that? Although lumped at the back of his cubby, Gotham for a long while accepted my petting, even leaned a little against my hand and blinked with my soft words. Then his posture indicated that he needed a break(see video). later on, when I came back for him, he was stress meowing at his door and came in and out his "living room" for pets. He was quite unsure of himself but he was trying, something that deeply affected "hoarding" cats do not do usually. I am hopeful that Gotham will come out of his shell and that a caring and experienced adopter will see my plea for him and give him a chance at a new page in his life. Gotham is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

256382.name: Layla
256382.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Layla is a ten year old dame who is with us as her family sadly was displaced. She is said to be a "nice, friendly and chill pet" who might need time to warm up but enjoys spending time with her people(comprising children). Layla is pretty shy at the care center but the hustle and bustle of a very busy and noisy city shelter is not geared to foster a gregarious behavior. Layla stays in her little corner but she appreciates kindness and petting and absolutely loves treats and gourmet food. She is I must say quite on the thin side and although she has a coat in tip top condition, Layla could use to gain a little bit of weight. Layla is apparently healthy, has a normal senior blood panel, owns quite good teeth for her age and did well on her behavior evaluation only pointing to her shyness. Sweet Layla so deserves to be once again at home, safe, well cared for and cherished for her golden years. Come and meet her very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!




Layla is a sweet but very shy cat who was curled up at the back of the kennel with a tucked tail, large pupils, and sideways ears. She scrunched backward when approached but allowed petting on her cheeks, head, and along her back. She tolerated being picked up, and when set back down, she gave a tiny little hiss and remained in place.

Layla tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

256407.name: Arlo
256407.summary:
Meet Arlo!
Arlo is a friendly, affectionate dog who came to us after living in a home with her family. She loves being around people, enjoys attention, and is happiest when she's included in the action. Whether she's exploring on a walk or leaning in for pets, Arlo is eager to spend time with her favorite humans and is ready to find a family who will help her settle into her next chapter.

My Ideal Home
Arlo would thrive in an adult-only home where she can receive regular exercise, enrichment, and continued positive reinforcement training. She is an active, intelligent dog who will benefit from structure and consistency, particularly when working on impulse control and leash manners. Because she can become anxious when left alone, a family prepared to help her build confidence and provide plenty of mental stimulation will help her succeed.

Good with Kids?
Although Arlo previously lived with children, we are recommending an adult-only home due to her history of resource guarding and sensitivity to certain handling.

Good with Other Pets?
Arlo has lived successfully with familiar dogs in the past but has shown discomfort and reactivity toward unfamiliar dogs in the shelter. She should be the only pet in her new home and is not recommended for homes with cats or other small animals. Dog parks are also not recommended.

Overall Health
Healthy overall.

Behavior Determination
Level 4 - Experienced Adopters. Arlo has a history of resource guarding, anxiety, handling sensitivity, and reactivity toward unfamiliar dogs. She will do best with adopters who can continue using positive reinforcement training, respect her boundaries, and provide appropriate management while she adjusts to her new home. With structure and patience, Arlo has the potential to be a wonderful companion.

Other Fun Facts
Arlo loves car rides, enjoys learning (especially when treats are involved!), and is a social, affectionate companion who likes to stay close to her people. Volunteers describe her as easy to handle outside of her kennel, and she enjoys sniffy walks, leaning in for affection, and bouncing happily alongside her favorite humans.

256408.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Mumsy is a sometimes vocal, very food-motivated, and very sweet cat who was on top of the den and was chatting earlier, but was quiet after the kennel door was opened. She immediately came down to sniff treats with a high tail and an arched rear when pet along her back. She leaned in for cheek rubs and pushed her head gently against the assessor's hand. She loves squeeze-up treats and was calm when picked up and held and remained so when set back down and resumed eating.

Mumsy interacts with the assessor,  solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.   This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
A volunteer writes: If Mumsy could text, here's what she'd tap with a heart emoji: squeeze-up treats, chitchats, attention from people, petting sessions, and being picked up and held. This sweet, slender girl came to us without a history. But she's so friendly and mellow, she clearly had a previous home where she was socialized well with humans. When I met her the other day in the cat adoption room, she impressed me with her calm vibe and warm eyes, and I actually felt like she was really listening to me when I told her we're doing everything we can to find the perfect forever home for her. Maybe yours?

256414.name: Princess Carolyn
256414.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Princess Carolyn is standing upright at the back of her cubby, eyes wide and slightly tense as the assessor approaches. When the cubby door is opened, she appears to take a moment to process the situation before meowing softly, rubbing her cheeks/head bunting the side wall before approaching the front of the cubby to greet the assessor. She leans forward to sniff their hand before pulling away. With some soft talk she leans forward and softly head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting. She is easily coaxed to the main area of the kennel, continuing to meow softly at the assessor. She allows all petting, leaning in and raising her back as she is pet, tail held high. Princess Carolyn is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm for several seconds before lightly squirming and stress meowing to be placed back down. When she is placed back into her kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting. When a squeeze up is offered before the interaction is ended, Princess Carolyn quickly begins eating it. 

Princess Carolyn interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

She leans forward to sniff their hand before pulling away. With some soft talk she leans forward and softly head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting. She is easily coaxed to the main area of the kennel, continuing to meow softly at the assessor. She allows all petting, leaning in and raising her back as she is pet, tail held high. Princess Carolyn is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm for several seconds before lightly squirming and stress meowing to be placed back down. When she is placed back into her kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting. When a squeeze up is offered before the interaction is ended, Princess Carolyn quickly begins eating it.

Princess Carolyn interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

256415.name: Esther
256415.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Finally!!! Esther came out of her shell! Esther came to us with two housemates(already adopted) as their owner moved out of state. Esther was very shy to start with(although never aggressive) and hid behind her litter box at the very back of her cubby. She accepted petting but stayed put... Something changed and Esther came forward, not for treats but to interact with me. She rolled gently on her side, head bunted my hand, purred and even got up to eat tuna and even later on, rest in her kennel main area. No more cubby! I was so happy that Esther finally decided to show the world that she is a lovely pet! She is known to be a sweet, affectionate, quiet and shy cat who needs time to show her sweet nature, which we are seeing during her stay at the care center. Esther is apparently healthy, did well on her behavior evaluation, is litter box trained and will be able to go home after her spay. A lovely gal she is ready to be your forever best friend for years to come.






What my friends at ACC say about me:
Esther has made wonderful improvements since her first assessment and is now out in the main part of the kennel. She is sweet and friendly and came forward, enjoying petting on her head, cheek, and along her back, with a raised tail and a slightly arched back when pet there. She leaned in for cheek rubs, ate treats and squeeze-up, and was calm when she was picked up and held and remained calm and relaxed when set back down.

Esther interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

256422.name: Mr. Thomas Mittens
256422.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Mr Thomas Mittens came to the Manhattan Care Center with a bunch of other cats  as their home counted too many pets. Although apparently healthy, Mr Thomas Mittens was found to have blood and crystals in his urine for which he is on a special diet to prevent any urinary blockage, a not so uncommon medical condition in male cats. He is feeling quite well now and is a real great cat to spent time with. He loves to eat(even his special diet) and to play with lots of good energy(see his video-his family says that he could play rough or gently) and he does not mind at all to come on the lap without complaining too much when he is put back in his kennel...Petting is up his alley too and he bakes tons of biscuits! Young Mr Thomas Mittens is a very pleasant kitty who likely would do better with experienced cat parents who enjoy an active cat and are willing to keep him on his special diet and with appropriate veterinary follow up. Mr Thomas Mittens is waiting for his new family at the Manhattan Care Center!








What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I am playful and cute!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

256448.name: Potato
256448.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Potato is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Potato is social with staff and enjoys engaging in play when brought out for Playgroup. Recently, however, she appears to be struggling with the stress of the shelter environment. Staff have observed an increase in mouthy behavior, including nipping at hands and ankles. Medically, Potato is apparently healthy.

Potato arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. Initially while in care, Potato was observed to seek contact from handlers and lean into them with a soft body and wagging tail. Recently Potato has begun biting the handler's ankle, pant leg, and shoelaces. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.  

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

My Boroughbreaker writes: She is extremely friendly, to all people and calm / curious about other dogs (even those that were reactive towards her, she took no notice). She can be jumpy / mouthy when excited, as a classic puppy! But responded well to strong commands and will "sit" for treats on demand.
She is high energy and was quite prone to chewing things 😊 so would also benefit from lots of mental stimulation / chew toys to keep her engaged. I think she'd be well suited to most adoptees, provided they are ready to do some training.

256452.name: Lion
256452.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Lion is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Lion has been reluctant to go for walks or leave the building. He has been seen pancaking in the middle of hallways, refusing to leave the building for a walk. On another occasion, he pancaked in the hallway immediately after leaving his room. Lion has been easy to remove from the kennel and will take high-value treats with a soft mouth when trying to coax him to walk, before he pancakes again. Medically, Lion is overweight.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

A volunteer writes: Lion 🦁 with a name like Lion, you might think you were meeting a very brave boy. But our Lion is more reminiscent of the Lion from the Wizard of Oz - still searching for his bravery. When I read the circumstances he was found in, I'm not surprised. Lion was found with his collar covered in duct tape, attached to retractable leash that was tied around a tree. He was there all night, and still there when police arrived the following morning at 9am. I can't imagine how scary that would be - how terrifying to be outside with no way to move in the middle of the night, waiting for someone to rescue you. In spite of that he was friendly with responding officers, who pet him through the window of their car during intake.

While clearly stressed when we met, he lay at our feet to relax as best he could. He never quite fully relaxed, but I imagine this boy will find comfort being in a good and patient home that will let him decompress from all he's been through.

Lion is now looking for that home, and for now based on his fear he needs an adult home or one with older kids.

Pre-Screener Form

Boo-Boo is on the at risk list for medical reasons. Boo-boo is an emaciated kitten with a URI and conjunctivitis that is not gaining weight appropriately in shelter. He needs more care and attention than can be provided in shelter, including frequent feedings to encourage and ensure he is eating well, cleaning, medication administration, etc. Behaviorally, he is very sweet and amenable to all handling.

While with us, Boo-Boo has been very sweet and allowed all handling from staff for feedings and cleaning.  Boo-Boo needs placement with a rescue partner where they can receive additional care and attention.

256466.name: Manuka Honey
256466.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Manuka Honey is laying curled up in the back of her top cubby, observing the room with her head up and eyes wide. When the cubby door is opened and she is spoken to softly, she hesitates for a few moments before rolling around on her side. Manuka Honey allows and leans into petting on the head and cheeks. When noises and activity occur around the room, she pauses, lip licks, and stares towards the source of the sound. She recovers quickly with more soft talk, rolling onto her side and making biscuits. She leans into all petting, tensing momentarily when pet down her shoulders and back before appearing to settle and leaning into it. Crunchy treats are offered and she leans forward to sniff them before beginning to eat. She is able to be slowly pulled forward from the back of the cubby and allows pickup, tensing slightly when she is held but tolerating it. When she is placed back into the cubby, she returns to her position laying curled up at the back of it, continuing to allow further petting on the head and cheeks.

Manuka Honey interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

Crunchy treats are offered and she leans forward to sniff them before beginning to eat. She is able to be slowly pulled forward from the back of the cubby and allows pickup, tensing slightly when she is held but tolerating it. When she is placed back into the cubby, she returns to her position laying curled up at the back of it, continuing to allow further petting on the head and cheeks.

Manuka Honey interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

256498.name: Bluey
256498.summary:
Meet Bluey!
Bluey arrived at the shelter as a stray, so while we don't know much about his past, we do know one thing for sure: this sweet boy loves making connections with people! Bluey is a social, affectionate pup who happily leans into pets and is always ready to spend time with his favorite humans. Now he's looking for a family who can help him continue learning and growing.

My Ideal Home
Bluey would thrive with an adopter who enjoys an active, playful companion and is excited to continue working on his manners. He is a smart and eager-to-learn pup who will benefit from positive reinforcement training, daily exercise, and enrichment activities that help him channel his enthusiasm in fun ways. With a little guidance, Bluey is ready to become your best adventure buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
Bluey's history with other animals is unknown, but he has shown interest in meeting other dogs while at the shelter. He has had some appropriate greetings with other dogs, though he can become tense when seeing dogs while on leash. Slow introductions and continued positive reinforcement training will help him feel comfortable and successful around canine friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Bluey's energetic play style and leash-related behaviors, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. He would do best with people who can help him practice polite greetings and build confidence through training.

Things to Know
Bluey is a happy, people-loving pup who can get a little excited when greeting his favorite humans. He may jump up when seeking attention and has been known to grab the leash when overstimulated, so continued practice with calm walking and impulse control will help him succeed. Bluey loves affection, enjoys learning, and is ready to find someone who will give him the structure, patience, and love he needs to shine.

256510.name: Five
256510.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Five is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Five's previous owner reported that he will jump, snap, or bite small animals while on leash. While in care, Five has been observed to be highly kennel reactive. Noted to pull hard towards the other dogs in the kennel room. When the handler pulls him away, Five is noted to jump up on them with an open mouth and, in one instance, snap at them. Five's previous owner describes him as loving and playful. They also state that he may know the cues sit, stay, and down. Medically, Five is apparently healthy.

Meet Fives!  According to his previous owner, Five loves to run and would make a great match for an active adopter who enjoys spending time outdoors.

At home, Five can usually be found relaxing in the living room, enjoying time with his people. He tolerates bathing and brushing well, making grooming a breeze. Five already knows several basic commands, including sit, stay, and lay down.

Five is accustomed to a daily walk of about an hour and a half and enjoys getting plenty of exercise. On leash, he can pull moderately to strongly, so he may benefit from continued training and guidance during walks. He has experience spending time in a crate, though he may whine at first. Car rides can make him a bit nervous, so patience and positive reinforcement will help him build confidence.

In shelter, Five has shown some fearful and reactive behavior.  Due to this, we recommend an adult only home with an experienced adopter.

256566.name: Grogu
256566.summary:
Meet Grogu!
Grogu was found tied to a bench and is now safe in our care, bringing a lot of personality packed into a small, bouncy package. Much like his namesake, he's got a playful, curious spirit and tends to win people over quickly once he's out and about.

My Ideal Home
Grogu would do best with an adopter who can match his enthusiasm with structure and positive reinforcement training. He'll thrive in a home that can provide daily mental and physical enrichment, along with consistent guidance to help him build better impulse control. He's a great candidate for fun training games, food puzzles, and interactive play.

Good with Other Pets?
Grogu has shown loose, social behavior around another dog in care, but his full history with other animals is unknown. Slow, supervised introductions would be best if living with another pet.

Good with Kids?
Due to his high energy and tendency to jump up socially, Grogu would do best in a home without very young children at this time.

Things to Know
Grogu is a social, people oriented boy who enjoys attention and engagement. He can be a bit jumpy when excited and benefits from gentle redirection and consistent training to build calmer greetings. He's easily motivated by interaction and will shine in a home that channels his enthusiasm into structured play and learning. With the right support, he has all the makings of a fun, affectionate companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Grogu is a little bundle of joy with a big personality. He greets the world with curiosity and bounce, often coming right up to say hello and then happily engaging in play or attention. He can be a bit jumpy when excited, but it's all social enthusiasm and easily redirected with treats or toys. He's the kind of dog who makes you smile without even trying, especially when he's proudly working the room like he owns the place.

Fun Fact
Grogu's superpower is making instant friends, no Jedi training required.

A volunteer writes:
Grogu's superpower is making instant friends - no Jedi training required. Though he's only been at the shelter for a little over a month, he's quickly become a volunteer favorite. As one says, "He's the kind of dog who makes you smile without even trying, especially when he's proudly working the room like he owns the place." He's a connoisseur of treats (he's got to try everything on offer, because he's intent on expanding his palate) and toys alike. When we take him to the yard, he goes back and forth between a tennis ball and stuffed animal, determined to figure out how to play with them simultaneously.

Despite his big personality, Grogu is just a baby. He's estimated to be only a year old, and we don't know much about what this last year of his life has looked like, but we do know it hasn't dampened his spirit one bit. He was tied to a bench outside of a building when a good samaritan found him and brought him to the shelter. Upon intake he was wiggly and loose and excitedly ate all the treats offered to him.

Grogu is a social, people-oriented boy who enjoys attention and engagement. He's a lot of fun on walks and loves the treat toss game - where we toss treats and he finds them. He's also shown loose, bouncy behavior around another dog in the shelter's care, but his full history with other animals is unknown. Grogu is publicly adoptable to beginner homes (a bonus, of course, if they have a rotation of delicious treats for him to sample),

256590.name: Harlem
256590.summary:
Meet Harlem!
Harlem was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now this handsome, affectionate boy is ready to find his next forever family. He's a social, playful dog with a big heart, a love for belly rubs, and plenty of personality. Bonus points if you speak Spanish because Harlem knows tricks in both English and Spanish. Talk about a bilingual best friend!

My Ideal Home
Harlem is looking for an active home that can keep both his body and mind engaged. He enjoys walks, enrichment activities like food puzzles and long-lasting chews, and loves learning with positive reinforcement. After a day of adventures, he's just as happy to stretch out for belly rubs and relax with his favorite people.

Good with Other Pets?
Harlem should be the only pet in a home without cats or other small animals, as he has a history of chasing them on walks. Slow introductions to other dogs may be possible, but dog parks are not recommended.

Good with Kids?
Harlem would do best in a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Harlem is an affectionate, intelligent dog who loves spending time with his people. He's crate trained, enjoys car rides, and already knows several cues, making him a wonderful companion for someone looking for a dog with a great foundation. He can become excited around high-value items, so continuing positive reinforcement training and providing appropriate enrichment will help him thrive. With his sweet nature and goofy charm, Harlem is ready to make himself right at home.

BoroughBuddy Notes
A BoroughBuddy writes: Harlem is a move-in ready dog! He is gentle and wonderful on a leash. We encountered many pigeons, squirrels, and kids and Harlem was unfazed. He is a very mellow dog. If you stand in one spot for more than a minute, he'll happily settle down by your feet. One of his cutest quirks is celebrating with joyful rolls on the ground whenever he's happy. Although he wasn't able to play with other dogs, he showed polite interest with an adorable play bow. He loves pets, snuggles, and taking his time to read and respond to all the neighborhood "pee-mails." Harlem is ready to be someone's loyal adventure buddy and couch companion all in one.

256604.name: Eucalyptus
256604.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Young Eucalyptus comes from a house full of cats, all of them as shy as he is. He lived with one adult only, knows a lot about cats but has no experience what so ever with strangers, children or dogs. Imagine landing on another galaxy.. This is how Eucalyptus must feel at the care center, unsure, fearful and worried about what could come next.. He is stationed mainly in his cubby. To avoid any hissing, open gently his door, speak softly to him and you might get slow blinks in return. Attempts at petting send him to the back of his cubby but a feather wand is not seen anymore as a foe. Eucalyptus can actually play with his guest and by himself too. His former owner told us that Eucalyptus was high energy, quite playful and very gentle with his housemates. Eucalyptus is making very slow progress and needs a low traffic home, may be with another kitty and an understanding and patient new owner in order to bloom into amore confident and happy pet. Will you give Eucalyptus a chance. He is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.





What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Eucalyptus is laying in the back of his den, pupils dilated and body tense as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and the den cover is lifted, he backs himself further into the den. Petting is attempted with the scratcher tool, and he is initially tolerant of all petting, but after a few seconds he turns around, swatting hard and hissing at the tool to avoid contact. The interaction is ended to reduce stress.

Pre-Screener Form

Baby Boy came into the care center as an owner surrender due to his owner's declining health issues. Baby Boy's prior owner noted that he is is a fearful and prefers contact on his own terms initially, after warming up he is described as social and affectionate. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

256624.name: Luc

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
Luc is at the front of the kennel, leaning against and head bunting the kennel door with a soft body and her tail held high as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting. Luc is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, Luc remains at the front, continuing to head bunt and lean into all further petting and attention. During the interaction, Luc did display piloerection at the base of her tail. She did not appear to overstimulate even with extended petting and handling. 

Luc interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

256633.name: Xola
256633.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Xola!
Xola came to ACC when her owner could no longer care for her. This sweet girl is looking for someone who understands that trust takes time and that the best friendships are built one step at a time. Once she feels comfortable, Xola enjoys attention, treats, and spending time with her favorite people. She is searching for a patient adopter who will help her feel safe and confident as she settles into her new life.

My Ideal Home
Xola would thrive with an experienced adopter who is willing to continue building her confidence through positive reinforcement training. She will benefit from a calm, predictable environment, slow introductions, and someone who understands canine body language. With patience and consistency, Xola can continue learning that the world is a safe and rewarding place.

Good with Other Pets?
Xola has lived with dogs previously and can be playful and social with familiar canine friends. She can be unsure around unfamiliar dogs and may need slow, thoughtful introductions to help her feel comfortable. Continued positive reinforcement training will help her build confidence around new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Xola's history of feeling overwhelmed with unfamiliar people and her potential for defensive behaviors, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. She would do best with people who can respect her boundaries and allow her to approach new experiences at her own pace.

Things to Know
Xola is a smart and spirited pup who is learning that new things don't have to be scary! She can be a little selective with her friendships, but once she trusts you, she enjoys attention, treats, and companionship. Xola is also working on her manners and leash skills, so her future family should be ready to help her shine with patience, structure, and plenty of encouragement.

256646.name: Ghost
256646.summary:
Ghost arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. His previous owner describes him as affectionate and independent. While in care, Ghost has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to show whale eye and growl when handled. During his assessment, he did not allow handling and would freeze when handlers attempted to interact with him. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

A staff member writes: Ghost is a sweet, gentle pup who loves spending time with people he knows and trusts. He greets familiar faces with a wagging tail, enjoys pets and treats, and is always ready for a chance to stretch his legs. Outside, he walks nicely on leash with only mild pulling and loves to zoom around the yard before checking in with his handlers. Ghost can be a little sensitive to sudden noises or fast movements, so he'll thrive with a patient adopter who can help him continue building confidence. He's also participated in dog introductions and playgroups, making him a great candidate for slow introductions to canine friends. If you're looking for a kind-hearted companion to grow with, Ghost may be your perfect match.

256647.name: Lily
256647.summary:
Meet Lily!
Lily was surrendered alongside five other dogs when her owner could no longer care for them. This sweet, gentle girl may be a little shy at first, but once she feels comfortable, her soft personality begins to bloom. With a little patience, Lily is sure to blossom into a loyal best friend.

My Ideal Home
Lily would love a calm home where she can settle in at her own pace. She has a medium energy level and enjoys leisurely walks, tasty treats, and spending quiet time with her people. Positive reinforcement and a predictable routine will help her build confidence as she adjusts to her new life.

Good with Other Pets?
Lily previously lived with other dogs and was described as friendly with both familiar and unfamiliar canine companions. At the shelter, she has shown polite interest in other dogs, though she appreciates respectful introductions and would do best with slow, positive meet and greets.

Good with Kids?
Because Lily can be timid in new situations, a home with children over the age of 5 is recommended. She'll thrive with people who will let her build trust at her own pace and help her feel safe.

Things to Know
Lily is a sweet, sensitive soul who enjoys gentle affection and happily accepts treats while getting to know new people. She is still working on her housetraining and may need a little patience as she settles into a new routine. Give her a little time, a lot of love, and she'll have you falling head over paws in no time.

256654.name: Andy
256654.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
A volunteer writes: Andy misses the life he had before his elderly owner could no longer take care of him--his own space in the living room, a soft carpet to nap on, and the security of knowing he belonged to someone. Now he's at the Care Center, where he's doing his best to show what a good boy he is. Shy at first, Andy is a fan of slow blinks and gentle pets on his head. Toys don't interest him as much as treats do; he relaxes when humans talk to him. This chunky monkey seems to prefer an easygoing life of laying around and being loved, and we just know there's a pet parent or family out there who can make that happen for this sweet, subdued guy. Meet Andy at the Manhattan Care Center today!

A volunteer writes: There are currently 4 cats (mixed gender) in our community cat room. When I was in there, there were all very relaxed and peacefully coexisting. They had relaxed body language and accepted all pets. They were all sweet a bit reserved at first but gentle souls. 

I have lived with cats at ACC and I'm doing well with them in the Free Roaming Room, so I would likely do well in a multi-cat home.

256656.name: Baulette
256656.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Baulette!
Baulette came to ACC when her owner could no longer care for her, and now this sweet girl is looking for a fresh start. She may be a little low key, but she has a lot of love to give and enjoys taking in her surroundings at her own pace. Baulette is a gentle pup who is ready to find a family that will appreciate her calm personality and help her continue building confidence.

My Ideal Home
Baulette would thrive with an adopter who enjoys a more relaxed companion and can provide daily walks, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. She is a low energy girl who does not need a packed schedule, just a loving home where she can feel comfortable and cared for. With patience and encouragement, Baulette is ready to be your new best friend.

Good with Other Pets?
Baulette has shown some feelings when seeing other dogs while on leash. She may stare, fixate, or pull toward them, but she is easily redirected with guidance. Continued positive reinforcement training and slow introductions will help Baulette feel more comfortable around canine friends.

Good with Kids?
Baulette has been comfortable with handling and enjoys gentle interactions. As with any dog, respectful introductions and supervision are recommended to help her feel successful in her new home.

Things to Know
Baulette is a sweet, easygoing older lady who enjoys sniffing around, taking treats, and spending time with her people. She may have a little bark when she sees another dog, but she's learning that she doesn't have to be the neighborhood announcer. With a little guidance and a lot of love, Baulette is ready to find a home where she can relax, unwind, and be the belle of the ball!
