256666.name: Nala
256666.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Nala, a sweet, quiet, and independent little lady with a heart of gold! She enjoys life at her own pace and loves spending time near her people. Whether she's curled up on your lap, napping on your chest while you relax, or checking in to see what you're up to, Nala is wonderful company.
She loves chasing wand toys, batting around bottle caps, and showing off her playful side during her morning and evening zoomies. She's also the self-appointed guardian of the home-any mysterious sound outside the front door immediately gets her full attention!
Nala thrives with a patient adopter who understands that the best friendships are built on trust. Once she feels comfortable, she'll reward you with quiet companionship, gentle affection, and plenty of adorable moments. If you're looking for a calm, loyal companion with a playful streak and a charming personality, Nala may be your perfect match.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
Nala has improved since her first assessment and was lying at the back of the kennel, appearing slightly subdued but curious. She sniffed treats and then allowed petting on her cheek, her head, and along her back. A couple of times, she appeared as if she might want to jump up on the shelf to get away, but she didn't, and she remained in place and was reasonably calm. She resisted being picked up and retreated farther to the back, but didn't struggle in any obvious way.

Nala tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

256670.name: Umi-Zumi
256670.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Umi-Zumi came into the care center as an owner surrender due to losing housing.  In the prior home he is noted to be Social/Affectionate, Very active & Playful.Due to all noted concerns displayed in a home environment, the behavior department recommends Umi-Zumi be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow Umi-Zumi to acclimate comfortably to his new environment; force-free, reward based training only is advised when introducing Umi-Zumi to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Umi-Zumi presents with outside of the care centers.

256678.name: Seven
256678.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Seven is at risk due to behavioral concerns in the finder's home. Seven was reported to have engaged in an altercation with the resident dog. When attempting to separate the two dogs, Seven bit the finder's sibling on the hand, drawing blood.  No other information is known regarding the bite incident.  During his stay in care, Seven was initially tense bodied, but allowed leashing. As his stay has progressed, Seven occasionally accepts treats and engages in fetch. Medically, Seven has dental disease. 

Seven was surrendered into care as a stray due to a bite incident in his finder's home.  Seven was in his finder's home for three weeks. Seven and the resident dog were reported to have had an altercation. In attempting to separate the two dogs, the finder's sibling was bit on the hand by Seven.  The bite did break skin and draw blood. During the initial part of his stay, Seven was nervous, but he has since warmed up with a slow approach during interactions that are reward-based. During his handling assessment, he readily solicited attention from handlers, jumping into their laps to seek further contact. He does enjoy most forms of treats and playing with plush toys, but he was noted to guard his toy during her handling assessment. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Seven be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

256688.name: Stormy
256688.summary:
My foster writes:
Stormy is a young guinea pig with a big personality packed into a tiny body! He's curious, vocal, and loves to let you know when it's time for snacks. While he can be a little shy in new situations, once he settles in, his playful and sweet side starts to shine.
Stormy enjoys fresh veggies, cozy hiding spots, and listening in on everything going on around him . Hes looking for a loving home that will give him patience, good food, and plenty of space to explore and popcorn around.
If you're looking for a guinea pig with charm, personality, and plenty of adorable squeaks, Stormy might be the perfect addition to your family!

If you're looking for a guinea pig with charm, personality, and plenty of adorable squeaks, Stormy might be the perfect addition to your family!

256693.name: Dyno
256693.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
My purr motor is always running!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
Dyno is laying curled up at the front of the kennel, eyes closed and appearing asleep as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she picks her head up and trills. She gets up to greet the assessor, leaning forward to sniff their hand before softly head bunting it. Dyno allows and leans into all petting, purring as she is pet. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm, continuing to purr, and leaning against the assessor as she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, Dyno remains at the front, continuing to lean into all further petting. When the interaction is ended and the kennel door is closed, she calmly walks over to her bowl of dry food to begin eating.

Dyno interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

256695.name: Reign
256695.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.

A volunteer writes: Reign takes care of those he loves, comforting them when they need and being a friendly and helpful kitty whenever he can. Reign's found himself at the shelter through no fault of his own, but he's a cheerful guy who wants to be in the mix so he's welcoming whatever he can as he waits. Hopping right off his bed to say hello, Reign leaped into my arms and flopped on his side. Celebratory in his affection, Reign nuzzled this way and that before deciding that he just wanted to knead the air while using my hand as a little pillow. Reign's shelter presence combined with his glowing notes make him pretty much everything people look for in a cat. A well known lapcat, he's affectionate and loves to cuddle. Reign loves to play with water and will even play fetch. The only thing is that Reign isn't always a fan of new environments and even though that makes the new shelter environment a little bit of a challenge, he's trying his best and hopes to meet you soon.

256734.name: Thumper
256734.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Thumper came to us with friend Bambi as their house counted too many kitties. One year old Thumper is said to be a sweet pet who plays gently with other cats and kids(he lived with a 12 year old child). At the care center, Thumper acts quite timid, staying at the back of his cubby. He is a bit stressed too as witnessed by the hair found on his blanket. I love his coat though, ebony with hues of chocolate. Thumper is a sweet cat who despite feeling insecure, allows petting with the hand, soft blinks as I talk to him and even leans a bit. He is desperate for love, feeling safe and belonging to a place that will be his for the rest of his life. Thumper for now needs a quiet home and a patient and understanding new owner who believes in him and in his chances to be once again the lovely pet he used to be. Come and meet Thumper at the Manhattan Care Center.

256736.name: Marley
256736.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Seven year old Marley and Peanut were brought to the Manhattan Care Center as their owner sadly passed away. Marley is said to be a shy gal, a calm, sweet couch potato who needs time to warm up and gets along very nicely with her sister Peanut. At the care center, she acts timid but slow blinks with gentle words, leans into pets(see her video) and even comes down her kuranda bed to be petted and eat treats. It must be really tough and unsettling to loose everyone and everything she knew and find herself all alone in a kennel even if staff and volunteers are nice with her. I trust that with a little time, Marley, who seems like a very sweet cat, will come out of her shell. A home sweet home, quiet, understanding and may be without boisterous little children is likely the answer....Come and meet Marley and twin Peanut at the Manhattan Care Center. They are both apparently healthy, spayed and did well on heir behavior evaluation.

I lived with children in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!

256742.name: Miia
256742.summary:
Meet Miia!
Miia came to the shelter with Miia 256742 after their family experienced housing insecurity. This sweet, affectionate girl is equal parts cuddle bug and couch potato, happiest when she's relaxing near her favorite people or handing out kisses to everyone she loves.

My Ideal Home
Miia is looking for a calm home that will appreciate her gentle, easygoing personality while also keeping her mind engaged with walks, enrichment toys, and positive reinforcement training. She enjoys spending time with her family, loves car rides and bath time, and already knows cues like "sit," "stay," and "paw."

Good with Other Pets?
Miia has lived successfully with another dog and is friendly with familiar canine companions. She can be shy around unfamiliar dogs and is uncomfortable with off-leash greetings, so slow introductions are important. Because she can be reactive to unfamiliar dogs and small animals, dog parks are not recommended.

Good with Kids?
A home without young children is recommended. Miia can become protective of high-value items like toys and prefers to enjoy them without interruption, so an older household that can respect her space will help set her up for success.

Things to Know
Miia is a loving, low-energy companion who enjoys following her people from room to room before settling in for a cozy nap. She can be anxious when left alone and prefers gentle handling, especially around her paws, which can sometimes be uncomfortable. She also likes to keep her favorite toys to herself, so teaching fun trade games and giving her space with treasured items will help her succeed. With patience, consistency, and lots of love, Miia will reward her new family with endless affection, quiet companionship, and plenty of sweet kisses.

A volunteer writes: Meet momma Miia! I can't decide if it's more fun to cuddle with her or watch her fetch. Round in all the right places, surprisingly quick on her feet! When I call, she trots over with a joyful jiggle, tail wagging, and leans into cuddles. Her signature move is crawling into a hug when you put out your hand asking for paw. This smart girl gets praise from the canine behavior team for her exemplary work on "leave it" and engaging with positive reinforcement training. Out for a walk, she is chill on a leash and non-reactive, and has been housebroken with regular walks. 

Miia came to us with her sister, Myyha (ID 256743), when their guardian experienced housing insecurity. She had lived with older kids and dogs, and was described as friendly with familiar dogs, though at times shy with unfamiliar ones. In a shelter dog intro, she approached with a loose, neutral body, and disengaged. She's reported to love bath time and water, car tides, know multiple cues, and shower her people with affection and kisses.

256743.name: Myyha
256743.summary:
My foster writes: Myyha gets all the compliments for her looks, and her love style will keep you warm at night, but she's also youthful, strong, energetic and ready to help you stay healthy and social.

Meet Myyha!
Myyha came to the shelter with Mia 256742 after their family experienced housing insecurity. This social, affectionate girl is full of personality and loves being part of whatever her people are doing. Whether she's joining you for a car ride, splashing around in the water, or soaking up cuddles, Myyha is happiest by your side.

My Ideal Home
Myyha is looking for an active home that can keep up with her playful energy. She'll enjoy daily walks, enrichment activities, and positive reinforcement training to help channel her enthusiasm. She's very food motivated, knows cues like "sit," "stay," and "paw," and loves meeting new people, making her a fun companion to continue learning with.

Good with Other Pets?
Myyha has lived successfully with another dog and enjoys familiar canine friends. She can be uncertain around unfamiliar dogs, so slow introductions are recommended, and dog parks are not the right fit for her. She should also live in a home without cats or other small animals, as she has a history of chasing them on walks.

Good with Kids?
An adult-only home is recommended. Myyha can become protective of high-value toys and prefers to enjoy them without interruption, so a home that can respect her space will help her feel comfortable and successful.

Things to Know
Myyha is an energetic, affectionate girl who loves cuddles, adventures, and spending time with her favorite people. She can be enthusiastic on walks and will benefit from continued leash training using positive reinforcement. Giving her space with treasured toys and teaching fun trade games will help her thrive. If you're looking for a loyal sidekick who's always ready to join the fun, Myyha can't wait to meet you!

A volunteer writes: "Always happy to meet new people" - this was how Myyha's former guardian described her, and I quickly learn she is indeed quite a social butterfly. When I sit down in the play yard, this chonky little athlete abandons the ball she's been playing with to join me, asking for cuddles with a soft body. She even rolls onto her back, paws pointing to the sky, as belly rubs are clearly the most important business of the day! Out for a walk, she's easy on a leash and non-reactive, at times looking back at me for reassurance, if a lot is going on around us. She's also been housebroken with regular walks.

Myyha (and her sister Miia, ID #256742) lost her home, where she had lived with adults, older children, and other dogs, due to housing insecurity. Myyha is described as friendly with familiar dogs. In a shelter dog intro, she approached with a loose frame, but later became conflicted. She's reported to love car rides and water, and it's a joy to watch her fish for treats in our little pool. As I return her to the pop-up crate she temporarily calls her home, she obediently goes in, and looks back as if to ask, "We'll do this again, right?". This glass-half-full kinda girl is waiting at Queens (NYC) ACC.

Myyha came to the shelter with Mia 256742 after their family experienced housing insecurity. This social, affectionate girl is full of personality and loves being part of whatever her people are doing. Whether she's joining you for a car ride, splashing around in the water, or soaking up cuddles, Myyha is happiest by your side.

My Ideal Home
Myyha is looking for an active home that can keep up with her playful energy. She'll enjoy daily walks, enrichment activities, and positive reinforcement training to help channel her enthusiasm. She's very food motivated, knows cues like "sit," "stay," and "paw," and loves meeting new people, making her a fun companion to continue learning with.

Good with Other Pets?
Myyha has lived successfully with another dog and enjoys familiar canine friends. She can be uncertain around unfamiliar dogs, so slow introductions are recommended, and dog parks are not the right fit for her. She should also live in a home without cats or other small animals, as she has a history of chasing them on walks.

Good with Kids?
An adult-only home is recommended. Myyha can become protective of high-value toys and prefers to enjoy them without interruption, so a home that can respect her space will help her feel comfortable and successful.

Scott has made lovely improvements since her first assessment and, while remaining slightly shy and a little avoidant of touch, she was in the main cubby, curious, gentle, and sweet. She allowed petting on her cheek, and when pet along her back, she lowered her back as if to avoid being petted, but she tolerated it. She did even better while eating. She was then picked up and held and was reasonably calm in the assessor's arms and remained so when set back down. She ate squeeze-up treats with gusto.

Scott interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in some nervousness, reluctance to be pet and potential arousal. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

256777.name: Citrine
256777.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Citrine is on the at-risk list due to medical concerns. Citrine is a very friendly dog who came in as a stray. We have assessed that Citrine has elevated liver enzymes possibly due to cholestasis (bile not flowing into intestines correctly) or due to a hormone issue. Citrine will need additional diagnostics to determine the underlying cause of his elevated liver enzymes, and may need medication to manage this. Citrine has allowed all handling and seeks attention during their exams. He has been very sweet with the staff.

My foster writes: Woof! I'm Citrine, a sweet wiry terrier mix on the lookout for my fur-ever home.
If you're looking for a loyal sidekick who balances curiosity with a mellow attitude, I'm your boy. I love keeping you company, whether we're going for casual strolls, hanging out at the park, or just cuddling on the couch. I'm a fantastic co-pilot, too-put me in a car, and I'll happily snooze the whole ride.
My foster parent says I'm an absolute gentleman. I'm completely house-trained, well-behaved, and perfectly content spending some quiet time on my own. Bonus: I have a soft, wiry coat that is very low-shedding and allergy-friendly!
I have a slight preference for wet food and tasty treats (yum!), and an even bigger preference for making you happy. I can't wait to meet you!

256795.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Ginger Spice is on the at-risk list for medical reasons. Ginger Spice has a luxated right hip and is obese, which makes recovery tricky. It would be ideal for him to see an orthopedic surgeon to discuss options as surgery will be ideal. Weight loss will also be necessary. Behaviorally, Ginger Spice is timid, but has allowed all medical handling.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

A volunteer writes: Ginger Spice needs emergency placement and has been doing his best to put himself out there. Sleeping with his little face and ears pressed up against the door, he seems so squishy and sweet, but for a cat with so much going on and in need of a whole lot of gentleness, we especially have to respect his efforts. Ginger Spice was found patiently waiting for help, immobile and unsure. Thankfully he trusted the Good Samaritans who brought him to us where we learned he has a luxated hip. We'd love for Ginger Spice to find a family who will love him through getting the care he needs and welcome him for who he is.

256801.name: Mimi
256801.summary: A volunteer writes: Mimi welcomed me to the Care Center by staring at me through the door and then returning to her cubby when I proved to be less interesting than she'd hoped. I love an honest cat but I also know I'm not the forever family she's been hoping to find. I would, however, really love to tell you more about Mimi who is really in need of one. We won't say that Mimi loves the shelter, having found herself here through no fault of her own, but she's a quiet cat who kind of likes to do her own thing. Leaning her whole little cat neck into my hands, Mimi decided that I was kind of interesting after all and is hoping to find a patient and loving family where she can be herself.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!
Chica Little was in the den on top of the litter box and was reasonably calm and alert, but slightly wary of contact. She barely sniffed treats but allowed petting on her cheek and head while remaining in place. She sniffed Squeeze Up without eating it and allowed more petting, at one point pulling back ever so slightly and doing a little lip licking. She's a sweet cat who may just need a little extra time to warm up to her new home.

Due to unusual attention seeking and/or overarousal, Adopters should be mindful of giving Chica Little too much attention at times or too little at other times. Chica Little, due to prior owner history (see separate notes) and a bite/scratch history we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced cat parent home who has received detailed counseling.

256825.name: Goob
256825.summary:
Goob arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. During intake, Goob was observed to chew on traffic cones and thrashed when handlers attempted to place him in kennel. Throughout his stay in the care center Goob has warmed up to handlers. However, during his assessment, Goob became tense, retreated from handlers and thrashed mildly when the handler attempted to place a collar on him. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home. 

A staff member writes: Goob is a fun-loving, enthusiastic boy with a zest for life! He's always excited to get out and explore, loves sniffing around on walks, and enjoys learning new things. He's already practicing cues like "sit" and "down" and has even started clicker training, showing he's eager to engage with his handlers-especially when treats are involved! Goob is looking for an active family who can continue building his manners while embracing his goofy, affectionate personality.

256849.name: Orlando
256849.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Orlando is on the at-risk list for behavior concerns. Orlando continues to display challenging behavior during interactions. He is extremely intelligent and high energy, and needs to expend energy constructively with interactive play sessions 3-4X/day. In addition to playtime, this cat would also benefit from mental exercise from activities such as puzzle toys/games, lick mats, or clicker training. Without providing activity for his/her mind and body, the cat may react with rough play, potentially resulting in bite/scratch incidents. It is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with feline body language, overstimulation, rough play, and who have the time to invest in managing these behaviors on a consistent basis to avoid bite/scratch incidents.

A volunteer writes: I love it when cats knead to themselves. It looks like the most welcoming of kitten greetings, an adorable effort to make friends or a way to show the comfort and happiness they find in their world. Orlando seems to knead as a way of processing some very big feelings and while this makes him look very approachable, Orlando's preferred version of approaching means something a little different in the shelter. We don't know much about his life before the shelter as he was brought to us by police, but Orlando likes when we bring him treats and toys. He's eager to flop over onto his side when we pet him with our scratcher tool, but less so when we pet him with our hands. Orlando would love a chance to meet you and show you his kneads and the love he has in his heart.

256856.name: Marshall
256856.summary:
Marshall came to us as a stray and was dealing with pyoderma when he arrived. The good news is that his skin is responding very well to treatment, and with a specific diet, his condition is clearing up quickly.

Marshall has been a friendly, affectionate dog from the start. He enjoys meeting new people and is quick to lean in for pets and attention. His social nature and eagerness for human interaction make him a wonderful companion.

Like many dogs adjusting to a new environment, Marshall could benefit from some basic manners training to help him become the best version of himself. With consistency, positive reinforcement, and continued guidance, he has all the potential to be a loyal and loving family member.

If you're looking for a friendly dog who enjoys being around people and is ready for a fresh start, Marshall may be the perfect match for you.

256859.name: Jovan
256859.summary:
Jovan came to us as a very fearful dog and initially found the shelter environment overwhelming. Since arriving, he has been making steady progress and is beginning to build trust with the staff and handlers who care for him each day.

Once Jovan has a chance to get to know someone, his confidence starts to shine through. With a gentle, patient approach, he warms up fairly quickly and has shown that he wants to connect with the people around him. As his trust grows, so does his ability to relax and engage.

Jovan is looking for an understanding adopter who will give him the time and space he needs to settle into a new home and continue building confidence at his own pace. At this time, we recommend a home without children.

For someone willing to invest a little patience and kindness, Jovan has the potential to become a devoted and rewarding companion.

256903.name: Pryce
256903.summary:
Meet Pryce!
Pryce was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. His former family describes him as social, affectionate, playful, and very active. Whether he's cuddling on the couch, rolling around in the grass, or joining you for a car ride, Pryce is happiest when he's spending time with his people.

My Ideal Home
Pryce is looking for an active, adult only home that can keep up with his playful personality while helping him learn to settle. He'll thrive with plenty of daily exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He already knows cues like sit, stop, shake, lay down, and "stop barking," and loves healthy treats like carrots and cucumbers.

Good with Other Pets?
Pryce previously lived with both a small and a medium sized dog. According to his former owner, he is playful and outgoing with familiar dogs and initially shy around unfamiliar ones. At the care center, he greeted another dog politely through a barrier with loose, friendly body language after warming up, so slow introductions to resident dogs are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his high arousal level, jumping, and mouthy behavior, ACC recommends an adult only home for Pryce.

Things to Know
Pryce is a high energy dog who will need regular physical exercise and mental enrichment to help him thrive. With structure, patience, and force-free training, Pryce has all the ingredients to become an incredible companion for an active family.

Fun Fact
Pryce loves playing in the grass, enjoys car rides, and would never turn down his favorite snacks: crunchy carrots and cucumbers.

A volunteer wrtes: Pryce is just a special boy. He is only 9 months old and an interesting mix of breeds! He reminds us of a shar pei with his tiny corn chip ears and curly tail, but he is thinner and less fluffy. He is reported to be a shar pei doberman mix! Pryce's ultimate special feature is his toes! He has many extra! His back feet look like he has 2 extras toes per foot! 

Pryce is also just a wonderful personality. He is sweet, social, playful and I am truly shocked he wasn't adopted immediately. Pryce came to us when his owner was homeless. He had been living with his owner in a car, but ultimately that was not sustainable. He had spent time around strangers and children and was friendly and gentle. He spent time with a small and medium dog, both of which he was outgoing and playful with. He can be shy around novel dogs. At the shelter he greeted a dog with a soft neutral, and wiggly frame. He enjoys car rides, knows basic cues, and he likes to cuddle and play. He is a healthy boy and his favorite snacks are carrots and cucumbers!

256913.name: Koka Kola
256913.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Koka Kola is at risk due to behavioral reasons. His previous owner describes him as a social and active dog who lives with dogs, cats, and children.  While in care, Koka has been observed to jump up and bite the leash while in kennel. In one instance, when a handler attempted to distract him with spray cheese, he lunged and bit their hand. This bite did not break skin. Koka has also been observed to attempt to bite handlers through the kennel door. Medically, Koka Kola has undetermined allergies, alopecia, and otitis externa. 

Meet Koka Kola!  Koka is a fun-loving, affectionate 1-year-old mixed breed with lots of energy and an even bigger personality! He loves being around his people, enjoys playing with children, and has previously lived successfully with another dog, two cats, and even birds. He already knows "sit," is crate trained, and is always happy to earn a Milk-Bone or two.

Koka is looking for an active home that can help him continue learning good manners. He can be strong on leash and tends to jump up when he's excited to greet people. He has also shown food guarding behavior, so his new family should be prepared to manage meal times and continue positive reinforcement training. While he enjoys familiar dogs, he may bark or react to unfamiliar dogs, especially off leash.

256919.name: Bearstein
256919.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Bearstein is at risk for behavioral reasons. Bearstein has been observed to be dog and kennel reactive. He has been noted to push off the walls upon exiting the kennel, lunging towards passing kennels. On walks, it has been reported that Bearstein stares towards dogs with a stiff body and is unable to be redirected. With handlers, Bearstein allows petting and will lean into handler's legs with a soft body and wagging tail. Medically, Bearstein is apparently healthy.

Meet Bearstein!
Bearstein was found tied up on the street and is now looking for a patient adopter who can show him that the world can be a safe place. While he's understandably cautious in new situations, this gentle boy has already started making steady progress and is slowly learning to trust the people around him.

My Ideal Home
Bearstein would do best in a quiet, predictable home with someone who understands that trust takes time. He'll thrive with gentle encouragement, a consistent routine, and positive reinforcement as he continues to build confidence. Letting him move at his own pace will help him settle in and truly shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Although his history with other dogs is unknown, Bearstein has shown promising social skills at the shelter. He has enjoyed relaxed greetings, engaged in playful interactions with another dog, and has generally ignored dogs while out on walks. As always, slow introductions to resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful nature and need for a calm environment, ACC recommends an adult only home.

Things to Know
Bearstein can be shy around new people and may retreat or become uncertain when approached too quickly. He's made wonderful progress during his time at the shelter, now walking beautifully on a loose leash, calmly passing people and dogs, and allowing gentle handling with patient, low-pressure interactions. He'll do best with an adopter who understands that confidence is built one positive experience at a time and is willing to let him come out of his shell at his own pace.

Fun Fact
Once he's out on a walk, Bearstein is a true gentleman, strolling politely on a loose leash and taking in the world one sniff at a time.

256941.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Nino is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Nino has been observed displaying high arousal during handling. Most recently, while being returned to his kennel, he repeatedly jumped up, snapped at the leash and the handler's hand, and began thrashing against the leash when trying to be put into kennel, making it difficult to handle him safely. Nino is social staff and typically affectionate but is struggling to acclimate in the care center. Medically, Nino has a tracheal tear and has CIRDC.

Meet Nino! Nino is described as friendly and outgoing with people by his previous owner.  Nino has lived with children of all ages and is described as tolerant, playful, and well behaved around them. He loves games of fetch, chasing balls, chewing on toys and bones, and spending time with his favorite people.

This smart boy is housetrained, knows cues like sit, paw, come, and heel, walks three times a day, and settles well in a crate for short periods. While Nino thrives with people, he can be fearful around other dogs, so any introductions should be taken slowly. He may also bark when his paws are handled or during nail trims.

256959.name: Tazzie
256959.summary:
My foster writes: When you first meet Tazzie she is shy and reserved, but don't let that fool you. Once you get to know her you will feel as if you've known her for ages! Tazzie is a sweet and caring dog who is a sucker for cuddles, belly rubs and chin rubs. She is a very loyal girl who will give you all the love in her heart and is sure to stay by your side. She is the perfect balance between chill and energetic: She can handle long walks in the park, playing fetch until her tennis ball is worn out, but is also down for a chill day at home where she can just lay down and snore away! She also does very well in car rides and will either sleep the whole ride or silently watch out the window. Whatever the plan is with Tazzie, she is the perfect dog to have by your side and will mold perfectly into a calm, loving home!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

A scaredy cat when he first arrived at the Care Center, he was making slow and steady progress--engaging with staffers by exchanging slow blinks and accepting hand pettings on his head. Now he's under the weather and no longer in one of the adoption rooms where potential pet parents can see and fall in love with this handsome young tabby. Bo Peep has what it takes to come out of his shell and blossom, and we're hoping hard an adopter is out there who understands shy boys like this one. Please consider Bo Peep--he needs to know what it means to be cherished, secure, and safe.

A volunteer writes: New York, let's not let Bo Peep slip through the cracks. A scaredy cat when he first arrived at the Care Center, he was making slow and steady progress--engaging with staffers by exchanging slow blinks and accepting hand pettings on his head. Now he's under the weather and no longer in one of the adoption rooms where potential pet parents can see and fall in love with this handsome young tabby. Bo Peep has what it takes to come out of his shell and blossom, and we're hoping hard an adopter is out there who understands shy boys like this one. Please consider Bo Peep--he needs to know what it means to be cherished, secure, and safe.

256993.name: Shelly
256993.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Shelly is a three-year-old tortoiseshell beauty surrendered from a home with three other female cats after some litter box troubles in a shared space(one litter box for four cats!). Since arriving at the care center, Shelly has been using her litter box perfectly, every single time. No accidents, no drama. Turns out that having her own litter box and privacy could be the answer?
There are a few mysteries in Shelly's file. She'd been with her family since she was a kitten, but when she arrived, she was lactating -True, we barely know anything about Shelly's past...
At the center, Shelly is gentle and affectionate, the type of cat who leans into a good scratch behind the ears and settles in for pets like she's been waiting for them. But don't let her calm demeanor fool you - hand her a catnip toy or a feather wand, and she transforms into a gleeful, pouncing athlete. It's a delightful contrast, and it's part of what makes her so much fun to know.
Shelly aced her behavior evaluation with a perfect score, and she's healthy through and through. All she needs now is a home of her own where she can show what a lovely and loving companion she really is.
Shelly is ready. Is her person out there?

I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

257029.name: Gingham
257029.summary:
A volunteerwrites:
Gingham was found roaming the hallways of an apartment building, all by his lonesome. A big guy he is, a "chonker" tiger at nineteen pounds, lots of cat to love! Gingham is friendly to all he meets. His finder, the veterinary team and to us, staff and volunteers. A major head bunter he is, purring away and never in hiding when someone knocks at his door or now enters the community room(playroom) where he resides peacefully with another cat. He started showing his playful skills and does not have overstimulation issues. Nice! Gingham enjoys brushing which he knows he needs to match his looks with his shiny personality! You've got to meet Gingham! He is a really nice cat who will make a new owner happy to share their life with him. Gingham is already neutered, aced his behavior evaluation(Level1)and is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!

I can go home today!
Gingham was inside his cat cave being quiet, and when the assessor went into the room with him and called him, he immediately came out, calm and curious. He rubbed up against the assessor's legs, looked up, and made calm eye contact, and then began enjoying petting on his head, his cheek, and along his back. He raised his tail and leaned in very nicely for cheek rubs, ate some treats, and was calm when picked up and briefly held and remained so when set back down. He enjoyed squeeze-up treats, and as the assessor started to leave, he went back into his cat cave, only to come out seconds later to continue eating his treats.

Gingham interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

257030.name: Ginger Spice
257030.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Ginger Spice!
Ginger Spice may have had a rocky start, but this sweet girl is ready to find a home where she can blossom. After coming to ACC due to housing insecurity, Ginger has been taking her time getting comfortable and is currently living in our Admissions Office where she has happily taken on the important role of supervising staff as a star employee. She's a quiet, gentle soul who just needs a little patience, understanding, and plenty of encouragement to help her confidence shine.

My Ideal Home
Ginger Spice would thrive in a calm, low traffic home with an adopter who understands that trust takes time. She'll do best with someone who can help her feel safe through slow introductions, positive reinforcement training, and a consistent routine. With patience and support, this shy girl is ready to add a little sweetness and spice to your life.

Good with Other Pets?
Ginger Spice's history with other animals is limited. Her previous family noted that she prefers to avoid other dogs, and she has shown uncertainty when meeting unfamiliar dogs at the shelter. Slow introductions and careful management are recommended to help her feel comfortable and successful.

Good with Kids?
Due to Ginger Spice's fearful nature and need for gentle, low pressure interactions, an adult only home is recommended at this time. She would do best with people who understand canine body language and will let her build confidence at her own pace.

Things to Know
Ginger Spice is a low energy pup who enjoys taking life one step at a time. She walks nicely on leash and is looking for someone who can help her discover that the world is full of good things. She may be a little shy at first, but with the right person, this sweet girl is sure to become the perfect sprinkle of love your life has been missing. She's ready to trade her office duties for a cozy couch and a forever family!

257045.name: Kool Aid
257045.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
My purr motor is always running!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

A volunteer writes: There are really only a couple of things that we know about Kool Aid's life before, but what she wants us to know is her project manager background. A multitasking queen she enthusiastically welcomes any coming her way only to exceed everyone's expectations including her own. Having done a truly stunning job redecorating her condo, she beamed up at me with pride. I believe in Kool Aid's work but I also believe in her. A sweet and joyful little cat making the most of things that quite frankly don't seem to have gone all that great for her recently, that Kool Aid was left in a carrier outside the fire department is probably the least interesting thing about her, but is to say that we don't have a lot of information about her life before. She swirled herself into my arms, snuggled with gusto and asked with hope that there will be a family coming her way any day now.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
Meowtini is at the front of the kennel, eyes and body soft as the handler approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he leans forward to head bunt their hands, allowing and leaning into all petting and raising his back as he is pet. He is able to be easily picked up but does begin to squirm after a few seconds. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to lean into all further petting and head bunting to solicit attention.

Meowtini interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Meowtini go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and decompression.

257058.summary:
Meet James, a friendly and easygoing companion who loves being around people. This affectionate boy has a laid-back personality and is happiest lounging near his favorite humans or joining them for a car ride-one of his favorite activities! James is known for his sweet nature and has been described as friendly with everyone he meets.

James has enjoyed having access to a yard and spending time with his people. In his finder's home, he was tolerant of resident cats, making him a promising candidate for a home with feline companions. If you're looking for a loving, relaxed dog who enjoys companionship and will happily be your couch buddy, James may be the perfect match for you.

Cookie is a calm, sweet, and noble boy with a quiet confidence. He's very independent and enjoys having his own space, but he'll happily follow you from room to room just to keep you company. He loves being near his people on his own terms and thrives with gentle affection and a calm environment where he won't feel overwhelmed.
Serena is his playful counterpart. She's quick on her paws, loves leaping onto the windowsill to bird-watch, and never passes up the chance to stretch out in a sunny spot for a cozy sunbath. She's curious, athletic, and brings a fun, lighthearted energy wherever she goes.
Together, they're the perfect balance. Cookie brings the calm, Serena brings the fun, and they absolutely adore each other. Whether they're relaxing nearby, quietly keeping each other company, or sharing a cozy nap, their bond is truly special. If you're looking for two built-in best friends who will fill your home with love, companionship, and plenty of adorable moments, Cookie and Serena are ready to meet you!

A volunteer writes: Calypso lives by the Golden Rule and trusts everyone even if she hasn't always had a reason to. Leading with her fluffy cheeks, Calypso bounded into my face purring a mile a minute. She was left behind in an auto body shop and came to the Care Center with an open heart, kind of like the one she wants to find one day. She welcomed us by nuzzling and headbutting as she very politely asked us for a chance. She's still asking for a chance and seems to good naturedly shrug her kitty shoulders when it doesn't come her way. Calypso has only her heart and friendship to offer, but she's hoping she'll find a family who wants to accept.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Cottage is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Cottage displays high arousal and on-leash reactivity, including persistent hard pulling, barking at dogs and people, fixating on handlers, kennel fighting, and becoming difficult to return to her kennel. She has also been reported to grab at a handler's pants during kennel re-entry. Cottage is highly food motivated, enjoys enrichment, readily engages with pools and with staff. Medically, Cottage recently recovered from CIRDC.

Cottage came into the care center as a stray due to this her behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Cottage has not adjusted well in the care center environment and is noted to show leash biting behavior and become mouthy towards handlers pants when going back inot to kennel. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

257142.name: Monchi
257142.summary:
My borough breaker writes:
I had the pleasure of taking Monchi (ID: 257142) out on a Boroughbreak, and overall it was a wonderful experience. She is a sweet, gentle dog who takes time to build trust, but once she feels safe, her loving personality really shines through.

At the start of our walk, Monchi appeared shy and cautious. She frequently stopped to scan her surroundings before continuing, clearly taking in everything around her and making sure she felt comfortable before moving on. It was important to let her set the pace and gradually earn her trust.

Once we arrived in Central Park, Monchi began to relax. She especially preferred the quieter, less crowded wooded areas, where she felt much more at ease. There, she confidently explored her surroundings, sniffed the ground, and seemed genuinely interested in taking in all the new scents.

Monchi enjoyed the treats I brought and responded well to them, happily sitting on command. As our walk continued and she grew more comfortable with me, she became very calm and trusting. She would either walk right beside me or confidently take the lead, showing just how much her confidence had grown.

We took a few breaks on the grass throughout the walk. At first, she remained alert, but after some gentle affection, she noticeably lowered her guard. On two occasions, she chose to sit or lie down right next to me, which felt like a meaningful sign that she had begun to trust me. She also clearly enjoyed being petted and receiving gentle kisses on the top of her head.

On our return trip, we followed the same route back, and the familiar path seemed to help her feel even more relaxed. She navigated stairs both up and down slowly and carefully. Near the end of our walk, she even surprised me with a short jog for about one block.

Throughout the outing, Monchi was occasionally intrigued by people passing by and was drawn toward women a couple of times. She didn't seem bothered by other dogs, squirrels, or birds, remaining calm around them. She also never pulled on the leash, making her an incredibly easy dog to walk once she got moving.

Overall, I had a fantastic time with Monchi. She is the kind of dog who will need a patient owner willing to invest time in earning her trust. However, once that bond is established, I have no doubt she will become an incredibly loving, loyal, and devoted companion.

Meet Monchi!
Monchi was surrendered with another dog when their owner could no longer care for them, and she is now looking for a calm, patient home where she can feel safe and move at her own pace. She is a gentle, observant girl who tends to be more reserved in new environments but softens with time and patience.

My Ideal Home
Monchi would do best in a quiet, structured home with adopters who understand fearful dogs and will allow her to build trust gradually. She benefits from predictable routines, slow introductions, and positive reinforcement training. Enrichment like food puzzles, sniffy walks, and chew toys will help her confidence grow over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Monchi arrived with another dog and has a known history of living with a canine companion. As always, introductions to other pets should be done slowly and thoughtfully to ensure comfort and compatibility.

Good with Kids?
Due to her fearful nature and need to interact on her own terms, Monchi would do best in a home without children.

Things to Know
Monchi is a sensitive but sweet girl who is still learning to feel fully comfortable in new environments. She may be tense or unsure at first, especially during handling, but she will approach for treats and explores once given space. 257142.summaryHtml:
My borough breaker writes: I had the pleasure of taking Monchi (ID: 257142) out on a Boroughbreak, and overall it was a wonderful experience. She is a sweet, gentle dog who takes time to build trust, but once she feels safe, her loving personality really shines through. At the start of our walk, Monchi appeared shy and cautious. She frequently stopped to scan her surroundings before continuing, clearly taking in everything around her and making sure she felt comfortable before moving on. It was important to let her set the pace and gradually earn her trust. Once we arrived in Central Park, Monchi began to relax. She especially preferred the quieter, less crowded wooded areas, where she felt much more at ease. There, she confidently explored her surroundings, sniffed the ground, and seemed genuinely interested in taking in all the new scents. Monchi enjoyed the treats I brought and responded well to them, happily sitting on command. As our walk continued and she grew more comfortable with me, she became very calm and trusting. She would either walk right beside me or confidently take the lead, showing just how much her confidence had grown. We took a few breaks on the grass throughout the walk. At first, she remained alert, but after some gentle affection, she noticeably lowered her guard. On two occasions, she chose to sit or lie down right next to me, which felt like a meaningful sign that she had begun to trust me. She also clearly enjoyed being petted and receiving gentle kisses on the top of her head. On our return trip, we followed the same route back, and the familiar path seemed to help her feel even more relaxed. She navigated stairs both up and down slowly and carefully. Near the end of our walk, she even surprised me with a short jog for about one block. Throughout the outing, Monchi was occasionally intrigued by people passing by and was drawn toward women a couple of times. She didn't seem bothered by other dogs, squirrels, or birds, remaining calm around them. She also never pulled on the leash, making her an incredibly easy dog to walk once she got moving. Overall, I had a fantastic time with Monchi. She is the kind of dog who will need a patient owner willing to invest time in earning her trust. However, once that bond is established, I have no doubt she will become an incredibly loving, loyal, and devoted companion. Meet Monchi!
Monchi was surrendered with another dog when their owner could no longer care for them, and she is now looking for a calm, patient home where she can feel safe and move at her own pace. She is a gentle, observant girl who tends to be more reserved in new environments but softens with time and patience.

My Ideal Home
Monchi would do best in a quiet, structured home with adopters who understand fearful dogs and will allow her to build trust gradually. She benefits from predictable routines, slow introductions, and positive reinforcement training. Enrichment like food puzzles, sniffy walks, and chew toys will help her confidence grow over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Monchi arrived with another dog and has a known history of living with a canine companion. As always, introductions to other pets should be done slowly and thoughtfully to ensure comfort and compatibility.

Good with Kids?
Due to her fearful nature and need to interact on her own terms, Monchi would do best in a home without children.

Hello Kitty has improved significantly during her stay at the care center. Hello Kitty is laying on top of her den as the assessor approaches, eyes wide and pupils dilated. When the kennel door is opened, she meows softly, getting down from the den and approaching the front of the kennel to greet the assessor with a head bunt. She allows all petting, leaning in as she is pet. When noises occur in the room, she pauses, ears slightly to the side and lip licking. Her attention is easily refocused with soft talk and further petting, and she continues to lean in and raise her back as she is pet. Hello Kitty is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when held. She is able to be placed in a carrier to transfer to the adoptions floor without issue. 

Hello Kitty interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Hello Kitty go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods, decompression, and fearfulness.

Tiana is fit for either an apartment or house she is an exceptional fit for senior adopters(40+ years old) she enjoys slow walks without pulling she rarely barks only speaking up when she truly needs to communicate,great with other dogs, adaptable and thrives on routine

Low- Medium energy no pulling easy leash manners and laid back pace She understands sit, out(go outside to the back yard) When I call her by name she walks toward me

What my friends at ACC say about me:

257176.name: Leo
257176.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Leo was left without much explanation in our center's lobby. Just like that! Well, Leo does not need much advertising...because he is a lovely cat and the promise of a great pet! He appears as a quiet soul, laying peacefully on his kuranda bed. Speak to him gently and he will start to roll on his side, head bunt, purr and raise his tush to the ceiling of his den. He is a pretty brave and solid cat, dealing pretty well with the hustle and bustle of the hallway he resides. Treats helping, Pebbles comes down to his main area to salute me, leans into pets that he clearly would love to last forever. Leo can be easily overlooked due to his location in the shelter(our alley). This friendly tiger is a must to meet, fall in love with and take home as your forever best friend for years to come. He is apparently healthy, aced his behavior evaluation(Level1) and will be ready to go home with you after his neuter. Ask about Leo when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!

257181.name: Monie
257181.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Meet Monie!
Monie was found in an apartment and is ready to find the loving home she deserves. This sweet girl is a total people person who lights up when she gets attention. With her wagging tail, happy personality, and love for cuddles, Monie is the kind of companion who will happily be your new best friend.

My Ideal Home
Monie is looking for a home that can help her channel her excitement into good manners. She is an energetic, playful girl who would love daily walks, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. She's eager to engage with people and loves learning, making her a fun partner for someone ready to continue building her skills.

Good with Other Pets?
Monie's history with other animals is unknown. Please speak with our staff about the best way to introduce her to any resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Due to Monie's mouthy behavior and enthusiastic play style, we recommend an adult-only home at this time. She would do best with people who can help her practice polite greetings and respectful play.

Things to Know
Monie is a social butterfly who loves making connections with people. She is eager to engage, enjoys affection, and has a playful personality that makes every interaction fun. She can get a little overexcited and may jump up or use her mouth when playing, but with consistent positive reinforcement and fun training games, she is ready to learn. 

A Volunteer Writes:
"As soon as the kennel door opened I knew I'd be smitten. Monie happily wagged her tail at me and looked at me with her gorgeous eyes, waiting for me to leash her up. She sweetly came out and away we went. Our walk together was effortless. We instantly felt like best friends as Monie happily posed for selfies. Every time I crouched down to snap a quick picture she leaned in for pets and kisses! I was able to get lots of adorable nose boop glamour shots! Throughout my shift I couldn't help myself from cooing at her and talking to her. I have no doubt Monie will be the ultimate bestie. From snoozing on the couch to taking a stroll on the town, Monie is up for anything!!!"

My Boroughbreaker writes: I spent the day with Monie in Central Park, and she was the perfect companion. She walks well on her leash and is friendly with both adults and children. During our walk, she was not reactive to bikes, skateboards, or cars, though she does pull when she sees other dogs. We did not interact with other dogs, so I am unsure how she would be with them.
When we took a break, she plopped right down next to me and rolled onto her belly for rubs. We received many compliments on how pretty she is! Monie will make a great sidekick, and I hope she finds her loving forever home soon.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Monie stole my heart before our borough break even began. When she was walked out to meet me, she was proudly carrying a tiny purple plush koala, happily tossing it in the air and catching it herself. Naturally, our first stop had to be the pet store so she could pick out a few more toys. After choosing some new stuffies, we headed to Central Park for a stroll and some time relaxing in the grass. Monie is a great walker, and when we found a shady spot for a water break, I brought out her new toys. She was absolutely delighted. She rolled around on her back in the grass with her stuffies, squeaked them with enthusiasm, and happily entertained herself without destroying a single one. Watching her play was impossible not to smile at. Monie is such a fun, spunky girl, and her adorable little raccoon markings only add to her charm. We also stopped for a pup cup, which she gobbled up. She never barked during our day together and only showed a little extra interest when passing other dogs. She's highly treat-motivated and redirected easily, making it clear she's eager to learn and would be a joy to train. More than anything, Monie seems to be looking for life's simple pleasures: toys to carry around, belly rubs, a cozy couch, and someone to love. Beneath her goofy, playful personality is an incredibly sweet girl who would love a family of her own. If you're looking for a dog who will make you laugh, keep you company, and remind you to find joy in the little things, Monie might be your perfect match.

257189.name: Maya
257189.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Maya is At Risk due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Maya displayed elevated arousal both inside and outside of her kennel. She was observed engaging in kennel fighting with neighboring dogs as she passed by them and would bite the leash while being removed from her kennel or during walks. Maya also exhibited jumping behavior toward handlers, at times reaching face level. Despite her high arousal, she readily accepts treats and is extremely social with people. Medically, Maya is overweight.

Maya arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Maya has been observed to have a low threshold for arousal. Noted to head whip towards handlers, jumping up on them, and grab their sleeves during leashing. During her assessment Maya was observed to bite the leash. While on leash, Maya is observed to jump off the walls when attempting to get closer to other dogs. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

257207.name: Knickolas
257207.summary:
My foster writes: Knickolas - Knicky, to his friends - is a laid-back gentleman who spends most of his day napping on the couch. But the moment a hand comes near, he perks right up: he'll gently guide it to exactly where he wants scratches (chin and belly are the sweet spots), and if you stop too soon, he'll tap you with a paw until you get the hint.
Knicky is curious, playful, and loves people of all kinds - he's especially fond of older kids, but needs to get better at keeping four paws on the floor. He already knows sit, stay, come, leave it, and drop it, and he's currently working on down, off, and fetch (he's got the "chase" part down - the "bring it back" part is still a work in progress).
Knicky loves other dogs, maybe a little too much. He gets so excited to say hello that he's still learning how to keep his cool around them, so he'll do best with a confident, dog-savvy adopter who can help him keep practicing. He's also not quite ready to be left alone for long stretches, so his ideal home has someone around often while he builds his confidence. In exchange, he offers total devotion - he'll be your calm, snuggly shadow, will protect you from the bathroom monster, and be the first face you see at the door every time you come home.
257207.summaryHtml:
My foster writes: Knickolas - Knicky, to his friends - is a laid-back gentleman who spends most of his day napping on the couch. But the moment a hand comes near, he perks right up: he'll gently guide it to exactly where he wants scratches (chin and belly are the sweet spots), and if you stop too soon, he'll tap you with a paw until you get the hint.
Knicky is curious, playful, and loves people of all kinds - he's especially fond of older kids, but needs to get better at keeping four paws on the floor. He already knows sit, stay, come, leave it, and drop it, and he's currently working on down, off, and fetch (he's got the "chase" part down - the "bring it back" part is still a work in progress).
Knicky loves other dogs, maybe a little too much. He gets so excited to say hello that he's still learning how to keep his cool around them, so he'll do best with a confident, dog-savvy adopter who can help him keep practicing. He's also not quite ready to be left alone for long stretches, so his ideal home has someone around often while he builds his confidence. In exchange, he offers total devotion - he'll be your calm, snuggly shadow, will protect you from the bathroom monster, and be the first face you see at the door every time you come home.

257213.name: Carl
257213.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Carl is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Carl has not acclimated well to the shelter environment. While initially he was defensive upon intake, with a reported bite that occurred during his pick up (did not break skin), he has shown social behaviors with select staff in a quiet environment, coupled with a slow, reward-based approach. Carl has continued to escalate towards handlers during leashing and when being returned - lunging, growling, snarling, biting the leash, and snapping. Medically, Carl has alopecia, pyoderma, and dermatitis.

Carl was brought to ACC as a stray, so his past history in a home environment is unknown. Carl was reported to have bitten one of the officers on their hand during his pick up, but the bite did not break skin due to their gloves. When stressed or startled, he has displayed growling, snarling, lunging, and muzzle punching at barriers. Outside of the kennel, Carl is able to relax and has shown affiliative behavior, readily seeking attention from multiple handlers and engaging positively with people. But has quickly begun to show fawning behaviors with handlers while growling. We recommend that Carl be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner due to his intense, escalating responses to handling, particularly around leashing and returning to his kennel.  Carl would benefit from placement with an experienced rescue partner that can provide a calm, structured environment and support his continued behavioral progress with the use of a certified professional trainer who utilizes positive reinforcement methods only.

257222.name: Gato
257222.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Gato was trying for days to enter an apartment through a window. She was eventually let in, given a bath and fed before to be brought to the Manhattan Care Center. Gato is a senior gal, a bit shy and feeling out of place with all these changes in her life. She comes forward with encouraging words, appreciates treats and mostly caresses(see video). The attention might remind her of her past life but she at times, retreats to her cubby as nothing seems to be the same and rather confusing. I can only imagine what an abandonment must feel to a cat's brain...What is important to know though is that a new, understanding, caring and loving home will bring warmth and trust to Gato's heart. She is a sweetheart who so deserves you for her golden years. Come and meet Gato very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

257246.name: Logi
257246.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Logi was surrendered to the Care Centers due to his previous owner working long hours. His previous family described him as a social, affectionate, couch potato who spends the majority of his time in the living room of the home when he is not in his crate. Logi allowed his family to bathe and brush him and is accustomed to spending up to 9 hours in a large crate, going on 3-4 20-min-long walks a day during which he pulls moderately on his leash. Logi loves going for a car ride, playing fetch, snacking on dry liver treats, and having chicken broth with his food (dry & wet varieties of Taste of the Wild). During his stay in care, Logi has been highly fearful and avoided interactions with handlers and staff. He has escalated to growling and lunging in the kennel, dodging leashing on one occasion when being removed from the kennel. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and reevaluate her behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

257255.name: Magic Eight Ball
257255.summary:
A volunteer writes:
When I first met Magic Eight Ball, a young damsel found all by her lonesome wandering an apartment building, she was elegantly posing on top of her little "house"(see pictures). Over the next few days, unsettled in her new environment, she bounced between being friendly and being swatty....Clearly, Magic Eight Ball needed more time to adjust to shelter life, the settings, the people, so many other cats in kennels...Magic Eight Ball has a cold right now but her demeanor improved a lot overtime. She loves to eat and to play, that's for sure and she always did! But she enjoys petting at each of our encounters and never seems to be tired of caresses and sweet words, even after a good game with a feather wand. Magic Eight Ball's cold needs to get better but, please, do consider this charming and pretty young gal as a potential for ever best friend. A quiet home and an experienced owner would give Magic Eight Ball the best chance to bloom into a most lovely pet! Come and meet her very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.


I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

Magic Eight Ball tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

257273.name: Glimmery
257273.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Glimmery was found in the lobby of an apartment building, likely let go by her owners. She is a shy and cute middle aged gal, a little tabby who prefers to stay in the safety of her cubby where she "blinks" in response to sweet words, makes biscuits and leans softly into pets. It took some convincing to have her venture outside her den, eat gourmet food and enjoy cuddles but she did and that is what counts(see video). Glimmery is an endearing kitty who was thrown off from whatever her life was, is unsure about what she is experiencing now but  has clearly the potential to bloom into a most lovely, sweet and friendly pet with the caring person who will offer her their home and heart. Come and meet our Gliimery at the Manhattan Care Center and make her yours!






Glimmery is laying in the back of her den as the assessor approaches, pupils dilated and body tense. When the kennel door is opened and the den cover is lifted, she observes the assessor with wide eyes. She is softly spoken to and after a minute or two she begins softly making biscuits, poking her head out of the portal exit and head bunting the side of the door. She leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand before pulling her head back in, pressing herself against the back wall of the den and curling her tail around herself. With more soft talk, she once again begins to make biscuits. Petting is attempted and she is tolerant of all petting, leaning in slightly and purring when she is pet on the head and cheeks but a bit tense when pet down her body. Glimmery is unable to be coaxed out of the den. Pickup is attempted while she is in the den and she is tolerant of the assessor lifting her off the ground, slightly tense but without further issue. When she is placed back down, she remains in the back of the den, continuing to lean into petting on the head and cheeks.  

Glimmery is a sweet, shy girl. She tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

257298.name: Sunflower Seeds
257298.summary:
Meet Sunflower Seeds!
Sunflower Seeds arrived at the care center after being brought in by NYPD when she was found unattended at a precinct, and from the moment she arrived she's shown a friendly, social personality. This happy girl is full of life, curiosity, and enthusiasm for the world around her.

My Ideal Home
Sunflower Seeds would thrive in an active home that enjoys engaging, hands-on time with their dog. She's a bright, energetic girl who will benefit from structure, routine, and ongoing training to help her channel her excitement into positive behaviors. She loves treats and will happily work for them, making her a great candidate for reward-based learning.

Good with Other Pets?
Her history with other animals is unknown, so slow and thoughtful introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
It is unknown if Sunflower Seeds has lived with children previously, so careful introductions are recommended depending on the household.

Things to Know
Sunflower Seeds is a lively, social dog who can be very exuberant when meeting people and may jump up frequently due to her enthusiasm. On leash, she can pull moderately toward places she wants to explore, but she is otherwise friendly and responsive. In the care center, she's shown a playful, outgoing personality, enjoys interacting with handlers, and already knows cues like sit and paw. With consistent positive reinforcement training, she'll continue to blossom into a well-mannered companion.

Fun Fact
On her BoroughBreak, Sunflower Seeds explored Central Park, relaxed in the Conservatory Garden, and even enjoyed a picnic, proving she's just as sweet and fun as her name suggests.
