She loves treats and will happily work for them, making her a great candidate for reward-based learning.

Good with Other Pets?
Her history with other animals is unknown, so slow and thoughtful introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
It is unknown if Sunflower Seeds has lived with children previously, so careful introductions are recommended depending on the household.

Things to Know
Sunflower Seeds is a lively, social dog who can be very exuberant when meeting people and may jump up frequently due to her enthusiasm. On leash, she can pull moderately toward places she wants to explore, but she is otherwise friendly and responsive. In the care center, she's shown a playful, outgoing personality, enjoys interacting with handlers, and already knows cues like sit and paw. With consistent positive reinforcement training, she'll continue to blossom into a well-mannered companion.

Fun Fact
On her BoroughBreak, Sunflower Seeds explored Central Park, relaxed in the Conservatory Garden, and even enjoyed a picnic, proving she's just as sweet and fun as her name suggests.

257327.name: Mr. Milo
257327.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Mr. Milo is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Mr. Milo has displayed intense fearful and defensive behavior during handling, including dodging the leash, lunging, snapping, thrashing, gator rolling, head whipping, and vocalizing. Mr Milo has also been escalating during attempts to pick him up and snapping toward handlers, making contact with a handler's clothing but causing no injuries. Medically, Mr. Milo is apparently healthy.

Mr.Milo came into the care center as an owner surrender due to not having time for him and developing allergies. In the prior home he is noted to Resource Guard with children in the home. His prior owners noted that he is a social, affectionate, very active, and playful dog who spends most of his time where his people are in the home. He loves going for a car ride, is very clingy with those he loves, rolls on his back and moves his paws quickly when he wants attention. Mr.Milo has not adjusted to the care center environment and has allowed minimal handling and escalated to thrashing, vocalizing, and snapping at handlers when leashed or picked up. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

257358.name: True Blue
257358.summary:
True Blue appears to be a mellow and easy-going senior chonk, that is tolerant and appreciative of most handling while remaining aware of his surroundings/environment. He interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience, demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: True Blue is one snuggly little muffin of a cat. With his paws draped over the side of the bed, he gently folded himself into my hands for some scritches before making his way to the front for some pets and a not so subtle attempt to climb onto my lap. True Blue is a senior who was recently given to a family member but brought to us due to allergies but even these big shifts can't dull his brilliant shine. At the shelter it seems he spends his time curled up on his bed, but he loves to be invited to come forward. His experience has taught him that tomorrow can be better and True Blue is still so hopeful that he can become part of your forever family.

257364.name: Kitty
257364.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Kitty spots right away the visitors to his ward. He is at his door trying to get attention, almost dancing and definitively...singing. He rolls on his side, stretches and when his door finally opens, he head bunts his guest, makes biscuits and purrs a storm. Bring a feather wand and Kitty will show you what playing with an active cat is all about and lots of fun. Why is magnificent, friendly and welcoming Kitty with us? We do not have much information about his past life. We only know that a sudden and earsplitting noise seemed to have startled him and he scratched/bit his owner before to run away in another room. Did it ever happen before? We will never know but likely not. Kitty has been nothing but a charm while in our care. Still that unfortunate episode tells us that Kitty would thrive better in a house without young children and rather with experienced owners who are aware of and understand a pet's personality, strengths and weaknesses. This in mind, Kitty would be an amazing, fun and loving companion to cherish and enjoy for years to come. Come and meet Kitty at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

257368.name: Wiggly Piggly
257368.summary:
Meet Wiggly Piggly!
Wiggly Piggly was found wandering the streets on his own, but he's hoping his next adventure ends with a forever family. True to his name, this goofy guy is full of wiggles, loves attention, and isn't shy about rolling over for belly rubs. He's basically happiness on four legs!

My Ideal Home
Wiggly Piggly would love an active home that can keep him busy with walks, playtime, food puzzles, and plenty of opportunities to learn. He's eager to please and will thrive with positive reinforcement training that helps him channel all those happy wiggles into good manners.

Good with Other Pets?
Wiggly Piggly's history with other dogs is unknown. He has shown playful interest during shelter introductions, but slow, thoughtful introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Please speak with our staff to learn more about the best home environment for Wiggly Piggly.

Things to Know
Wiggly Piggly is a social, affectionate boy who loves pets, snuggles, and making new friends. He can get excited and may jump up when treats are involved, so he'll benefit from continuing to practice his manners with reward-based training. Like many shelter dogs, he was initially overwhelmed by the busy environment, so giving him time to decompress in a new home will help him settle in. With patience, enrichment, and lots of love, Wiggly Piggly is sure to wiggle his way right into your heart.

257370.name: Abigail
257370.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Abigail is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. Abigail came to us as a stray along with another dog with no known history. Intially in care Abigail was fearful but with a slow approach she allowed handling and would slightly loosen up. While on walks, Abigail was observed to be on leash reactive to people on bikes and pull towards the other dogs in the kennel room. Abigail started to quickly deteriorate becoming difficult to leash, noted to quickly escalate to growling and snapping when handlers are attempting to leash her. Recently Abigail has been jumping up to bite the leash as well. Medically, Abigail is on treatment for CIRDC.

Abigail arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Abigail has been observed to be on leash reactive. Noted to hard bark at people on bikes and pull towards the other dogs in the kennel room while pushing off the wall and barking. Abigail has also allowed limited handling, noted to quickly escalate to growling and snapping when handlers are attempting to leash her. Abigail may know the cue sit and is receptive to treats. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home. 

Meet Abigail!
Abigail came to the shelter with another dog when her owner could no longer care for them. This sweet girl is still finding her footing in the shelter, and while new environments can make her feel a little nervous, she has a gentle side that's worth getting to know. With patience and kindness, Abigail is ready to start her next chapter.

My Ideal Home
Abigail would thrive in a calm, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. Daily walks, enrichment activities like puzzle toys and long lasting chews, and positive reinforcement training will help her build confidence and feel secure. A predictable routine will go a long way in helping her blossom.

Good with Other Pets?
Abigail came to the shelter with another dog, but she has shown that she is uncomfortable around unfamiliar dogs in the shelter environment. She is looking for a home where she can be your one and only pet, and dog parks are not recommended. Slow, positive exposure to dogs from a distance can help her continue building confidence over time.

Good with Kids?
Because Abigail can be fearful in new situations and is still working on building confidence, an adult only home is recommended where she can feel safe and settle in without added stress.

Things to Know
Abigail enjoys treats, gentle interactions, and taking things one step at a time. She may bark or become worried when other dogs are behind barriers, but with patient, reward based training and a quiet home, she has every opportunity to gain confidence. Give this lovely girl the time she needs, and she'll reward you with a lifetime of quiet companionship.

Daily walks, enrichment activities like puzzle toys and long lasting chews, and positive reinforcement training will help her build confidence and feel secure. A predictable routine will go a long way in helping her blossom.

Good with Other Pets?
Abigail came to the shelter with another dog, but she has shown that she is uncomfortable around unfamiliar dogs in the shelter environment. She is looking for a home where she can be your one and only pet, and dog parks are not recommended. Slow, positive exposure to dogs from a distance can help her continue building confidence over time.

Good with Kids?
Because Abigail can be fearful in new situations and is still working on building confidence, an adult only home is recommended where she can feel safe and settle in without added stress.

Things to Know
Abigail enjoys treats, gentle interactions, and taking things one step at a time. She may bark or become worried when other dogs are behind barriers, but with patient, reward based training and a quiet home, she has every opportunity to gain confidence. Give this lovely girl the time she needs, and she'll reward you with a lifetime of quiet companionship.

257372.name: Leonardo The Lion
257372.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Leonardo The Lion appreciates attention and petting once adjusted to a new environment but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He will likely need time to warm up to his new home and family. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Leo can be intimidated by children, and should go to an adult-only home. Due to his history in his previous home, Leo needs to be the only cat in the home and will thrive as the only child.

My foster writes:
This big boy with captivating golden eyes loves to explore and supervise his domain from high perches (you might even find him roosting on top of the kitchen cabinets!). Curious and talkative, Leo will happily come down to chat, especially if his favorite treats are on the menu (he'll even fetch them if you toss them!). He is fine with being picked up, but only if it leads to lap cuddles, and will lean right in for head and cheek scratches. Leo is clear about his boundaries and will give a gentle nip when he's ready for a break. If you're looking for a handsome, adventurous, and quirky companion, Leo is ready to meet you!

Camila is highly fearful in the Care Centers and has been observed lunging, baring her teeth, and snapping at staff when they attempt to remove her from her kennel. She does not respond to treats or other high-value food items. Her owner reported that she is shy around strangers but enjoys balls, stuffed toys, and bones. Noted to have a tense body, whale eye, and low tail. She is reported to escalate to snapping when handlers approach. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

257376.name: Victoria
257376.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Victoria is at risk for behavior reasons. Victoria has been showing conflicting behavior during socialization. She can become quickly aroused, jumping up at staff with a tense body, ears back. She has behaved well on walks. Medically, she has some dental disease, signs of chronic otitis, and a dermal mass. 

Meet Victoria!

Victoria came to us as a stray, so her past remains a bit of a mystery. What we do know is that she has been friendly and sweet with our staff and volunteers since arriving at the shelter. Victoria is sure to turn heads with her striking appearance, featuring two different-colored eyes and an adorable pink nose that make her truly one of a kind. She enjoys spending time with people and has been a pleasure to get to know.

Victoria can become easily excited and has a low threshold for arousal, so she will likely do best with an adopter who can provide structure, consistency, and positive outlets for her energy. As we continue learning more about her personality, we are excited to help her find a loving home where she can thrive. If you're looking for a unique and charming companion, Victoria may be the perfect match for you!

257388.name: Epilogue
257388.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Epilogue (Epi)!
Epi is a big, fluffy sweetheart with stunning green eyes, an adorable trill, and a heart that's learning what it means to be loved. Like many former strays, Epi didn't know if humans could be trusted. When he first came into foster care, he spent his days hiding, hissing, and refusing to come out.
But with time, patience, and plenty of quiet company (and shared mealtimes), Epi began to realize he was finally safe. Watching him blossom has been incredibly special. The first time he climbed onto the bed to nap beside me felt like the greatest compliment, I knew he had chosen to trust.
Today, Epi is a lovable, slightly awkward giant who loves long naps, good meals, and discovering the joy of toys. Seeing his eyes light up with excitement during playtime is a reminder that he's still experiencing so many "firsts." He's talkative in the sweetest way, greeting you with soft little meows and happy trills, and when he gives you a head butt or curls up next to you, it feels like you've truly earned his love.
Epi is looking for someone who understands that trust takes time. He'll thrive with a patient adopter who will let him settle in at his own pace and continue showing him that the world is a safe place. In return, you'll gain an incredibly loyal, gentle companion whose affection is genuine, hard-earned, and absolutely priceless.
If you're looking for a cat with a beautiful story and an even more beautiful heart, Epi is waiting to choose you

Meet Epilogue. He is a big, fluffy former stray who is still figuring things out. Right now, he's more of an observer than a participant, often choosing a cozy perch where he can watch the world from. While he's still building his confidence around humans, he does have a soft spot for treats and his gentle eyes give a glimpse into the sweet boy beneath.
We know shelter life can be pretty overwhelming, especially for sensitive cats like Epilogue. He is looking for a patient best friend that understand trust takes time. Just like the very best stories. He'd likely settle in best in a calm, experienced home without small children. We think that with a little love and lots of understanding, he has a beautiful next chapter ahead of him.
Could you be part of his happy ending?

257390.name: Azriel
257390.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Azalea is a young man found scared frozen in a park by a Good Samaritan who thought he was hurt. Thank goodness, he was not!. What a cute kitty, cream and orange, shy but curious and wanting to make friends. Azalea takes a while to come out of his hiding box, his safe place, one step forward, two steps backward but in the end, the desire to be petted and loved is stronger(see his video). Nothing is known about Azalea. He is for sure a gentle cat who nevertheless will need for a start an understanding, loving and patient adopter who will give him time to come out of his shell and bloom at his own pace. Azalea is too adorable..You need to meet him! Come to the Manhattan Care Center and adopt this little jewel!








What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Azriel was in the den looking out and appearing calm while in the load position. He sniffed treats and then enjoyed all petting, leaning in for cheek rubbing and gently closing his eyes. He is a sweet cat who remained in place but is doing very well.

Azriel interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

257405.name: Loki
257405.summary:
My foster writes: I am a super loving dog, need to be by my people all times of the day but I am very trusting and do great around strangers, just not alone! I am very relaxed and like to sleep and lay around all day but don't be fooled because I still am social and will make sure you know how much I love you even if im sleeping all day! (I will sleep ontop of you!) I am great at potty trained, going to bed, staying asleep, and dealing with chaos. I am friendly to strangers and won't go crazy if I see another dog or animal or loud noise! I am trained to sit and know basic body language movements. I love car rides, putting my head out of the window but most importantly I love humans. My dream day would be where I can go on a walk with my owner, sit in the grass for a while with them, and then go home and cuddle up with them to watch a movie and maybe get 1 bite of leftovers (sushi is my favorite!) If you are not petting me I will make sure to show you I want to be petted by nudging you until you pet me! I will also do the same until you let me on the bed with you! I am super easy going you do not have to worry about me in busy places, overwhelming and loud places, quiet and dark places, etc. I can manage it all! (just as long as you are by my side!)

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.

257406.name: Diva
257406.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Diva, the pup who has the best personality! Sweet, observant, and wonderfully easygoing, Diva would be perfect for someone looking for a calm companion who is loving but also independent. Diva loves being part of your day. Compared to toys, Diva put all her attention to people. She will follow you from room to room, check in on what you are doing, and then settle into her own spot for a nap. When craving for human food, she likes to sit nearby and watch every bite with hopeful eyes, but she is never demanding. When you come home, she will greet you with enthusiastic tail wags, tiny happy whines, and plenty of affection. She rarely makes a sound, but she is an excellent communicator-she is an expert of using her body language to express her needs. She learned "paw" in only two days, so there is more potential to explore!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older pup, looking for the perfect forever home!
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

257442.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Tyone is at risk due to behavior concerns. Despite leaning into contact from handlers, he is intensely fearful in care, thrashing and leash biting when he is walking in the hallway or being returned to kennel. This behavior was seen by his previous owner as well. His owner reported that once comfortable Tyone becomes playful and affectionate. He can be lazy, plays with his ball, and enjoys napping by his people. Due to intense thrashing and leash biting for staff and Tyone's safety he is unable to be walked. Medically, Tyone is apparently healthy.

Tyone arrived at the care centers after his owners could not take care of him any longer. Tyone in the care centers has been struggling to acclimate, he was reluctant to be leash and be taken out of kennel, and when returning thrashes intensely, making it difficult to walk him safely. Tyone is affectionate and playful, but struggles to acclimate in the care center. As a result, we recommend he is placed with one of our New Hope Partners.

Pre-Screener Form

Bingo was surrendered due to his owner no longer having the time to care for him. His family described him as a social, affectionate, vocal, very active, and playful dog who spends most of his time in the living room of the home. He was noted not to go on walks due to having access to a backyard. During his stay in care, Bingo has been highly fearful and is only allowing for minimal handling. There have been intermittent instances of Bingo being reluctant to walk, and does not readily take treats or toys as reinforcers. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

257449.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Lychee is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

A volunteer writes: Lychee tucks himself into a little ball for his naps and for as adorable and inviting as he looks, it might not be the most accurate representation of how he's been feeling on the inside. Lychee doesn't love the Care Center and we can certainly see why. There are always plenty of new sights and sounds and that's not really Lychee's thing as he prefers a more thoughtful introduction when it's time to begin something new, which we also understand because we've heard that once he gets that time, he's his friendly and outgoing little self. He has lived with another cat and was curious, friendly, playful, and affectionate with them. While we may not be seeing Lychee on his best day, we hope you'll give him a chance to get to show you.

257466.name: Boom Dee Yadda
257466.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Boom Dee Yadda is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Boom Dee Yadda was noted to become reactive toward other dogs and has been reported to growl and become aroused, and redirect his frustration onto staff leashes, biting the leash in the play yard. When on street walks, Boom Dee Yadda participates in decompression training and is social with staff, allowing them to pet him. Medically,  Boom Dee Yadda CIRDC has  resolved.

Meet Boom Dee Yadda!
Boom Dee Yadda came to the shelter as a stray, so his past is a bit of a mystery, but one thing is clear: this goofy guy is ready to fill your life with fun. He greets people with a wagging tail, loves zooming around the yard, and happily leans in for affection once he feels comfortable. With his playful spirit and eagerness to learn, Boom Dee Yadda is ready to make every day a little brighter.

My Ideal Home
Boom Dee Yadda would thrive with an active, adult only household that can provide structure, exercise, and positive reinforcement training. He already enjoys learning new skills and has impressed staff with how quickly he picked up the "touch" cue. Daily walks, enrichment, and fun training sessions will help him channel his energy and continue building confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Because Boom Dee Yadda arrived as a stray, his history with other pets is unknown. At the shelter, he has shown interest in meeting other dogs but can become unsure during introductions, so slow, carefully managed meet and greets are recommended. He may be happiest as the only pet or with a well matched canine companion after thoughtful introductions.

Good with Kids?
An adult only home is recommended for Boom Dee Yadda while he continues building confidence and learning to navigate new situations. He'll do best with adopters who understand canine body language and will let him settle in at his own pace.

Things to Know
Boom Dee Yadda is an affectionate, active pup with a big personality and an even bigger zest for life. He can be sensitive to handling and may become overwhelmed in unfamiliar situations, but with patience, positive reinforcement, and plenty of encouragement, he continues to make wonderful progress. Give this boy a chance, and he'll have you saying "boom dee yadda" about every adventure you share together!

What Staff Has to Say
One staff member describes Boom Dee Yadda as a fun loving, energetic boy who's always ready for his next adventure. He greets people with a wiggly body and wagging tail, loves to zoom around the yard, and happily leans in for pets. He's also a quick learner who has already mastered the "touch" cue and is eager to keep learning alongside his future family.

Sweet Rocci was left in a soft carrier in front of our door at the Manhattan Care Center. Such a lovely tiger he is! He was resting in his cubby when I first spotted him but as soon as I opened his kennel door, he ran to his balcony and jumped down to salute me. Rocci is a very friendly and gentle cat who loves to be petted before to sample even the best treats(see his video). He is quite good looking, well dressed, so easy going and sociable, clearly a well brought up cat who fell out of luck. Well, he came to the right place. Rocci is a good cat, very friendly, welcoming, apparently healthy, already neutered and who passed his behavior evaluation with flying colors. Ask to meet Rocci when you visit us at the care center. He is a love boy sure to give his new owner or family a lot of joy!

257489.name: Ruffin
257489.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Ten year old Ruffin came with friend Teeny(8 year old neutered male)) as their owner was displaced. Ruffin was wary when he first arrived at the care center. His pet parent, his brother, his home...all gone! We understand. It did not take long though for Ruffin, a good and smart cat, to understand that we wanted the best for him. He is such a sweetheart too! He was already a gentle soul when I made his first video but now that he is in our big playroom, he is a much happier camper. Ruffin is a sweet looking tiger with saucer eyes who dreams to be home again, loving and being loved. He aced his behavior evaluation and is already neutered. Come and meet Ruffin very soon at the Manhattan Care Center. 
Ruffin is laying in a loaf position at the front of the kennel as the assessor approaches, coming forward when the assessor enters the room. He allows all petting, leaning in and raising his back with his tail held high as he is pet. 257489.summaryHtml:
A volunteer writes: Ten year old Ruffin came with friend Teeny(8 year old neutered male)) as their owner was displaced. Ruffin was wary when he first arrived at the care center. His pet parent, his brother, his home...all gone! We understand. It did not take long though for Ruffin, a good and smart cat, to understand that we wanted the best for him. He is such a sweetheart too! He was already a gentle soul when I made his first video but now that he is in our big playroom, he is a much happier camper. Ruffin is a sweet looking tiger with saucer eyes who dreams to be home again, loving and being loved. He aced his behavior evaluation and is already neutered. Come and meet Ruffin very soon at the Manhattan Care Center.

257490.name: Teensy
257490.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Teensy needs placement for medical reasons. He has inconsistently been eating in the shelter and now has become anorexic as he fights an upper respiratory infection. He has tolerated some handling, but is not tolerant of handling for more aggressive supportive care. Due to Teensy's size he is at risk for developing hepatic lipodosis the longer he remains anorexic in care. Teensy needs more care than we can provide.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Teensy tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

A volunteer writes: I'm so glad Teensy gave me a chance. He doesn't do this as freely as we'd hope and admittedly our friendship came in steps, but it's one I'm left thinking of long after meeting him. Teensy was brought to us with another cat when their guardian faced an emergency situation. He seems inclined to keep his cards close, but the last thing he wants to do is shut everyone out even if everything else says otherwise. Teensy's in a bottom corner condo, perhaps among the last places people look, he's a bit older, and he's a little too eager to air his grievances about the whole thing. I sat by him and he grumbled, I offered treats and he grumbled, I pretended to ignore him as I read my book and he grumbled, I extended the scratcher tool and he grumbled, but I waited because I recognized his curiosity. I took a little chance and extended my hand and Teensy very sweetly leaned into me (and grumbled) again and again. He softly traded his grumbles for cuddles and I sincerely hope he gets the chance he seems so determined not to ask for.

257492.name: Magnolia
257492.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
My purr motor is always running!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
Magnolia is laying at the front of the kennel, eyes soft as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he gets up, gently leaning forward to head bunt the assessor's hand. Magnolia allows and leans into all petting, tail held high in a question mark shape. He is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm, leaning against the assessor's body, and beginning to purr as he is held. When he is placed back into his kennel, Magnolia remains at the front, continuing to softly head bunt and lean into all further petting. He is offered a squeeze up and quickly eats all of it, continuing to allow all petting as he eats.

Magnolia interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

257493.name: Dos
257493.summary: Dos interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that she go to an Adult-only home with adopters with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in her behavior history in her previous home, as well as fearful cat behavior, and a potential for overstimulation. Dos is a sweet and social girl that appreciates attention and pets, but may take a moment to adjust, and does not do well with children. However, she will thrive in a calm and adult-only home that can provide her with all the attention she desires!

257495.name: Maple
257495.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Maple interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience. 

A volunteer writes: It seems like everyone who meets Maple walks away with the same sentiment: He's a perfect cat. That's probably why I saw staff and volunteers alike sneaking away for a few extra moments of cuddling with him and also probably why he was enthusiastically introduced to me as such. Maple chirped as soon as I opened his condo door and, hoping for a chance to be included, stretched right to the front to greet me. Snuggling into my arms and peering out the window, Maple has been on the lookout for a forever family for some time now. Abandoned in a carrier at the park, Maple was brought to us by Park Rangers so while we don't know much about his history, we know he'd really love a chance to shine.

257503.name: Oreo Cakester
257503.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I may enjoy casually batting at a toy mouse every now and then, but my favorite activity is snuggling on my favorite person's lap!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

A volunteer writes: Oreo Cakester invited me like he was proud to have me over. Brought to us in a stroller and initially found in a parking lot, Oreo Cakester has been through a series of changes that we can only think have brought him that much closer to you. He sits so nobly at the front and chirps out hellos, but I'm inclined to think this former component is a bit of a ruse because as soon as I opened the door, Oreo Cakester was stretched out on his side extravagantly rolling himself into my arms. A big guy who likes to throw himself right into the middle of things to get started, he seems to really enjoy being around people. We've learned that Oreo Cakester likes to take care of his grooming himself, but would cherish the chance to be part of your family.

257508.name: Cleo
257508.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Cleo is on the at-risk list due to medical concerns. Recent bloodwork and physical exam suggest that Cleo may have cushings disease, which is an endocrine disorder. Behaviorally, Cleo has very high fear anxiety stress (FAS) in shelter. During handling times, she is seen trembling, retreats from contact, and seeks exit. Once outside Cleo sticks closely to handlers and ignores other stimuli like people and dogs. To confirm diagnosis and reduce Cleo's FAS, she will require further diagnostics we cannot provide in the care center.

Cleo arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. During intake she was observed to be balk on leash and needed a sling to be placed into kennel. While in care, Cleo has remained fearful and was observed to show whale eye and seek exit during her assessment. Due to the fearful behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

257510.name: Nala
257510.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Nala and friend Rocky were brought to the care center as their family moved to a place not allowing pets. Nala is a shy kitty who needs time to warm up but when she does, she is friendly, affectionate and plays gently with all. She is said to be a calm pet who loves treats...Nala has been almost three weeks with us. Her timid side is still overshadowing her true nature. It is not easy to have lost everything and everyone and be resilient. Nala is showing soft signs that she might emerge from the deep well she is in...We are all supporting her in her efforts. She is such a beautiful tabby girl. I love the orange hues coloring her dress and her golden eyes. A home sweet home, a low traffic home and an understanding and patient new owner are the keys to bring the real Nala back. Will you give Nala a chance? She needs you!









What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

257511.name: Rocky
257511.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Rocky is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
Rocky tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

257518.name: Bacalao
257518.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Bacalao is on the at risk list for medical reasons.  She is a sweet, mature girl with an upper respiratory infection, chronic kidney disease and dental disease. She is not eating in shelter and needs supportive care in a veterinary clinic to recover from her infection. She will need a kidney friendly diet indefinitely in her new home.

A volunteer writes:
I dreaded Fridays when I was a kid. My aunt prepared "bacalao". Just the smell of it made me shrink in my chair... So, I was wondering about the Bacalao I was going to meet...What a lovely cat! Not an encounter I would have bad memories about! Bacalao is at her door, ready for a meet and greet, curious, meowing softly and gently. As I open her den, she leans into pets, purrs very softly and comes even closer, indicating that she would not mind coming into my arms. Bacalao is so sweet. She was abandoned in the hallways of a small apartment building and brought to us by a Good Samaritan. She does have senior teeth that might need to be attended to, aced her behavior evaluation and is ready to go home  with a senior cat lover. Come and meet lovely Bacalao at the Manhattan Care Center.

Bacalao is at the front of the kennel, observing the assessor with slightly dilated pupils and meowing softly as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, she leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand before softly head bunting it. She allows and leans into all petting, tail held high as she is pet and beginning to knead. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm and purring when she is pet and leaning against the assessor. When she is placed back into her kennel, Bacalao remains at the front, continuing to head bunt and lean her body against the assessor's hands, appreciating more petting. When the kennel door is closed and the interaction is ended, Bacalao softly meows at the assessor, gently pawing at the door to solicit further attention. 

Bacalao interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

A volunteer writes:
Scimitar caught quickly my eyes when I entered her ward. What a pretty and elegant damsel, so friendly too, shiny ebony, a little jewel of a cat! Scimitar came right away to me, leaned into pets and purred like she knew me for ever. She is with us as her owner was displaced and could not unfortunately take her along. 257539.name: Marble Swirl
257539.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Marble, a handsome gentleman who perfectly blends high-stamina athleticism with silly, pretzel-shaped couch snuggling. As a true "velcro" companion, he loves nothing more than sleeping right on top of you, treating you to a symphony of adorable sleep twitches and paw fidgets as he dreams. Beyond his goofy nap habits, Marble is an absolute gentleman (he will automatically sit anywhere just to show off his manners, walks into his crate politely to wait for praise, and takes treats from your fingers so gently you will barely feel his mouth). Because he learns best through kindness, this sweet boy requires a patient, active family committed to a peaceful, high-praise home that uses positive reinforcement and never yells.

Meet Marble Swirl!
Marble Swirl is a handsome brindle boy with an even more beautiful personality. Found tied up in a stairwell, he hasn't let his past dim his bright spirit. From the moment he arrived at ACC, Marble Swirl has been friendly, affectionate, and eager to make new friends. He loves being with people and is always ready to greet you with a loose, wiggly body and a happy smile.

My Ideal Home
Marble Swirl would love a home where he can be part of the family and enjoy plenty of quality time with his people. Whether it's neighborhood walks, learning new tricks, or relaxing together after a fun day, he's happiest when he's included. He's an active but easygoing companion who will thrive with regular exercise, positive reinforcement training, and lots of affection.

Personality
Marble Swirl is the definition of a people dog. He is highly social, seeks out affection, and loves interacting with his handlers. During walks he stays close, walks nicely on leash, and happily checks in with his person. He's food-motivated, eager to learn, and has already shown he enjoys practicing cues like "touch." His enthusiasm sometimes leads to a few happy jumps for attention, but it's all part of his charming, affectionate nature.

Behavior Assessment
Marble Swirl has earned a Behavior Assessment Level 2. He is friendly, social, and enjoys meeting new people, but can become a little overexcited and may jump up when greeting handlers. Positive reinforcement training and reinforcing calm behaviors like "sit" will help him continue polishing his manners. Because of his enthusiasm, ACC recommends a home without very young children. He has also participated in dog introductions at the shelter, and adopters should plan slow, thoughtful introductions to any resident dogs.

Overall Health
Marble Swirl is neutered, microchipped, vaccinated, and ready for his new family. He was recently treated for a mild upper respiratory infection (doggy cold) and is recovering well. He also has mild dental tartar, but otherwise appears to be in good health.

Why You'll Love Him
Marble Swirl has all the makings of a wonderful companion-kind, affectionate, playful, and eager to connect with people. He's the type of dog who will happily walk by your side, lean in for pets, and remind you every day just how rewarding it is to open your heart to a shelter dog. If you're looking for a loyal best friend with a heart as big as his smile, Marble Swirl is waiting to meet you.
```

257554.name: Bello
257554.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Bello is a handsome and well named orange and cream young cat with one blue eye, the other one being gold.It would be great if such a beauty would be less shy but not every cat does well in a kennel after having been a house pet. Bello likes to stay on his balcony, in a corner, hoping likely to be left in peace. Should I make contact, should I pet him? Bello slow blinks as I talk to him and neck bunts my hand as I caress his neck. He does not move but I feel he appreciates the attention. We have no history on Bello as he might have been found in the street, clearly not a stray cat, though. A low traffic home and an understanding owner is what Bello needs to fall back on his four once he feels safe and loved. Bello is apparently healthy, was neutered and is ready to go home with you...today. Come and meet Bello at the Manhattan Care Center! 







What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Bello is nervous and shy and was inside the den with large pupils and barely sniffed treats and squirmed to get away. When treats were offered inside the den, he partly bolted outside the den as if to try and escape, but then decided to return inside it. He then allowed petting inside the den while remaining in place and ignored treats and was in a tense body position throughout. He should be given a slow introduction to the home as he is likely to hide if given the chance.

Bello tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior and the likelihood of hiding if given the chance.

257601.name: Floofy
257601.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Floofy, your future fluffy best friend! Floofy is a shy little sweetheart who may start off...a little reserved. But give her a calm corner and a few gentle treats, and she'll blossom right before your eyes! Floofy absolutely adores being petted once she feels at home, and she's the kind of independent kitty who just appreciates a peaceful environment. If you're looking for a quiet but loving companion, Floofy might just be your perfect match!

**Floofy - Adoption Summary**

Floofy is a sweet, affectionate 2-year-old cat who is looking for a patient home where she can settle in at her own pace. In her previous home, she lived successfully with multiple cats and was described as friendly, social, playful, and very people-oriented. She enjoyed spending time near her family, watching the world from the window, chasing bugs, and playing with crinkly toys. Floofy also enjoys being brushed, picked up, held, and carried when she feels comfortable.

Since arriving at the shelter, Floofy has been understandably overwhelmed by the unfamiliar environment. She has appeared timid and fearful, often preferring to stay tucked away and observe from a safe distance. Despite her nervousness, she has remained tolerant of gentle interaction and has shown small signs of wanting to connect, occasionally leaning into petting before becoming unsure again.

Floofy's history suggests that once she has time to adjust, her affectionate and outgoing personality begins to shine through. Her previous owner reported that she may be shy with new people at first but typically warms up with patience and consistency, becoming a friendly and playful companion.

Floofy would do best with adopters who understand that she may need a gradual adjustment period and are willing to let her build confidence at her own pace. She has lived well with other cats and may enjoy a feline companion pending a proper introduction. Due to her fearful behavior in the shelter and history of rough play, a home without very young children is recommended.

If you're looking for a gentle, loving cat who just needs a little time to feel safe, Floofy may be the perfect match.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

257634.name: Tux
257634.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
Tux is laying in her den as the assessor approaches, pupils dilated and poking her head out of the portal exit as the kennel door is opened. When the assessor initially offers their hand, Tux leans forward to sniff it before backing away. With some soft talk, Tux begins head bunting the side of the den door, allowing and leaning into petting on the head and cheeks and beginning to make biscuits. She is hesitant to exit the den, and it takes several minutes to coax her out. Once out of the den, she hesitantly approaches the front of the kennel, softly head bunting and leaning into all petting. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when held. When she is placed back, she tail flicks for a short moment before relaxing and coming forward to head bunt the assessor's hand again, allowing and leaning into all further petting.

Tux interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

257635.name: Red Bull
257635.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Red Bull is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Red Bull has not acclimated well to the shelter environment, displaying a concerning level of arousal which has made walking him safely difficult. Red Bull has been easy to remove from his kennel, but will pull hard on leash/outside and persistently jump up towards staff/handlers' faces. He will occasionally stop to take treats, but has fixated on leads, intensely sniffing their knees, and has torn clothing near their stomach potentially by his nails. In calmer settings, Red Bull has been able to engage with snuffle mats and scented enrichment toys. Medically, Red Bull was treated for an ear infection but is otherwise apparently healthy. 

Red Bull was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior with other dogs is unknown. Red Bull has been social with handlers, readily accepts treats, and has loose, wiggly body language. But Red Bull quickly becomes aroused, jumping up persistently and at times nearly head/level. He is currently being managed with tossing treats, but once he is done eating, Red Bull resumes the aforementioned behaviors. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

257653.name: Poppie
257653.summary:
My foster writes: POSITION AVAILABLE: PERSONAL BUTLER / HOUSEHOLD SERVANT
Employer: Sir Poppie, Lord of Snacks - "I expect excellence. And cucumbers."
Employment Status: Full-time, permanent
His Excellency Poppie, a distinguished gentleman of excellent breeding, seeks a dedicated Butler/Household Servant to attend to his daily needs.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Provide premium hay, vegetables, and snacks promptly at intervals that Poppie may invent on short notice.
- Respond immediately to all wheeks, squeaks, and other official communications.
- Recognize that Poppie's naps are not to be disturbed under any circumstances.
QUALIFICATIONS: The ideal candidate will possess:
- Strong vegetable procurement abilities
- Comfort working for a supervisor who may spend most of the workday lying down
- Previous experience in aristocratic households is preferred but not required.
COMPENSATION: Poppie offers a competitive benefits package, including:
- The privilege of Poppie's company and unlimited opportunities to hear Poppie's opinions
- Daily exposure to an exceptionally handsome brown-and-gold gentleman
- A rewarding career in executive-level guinea pig management
HOW TO APPLY: Qualified candidates should submit a résumé demonstrating their experience in vegetable delivery, household service, snack procurement, and responding to highly vocal supervisors. Poppie is an equal-opportunity employer.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ms. Chili Peppa is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Ms. Chili Peppa displays fearful and conflicted behavior during leash handling, including growling, lunging toward handlers' hands, barking, retreating from the leash, whale eye, and vigilance during kennel removal. She also displays high arousal once out of the kennel, including hard pulling and jumping toward handlers and the leash. Ms. Chili Peppa is social once comfortable, seeks out affection, leans into petting, and is able to be safely handled and returned to her kennel with appropriate management but intermittently has issues with being removed from kennel from select staff. Medically, Ms. Chili Peppa has CIRDC.

Miss Chili Peppa was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Miss Chili Peppa has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and has been difficult to remove from her kennel safely. She has escalated to lunging, snapping, hard barking, growling, and dodging handlers' leads. Once out of the kennel, she has shown some sociable behaviors when given time, a slow approach, and higher-value treats. Due to these concerns, we recommend that she be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can address her challenges with the use of a certified professional trainer that uses positive reinforcement methods only.

Due to these concerns, we recommend that she be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can address her challenges with the use of a certified professional trainer that uses positive reinforcement methods only.

257660.name: Enamor
257660.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Enamor - Your New Little Shadow 💛
Enamor is the sweetest, most easygoing girl you'll ever meet - and she wants nothing more than to be wherever you are. Cooking, working, working out... doesn't matter. She'll be your quiet little shadow, content just to keep you company.
Despite being gentle and calm, Enamor is SO smart - she learned "sit" in just a few tries, and picked up fetch in about 10 minutes flat (she now proudly brings the ball right back to you!). Give her a job to do and she'll surprise you with how fast she catches on.
She's wonderfully steady with people, other animals, and kids alike, and adapts easily to new situations. A tennis ball met its match with her - RIP to one very well-loved chew toy 🎾 - and she also loves puzzle-style toys where she gets to "hunt" for hidden treats.
Speaking of treats: this girl has ZERO off-switch when it comes to food. She's been known to sneak a snack left within reach, so a watchful eye at snack time is a must - she just doesn't know when to stop!
Enamor came from a shelter stay and is still building confidence with alone time, but she's already made huge strides - going from anxious to calmly walking into her crate on her own. With patience and consistency, she just keeps growing more secure every day.
If you want a sweet, smart, endlessly affectionate companion who'll be by your side through it all, Enamor might just be your perfect match. 🐾

I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

A volunteer writes: Lazuli was brought to us in a pillowcase and without much information. That's a tough start but it's ok! We can always work with what we've got and what we're given to help us learn what the best forever family for someone looks like. It's just that Lazuli hasn't been particularly forthcoming. Loafed on top of her little den on a little nest of blankets, Lazuli greeted me like she was already totally over my visit. This is both completely fine and fair, but Lazuli's lack of interest in treats, toys, and pets have served to show us that she's in need of a little extra patience, a lot of extra love, and time to become the cat she wants to be.

257666.name: Sheba
257666.summary:
My Boroughbreaker writes: We took Sheba, an adorable, sweet, and very social pup, to Central Park. She began the day as if she was seeing the world for the first time. She walked exuberantly to the park, anxious to see what was around every corner, darting back and forth, and taking in everything around her.
Sheba is a very active and happy dog and she showed this is multiple ways. Once we got to the park, she was interested in all the people, dogs, and wildlife around her. Of all the dogs we have taken on a BoroughBreak to the park, she was the only one who paid attention to the birds and pigeons. She especially enjoyed running into the flocks of pigeons around her in order to disperse them.
Sheba's cute little high-pitched squeal of a bark had everyone thinking she was a puppy and this garnered a lot of attention throughout the day.
After lunch and a game of fetch, Sheba settled down on the grass in the shade and chewed on a toy for a while, then promptly fell asleep under the tree. She would occasionally awaken, notice that she was a little too far away from us for her liking, and do the "army crawl" to get closer before falling asleep again.
Sheba is such an adorable and sweet girl and would make a wonderful family pet. She would benefit from leash training, learning some basic commands, and controlling her desire to jump up on those around her.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I love to play and will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

257667.name: Oreo Cookie
257667.summary:
Meet Oreo Cookie!
Oreo Cookie was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her and is ready to start a new chapter with a loving family. She is an affectionate girl who enjoys leaning in for pets, spending time with her people, and exploring the world by your side. With a little patience and guidance, Oreo Cookie is sure to be one sweet companion.

My Ideal Home
Oreo Cookie would thrive in a patient home that can provide a consistent routine, positive reinforcement training, and plenty of enrichment. Daily walks, puzzle toys, and fun training sessions will help keep both her mind and body busy. She may need a little extra support as she adjusts to being left alone, but with time and reassurance, she'll continue building confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Oreo Cookie previously lived with a small dog and was described as friendly with familiar canine companions. She can be uncomfortable around unfamiliar dogs while on leash, so slow introductions and continued positive reinforcement training will help her succeed. Dog parks are not recommended, as she is happiest meeting dogs in calmer, more controlled settings.

Good with Kids?
Because Oreo Cookie can be sensitive in new situations and is still building confidence, a home without very young children is recommended. Older children who understand how to respect her space may be a great fit.

Things to Know
Oreo Cookie loves attention and happily leans in for affection, though she may jump up when she's excited to say hello. She can be startled by unfamiliar situations and may need slow introductions to new experiences, but she responds well to gentle, reward based training. With a little patience and a lot of love, this sweet cookie is ready to become the best part of someone's day.

257668.name: Lucy
257668.summary:
Meet Lucy!
Lucy came to us after living her life as a beloved indoor companion and is now looking for a quiet home where she can settle in and be cherished once again. She may be a little shy at first, but beneath her timid exterior is an affectionate lap cat who enjoys gentle attention and forms close bonds with the people she trusts. With a little patience, Lucy's sweet and loving personality is sure to shine.

My Ideal Home
Lucy would thrive in a calm, low-traffic home with adopters who understand that she may need a little time to adjust. She enjoys cozy places to relax, gentle play sessions, and spending time with her favorite people. A family willing to let her settle in at her own pace will be rewarded with a loyal and affectionate companion.

Good with Kids?
Lucy has no history of living with children. Because she can be timid in new situations, a home with older, respectful children or adults is recommended.

Good with Other Pets?
Lucy has no known experience living with cats or dogs. If introduced to other pets, slow and gradual introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health
Lucy has moderate to severe dental disease, is FIV positive, has a heart murmur with no current clinical disease, and is suspected to have a chronic geriatric condition. She is also overweight. Our staff can discuss what this means for her future care.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 - Lucy is a gentle, affectionate cat who has shown signs of stress in the shelter environment but continues to welcome gentle petting and attention. She will do best with adopters who can give her time to adjust and understand that fearful behavior in the shelter does not reflect the loving companion she has been in a home.

Other Fun Facts
Lucy is a true cuddle bug! She loves being brushed, enjoys being picked up and held, happily accepts belly rubs, and has been described as a quiet lap cat who enjoys hide-and-seek, stuffed toys, window watching, and even baths. Her previous family's favorite things about her were just how sweet, loving, and cuddly she is.

A volunteer writes: Lucy finds herself hanging back a bit these days, not because she wants to but because she hasn't heard many people inquire about older cats, FIV+ cats, or black cats. Sure enough, Lucy fits neatly in all those categories but only in addition to several others. Lucy is quick to play and pounces after her pipecleaner feather like a professional kitten. She's charmingly affectionate and big on side leans with matching purrs. Lucy has been here since June and tends to hang back until she's asked. Lucy had one home her entire life and has been cherished for all of it, but she finds herself here due to the heartbreak of housing instability. While she doesn't have a lot of experience with other animals, her previous guardians described Lucy as so sweet, loving, and cuddly. We couldn't agree more and are hoping another chance will be coming her way.

257685.name: Lee Lee
257685.summary:
**Meet Lee Lee - A Remarkable Senior Looking for a Soft Place to Land**

At approximately 19 years old, Lee Lee is a truly special cat with a gentle spirit and plenty of love left to give. Despite her advanced age and several age-related medical conditions, Lee Lee continues to greet people from the front of her kennel, happily seeking attention, chatting with visitors, and enjoying her meals with enthusiasm.

Lee Lee is an affectionate, social girl who has won over staff with her sweet personality. She purrs during handling, enjoys human companionship, and remains bright, engaged, and interested in the world around her. For a cat of her age, her quality of life is currently good, and she continues to show a strong will to enjoy each day.

Medically, Lee Lee is considered a hospice/rescue candidate. She is underweight and has significant muscle loss, likely related to chronic kidney disease and other age-related changes. She also has dental disease, an umbilical hernia, elevated kidney and liver values, and chronic nasal discharge. While her prognosis is poor due to these underlying conditions, she remains comfortable, active, and eating well at this time.

Lee Lee doesn't need perfection-she just needs kindness. She is searching for a compassionate adopter or rescue placement willing to provide comfort, love, and a peaceful home where she can enjoy her golden days surrounded by care.

If you've ever wanted to make an extraordinary difference for a deserving senior, Lee Lee is waiting to meet you.

257689.name: Simon
257689.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Simon is a handsome 6-month-old orange kitten with a big personality to match his big orange energy. Litter box trained, endlessly curious, and always on the move, Simon is looking for his forever home.
Simon was originally adopted from his litter into a loving family, but after a few months it became clear he needed a different kind of home. He's a big fan of rough-and-tumble play - chasing, pouncing, the works - and while he's incredibly affectionate and loves a good cuddle session, he can get overstimulated during play and nip or bat with his paws. He responds well to gentle correction and will happily settle back into snuggle mode once redirected.
Because of this, Simon does best in a home without children and without other pets - he hasn't shown much interest in feline friends, and his play style is a bit much for little ones. He'd thrive with an experienced adult cat owner who understands kitten energy and knows how to work with (not against) his instincts.
Simon isn't a "problem cat" - he's a smart, affectionate, high-energy kitten who just needs someone who gets him. Give him structure, playtime, and patience, and he'll give you all the cuddles in return.











What my friends at ACC say about me:
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other animals.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!

257690.name: Maxwell
257690.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Maxwell is a geriatric cat with several medical issues including heart murmur and suspected heart disease, dermatitis, aural masses, and dental disease. He would benefit from a cardiology consultation with an echo to assess his anesthesia risk. If deemed appropriate, he should also have a dental procedure. Alternatively, palliative care is also an option. Behaviorally, Maxwell has been friendly, but has resisted medical restraint during a blood draw.

A volunteer writes: Trying his very best to introduce himself to everyone walking by, Maxwell knows very well the number next to his age and the possibility you'll notice it too, but Maxwell's hoping to be noticed for who he is. A well loved 18 years, he was brought to us out of an abundance of love and hope that a second chance will be his for the taking and, to his credit, Maxwell has been doing his best to make the most of shelter life. I opened his condo door and he came to see me, nuzzling his cheeks into my hand and waiting for what would happen next. We cuddled for a bit and he truly reveled in the treats and toys I had to offer and then it was time for me to go. It broke my heart just a bit when I peeked back to check on him and he was back facing his window looking for anyone who might also want to be his friend.

257707.name: Rockwell
257707.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Saturday, July 18 from 11AM - 5PM or Sunday, July 19 from 11AM-4PM, Pop-Up Adoption Event at The Spot BK, 232 Varet St, Brooklyn, NY 11206 (Sponsored by Best Friends Animal Society!). Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!
 What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
Rockwell interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting (except along her sides). We recommend that she go to a home with adopters with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in touch sensitivity. Due to her sensitivity to touch along certain parts of her body, she would do best in an adult-only home.

A volunteer writes: Confidently stretched out at the front of her condo, Rockwell holds her toys high above her head as she daydreams about all the different ways she can introduce herself. With a pretty defined tendency to go with her heart, Rockwell's introductions seem to have run the gamut recently. Making her way into someone's home through their fire escape, Rockwell tried to convince them she could stay but huddled in the corner when she realized that wasn't the case. Now Rockwell's waiting for her next chance and hoping that the next introduction she dreams up will be the one to win your heart. Momentarily distracted as she bounced into cuddles and playfully pounced after her toys, Rockwell's looking to improve enough to impress you.

257709.name: Blue Raspberry
257709.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Blue Raspberry is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Blue Raspberry has displayed high arousal on leash, including persistent hard pulling and leash biting intensely making it difficult to walk him safely at times. He is highly interested in exploring his environment and can be difficult to redirect while walking at times. Blue Raspberry engages appropriately with handlers and enrichment but is struggling to acclimate. Medically, Blue Raspberry is apparently healthy.

Blue Raspberry was brought to the Care Centers as a stray, with owner history. Blue R. was described as a social and affectionate dog with a high energy level. He is reported to love car rides and bath time/water. Upon arrival, he was tolerant with staff but hyperaroused. He has remained fearful and wary of interaction with handlers, selectively taking high-value treats. Due to her ongoing fearfulness and avoidance of interaction, Blue Raspberry should be placed through a New Hope Partner into an adult-only home that can help his build confidence and manage his behavior using positive reinforcement-based methods.

257711.name: Mozz
257711.summary:
Another foster writes:
Meet Mozz A. Rella (Mozz for short) a silly, snuggly velcro girl who's never met a stranger. Her favorite activity is to hang out on a patch of grass on a nice summer day and people watch. She loves peanut butter, squeaky toys, and pretty much any type of treat. She's great at catching things that are tossed her way and responds well to "sit" and "stay" commands.
After a careful introduction, Mozz would do great with another canine companion that matches her energy!

My foster writes: Mozz is an adopter's dream! Cannot overhype her enough! Extremely well behaved on the leash. She's calm passing fellow dogs, responding well to "wait" commands. Mozz loves watching runners and kids playing. Be prepared to make a lot of friends on your walks - Mozz is a stunner and several people will stop you to tell you so. She's a powerful presence but even little kiddos will run up to pet her.
At home her favorite place to be is attached to your hip. She won't jump on furniture if not allowed but she'll certainly keep asking to join you. (And if you do allow her to sit with you she will not accept any other position but her head on your lap.) Shes not a barker, but instead will give the true definition of puppy eyes if shes craving your attention. Big fan of kisses! Great with basic commands: sit, lay down, wait. She's learning to take treats softly. She's been left alone for up to 10 hours without any destruction. 10/10 recommend.

Meet Mozz!
Mozz came to ACC after her owner passed away, and while her past is unknown, she's shown herself to be a social, playful, and people-oriented dog who enjoys attention and treats. She's a happy greeter who leans into interactions and is eager to engage with handlers.

My Ideal Home
Mozz would do well in an active, structured home that can continue teaching her polite manners and impulse control in a positive, consistent way. She thrives with engagement, training, and clear boundaries, especially around excitement and food rewards.

Good with Other Pets?
Mozz ignores other dogs in leash observations. Slow and careful introductions with resident pets are always recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to her mouthiness and high arousal when taking treats, Mozz is recommended for a home without young children under 5. She may be open to older, respectful children after a meet.

Things to Know
Mozz is an affectionate, playful dog who gets very excited during interaction and can jump up frequently when seeking attention or treats. She takes treats with a very hard mouth at times, so continued positive reinforcement training around impulse control and gentle mouth behavior is important. She is otherwise tolerant of handling, enjoys engagement, and walks nicely on leash with only mild pulling. With consistency and structure, Mozz has strong potential to channel her enthusiasm into great manners and reliable behavior.

Fun Fact
Mozz is the kind of dog who always shows up with enthusiasm. She just needs a little guidance to make sure all that excitement turns into good manners.

257720.name: Joe
257720.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Who does not like Gingers? Joe is a young and handsome genuine one. Friendly too, always ready for a meet and greet and petting. Joe has a cold right now but I would love for you to hear about him and be ready to adopt him as soon as his URI is over! Joe was found in a carrier in front of a veterinary clinic with two of his "orange" brothers who have already left our care center. The trio was so very very hungry that one of them(by accident) bit the little finger of a staff feeding them. The culprit did not "speak up" and all three gents were deemed guilty...It reminds me of school...Anyway, Joe is a charm, a super friendly and welcoming cat who beams when a visitor is at his door. He enjoys petting and playing in a relaxed way and is also a well mannered kitty. Beside his present cold, Joe is a healthy young cat who performed very well on his behavior evaluation. Be prepare to meet him when he feels 100% better! Joe is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!
