257723.name: Cuppie Cakes
257723.summary:
A volunteer writes:
I fell in love with Cuppie Cakes the moment I met her, shortly after her arrival at the care center, brought by the police without an ounce of information about her past. Cuppie Cakes was initially timid but just few days down the line, she showed herself to be a very sweet, welcoming and loving kitty. She has this "stick" of extending one foreleg when a guest opens her door, like to ask:"will you be my friend, I am a nice gal with a big heart and so much love to give?" Cuppie Cakes indeed really enjoys company and petting and she is also a pleasure for the eyes with her colorful dress. Cuppie Cakes does have senior teeth an outside veterinarian will need to address. She has otherwise a normal bloodwork and did quite well on her behavior evaluation that is just stressing initial shyness. Cuppie Cakes promises to be your loving and loyal friend for many years to come. Come and meet her very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!

Cuppie Cakes is laying on her side in her top cubby, head up and observing the room with a neutral body as the kennel door is opened. When she is called over, she immediately comes to the front of the kennel to greet the assessor with a head bunt. Cuppie Cakes allows and leans into all petting, raising her back and making biscuits as she is pet. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into her kennel, she remains at the front and continues to allow and lean into all further petting.

Cuppie Cakes interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

She allows and leans into all petting, making biscuits as she is pet and trying to walk out of the kennel to be closer to the assessor. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm, purring, and leaning against the assessor as she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all petting, purr, and knead. 
Moonbeam interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

A volunteer writes: Moonbeam looks like she's been waiting five years, a.k.a. all of her life, for some love and care. This little ragamuffin is underweight, though she looks a bit more robust because of her lovely long grey and white fur. 
Moonbeam is as sweet as cotton candy and probably about as soft and fluffy. She doesn't ask for anything but appreciates kind attention. When I met her, she was so timid, she was facing away from her door at the back of her space. However, when she at last realized I was bringing food, friendship, and comfort, she came forward and stayed awhile. After a few minutes of gently petting Moonbeam and speaking to her softly, I even heard a quiet little purr. If you've ever longed for a gentle soul to take care of, this is your little girl.

257759.name: Blanko
257759.summary:
Meet Blanko!
Blanko came to the shelter when his owner could no longer care for him and is looking for a fresh start with an experienced adopter. This energetic, playful boy loves spending time with people and is always ready for fun. He has a big personality and an even bigger heart, and with the right guidance, he's ready to become an incredible companion.

My Ideal Home
Blanko would thrive with an active, adult only household that can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. Puzzle toys, long walks, training sessions, and interactive games will help keep both his body and mind engaged. A predictable routine and patient guidance will help him build confidence and practice calm behaviors.

Good with Other Pets?
Blanko has lived with and enjoyed spending time with familiar dogs, but he can be uncomfortable around unfamiliar dogs and has a history of conflict with other dogs. For that reason, he is looking for a home where he can be your one and only pet, and dog parks are not recommended.

Good with Kids?
Blanko is searching for an adult only home. He is an enthusiastic dog who sometimes forgets just how big he is and can become overly excited, so he'll do best with adults who can help him continue working on his manners and impulse control.

Things to Know
Blanko is an active, social dog who loves to play but is still learning how to channel his excitement appropriately. He may jump up when greeting people, pull on leash, or become overstimulated in busy environments, but he responds well to positive reinforcement and will benefit from continued training. He can also be anxious around loud noises or when left alone, so a calm, patient home will help him settle in. With structure, consistency, and lots of love, Blanko has all the ingredients to become a wonderful lifelong companion.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I love to play and will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.
Yeye appears to be fearful and may not have had much human interaction up to this point. During the assessment she flinched and was avoidant of petting at the start and is fearful of interactions with humans. She would benefit from extra socialization. We recommend that this cat go to a home with cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff. Contact with young children should be avoided or done under strict supervision to prevent provoking a fear response, further delaying socialization. She would do best in an Adult-Only home.

257772.name: Floyd
257772.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Floyd!
Floyd came to ACC when his owner could no longer care for him. This gentle guy may be a little shy at first, but once he feels comfortable, his sweet personality starts to shine through. Floyd enjoys taking things at his own pace and is looking for a patient person who will help him build confidence and feel safe in his new home.

My Ideal Home
Floyd would thrive in a calm, predictable environment with an adopter who understands that trust takes time. Slow introductions, positive reinforcement, and plenty of patience will help Floyd feel comfortable as he adjusts to his new life. He is looking for someone who will celebrate the small victories and give him the space he needs to blossom.

Good with Other Pets?
Floyd's history with other animals is unknown, but he has shown interest in meeting other dogs while at ACC. He may enjoy canine companionship with the right match, but slow introductions will be important to help him feel comfortable and successful.

Good with Kids?
Due to Floyd's shy and sensitive nature, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. He would do best with people who can respect his boundaries and allow him to approach new experiences at his own pace.

Things to Know
Floyd is a sensitive sweetheart who is learning that the world can be a safe place. He enjoys exploring, playing with toys, and checking in with his favorite people once he feels comfortable. This handsome boy may need a little extra time to warm up, but with patience and kindness, Floyd is ready to become someone's loyal companion.

257782.name: Temu
257782.summary:
Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am playful and cute!

257793.name: Musk Ox
257793.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Musk Ox is laying in his den as the assessor approaches, eyes wide, pupils dilated, and slightly tense. When the kennel door is opened and he is softly spoken to, he leans forward hesitantly to sniff the assessor's hand, head bunting it before pulling back. Crunchy treats are offered and he immediately begins eating them. He is able to be coaxed to the front of the kennel with treats, allowing and leaning into all petting. He is able to be easily picked up, slightly tense when held but showing no further issue. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all petting.

Musk Ox interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Musk Ox go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and decompression.

257812.name: Hazel
257812.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Hazel is on the At Risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display challenging behavior during interactions. She is extremely intelligent and high energy, and needs to expend energy constructively with interactive play sessions 3-4X/day. In addition to playtime, this cat would also benefit from mental exercise from activities such as puzzle toys/games, lick mats, or clicker training. Without providing activity for her mind and body, the cat may react with rough play, potentially resulting in bite/scratch incidents. It is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with feline body language, overstimulation, rough play, and who have the time to invest in managing these behaviors on a consistent basis to avoid bite/scratch incidents.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

Hazel's Foster Parent says: "Hazel is a bright-eyed and curious sweetie who loves flopping on her back and playing. Though she startles easily, she also recovers quickly and goes right back to exploring. She is great at using her litter box and has the cutest little meow. When she plays and rolls around
from side to side, it's very very cute. In the day, she was pretty low energy, mostly she napped and relaxed. She was always excited to play when we entered her space and curiously sniffed us." 

Hazel may not have been ready for pets, "while warming up to us in the first 24 hours, she did [communicate her boundaries by hissing] if our hands got too close to her - but does enjoy scritchies from a little backscratcher we used."

Her foster noted that Hazel can escalate when startled and when she gets overstimulated, and  would do best in a home with "no children, and people who can understand cat body language... but it's pretty easy to tell when Hazel is uncomfortable."

Hazel's looking for a patient family who will learn with her and at her pace, carefully reading and celebrating her messages the way she intends.

257821.name: Jujubee
257821.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Jujubee is at risk for behavior reasons. Jujubee has begun to deteriorate in care, leash biting, helicoptering, and causing herself to faint when exiting the building. She has shown resource guarding with certain items such as the wobble wag ball, escalating to snapping when in an aroused state engaged with the toy. Jujubee loves to relax in the yard, lying across the bench with a tennis ball. When walked on her harness, she is pulling hard at the end of the leash. Medically, she is apparently healthy.   

Meet Jujubee!
Jujubee was found near a school and is a young, social, and enthusiastic girl who is always ready to engage with her people. She has a bright, friendly personality and loves staying close to her handler, showing lots of interest in attention and interaction.

My Ideal Home
Jujubee would do best in an active home that can provide daily physical exercise, mental stimulation, and structure. She will thrive with enrichment like food puzzles, long-lasting chews, and interactive games to help channel her energy in positive ways.

Good with Other Pets?
Jujubee has been observed to ignore other dogs on walks and showed a soft, polite greeting during a controlled introduction. Slow, supervised introductions are always recommended for any resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Due to her high energy and jumpy, enthusiastic greetings, ACC recommends a home without very young children (under 5). Older children who are comfortable around active dogs may be a good fit after meeting her.

Things to Know
Jujubee is highly social and affectionate, often seeking out her handlers for attention and physical closeness. She can be very enthusiastic, including jumping up and rolling over during interactions, so she will benefit from consistent, reward-based training to build manners and impulse control. She enjoys engaging play, follows her handler readily, and responds well to positive interaction. With structure, enrichment, and continued guidance, she has all the makings of a fun and loving companion.

Fun Fact
Jujubee doesn't just like attention, she actively seeks it out, making her a cheerful, people-loving pup who's always ready to be part of the action.

257823.name: Corazon
257823.summary:
Meet Corazón
Corazón was found tied to a light post and is now safe in our care, slowly learning that the world can feel a little softer and kinder. True to her name, she's a gentle "little heart" who is starting to show her sweet personality as she warms up to new people and surroundings.

My Ideal Home
Corazón would do best in a calm, patient home that allows her to adjust at her own pace. She benefits from gentle structure, predictable routines, and positive reinforcement as she builds confidence. A quieter environment will help her feel secure while she continues to come out of her shell.

Good with Other Pets?
Corazón has shown neutral, polite behavior around other dogs in care, though her full history is unknown. Slow, thoughtful introductions would be ideal if she were to live with another pet.

Good with Kids?
Due to her initial fearfulness and need for a slow, predictable environment, Corazón would do best in a home without very young children at this time.

Things to Know
Corazón is a soft, thoughtful girl who starts off a bit shy but becomes more comfortable with gentle encouragement. Once she trusts you, she allows handling, takes treats nicely, and shows calm, steady engagement. She will thrive with gradual desensitization to new environments and continued positive reinforcement training to build her confidence. With time, patience, and kindness, she has all the makings of a truly loving companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Corazón is exactly the kind of dog who quietly wins your heart. At first, she takes a moment to take in her surroundings, but once she feels safe, she gently comes forward for pets and leans into calm attention. She enjoys soft interaction, takes treats politely, and shows her sweet, sensitive side when given time to relax. Her name means "heart," and it fits her perfectly. She may not rush into love, but she gives it in the most sincere, meaningful way once she's ready.

Volunteer Notes
What a mush! She is a chill happy dog and is the biggest cuddlebug. 5 minutes after meeting me she was giving kisses and asking for belly rubs. I adore her, she is such a great dog. She seems a bit dog reactive in her kennel and within the shelter but the second she was outside she was entirely ambivalent to any other dogs. She also seems to be housebroken!

My Boroughbreaker writes: She met some dogs on the street, they sniffed each other and left, never heard a bark from her. She was not distracted by other dogs or people in the park. She was happy and well mannered the entire day. She drank water during breaks but was not so interested in treats. Overall, 5 out of 5!

Corazón is full of joy and has the sweetest, most endearing personality. When she's ready to play, she'll pick up her favorite toy, carry it over, and gently nudge you with it to let you know it's time for a game of tug. She also has the cutest tail wag whenever you talk to her, making it hard not to smile right back. She walks great on a leash! On walks, she loves checking in with you showing how attentive and connected she is. And when she's ready for a nap, get ready for some seriously adorable sleeping positions! She's playful, affectionate, and wonderfully joyful. With her sweet little quirks and happy spirit, she has so much love to give and would make a wonderful companion for someone lucky enough to call her family. She will lounge comfortably in her crate when she's home alone and looks like she may also do well in a home with other animals as she's shown neutral behavior during walks.

Handsome Gato was brought to the care center as his owner became unable to care for their pet.He was rather on the shy side when I first met him but his gentle and loving personality is starting to shine through. We have no information about Gato's former life as a pet but what we can see is a well mannered and quiet kitty who really loves petting(he head and neck bunts, stretches, closes his eyes with soft words...see his VIDEO), keeps orderly quarters, uses his litter box and is never in hiding. According to the veterinary team, Gato is an apparently healthy and well kept cat who still needs to be neutered(by us). He did very well on his behavior evaluation and would love to meet very soon his new owner or family. Magnificent and sweet Gato is waiting for you on E109th street!

A Good Samaritan saw Miffy being "let go" in the street and brought her to safety to the Manhattan Care Center. Miffy is just too adorable. Her finder would have kept Miffy as a pet but her building had a "no pet" policy. Miffy is apparently healthy, spayed and passed her behavior evaluation with flying colors. She is ready to start a new chapter in her life ...with you so come and meet her very soon at the care center and take her home!

Miffy interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience, and should go to a home with no other cats. 
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!

257849.name: Taja
257849.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Taja!
Taja arrived at ACC as a stray, and while we don't know much about her past, we know this sweet girl is hoping for a fresh start. The shelter environment can feel like a lot for Taja, but beneath her nerves is a gentle pup who is ready to build trust with a patient person. Give her some quiet time, tasty treats, and a little space, and you'll begin to see her sweet personality shine.

My Ideal Home
Taja would flourish in a calm, low-traffic home with someone who understands that confidence grows one small step at a time. She will benefit from slow introductions, a predictable routine, and positive reinforcement training to help her feel safe and secure. Her future family should be ready to let Taja set the pace as she adjusts to her new surroundings.

Good with Other Pets?

257850.summary:
Mama Capps is a gentle, medium-energy dog who is still building confidence in new environments. She walks well on leash with no pulling, ignores other dogs and people while outside, and shows generally calm, neutral behavior during handling, though she may appear nervous or distracted at times. She can be fearful in new situations and benefits from a slow, patient approach that allows her to initiate interaction at her own pace.

Due to her sensitivity, Mama Capps would do best in a calm home with older, respectful children (no children under 5). She may need time to adjust to a home environment and thrives with positive reinforcement, structure, and a quiet space to settle in. With patience and understanding, she is likely to continue gaining confidence and comfort.

257855.name: Nala
257855.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Nala is on the at-risk list due to medical concerns. Nala is a sweet old cat with a chronic wound (owner's report they've been struggling with it for 4 years). She also has severe dental disease. Nala will need veterinary follow up to ensure her wound is healing appropriately as well as a dental procedure. Behaviorally, she has been soliciting attention and allows handling. However, depending on her healing process and how the stress-induced likely compulsive behavior (that resulted in her wound) does or does not continue to manifest - Nala will require continued behavioral and veterinary intervention to manage her condition to maintain a suitable quality of life.

Nala is a senior spayed female Domestic Short Hair who was recently surrendered to the shelter. She is a quiet but sweet, medium-energy cat who tended to keep to herself in her previous home and prefers calm, predictable environments. In her previous home, she lived indoors with adults and children and was described as shy and timid with unfamiliar people. In shelter, she has been very sweet and shoulder, soliciting attention and displaying a relaxed demeanor. She has no bite history and allows full handling, including brushing, nail trims, and carrier placement. She would benefit from living in a new home with only adults.

Nala has been experiencing inconsistent litter box avoidance for approximately 8 months, recently becoming daily in the context of environmental stressors. She is reported to urinate and defecate outside the litter box, often under the bed.

Medically, Nala is a geriatric cat with severe dental disease, a chronic self-inflicted wound on the neck likely related to stress, and mild non-regenerative anemia. She is currently under treatment including pain control and antibiotics, with ongoing monitoring. Her prognosis is considered fair, with improvement likely dependent on a low-stress environment and continued medical management.

Despite her medical and behavioral challenges, Nala is affectionate, appreciates all petting and attention, head bunts and will paw at staffs' chests in order to show off her party trick. She without fail, will try and climb up onto staffs' shoulders and lay there like a warm orange scarf for a moment, generally seeming to enjoy being perched up on shoulders. She is best suited for a calm, experienced adopter or rescue placement that can provide a quiet home, consistent care, and support for her medical needs.

Ideal placement: Low-stress home, minimal environmental changes, ongoing veterinary follow-up, and understanding of geriatric medical needs and litter box behavior concerns related to environmental stressors.

257857.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Buddy is at risk due to behavioral reasons. While in care, Buddy has been observed to be kennel reactive and have a level of anxiety. Noted to lunge towards other dogs in pop up crates and was seeking exit while heavily panting during their assessment. In his previous home Buddy is noted to know the cues sit, stay, down, and come. They described him as a high energy dog that loves dancing to music.
Medically, Buddy is apparently healthy.

Buddy came into the care center as an owner surrender due to moving to a no pet policy home. In the prior home he is noted to have high energy, Buddy is a smart guy and knows lots of tricks- sit, stay, lay down, come. According to a prior owner, Buddy "loves hugs, kisses, and dancing to music." Buddy has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has show Kennel reactivity behavior lunging towards dogs in crates and high level of anxiety seeking exit, flushed face and heavy panting. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

257863.name: Glover
257863.summary:
My Foster Writes: Glover is a curious, playful, and quirky cat with a kitten-like energy and a wide-eyed zest for life. He quickly embraced the cushy indoor life of his foster home and is endlessly fascinated by the new sights and smells, chirping to himself as new things excite him. He has an affinity for running water, and will perch happily between the shower curtains while the shower runs, and even be entertained by watching you wash dishes. He's happy to be your shadow, but his playful side comes out in the evenings when he gets to play with his favorite wand toy. Glover will do well in any home that wants a sweet, playful companion.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Glover has warmed up nicely since his first assessment and interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Glover go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in the potential for overstimulation.

It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

257889.name: Grizelda
257889.summary:
My # BoroughBreak Buddy writes:
Grizelda is amazing. She's a sweet, gentle girl who just wants to be wherever you are to calmly keep you company and snuggle as much as possible. She is a quick learner and figures out puzzle toys super fast! She likes walks and was friendly and calm when meeting new people. She enjoyed squeaky stuffies and toys, especially before naptime. She took treats gently and politely, and definitely enjoys a well deserved pup cup. Her snuggling skills are phenomenal, 10/10! Her snoring is also a 10/10, absolutely adorable. She is a great companion in the car, at the park, and on the couch. Loved every minute with her.

Meet Grizelda!
Grizelda was surrendered due to housing insecurity and is ready to find a loving family to call her own. This happy, social girl loves being around people and is always eager to soak up attention, pets, and snuggles. With her affectionate personality and playful spirit, Grizelda is sure to brighten every day.

My Ideal Home
Grizelda would thrive with an active family who enjoys including their dog in everyday adventures. She has a medium energy level and will benefit from daily walks, playtime, and enrichment like puzzle toys and long-lasting chews. She loves being where her people are and is happiest when she can spend quality time with her family.

Good with Other Pets?
Grizelda's history with other dogs is limited, as she had no previous experience with other dogs in her home. She has done well greeting dogs at a gate in care. Slow introductions to any new canine companions are recommended to help set everyone up for success.

Good with Kids?
Grizelda previously lived with children and did well, but because she can get excited and jump up when greeting people, a home with children over the age of 5 is recommended. Older kids who are comfortable around an enthusiastic, affectionate dog would make great companions for her.

Things to Know
Grizelda is described as social, affectionate, playful, and always ready for cuddles. She is housetrained, enjoys car rides, and is comfortable with bathing and brushing. She may pull a bit on leash when she's excited, but with continued positive reinforcement training she'll continue polishing her manners. If you're looking for a loyal shadow who will happily shower you with love, Grizelda might just be your perfect match!

257895.name: Charly
257895.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Charly arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. Her previous owner states that she is shy and prefers contact on her terms. While in care, Charly has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to have a tense body and maintain her distance with handlers. When a handler reaches towards her, Charly retreats quickly and hides behind the secondary handler. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult-only home. 

Meet Charly!
Charly was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and now this sweet girl is looking for a patient family to help her feel safe and loved. While new situations can be a little overwhelming for her, Charly has shown that she is capable of forming bonds and enjoys gentle, low-pressure interactions with people who give her the time she needs.

My Ideal Home
Charly would thrive in a calm home with someone who understands that confidence takes time. She will benefit from a predictable routine, slow introductions, and positive reinforcement training to help her feel more comfortable in new environments. Long walks, enrichment activities, and puzzle toys can help keep her mind busy and support her overall well-being.

Good with Other Pets?
Charly has shown interest in playing with other dogs while on walks and does not react negatively to dogs in her care center assessments. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended to help her feel comfortable with any future furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Charly's fearful nature and preference for approaching people on her own terms, she would do best in a home without children.

Things to Know
Charly is a sensitive girl who may need a little extra patience while adjusting to her new surroundings. She can be nervous when meeting new people or experiencing unfamiliar situations, but she appreciates gentle handling and the chance to make choices at her own pace. With a quiet home, a caring person, and plenty of encouragement, Charly can continue building confidence and become a wonderful companion.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Zoey is laying in her den, resting her head on her front paws and observing the assessor with a neutral expression as they approach. When the kennel door is opened and she is spoken to softly, she quickly exits the den, greeting the assessor at the front of the kennel with a firm head bunt and soft meows, stopping for a moment and low growling before continuing to head bunt. She allows and leaning into all petting and is tolerant of extended handling. She is able to be easily picked up but begins to grumble when she is held. She is tolerant of being held for a few seconds but does continue to grumble. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front, softly meowing and tolerating further attention and petting, displaying some piloerection at the base of her tail but not escalating further. 

Zoey interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Zoey go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression, and pickup discomfort.

I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!

I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

Zoey is laying in her den, resting her head on her front paws and observing the assessor with a neutral expression as they approach. When the kennel door is opened and she is spoken to softly, she quickly exits the den, greeting the assessor at the front of the kennel with a firm head bunt and soft meows, stopping for a moment and low growling before continuing to head bunt. She allows and leaning into all petting and is tolerant of extended handling. She is able to be easily picked up but begins to grumble when she is held. She is tolerant of being held for a few seconds but does continue to grumble. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front, softly meowing and tolerating further attention and petting, displaying some piloerection at the base of her tail but not escalating further.

Zoey interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Zoey go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression, and pickup discomfort.

257915.name: Octopus
257915.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.


Octopus is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

A volunteer writes:
Octopus gave birth in a laundromat. I guess, she wanted a clean environment for her brood. She was not allowed to stay and was brought to the Manhattan Care Center with her few days old babies. Octopus was stressed and had a very hard time nursing so the eight babes were placed and fed in an incubator. Octopus remained defensive with her caretakers and not open to having a trusting relationship with them. Lately, Octopus is showing signs that she might want to engage with staff and volunteers. She likes treats and as she spends more time on top of her hiding place than in, I presented her with a tray of high end cat food that I held. She came forward and after some hesitation and back and forth, she ate while I was with caution, petting her(see video). I was not so lucky with feather wands she seemed to be scared of. Nothing really is known about Octopus. Was she a stray, a pet who got out of luck? We all wish Octopus could be given a chance because even if she shows tiny improvements at the care center, being in a quiet home with a compassionate while experienced adopter or foster could be the light at the end of the tunnel for her...Will you be Octopus' hero?


What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
Octopus tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. Any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

257934.name: Rocky Meowboa
257934.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Rocky Meowboa is on the at risk list for medical. Rocky has a moderate upper respiratory infection and is eating but not well. He needs supportive care, robust nursing, and medication. 

A volunteer writes:
Rocky Meowboa is a very handsome two year old Tuxedo in our care as a family member developed allergies to his dander. He is said to be friendly to all(he would not be a fan of other cats, though), quiet, well mannered, playful and liked to be carried. Coming to the care center has been a very rough change in Rocky's life. He is not home with his family, nothing is "happening", he is stuck in a kennel and whenever his door open, he does not recognize his familiar faces...Rocky Meowboa accepts petting, occasionally slow blinks and slightly leans into pets but his heart is somewhere else...A new home, a new owner will most likely make Rocky Meowboa feel better and slowly put him on the road to recover his livelihood. So, come to the Manhattan Care Center and adopt sweet Rocky!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

257942.name: Baxter
257942.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Baxter is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Baxter displays fearful behavior during handling, including startling easily, seeking distance from people, backing away during leash handling, head whipping when approached to unclip the leash, and being reported to snap during leashing attempts. Despite his fearfulness, Baxter is able to be leashed with patient, low-stress handling and has shown increasing comfort approaching handlers and participating in training games but is still struggling. Medically, Baxter is apparently healthy.

Baxter came into the care center as a stray due to this, his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Baxter has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

257963.name: Batman Deluxe
257963.summary:
Meet Batman Deluxe!
Batman Deluxe was surrendered by his previous family and is looking for a fresh start. This handsome boy is affectionate, gentle, and enjoys being close to his people. While he can be shy when meeting someone new, once he feels comfortable his sweet personality shines through, and he loves spending time with the people he trusts.

My Ideal Home
Batman Deluxe would thrive in a calm home where he can settle in at his own pace. He would do well with adopters who understand that he may need a couple of weeks to fully adjust and build confidence. He enjoys companionship, cozy places to lounge, and interactive playtime, making him a wonderful fit for someone looking for a loving feline companion.

Good with Kids?
No young children under 13 years old. Batman Deluxe can be timid in new situations and would do best with older, respectful children who understand how to give him space while he adjusts.

Good with Other Pets?
Batman Deluxe previously lived successfully with a dog and was described as friendly, tolerant, and gentle during play. He has no known history of living with other cats, so slow introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health
Overall healthy with moderate dental disease.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 - Batman Deluxe has shown some fear and stress in the shelter but remains social and enjoys gentle petting. He is comfortable interacting with people once he feels safe but may be sensitive about being picked up. He would do best with adopters who can give him time to adjust and respect his boundaries.

Other Fun Facts
Batman Deluxe is the perfect mix of playful and laid-back! He's a lap cat who loves lounging near his people, watching the world from the window, playing hide-and-seek, chasing bugs and moths, splashing at water, and batting around crinkly toys. When he's happy, he'll greet you with an adorable quivering tail and affectionate head bunts for more pets.

A volunteer writes: Batman Deluxe won my heart with his very good natured insistence that he has special permission to walk around Adoptions. He doesn't, but a cat who climbs onto a lap after a two second introduction is sure to be successful in making friends. We also hope, of course, successful in finding a forever family. Batman Deluxe is a playful and active cat who was brought to us due to housing insecurity. With a list of outstanding qualities, including his love of quality time with people and playing gently with crinkle toys, Batman Deluxe has literally hopped right into shelter life, but this very sweet and cuddly boy is ready to find you.

257978.name: Mimi
257978.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Mimi is a delightful dame who charmed me with her "generous" size and her gentle, calm and welcoming personality. She was surrendered for GI(vomiting) issues we have not observed at all at the care center. Could it be that she needed a change in her diet? Possible! She is said to be at first a bit shy with strangers but a very good pet otherwise. Mimi is indeed a bit timid when you first meet her but she quickly eases into a very friendly cat who likes to stay next to her visitor for petting or just company she is very fond of. Once a guest enters her room, the "little tiger" emerges from her resting place, looking to meet and greet. She does not mind me placing a bow around her neck for the photo shoot.  Once settled, she makes biscuits and just waits for her caretaker to stay with her forever. Of course, a home sweet home would be so much better! Mimi does like brushing(an overweight cat, beside a proper diet should be combed regularly to avoid matting). Lovely Mimi appears reasonably healthy(beside being overweight) for her eleven years of age, has a good blood senior panel, is already spayed and did very well on her behavior evaluation. She could go home with you...today for many years of loving and loyal companionship!


What my friends at ACC say about me:
What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

257986.name: Anthony
257986.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Anthony is a petite, cute, slender and featherweight Tuxedo who arrived into our care bundled with eight other cats in a dog crate. Wow....Nothing is known about them and like sweet Anthony, all his friends are looking for a home sweet home. Anthony, being quite thin, loves to eat. He is at first a little fidgety but quickly eases into a lovely, friendly and very welcoming host hungry for cuddles. Anthony gets a lot of attention from staff and volunteers as he is so pleasant to spend time with. He did very well on his behavior evaluation, is already neutered and 100% ready to go home with a new owner. Anthony might be tiny but he is mighty friendly and will bring joy and happiness to his forever family!




What my friends at ACC say about me:
My purr motor is always running!
Anthony was in the cubby looking curious and immediately came out onto the shelf when offered treats, then quickly came down into the main part of the kennel. He was very sweet, repeatedly arching his back with a high tail when pet along it, and enjoyed cheek rubs while investigating his treats. He's a sweet, curious, and fairly confident cat who allowed himself to be picked up and briefly held before jumping back into the kennel. He then ate squeeze-up treats until they were gone.

Anthony interacts with the assessor, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

Benedict was in the cubby at the back and appeared somewhat subdued, with a downcast expression. He pulled back slightly when the door was opened but allowed himself to be approached and pet, remaining quiet and in place throughout. He was pet along his cheek and back and didn't seem to mind it. He ignored treats and remained in place when the assessor was done. He's a sweet cat who likely just needs some time to warm up.

Benedict interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior. 
A volunteer writes: Treats? Nah. Toys? Pass. But pettings from humans--now that's Benedict's weakness! This sleek young guy has been in heaven getting so much affection from Care Center staffers and volunteers, and his calm demeanor while being treated to cheek scratches and body pets shows us that he's super comfortable with people. Benedict did very well on his behavior exam, with the team noting that he appreciates attention, is easy to handle, and would be a great fit in almost any kind of household. Meet our very good boy Benedict at the Manhattan Care Center today!

My purr motor is always running!

Benedict was in the cubby at the back and appeared somewhat subdued, with a downcast expression. He pulled back slightly when the door was opened but allowed himself to be approached and pet, remaining quiet and in place throughout. He was pet along his cheek and back and didn't seem to mind it. He ignored treats and remained in place when the assessor was done. He's a sweet cat who likely just needs some time to warm up.

Benedict interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: Treats? Nah. Toys? Pass. But pettings from humans--now that's Benedict's weakness! This sleek young guy has been in heaven getting so much affection from Care Center staffers and volunteers, and his calm demeanor while being treated to cheek scratches and body pets shows us that he's super comfortable with people. Benedict did very well on his behavior exam, with the team noting that he appreciates attention, is easy to handle, and would be a great fit in almost any kind of household. Meet our very good boy Benedict at the Manhattan Care Center today!

257991.name: Eloise
257991.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Eloise is on the at-risk list for medical concerns. He has very painful gum disease, and he gets agitated if you go near his mouth. He is eating some canned food, but he is underweight and unthrifty. He may need full-mouth, teeth extractions and anti-inflammatory medications. He needs care and attention that we cannot provide.

Eloise has made wonderful progress since his first assessment and is now a calm, sweet, and friendly cat. He was resting comfortably on top of the den, looked at the assessor with a calm face, and immediately sniffed and began licking treats. He loved all petting, leaning in very nicely for cheek rubs, and remained calm when petted along her back. During a partial pick-up, he remained calm as well, and when set back down, he continued to show gentle interest in the assessor and the treats. He ate squeeze-up treats and otherwise was relaxed and very sweet.

Eloise interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

A volunteer writes:
Police were alerted by a Good Samaritan about a dog crate containing nine cats sitting in a big mess...Young cats, middle aged cats and one oldie, Genevieve. All on the thin side, the young ones needing mostly just basic care and love(some have already been adopted). When staff brought Eloise to the adoption area, I thought he was one more of the many seniors who arrived at the care center over the last few days. Eloise is a very poorly kept(he was bathed in the medical room) and very underweight(5 lbs)Tuxedo with a hanging tongue and a thick saliva as he has severe and painful stomatitis for which he gets symptomatic treatment. One year old...There must be some mistake....Well, no, Eloise is a youngster whose Lucky Star never shone on. He stayed crumpled in a corner, defeated and likely hoping to be left alone. I padded his kennel with freshly bought baby blankets and gave him "Delectables" which he ate almost in its entirety. He put up with some petting and turned around, asking for a rest. Right now, we are trying to make Eloise comfortable and make sure he eats. What he needs, beside veterinary follow up, is a caring and experienced  foster/adopter and a home sweet home where he will feel safe and loved. Will you be Eloise's real Lucky Star?
	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

257992.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Francesca is a handsome, all ebony and sleek kitty found with eight other cats, all cramped in a dog crate. Pretty sad but thankfully, they were brought to the Manhattan Care Center for us to find them a home. 257993.name: Genevieve
257993.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Police were alerted by a Good Samaritan about a dog crate containing nine cats sitting in a big mess...Young cats, middle aged cats and one oldie, Genevieve. Genevieve is an all ebony gentleman who like most of his housemates is shy, underweight, a bit shabby and in need of TLC. All his friends have been rescued or adopted and Genevieve is still waiting for his forever. Genevieve has made great progress. True, he still likes to stay in his cubby, his safe place but his feelings toward us have changed for the better. Trust settled in and Genevieve now comes forward for petting, leaning into pets and rubbing his head against my hand. He is really a sweet eleven year old gent who soooo deserves a home and a family, a safe, permanent and loving place where he can finally feel cared for and happy. I enjoy every bit of my time spent with Genevieve. Since June 26 when he first arrived at the care center, I have grown to really enjoy and love this sweet cat who took a while to show his true and gentle personality. I hope a quiet, loving and comfortable home materializes soon for sweet Genevieve!
Addendum:Genevieve surprises me every day. He finally started to play!!!

What my friends at ACC say about me:I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

258005.name: Spot Mewlgrim
258005.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Spot Mewlgrim is laying in front of the window, flopping over on his side as the assessor approaches. He allows all petting, making soft eye contact, leaning in, and making biscuits as he is pet. He is tolerant of pickup, a bit tense but without any further issue. When put back down he continues to allow and lean into all petting.

Spot Mewlgrim interacts with the observer, solicits/ appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods and decompression. 

A volunteer writes: There are currently 4 cats (mixed gender) in our community cat room. When I was in there, there were all very relaxed and peacefully coexisting. They had relaxed body language and accepted all pets. They were all sweet a bit reserved at first but gentle souls. 
Addendum: Spot Mewlgrin has come a long way since his arrival at the care center when his owner was taken into care. He was subdued, glued to the floor of his kennel, moving only for the bare necessities. Spot was moved to our community room where he is a much happier cat! He probably kind of feels home in the large space provided with hide outs, nice places to rest and there are always humans at hand, ready to give a pet and a treat. Lets not forget something very important, Spot Mewlgrin gained 3 friends he still is learning to know. Of course, senior Mewlgrin would love a new family and a home sweet home for his golden years. So, when you visit us at the care center, asl to meet Spot Mewlgrin!

258010.name: Wisteria
258010.summary:
Meet Wisteria!
Wisteria is a sweet 9 year old girl who was found tied to a post, and now she's hoping her next chapter is filled with the love and security she deserves. This gentle senior has a calm, easygoing personality and wins people over with her kind eyes and quiet charm. She's ready to trade uncertainty for a cozy home and a family to call her own.

My Ideal Home
Wisteria would love a peaceful home where she can enjoy leisurely walks, soft places to nap, and plenty of affection. She's the perfect companion for someone looking for a mellow best friend to share life's quieter moments with.

Good with Other Pets?
Wisteria has been calm and neutral around other dogs at the shelter. As with any new pet, slow, thoughtful introductions to resident animals are always recommended.

Good with Kids?
Wisteria has shown a gentle, social demeanor at the shelter. As always, we recommend respectful interactions and supervision with children while everyone gets to know each other.

Things to Know
Wisteria walks beautifully on leash without pulling and enjoys meeting new people with a friendly, relaxed attitude. She has been easy to handle, enjoys treats, and has shown herself to be a calm, steady companion. If you're looking for a low-key dog who is happiest simply spending time by your side, Wisteria may be your perfect match.

Fun Fact
Like the beautiful flowering vine she's named after, Wisteria brings a gentle, peaceful presence wherever she goes. All she needs now is a forever home where she can bloom.

My Boroughbreaker writes: Hung out inside and enjoyed the AC! We practiced and nailed commands like 'sit', 'shake', and 'stand up'. We cuddled, took a nap on the kitchen floor, and politely asked for lots of pets and belly rubs. Wisteria is a lovely girl. Slow in movement warms up to you quickly, and never barked/growled or showed any signs of aggression.

258029.name: Shimmer
258029.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Shimmer is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Shimmer has displayed high arousal, including hard pulling and leash biting making it difficult to walk her safely at times. Most recently, while playing in the yard, Shimmer became increasingly aroused and redirected onto the handler, jumping up, air snapping, and repeatedly snapping toward their feet and legs while leash biting as well. Outside of these moments of peaked arousal, Shimmer is social with handlers, enjoys toys and play, takes treats gently, and is easily leashed and returned to her kennel. Medically, Shimmer is apparently healthy.


Meet Shimmer!
Shimmer was dropped off at a precinct when his owner could no longer care for him, and he is now looking for a fresh start with a family who can give him structure, love, and plenty of outlets for his energy. He is a wiggly, happy boy with a bright personality and a love for movement and attention.

My Ideal Home
Shimmer would do best in an active home that can provide daily physical exercise along with mental enrichment. He thrives with routine, positive reinforcement training, and fun activities that keep his busy mind engaged, like food puzzles, sniffy walks, and interactive games.

Good with Other Pets?
Shimmer has shown neutral behavior around other dogs in the shelter setting, though his full history is unknown. As with any new placement, slow and supervised introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
No specific concerns noted in care; however, because he is energetic and still getting to know his environment, older children who are comfortable around active dogs may be the best match.

Things to Know
Shimmer is a fun, affectionate, and energetic dog who enjoys being around people and getting pets.  With structure, enrichment, and consistent training, Shimmer is likely to shine even brighter in a home.

I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

A volunteer writes: Stallone's a little cutie pie who isn't always sure he wants to be one. We get that. 258039.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

A volunteer writes: Shelly Winters knows when someone is there to see her. She kneads and purrs in place, sweetly tucking her head into her blankets happily inviting them to visit in her own way. Here's where it may be helpful to note that Shelly Winters has a very particular way. This is mostly because she hasn't been too sure about pets in the traditional sense though she'll accept them in her own way. Shelly Winters has lived very successfully with both (familiar) cats and (calm) dogs, finding her Care Center footing has been a little touch and go. We've heard she can be very affectionate when she warms up to people and though she prefers to run, direct, and manage the show when it comes to cuddles, she also prefers to be near the people she loves when she isn't at her window. We think Shelly Winters really wants to shine, which is why we see her chirping out to the room, she just isn't sure how, which is perhaps why we see her back up when we open the door. Shelly Winters could use a little chance and we sure hope you'll come meet her soon.

258053.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Chess Piece is a handsome Tuxedo gent found sitting all by his lonesome on the staircase of an apartment building. A Good Samaritan took him in for a week and he mingled nicely with her own pets. Lack of space and financial constrains brought Chess Piece to the Manhattan Care Center where he is doing well, happy to meet staff, volunteers and visitors, appreciating petting, sampling treats and playing occasionally with feather wands and catnip toys. Although reserved, well adjusted and well rounded, Chess Piece, clearly would love to step out of his kennel and start a new page in his life...with you! Chess Piece is apparently healthy, neutered, good looking, did very well on his behavior evaluation and is ready to go home with you...today!

258071.name: Sugar Crumble
258071.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Sugar Crumble and friend Twixie were stationed on a scaffold for a few days until a Good Samaritan brought them to safety to the Manhattan Care Center. Both gals were very shy and are still in hiding at the back of their cubby. Sugar Crumble is a bit more daring and decided to play hide and seek with me. Yes, true, she was a bit wary but I felt that she appreciated my soft words and gentle petting(see her video). Sugar Crumble is really pretty in her vibrant Tortie dress. She is a sweet gal who needs still to trust a little bit more after her ordeal and she will be ready to meet her new family. Life has been harsh for many former pets into our care and starting a new page in their life will often be challenging. Patience, understanding and love are keys to success! Sugar Crumble is hoping to meet very soon her new and forever family!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Sugar Crumble has improved significantly since her first assessment. She was in the cubby, appearing calm and slightly curious, and leaned her head slightly forward for treats and was attentive. She gave some slow blinks and then allowed and appeared to enjoy petting on her head and cheek, leaning in slightly and then leaning forward a little bit more. She kept her tail wrapped but was curious and alert.

Sugar Crumble interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

258086.name: Ginger
258086.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Ginger is a beautiful Tortie with vibrant eyes who came to us with sixteen of her housemates counting cats and dogs as their owner was taken into care. Ginger is a reserved cat, a bit serious looking, a senior whose life was turned up side down when she lost her family, her home and her friends. She is trying to make the best of her ordeal, hoping to find comfort with staff, volunteer and visitors. She leans into pets, head bunts very gently, makes biscuits and purrs softly. She comes willingly in her caretaker's arms and lap, may be as a reminder of past life. Her ears bother her for now  but we are treating her for the matter. Ginger can often be found in plain view(and not in hiding), resting lavishly on her kuranda bed and I guess, hoping for the best, a safe and loving place for her golden years. Ginger did very well on her behavior evaluation, is already spayed and could go home...today! Ask to meet Ginger when you visit us at the care center.



What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
My purr motor is always running!
Ginger was asleep at the back of the kennel in the litter box and looked at the assessor with sleepy, half-open eyes. She woke up when spoken to and gently pet, and immediately began eating the treats that were offered. She was then coaxed forward with more treats, coming all the way to the front, and enjoyed petting while remaining calm. She was very gentle and delicate when picked up and held by the assessor, sitting sweetly in his arms and looking cozy and friendly. She went back into the kennel, where she ate more treats and then began eating squeeze-up while remaining calm and quiet throughout.

Ginger interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

258090.name: Binx
258090.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

Binx is at the front of the kennel as the assessor approaches, pawing the corner of the kennel door to solicit attention. When the kennel door is opened, he head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting and purring as he is pet. Binx repeatedly walks out of the kennel, appearing interested in exploring. He is able to be easily picked up but does become a bit tense when held for an extended period. When he is placed back into the kennel, he continues to allow all further petting and handling, leaning in as he is pet.

Binx interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Binx go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and decompression. 

A volunteer writes: Shy, calm Mr. Binx isn't asking for much. He'd love to find patient pet parents who let him come out of his shell at his own pace, who understand that though he comes from a home, he'll need a little time to adjust. He might also enjoy having other cat pals in the household, as his previous owner had multiple cats and even a few small dogs. He'd be happy with a windowsill or sofa to curl up on, so he can spend his golden years feeling comfy and secure. Toys and treats aren't at the top of his wish list, but new humans who give him a soft place to land are. Looking to take on this low-key gentleman? Binx is waiting to meet you at the Manhattan Care Center.

UPDATE:Surprise! Binx decided to come out of his shell! He was calling me from his window, rolling on his side and making biscuits! I opened his kennel and there he was, asking for pets and head bunting my hand, even purring. What a tiny little man he is but so cute and clearly happy to have company and receive some love. Binx has been working on himself. Come see the results...A sweet senior dreaming of a home and a family.....
258090.summaryHtml:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

I have lived with cats in my previous home.

I have lived with dogs in my previous home.

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

Binx is at the front of the kennel as the assessor approaches, pawing the corner of the kennel door to solicit attention. When the kennel door is opened, he head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting and purring as he is pet. Binx repeatedly walks out of the kennel, appearing interested in exploring. He is able to be easily picked up but does become a bit tense when held for an extended period. When he is placed back into the kennel, he continues to allow all further petting and handling, leaning in as he is pet.

Binx interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Binx go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and decompression.

A volunteer writes: Shy, calm Mr. Binx isn't asking for much. He'd love to find patient pet parents who let him come out of his shell at his own pace, who understand that though he comes from a home, he'll need a little time to adjust. He might also enjoy having other cat pals in the household, as his previous owner had multiple cats and even a few small dogs. He'd be happy with a windowsill or sofa to curl up on, so he can spend his golden years feeling comfy and secure. Toys and treats aren't at the top of his wish list, but new humans who give him a soft place to land are. Looking to take on this low-key gentleman? Binx is waiting to meet you at the Manhattan Care Center.

UPDATE:Surprise! Binx decided to come out of his shell! He was calling me from his window, rolling on his side and making biscuits! I opened his kennel and there he was, asking for pets and head bunting my hand, even purring. What a tiny little man he is but so cute and clearly happy to have company and receive some love. Binx has been working on himself. Come see the results...A sweet senior dreaming of a home and a family.....

258091.name: Biscuit
258091.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
My purr motor is always running!
Biscuit was inside the den, appearing curious and slightly shy, but poked her head out to get the squeeze-up and then allowed petting while pulling back slightly, but then enjoying it while eating. She could not be fully coaxed out of the den, but she did stretch her neck out farther to get more of the squeeze-up when it was placed a little farther away from the door. She's a sweet cat who just needs a little time to warm up.

Biscuit interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior. 
A volunteer writes: Mellow, social, curious, sweet--these are just a handful of words our behavior team uses to describe Miss Biscuit! Arriving at the Care Center from a home environment, she's since impressed staffers and volunteers with her sunny personality and interest in everything going on around her, from the pettings humans keep showering on her to the yummy squeeze-up treats she'll never refuse. Though she can be shy at first, she did awesome on her behavior exam and has been deemed to be a great fit for pretty much any kind of household. Looking for a spunky little lady to lift your spirits and keep you amused with her silly antics? Introduce yourself to Biscuit at the Manhattan Care Center today!

258100.name: Soccerball
258100.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Soccerball needs at risk placement for medical reasons. He is a sweet, young cat with a poor appetite due to a severe upper respiratory tract infection. He needs supportive care in a veterinary clinic in order to recover.

A volunteer writes:
Soccerball is a handsome gent found in a large hospital parking lot. A worker spotted him three days in a row and decided to bring him to safety. Soccerball is quite a catch, sparkling white with an all ebony coiffe crowning his beautiful head. Soccerball likes to lounge and sometimes can be found in a deep sleep. Tap on his shoulder and he will be ready for his meet and greet!Indeed, Soccerball is a friendly and welcoming kitty, super playful too and the good thing, he does not get overstimulated and enjoys petting while playing. Soccerball's SNAP test was found positive for FeLV, an immunological condition that predisposes cats to infections as well as other medical issues and can shorten their lifespan. It is only contagious to other cats. Therefore FeLV+ cats should be the only pet in the house or live with other cats with the same condition. Soccerball's diagnosis should be confirmed or discarded by other tests that will need to be done by an outside veterinarian. Soccerball is so worth to meet and if your household meets his needs, why not considering him as your forever best friend? 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Soccerball is a cat's cat who is sweet, friendly, and knows who he is! He was in a deep sleep, but with enough petting, he woke up and was very curious, ate treats, and enjoyed petting. In time, he was coaxed down with a squeeze-up treat and was at the front eating it while continuing to enjoy petting on his head, cheeks, and along his back. He struggled a bit during the pick-up, but he allowed himself to be picked up and held in the assessor's arms. When he was set back down, he resumed eating and being his calm and curious self.

Soccarball interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

258101.name: Purrfect
258101.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Purrfect's world turned very imperfect when his owner went into care, leaving behind seventeen kitties and doggies. Nothing is known about these former pets. Purrfect was kind of lost and for days, hiding at the back of his cubby and wary of visits from staff and volunteers. Time often does its job as well as the enrichment provided to the cats in our care. Purrfect, today, timidly, treats helping, decided that it was ok for him to trust me as I spoke softly to him and moved my hand toward his head. He gently and slowly head bunted me and rolled on his side, moving forward to get more in depth petting. I was sooo happy! This is the beginning of starting a new life as a loving, trusting and happy pet. Of course, more time is needed for Purrfect to reach his full potentials but an understanding owner or foster and a home sweet home will  give him the chance he needs to just do that. Purrfect is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.




What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Purrfect has made lovely improvements since his first assessment and was lying quietly on the shelf in the loaf position. He was curious, sniffed treats, began eating them, and enjoyed all petting, leaning in very nicely for cheek rubs and remaining calm when petted along his back, arching it slightly. He remained in place, was very sweet, and gave a little meow when first approached. He may need some time to warm up to his new home.

Purrfect interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

258102.name: Purrrisan
258102.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

A volunteer writes: Our little three-year-old Purrrisan really is a bit of a toothless wonder. This little charcoal-and-white girl with a dainty pink nose makes good use of her paws (and claws), poking them out of her space to buttonhole visitors. At first I misunderstood her intentions. Then I realized she was simply trying to catch my attention - or, more accurately, to catch me - and pull me over. It turns out she's addicted to head rubs and would do almost anything to force her way into my arms. She did make quite a mess of her space - so intent was she on claiming me each time I passed that, in her rush to do so, she knocked over her food and water and scattered her litter. Purrrisan is a lovely little cuddle bug who also enjoys a furry mouse toy and would make someone an enthusiastic playmate and pal.

258103.name: Catana
258103.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home! Catana tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: Catana's upstairs shelter neighbors are a group of boisterous kittens constantly engaged in their perfectly adorable kitten chaos. They are just learning about the world and do all sorts of entertaining antics. This particular group is keen to get your attention and they probably will, but this isn't about them. This is about Catana who patiently waits to be noticed herself. At ten years old she knows enough about the world to know that she has to do a little more to stand out and she wants to, but it's much easier said than done. Catana was brought to us with many other cats and dogs when their guardian went into care. We don't have many details about her life before but she welcomed me, tentatively at first but then much more warmly. Catana was in and out of her box bed sharing light snuggles and a hope that someone will notice her too.

258106.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Pumpkin is on the at risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and is deteriorating in the Adoptions room. He is now displaying consistent and escalated distance increasing behaviors such as hissing, swatting and lunging. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.
