258108.name: Crumb
258108.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Crumb is a pretty Tortie gal who came to us with her two babies as their family was displaced. She  was brought with lovely comments:friendly, affectionate, loves to be brushed, makes biscuits and cuddles with her owners at night.....Crumb would be shy, though and needs to warm up to new people and new situations and we have experienced this with her at the care center. Crumb acts reserved but once she knows you, she might want to come in your arms. She head bunts gently, purrs softly and is all together a sweet and well mannered kitty. Crumb is apparently healthy, is already spayed, did very well on her behavior evaluation and could go home today! So, ask to meet her when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!








I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Crumb was on top of the den, looking slightly wary but sweet. She sniffed treats and then allowed petting while remaining fairly neutral. She loves squeeze-up treats and would raise her tail somewhat with lower back petting and seemed to enjoy cheek rubs and petting on her head. She was calm when a little upward pressure was exerted on her abdomen as a partial pick-up and continued eating during the partial pick-up and while being pet. She's just slightly shy and could not be coaxed off the den, but she's very sweet. Then, to the assessor's surprise, when she was finished with her squeeze-up, she jumped down and came forward, allowed herself to be picked up and held, remained fairly calm, and remained so when set back down. She continued to eat more squeeze-up at the front of the kennel.

Crumb interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

258110.name: Ducky
258110.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Ducky is not one to hide! She is upfront and center in her kennel ready for treats and cuddles! Despite the ordeal she shared with sixteen of her housemates, Ducky seems to see "the glass half full" and decided to make the best of the situation she is now in. Yes, she had a home and an owner, just yesterday and she sadly lost it all...Ducky is a girly girl, so cute and friendly, easy going, calm, gracious and well, she stole my heart...Ducky is a twelve year old senior gal who does have as expected some medical issues related to her age(she does have though an unremarkable bloodwork), aced her behavior evaluation, is already spayed and could go home today where she could, safe and loved, spend her golden years. Come and meet this lovely lady...today at the Manhattan Care Center.







What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.

Splitzy is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

258136.name: Mumble
258136.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Mumble tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.,/p>

A volunteer writes: Someone put Mumble outside in a carrier and left him. Someone else saw and brought him to their porch where Mumble didn't want to leave his carrier no matter what was put in front of him and though we're kind of seeing the same thing, there's a difference now. With a little extra patience, Mumble's shown himself to be very sweet though also very unsure.  Mumble comes out of his hidey box for treats and will very sweetly accept some pets. We know Mumble's been through a lot and asking for the chance he needs hasn't really been his thing, but we sure hope you'll come and give him a chance.

258138.name: Baby Blue
258138.summary:
My foster writes: This sweet Baby Blue was sadly left in a carrier outside the shelter, but he hasn't let his rough start stop him from being loving and playful.
He loves greeting you at the door and when you wake up, and he's happiest when he's around his humans. He has plenty of energy for wand-toy play sessions and is always up for some fun! He enjoys head scratches and affection on his own terms, and he's a big fan of dry food and treats. He uses his litter box everyday with no incident and he loves to groom himself.
He's not much of a climber and is perfectly happy hanging out beside you while also giving you your space. He's a wonderful mix of playful, affectionate, and independent and he's ready for a loving forever home!

A volunteer writes: Left in a carrier outside the shelter gates, Baby Blue would love a chance to turn things around on his own terms. We don't know much of anything about his life before but can say with some confidence that the shelter isn't quite his style. It can be a lot on even our most confident pals and I'd certainly be inclined to describe Baby Blue as such. He very sweetly put his feelings about the shelter to the side in order to come forward to greet me and I fell in love with his greeting. Stretching out into my arms, Baby Blue kneaded his big mittened paws and leaned his head into my hand. Keeping an eye on the shelter happenings might be par for the course at the moment, but I have to admire his openness in the face of all these changes and his determination to find the family he's meant to.

258143.name: Salem
258143.summary:
Meet Salem!
Salem may have had a rocky start after being found abandoned near a police precinct, but this sweet boy is ready to turn the page and find a loving home. While he can be a little shy when meeting new people, Salem has shown that he has a gentle heart and enjoys affection once he feels comfortable. With a little patience and a lot of love, this sweet pup is ready to cast a spell on his forever family.

My Ideal Home
Salem would do best with a patient adopter who understands that confidence takes time to grow. A calm, predictable environment and slow introductions will help him feel safe as he adjusts to his new surroundings. He will thrive with someone who can help him build confidence through positive reinforcement, enrichment, and plenty of encouragement.

Good with Other Pets?
Salem's history with other animals is unknown. During his time at the shelter, he has shown some uncertainty around unfamiliar dogs, so slow and controlled introductions would be the best way to help him feel comfortable. A home without dog parks is recommended so Salem can continue building positive experiences at his own pace.

Good with Kids?
Due to Salem's shy nature and need for gentle interactions, he would do best in a home with adults or older children who can respect his boundaries and give him time to warm up.

Things to Know
Salem is a gentle soul who enjoys quiet moments and taking life one paw at a time. He walks nicely on leash, enjoys treats, and will happily lean in for pets once he feels comfortable. Salem can become anxious in new situations, so a patient adopter who can help him feel safe will be the key to helping this sweet boy blossom. If you're looking for a loyal companion who just needs a little time to let his true colors shine, Salem might be your perfect match!

258174.name: Paula
258174.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Paula is at risk due to behavioral reasons. While in care, Paula has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to flinch at any stimuli and seek exit when the handler attempts to interact. With unfamiliar handlers, Paula takes a considerable amount of time to warm up and will begin taking treats; however, she will maintain her distance. With familiar handlers in the yard, Paula is observed to have a loose and wiggly body. Medically, Paula is apparently healthy.

Paula came to ACC as a stray, so we don't have much information about her prior to coming into our care.  She has been observed to be very fearful in shelter - flinching at most stimuli and often seeking exit.  With a slow approach, she has begun to warm up to familiar handlers.  She will need a quiet low-traffic home where she can decompress and be her best doggy self.

258175.name: Aria
258175.summary:
My foster writes: Aria is true gentle giant with the biggest heart! Aria is a sweet, loving pup who adores people, children, and other dogs. She is incredibly friendly, calm, and affectionate - her favorite thing is being close to her humans. Whether she's cuddling on the couch or resting her head in your lap while you work, Aria just wants to be loved.
Aria is very smart and food motivated. She knows "sit," and picks up on things quickly. She is also great on a leash! She may pull a little when she gets excited, but she is very manageable and enjoys her walks.
Aria is crate trained and is comfortable spending time alone. We left her crated for several hours and she relaxed the whole time. When we came home, she was happy to see us but showed no signs of anxiety.
She loves toys, cuddles, and attention. She is playful but also a professional napper - her large size means she tires out easily and loves to relax after a walk. She currently enjoys three short walks a day and is happy to lounge afterward, making her a great fit for an apartment or home.
Aria would do best with someone who loves having a big, affectionate companion by their side. She is extremely loyal and deserves to be with someone who can fully commit to her.

I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Saturday, July 18 from 11AM - 5PM or Sunday, July 19 from 11AM-4PM, Pop-Up Adoption Event at The Spot BK, 232 Varet St, Brooklyn, NY 11206 (Sponsored by Best Friends Animal Society!). Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

258191.name: Tattoo
258191.summary:
My #Borough Breaker writes:
Tattoo and I had a lovely day in the shady and not so hot weather!Tattoo is an unbelievably sweet boy. He loves treats so much, and quickly learned to shake paws when he realized he'd get a reward! 258194.name: Mika
258194.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Mika is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In Mika's previous home, it was reported that Mika has a multiple bite history due to her stranger danger and resource guarding behavior. Her owner reported Mika can be very affectionate when given the time to get comfortable with new people and environment. Overall she prefers contact on her own terms and will growl, snap, and bite if not followed. She is crate trained and when new people would visit owner would place in crate. While in care, Mika allows limited handling. She has lunged, hard barked, and attempts to bite staff. Medically, Mika is apparently healthy.

Mika was surrendered by her previous owner due to their moving out of the country. Mika was described as having a high energy level and was very affectionate with her family but needs time to get comfortable with new things. Mika is reported to have a multiple-bite history and intense stranger danger. She is reported to not get along with strangers, children, dogs, and cats. Her owner noted that she guards food and will snap when approached while eating. During her intake, Mika escalated to lunging, barking, growling, and snapping at staff and their ankles as she was walked into the building. She also had to be sedated for her medical exam due to her behavior. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Mika be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can provide consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Mika presents with outside of the care centers.

258201.name: Chester The Chunk
258201.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Chester The Chunk interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with any level of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: This deconstructed Adoptions box means the world to Chester the Chunk because even though it's missing some sides, it contains the promise of a forever family. Chester the Chunk will get a new one to go home in, but in the meantime this gentle giant of a cat has tried to make it her very own. She very sweetly came up to welcome me, offering her cheeks in greeting and her heart in friendship. A social and outgoing creamsicle star, if she's worried about not standing out due to her age, she certainly doesn't show it. Chester the Chunk was brought to us without much information after being found waiting on her own for a few days in a building hallway. With no one to claim her as their own, she's come to us where she's been an absolute darling. Chester the Chunk is waiting in her Adoptions box to meet you.

258205.name: Billy Bob
258205.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Billy Bob is at risk due to behavioral reasons. Despite our best efforts at making him comfortable. Billy has been showing signs of stress while in kennel. Such as persistently finger painting his kennel and digging at the transfer door while jumping at it. Billy Bob is noted to display kennel reactivity, pulling towards dogs in kennels. While out of the kennel with handlers Billy is social and allows petting. Medically, Billy Bob is apparently healthy. 

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
Not only do I pull at heart strings, but I also pull on leash! I will need someone to help me with my leash manners.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

A volunteer writes: Talk about laid back, this guy wins the prize. I led Billy Bob out of his kennel yesterday, it was easy as could be. We went to the back yard where we hung out for a long time. This guy is wonderful! It was a hot day, so we didn't do much. BB wandered around a bit, went after a tennis ball a few times (he is not a fetcher type). Now and then he stared at a dog in the next pen. The majority of the time, he hung out with me on or next to the bench. He seemed to like attention and pets. Eventually Billy Bob lay down and went to sleep under my legs. Talk about "chill", this guy gets first prize. Come meet Billy Bob at Manhattan ACC.

258208.name: Roman
258208.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Roman is a sweet, affectionate couch potato who loves nothing more than relaxing by your side. A true velcro dog, he enjoys staying close to his people and consistently remains near his handlers during socialization. He walks nicely on a leash with very little pulling and is happy with one or two 20-minute walks each day. Roman knows "sit" and "down," loves bath time and water, and is always excited to earn a tasty treat. While he has been crate trained, he does not do well when confined and would do best in a home where he can spend plenty of time with his family. If you're looking for a calm, loyal companion who will happily be your shadow, Roman may be the perfect match.

Soraya interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

A volunteer writes: Believing the condo ledge to be merely a suggestion of space, Soraya leans halfway out in order to get all the pets and cuddles she can. Further emphasizing her commitment, Soraya stays close to the ground making it easier to nuzzle into any hand she sees. Soraya has been all welcoming and heartfelt cuddles at the shelter, so I never would've guessed that what came before was so challenging. Found not moving behind a car tire, Soraya clearly needed a little hand. Thankfully the owner of the car scooped her up and brought her inside where she gently meowed to the Good Samaritan on her way to us. Soraya is nothing if not irresistible, so we hope you'll come and meet her at the Queens Care Center.

258244.name: Sirius
258244.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Sirius is on the At Risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display challenging behavior during interactions. He is extremely intelligent and high energy, and needs to expend energy constructively with interactive play sessions 3-4X/day. In addition to playtime, this cat would also benefit from mental exercise from activities such as puzzle toys/games, lick mats, or clicker training. Without providing activity for his mind and body, the cat may react with rough play, potentially resulting in bite/scratch incidents. It is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him/her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with feline body language, overstimulation, rough play, and who have the time to invest in managing these behaviors on a consistent basis to avoid further bite/scratch incidents.

A volunteer writes:
Sirius is a handsome young tiger, healthy, lively, playful, curious and very sociable. So, why is Sirius with us at the care center when he is described by his former owner as  affectionate, talkative, very loving and super funny? Sirius is an energetic  kitty who can at times go overboard(overstimulated), play rough, using mouth and claws and even scratch or nip. He is not neutered and of course that does not help.Sirius was not a happy camper when he first arrived at the care center but time did help. He is always at his door or on his balcony, hoping for a visitor to show up but also trying to avoid boredom as he is stuck in a kennel. As I open his door, I know he wants to come out. I talk to him softly and slow blinks with the same in return. What a beautiful cat he is! Sirius plays excitingly with a feather wand, then genuinely, accepts petting and leans against my hand. Sirius did live at some point with a small dog but we do not know the nature of their relation ship. He never had contact with other cats or children. Sirius deserves a second chance with an experienced owner familiar with overstimulation and able to provide a quiet while stimulating environment for him. Will you be Sirius new teacher and owner? He is waiting, hopeful at the Manhattan Care Center.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

Sirius tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

258245.name: Fubu
258245.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
Fubu appears to be fearful and may not have had much human interaction up to this point. During the assessment he hissed, tried to flee and would benefit from extra socialization. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff. Contact with young children should be avoided or done under strict supervision to prevent provoking a fear response, further delaying socialization. 
While ​Fubu​ may require a slightly slower approach right as he settles in to make sure his positive progress continues, he shows behavior suitable for adopters with an average level of cat experience with cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff. Contact with young children as they are settling in should be limited or under close supervision to ensure continued positive progress. Fubu has a very high energy level and will need a lot of play time in his new home.

258275.summary:

Rosemary is on the at risk list for medical reasons. Rosemary is a sweet, underweight, old cat with some severe bloodwork changes that are suggestive of cancer. She is clinically doing well in shelter (bright, interactive, great appetite), and her bloodwork values and weight have improved, but her long term prognosis remains guarded to poor. Behaviorally, Rosemary is amenable to handling and petting.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

258276.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Dragon Tales is at risk due to behavioral reasons. While in care, Dragon has been observed to be dog and rope reactive. Noted to bark and lunge towards other dogs. During one instance when a handler pulled him away from another dog, Dragon turned and snapped at the handler. Recently, Dragon Tales has also been observed to bite the leash when handlers are attempting to leash him. Noted several times to chew through the handler's leash. When out of kennel with handlers, Dragon Tales is receptive to treats and treat lures. Medically, Dragon Tales has pyoderma.

Dragon Tales arrived at as a stray with no known history. While in care, Dragon has been observed to be dog reactive. Noted to bark and lunge towards other dogs. During one instance when a handler pulled him away from another dog, Dragon turned and snapped at the handler. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

258278.name: Shiloh
258278.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Shiloh was surrendered by his previous owner due to allergies and behavior concerns. His previous family described him as a social, affectionate, vocal, independent, very active, and playful dog who prefers contact on his own terms. He spends most of his time at home in the bedroom or where his people are, enjoys going on long walks, and begs for treats using his paws. He is reported to have bitten multiple times in the home; two bites were reported to be unprovoked, and the other two were to family members who entered a room to check on him. The bites were bites and releases and did break skin. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Shiloh be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner coupled with consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist, as is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Shiloh presents with outside of the care centers.

258302.name: Pond
258302.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Pond!
Pond arrived at ACC as a stray, so her past is a bit of a mystery, but this playful pup is ready to make a splash in someone's life! Pond is an energetic girl who loves exploring her surroundings, meeting new friends, and showing off her silly side. While she may need some time to feel comfortable with new people and handling, she has shown that she can be a sweet and engaging companion once she feels safe. Pond is ready to find a forever home where she can bloom at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Pond would do best with an experienced adopter who can help her build confidence through patience, structure, and positive reinforcement training. She will benefit from daily exercise, enrichment activities, and a calm environment where she can relax and learn that good things are around every corner. With the right person by her side, Pond is sure to become a wonderful companion and make a real splash!

Good with Other Pets?
Pond's history with other animals is unknown, but she has participated in dog introductions at the shelter. She has shown interest in meeting other dogs and can engage in playful behaviors, though she may become overwhelmed during interactions. Slow introductions and continued positive reinforcement will help Pond feel comfortable and successful around canine friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Pond's handling sensitivity and fearful behaviors, an adult only home is recommended at this time. She would do best with people who understand canine body language and will give her the space and time she needs to feel comfortable.

Things to Know
Pond is a fun loving pup who enjoys exploring, treats, and spending time with her favorite people. She is working on feeling more comfortable with handling and learning that she does not need to worry when new things happen. Pond can be a little protective of her favorite toys and treats, so her future family should continue practicing positive reinforcement and trade games. If you're looking for a pup with personality, playfulness, and plenty of potential, Pond may just be the perfect little companion to jump into your life!

258303.name: Junebugg
258303.summary:
Meet Junebugg!
Junebugg was found running loose on the street by himself, and while his history is unknown, he's already shown that he's a sensitive boy who needs a little time and space to feel safe. Once he warms up, he is willing to engage and even takes treats, showing that there's a thoughtful, treat-motivated pup underneath his initial worry.

My Ideal Home
Junebugg would do best in a calm, patient home that can give him slow introductions to new people, places, and routines. He benefits from structure, predictable handling, and positive reinforcement to help him feel secure. A quieter environment without overwhelming stimulation will help him continue to build confidence at his own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
Junebugg's history with other animals is unknown, and he has shown discomfort during initial introductions at the shelter, so careful, controlled introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his sensitivity to handling and new stimuli, Junebugg is recommended for an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Junebugg walks well on leash once outside the kennel and is generally loose-leashed and non-reactive in open environments, though he can be vocal and tense in confined spaces. With time, consistency, and force-free training, Junebugg has strong potential to become more comfortable and trusting in his environment.

Fun Fact
Once Junebugg feels safe, he shows a softer side, especially when cheese is involved, which quickly helps him settle and engage with the world around him.

258305.name: Silvie
258305.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Silvie's owner words:"she is attentive, lovable, a true sweetheart-she is friendly, gently playful and outgoing with all, including kids and cats". Silvie who was surrendered  because her house counted too many pets is withdrawn at the care center, anchored at the back of her cubby and wary to see my hand coming close to her head. No hissing, no swatting just frozen in place. There is so much more to Silvie who by the way gave birth recently(all the babies found a home c/o former owner) and once before. No wonder the little gal is having a hard time although I sensed some improvement at my last visit with her. Silvie is pretty in her little black dress, apparently healthy  and is awaiting her spay(scheduled for the 31st). Silvie has sooo much to give and really should be given the chance at a safe, quiet(without boisterous small children), patient, understanding and loving new home. Come and meet lovely Silvie at the Manhattan Care Center!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I am finding the shelter a bit overwhelming. Outside one-on-one I am a great big cuddle bug.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Sylvie is laying in the back of her kennel, smushing herself close to the back corner, body tense with her front paws tucked under her chest. When the kennel door is opened and she is softly spoken to, she stays unmoving in the back corner. She is tolerant of all petting, remaining tense but leaning in just slightly when she is pet on the head. She is tolerant of the assessor maneuvering her forward and allows them to pick her up, still tense when held but tolerating being held for several seconds without issue otherwise. When she is placed back in her kennel, she returns to the back corner and curls up on herself, tolerating all further petting but remaining frozen in place.

258310.name: Calculator
258310.summary:
**Meet Calculator!**

I'm a sweet kitty looking for a loving home where I can finish recovering from an upper respiratory infection (URI)-the feline version of a common cold. It can cause sneezing, congestion, watery eyes, or a runny nose, but with proper care, rest, and any prescribed medication, many cats recover very well.

A quiet home where I can relax while I heal would be the perfect place for me to thrive.

258325.name: Islander
258325.summary:
My foster writes: Little Islander is a dream kitten! He truly has the best temperament of any kitten I've fostered. He loves to play and get feisty, but will also snuggle up against you, lay on you and purr. He would do great with another cat who wants a playful companion but he also respects the boundaries of others if they aren't in the mood to play. He does great in his carrier and at the vet, and loves being picked up (he starts purring without hesitation).
Because of Islanders past where he came in as a stray with a bad upper respiratory infection, he has permanent scarring on his right eye. After a consultation with an eye specialist, they said he will have the scarring forever but he is not in pain, does not require any medication or surgery, and can still see out of the eye. All this to say, his eye does not hold him back in the slightest and reminds us of what a brave and driven kitten he is.
Please give little Islander a chance, he would be the perfect addition to your family!

258328.name: Lucky Lady
258328.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Lukcy Lady is at risk due to behavior concerns. Lucky Lady has been observed to show dog reactivity and resource guarding. Despite our best efforts to keep her comfortable while in the care center, she has now also begun to show kennel stress. Lucky Lady has been known to kennel fight with dogs walking by her kennel. She is affiliative with handlers and will lean in to solicit attention. Medically, Lucky Lady has alopecia and recently was treated for CIRDC.  

Lucky Lady arrived at MACC as an owner surrender. While in care, she has been obsvered to be highly kennel reactive. Noted to pull hard towards the other dogs in the kennel room. She will also fixate on other dogs while on leash. In her previous owner Lucky was reported to have a high level of resource guarding, handling sensitivity, and on leash reactivity. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

258331.name: Musa
258331.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Musa was inside the den, appearing somewhat fearful with a hunched body and large pupils. He hissed when approached with the treat bag but then sniffed the treats. He was then offered squeeze-up, which he ate from the tube before sticking his head out of the den to lick it from a bowl. At this point, he started licking squeeze-up repeatedly from the assessor's finger and allowed brief touch and petting, pulling back slightly each time. He's a sweet cat who needs some time to warm up to his new home.


Musa tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.
	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

258337.name: Shannon
258337.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am not one to sit still and will love interactive playtime in my new home!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

A volunteer writes: Shannon's first impressions simply can't be overstated. I met him when I was reading to one of his neighbors and, wanting to participate in the story, he began rolling over to show me his belly like and batting at a toy suspended from his condo ceiling. I glanced over making eye contact and Shannon was at the front, hoping to share a proper greeting and make a friend. Nuzzles, cuddles, kneading, and joy I was in love, but Shannon's well known around the Care Center for his dedication to exploring. Trying to hop out seems to be one of his ways of making friends. We don't know much about his life before as he was brought to us by police when he was seen in a building stairwell. Not one to dwell on that, he's hopeful that someone will share with him another chance. Come in and meet Shannon today as he's sure to win your heart.

258339.name: Princess Nina
258339.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Princess Nina is on the At Risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and is deteriorating in the Adoptions room. She is now displaying signs of overstimulation. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Princess Nina tolerates attention and petting when well fed but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter and can act aggressively when very hungry as a result of a medical condition detailed above.   Until her illness is controlled we suggest that she be fed before handling is attempted or whenever handling is going to be attempted when she is very vocal or appears to be aroused or upset. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents who are well counseled in her medical concerns and the need to get her hyperthyroidism under control.

A volunteer writes:
Princess Nina, owned since kittenhood, became very unhappy when another female cat was brought in to share her life. She acted up toward the "intruder" and even started to soil(something she does not do at the care center). Princess Nina was therefore brought to us in order to find her a new place to live. A tall order when a cat is fourteen year old, has an untreated known thyroid condition and has even the beginning of kidney disease. Princess Nina is a sweet gal and we will try our best to help her....She is a pretty kitty, semi long hair, matted, all ebony dame, very welcoming, friendly and enjoying attention and petting.. Her stay in a kennel though started to take a toll on her and she is often antsy when someone opens her kennel, giving at times a little swat or a hiss. Princess Nina is super thin and as hungry as a bear. The thyroid medicine will soon do its job, relax her, lessen her appetite and promote some weight gain !Lovely Princess Nina needs a home sweet home, may be low traffic, without other cats or pets and an understanding new owner who likes seniors who quite often come with medical issues. Princess Nina would love to meet you and be your four legged best friend!

258342.name: Rainbow Dash
258342.summary:
My foster writes:
Ever given your whole self to a relationship only to be left all alone and no longer young? This is where dear Rainbow Dash finds herself in her later years, found wandering the streets after likely once having a family/home. Her body suggests she has birthed many litters. Her intimidating exterior is just a front - she's the sweetest and most affectionate soul around.
Rainbow Dash is the perfect apartment dog and made herself right at home during her 4 day straycation out of the shelter. She doesn't need a lot of space or activity other than a comfy couch or chair. As a heavy-duty low rider, and mature mama, her ability to jump on/off furniture (and people) is limited. She likes to keep her walks on the short side, and is crate trained and a potty pro. Other than snoring and snuffling as she dozes, she isn't very vocal. She is happy to keep an eye on you rather than chase you around when you are busy but she is very affectionate, smushing next to you whenever possible. She tucks in for the night around 9:15 and if you dawdle she will put herself to bed.
Rainbow Dash was excellent during her straycation living with an 11yr old, immediately affectionate and laid her head on the kid's lap, eager and affectionate in all her interactions with humans. She enjoys all pets and snuggles! She seems to be interested in other dogs around her size, likely wanting to play/socialize. She doesn't appear to enjoy small dogs, particularly those who tend to bark/lunge at her.
She was great in the bath - calm and compliant even if not thrilled. Good in the car (for a short drive). She takes doggie treats very sweetly, and is very interested in people food (especially cheese). She will sit attentively and silently beg (no whining or scratching).


A volunteer writes: We imagine right about now you could use a little sunshine on this stormy, gloomy day. Maybe even a rainbow would appear...A Rainbow Dash perhaps? This ten year old short stack is always my ray of light when I'm at the shelter, she has the biggest personality and is so, so cute! Whether participating in our recent hot dog eating contest, cooling off in the pool or even being the first to try out the new bench we have in the yard, Rainbow Dash is always up for anything!

258345.name: Gudetama
258345.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Gudetama is a very quiet and well mannered kitty but unlike the cartoon character, he is no lazy "egg". It is just that when one is stuck in a kennel in order to heal better, it is difficult to jump, run and do zoomies. Gudetama has lots of love to give and he gets plenty in return as everybody loves him in the medical room. He plays nicely with feather wands, stretches, makes biscuits and is always available for cuddles. Gutetama got bitten by another animal, likely a free roaming cat.  He was brought to us with a few bites, the larger one being on one of his thighs and healing, slowly but surely. As soon as the veterinary team gives the green light, Gudetama could be fostered or adopted under veterinary and DOH surveillance((DOH stipulations for follow up are available from the veterinary department) for the rest of his home quarantine that will end at the end of December 2026. Gudetama is a fabulous kitty, sweet, friendly and loving. It would be wonderful for him to find the safety and the warmth of a home sweet home after the ordeal he lived through. Gudetama is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.





What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!

Hi there! My name is Gudetama! I arrived as a stray so the staff don't know what my life was like before coming to ACC, but I had various injuries that I'm recovering from really well. I only require a little extra paperwork to be filled out and a few extra vet visits this year because one of my injuries was likely a bite wound. I'm thankful for everyone at ACC taking such good care of me, but I think I'd like to find my forever home now. So what are you waiting for? Ask about me today!

258358.name: Swizzel
258358.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Twizzle and Swizzle are two lovely youngsters who will pull at your heartstrings. A Good Samaritan found them, abandoned in a park together with a small dog we named Pretzel. Twizzle and Swizzle are one of a kind. They have cerebellar hypoplasia(CH), a non progressive neurological condition that makes them wobbly and prone to fall(this is why we placed bathmats in their kennels and provided special accommodations so they do not slip). CH per se does not shorten a cat's lifespan. They are eating and drinking well and using their litter box. T and S like each other and even share a ball at times. They are playful and quite friendly, enjoying treats and cuddles. They like to do all the things young cats enjoy but of course, their environment has to be made safe for them so they do not hurt themselves. Twizzle and Swizzle are really cute Tabbies, full of life, friendly and always ready to meet new friends. Both little girls are awaiting their spay, did very well on their behavior evaluation and are hoping to start very soon a new page in their life with you! Come and meet them very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!

Swizzel is at the front of the kennel as the assessor approaches, eyes wide as she observes the area around her. Swizzel does have cerebellar hypoplasia, causing her to be unsteady and wobbly throughout the assessment. This does not appear to be affecting her behavior and she exhibits a friendly, social demeanor during the interaction. When the kennel door is opened, she meows softly, leaning forward to head bunt the assessor's hand and lean into all petting. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm and making air biscuits as she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting. 

Swizzel interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

258394.name: June Bug
258394.summary:
Meet June Bug

June Bug is a sweet, medium-sized girl who is still learning that the world can be a safe place. The shelter has been a scary experience for her, and it often takes her time to gather the courage to leave her kennel. Once she's out, you'll quickly see that what she wants most is comfort and reassurance.

June Bug is looking for a calm, patient home where she can continue to gain confidence at her own pace. A predictable routine, gentle encouragement, and lots of kindness will help her blossom. While she may not be the dog who rushes up to greet new people, those who give her the time she needs will have the opportunity to watch her transform into a devoted and loving companion.

If you have room in your heart for a dog who just needs someone to believe in her, June Bug is ready to begin that journey with you.

She is very loving and will curl up on the couch or politely chat with you while you cook. She enjoys gently playing with toys, watching the world through windows, and LOTS of treats! Chocolate will make the most wonderful addition to any home looking for a kitty to love.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

258416.name: Goldiepot
258416.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
Goldiepot is standing at the front of the kennel, body and eyes relaxed and meowing softly to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she leans forward, firmly head bunting the assessor's hand. She allows and leans into all petting, purring, making biscuits, and raising her back as she is pet. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm and continuing to purr as she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting, giving the assessor a very soft, gentle nip on the hand without pressure as she continues to head bunt the assessor's hand (appearing to be social behavior rather than indicative of overstimulation.) She continues to allow and lean into all petting for the remainder of the interaction, body remaining relaxed and continuing to purr.

Goldiepot interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

258418.name: Solitare
258418.summary:
Solitare interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience. 

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Solitare is on the at-risk list for medical concerns. Solitare is one of 5 kittens in a litter that has been diagnosed with ringworm. Ringworm is difficult to effectively treat and manage in the current shelter population due to overpopulation, staffing, resources. Placement would include topical and oral treatment as well as veterinary follow-up. 

Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconozole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

Jimmy interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. Although Jimmy did not escalate further, he does appear to have a high energy level and his swaying tail can potentially be an indicator of overstimulation. For this reason, in an overabundance of caution, we recommend that he go to a home with adopters with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in feline body language and overstimulation in cats. 258457.name: Dexter
258457.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Dexter and friend Cairo came to us as their owner going through very difficult times became unable to care for them. It is tough for older cats to leave behind a lifetime of love and habits to find themselves in a cage. So much is asked from these former pets to act as they were perfect or almost perfect when they heart aches sooo much. Dexter was a bit shy when I first met him two days after his arrival at the care center. I could see, though that there was a lovely cat in him, just waiting to show for himself. And there he was as in his video, happy to feel loved again, rolling, making biscuits and head bunting my hand. I really like Dexter who might be less extroverted than Cairo but a cat with the promise to bring lots of love to his new family! Dexter is already neutered, seems reasonably healthy(he does have senior teeth, though) and his behavior evaluation  is the witness of his initial weariness. Dexter's bag is ready.... Just come and meet him and....take him home!









What my friends at ACC say about me:
Dexter has shown dramatic improvement since his first assessment and is now curious, sweet, and friendly. He was on top of the shelf, curious and interested in treats, and was easily coaxed down into the main kennel when offered more of them. He enjoyed all petting, leaning in gently for cheek rubs, and remained calm. He struggled when picked up, but he was reasonably tolerant of the experience and didn't escalate. After being set back down, he resumed his curious and sweet self.

Dexter interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience but should be counseled on his prior fearfulness..
I can go home today!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

258459.name: Little  Prince
258459.summary:
Meet Little Prince!

Little Prince came to ACC as an owner surrender and is looking for a patient, experienced home where he can feel safe and understood. He can be a little cautious with handling and may become defensive when frightened or startled, so he needs someone who will respect his boundaries and give him time to build trust. He has a sweet side and was social and easy to walk when he first arrived at ACC.

My Ideal Home

Little Prince would do best with an experienced, adult-only adopter who understands canine body language and is comfortable working with a dog who can be sensitive to handling. A calm, predictable home with positive-reinforcement training will help him feel more secure. He should have his own space and should never be forced into handling or have valued items taken from him without a safe trade.

Good with Kids?

No. Due to Little Prince's potential for defensive behavior when frightened and his resource guarding history, ACC recommends an adult-only home.

Good with Other Pets?

Little Prince's history with other pets is unknown. A recent dog introduction showed increasing tension, so he is recommended for a single-pet home and should not visit dog parks.

Overall Health

Little Prince is an older gentleman with some ongoing medical needs, including chronic eye disease and dental concerns. He recently recovered from a respiratory infection and will benefit from continued veterinary follow-up, particularly for his eyes.

Behavior Determination

Level 4 - Experienced, adult-only, single-pet home. Little Prince has a history of resource guarding and can be fearful and sensitive to handling. He has previously escalated quickly when frightened, including lunging and snapping during a veterinary exam, so his adopter should be prepared to use calm, reward-based handling and work with a qualified behavior professional.

Other Fun Facts

Little Prince enjoys treats and toys and will happily follow along when he feels comfortable. He can walk nicely on leash and, with a patient approach and plenty of positive reinforcement, may show you the affectionate companion hiding beneath his cautious exterior.

258464.name: Mirabella
258464.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Mirabella!
Mirabella is a playful pup who came to ACC when her owner could no longer care for her. This sweet girl has a fun, wiggly personality and loves exploring her surroundings. She may be a little independent at first, but once she gets comfortable, her silly and affectionate side shines through. Mirabella is ready to find a family who will enjoy all the fun and love she has to offer.

My Ideal Home
Mirabella would thrive with an adopter who enjoys an active, playful companion and is excited to continue working on her manners. She will benefit from daily exercise, enrichment activities, and positive reinforcement training to help her practice polite greetings and channel her enthusiasm in fun ways. With a little guidance, Mirabella is ready to be your new adventure buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
Mirabella has experience living with other dogs and has shown friendly and playful behaviors during dog introductions at ACC. She enjoys meeting canine friends and has shown a loose, wiggly play style, though she may benefit from continued guidance to help her practice polite interactions. Slow introductions are always recommended to make sure everyone feels comfortable and happy.

Good with Kids?
Mirabella lived with children in her previous home, but due to her enthusiastic play style and jumping, a home without very young children under 5 is recommended. Older children who are comfortable around an energetic dog may be a great match with proper introductions.

Things to Know
Mirabella is a fun loving pup who brings plenty of wiggles and personality wherever she goes! She can get excited when greeting people and may jump up to say hello, but she is eager to engage and ready to learn. If you're looking for a playful companion who will keep you smiling, Mirabella may be the perfect match to add a little extra sparkle to your life.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Brooklyn is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Brooklyn's owner reported that he had never left the home prior to arriving at the Care Centers. Since intake, Brooklyn has displayed fearful, defensive behaviors. He has been observed growling, hard barking, and thrashing when being placed into the kennel. During walks, he has pancaked and remained fearful throughout the outing. His owner noted that he was social with both children and adults within the home. Medically, Brooklyn has pyoderma.

In the Care Centers, Brooklyn is extremely fearful. He was noted to pancake, grow and hard stare when staff attempt to remove him from the kennel. When he is removed he remains fearful and anxious, pancaking on walks. His owner stated, Brooklyn never went outside for walks. He is social with the children and adults in the home. Brooklyn should go to a home through a New Hope partner that can manage his behaviors using positive reinforcement.

258492.name: Zoolander
258492.summary:
Meet Zoolander!
Zoolander came to ACC when his owner could no longer care for him. He's a fun-loving, outgoing pup who greets life with enthusiasm! He loves people, enjoys playtime, and is always ready for his next adventure. Shelter life has been a little overwhelming at times, and his excitement can get the best of him, but beneath it all is a friendly dog looking for an active family to help him channel his energy in positive ways.

My Ideal Home
Zoolander is looking for an active, experienced home that can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He will benefit from learning polite manners, especially around greetings and walking on leash when he's excited. A family committed to continuing his training will help him thrive and bring out his very best.

Good with Kids?
Due to his exuberant play style, social over-arousal, and sensitivity to handling around his neck, Zoolander is recommended for a home with children 13 years and older.

Good with Other Pets?
Zoolander previously lived successfully with other dogs and was described as friendly, outgoing, and playful. In the shelter, he remained appropriate during a dog introduction, greeting another dog calmly through a barrier. He may do well with a compatible canine companion after slow introductions. His previous owner described him as curious about cats.

Overall Health
Zoolander is healthy overall. He has mild dental tartar and gingivitis, and our veterinary team recommends a dental evaluation after adoption.

Behavior Determination Level 4 - Experienced Adopters. Zoolander is a friendly, social dog who becomes easily overstimulated when excited. He will do best with adopters who can continue reward-based training to build his impulse control, teach calm behaviors, and respect his sensitivity to handling around his neck.

Other Fun Facts
Zoolander loves squeaky toys, enjoys fruit as a treat, and has an adorable habit of carrying his leash around in his mouth! He has a playful, goofy personality and is sure to keep his future family smiling with his enthusiasm for life.

I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Saturday, August 8 | 12PM - 4PM with the Animal Welfare Caucus at 1199 Elton St, Brooklyn, NY 11239 . Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Nintendo tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She will likely need time to warm up to his/her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconozole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

258502.name: Marble
258502.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Young Marble (he is only one year old) came with a bunch of his littermates as their house counted too many cats. Marble was scared when he arrived at the care center but consolable with gentle words. Now, he got used to his hopefully temporary settings and although still shy, he comes forward(see his VIDEOS) and enjoys very much company and petting. Marble is truly a sweet and endearing little guy like all the members of his feline family. Nothing much is known about him or his siblings but he will likely be a very sweet pet to have in the home and for many years to come. Marble is apparently healthy and will be neutered before to leave us . He did quite well on his behavioral evaluation(pointing only to his timid side in the shelter environment) and is ready to meet his new family. Ask about Marble when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center.








What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

258511.name: Soot Sprite
258511.summary: Soot Sprite is an elegant addition to his future domicile. His medium-gray coat has a silver lustre that compliments his pale green eyes. He blinks, eventually. His magnificent rabbit ears are almost as long as his graceful rabbit legs. Soot Sprite will show you his legs and tummy at soonest convenience, before, during, and after some serious snuggles. Soot Sprite has stayed under a handkerchief tucked around him, knowing the kerchief meant cuddle time would soon resume. He needs time and touch (and space away from touch) to decompress from his mysterious past then the Soot Sprite will show his personality. So far he enjoys catnip, a crinkle kick toy, and a bouncy ball. Whether you need a naps coach or you're well into your journey of rest, Soot Sprite will be purring at your side.

258518.name: Bluee
258518.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bluee is at risk due to behavioral reasons. When Bluee initially arrived at the care center, he was observed to be social and friendly. Despite our best efforts at keeping Bluee comfortable while in care, he has begun to show signs of kennel stress. He has been reported to jump repeatedly at the door of his kennel, and this behavior is not easily redirected. He is also observed to leash bite and barrel roll in the hallway outside his kennel. Bluee has been receptive to treats and is affiliative with handlers. Medically, Bluee is apparently healthy.

Bluee came into the care center as a stray due to this his behavioral history in a home environment in unknown. In the care center Bluee has not adjusted well to the care center environment,Bluee displays a low threshold for arousal and poor leash skills, with intense barking/jumping in his kennel and frequent hard pulling, vocalizing, and attempts to move toward dogs and people while on leash. He has also been reported to leash bite and barrel roll in the hallway. He has allowed handler to pet and engage with him. He would benefit from structured, force-free handling and management with distance from triggers. Bluee is available for rescue through one of our new hope partners.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Flash is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. Flash entered the care center as a stray. While in care Flash has fearful and arousal behaviors. While on a walk Flash started to leash bite and lunged forward to staff member. Additional staff were needed to assist to return to care center. Flash in the care center is generally fearful of his surroundings and having a hard time regulating his arousal. Flash does solicit attention, social, and playful when in low-stress areas in the offices or yard areas with staff. Medically, Flash is apparently healthy.

Flash was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Flash intially was highly fearful during his stay in care, staying at the back of his kennel with a tense body and trembling. Once out of the kennel, he would mostly maintain his distance but has approached handlers when given time, moving at his pace, and through reward-based interactions. Flash has warmed up to handlers as his length of stay has progressed. He has recently begun to leash-bite. He did have one occasion where he escalated to lunging at a staff member after becoming aroused. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Flash be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can allow him the time and space to acclimate and decompress on his own terms.

Once out of the kennel, he would mostly maintain his distance but has approached handlers when given time, moving at his pace, and through reward-based interactions. Flash has warmed up to handlers as his length of stay has progressed. He has recently begun to leash-bite. He did have one occasion where he escalated to lunging at a staff member after becoming aroused. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Flash be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner that can allow him the time and space to acclimate and decompress on his own terms.

258532.name: Sadie
258532.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
A volunteer writes: Cow-spotted Sadie arrived at the Care Center because her former person was moving. The change in her living situation left her down in the dumps, and at first she seemed to prefer facing away from the staffers and volunteers who wanted to get to know her. Slowly she's seemed to open up more--accepting crunchy kibble and squeeze-ups and allowing lots of pettings as well. She's been purring and head bunting too, and we're hoping her sadness is lifting. This is a calm, sensitive lady who has had her world turned upside down and is doing her best to adjust. She'd love to find forever pet parents as tender as she is, who appreciate her low-key nature and love of pettings. Sound like your kind of cat? Meet this beautiful girl today!

Sadie is laying in her cubby, getting up and greeting the assessor at the front of the cubby with a soft head bunt when the door is opened. She allows all petting and is able to be coaxed to the main area of the kennel, hesitating for a brief moment before exiting the cubby and coming forward. She allows and leans into all petting, purring as she is pet. Sadie is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front of the kennel, allowing all further petting with her tail held high. 

Although Sadie started out very shy and shut down, she has warmed up well throughout her stay at the care center! She interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and leans into all petting. We recommend that Sadie go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in decompression and new home adjustment.

258545.name: Sky
258545.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Sky!
Sky lost her home when her owner could no longer care for her, and she's looking for a patient person who will help her feel safe and comfortable again. This sweet girl may take some time to warm up in new situations, but when she feels comfortable, she enjoys gentle affection and will happily lean in for cheek rubs. Sky is ready to find a home where she can relax, decompress, and be loved at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Sky would do best with an experienced, patient adopter who understands canine body language and will give her the time and space she needs to build trust. A calm, predictable environment and positive, reward-based training will help Sky feel more confident as she adjusts to her new home.

Good with Other Pets?
Sky previously lived with another dog, but she has limited experience with unfamiliar dogs. She would benefit from slow, thoughtful introductions and should not visit dog parks at this time.

Good with Kids?
Sky would do best in an adult-only home where her boundaries can be respected and she can continue building confidence in a calm environment.

Things to Know
Sky is a medium-energy pup who enjoys walks and spending time with her people. She can be sensitive when it comes to handling and prefers to make the first move when meeting new friends. She also feels strongly about her favorite things, including food, treats, and toys, so her future family should use positive reinforcement and careful management around her special treasures. If you're looking for a loyal companion who will reward your patience with trust and affection, Sky may be your perfect match.

258546.name: Socky
258546.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Socky was surrendered into care due to his previous owner leaving the country. His previous owner described him as affectionate and enjoyed cuddling with his family during quality time. He is noted to not be picky with food or treats and plays with most forms of toys. During his stay in care, Socky has been highly fearful and shut down. He does not walk when removed from the kennel and will remain frozen in place. Due to his level of fearfulness, we recommend an adult-only home for Socky through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home after he has had time to decompress and acclimate at his own pace.

258558.name: M & M
258558.summary:
A volunteer writes:
M&M(formerly Tootsie) is a sweetheart with a frown....He certainly has reasons to be unhappy as he was left behind when is family was displaced. He was alone for days and fed by the super of his building. M&M does not hold any grudge, though. He was a sweetheart when he arrived at the care center and even with the veterinary team. As soon as someone shows up at his door, he comes out to salute his visitor, head bunts gently and purrs. He is really a cute cat with his grey and white semi long hair coat, a bit thin and in need of a good brushing for his matted hair. What a beauty he will be after a good home spa and proper nutrition! M&M is in need of some TLC that I bet wonderful adopters will be happy to provide. He is already neutered, aced his behavior evaluation and could go home today with you. Come and meet M&M very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!

258560.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, July 19th from 11AM-4PM, Pop-Up Adoption Event at The Spot BK, 232 Varet St, Brooklyn, NY 11206 (Sponsored by Best Friends Animal Society!). Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!



A volunteer writes:
Twins Leo and Lex, two handsome Gingers were brought to us as their family moved to a place not allowing pets. Not much is known about them except that they lived with other cats and dogs and did not have much dealing with strangers or children. No wonder the pair is on the very shy side since their arrival in a large city shelter! Lex is a bit more timid than his brother Leo but allows some hand petting. No hissing, no swatting, he just makes himself a bit smaller...Lex seems to like to play, though and a feather wand gets him all excited(see pictures). A little bit more time seems to be needed to get Lex out of his shell. An experienced new owner who can picture Lex past lifestyle and understands how it can affect his behavior at the shelter and the need for time and patience to acclimate to a new home, is what Lex very much needs. May be it could be with you? I bet his brother Leo would love to be adopted with him.....

I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.

258566.name: Molly
258566.summary:
Molly is a sweet, social, and affectionate girl who loves being close to her people. She naturally prefers to spend her time wherever her family is, making her a wonderful companion for someone looking for a loyal canine friend.

Molly knows how to sit and offer her paw when a treat is involved, so she's food-motivated and may enjoy continuing her training with positive reinforcement. With consistency and rewards, she has the potential to learn even more.

Molly will require some follow-up care with a vet as she has some dental issues which caused her to have an abscess on her face which we are monitoring in care. 

If you're looking for an affectionate companion who enjoys spending time by your side, taking leisurely walks, and riding along on car trips, Molly may be the perfect match for you!

258605.name: Snow Cone
258605.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Snow Cone is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Snow Cone has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and has escalated towards handlers during attempts to return him to the kennel. While he readily accepted treats during his behavior assessment and played with plush toys, he was noted to grumble and move away during the toy portion of his assessment. Snow Cone pancakes, and when leash pressure is applied, he snarled and lunged at a handler, requiring him to be double leashed to be placed in his kennel safely. Medically, Snow Cone is matted, overweight, and has dermatitis.

Snow Cone was surrendered as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Snow Cone initially presented as easy to remove from the kennel, accepted treats with a soft mouth, but did begin guarding a toy on his handling assessment. When returned to the kennel, Snow Cone pancakes and is reluctant to move despite being offered treats or coaxed by handlers. He has escalated to growling, snarling, and lunging, requiring him to be double leashed to be put back into his kennel safely. Due to these concerns, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I don't always like to share my toys with others.

A volunteer writes: Flower Power just wanted a job, so she walked into a store and handed them her kitty resume only to be told they weren't hiring. Rejection is always tough so she hid in the basement for a little while and then was very kindly brought to us where we gently explained that she could be on a path to find her forever family. Flower Power's still determined to use this chance to demonstrate her strengths and does so at every turn. She's amazing at introductions and happily walked out onto my lap to say as much. She's amazing at all pipe cleaner feather games and reaches her paws out wide to fully participate. If you love a self starter as much as we do, we think you'll really like to meet Flower Power.

258640.name: Chewsday
258640.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Chewsday is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Chewsday has not acclimated well to the shelter environment despite best efforts to keep her comfortable. She has intermittently refused to walk once removed from the kennel, needing prolonged periods of coaxing and treats to successfully get her out of the building for walks or interactions. In her kennel, she has alternated between coming forward for treats but then retreating during leashing. As her length of stay progressed, Chewsday began leash biting and escalated to snapping and attempting to bite when staff/handlers are in the process of removing her from the kennel and, on another occasion, immediately upon exiting the kennel. Medically, Chewsday is being treated for CIRDC, has dental disease, a healing wound, and is considered geriatric.

Chewsday was surrendered as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Chewsday has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. She has escalated to hard barking, growling, snapping at feet, and attempting to bite a handler's foot when trying to remove her from her kennel for a walk. Once out of kennel, she has been reluctant to walk and has been reported to leash bite. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Noted to jump up towards the leash during the jog portion of the assessment. He has also been reported to balk while on leash. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

A volunteer writes: A Good Samaritan left their house to go to work one morning and saw Coriolanus huddled in the corner of the hallway. When they returned later that evening, Coriolanus was still there, unmoving and unsure about what was to happen next. With no one to claim him as their own, the Good Samaritan brought him to us where Coriolanus started out a little bit unsure still. This is understandable but even though his story is full of gaps, we know there's more to the story here. When I first saw Coriolanus, he was simply radiating joy as he played with his toy. Lovingly holding it to his face with perfectly puffed cheeks, I wanted nothing more than to join in but Coriolanus told me in not so many words he wasn't looking for that.
