258674.name: Linda Cod
258674.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Linda Cod is a pretty tabby/calico gal, only one year old who came with her 3 self sufficient kittens from a house full of kitties. Nothing else is known about her... Linda was pretty shy from the start and kind of lost her appetite for a while. All these changes(plus a cold) are traumatic for a delicate cat's brain...Linda Cod feels better, is eating well again and is back to her lovely and sweet self. She is well mannered and enjoys gentle words and petting(see her video). Linda did well on her behavior evaluation and is already spayed. She is ready to go home with you...today! Come and meet Linda Cod very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!







Linda Cod is laying in her den, head up, eyes wide, pupils dilated and ears forward as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and she is softly spoken to, she stays in her laying position and lip licks a few times. Petting is attempted with the scratcher tool, and she tolerates petting on the head and cheeks without issue. With more soft talk, Linda Cod begins kneading, returning a slow blink. She tolerates all petting with the assessor's hand, remaining slightly tense but leaning in when pet on the head and cheeks. She is unable to be coaxed out of the den, so full pickup is unable to be attempted. She is able to be lifted up a few inches from inside of the den without issue, continuing to allow petting when placed back down.

Linda Cod tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

Beethoven appears to be fearful and given her age at the time of the assessment (8 weeks old) we believe that she hasn't had much human interaction up to this point and as a result is under-socialized; a condition that should be temporary if she is given appropriate interactions. During the assessment she attempts to flee and is avoidant of contact. She needs intensive socialization at the present time. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff. The speed at which the kitten will become socialized is hard to predict but given her age it may take some time.

258701.name: Ragnar
258701.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ragnar is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Ragnar has shown fearful behavior, including reluctance to walk, pancaking, avoiding handlers, and has on multiple occasions mounted handlers incessantly making it difficult to walk him safely at times. Ragnar has shown improvement over time, and has become social with select staff, though he continues to become overwhelmed in busier environments. Medically, Ragnar has Otitis externa

Ragnar was surrendered into care due to his previous owner due to landlord conflict. His previous family described him as a social and affectionate 4-year-old large dog. He is very active/playful and loved spending his time where his people are. He previously went on 3-4 walks a day for 30 minutes each with mild to moderate pulling. Ragnar loves going on car rides, loves having meat with his treats, and playing with squeaky toys. He was noted to guard his food from the other dogs in the home, would lunge at the resident cat, and was anxious when left alone in the home. During walks, he reacts to strangers, cats, small animals, large dogs, and small dogs by lunging and growling/Hard barking. During his stay in care, Ragnar has presented as fearful but quickly becomes aroused and starts persistently mounting handlers. He is also reluctant to return to the building after walks. Due to the concerns reported in the previous home and concerns observed in care, we recommend that Ragnar be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow him to acclimate comfortably to his new environment; force-free, reward-based training only is advised when introducing Ragnar to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Ragnar presents with outside of the care centers.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Baloo is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Baloo has recently begun to kennel fight, vocalize, or pull towards the kennels once she is removed from her kennel. On one occasion, Baloo attempted to redirect onto a hadnler once out of the kennel and then began kennel fighting as she was walked out of the room. She initially presented as fearful during the beginning of her stay. Baloo has now warmed up, is easy to remove from the kennel, solicits petting when comfortable, and recently found another dog that matches her playstyle in playgroup. Medically, Baloo is apparently healthy.

Baloo was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Baloo has been social with handlers in care but intially presented as fearful. She has warmed up over the length of her stay, displaying resource-guarding behaviors with toys, a lack of manners, and recently has begun to kennel fight when removed from the kennel. On one occasion, Baloo attempted to redirect onto the handler walking her once she was out of the kennel. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Baloo be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) Baloo may need when she leaves the care centers.

258715.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

A volunteer writes: Applesauce's persistent and froggy meows ensure she won't be forgotten, but they also indicate she understands the potential for that to happen. We know she's about 16 years old but don't have much information on her life before, only that Applesauce has been heartbreakingly agreeable and open to anything we have to offer. This began with her patiently waiting in a building for a week with no one to claim her. Noticing her looking a little worse for wear, Applesauce readily allowed a Good Samaritan to help with some matted fur and was friendly with them and us along the way. Applesauce knows she isn't a kitten but she does look amazing as diligently watches for visitors from her little window. Racing to the front whenever someone takes a moment to visit with her, she's a sweet and hopeful girl waiting for a second chance.

258739.summary:
Meet Mia!

Mia came to the care center as a stray alongside two other dogs. Understandably, the shelter environment has been overwhelming for her, and she initially displayed a high level of fear. With time, patience, and gentle handling, Mia has started to come around and is slowly gaining confidence. She is looking for a calm, patient home that will allow her to adjust at her own pace and continue building trust. With kindness, consistency, and understanding, Mia has the potential to blossom into a loving and loyal companion.

258740.name: Chestnut
258740.summary:
Meet Chestnut! 🐾

Chestnut is a handsome 6-month-old boy with the cutest face that's impossible to resist. This sweet pup loves people and is always happy to soak up attention, making him a wonderful companion for a family or individual looking for a loyal best friend.

Chestnut came to us with two older dogs, but like many young pups, he'll do best with a slow, thoughtful introduction to any new pets in his future home. With patience and proper introductions, he'll have the best chance to settle in successfully.

As a growing puppy, Chestnut could benefit from some basic manners training. He's at the perfect age to learn, and with consistency, positive reinforcement, and plenty of love, he's sure to blossom into an amazing companion.

Chestnut has so much love to give, and anyone who welcomes him into their home will be incredibly lucky. If you're looking for a sweet, affectionate young dog with a heart as adorable as his face, Chestnut can't wait to meet you!

258741.summary:
Meet Lumi!

Lumi came to the care center as a stray alongside two other dogs. The shelter environment has been overwhelming for her, and she has been highly fearful while in our care, requiring a slow, patient, and considerate approach to help her feel safe. While she may be shy at first, Lumi is looking for a calm, understanding home where she can build trust at her own pace. With gentle guidance, consistency, and plenty of time to adjust, Lumi has the potential to blossom into a devoted companion. If you have a quiet home and the patience to let a timid dog, come out of her shell, Lumi may be the perfect match for you.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Monay is at-risk for behavior reasons. She entered the Care Center with a previous scratch history. 258765.name: Hot Sauce
258765.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am playful and cute!
Hot Sauce is at the front of the kennel, meowing and stretching a paw outside of the kennel door to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he immediately comes forward, continuing to meow and head bunting the assessor's hand to solicit attention. He allows and leans into all petting, remaining calm when he is held. When placed back in the kennel, Hot Sauce continues to try to exit to solicit more attention from the assessor, remaining easy to pick up and place back into the kennel.

Hot Sauce interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

258774.name: Tigger
258774.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Tigger and Tiger, two brothers were surrendered into our care as their owner moved to a place not allowing pets. Both cats were quite affected by their relinquishment. Tigger did not really allow petting and stayed at the back of his cubby, coming out to eat or use his litter box. Today was the day! As I opened the door to his "bedroom", Tigger moved forward, saluting me and asking for pets! I was amazed, so happy and proud of him... Tigger's owner said:friendly and affectionate, good with cats and dogs(he lived with one).Tigger is a cute tabby who worked on himself to show the world what a good kitty he truly is. Now, time to meet his new family and go home! Tigger is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

Tigger tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I am playful and cute!

Beanz tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter and may be intimidated by small children. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
.

A volunteer writes: Beanz was sleeping at the front of his condo with his paw tucked over his face. I tried to admire him for as long as I could, but it lasted all of three minutes because Beanz is here for the party and won't be caught sleeping through it. I assured Beanz I had nothing planned, so he could return to napping if he wanted, but he waltzed to the front with his eyes half open and draped his paws over the ledge. Happy to knead to himself as he watched the comings and goings of the shelter, it isn't so surprising that a cat who can relax with so much charm can just as easily snuggle into the arms of a new friend. Beanz was brought to us as the last possible option his previous guardian had and with notes that describe a very loving cat who loves to play and say hello to people. He's hoping to find a second chance with you.

258785.name: Clover
258785.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Clover is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns in his previous home. In the home, Clover displayed significant fearful and defensive behavior shortly after adoption. On his first night in the home, he growled before biting a child on the hand, causing a puncture wound/breaking skin. He was also reported to have bitten two other children, causing bruising without breaking skin, and reportedly bit a total of four times during his time in the home. Clover in the care center has been comfortable with staff, and enjoys going on his walks. Medically, Clover has CIRDC, matted, emaciated and has diarrhea.

Clover was surrendered as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is mostly unknown. The caretaker had Clover in the home for 1 day after his rehoming. Clover's original owners did not report any behavioral or medical concerns and previously lived with 5 children. After entering the caretaker's home, the youngest child approached Clover excitedly, and Clover began fowling before he bit the child on the right hand, drawing blood and leaving a puncture. Clover was reported to then retreat but would charge at anyone in the home who approached him. Clover was reported to have bitten the other 2 older children in the home and left bruising but no broken skin. During his stay in care, Clover has been fearful but does begin to approach handlers when given a slow approach with treats. He had briefly solicited attention from the assessor during his handling assessment. Due to Clover's behavior concerns in the caretaker's home, we recommend for Clover be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

258806.name: Gerry
258806.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Gerry!
Gerry came to ACC as a stray, so we don't know much about his past, but we do know this gentle guy is looking for someone who will give him the time and patience he needs to feel safe. Gerry has medical needs that staff will discuss with you when you meet him. He can be a little unsure when meeting new people and places, but he has shown that he is willing to take treats and slowly warm up. With a calm environment and a caring family, this sweet boy is ready to start his next chapter.

My Ideal Home
Gerry would thrive in a quiet home with a patient adopter who understands that confidence is built one small step at a time. A predictable routine, positive reinforcement training, and enrichment activities like food puzzles and long lasting chews will help him feel comfortable while he continues to learn about the world around him.

Good with Other Pets?
Because Gerry arrived as a stray, his history with other animals is unknown. He has been able to meet other dogs at the shelter, but he may benefit from slow, thoughtful introductions to help him feel comfortable with canine friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Gerry's fearful nature and need for gentle interactions, an adult only home is recommended at this time. He would do best with adopters who will respect his boundaries and allow him to approach new experiences at his own pace.

Things to Know
Gerry is a shy pup who may need a little extra time to come out of his shell, but every brave step he takes is worth celebrating. He walks nicely on leash, enjoys tasty treats, and is learning that new people can bring good things. If you're looking for a quiet companion to share peaceful days and gentle moments with, Gerry may just be the missing piece to your puzzle.

258839.name: Mr. Speckles
258839.summary:
Meet Mr. Speckles!
Mr. Speckles was found abandoned in an apartment building and is now looking for a safe, loving place to call home. While his past is a mystery, this gentle boy has shown that he wants to connect with people and is ready for a patient person who will help him feel comfortable at his own pace.

My Ideal Home
Mr. Speckles would do best in a calm, quiet home with someone who understands that confidence takes time. He will need slow introductions to new people and places, along with plenty of patience, routine, and positive reinforcement to help him feel secure. A peaceful environment where he can decompress and learn that he is safe will help him shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Mr. Speckles has not shown reactivity toward other dogs while in our care, but his history with other animals is unknown. Slow and thoughtful introductions are recommended for any resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful nature and need for a slow approach, Mr. Speckles would do best in an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Mr. Speckles is a shy and sensitive pup who may need extra time before he feels comfortable in a new environment. He appreciates gentle interactions and should always be allowed to approach people and new experiences at his own pace. Once he feels safe, his sweet personality can begin to shine. If you have a quiet home and a big heart for a dog who needs a little extra patience, Mr. Speckles may be the perfect companion for you.

258841.name: Splasher
258841.summary:
Meet Splasher!
Splasher was brought to the shelter by the NYPD and is now looking for a family to help her write the next chapter of her story. This sweet, wiggly puppy is full of potential and is ready to grow into an amazing lifelong companion. Like any young pup, she's curious, playful, and eager to learn, especially when toys are involved!

My Ideal Home
Splasher is looking for a patient adopter who understands that puppies are a work in progress. She will thrive in a calm, low traffic home where she can settle in at her own pace while learning all about the world through positive reinforcement, consistency, and lots of love. Regular playtime, training, and enrichment will help her grow into a confident adult dog.

Good with Other Pets?
We're still getting to know Splasher, so her history with other animals is unknown. As with any puppy, slow introductions and positive experiences will help set her up for success with future furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Splasher's ideal home is one that can give her the time and patience every young puppy needs as she learns new routines and builds confidence. Gentle, respectful interactions will help her feel safe as she settles into family life.

Things to Know
Splasher is still just a baby, so she's ready to learn everything from basic manners to fun new tricks. She loves toys, enjoys playtime, and is looking for someone who will celebrate every little milestone along the way. Splasher also has some medical needs that our staff will be happy to discuss with you when you meet her. If you're ready for puppy kisses, happy wiggles, and a lifetime of adventures, Splasher can't wait to meet you!

258843.name: Thunder
258843.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Thunder came to us with housemate Bello as their family moved to a place not allowing pets. Thunder looked shy at first, laying at the very back of his cubby, his safe place. I can only imagine the eery situation he finds himself in, separated from his owners, his friend and away from his familiar place! As I started speaking to him softly, Thunder indicated some interest and started rolling on his side and sliding forward, enjoying petting, head bunting and purring. What a cutie in his bright orange coat and truly, what a sweetheart!!Thunder lived with many cats and dogs and is said to be good with all, including children, all together a friendly and affectionate pet. Thunder would love to start a new page in his life with you(just remember he could be a bit timid for a start) so come to the Manhattan Care Center and ask for a meet and greet!







Thunder has improved since his last assessment and was in the cubby, looking slightly cautious. When I approached with treats, he was curious and sniffed them, gave the tiniest of hisses, and then began enjoying petting, leaning in nicely for cheek rubs. He did not tire of the petting and then ate squeeze-up treats. He's a very sweet cat who was more nervous earlier during his stay with us.

Thunder allows and enjoys attention and petting but appears to be mildly nervous stressed in the shelter and was more nervous earlier.  He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

A volunteer writes: Bello is a cat for the books. Stretching his paws on my leg as he went to walk into my lap, he decided he'd do me one better by hopping onto my shoulder. Nuzzling my face like we have always been best friends, Bello admitted that he's actually looking for one. A best friend, a family, someone to give his heart to, but in the meantime he seems to be handing his heart to everyone. Bello was brought to us with other cats and with loving notes describing an affectionate and sweetly curious cat who enjoys his scratching post and likes to be held and kissed, which we can definitely see. Bello's an allstar who's only missing one thing now - a forever family.

A volunteer writes: Kipper's condo door is almost always open because someone is there cuddling with her as they sing her praises to anyone in the room because, in spite of being a staff and volunteer darling, Kipper is still without a family to call her own. Found in an abandoned car with kittens, Kipper and the group were scooped up and brought to safety. Kipper is blind and was in need of a little extra hand so she graciously accepted and has been winning hearts as she settles into shelter life. It's really no wonder why someone is always visiting with her because she's been an absolute delight, peering over our shoulders and out the window, snuggling into every open hand that comes her way in great and open hearted hopes that the next one that does will belong to her forever family.

258908.name: Boxer
258908.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Boxer was on top of the den, alert and somewhat apprehensive, with dilated pupils and a somewhat stiff body. She hissed when approached with the treat bag, but then sniffed the treats and gave a few more hisses before allowing petting with the scratcher tool on her cheek, head, and along her back while remaining in place. She ignored squeeze-up treats. After the door was shut she ate them. There is a possibility that she will improve soon.

Boxer tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: Having found herself on the other side of a pretty stressful ordeal, Boxer likes to sleep as close as she can to the front of her cubby. Not so long ago she was in a taped cardboard box with other cats outside of a building. Things have changed, so she fluffs her little paws out to press them against the door. I couldn't help but admire and it seems like that's where Boxer likes to keep things at the moment. We understand the benefits of a slower approach, especially for someone like Boxer and even though she wasn't the most forthcoming with me, there are a few other things we've learned. She loves trying different types of treats and is sometimes accepting of pets, but what Boxer would really love is a chance to find a family to call her own.

When she is placed back into the kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to allow all further petting, handling, and attention.

Rainbow Dash interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

258955.name: King Julius
258955.summary:
A volunteer writes:
I love spending time with cats like King Julius, an easy peasy and friendly gentleman who keeps giving without even asking. Do not worry..I gave him "Temptations" and lots of cuddles because he was such a treat in my long day at the care center! King Julius, although he likes to stay on his kuranda bed, loves attention, company and endless petting and sweet talks. He rolls on his side or back, his four in the air and making tons of air biscuits. It feels good to be so welcomed!!King Julius was surrendered because of developing allergies in a household member. He is said to be a friendly and affectionate lap cat, very talkative and who likes to snuggle. He would get excited at time with too much petting but we have not seen any of this at the care center. King Julius is a great cat who will make an amazing forever best friend. He is apparently healthy, did very well on his behavior evaluation and is waiting for his neuter. Come and meet this lovely gent at the Manhattan Care Center!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
King Julius is laying on top of his kuranda bed, eyes wide and observing the assessor as they approach. When the kennel door is opened and he is softly spoken to, he begins rolling around on his side. When loud noises occur in the hall, he does pause, backing up and needing a moment to recover. His attention is able to be refocused with more soft talk and petting, but he still will occasionally back up and hesitate. King Julius allows and leans into all petting, head bunting and rolling around as he is pet and tolerating extended petting without issue. He is able to be easily picked up, remains calm when held, and continues to be receptive to further attention and petting when he is placed back into the kennel.

King Julius interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

258987.name: Grillmaster
258987.summary:
Grillmaster arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, he has been observed to have a low threshold for arousal. Noted to head whip with an open mouth and begin running around the room when the handler attempts to interact with him. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult-only home.

A staff member writes: Grillmaster is a calm, easygoing pup who loves leisurely walks, sniffing his surroundings, and spending time with his people. He's a polite walking companion with little to no leash pulling, happily ignores dogs, people, and bicycles, and enjoys gentle pets, treats, and making his crate cozy by collecting blankets and toys. At the care center, he has shown friendly social skills, relaxing quickly during introductions and offering playful bounces and a play bow. If you're looking for a mellow, affectionate companion, Grillmaster is ready to meet you!

258988.name: Tigger
258988.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Tigger!
Tigger is all love! He adores snuggling up next to his favorite person, soaking up belly rubs, and following his humans wherever they go. He already knows sit, down, and paw, and he's ready to learn even more with someone who enjoys teaching new tricks.

My Previous Foster Says
Tigger is all love. His favorite place is snuggled up next to his favorite human, but he'll hop at the chance to go for a walk or play with a soccer ball. He wants all the pets and belly rubs while you're snuggling and watching TV, which is hard to refuse with those big, sweet eyes. He already knows sit, down, and paw, and he's motivated to learn more! He could use some help walking on a leash, but he tires easily and then trots calmly next to you. He doesn't beg, bark, nip, or growl, just a chill, adaptable gentleman who would make a great addition to any home! 

My Ideal Home
Tigger would love a home where he can get plenty of affection, playtime, and leisurely walks. He's still working on his leash manners and can be quite enthusiastic when meeting people, so a patient adopter who can help him practice calm greetings would be a great match.

Good with Other Pets?
Tigger's history with other animals is unknown. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended with any potential furry siblings.

Good with Kids?
Because Tigger can be very enthusiastic and jumpy when excited, ACC recommends a home without children under 5.

Things to Know
Tigger may be a little bouncy, but underneath all that enthusiasm is a sweet, affectionate guy who just wants to be close to his people. If you're looking for a cuddle buddy with a playful side, Tigger may be your perfect match!

On my straycation

**Meet Tigger! 🐾**

Tigger is an absolute sweetheart who loves nothing more than snuggling up next to his favorite person-but he's always ready to hop up for a walk or a game of soccer or basketball! During his 3-day Straycation, he was calm, adaptable, and easygoing in new places. He never barked, nipped, or showed aggression, and he happily settled into new environments.

Tigger enjoys long walks and exploring, though he could use a little leash-walking practice. Once he gets tired, he trots calmly right alongside you. He was unfazed by birds, squirrels, loud noises, and city activity, and he showed friendly curiosity toward other dogs. He also met new people politely without jumping.

At home, Tigger is the perfect couch companion. He doesn't beg while people eat, knows **sit, down, and paw**, and is eager to learn more. He even took his medicine like a champ! He had no accidents during his stay and would whine at the door when he needed to go out.

With his big sweet eyes, love of belly rubs, playful side, and chill personality, Tigger is the kind of dog who makes it very easy to fall in love. **He's a snuggly, silly sweetheart who could be a wonderful addition to his forever home.** ❤️🐶

259009.name: Mylo
259009.summary:
Meet Mylo!
Mylo came to ACC when his owner could no longer care for him. This young pup is a fun-loving, playful guy who enjoys being around people, but he can also be a little shy when faced with new experiences. Once he starts to feel comfortable, his goofy personality comes out-he loves to greet people enthusiastically and is eager to be part of the action. He's looking for a patient family that will help him continue building confidence while teaching him good manners.

My Ideal Home
Mylo would do best with an adopter who is committed to positive reinforcement training and can provide him with structure, consistency, and plenty of exercise. He'll benefit from continued work on polite greetings, impulse control, and becoming more comfortable with handling, especially around his head and neck. A patient home that allows him to settle in at his own pace will help him thrive.

Good with Kids?
Due to his handling sensitivity, mouthy play style, and tendency to become overwhelmed, Mylo is recommended for a home with children 13 years and older.

Good with Other Pets?
Mylo's history with other dogs is unknown. In the shelter, he has shown appropriate social interest during introductions and was tolerant of another dog, though he occasionally became overexcited and attempted to hump. Slow introductions with any resident dogs are recommended. His history with cats is unknown.

Overall Health
Mylo is healthy overall. He can be sensitive to handling around his head and neck and may become nervous in unfamiliar situations, but he has otherwise done well during his care.

Behavior Determination Level 3 - Experienced Adopters. Mylo is a friendly, playful dog who is still learning how to manage his excitement and build confidence with handling. He will do best with adopters who will continue reward-based training, respect his boundaries, and help him develop polite manners as he matures.

Other Fun Facts
Mylo loves treats and is eager to interact with people once he feels comfortable. He's crate trained for short periods, has a playful, goofy personality, and is sure to keep his future family smiling as he grows into a confident, well-mannered companion!

259045.name: Ethan
259045.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ethan is at risk due to behavioral concerns in his previous home. Ethan has a multiple-bite history that has broken skin and drawn blood, and were typically bites and releases. During his stay in care, Ethan has been fearful and mostly avoidant of interaction. He is slowly allowing for select handlers to remove him from the kennel and lean into some contact in calmer/quieter settings. Medically, Ethan is apparently healthy.

Ethan was surrendered by his previous owner due to behavior concerns in the previous home. Ethan is reported to have a variety of behavior concerns, including a multiple-bite history, resource guarding of food and toys, and handling/touch sensitivity. His family described him as a social, affectionate, and very active dog who prefers to spend most of his time around people, becomes nervous when getting into or riding in the car, but travels comfortably when sitting on a person's lap or in a carrier. Ethan seemingly has a soft spot for "lambie" plush squeaky toys. During his stay in care, Ethan has been highly fearful and mostly avoidant of interaction.  Due to the concerns reported in the previous home, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

259046.name: Rosebud
259046.summary:
Rosebud is a friendly, affectionate girl who came to the shelter as a stray alongside a large male mixed-breed dog. Since arriving, she has been sweet, social, and eager to interact with staff, winning everyone over with her loving personality.

During her behavior assessment, Rosebud showed that she can become easily over-aroused when she's excited. With continued positive reinforcement, consistent routines, and appropriate outlets for her energy, she has the potential to thrive in a home that understands how to help her settle and succeed.

If you're looking for a happy companion and are willing to invest a little time in helping her channel her enthusiasm, Rosebud could make a wonderful addition to your family. Come meet this sweet girl and see if she's the perfect match for you!

259047.name: Redford
259047.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Redford is at risk for behavior reasons. Redford quickly began to deteriorate in care. He has been observed to be circling in kennel, screeching on return and fixating on the transfer doors to neighboring kennels. His kennel reactivity is becoming more difficult to manage. He is much more relaxed when walked away from the shelter but once handlers begin to head back, his stress levels increase. Redford warms up quickly and is social enjoys petting. Medically, he is apparently healthy. 

Meet Redford!

Redford is a handsome boy who came to the shelter as a stray alongside a female large mixed-breed dog. He has been adjusting to shelter life but is showing signs of stress, including whining in his kennel and vocalizing when leaving the building. During social interactions, he may display displacement behaviors when he's feeling unsure or overwhelmed.

Redford would do best with a patient adopter who can give him time to decompress, build his confidence, and settle into a consistent routine. With positive reinforcement and a calm environment, he's likely to become a loyal and loving companion.

If you're looking for a dog to grow with and help feel at home, come meet Redford!

259057.name: Kingston
259057.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Kingston is very smart and a good guard dog for any home. He accepts affection from the humans that offer it and loves to be by his handler's side. He didn't seem to care about kids, birds, or squirrels. The only exception is he is reactive when other dogs are nearby. He will hard bark at the other dog (no matter how big or small) which is hard to redirect. However, when he sees the dog while he is moving, he has an easier time being pulled along and he will forget about it. He will benefit from a home with a family that is committed to training him to use his intelligence and protective qualities to everyone's advantage. He will benefit from long walks and puzzles to help keep him happy, healthy, and intellectually stimulated. On our break, we sat on a stoop together and he happily relaxed next to me and laid down, accepting pets and love. Kingston is a great dog that needs a fantastic owner to help him meet his potential.

259059.name: Charlie
259059.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Charlie!
Charlie arrived at ACC as a stray, and while we don't know much about his past, we do know this sweet boy deserves a fresh start. Found tied up to a staircase, Charlie has shown incredible resilience and a gentle spirit despite everything he has been through. He is a soft-hearted pup who enjoys spending time with people and is ready to find a family who will show him the love and security he deserves.

My Ideal Home
Charlie would thrive with a patient adopter who can help him continue building confidence at his own pace. He will benefit from gentle introductions, positive reinforcement training, and a calm environment where he can feel safe and comfortable. With time and trust, Charlie is ready to become a loving and loyal companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Charlie's history with other animals is unknown. He has been calm and neutral around other dogs while at ACC, but slow introductions will help him feel comfortable and allow any potential furry friendships to develop naturally.

Good with Kids?
Charlie's history with children is unknown. Because he can be a little sensitive and head shy, any interactions with children should be slow and respectful of his boundaries. He would do best with people who understand that trust is built one gentle moment at a time.

Things to Know
Charlie is a gentle soul who has already shown that he wants to connect with people. He enjoys pets, approaches with a loose body, and has a sweet way of asking for affection. After such a difficult beginning, Charlie is ready for the simple joys of life: a cozy bed, kind humans, and a forever home where he can finally feel safe.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
Monsoon appears to be fearful and given her age at the time of the assessment (11 weeks old) we believe that she hasn't had much human interaction up to this point and as a result is under-socialized; a condition that should be temporary if she is given appropriate interactions. During the assessment she is avoidant of contact, leaning away, fleeing, and flinching when handling is attempted. She needs intensive socialization at the present time. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff. The speed at which the kitten will become socialized is hard to predict but given her age it may take some time.

We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff. The speed at which the kitten will become socialized is hard to predict but given her age it may take some time.

259102.name: Stellaluna
259102.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Stellaluna is at risk due to behavior concerns. She arrived at the care centers as a stray with no known history. During her intake she tolerated handling but escalated to growling and snapping when put on the scale. Throughout her stay, Stellaluna has consistently displayed kennel stress and barrier frustration. She has often escalated to lunging, hard barking, snarling, and snapping at handlers when returned to her kennel. On her walks, Stellaluna often balks and has to be coaxed forward and was also reported to leash bite. She has been able to get through an adoption interaction and accepted pets. Medically, she has Brachycephalic Syndrome, CIRDC, Dental Disease, and was treated for being underweight.

Stellaluna was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Stellaluna has not acclimated well to the shelter environment despite best efforts to keep her comfortable. She has shown the potential to show sociable behaviors with handlers in calmer settings where she can interact at her own pace and through reward-based interactions, but she has escalated to higher-level warnings during her medical exam and when being returned to her kennel. Due to these concerns, we recommend that she be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can address her challenges with the use of a certified professional trainer that utilizes force-free, reward-based methods. 

A volunteer writes: Stella Luna is a meatball lowrider who's right up my alley.  My first thoughts when meeting her were, "How can I take you home?"  The bad news is, my house is full and I can't adopt Stella, the good news is, you can! She is soooo cute.  Stella Luna resembles her namesake with huge bat ears and looks like a giant Frenchie who trots along at my side at a leisurely pace.  She lets me pick her up and put her in my lap where she relaxes for a while until she's ready to get a drink from the hose.  It's a hot day and she worked really hard on her short walk, after all ;)  

Stella was picked up by police after someone reported she was tied to a pole.  They reported that she was friendly and social and easily transported in their care to QACC. Stella has had a hard time adjusting to the stressful kennel environment and has been uncomfortable with the slip lead.  Stella will benefit from rewards based, force free training to help her adjust to new situations. During gate greets with dogs she has been anxious and tense. For these reasons, Stella Luna is available to foster through a New Hope rescue. 



What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

259121.name: Funfetti
259121.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Funfetti! 🎉
Looking for a best friend who's equal parts sweet, gentle, and quietly devoted? Meet Funfetti.
This beautiful calico is the definition of calm. She's happy entertaining herself with a cozy nap, but she also enjoys checking in and spending quiet time with her people. When you come home-or even just say good morning-she'll greet you with the cutest little trill, as if she's saying, "Oh, there you are!"
After a luxurious nap (her favorite hobby), Funfetti starts her day with a dramatic stretch worthy of a yoga instructor before making her way over for affection. She'll gently head-butt your hand, flash those irresistible "please love me" eyes, and happily melt into cheek scratches, long head-to-tail pets, and butt scratches.
She isn't interested in constant attention. Instead, she's the kind of cat who loves having her own space but will let you know when she's ready for affection. Her perfect evening is stretched out beside you on the couch or curled up by your feet while you unwind, simply happy to share the moment.
Funfetti would be perfectly content as your one-and-only cat, soaking up all the love and cozy spots in the house. She'd also do wonderfully with another calm, respectful feline companion who appreciates a peaceful home.
If your dream cat is affectionate without being demanding, docile without being aloof, and happiest sharing life's quieter moments, Funfetti is ready to make your house feel like home.

259122.name: Mini Muffin
259122.summary:
My foster writes: Meet Mini Muffin! 🧁
Tiny name. HUGE personality.
Mini Muffin is a fearless little adventurer who treats every spring toy like it's his greatest prey and every taco toy like it owes him money. He's always zooming, climbing, pouncing, and trying to attack the corner of his blanket, making him the perfect sidekick for anyone who loves a kitten with endless entertainment value.
When he's finally worn himself out, he'll happily curl up in your lap, trail behind you from room to room, and supervise whatever you're doing-especially if it means he can watch Chopped or X-Men 1977 (He has thing for TV and loves to watch these shows specifically.)
He's not exactly a morning cat, but give him a few minutes and a friendly hello, and he's ready to start the day's adventures.
Mini Muffin would thrive in a home with another playful kitten or a young, high-energy cat who can keep up with his wrestling matches and zoomie sessions. If you're looking for a kitten who's equal parts comedian, explorer, cuddle bug, and loyal little shadow, Mini Muffin is ready to steal your heart.

259126.name: Ochoa
259126.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Sunday, August 9 at 12PM - 4PM with Neighborly Events - 125-04 84th Road, Kew Gardens, NY 11415 . Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Ochoa is one of the best pups I've had the chance to spend time with. He was slightly energetic when we first met, but he quickly settled in and became comfortable lounging around, whether he was watching TV with my roommates or sleeping in my bed. Ochoa loves to follow you wherever you go, but he's also very patient. He'll happily wait by the bathroom door until you're finished, just so he can continue following you around afterward. Ochoa would do great in a laid-back home that also enjoys throwing toys for him to fetch and giving him plenty of treats. One of his funniest quirks is that after he pees or poops, he'll kick his back legs and then look at you proudly, as if he thinks he's successfully buried his poop and you no longer have to pick it up. Unfortunately for him, he's wrong! No matter what he was doing, my roommates and I loved watching Ochoa prance around the room. He's such a fun, sweet pup and would make a wonderful addition to a loving home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

259134.name: Mister Cat
259134.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Mister Cat is on the at-risk list due to medical and behavior reasons. Mister Cat is an obese cat with a very poor appetite in shelter. We are unable to handle him due to behavior and he has an increased risk of hepatic lipidosis with prolonged anorexia due to his obesity. Mister Cat needs a calm, quiet, low stress environment with placement. If he continues to have a poor appetite, he will need veterinary care. Behaviorally, Mister Cat is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

Meet Mister Cat!  Mister Cat was surrendered to ACC by his previous owner following a move.  Mister Cat is described as an independent and bold cat who prefers contact on his own terms.  He can play exuberantly and would do best in a home with an experienced cat owner who can provide him daily enrichment and stimulation to help him thrive.

259135.name: Curry
259135.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Curry is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Curry has demonstrated reactivity toward other dogs. He has been observed hard barking and, at times, screeching. While on leash, he may lunge toward other dogs and can be difficult to redirect. In the past, following walks, Curry would grab the staff slip lead but would release it when offered treats. When working one-on-one with staff, Curry is social and allows petting. He also participates in decompression training. Medically, Curry has a history of an old leg fracture, was recently treated for CIRDC, and is otherwise healthy at this time. 

Curry was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Curry was reported to be hard barking and growling at officers when they arrived to pick him up. Due to his behavior, he was sedated for his transport to ACC. During his stay in care, Curry has shown the ability to show social behaviors with a slow approach with select handlers. He has hard-barked at novel items and sounds. But he has also displayed concerning on-leash reactivity towards other dogs during walks, kennel fights with other dogs in and out of the room, and will grab the leash once back in the kennel, releasing when offered treats. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Curry be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Faith is on the at-risk list for medical reasons. Faith has bladder stones and a urinary tract infection that is resistant to most antibiotics. 259159.name: Coco
259159.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Coco is on the at risk list for medical reasons. Coco is a geriatric dog with comorbidities. She has been diagnosed with a UTI and is currently being treated. She also has dental disease, a mammary gland tumor, heart murmur, rough haircoat, elevated liver and kidney values on bloodwork. Coco will need follow up with a vet for geriatric care, long-term planning. Behaviorally, Coco has allowed all medical handling.

Meet Coco, a sweet 10-year-old little lady who's ready to spend her golden years with a loving family. This affectionate, low-energy pup is happiest lounging near her favorite people and enjoys a relaxed routine filled with short walks, cozy naps, and the occasional tasty treat.

Coco is friendly with strangers, does well with children, and is tolerant of other dogs. She is housetrained, walks beautifully on a loose leash, and even knows cues like "sit," "come here," and "get in your bed." She loves squeaky toys, furry toys, and snacks for a job well done.

Like many senior dogs, Coco has a few quirks. Loud noises, being left alone for long periods, and car rides can make her nervous, and she'll often let you know when someone is at the door. She also prefers that her nails be trimmed by a professional and has sensitive skin that makes brushing uncomfortable.

If you're looking for a gentle, loyal companion who will happily curl up beside you and fill your home with quiet companionship, Coco may be the perfect match. Her previous family describes her as incredibly sweet and friendly-and she's ready to share that love with her next family.

259177.name: Kodak
259177.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Kodak came into the care center after his owner left him in the care of a family member, and Kodak does not get along with the resident dog in the home and is noted to play too rough with the small dog. In the prior home he is noted to be very active and playful dog. He enjoys spending his time where people are. Previous owner's favorite thing about him is his playful demeanor and smartness. Kodak's favorite activities and toys are walks, Squeak toys, and bone treats Kodak has not adjusted well to the care center environment and has displayed fearful behavior around handling and leashing.  Outside of the kennel, he is able to decompress, explore, and gradually relax. Kodak will benefit from a patient adopter/foster who can use slow, low-stress handling techniques and positive reinforcement to continue building his confidence. Kodak is available for rescue through one of our New Hope rescue partners.

A volunteer writes: Some dogs split your heart right in half the second you meet them, and Kodak is one of those dogs. Kodak was surrendered after his guardian left him in the care of a family member, but he did not get along with the resident small dogs, playing a bit too rough with one of them. His former people say he is active, playful, and enjoys spending time where people are, and noted their favorite things about him are his playful demeanor and intelligence. He is said to be friendly and outgoing with strangers and children, loves squeaky toys, and is often very excited (he is, after all, just a baby!).

Kodak has been quite scared and struggled to get comfortable at the shelter, even hesitating to engage with toys. It's heartbreaking to think about the enthusiastic dog he was in a home just a few short weeks ago. But he's gaining a little more courage every day. When he makes his way out of the building with me, a staff member congratulates him on how far he's come in a week-when he arrived, he was so nervous he would soil himself and was scared to leave his kennel altogether. Kodak is a sensitive soul, and we can't blame him for being scared in a noisy and overcrowded shelter after spending time in a loving home.

259181.name: Nino Bell
259181.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Nino Bell is at risk due to behavioral reasons. It was reported that while in his crate, in his previous home, Nino Bell was lunging and snapping towards the neighbor that was trying to feed him. While in care, Nino Bell has been observed to have a low threshold for arousal when handlers interact with him. During his assessment, Nino Bell was observed to jump up on handlers frequently and wrap his front paw around them as if to begin mounting. Nino has also been observed to jump up high and bite the leash. During one instance he almost caught the handler's hand. While out on the street, Nino will check in with the handler and have soft eyes. Medically, Nino Bell has CIRDC.

Nino Bell arrived at MACC after being picked up by field. It was reported that while in his crate Nino Bell was lunging and snapping towards the neighbor that was trying to feed him. While in care, Nino Bell has been observed to be fearful of handling and have a low threshold for arousal when handlers interact with him. During his assessment, Nino Bell was observed to jump up on handlers frequently and wrap his front paw around the handler as if to begin mounting. During handling, Nino Bell was noted to head whip persistently. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

259183.name: Panther
259183.summary:
A volunteer writes:
It took me a good ten days before I could take a decent photo of Panther, a two year old all ebony semi long hair beauty. I almost gave up....No one should give up on the former pets in our care as miracles, break throughs do happen every day! Today was the day Panther decided to come out of her shell, slowly but surely and it absolutely made...my day! Panther was a bit hesitant but sweet words and slow moves made her lean into pets, head bunt gently my hand and even purr slowly.  She has still a way to go but I know she will get there with our help. Her former owner told us that Panther was a shy cat who was rather timid with all, so, no surprise she had difficult debuts at the care center. We know now that Panther is capable to bond and be sweet. She will need therefore a new owner or family who will give her time to come around on her own with their help of course. Panther would love to meet you when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

259184.name: Coconut
259184.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Coconut was "let go" in the lobby of an apartment building together with a sack of litter...Another mystery kitty... The little girl deserves so much better....Coconut is two year old, a skinny little marshmallow with a rather thin coat and so much in need of TLC. She is quite lively, curious, sociable, friendly but also a bit skittish(she can give occasional nips) as observed by some staff and volunteers. She was quite welcoming with me, rather playful with toys and appreciating caresses and sweet words. Her tail swishes some , letting you know that like with a "heated up kid in play", it is time for "time out".  Coconut  is a young gal who might not have had the easiest life as a "pet". She needs to feel safe, cared for and loved to give the best she can give. A quiet home, an understanding and experienced owner are the keys to give Coconut her health, happiness and balance back. Coconut is waiting for you at the manhattan Care Center.









What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

259187.name: Dream
259187.summary:
Meet Dream!
Dream may be a little shy at first, but she's hoping her forever home is where all her dreams come true. She takes a little time to warm up and prefers to come to you when she's ready for pets, so she'll appreciate someone who understands that the best relationships are built at her own pace. Give her some patience and a little space, and you might just become her dream come true!

My Ideal Home
Dream would love a calm, patient adopter who will let her take things one step at a time. She's not looking to rush into anything, and she'll need time to feel comfortable in her new surroundings before she's ready to fully come out of her shell.

Good with Other Pets?
Dream's history with other animals is unknown. She was cautious when meeting another dog at ACC and chose to walk away, so any introductions should be slow and respectful.

Good with Kids?
ACC recommends a home without children. 

Things to Know
Dream is a gentle, sensitive girl who prefers to make the first move when it comes to affection. She's not quite ready to wake up from her shelter dream just yet, but with the right person, her happily-ever-after could be right around the corner.

She gave a single hiss, then came forward and was sweet and gentle, leaning in for cheek rubs and enjoying being pet along her back. She struggled slightly when picked up, but tolerated it, and when set back down, she remained calm. She jumped out of the kennel and temporarily escaped. She is an active cat who will benefit from enrichment in the home.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Galloway is at risk due to behavior concerns. Galloway repeatedly pulls with extreme force, resulting in heavy panting and multiple episodes of briefly passing out, including while wearing a harness. She also frequently jumps on handlers and fixates on people, requiring frequent redirection. Galloway has additionally displayed resource guarding around food, including growling, hard barking, lunging, and baring teeth during feeding and kennel interactions. She may also bark and lunge at dogs passing her kennel, although she has generally been non reactive to dogs and people while walking. Galloway was observed to do very well with training knowing sit and paw. Medically, Galloway is healthy at this time.e.

Galloway arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Galloway had been observed to be on leash reactive. Noted to hard bark and lunge towards other dogs. In care, Galloway has been observed to growl, hard bark, lunge, bare teeth, and snarl when handlers go to feed her. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

259204.name: Maverick
259204.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Little Maverick, a cute and young Tuxedo was left in front of a veterinary clinic by an unknown person. A mystery kitty!!! Maverick had a large scrape on his right cheek. He was treated and is presently on the mend. Looking at Maverick you might wonder:why does he have one fluffy cheek and the other one is flat? Well, he had to be shaved to treat his wound, that is why! No worries, hair will grow back to give him back his natural tomcat looks! Maverick is a very friendly cat, curious, eager to meet and greet and would not mind jumping off his cage into his visitor's arms. He is a great cat with everyone, including the police who brought him to the care center and the doctors who are helping him. Imagine how great he will be in a home, as a pet, cared for and loved....You can not go wrong with Maverick. His little cosmetic issue is just temporary, he is healthy, aced his behavior evaluation and will be ready to go home after his neuter! Come and meet Maverick at the Manhattan Care Center!
Addendum: Maverick scrape is healing nicely and his hair is growing back. Soon he will have once again two chubby cheeks!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
Maverick is a very sweet cat who was lying quietly, partially asleep, and woke up to the sound of the assessor's voice. He stood up and came forward, curious, and immediately began eating treats. When petted along his back, he quickly arched it with a high tail. He enjoyed all petting and remained calm when briefly picked up, and remained so when set back down.

Maverick interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.</P

259223.name: Coco Bean
259223.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Coco Bean is a cute all ebony young damsel surrendered into our care as her owner moved to a place not allowing cats. It would have been great to learn a bit about her past life as a pet, as we all know that most of the time, behavior in a shelter and at home can be quite different...Coco was a bit stressed from day one at the care center, asking for petting, giving a little cry or a little quick swat and then asking for petting again. She trusts a bit more now and meeting and petting are her most sought wish and activity when a guest opens her kennel.She leans into pets, head bunts, even purrs, backs off occasionally and then comes back for more. As time goes by, Coco Bean, the lovely gal in the little black dress, feels better and better. Still, Coco Bean needs an experienced and patient new owner and a quiet environment to bloom into a most lovely and loving forever best friend. Come and meet Coco Bean at the Manhattan Care Center!








What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cocoa Bean has greatly improved and calmed down since her first assessment. She is still a high-energy, very interactive cat who is chatty and sweet, but she is now able to be interacted with without much, if any, escalation. She loves petting, lay on her side purring loudly, and wanted as much petting as she could get. She was very calm when picked up and held, a change from before, and remained interactive, curious, and energetic when set back down. After a little more petting, she gently tapped the assessor's hand once with her paw, and it is possible that she could still escalate if overstimulated. However, she is a sweet and loving cat who needs plenty of interaction, play, activity, and affection.

Coco Bean interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting although she may still ramp up with too much petting or attention. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in cats who ramp up and might get slightly swatty.

259226.name: Timba
259226.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Timba is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Timba has not acclimated well to the shelter environment, remaining highly fearful and shut down. When approached in the kennel, Timba is tense, shaking, has wide or whale eyes, has avoided leashing, does not take any form of treats or food (including chicken breast, sausage, sliced cheese), and avoids all interaction with handlers. timba's previous owner describe him as an active, playful, and independent dog.  Medically, Timba is obese and has an ear infection. 

Timba came into the care center as an owner surrender due to him being too big for the residence. His owner described him as a active, playful, and independent dog who prefers contact on his own terms. He spends most of his time in the living room of his home and he enjoys snacking on beef and chicken treats. Timba has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

259227.name: Juno
259227.summary:
Meet Juno!
Previously in foster with her 4 adorable kittens & is now up for adoption. She is a beautiful cat with a sweet & patient demeanor. As her foster mom, sometimes I forget that she's not just a cat mom. She's also just a girl! It warms my heart when I randomly catch her playing with toys and staring out the window. Just doing regular cat things. Because otherwise she would be busy nursing & taking care of her 4 little terrors 24/7. She's super patient and loving to her babies and people. She is the sweetest girl who always greets me with purrs and chirps for attention. Super laid back. She's got beautiful black spots throughout her fur and gorgeous yellow eyes. She would make a great addition to any loving family.

259233.name: Chance
259233.summary:
Chance is a sweet but sometimes conflicted cat. She was on top of the den, lying quietly. She was curious and stood up when spoken to by the assessor and was easily coaxed down for treats. She loved being pet, leaning in nicely for cheek rubs with a high tail that was even quivering in (good) excitement. However, while she was enjoying the petting, she also repeatedly hissed at the assessor while still seeming curious and to enjoy the interaction. She was given a little break and then the assessor tried again. Once again, she enjoyed the petting and resumed hissing. After another short break, she went back up on top of the den, and the assessor approached one more time. She was inquisitive and curious and allowed a little touching but seemed wary, so the interaction was stopped. She also did a little low growling during both interactions. After a break of a few hours the assessor went back and she was on top of the den and leaned forward with interest when the assessor approached and she allowed petting and was sweet without showing signs of confliction this time.

Chance interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is sometimes easy to handle and tolerates all petting much of the time.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior and who are well counseled in confliction, some petting induced aggression and potential new home adjustment.

A volunteer writes: Chance needs another chance--to find new pet parents who take a go-slow approach, who let her get his bearings in a new home, who know that cats need to adjust and open up at their own pace before they're ready to show affection to their new people. This petite tuxie beauty would fit it well with a forever family who redirects her teenage energy into toys and scratching pads. She'd love it if her humans showered her with short bursts of affection and then let her have a little independent time to relax and recharge. Feisty, friendly, and curious about everything, Miss Chance is ready for a second chance at the forever home she deserves.

259235.name: Dove
259235.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Dove is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she does attempt to flee and avoid human contact. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.

Monterey is looking for a calm, understanding home where he can build confidence and settle into a predictable routine. With kindness, patience, and plenty of gentle encouragement, this sweet little guy has all the potential to blossom into a wonderful companion.

259265.name: Baked Alaska
259265.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

Baked Alaska is laying in her den, poking her head out of the portal exit and meowing as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she runs to the front of the kennel, greeting the assessor with firm head bunts. Baked Alaska allows and leans into all petting but does periodically get distracted by noises around the room, pausing before her eyes dart around. Her attention is easily refocused with soft talk, and her focus returns to the assessor, leaning in for further petting and attention. When pickup is attempted, Baked Alaska stands firm and begins vocalizing. She is given a moment to settle before pickup is attempted again. She is able to be picked up but tenses and vocalizes a bit when held. When she is placed back down, she remains at the front, pausing and lip licking for a moment before continuing to solicit attention with head bunts, allowing further petting, and raising her back as she is pet. 


Baked Alaska interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Baked Alaska go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment periods and cats who aren't fully comfortable with pick up.

259272.name: Portia
259272.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Portia is the prettiest sight, an all ebony, fluffy and plushy kitty who looks more like a pricy stuffed toy than a real cat..Portia IS a real cat, though and a very sweet and friendly one. She is really a pleasure for the eyes(and the hand as her coat is sooo soft) and a lovely kitty to spend time with. Her former owner describes her as a quiet, gentle, sweet and loving pet. So, why is Portia at the Manhattan Care Center? Few months ago, Portia developed bladder stones(she had crystals in her urine) and started voiding outside her litter box. Her family could not afford her general and medical care anymore and Portia was brought to the care center where she is observed and doing well without presently any urinary symptoms or litter box issues. She might need to go on a special diet to prevent more stones formation  and that should be discussed with our adoption counselors. Portia is a delight of a cat. True, she does have a medical issue but many cats or dogs do. Like anyone, she deserves a good and loving home. Come and meet lovely Portia at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
