What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
Sid is standing at the front of the kennel, meowing and extending a paw outside of the kennel door to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he attempts to push past the assessor to exit, appearing interested in exploring. He is able to be maneuvered back in before attempting once more, placing his paws on the assessor's shoulders. The assessor gives him a moment to settle, speaking softly to him. When further interaction is attempted, Sid leans forward to head bunt the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting, tail swooshing but not escalating. He is a bit resistant when initially attempting pick up but does allow it, body slightly tense but without further issue. When he is returned to his kennel, he remains at the front, leaning in and remaining tolerant of extended petting. When the interaction is ended, he is seen rolling around on top of his den, entertaining himself by playing with his blanket.

Sid interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

259300.name: Kogi
259300.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Too many cats!The very reason why lovely Kogi is with us at the care center with so many of his housemates. Kogi is a gentle and shy cat who has been quite sweet since the beginning of his stay. Time made him even more friendly and he is quite a pleasant cat to spend time with. He does not stay in hiding when a visitor is at his door. He head bunts, purrs, makes biscuits and rolls on his kennel floor for in depth petting. He could gain some weight and a good brushing and he would just look absolutely gorgeous. I forgot to say that Kogi is a lap cat at the care center! Kogi will make a wonderful friend and for many years to come. He is apparently healthy, is already neutered, did well on his behavior evaluation and can go home today with you! Ask about Kogi when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!









Kogi is standing upright in his den, observing the assessor with wide eyes and dilated pupils as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, he is initially hesitant to come forward. With soft talk and treats he is able to be coaxed to the front of the kennel, eating all of the treats before looking around the room with his tail held low. Kogi allows all petting and leans in when he is pet on the head and cheeks. He is able to be easily picked up and remains calm when held. When he is placed back down, he remains at the front, continuing to allow further petting and handling. When sounds occur in the room, Kogi pauses before walking back into his den. He continues to be easily coaxed with treats and soft talk.

Kogi interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

259307.name: Lululemon
259307.summary:
Meet Lululemon!
Lululemon came to ACC when her owner could no longer care for her. This affectionate girl loves being around people and has a playful, social personality that shines through even while she's adjusting to shelter life. Although the shelter can make her feel a little anxious at times, she's friendly with everyone she meets and is ready to find a family to call her own.

My Ideal Home
Lululemon would love an active home where she can enjoy daily walks, playtime, and plenty of time with her people. She's happiest when she's included in family activities and will benefit from a consistent routine while she settles into her new home. A little patience as she decompresses and positive reinforcement training will help her confidence continue to grow.

Good with Kids?
Yes! Lululemon previously lived with children and was described as friendly, outgoing, and playful. As with all dog-child interactions, respectful introductions and supervision are recommended.

Good with Other Pets?
Lululemon has lived successfully around other animals. She was described as playful with familiar dogs, friendly with unfamiliar dogs on leash, and friendly toward cats. As always, slow introductions to resident pets are recommended.

Overall Health
Lululemon is healthy overall. She has shown some anxiety in the shelter environment, including heavy panting and wide eyes, but she remains friendly and affectionate. We expect her to continue relaxing as she settles into a home.

Behavior Determination Level 2. Lululemon is a friendly, social dog who has shown mild anxiety while adjusting to the shelter. She is expected to do well with adopters who provide a calm environment, regular exercise, enrichment, and time to decompress.

Other Fun Facts
Lululemon loves being wherever her people are and isn't picky when it comes to toys, treats, or food! She enjoys walks, playtime, and has been described as an affectionate companion who is always ready to join in on family activities. She also made quite the impression on our veterinary team with her wiggly body and enthusiasm for Vienna sausages!

259308.name: Sierra
259308.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Sierra!
Sierra arrived at ACC as a stray, so her history is a bit of a mystery, but this sweet girl is ready to start a brand new chapter. Sierra is a curious pup who enjoys exploring her surroundings and happily approaches people with a soft body and wagging tail. She may still be learning about the world around her, but she is showing that she has plenty of potential to become someone's perfect companion.

My Ideal Home
Sierra would do best with an adopter who can provide daily exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training to help her continue learning and growing. Activities like food puzzles, long lasting chews, and fun games will help keep her engaged and give her plenty of opportunities to show off her smart side. With patience and consistency, Sierra is ready to become your new adventure buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
Since Sierra arrived as a stray, her history with other animals is unknown. She has not shown any concerns around other dogs while in our care, but slow and thoughtful introductions are always recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to observed behaviors and Sierra's need for continued training and guidance, an adult only home is recommended at this time. She would do best with people who can help her practice polite interactions and set her up for success.

Things to Know
Sierra is a sweet and curious pup who loves exploring, accepting treats, and spending time with people. She is still working on learning appropriate ways to show affection and would benefit from positive reinforcement training to help her practice good manners. If you're looking for a dog with a lot of potential and a heart ready to grow, Sierra may be the perfect match!

Activities like food puzzles, long lasting chews, and fun games will help keep her engaged and give her plenty of opportunities to show off her smart side. With patience and consistency, Sierra is ready to become your new adventure buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
Since Sierra arrived as a stray, her history with other animals is unknown. She has not shown any concerns around other dogs while in our care, but slow and thoughtful introductions are always recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to observed behaviors and Sierra's need for continued training and guidance, an adult only home is recommended at this time. She would do best with people who can help her practice polite interactions and set her up for success.

Things to Know
Sierra is a sweet and curious pup who loves exploring, accepting treats, and spending time with people. She is still working on learning appropriate ways to show affection and would benefit from positive reinforcement training to help her practice good manners. If you're looking for a dog with a lot of potential and a heart ready to grow, Sierra may be the perfect match!

259310.name: Snacks
259310.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Snacks is on the at risk list for medical concerns. Snacks is a senior cat with an abnormal cystic mass on his neck. The mass was lanced and drained, but quickly filled back up. With placement, it would be recommended that the cystic mass be removed. Because Snacks also has dental disease, a dental procedure could be considered at the same time. Behaviorally, Snacks has allowed medical handling.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
My purr motor is always running!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.

A volunteer writes: An injured and older gentleman, Snacks was totally prepared to make his own chance when he'd really been getting anything but. Cheerfully greeting the people he met, quietly imploring them to look at his heart rather than the cuts and growths adorning his distinctively beautiful face. Snacks' efforts paid off, if not the forever home he'd been hoping for, a pathway to one. When I met Snacks, he was doing his little marching kneads right at the front. I opened the door and Snacks promptly flopped over on his catnip pillow and began kneading the sky. I don't know what else to say to convey how amazing Snacks is but I would like to add that cuddling with him is a dream. He's sweet and affectionate, open hearted and hopeful that all of his work is bringing him that much closer to you.

259320.name: Dex
259320.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
At this time, Dex is displaying a very high level of FAS in shelter and tolerates a very limited amount of touch, escalating to some distance increasing behaviors when pet along his lower back and consistently hissing throughout. He is described as a friendly, affectionate, and lazy indoor couch potato who spends most of his time in the living room or bedroom of his home when he is not relaxing by an available window. He plays gently, will fetch items, chase bugs, and chase/pounce on feet. Due to him being reported to eventually warm up to strangers and be friendly and outgoing, playing gently, after he initially is actively avoidant and prefers contact on his own terms, the behavior team feels that these highly reactive and distance increasing behaviors may be shelter-specific. Dex would make a great pet, but is really struggling in the shelter environment. This cat is suitable for adopters with previous cat experience who are willing to work with a cat who needs time and patience to help him adjust to their new home.

259326.name: Ian
259326.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Ian is a sweet, very confident, and friendly cat who was reaching gently through the bars toward the assessor while the assessor was looking at another cat. When the kennel door was opened, Ian stood at the front, looking out, curious and calm. Ian enjoyed all petting, leaning in very nicely for cheek rubs, purring gently, and arching his back with a high tail. He had forward-facing whiskers and a very curious demeanor, and he was looking toward another kennel as if curious whether there was another cat nearby. When picked up, he gave a single meow but was calm and tolerant, and when set back down, he came right back to the front, as curious as ever.

Ian interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am playful and cute!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

259334.name: Socks
259334.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Socks, a cute and young Tuxedo was brought to the care center without any explanation. He was timid upon arrival but became more and more stressed as time went by. He just could not accept the situation he was in... Enrichment and time worked on Socks and I was so pleased to see him playing with me and accepting my petting. He came forward, a little unsure may be, teased a feather wand, accepted head and neck scratches and even made biscuits! The staff who assessed him picked him up without any issue. Way to go, Socks! Socks would love to be home with a new owner who will understand the difficult times he is going through and will give him space and time to adjust to his new life. Socks is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!








What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Socks is at the front of the kennel, pupils slightly dilated and meowing softly at the assessor as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, he leans forward to head bunt the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting with his tail held high. He is able to be pet for a prolonged period, making biscuits as he is pet. Socks is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, displaying slight piloerection at the very base of his tail but continuing to engage with extended petting without any escalation.         

Socks interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that Socks go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression, and overstimulation.

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Harrisa is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Harissa is displaying behaviors that preclude placement in the adoptions room and/or may require further investigation before placement in a home.  He has tried to swat and bite is extremely fearful in the shelter environment and does not currently tolerate petting or handling. The behavior department feels that placement with a New Hope Partner is the best option at this time.  He may have a known history (biting) of behavioral issues that need to be addressed.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Papa Jean on the at risk list for medical reasons. Papa Jean has severe CIRDC and suspected pneumonia. He is not eating. We have started supportive care and injectable antibiotics, but he is not improving. He will need to be hospitalized until he is eating and improving. Behaviorally, he has allowed medical handling. 

Papa Jean came into the care center as an owner surrender due to not having time for him and his behavioral concerns. In the prior Papa jean knows cues "sit and stay" and loves to play fetch with a ball. He has a lot of energy, so walks are very important to him. Papa Jean enjoys quality time with family and will usually be in whatever room people are in. Papa Jean has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

259372.name: Thomas
259372.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
Thomas is laying curled up at the front of the kennel, head up and observing the assessor as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, he gets up, head bunting and leaning his body against the kennel door to solicit attention. He allows all petting, leaning in and raising his back as he is pet, tail held high. With a little coaxing, Thomas calmly walks out of the kennel. He is able to be easily picked up and remains calm when held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front and continues to allow all petting and attention.

Thomas interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Lilo is on the at-risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. She has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to her stress levels, it is in her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with kitten socialization and helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

259391.name: Theodore
259391.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Theodore needs at risk placement for medical reasons. He is a friendly, senior cat with mild chronic kidney disease and a heart murmur. He needs a special diet indefinitely and blood pressure monitoring by a local veterinarian.

A volunteer writes:
Senior Theodore was brought to us as his owner became unable to take care of his pets for quite a while and and was taken into care. A nice person was feeding all these cats, even placed them but Theodore kept in hiding, not willing to leave his home. No wonder he was in shock when he arrived at the care center. His lovely nature, though has surfaced and sweet Theodore leans now into pets, purrs and makes lots of biscuits(see his video). He is a very endearing, loving and lovable gentlecat! Theodore does have a host of medical issues. Among them are his very senior teeth(he eats well, though), a heart murmur with a stressed myocardium(proBNP of 1030) and chronic kidney disease for which he is on a special diet. My heart goes to Theodore who has still a lot of love and gentle companionship to give to the new owner who will give him the chance to feel safe, well cared for and loved. If you are that wonderful person, Theodore(and us) would be blessed to have you meet him at the Manhattan Care Center!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Theodore is laying in his den, eyes wide, pupils dilated, and slightly tense as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and he is spoken to softly, he pokes his head out of the portal exit, slow blinking. He is tolerant of all petting, a bit tense when pet down his shoulders and back but leaning in and closing his eyes when he is pet on the head and cheeks. Theodore is able to be maneuvered out of his den and is tolerant of pickup, tensing but not displaying further issue when held. When he is placed back down, he walks back into his den, curling up and turning to face the back wall, tolerating some more petting on the head before the interaction is ended.

Theodore tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

259394.name: Crush
259394.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Little Crush, a ten month old babe was abandoned at a PETCO store and was brought to the Manhattan Care Center for us to find her a home. She was scared when I first met her but being a youngster, she quickly bounced back! Crush is a pretty tiger, slender, friendly, curious while still a little worried with sudden noises and moves. She enjoys petting and is always ready for treats and more food. Yesterday, she seemed to indicate that she wanted to come on my lap, so I gently picked her up and carried her in my arms(something she did not like in her first days at the care center). She was totally cool with it. We are proud of your progress, little girl!Crush is dreaming of a home sweet home where sge will feel safe and loved. Come and meet her very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!










What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
Crush is inside the cubby sitting up making biscuits. She has forward ears and soft eyes. When the kennel door is opened, she comes forward to greet the assessor, all the while still making biscuits. She allows extended petting on her cheeks and along her body with a high curled tail. During pick up, Crush does tense her body slightly but immediately when set down starts making biscuits again. When the kennel door is closed she rubs her body along the kennel. 

Crush interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

I love to play and will need appropriate toys and positive outlets for my energy.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Shadow is a sweet and slightly shy cat. He was in the den, watchful and calm. He sniffed treats but did not eat them, then allowed petting on his cheek, head, and along his back while remaining calm and lying quietly in place. He ate squeeze-up treats, and when the door was closed, he poked his head out of the side door of the den. Pick-up was not attempted.

Shadow interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

259405.name: Moon Boots
259405.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am not one to sit still and will love interactive playtime in my new home!
Moon Boots is sitting upright at the back of his kennel, observing the assessor with wide eyes as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, he bolts out of the kennel, appearing interested in exploring his surroundings. He is able to be easily picked up and placed back into his kennel. Once back in the kennel, Moon Boots does briefly retreat to the back, sitting upright and tail flicking. He does not escalate and is able to be called to the front of the kennel, where he allows all petting. He is very interested in play, batting at the assessor's hands both while inside of and from outside of the kennel, flopping onto his side as he does so and pouncing. Throughout the day, Moon Boots displays high levels of energy and is observed to pounce and bat at toys, roll around on his side, play with his water bowl, and have general zoomies in his kennel. 

Moon Boots is a fun, playful, social kitty with lots of energy! He interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, and enjoys all petting. We recommend that Moon Boots go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in rough play and high energy cats.

259415.name: Jada
259415.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

White Lightning was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past history in a home environment is unknown. White Lightning has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and has only been allowing for minimal handling from staff. In the kennel, she begins growling, moving away, or retreating to a back corner of her kennel. White Lightning begins growling while dodging leashing attempts, using her front paw to bat at or remove the lead. She has escalated to snapping during leashing; once out of the kennel, she remains highly fearful and shut down, avoiding any form of interaction with handlers. She has also growled at handlers when they approached to interact. Due to these concerns, we recommend that White Lightning be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope Rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification using force-free, positive reinforcement-based training to safely manage/modify any behavior White Lightning presents with outside of the Care Centers.

259423.name: Isabella Rose
259423.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Isabella Rose is laying at the back of her cubby, curled up with her ears forward and a slightly tense body as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she is initially hesitant to interact. Crunchy treats are placed in front of her, and she is softly spoken to. After a couple of minutes of soft talk, Isabella Rose slowly rolls onto her side and gently rubs her face and cheeks against the side wall of the cubby. She allows all petting, leaning in and purring as she is pet before getting up and beginning to eat her crunchy treats. She remains a bit timid throughout the assessment, hesitant to come forward and backing away when noises occur in the room. She shows no signs of escalation and remains receptive to all handling throughout the interaction. It takes a few minutes to coax her out of the cubby and to the main area of the kennel, and she walks up to the front hesitantly before leaning forward and softly head bunting the assessor's hand. She continues to allow and lean into all petting and is able to be easily picked up, slightly tense when she is held but without further issue. When she is placed back into the kennel, Isabella Rose walks back into her cubby, curling up at the back. She continues to lean into petting on the head and cheeks and purrs as she is pet.

Isabella Rose is a sweet, shy, gentle girl who interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

259438.name: Bentley
259438.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Bentley!
Bentley is a 7 month old puppy who arrived at ACC as a stray, so his history is a bit of a mystery. What we do know is that this young pup is full of energy, curiosity, and puppy enthusiasm! Bentley loves to explore, play, and spend time with people, and he is ready to find a family who can help him learn, grow, and channel all that puppy energy in positive ways.

My Ideal Home
Bentley would thrive with an adopter who is excited to continue his training journey. As a young and energetic pup, he will benefit from daily exercise, enrichment activities, and positive reinforcement training to help him practice calm behaviors and good manners. With patience, structure, and plenty of playtime, Bentley is ready to become your lifelong adventure buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
Bentley's history with other animals is unknown, but he has shown interest in meeting other dogs while at the shelter. He may benefit from slow introductions and continued positive reinforcement to help him learn polite play and social skills.

Good with Kids?
Due to Bentley's high energy level and tendency to become overexcited, an adult only home is recommended at this time. He would do best with people who can help him practice impulse control and set him up for success as he grows into adulthood.

Things to Know
Bentley is a fun loving pup with a big personality packed into a puppy sized body! He can get a little too excited when greeting people and is working on learning that four paws on the floor gets him even more attention. Bentley loves toys, treats, and learning new skills, and with the right guidance, this energetic boy is sure to be a star in his new home.

259450.name: Amora
259450.summary:
My foster writes:
This gorgeous mini panther is looking for the right adopter who will provide a patient and stable home. This spicy tiny tiger is still in need of that breakthrough, where she learns that human hands are the source of a great many pleasures. She loves to eat, and she learned that I bring yummy things. She especially likes quality wet food, roast chicken and baby food. She is super energetic and loves to play with string toys that are pulled along and jiggled, I used twine and shoe laces. She loses herself, forgets she is afraid and rolls around, jumps and gets closer to me then she would otherwise. She is easy to love, so fierce and beautiful! I wish that she find that person who can get her to that place, where she accepts caressing, love and companionship and finds comfort. Thank you for loving her and taking the time, whoever you are.
Amora tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

259467.name: Kayda
259467.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Kayda is on the at-risk list for medical concerns. Kayda is one of two kittens in a litter that has been diagnosed with ringworm. Ringworm is difficult to effectively treat and manage in the current shelter population due to overpopulation, staffing, resources. Placement would include topical and oral treatment as well as veterinary follow-up.

Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

259474.name: Tesoro
259474.summary:
A volunteer writes: Tesoro is a sweet girl only about a year old. I found her lounging peacefully on her bed and she was very relaxed. Despite going through a lot she was so so sweet towards me. This youngin has a lot of love to give. She is curious as she peeks her head into the hallways and also rolls on her back showing her silly side. This sweet girl is looking for his forever home.

Another volunteer writes:
Tesoro is a little treasure as indicated by her given name. She was seen being attacked by a dog in a park. Not much harm was done, just a scrape on her chin but she was terrified when the rangers picked her up. It looks that Tesoro put her ordeal way behind her. She is one lively and friendly little gal, quite  welcoming and ready to play. She is as sweet a pie and even comes in the arms. Tesoro has a scar on her left eye, likely the result of a past eye infection when she was a kitten. She is otherwise a healthy(although a little underweight) young gal who aced her behavior evaluation and so would love to be a happy member of your family. Come and meet sweet Tesoro at the Manhattan Care Center!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Tesoro is laying at the front of her kennel, getting up and meowing softly at the assessor as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, she stretches before leaning forward to head bunt the assessor's hand. Tesoro allows and leans into all petting, raising her back as she is pet. She is easy to pick up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into her kennel, Tesoro remains at the front, continuing to head bunt and lean into all further petting. When the interaction is ended and the kennel door is closed, she stands at the front of the kennel and softly meows to solicit further attention.

Tesoro interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

259476.name: Apollo
259476.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Apollo is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Apollo has shown fearful behavior and difficulty walking in and out of the kennel area, including dodging the leash, balking, refusing to walk, and becoming overwhelmed by barking dogs and sudden sounds. More recently, Apollo has become highly aroused around other dogs, hard barking, pulling, thrashing, rolling, and attempting to back out of the leash. Outside of these moments, Apollo is social and affectionate with handlers, leaning into petting and seeking attention. Medically, Apollo is apparently healthy.

Apollo came into the QUACC after being brought in as a stray. In the care centers, Apollo has been fearful and hesitant to leave his kennel, requiring leash pressure and coaxing to walk. Once out of the kennel and given time to warm up, he becomes more social and will lean into petting and solicit attention from staff. As a result, we recommend Apollo is placed with one of our New Hope Partners.

259488.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Cash is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the prior home, Cash was reported to display significant resource guarding, particularly around his crate. Cash has a reported history of three bite incidents, including one that occurred when someone attempted to remove him from his crate. All reported bites were bite-and-release incidents. Cash does interact with most enrichment items given to him, especially food based enrichment Medically, Cash was matted, but was recently shaved.

Cash was surrendered by his previous owner due to behavior concerns. His previous family describes him as a fearful dog who would spend most of his time around his people, in the living room, and in his crate. Cash is reported to have a multiple bite history; all three bites were bite and releases and did break skin. He is reported to not have allowed any form of Grooming and did bite as a result, as a resource guarder that would guard food, toys, treats, and his crate. One of Cash's bite incidents was due to a friend of the owner trying to remove him from his crate. His previous owner noted that getting in and being in a car makes Cash nervous, but he would love to greet his family when they came home and loved playing with hard toys that he could throw in the air and Chase. Due to the multiple Behavior concerns noted in his previous home, we recommend for Chase to be placed in an adult-only home where he can be the only dog through a New Hope Rescue partner that can address Cash's Behavior concerns with the use of a certified professional trainer or behaviorist that utilizes positive reinforcement methods only.

259495.name: Sherly
259495.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Sherly, a pretty calico girl was surrendered into our care because of her building no pet policy. She comes with lovely comments and would be very friendly, outgoing and playful with all including strangers, cats and kids. Sherly is not a happy camper at the care center, though. She sits at the back of her cubby, most often shrunk in a small loaf, one eye half closed, something I have noticed in many stressed kitties. She does slow blink in response to gentle words and occasionally will tilt her head toward my hand. She misses her family, she misses home and she does not know how to get her life back...We are trying to make her feel better, give her hope while waiting for a new owner, a new family to give her the chance to be once again a beloved pet! Ask about Sherly when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
Sherly is laying in the back of her den, eyes wide, pupils dilated, body tense and scrunching her face as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and the den door is lifted, she shuffles herself to lean closer to the back wall of the den. She is softly spoken to, and a squeeze up is offered, but she does not respond to them. With some more soft talk, Sherly begins to return some slow blinks. She allows all petting, a bit tense when pet down her shoulders and back but leaning in and closing her eyes when she is pet on the head and cheeks. She is unable to coax from the back of the den, so full pickup is unable to be attempted. She is able to be lightly lifted off of the ground from within her den, tensing slightly but showing no further issue. 

Sherly tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

259513.name: Leon
259513.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Leon was recently returned to the care center following concerning behaviors in the home. Leon quickly escalated to biting when they attempted to remove him from the couch and when they attempted to take a toy from him. These bites did not break skin but did leave a scar from his teeth grazing them. During his previous stay in the care center, Leon was noted to snap at the handler when they picked him up to return him to kennel. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only home.

259525.name: Cam
259525.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Cam is on the at-risk list due to behavior. He is not thriving in the care center and continues to display distance-increasing behavior when approached for interactions. He has not warmed up despite staff using treats to build a positive association. Due to his stress levels, it is in his best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. He would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give him plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with kitten socialization and helping a fearful cat adjust to strangers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
 Cam appears to be fearful and given his age at the time of the assessment (10 weeks old) we believe that he hasn't had much human interaction up to this point and as a result is under-socialized; a condition that should be temporary if he is given appropriate interactions. During the assessment he was tense and avoided contact. He needs intensive socialization at the present time. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents who are preferably familiar with kitten socialization or are open to detailed counseling by staff.

259528.name: Sage
259528.summary: Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconozole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

259543.name: Missy
259543.summary:
Meet Missy!  Missy is friendly with new people, though she prefers to approach on her own terms. She may be a little shy around children at first, but her curiosity usually wins out. She has lived happily with other cats and enjoys their company, though she has no experience with dogs.

This sweet girl loves gentle play, happily uses scratching posts, and isn't picky about her food or litter setup. She has no history of biting or scratching. Missy can become vocal when being placed into a carrier.  Missy does have on-going medical issues that will need attention.

If you're looking for an affectionate young cat who enjoys companionship while still appreciating a little independence, Missy is ready to find a home to call her own.

259551.name: Papa
259551.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Papa is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Papa has displayed significant dog-directed reactivity, including kennel fighting, hard barking, muzzle punching kennel doors, and digging toward a neighboring dog in his kennel. He has also redirected onto a handler's leg while being moved away from another dog, though no skin was broken. Outside of these situations, Papa is easy to leash, social, and engages with handlers. Medically, Papa is apparently healthy.

Papa was surrendered into care due to his owner becoming homeless. Papa was described as very affectionate by his previous family. He is reported to love car rides and long days at the park at least 3 times a day. Papa is reported not to get along with unfamiliar dogs due to an altercation with another dog in the past.  During his stay in care, Papa has been easy to remove from the kennel and readily accepts treats. He has shown kennel reactivity with one select neighboring dog in the room. He has escalated to redirecting and biting a staff member on the leg as a result of his kennel fighting. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Papa be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.


What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.

259571.name: Bagheera
259571.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Bagheera , a young and handsome Tuxedo can often be found snoozing soundly, smudged against one of his kennel's windows. He is all surprised when I come in as a guest, initially retreating to the back of his cubby but shortly after, coming to meet me upfront as I speak softly to him. Bagheera starts rolling on his side, head bunting my hand, purring and really enjoying our encounter. Me too!!!Bagheera is with us for no fault of his own. An elderly relative, very allergic to cats, moved in with his owners and poor Bagheera was brought to the care center but with great comments from his former family. A funny note..Bagheera would love to be dressed and was brought in with many clothing items. I am not sure I would recommend this practice but as a young teen, I used to dress my very first cat, a Tuxedo too... Bagheera is apparently healthy, already neutered, did well on his behavior evaluation and is 100% ready to go home with you!. Come and meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!



What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I lived with children in my previous home.

259579.name: Raven
259579.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Raven is a beautiful and unusual looking cat dressed in a shiny pitch black coat. He truly reminds me of a black panther of the friendly kind. Raven was surrendered with some housemates as his house counted too many cats. More are still to join him. Raven was sooo shy upon arrival at the care center and yesterday, I was so happy to see his transformation(after a few prompts) into a sweet, friendly and quite loving kitty, leaning into pets, head bunting my hand, purring and rolling on his kennel floor for more petting(see photos and video). Raven lived with adults, a child, many cats and even dogs. He is described by his former owners as a lap cat, quiet, friendly, affectionate, independent too and staying where people are. He would not be too fond of dogs, though. He has a history of voiding outside the litter box but who knows how many cats he had to share this box with? Raven is using his litter box at the care center. Raven is apparently healthy(he does have a crinkled right ear, the result of an ear infection, untreated), will soon be neutered and did well on his behavior evaluation showing his shy side. He is ready to go home with you!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I lived with children in my previous home.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have lived with dogs in my previous home.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!

259590.name: Furcules
259590.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Furcules was surrendered as a stray, but he spent 2 weeks in his finder's home. The finder described him as a generally nervous dog who was scared of loud noises, was not picky about food or treats, and had a low energy level. During his stay in care, Fercules has been observed to warm up slowly to handlers, taking some time to acclimate before seeking attention or displaying social behavior. When introduced to novel stimuli, Fercules reverts to his fearful behaviors, seeking an exit, including when in calmer environments like the behavior office and during walks outside. Due to these concerns, we recommend for Furcules to be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

259598.name: Nicky
259598.summary:
My foster writes:
Meet Nicky 🐾🤍 a tiny little gentleman with a surprisingly big personality. He's curious, chatty, affectionate, and very serious about supervising whatever his human is doing, especially if it involves eating, applying make-up or a bathroom. 😂
He loves exploring, following you around, and having little conversations with you through his adorable meows. Give him a good play session and he's perfectly happy curling up afterward for a well-earned nap. He is very funny; has an extra little toe and will make you laugh out loud at his cute actions.
Nicky has been through a big change after losing his previous owner, but he still has so much love and companionship to give. He's the kind of cat whose little presence very quickly becomes part of your everyday routine.
He doesn't just want a home - he wants his person. 🥹
If you're looking for a sweet, funny little companion who will keep you company, make you laugh, and quietly steal your heart, Nicky might just be your boy. 🤍🐈
With a little bit of patience, kind words and slow blinks, Nicky will very quickly become your new best friend.

259600.name: Micky
259600.summary:
Just like his adorable thumbs and extra toes, Micky is one-of-a-kind! Micky is the perfect mix of playful, affectionate, and wonderfully goofy. He loves spending time with his favorite people, soaking up cheek and chin scratches, chasing his beloved feather wand toy, and curling up beside you after a fun play session-often in the funniest sleeping positions!
This handsome polydactyl kitty is incredibly smart, learns quickly, is wonderfully well-behaved, and has never had a litter box accident. While he can be a little shy in new situations, with patience and love his sweet personality shines through. Before long, he'll be following you from room to room, quietly keeping you company and showing just how deeply he loves his people.

Marcus is a 7-month-old male dog looking for an experienced, committed adopter who understands the needs of an energetic adolescent dog. As a young dog, Marcus is still learning appropriate behaviors and will require consistent training, structure, and clear boundaries to help him mature into a well-rounded companion.

In his previous home, Marcus displayed significant mouthy behavior that escalated to biting, resulting in bruising and broken skin. He has also shown resource guarding tendencies with stolen items, particularly paper towels, so his new family should be prepared to safely manage his environment and work on behavior modification using positive, reward-based training techniques. Marcus has also been reported to be destructive in the home when his physical and mental needs are not being met.

Marcus will thrive with an owner who is experienced in canine behavior and committed to providing daily exercise, enrichment, training, and supervision. Puzzle toys, interactive games, training sessions, and appropriate chew items will be important outlets for his energy and intelligence. Because of his behavior history, Marcus is best suited for a home that can provide patient, consistent guidance and continue helping him develop appropriate coping skills.

With the right adopter who is willing to invest the time and effort into his training, Marcus has the potential to make meaningful progress and grow into a successful lifelong companion.

259640.name: Ocean
259640.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Ocean is laying in his litter box, slightly tense with his face scrunched and his ears facing to the sides as the assessor approaches. The cubby door is opened, and he is spoken to softly, and after a few minutes he hesitantly approaches the front of the cubby. Ocean is initially tense and stiff before appearing to settle and allowing all petting, leaning in when he is pet on the head and cheeks. After he is pet, his ears go into a neutral, forward position. He is tolerant of pickup, slightly tense but calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he moved to go stand at the back of the top cubby. With more soft talk he is able to be coaxed forward again, continuing to lean into more petting on the head and cheeks.

Ocean interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

259647.name: Benji
259647.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Benji is laying on top of his kuranda bed as the assessor approaches, eyes wide and pupils dilated. When the kennel door is opened and he is softly spoken to, he is initially a bit tense. After a few minutes of soft talk, he flops onto his side, rubbing his cheeks against the side of the kuranda bed. He allows and leans into all petting, head bunting the assessor's hand and continuing to roll around on his side. He does tail flick throughout the interaction but does not escalate even with extended petting. He allows the assessor to pick him up from on top of the kuranda bed, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into his kennel, he continues to allow and lean into all further petting. 

Benji interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bananabelle was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is unknown. During her stay in care, Bananabelle has been highly fearful and shut down. She avoids all forms of interaction, and when off leash in the behavior office, she will flee from handlers when they approach. Due to her level of fearfulness, we recommend an adult-only home for Bananabelle through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home after she has had time to decompress and acclimate at her own pace.

259666.name: Mabel
259666.summary:
A  volunteer writes:
Ten month old Tasmanian was left at a veterinary clinic and never picked up....Such a cute little tiger, so shy but so sweet too. When I first met Tasmanian, she was at the back of her cubby but sweet talks and a few Temptations got her moving, slowly dropping on her sight and enjoying petting. She even followed me to her main cabin where I rewarded her with Squeeze ups. Tasmanian is so pretty. I love the pale orange "feather" she has in the middle of her forehead. Tasmanian is a healthy little gal who still needs her spay. She did well on her behavior evaluation just stressing her timid side and would love to meet a lovely family who will appreciate how sweet she is and give her time to adjust to her new life with them. Tasmanian is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!






What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
Tazmanian is laying curled up at the back of her top cubby, resting her head on her front paws as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she initially gets up, tail tucked and walking to the other side of the kennel to avoid contact. With soft talk she begins to slowly roll around on her side. She is tolerant of all petting, leaning in when she is pet on the head and cheeks but mildly tense when she is pet down her back. She is able to be easily picked up, slightly tense when she is held but without further issue. When she is placed back into her kennel, Tazmanian walks back into her cubby, tail tucked. She continues to allow and lean into further petting on the head and cheeks.

Tazmanian tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

Snickers is an eight month old little tiger who was found outside a very large apartment complex. A Good Samaritan saw how frail and underweight she was and brought her to the Manhattan Care Center to give her the TLC she so much needed. Snickers had been freshly spayed, something quite strange but that makes her ready to go home with you right away. Snickers is curious and enjoys her cuddles while she can be a little skittish with sudden noises and moves. Who knows what kind of life she lived and "treatment" she got before her savior took her to safety. Snickers is ravenous for food and we are hoping that very soon her weight will go up! Snickers will thrive better in a quiet home without boisterous small children and with a new owner who will give her time to trust and adjust to her new life. Snickers is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!

I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

259676.name: Jeter
259676.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Jeter!
Jeter came to the shelter as a stray, so his past is a mystery, but he's already winning people over with his friendly personality. Even while recovering medically, he's been a sweet, wiggly boy who happily greets handlers with a wagging tail and enjoys gentle affection. This all-star pup is ready to step up to the plate and find a loving home of his own.

My Ideal Home
Jeter would love an adopter who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement as he continues to settle into home life. Long walks, food puzzles, and interactive games will help keep his body and mind active. Most of all, he's looking for someone who will cheer him on every step of the way.

Good with Other Pets?
Because Jeter arrived as a stray, his history with other animals is unknown. Slow introductions to any resident pets are recommended to help everyone get off to a great start.

Good with Kids?
Jeter has been friendly and tolerant with the people he's met at the shelter. As with any new dog, respectful introductions and supervision are recommended while everyone gets to know one another.

Things to Know
Jeter walks nicely on leash with only mild pulling, knows "sit," and takes treats gently from your hand. He has been easy to handle during his medical care and enjoys leaning into attention from his favorite people. As he continues recovering and settling into a home, his personality will only continue to shine. If you're looking for an MVP to join your family, Jeter is ready to knock it out of the park!

259697.name: Caramel
259697.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Caramel is a quiet, low-energy dog who enjoys a relaxed lifestyle and is happiest lounging or resting in his crate, where he feels safe and secure. He is crate trained, walks well on a leash with minimal pulling, and knows the cue "sit." 

Since arriving at the care center, Caramel is still adjusting to his new environment and has been extremely fearful. He is currently uncomfortable with handling and grooming, including bathing, brushing, and nail trims. His fear has also extended to leash handling, and when he becomes overwhelmed, he may escalate to snapping at the leash. Caramel will benefit from a patient, understanding adopter who can give him time to decompress, build trust at his own pace, and use positive reinforcement to help him feel safe. With consistency, a predictable routine, and a calm home environment, Caramel has the potential to become a loyal companion once he learns that he can trust the people around him.

259716.name: Legend
259716.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Legend is a skinny(but cute) little guy with a serious face and a frown that do not match his welcoming personality. He is uncomfortable, not with us but with his itchy skin that brought him to the care center as his owner could not handle Legend's dermatological issue. Legend is lively, itchy and as hungry as a bear, kind of small and a bit too thin for his age of two. He really cares being attended too, petted and "scratched" and would not might exploring the premises outside his kennel. He is presently observed in our medical room, fed a special diet and treated with oral steroids in the hope that his skin condition (thought to be the result of allergies) will get better. Legend is an endearing little mensh who is said to be a sweet and friendly pet but would prefer to be the one and only in the house. He will soon need a home sweet home. May be it could be with you? Legend is at the Manhattan Care Center dreaming of a peaceful place and loving family...









What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other pets.
Legend is at the front of the kennel, patting at the corner of the door to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he gives a gentle head bunt, allowing and leaning into all petting. He calmly exits the kennel, doing a big stretch forward before leaning against the assessor. He is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he repeatedly attempts to exit but is tolerant of maneuvering back into the kennel with minimal issue. He leans into all further petting, beginning to purr as he is pet.

Legend interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

259750.name: Bon Bon
259750.summary:
My Boroughbreaker writes: Bon Bon is an incredibly happy, cuddly puppy dog! I am genuinely surprised she hasn't been adopted yet. She won over the hearts of so many strangers throughout central park, getting belly rubs and comments on how beautiful she is (especially her eyes). Bon Bon loves everyone that wants to give her attention, she was very social! Her desire and excitement to be close to you translates into some puppy behaviors like jumping, but once we got some energy out, she listened to "down" and "sit" every time. In the beginning of our walk, she would stop and stare at other dogs with a stiff body until they passed. At the end of the day, she would still stop at the sight of another dog, but she was much more relaxed and nonreactive even when small dogs barked at her on the sidewalk. I did not hear her bark all day! I believe she would be dog friendly with a proper introduction by a trainer. Bon was a chaser of squirrels and obsessed with the ducks swimming in the water. It was very cute watching her curiosity about the creatures in and around the lake. Many people expressed wanting to take her home on our walk back! She brightened many people's day that day, I know Bon Bon will make an excellent new member to anyone's home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am playful and cute!

259751.name: Frisbee
259751.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Frisbee was brought into the care center as a stray. He was initially friendly and tolerant of handling from staff. He quickly deteriorated in care becoming highly over aroused when being taken out of kennel, leash-biting intensely and jumping over 5 feet in the air. He has shown some on-leash reactivity, pulling towards other dogs, difficult to break his focus. Medically, he has mild entropion and was treated for otitis externa. 

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Frisbee is a handsome boy who initially greeted shelter staff with friendly behavior and was tolerant of handling. As his stay in the shelter continued, however, the stress of the environment began to affect him significantly. Frisbee has developed behaviors such as leash biting and becomes highly aroused when staff attempt to remove him from his kennel. At this time, he is difficult to redirect with treats or toys and is capable of jumping very high at the front of his kennel, making handling and kennel exits challenging.

When Frisbee is able to settle outside of his kennel, he has shown an aloof but relaxed demeanor during socialization. He would likely benefit from leaving the shelter environment and decompressing in a patient, structured home. His adopters should be prepared to work with him on leash manners and handling while providing consistency, positive reinforcement, and time to adjust to his new surroundings.

He quickly deteriorated in care becoming highly over aroused when being taken out of kennel, leash-biting intensely and jumping over 5 feet in the air. He has shown some on-leash reactivity, pulling towards other dogs, difficult to break his focus. Medically, he has mild entropion and was treated for otitis externa. This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Frisbee is a handsome boy who initially greeted shelter staff with friendly behavior and was tolerant of handling. As his stay in the shelter continued, however, the stress of the environment began to affect him significantly. Frisbee has developed behaviors such as leash biting and becomes highly aroused when staff attempt to remove him from his kennel. At this time, he is difficult to redirect with treats or toys and is capable of jumping very high at the front of his kennel, making handling and kennel exits challenging. When Frisbee is able to settle outside of his kennel, he has shown an aloof but relaxed demeanor during socialization. He would likely benefit from leaving the shelter environment and decompressing in a patient, structured home. His adopters should be prepared to work with him on leash manners and handling while providing consistency, positive reinforcement, and time to adjust to his new surroundings.

259760.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response. Pre-Screener Form

Nyla is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Nyla has not acclimated well to the shelter environment despite best efforts to keep her comfortable. She has displayed high levels of anxiety and arousal, which has mainly manifested as leash biting. Nyla has been loose and wiggly with handlers, but she has become increasingly difficult to remove from the kennel due to the intensity of her leash biting and is unable to be redirected with treats or toys. On one occasion, during her leash biting, Nyla's teeth grazed a staff member's hand when they were attempting to leash her for her midday walk. Medically, Nyla is being treated CIRDC.

Nyla was surrendered into care due to her owner being evicted. Nyla's previous family described her as a social, affectionate, active, playful, quiet, and lazy couch potato who spends most of her time roaming around her home or following her people. She loves bath time and water, allows her family to bathe her, brush her, and trim her nails, and was accustomed to going on 1-2 walks a day for 20 mins at a time. During her stay in care, Nyla has been wiggly with handlers, but she displays a low threshold for arousal that has manifested as leash biting and high levels of anxiety. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Nyla be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner where she can have time and space for her to decompress and acclimate at her own pace.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!

259766.name: Billy Jr
259766.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Billy Jr is a very shy cat who hides from strangers and will warm up when he gets to know the person...You can imagine what being relinquished into a shelter environment can do to that kind of cat...Just look at Billy Jr's photo. A beautiful ginger cramped at the back of his hiding box, softly hissing and grumbling when his door is open. Billy Jr came with Oreo with whom he got along well. He might very well be the father of the five little ones she delivered at the care center. Billy Jr's owner told us that he liked feather  and catnip toys and for the first time, yesterday, I saw a spark in his eyes when I waved a feather wand in front of him. No hiss, no grumble and he even touched the feather. Billy Jr was found to be FIV+ on a SNAP test. FIV+ can cats can live a very normal and long life and coexist with non FIV+ cats. We hope that Billy Jr will show further improvement during his stay with us but a caring, patient and understanding new owner is what he truly needs to be a happy pet. If you believe you can help Billy Jr, come and meet him at the Manhattan Care Center.






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

259804.name: Tank
259804.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Tank is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Tank has shown fearful behavior, including avoiding the leash, retreating within his kennel, and presenting with a tense body and tucked tail around unfamiliar handlers. Tank has shown steady improvement over time, becoming more comfortable approaching handlers for treats, accepting handling, and walking calmly once out of his kennel but is still struggling to acclimate in the care center environment. Medically, Tank has Ataxia.

Tank was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Tank has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. He has whale-eyed and moved to the back of his kennel when a handler approaches. During his medical exam, Tank was growling and hard staring at handlers when they approached his kennel. He escalated to snapping and attempting to bite during muzzling attempts, prompting for him to be sedated for the exam due to his behavior. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Pre-Screener Form

Roy is at risk due to behavioral concerns in the care center. Roy is displaying on-leash reactivity toward other dogs characterized by growling, barking, lunging, baring teeth. He has also lunged toward people with an open mouth on walks. During his behavioral assessment, he displayed resource guarding by becoming tense and snapping at the assess-a-hand while holding a toy. Roy has also shown fearful behavior around handling, avoiding the leash, planting during walks, and requiring treats to distract him for leashing. Roy is noted to headwhip when touched on his head but will allow the handler to pet by his tail. Medically, Roy has recently recovered from CIRDC and is healthy at this time. 

Roy came into the care center as a stray with Joy, Due to this his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Roy has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake and noted to have to be belly band when taken back to kennel. Recently Roy has become highly on leash reactive. Noted to lunge at people with an open mouth and pull very hard towards other dogs while growling, barking, lunging, and baring teeth. When pulled away the dogs, Roy pulls back towards them repeatedly and continues hard barking. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Roy has also shown fearful behavior around handling, avoiding the leash, planting during walks, and requiring treats to distract him for leashing. Roy is noted to headwhip when touched on his head but will allow the handler to pet by his tail. Medically, Roy has recently recovered from CIRDC and is healthy at this time. Roy came into the care center as a stray with Joy, Due to this his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Roy has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake and noted to have to be belly band when taken back to kennel. Recently Roy has become highly on leash reactive. Noted to lunge at people with an open mouth and pull very hard towards other dogs while growling, barking, lunging, and baring teeth. When pulled away the dogs, Roy pulls back towards them repeatedly and continues hard barking. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
