259832.name: Linda
259832.summary:
Linda tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. It is also of note that due to her leg injury and her splint - she has limited mobility and cannot really remove herself from interactions if she desires. Based off of the behavior observed at the time of the assessment, the behavior team feels that Linda would do best with an experienced adopter in an adult-only home.

A volunteer writes: Linda's a very sweet looking cat even though she's been looking a little worse for wear. Between her cone and the stitches on her little leg, she looks like she could just use a little break. It's been a long road, but she's well on her way! Linda was found injured on her own and was brought to us for some much needed help. Since she's gotten situated with her paw fracture, we can focus on the very big and important job of helping her to find a forever family to call her own. When I met Linda, she was snuggled in the back of her condo, but she looked out at me curiously. Linda's hoping to find a calm and patient forever home where she can fully recover and become her best kitty self.

259843.name: Champion
259843.summary:
My foster writes:
Champion is a great dog, He is very obedient, ( sit, wait , place etc ) and well behaved. 100 percent house trained. After long walks, or plays in the yard, he just wanted to sleep by human. He also allowed all handlings. It did not look he is used to riding a car. He was nervous on the trip from/to our house - MACC. but stayed calm in the car. When he met my dog through a gate, he got excited, and wanted to say hi to her. His body was not tense, I did not see any concerning body languages, he did not get vocal. We passed several dogs during walks and he was also calm. I would say he can go to a beginner adopter/ foster, his anxiety in the crate can be a bit challenging, though.

My boroughbreak buddy writes:

Champion was the best doggy on our Boroughbreak. He did so well on walks, knowing when to stop and go and listening to commands. He was able to calmly walk past any barking dogs(mainly small ones) that we passed. He was interested in larger dogs that we either passed by on our walk or saw at the Barking Dog when we ate lunch and would sometimes making a whining noise occasionally. He showed me his sit and shake(both paws!) tricks, and would lay and lounge whenever we were sitting. I noted he did not poop or pee at all while we were out. I tried bringing him to grassy areas, and he would just sniff around. He ate a few of his treats but had a lot left. He ate grilled chicken at the Barking Dog but waited until it was cooler. I got him a pup cup there too, but he licked it twice and decided he wasn't interested. A nice sales associate at Ulta offered him a dog treat, but again he licked it and wasn't interested. Champion never barked, pulled too much except slightly when he saw a big dog but would come when he was called a few times. He was friendly and receptive to any humans who approached him like the waitress. He has such an easygoing and sweet demeanor with the best doggy manners. I want him to go to a loving home but also 10/10 would Boroughbreak with him again!!!

This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Chonks is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Chonks has shown concerning behavior in kennel, including lunging and snapping toward two staff members as she was being removed. It is unclear if she may have been guarding her bedding or a toy at the time. She has also recently been reported to vocalize and pull toward other dogs on walks and now towards strangers.. Outside of this incident, Chonks has been social and affectionate with handlers, approaching for attention, leaning into petting, and taking treats readily but is struggling to acclimate. Medically, Chonks is Overweight has suspected allergies, dermatitis.

Chonks was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Chonks presented as intially fearful and was noted to hard-bark and bare her teeth in her kennel when approached before being leashed for her medical exam. She has shown the potential to be social in calmer, quieter settings when allowed to approach on her own terms and reward-based interactions with handlers. She readily accepts treats and will solicit brief petting before walking away. Chonks escalated to lunging and snapping at staff after being removed from her kennel, but allowed handlers to treat and trail her out of the kennel. On walks, she has been reported to vocalize and pull towards other dogs. Due ot these concerns, we recommend that Chonks be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

A volunteer writes: Wave 🌊 is indeed a great name for this boy: he can be both a gentle, calm boy and a happy joyful kiddo when it's time to play. While I love walking this mellow, lovely boy, it's when we sit on a stoop for pets and he leans his chin on my leg and softens fully into my legs that I truly feel the blessing of this sweet ocean boy. There is no doubt Wave's love language is touch and I am so glad to be the lucky recipient. 

Wave was surrendered with another dog (Surfer 259850). He has done well when meeting female dogs.

259850.name: Surfer
259850.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Surfer!
Surfer came to ACC when his owner could no longer care for him, and this sweet, easygoing boy is ready to ride the wave into his forever home. He has a gentle nature, loves spending time with people, and is happiest when he's soaking up attention, belly rubs, and tasty treats. With his big smile and affectionate personality, Surfer is sure to make a splash wherever he goes.

My Ideal Home
Surfer is looking for a family that can provide plenty of love, daily enrichment, and positive reinforcement as he continues learning and growing. He enjoys getting out for walks, exploring his surroundings, and relaxing with his favorite people after a day of adventure. He recently even learned to "sit" and is excited to keep adding new tricks to his repertoire!

Good with Other Pets?
Surfer's history with other pets is unknown, but he has shown friendly interest in meeting dogs while at ACC. He may do well with a compatible canine companion after slow introductions and thoughtful management.

Good with Kids?
Surfer's history with children is unknown, but he has been friendly and social with the people he's met. As with any new pet, slow introductions and respectful interactions are recommended.

Things to Know
Surfer is a gentle, affectionate pup who loves treats, cozy couch time, and exploring the world around him. His Boroughbreaker shared that he was a wonderful houseguest who was potty trained, great in the car, and loved meeting new people. He's still polishing up his leash manners, but with his sweet personality and eagerness to learn, Surfer is ready to catch the perfect wave straight into a loving home.

My Boroughbreaker Says...
Surfer was the sweetest dog! He was wonderful in the car, loved meeting new people, and happily curled up on the couch for belly rubs. He was fully potty trained, did great with stairs, and even learned to sit during his Boroughbreak. He enjoys treats, taking time to sniff on walks, and after settling in, he relaxed beautifully around the apartment. Any family would be lucky to have this gentle, loving boy.

A volunteer writes: There have been some texts going around between volunteers recently regarding Surfer with phrases like "perfect boy" and "LOVE him" being used. I myself might have even written "I would adopt this boy if I were looking". 

Why are we so smitten? Is it his soulful hazel eyes or the way his ears fold back so daintily? Or is it the way he leans into you when you sit with him, watching dogs and people walk by but opting to stay right where he is for some good scritches? 

Really, though, we're probably just scratching the surface of all the wonderful things Surfer is, things his very lucky adopter will find out.

Surfer came to us with Wave (259849) mid July and what we know about him indicate a hard life pre-shelter: an arrested owner,  unwanted by the person he was left with, unfed for two days before the police were called to pick him and Wave up, both of them fearful on the transport to the shelter. 

And yet in the shelter's care he has been noted to be loose in his body and gentle with treats during assessments and is walkable by our newest volunteers. He loves human attention and walks loosely on leash and is a snuggle king. 
Surfer is available to a Level 1 adopter. He is currently living in a pop up crate & his adoption fee is waived as part of the shelter's pop up promotion. His adopter will also receive a $50 Chewy gift card.

259851.name: Evening
259851.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

A volunteer writes: Meet our sweet boy Evening! Barely out of kittenhood, this tabby teenager is a shy-at-first cat who quickly warms up after being treated to a yummy squeeze-up (he'll lick it up fast!) and some pettings by human hand. Keep giving him pets on his head and back, and he'll remain chill, happily soaking up all the attention. Evening did well on his behavior exam, and our team deemed him to be a good fit in most households, thanks to his calm and tolerant demeanor. Come on New York, don't let this good boy wait any longer. Arrange for a meet and greet with Mr. Evening today!
Evening tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

A volunteer writes:
Sheeba and housemate Hunter were brought to the Manhattan Care Center as their owner was displaced. Sheeba is a beautiful and friendly silver grey kitty girl who enjoys company, petting and play. She comes right away to meet her visitor, stretches, head bunts and plays, plays, plays with a featherwand(see her video). 259922.name: Parker
259922.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Parker, a handsome young tiger was left behind when the bodega he "worked in" closed down. The new store owner allowed him to stay but in the end Parker was  brought to the care center as the hustle and bustle of the business was not to his like. Parker was a bit nervous upon arrival and for days but time and enrichment did their job. He is now quite welcoming, meeting his visitor at the kennel door, enjoying company(I love the way he closes his eyes and leans with petting) as well as playing actively with a feather wand(see photos). He loves treats of all kinds and chomped heartily special food while being petted. Most cats go through a lot before arriving at the shelter and being in a cage  does not help despite all the care and the attention we are trying to give them. Parker is likely an independent kitty who enjoys nevertheless very much company, love and play when it is mutually agreed upon. Just like us....A low traffic(without young kids) while mentally and physically stimulating home and an experienced new owner will be the perfect fit for a happy Parker! Come and meet him very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!









What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have potential behavior challenges that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.
I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

259934.name: Papaya
259934.summary:
Meet Papaya!

Papaya is a sweet, affectionate kitten who is ready to bring plenty of love and fun to her new home! She has lived indoors with both adults and children and is described as friendly, talkative, playful, and a true lap kitten. While she may hide briefly when meeting new people, she warms up quickly and enjoys being part of the family.

My Ideal Home

Papaya would do well in just about any home looking for an active, affectionate companion. She loves attention, enjoys being held, purrs happily during cuddles, and is always ready for playtime. She's curious, people-oriented, and would make a wonderful addition to a family or individual looking for an interactive kitten.

Good with Kids?

Yes! Papaya previously lived with children and is reported to be friendly and outgoing once she's had a little time to settle in.

Good with Other Pets?

Papaya has no known experience living with cats or dogs, so slow, supervised introductions are recommended if there are other pets in the home.

Overall Health

Papaya is a healthy, weaned kitten with a good prognosis. She is up to date on her initial veterinary care, including vaccines and parasite prevention. She currently has a temporary spay waiver due to a Department of Health rabies observation hold and will need to be spayed once the hold has been lifted.

Hi there! My name is Papaya and I've been at the Queens ACC since July (yes, you read that right)! I arrived as a stray so the staff don't know what my life was like before coming to ACC, but I had various injuries that I'm recovering from really well. I only require a little extra paperwork to be filled out and a few extra vet visits this year because one of my injuries was likely a bite wound (now fully healed). I'm thankful for everyone at ACC taking such good care of me, but I think I'd like to find my forever home now. So what are you waiting for? Ask about me today!

259937.name: Nefera
259937.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Nefera came into the care center as an owner surrender. Her previous owner described her as a social, affectionate, active, playful, and vocal dog with her person. She spends most her time in the bedroom. Due to all noted concerns displayed in a home environment and during her stay in care, the behavior department recommends Nefera be placed with a New Hope placement partner who is able to provide an experienced adult-only foster home. A period of decompression is recommended to allow her to acclimate comfortably to her new environment; force-free, reward-based training only is advised when introducing Nefera to new and unfamiliar situations. Consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Nefera presents with outside of the care centers.

259945.name: Oreo Mini's
259945.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Oreo Mini's is an adorable all ebony 9 month old little guy who was left behind in an empty apartment  after his owners moved away. He did appear shy at first but quickly fell back on his four and moved forward to meet me. He accepted a few treats, a bow around his neck and started to play, play, play. Oreo Mini's loves his cuddles too and is truly the true package:a lively, sweet and friendly young pet open to start right away a new page in his life...with you. He is apparently healthy, aced his behavior evaluation and is waiting for his neuter. Come and meet Oreo Mini's very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!





Oreo Mini's is standing up in the back of his cubby, coming forward and meowing softly as the assessor approaches and opens the cubby door. He leans forward to sniff their hand before head bunting it, allowing and leaning into all petting before flopping over onto his side. He continues to head bunt and begins making air biscuits, leaning into further petting down his back. Oreo Mini's is able to be called over to the main area of the kennel, continuing to be receptive to all interaction. He gently bats at the assessor's hand, playfully, gently, and without using claws. He is able to be easily picked up, remains calm when held, and remains at the front when placed back into the kennel, allowing all further petting and attention with his tail held high. Oreo Mini's appears to really enjoy play time, engaging with play with a feather toy. 

Oreo Mini's interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

259985.name: Nova
259985.summary:
Meet Nova! Nova is a sweet and affectionate young cat who came into ACC as an owner surrender. She can be shy at first and may hide when meeting new people, but she warms up quickly and enjoys gentle attention. Nova is a quiet, easygoing girl who loves lounging and playing with small toys.

My Ideal Home Nova would do best in a calm, patient home where she can take her time getting comfortable. She may need a little space when first settling in, but once she feels safe, she can show her affectionate and playful side. A family willing to let her approach at her own pace will help her feel confident.

Good with Kids? Nova may initially hide around children but has been curious and warmed up quickly in her previous home with familiar children. She may do best in a home with older children (please see behavior assessment recommendations).

Good with Other Pets? Yes! Nova previously lived with two cats and was described as curious and gentle with them. She has no known experience with dogs.

Overall Health No known medical issues were reported by her previous family.

Behavior Determination Nova may benefit from a patient adopter who understands that she can be shy in new situations and may need time to feel comfortable. She has no known bite history and was described as affectionate once settled.

Other Fun Facts Nova is a quiet couch potato who enjoys gentle play and small objects. Her previous family especially loved how well she cared for her kittens. She also enjoys catnip!

259994.name: Daisy
259994.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Daisy(who is a boy) is a kitty I love to spend time with. He really makes his visitor feel welcome and appreciated. As soon as one opens his kennel door, Daisy "drops" what ever he is doing and comes for a meet and greet. He is really starving for attention, enjoys gentle words and petting without a hint of having  ever enough. He has not shown yet his playful sides but I guess that it will not take long before he teases feather wands. Daisy is a good looking young gent in need of TLC. He wears a handsome coat with lovely markings but he does need more meat around the bones. We do not know much about Daisy's past's except that he was abandoned in an apartment building after his former owners left. Thanks to a Good Samaritan, Daisy is with us at the Manhattan Care Center. He is an amazing kitty, well mannered, calm, loving, curious, already neutered, apparently healthy(beside being underweight) and with a perfect score on his behavior evaluation. Daisy is ready to meet you and hopefully go home for many happy years to come!





p>What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
Daisy is laying in the back of his kennel, coming forward and gently pawing at the kennel door to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. The kennel door is opened, and Daisy leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting and raising his back as he is pet. He is periodically startled by loud noises, pausing and backing away, but recovers quickly each time and continues to be able to be coaxed to the front. Daisy calmly walks out of the kennel and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting and handling.

We do not know much about Daisy's past's except that he was abandoned in an apartment building after his former owners left. Thanks to a Good Samaritan, Daisy is with us at the Manhattan Care Center. 260027.name: Freckles
260027.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Freckles is a cute and petite gal who came to us with a little dog as their ailing owner could not take care of them anymore. Another kitty lived with them too but its whereabouts are unknown. Freckles looks so pristine in her perfectly groomed coat. She is a tinsy winsy timid but quickly gets to know that we are here for her. She leans into pets, makes biscuits and even softly purrs. We were told that she was owned since kittenhood and was sweet, well mannered and got along very well with her cat and her dog. Freckles is a must to meet. She is apparently healthy, did very well on her behavior evaluation(just pointing to some shyness) and will be spayed very soon, making her ready to go home with you! Freckles is hoping to be your forever best friend for many years to come!








Initially upon approach, Freckles is a bit hesitant, crouched in the back of her top cubby, tense with wide eyes as the door is opened. Freckles is spoken to softly and a squeeze up is offered, which she leans forward to sniff at, appearing interested but not eating it. After a minute or two of soft talk, she stretches forward, meowing softly and greeting the assessor at the front of the kennel with a gentle head bunt. Freckles allows and leans into all petting, tail held high and raising her back as she is pet. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into her kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting and handling, drooling a little bit before calmly walking over to her food bowl to eat.

Freckles interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

260033.name: Slip N Slide
260033.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Slip N Slide was found hiding in a closet in an abandoned apartment and brought by the police to the care center. A beautiful Tuxedo he is who just wanted to make himself small when he was placed in a kennel. It did not take long for Slip N Slide to show us what a lovely chap he truly is. That is a lot of work when there is no back story to make his case but he won me over in the end! Slip N Slide slowly gets up from his bed when someone is at his door. He would not mind exiting and exploring the room he is in. He settles for treats and petting, head bunts and purrs, even accepts a bow around his neck to enhance his natural  black and white beauty. Slip N Slide is a handsome, friendly and social kitty, already neutered, apparently healthy and who did very well on his behavioral evaluation(showing his initial shyness). He is ready to go home with you for many years of shared fun and happiness.







Slip N Slide is laying on his side in the back of his cubby, body tucked close to the back wall and resting his face against the side of the cubby, front paws tucked under his chest as the assessor approaches. When the cubby door is opened, he observes the assessor with dilated pupils, lip licking once. After several minutes of soft talk, he returns a few slow blinks and allows petting, leaning in slightly and closing his eyes when he is pet on the head and cheeks but tensing a bit when he is pet down his shoulders and back. He is unable to be coaxed forward from the back of the cubby, so full pickup is unable to be attempted. He is able to be lifted a few inches off the ground from inside of the cubby, lip licking a bit when placed back down. He is softly spoken to and leans in for a bit more petting on the head and cheeks.

Slip N Slide tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

Sesame tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter.  She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

260044.name: Nutmeg
260044.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Nutmeg arrived at the care center with a few of his friends as their owner was evicted. Like all his housemates, Nutmeg was quite shy although never antagonistic. Little by little(see his photos), Nutmeg came out of his shell and is now "open for business". He enjoys company, petting and even wants to play with catnip toys and feather wands. He is quite a handsome young fellow(he has gorgeous and striking tiger markings) who does not want to be in hiding anymore but part of your home, your family! Nutmeg might right now have a cold but he is otherwise a healthy and stunning lad. Time to go home! Nutmeg is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!







What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Nutmeg is a very sweet and slightly shy cat who is inside the den, looking out calmly. He sniffed treats, did some slow blinking, and allowed petting on his cheek and head, which he seemed to appreciate. He stuck his head out for squeeze-up treats but could not be coaxed all the way out of the den. Later, when the door was shut, he came all the way out to eat more treats, but when the assessor approached the outside of the kennel door, he backed up slowly and then slunk back inside the den.

Nutmeg interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
Basil is standing in the back of her den, pupils dilated, eyes wide, and body tense as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and she is softly spoken to, Basil pokes her head out of the portal exit, head bunting the side wall of the den and leaning forward to sniff the assessor's hand. Whenever sounds occur in the room, Basil will freeze before lip licking and ducking back into her den. Cardamom appears to be fearful and given her age at the time of the assessment (9 weeks old) we believe that she may not have had much human interaction up to this point and as a result is under-socialized; a condition that should be temporary if she is given appropriate interactions. The speed at which the kitten will become socialized is hard to predict but given her age it we believe it may take some time.

260064.name: Wirt
260064.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Wirt and friend MsGreg were left behind for over a week in an empty apartment. Wirt, like the cartoon character(and unlike silly Ms greg) is a bit wary and for cause...In addition to her abandonment, something did happen to Wirt in the past. A big irregular scar, the result of some kind of trauma, a burn may be, can be seen on her left side. It must have hurt quite a bit and be so scary....Wirt is a sweet gal, though and when she knows you, she is gentle and sweet, appreciating all petting and attention. Wirt so deserves love, peace and care in a home that will make her feel safe. We would love for you to meet Wirt and give her the home she never hoped for....She is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.






What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Wirt is a sweet, slightly shy, and affectionate cat who was inside the den, looking slightly concerned with somewhat enlarged pupils. As soon as petting began, she started leaning in for cheek rubs and almost rolled onto her side. She tolerated petting along her back and sniffed treats without eating them. She's very sweet and loves affection.

Wirt interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

260078.name: Mistletoe
260078.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I am playful and cute!

260099.name: Calicoco
260099.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Calicoco, a pretty Tortie was abandoned in a carrier in front of one of the ACC facilities. Nothing is known about her. She is an adorable little gal, sweet and friendly, never in hiding and welcoming gently her visitor(see her VIDEO). She can play too, so it seems that someone, in the past must have loved her and cared for her. Although she has presently a cold, Calicoco was deemed healthy by the veterinary team. She aced her behavior evaluation and could go home after her spay. Calicoco is adorable and will make a new owner very happy to have her as a pet for many years to come. Come and meet her at the Manhattan Care Center! 







What my friends at ACC say about me:
Calicoco was on top of the den, appearing calm and sweet, lying on her side and slightly asleep. When she heard the assessor, she got up and came down and forward, curious and sweet. She gave slow blinks with a normal, calm face, ate treats with interest, and then allowed and enjoyed petting, leaning in gently for cheek rubs with a high tail. She was very calm when picked up and held, sitting calmly in the assessor's arms, and then remained calm when set back down. She enjoyed squeeze-up treats.

Calicoco interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.
	It could be with you! Click here to learn more about the adoption process!

Pre-Screener Form

Smokey came into the care center, and an owner surrendered do to not being able to have large-breed dogs in their apartment. In the prior home, Smokey is noted to be a very active and playful dog! He can usually be found in the living room. Smokey allows for bathing and brushing. He knows sit, stay, and paw. He is used to going on walks once or twice per day for about 25 minutes and pulls moderate to hard on the leash. According to a prior owner, Smokey loves playing fetch and getting belly rubs! In the prior home and in the care center, he is noted to become dog reactive and begins to pull and hard bark towards dogs. He will benefit from a patient and experienced adopter/foster through one of our new hope partners who can provide a calm and structured environment, along with the appropriate behavior modification strategies to help him thrive.

He can usually be found in the living room. Smokey allows for bathing and brushing. He knows sit, stay, and paw. He is used to going on walks once or twice per day for about 25 minutes and pulls moderate to hard on the leash. According to a prior owner, Smokey loves playing fetch and getting belly rubs! In the prior home and in the care center, he is noted to become dog reactive and begins to pull and hard bark towards dogs. He will benefit from a patient and experienced adopter/foster through one of our new hope partners who can provide a calm and structured environment, along with the appropriate behavior modification strategies to help him thrive.

260117.name: Whiskey Float
260117.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Whiskey Float!
Whiskey Float is a handsome boy who's ready to start fresh after being surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. He enjoys leisurely walks where he can stop and sniff to his heart's content, and he's happy to spend time with people who offer him a little patience and encouragement. This sweet pup is hoping his next home will be his forever one.

My Ideal Home
Whiskey Float would love a calm home where he can settle in at his own pace. He can be startled by sudden movements, so gentle handling and positive reinforcement will help him build confidence and feel secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Whiskey Float has shown interest in other dogs but can become overly excited during introductions. Any future dog companions should be introduced slowly and thoughtfully to set everyone up for success.

Good with Kids?
Because he can be fearful at times, ACC recommends a home without young children under 5.

Things to Know
Whiskey Float is a gentle guy who enjoys taking life one sniff at a time. He appreciates a patient approach and will thrive with an adopter who can help him continue building confidence. If you're looking for a loyal companion to share quiet walks and cozy days, Whiskey Float could be the perfect fit.

260119.name: Remy Lebeau
260119.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Remy LeBeau!
Remy LeBeau was found tied to a pole and brought to ACC, and now she's hoping her next chapter is filled with love, patience, and security. While new people and unfamiliar places can feel overwhelming at first, this gentle girl has already shown that beneath her shy exterior is a playful pup just waiting to feel safe. Give Remy a little time, and you'll see her sweet personality begin to shine.

My Ideal Home
Remy would thrive in a calm, quiet home with a patient adopter who understands that trust can't be rushed. She will benefit from slow introductions, a predictable routine, and positive reinforcement training that allows her to build confidence at her own pace. Once she feels secure, she's ready to enjoy all the adventures that come with having a forever family.

Good with Other Pets?
Although her history is unknown, Remy has shown she enjoys the company of other friendly dogs while at ACC. Once she feels comfortable, she loves to play bow, zoom around the yard, and engage in playful games with canine companions. As always, slow introductions will help set everyone up for success.

Good with Kids?
Because Remy is still building confidence with new people and handling, an adult-only home is recommended. She'll do best with people who respect her boundaries and let her approach new experiences on her own terms.

Things to Know
Remy may be timid when meeting new people, but she's incredibly food motivated and responds well to gentle encouragement. It's especially heartwarming to watch her confidence grow around other dogs, where her playful, bouncy personality really comes to life. With patience, kindness, and a little time to decompress, Remy has everything she needs to blossom into a loving and loyal companion.

260130.name: Biscuit
260130.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Biscuit is so well named! She makes tons of biscuits when someone visits her, even if she does not know the person....She is sooo friendly, gentle in all her ways and provides a moment of peace and quiet for any guest she might have. Indeed, Biscuit is the pet you dream to have as a solid and loving companion for years to come. Biscuit is part of a large family of cats their owner could not care for anymore. Nothing is known about her or her housemates but she must not have been anything but a stellar pet! Biscuit came in with a little eye infection that we are treating of course and soon it will be history. Biscuit would love to meet you and be your best foot legged friend for many years to come. She is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!
Addendum:we discover every day new talents among the pets in our care...Just discovered that Biscuit could play with feather wands and catnip toys.Sweetness and playfulness, what a great combination!!

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!

260142.name: Memento
260142.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Memento is a pretty muted Tortie who was found with a neck wound by a Good Samaritan. She was weak and her appetite was down. The veterinary team took good care of her and her wound is on the mend. She is eating better too! Memento was on the shy side when she arrived at the care center. Who knows what ordeal she went through? She is opening up, though and very much appreciates gentle petting, sweet words and special treats. Memento is still getting some veterinary care but will very soon be in our adoption quarters for her to meet her new owner or family.  Ask to meet Memento then, fall in love and take her home!

260149.name: Pool Floatie
260149.summary:
Pool Floatie is standing upright on top of the den, stretching as he comes down to approach the front of the kennel, leaning against the kennel bars to solicit attention and meowing softly. When the kennel door is opened, Pool Floatie firmly head bunts the assessor's hand, allowing and leaning into all petting with his tail held high in a question mark position. He allows extended petting and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to head bunt to solicit further attention and leaning into all further petting.

A volunteer writes:
Pool Floatie is the cutest all ebony nugget who visited someone backyard for a few days, hoping to be welcome into their home. Brought to the Manhattan Care Center, he revealed himself to be a very friendly and easy going one year old kitty, seeking people attention and love. No shyness, no fear, a rather forward youngster dreaming to have a home and a family. Come and meet Pool Floatie at the Manhattan Care Center!

Pool Floatie interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting, but can be a bit protective of his food and or items. We recommend that Pool Floatie go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in overstimulation and new home adjustment.

260169.name: Tre
260169.summary:
My foster writes: Hi, I'm Tre!
I'm a sweet guy who can be a little shy at first, but I warm up quickly. Once I know you, I love being your little shadow and following you everywhere. If you're sitting in a chair, you might find me hanging out underneath it. I even come when you call my name for some pets!
I love curling up beside you to watch TV, often with one paw resting on you. I may even sit on your lap for a quick visit, brush up against you for affection, and just enjoy being close to my favorite person.
My favorite scratches are on my cheeks, chin, ears, and head. I'm happiest when those are the spots you stick to. I'll let you know when I'm ready for more. I also love my cat brush! If you hold it still for me, I'll happily rub my cheeks against it and give myself a brushing.
I'm also a high-energy, curious boy who loves to run, explore, and play! I'd thrive with plenty of playtime and enrichment, and I may do well with another playful cat who can help me get some of that energy out. Lasers and feather toys are some of my favorites!
I love my water fountain, Temptations treats, cozy blankets, horizontal scratchers, and relaxing in my cat donut cave.
I'm also a very good boy when it comes to my litter box!
I'd be happiest in an adult home or with older kids who understand cats and their boundaries. I'm an affectionate, playful boy who wants a home where I can feel safe, loved, active, and most importantly, close to my people.
Tre interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. He took a little bit of time to adjust to the shelter but from the start he showed signs of appreciating attention. We recommend that he go to a home with adopters with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in somewhat fearful cats and environmental/noise sensitivity. He would do best in an adult-only home.

260231.name: Sky Blu
260231.summary:
My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Sky Blu is an affectionate dog that wants nothing more than to be by their handlers side. She likely had a past life as a volleyball player as she can jump very high when she is excited. However, it is easy to redirect her and keep her on the ground. She listens to commands. I told her to drink and she drank. It was remarkable to see how much she understood! Don't let her age fool you; she is a great hiking buddy, walking companion, and was happy to go wherever I was going. When we got to a cafe or any indoor spot, she laid down appropriately and made herself comfortable. She showed me that she could be a good couch potato in addition to a energetic pup. She was an absolute ANGEL on leash. She did not pull whatsoever. She was always wagging her tail, a reminder to stay positive. When other dogs tried to enter her space or when she wanted to play, she would lightly pull or bark to get closer occasionally bark. She was highly redirectable, even without treats.
Sky Blu is the brightness your family needs. Please consider giving her a second chance at being your loyal companion.

Meet Sky Blu!
Sky Blu is a bright, affectionate girl who was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her. She loves spending time with her people, happily leans in for pets, and already knows cues like sit, down, stay, and paw. Her previous family says one of her best qualities is how well she listens, and she's ready to bring that same devotion to a new home.

My Ideal Home
Sky Blu would love an active family that can keep both her mind and body engaged. She enjoys daily walks, car rides, tasty treats (especially rice and chicken!), and will thrive with continued positive-reinforcement training to help channel her enthusiasm.

Good with Other Pets?
Sky Blu previously lived with other dogs, but because she has a history of lunging at cats, ACC recommends a home without cats or other small animals. Slow introductions are recommended with any future canine companions.

Good with Kids?
Sky Blu previously lived with children and may be a good fit for a home with older, dog-savvy kids. ACC recommends a home without very young children.

Things to Know
Sky Blu can become excited or overwhelmed in busy environments and is continuing to work on her impulse control and leash manners around other dogs. With consistency, enrichment, and patient guidance, she's sure to shine. If you're looking for a smart, loving companion who's ready for her next adventure, Sky Blu can't wait to meet you.

260240.summary:
Meet Bella Rose!

Bella Rose would thrive in a home that understands the importance of letting her settle in at her own pace. She does best with slow, positive introductions to new people and appreciates having the time and space to build trust. Once she feels comfortable, her true personality shines-she becomes affectionate, playful, and enjoys spending time with the people she loves.

Bella Rose is looking for a patient family that will celebrate her progress and give her the opportunity to continue blossoming. If you're willing to let her come to you on her own timeline, you'll be rewarded with a loyal, loving companion who is well worth the wait.

260243.name: Wii
260243.summary:
I'm available for adoption at ACC's Mobile Adoption Event on Saturday, August 15 from 12PM - 4PM at Koeppel Hyundai, 34-54 44th Street, LIC, NY 11101. Adoptions are in-person and first come, first served, so make sure to get there early. You can apply for me now, but it will not put me on hold for you. I can't wait to meet you!

Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!

260290.name: Chica
260290.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Chica is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Chica has shown fearful behavior, including retreating from the leash, remaining tense, raised hackles, flinching, and lip licking during handling. Chica has shown some improvement over time, becoming easier to leash and completing walks with a neutral body, though she remains reserved with handlers but still remains intensely fearful in the care center despite best efforts to keep her comfortable. Medically, Chica is apparently healthy.

In the Care Centers, Chica presents as fearful and has been observed escalating to thrashing and biting at slip leads. During her veterinary exam, she head-whipped and snapped. When staff allow her to move at her own pace, she remains fearful and tense. According to her previous owner, Chica will lunge at other dogs and unfamiliar people while on walks. However, with people, she can be friendly when allowed to approach and interact on her own terms, including with children. Chica would benefit from placement with an adult foster through a New Hope Partner who has experience managing fearful and reactive behaviors and can provide a structured, low-stress environment while using positive reinforcement-based training.

260296.name: Kiara
260296.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Kiara is at risk due to behavioral reasons. In the Care Centers, Kiara has demonstrated fearful and anxious behavior. When staff initially approached her kennel, she displayed a tense, low body posture and growled. Once outside her kennel, Kiara may jump on handlers for attention; however, she continues to present as fearful and highly anxious during walks, she even attempted to run away from a handler. Medically, Kiara has allergies, dermatitis, and is overweight.

Kiara was surrendered as a stray but spent two weeks in her finder's home. Her finder reported that she had a low energy level and initially hard barked at them when approached, but became more relaxed after giving her treats. She was noted to have a low energy level and preferred contact on her own terms. She preferred to spend most of her time in the bedroom and went on one to two walks a day for 20 minutes. During her intake, Kiara escalated to hard barking, growling, and lunging at staff while in the vehicle. Since her intake, Kiara remains fearful but has slowly begun taking treats from select handlers when approached slowly. During walks, she has escalated to hard barking, growling, and lunging at strangers and does not recover readily. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Kiara be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope Rescue partner that can address her challenges with the use of a positive reinforcement-only certified professional trainer.

260297.name: Clyde
260297.summary:
A volunteer writes:
The cutest little ginger ended up in the street, was found by a Good samaritan and was brought to the police who delivered the kitten to us at the Manhattan Care Center. Quite an Odyssey for a 4 month old kitten! Clyde was frightened upon arrival and remained scared for days although he was curious too. Well, he is a youngster. We met a few times and yesterday, although still unsure and untrusting, he started to play with a feather wand, with me but also by himself. He accepted hand petting, even leaned and purred as I advanced prudently my hand toward him. He became more and more entrusted(see photos and VIDEOS). When I left the shelter that night, big noises were coming from his kennel. Clyde was chasing a feather and a catnip toy! A young boy should not grow up in a cage! He already might not have been socialized by whoever owned him and he will need time and patience, a calm while enriching environment and a giving new owner to become all that he can be:an amazing adult! If you have the magic to help Clyde, ask to meet him at the Manhattan Care Center!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Clyde is sleeping in his box. The assessor gently wakes him by opening the kennel and he opens his eyes and stretches. He sniffs the assessors hand and begins leaning in for cheek pets. When pet along his body, he stretches. It takes him some time to stand up, but eventually he stands up with a high tail and accepts more petting. He slightly tenses during pick up but is otherwise very nicely improved.

260299.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Fionna is at risk due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Fionna is noted to display arousal concerns, often jumping up on handlers and becoming mouthy. On one occasion, she is noted to have jumped up and mouthed a handler's PPE. She is also noted to bite the leash when coming out of her kennel or during her walks. When returning to her kennel she has become reluctant to go back, requiring a secondary handler to help use a sling to help her back into her kennel. Despite this, Fionna is noted to seek attention from her handler, allowing petting, and will perform "sit" and "paw" cues. Medically, Fionna has dental disease but is otherwise healthy.

Fionna came into the care center as an owner surrender; due to this her behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Fionna has not adjusted well to the care center environment and is noted to bite the leash when coming out of the kennel and during her walks; she is noted to become mouthy with handlers and is noted to grab onto handlers' PPE. Despite this, she is noted to display soical behavioral with handlers, allowing petting, and will perform cues such as "sit" and"paw". She will benefit from a patient and experienced adopter/foster through one of our new hope partners who can provide a calm and structured environment, along with the appropriate behavior modification strategies to help her thrive.

Fionna is at risk due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Fionna is noted to display arousal concerns, often jumping up on handlers and becoming mouthy. When returning to her kennel she has become reluctant to go back, requiring a secondary handler to help use a sling to help her back into her kennel. Despite this, Fionna is noted to seek attention from her handler, allowing petting, and will perform "sit" and "paw" cues. Medically, Fionna has dental disease but is otherwise healthy. Fionna came into the care center as an owner surrender; due to this her behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Fionna has not adjusted well to the care center environment and is noted to bite the leash when coming out of the kennel and during her walks; she is noted to become mouthy with handlers and is noted to grab onto handlers' PPE. Despite this, she is noted to display soical behavioral with handlers, allowing petting, and will perform cues such as "sit" and"paw". She will benefit from a patient and experienced adopter/foster through one of our new hope partners who can provide a calm and structured environment, along with the appropriate behavior modification strategies to help her thrive.

260311.name: Zero
260311.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Zero is on the at-risk list due to medical concerns. Zero has severe dental/periodontal disease requiring a dental procedure, persistent low body condition/weight loss, and recent URI requiring treatment. His scheduled dental procedure was canceled due to his URI. He is also fearful and has limited tolerance for handling and oral examination, making ongoing medical assessment and treatment more challenging in the shelter environment. Placement is recommended for continued recovery, management of his medical needs, and eventual dental care.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
Zero tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children.

A volunteer writes: Zero was perched right at the front of his condo admiring all the comings and goings like the confident kitty he hopes to one day be. He was doing such a good job that I didn't expect him to hop on to his condo perch as soon as I opened the door, but he's had a bit of a time recently. Found injured on his own, Zero sat with his tail tightly wrapped around himself. We know a forever family where he can be himself will be the perfect fit for him.

260320.name: Franco
260320.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Franco!
Franco is a 6 month old puppy who came to ACC when his owner could no longer care for him. This playful pup is full of personality and puppy enthusiasm! Franco loves interacting with people and is always ready to make new friends, but he is still learning how to show his excitement in polite ways. With the right guidance, this energetic boy is ready to grow into an amazing companion.

My Ideal Home
Franco would thrive with an adopter who is excited to continue his puppy training journey. He will benefit from daily physical exercise, enrichment activities, and positive reinforcement training to help him practice impulse control and learn good manners. With patience, consistency, and plenty of fun activities, Franco is ready to be your new adventure buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
Franco has not shown concerns around other dogs while in our care, but his playful and energetic style means he would benefit from thoughtful introductions and continued training to help him learn appropriate ways to interact with his furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Franco's high energy, jumping, and puppy mouthiness, a home without children under 13 is recommended at this time. He would do best with adults who can help him practice calm greetings and teach him that gentle manners get the most attention.

Things to Know
Franco is a fun loving puppy with lots of enthusiasm and an even bigger heart! He is still learning that hands, clothing, and leashes are not chew toys, but he is eager to learn and loves spending time with people. With positive reinforcement, plenty of enrichment, and a little patience, Franco will be ready to trade his puppy chaos for being your best behaved best friend.

260322.name: Figaro
260322.summary:
A volunteer writes:
I thought that Figaro was a kitten! He is quite small, so cute, friendly, silly and lively. I was mistaken by his juvenile looks and behavior...Figaro right away jumps down his kuranda bed when someone is at his door. He wants to meet and greet! His kennel is located in our alley. The traffic and the barking dogs do not bother him at all. He is a real trooper! Figaro loves his cuddles, enjoys the arms(something done by staff during a quiet time at the care center) and plays heartily with a feather wand. What a lovely chap he is! Figaro was found by a Good Samaritan in a park, all by his lonesome. Figaro might behave like a fully visual kitty but he is not. His right eye (that appears shrunk) is blind and his left eye is cloudy. He might need enucleation of one or both eyes in the future. Visually impaired cats makes just as great pets as their non visually impaired counterparts. I know as I did own one for 15 years and she was one of the greatest cats I ever owned! Figaro dreams to go home and be the love of your life! If you are fine and able to care for a pet with a disability, Figaro is a great and amazing young cat for you!!

260323.name: Doritos Locos Taco
260323.summary:
Meet Doritos Locos Taco!
Doritos Locos Taco came to us as a stray, so we're still learning about his past. This little guy is sweet and affectionate once he feels safe, happily climbing into laps for comfort and leaning into gentle pets. New situations can be overwhelming for him, but with patience and kindness, his trusting side begins to shine through.

My Ideal Home
Doritos Locos Taco would do best in a calm, quiet home with experienced adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He needs a family that will let him move at his own pace, avoid forcing interactions, and use positive reinforcement to help him gain confidence. A predictable routine and plenty of encouragement will help him feel safe and secure as he settles into his new home.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13 years old. Doritos Locos Taco is fearful in new situations and would do best in a quieter home where his boundaries are respected.

Good with Other Pets?
There is no known history of Doritos Locos Taco living with other animals. Slow, carefully managed introductions would be recommended if resident pets are present.

Overall Health
Healthy overall.

Behavior Determination
Level 4 - Experienced Adopters. Doritos Locos Taco is a fearful dog who can become overwhelmed during leashing and when pressure is applied to the leash. In calmer environments where he is allowed to approach on his own terms, he quickly shows his affectionate side and enjoys gentle attention. He will thrive with adopters who can respect his boundaries, use force-free training methods, and allow him the time and space he needs to build confidence.

Other Fun Facts
Once he feels comfortable, Doritos Locos Taco is a total cuddle bug! He loves climbing into laps for reassurance, leaning into pets, and staying close to the people he trusts. Watching his confidence grow as he realizes he's safe is one of the most rewarding parts of getting to know this special little dog.

260335.name: Rubia
260335.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Rubia!
Rubia may be deaf and have some vision differences, but she doesn't let that slow her down one bit! This social, affectionate girl is full of personality and loves being wherever her people are. She greets everyone with a soft body, enjoys leaning in for pets, and is always ready to play. She especially loves toys, bath time, and any chance to be part of the action.

My Ideal Home
Rubia is looking for an active home that can match her energy and continue helping her learn. She'll thrive with daily walks, enrichment, and positive, reward based training that keeps both her body and mind busy. She loves being with her people and will happily join in on whatever the day has in store.

Good with Other Pets?
Rubia's history with other pets is still being learned, so slow introductions are recommended if she'll be sharing her home with another animal.

Good with Kids?
Rubia's enthusiasm sometimes gets the best of her, so ACC recommends a home without children under 5. Older, dog savvy kids who can handle her playful energy may be a wonderful fit.

Things to Know
Rubia is a high energy girl who loves to stay busy and enjoys toys, treats, and spending time with her favorite humans. Our staff will be happy to talk with you about her hearing and vision needs and how easy it can be to help dogs like Rubia thrive. She's ready to find a family who will embrace her exactly as she is and love her for the fun, joyful companion she is.

260336.name: Miracle
260336.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Miracle is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns in her previous home. In the prior home, Miracle was reported to bitea a child after the child approached her food. The bite was a bite-and-release to the hand, resulting in three puncture wounds that required medical treatment. Miracle in the care center has been social and affectionate with staff. Medically, Miracle recently was treated for CIRDC and is healthy at this time.

Miracle was surrendered by her previous owner due to a bite incident in the previous home. Her previous family described her as a social, affectionate, very active, and playful dog who enjoyed spending her time with her people or lounging in the living room. She has been reported to love going for car rides, playing tag, enjoys bacon flavored treats, chicken, and most biscuits she is offered. Miracle is noted to guard food and treats and escalated to biting the resident child when her food was touched while she was eating. The bite resulted in three puncture wounds to the hand and required medical attention. During her staying care, Miracle has been loose-bodied and mostly social with handlers. Due to the concerns reported in a previous home, we recommend that Miracle be placed in an adult-only home without cats or smaller animals through a New Hope Rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

260357.name: London Tipton
260357.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Meet London Tipton!
London Tipton came to ACC as a stray, so her past is largely a mystery. What we've discovered, though, is a gentle, thoughtful dog who enjoys taking life at her own pace. She may be a little reserved when meeting new people, but with patience and a calm approach, she happily accepts affection and quietly explores her surroundings. London has a sweet, easygoing personality and is ready to find a family where she can truly relax and feel at home.

My Ideal Home
London would do best in a calm home that allows her time to settle in and build confidence. She doesn't ask for much-just patience, kindness, and a predictable routine while she adjusts. She would be a wonderful companion for someone looking for a laid-back dog who enjoys gentle interaction and a peaceful environment.

Good with Kids?
Because her history is unknown, London would likely do best with older, respectful children who can give her the space she needs while she settles into her new home.

Good with Other Pets?
London has shown calm, appropriate behavior during introductions to another dog in the shelter and may do well with a compatible canine companion after slow introductions. Her history with cats is unknown.

Overall Health
London is currently being treated for dermatitis and an ear infection, and her skin is already showing improvement with medication. She also has a mild heart murmur that is being monitored by our veterinary team. Our adoption counselors can provide more information about her ongoing care and follow-up needs.

Behavior Determination Level 1. London has been friendly, easy to handle, and social with staff. She would be a great match for adopters looking for a calm companion who simply needs a little time to adjust to a new environment.

Other Fun Facts
London enjoys quietly exploring new spaces and has a gentle, thoughtful approach to life. During her dog introduction, she remained calm and polite, offering a few playful toe taps before deciding she'd had enough and walking away-a nice example of her balanced, respectful social skills. She also happily accepts treats (even if a bit cautiously at first) and enjoys gentle attention from people she trusts.

260367.name: Poutine
260367.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Meet Poutine!
Poutine came to the shelter as a stray, so her past is a bit of a mystery, but she's already proving to be one sweet girl. She may start off a little shy, but once she feels safe, she happily leans in for pets and lets her affectionate side shine. This lovable pup is just waiting for the right person to help her feel right at home, and trust us, she's worth the gravy train of patience!

My Ideal Home
Poutine would thrive in a calm home with a patient adopter who will let her settle in at her own pace. Daily walks, enrichment activities like food puzzles and long lasting chews, and gentle positive reinforcement will help her continue building confidence. Once she warms up, she's ready to serve up plenty of love and companionship.

Good with Other Pets?
Because Poutine arrived as a stray, her history with other animals is unknown. Slow introductions to any resident pets are recommended so everyone has the best chance to get acquainted comfortably.

Good with Kids?
Due to her shy nature and preference for warming up on her own terms, a home with children over the age of 5 is recommended. She'll do best with a family that understands she may need a little extra time to feel comfortable.

Things to Know
Poutine may be timid when meeting new people, but once she realizes she's safe, she blossoms into a sweet, affectionate companion who enjoys leaning in for pets. She walks nicely on leash, enjoys exploring, and will benefit from regular exercise and enrichment to keep both her body and mind happy. She's the perfect comfort food for the soul, just with a little more tail wagging!

A volunteer writes: Who doesn't like French fries with cheese and gravy? Well, maybe not everyone, but I think everyone will like this Poutine because she is a petite and adorable little package. She is just plain irresistible. Poutine is great on the leash. She marches along on walks and minds her own business. Poutine is friendly but a bit shy at first. I see that she comes around fast when she knows a person is to be trusted. Come meet this charming dog at Manhattan ACC.

260387.name: Pineapple
260387.summary:
Meet Pineapple!
Pineapple didn't wait around for someone to find her. This clever girl walked right into a police precinct all by herself and asked for help, and she immediately showed everyone just how friendly she is! Now she's at ACC waiting for the next chapter of her story, and she's ready to bring plenty of sweetness, belly rubs, and big personality to her forever home. She loves leaning into pets and will even roll over for belly rubs, so it didn't take long for her to become a staff favorite.

My Ideal Home
Pineapple would love a family that can give her plenty of attention, enrichment, and positive-reinforcement training. She's an enthusiastic girl who sometimes jumps up when she's excited to say hello, so she'll benefit from learning calmer ways to ask for attention. A predictable routine and plenty of opportunities to decompress will also help her feel comfortable and confident.

Good with Other Pets?
Pineapple has been calm around other dogs during her shelter assessment, ignoring them while on leash. As always, slow introductions are recommended when meeting potential canine roommates.

Good with Kids?
Because Pineapple has shown some mild resource guarding around valued items, ACC recommends a home without children under 5. She may be a good match for dog-savvy older children who understand how to respect a dog's boundaries and give her space around special things.

Things to Know
Pineapple is social, affectionate, and very happy to be around her people. She's still working on her manners and can get excited, but she responds beautifully to affection and attention. She has also shown some mild resource guarding, so her family should continue reinforcing positive associations around food and other valued items. And after making the bold decision to walk into a police precinct all on her own, we'd say Pineapple has already proven she knows how to find the right people!

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Muppet came into the care center as a stray and has spent time with his finder. His finder noted that Muppet was intermittently social but was noted to hard bark and growl at strangers and will bark, growl, snap, or attempt to bite when held or restrained. During his intake, Muppet escalated to similar behaviors in addition to attempting to bite a staff member's ankle. During the time spent with his finder, he was reported to be housetrained and went potty while outside on walks. In the care center, Muppet has not adjusted well and has only allowed for minimal handling. Muppet would be best set up for success with a rescue through one of our new hope partners.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Jackie is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Jackie has not acclimated well despite best efforts to keep her comfortable. She intially presented as fearful, staying at the back of her crate when trying to leash her for walks/interactions, refusing treats. As her stay progressed, she became easier to leash with the use of high values and slow approaches. In the behavior office, she would approach handlers for treats, briefly lean into pets, engages with enrichment items such as snuffle mats; at the end of her sessions, she would plant and refuse to return to her crate or kennel after she was moved. In her crate, she would bite and pull on the bars, denting the frame. Jackie has recently begun to leash bite, quickly intensifying to the point where positive means of interruption, as well as safety tools, are ineffective. Medically, Jackie has multiple mammary masses, mastitis, and is lactating. 

Jackie came into the QUACC after being brought in as a stray. In the care centers, Jackie has been very fearful and avoidant, remaining at the back of her kennel and at times not approaching staff for leashing. Jackie will allow some handling but remains intensely fearful. As a result, we recommend Jackie is placed with one of our New Hope Partners.

260423.name: Latoya
260423.summary:
Meet Latoya!

Latoya is a handsome, gentle cat who's still learning that people can be trusted. Since arriving at the care center, he's begun making small but meaningful progress-he's starting to venture out of his den, growing more curious about people, and will cautiously accept gentle attention. With patience and a calm environment, we're hopeful his confidence will continue to grow.

My Ideal Home

Latoya is looking for a quiet, adult-only home where he can settle in at his own pace. An experienced adopter who understands that shy cats need time to blossom will help him feel safe as he adjusts. Once he feels secure, we're excited to see more of his personality emerge.

Good with Kids?

An adult-only home is recommended. Latoya is timid and would do best in a calm, predictable environment while he builds confidence.

Good with Other Pets?

Latoya's history with other animals is unknown. Slow, supervised introductions are recommended if there are resident pets.

Overall Health

Latoya is recovering from fractures of his right hind leg (tibia and fibula) and is receiving pain management while his treatment plan is finalized. Surgery, including possible fracture repair or amputation, is being considered. Despite his injury, he is bright and alert, and his prognosis is fair with appropriate veterinary care. He currently has a temporary waiver for his neuter procedure until he has recovered from his orthopedic injury.

260425.name: Cat-Erine
260425.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Cat-Erine tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children. 

A volunteer writes: Cat-Erine is a smart cat who loves to solve problems, but not so long ago there was one she couldn't. Cat-Erine was left in a container inside an Amazon bag near the garbage. Abandoned with other cats, she waited for someone to come help, which they did and now she's been trying to figure out what to do next. Brushing up on her skills, she looks for things to do in her condo, like opening up doors and unlatching latched latches. Racing to the front of her condo to say hello, she'll nuzzle the glass but isn't always completely sure what to make of pets at the moment. Cat-Erine has come out on the other side of some pretty challenging circumstances, but she could still use a little help in the form of a forever family.

260441.name: Bilbo
260441.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bilbo is at risk due to behavior concerns. In the Care Centers, Bilbo has demonstrated a high level of reactivity toward other dogs. He has been involved in multiple kennel fights and has redirected his frustration onto the staff leash, making it difficult for staff to safely remove him from his kennel. During one incident, Bilbo redirected onto a staff member and bit them, breaking skin. When other dogs are not present, Bilbo has been social and interactive with staff, displaying a wiggly body. Medically, Bilbo is underweight. 

Bilbo arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, Biblo has been observed to be rope reactive and kennel reactive. He also has a bite history. Bilbo was reacting to another dog in the kennel room when he redirected and bit the handler on the arm. Due to the detailed behavior, we recommend an experienced adult only, single pet home.
