260476.name: Tutu
260476.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Tutu is on the at-risk list due to medical concerns. Tutu due to advanced age and multiple chronic medical concerns are difficult to fully evaluate and manage in the shelter setting. She is underconditioned with muscle wasting, suspected arthritis, severe dental/periodontal disease requiring a dental procedure with placement, and recently developed a suspected UTI. Further urinary tract/abdominal imaging has been recommended. Behaviorally, Tutu has shown limited tolerance for medical handling and would require sedation for further advance diagnostics. She is currently quiet with a fair appetite and would benefit from placement for continued monitoring, further diagnostic evaluation, and management of her needs.

Tutu is an older and highly independent cat that is somewhat tolerant of some attention and limited petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and is noted to prefer interactions and touch on her terms. Tutu appears to have the potential for overstimulation and prefers to have her boundaries respected, including not being picked up. She may prefer being admired from afar as she spends her golden years sitting loafed and observing, and may need time to warm up to her new home and family. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home comfortable with an independent older cat that is set in her ways and knows her boundaries.

260504.name: Toph
260504.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Toph is a young gal left behind when her owners were displaced. Nothing is really known about her except that she was very friendly as she was picked up and arrived at the care center. Toph was quite underweight and anemic when we first assessed her but feeling safe, loved and cared for, the little gal gained steadily weight and corrected her anemia. She was essentially undernourished....Toph is a very gentle and welcoming kitty girl, really pretty, girly, well mannered and who loves company and petting. She head bunts, purrs and leans strongly into petting. Toph is now apparently healthy, will be spayed on 8/14, passed her behavior evaluation with flying colors and is ready to go home with you! Come and meet Toph, our little gem, very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!









Toph is laying on top of her den as the assessor approaches, body and eyes neutral. When the kennel door is opened and she is spoken to softly, she leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand before giving it a gentle head bunt. Toph allows and leans into all petting and comes down from the top of the den to solicit further attention. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm and purring as she is held. When she is placed back into the kennel, Toph begins eating her wet food, continuing to lean into all further petting and purr.

Toph interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

260508.name: Sephora
260508.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Sephora is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is very apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she may attempt to flee and avoid human contact. It is difficult to predict if she will respond to socialization, but we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people.

260521.name: Louie
260521.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Louie(who came with friend Gumbo) is a beautiful tiger with round cheeks and striking markings who first appeared to me as very shy and subdued. Gentle and encouraging words, slow blinks and slow moves got him to pay attention to me and trust that I meant well. Louie tilted his head toward my hand, accepted petting, very quietly purred and slid on his side for more petting and scratching. What a lovely cat, gentle and appreciative of the attention! Louie comes with sweet comments from his former family. He can be timid but is across the board a gentle soul who gets along with everybody:kids, cats and dogs! Like any cat or dog entering a new home and part of a new family, Louie will need a period to adapt to his new settings but he is really all worth it! Ask for Louie when you come to the Manhattan Care Center! He might be the one you have been longing for!

260522.name: Gumbo
260522.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Gumbo needs at risk placement for medical and behavioral reasons. He is not eating in shelter due to a severe upper respiratory tract infection. Due to his high level of stress in shelter, he will not tolerate supportive care. He needs placement in a veterinary clinic to recover and a quiet home to thrive.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
A volunteer writes: In his previous home, Gumbo was a lover not a fighter--a well-behaved boy who played gently, hid whenever he felt scared, and got along well with other cats. (His cat brother, Louie, has already been adopted.) But clearly the adjustment to the Care Center has overwhelmed him, as he's avoided interacting with the staffers and volunteers who hope to see him come out of his protective shell. We get it; unfamiliar environments can wig out even the most confident cats. We're hoping that with time Gumbo will adjust and open up more. But this might not happen until he's in a real forever home with pet parents who boost his security with a go-slow approach. Have a soft spot for this handsome tabby with the gumdrop nose who needs a helping hand from a compassionate human? Gumbo is waiting for you on 110th Street today.

A volunteer writes: Milo Cyrus has been a treasured companion for all three years of his life but unforeseen events in his guardian's world meant the same thing happened to him. Milo Cyrus may have lost his home, but he hasn't lost his hope. Snuggled up on top of his cubby, I imagine the changes combined with shelter life has been quite a lot. We've heard (and have seen) that he can be a little unsure around new people, but we also know that he tries to find himself anywhere they are when he has the opportunity to get to know them a little bit better. He plays gently and sweetly when he gets the chance. Milo Cyrus could use a calm routine and he settles into his next chapter, which we hope will include you.

260568.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Decatur is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Decatur has shown deterioration and is noted to bite at his kennel wall. Decatur is noted to become tense and freezes, and fixate when seeing another dog, he will sometimes look away or is noted to be difficult to redirect his focus. Difficult to redirect. Decatur is noted in a calmer setting to allow petting from handlers, taking treats, and engaging with enrichment, but is still struggling to acclimate. Medically, Decatur is apparently healthy.

Decatur arrived at MACC as a stray with no known history. While in care, he has been observed to be highly fearful. Noted to have a tense, trembling body and freezes when the handler attempts to engage with him. Due to the detailed behavior we recommend an experienced adult only home.

260605.name: Isabella
260605.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Isabella is inside of her den, poking her head out with wide eyes and softly meowing as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she comes forward to greet the assessor, growling a bit before leaning her body against their hands, tail held high in a question mark posture and vibrating at the base. She allows and leans into all petting but is distracted by the other cats in the room throughout the assessment, craning her neck and growling intensely upon seeing or hearing the other cats in the room. She does not redirect, tolerating all petting and leaning in without issue. When pickup is attempted, Isabella stiffens to resist, she is able to be picked up but begins to growl again and squirms to be put back down. When she is placed back into the kennel, she lip licks once before approaching the assessor for further petting, tolerating extended petting without issue.

Isabella interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Isabella go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression, and discomfort with pickup.

260607.name: Pouki
260607.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I came in with my friend Tabbi and would love to find a home with them!
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

A volunteer writes: Pouki waits right at the front because he knows what it's like to be left behind. It happened to him but that was before and now he's ready to take matters right into his own little paws by enthusiastically presenting his optimism to anyone who looks his way. Quick with a nuzzle and a complete disregard of the physics of barriers, Pouki's efforts to be everywhere at the same time begin with his nose. Pushing his nose into my hand and his side into my arm, Pouki was all purry cuddles until he noticed a family walking around behind me. This was then he pulled out all the stops. I almost wanted to give him some glittery feathers or sequined jacket he could open up and spin around in, but then I remembered that Pouki doesn't need all that to stand out. He only needs a family to look his way and tell him they'll never forget him.

260610.name: Nana
260610.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Nana is a 16 year old dame we have the honor to host as her owner was taken into care. Nana is a real treat, so pretty and girly in her little grey dress, so friendly and welcoming(even with the veterinary team) when one opens her kennel door. She immediately comes down her balcony, slowly and lady-like and indulges with lots of petting and gentle talks. The kind of cat one does not want to leave! Nana is underweight, matted and has senior teeth...We are waiting for her labs that partially and surprisingly came back as normal for her age. She aced her behavior evaluation, no surprise, of course...No pet belongs to a cage and a senior even less as like babes, they are very fragile. A home sweet home is what Nana needs and what we dream for her. 






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I can go home today!
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
My purr motor is always running!

260649.name: Sassy
260649.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Sassy is at risk due to behavioral concerns in the previous home. Sassy is reported to have initiated altercations with one of the other resident dogs, reportedly unprovoked. Each time, her owner has had to physically pull her off the other dog, as she would aim for the neck each time. The most recent incident resulted in a puncture to the other dog's face that was cleaned/treated at home. During her stay in care, Sassy has been intermittently social with handlers on her own terms, but at times does need coaxing to be returned to the kennel. Medically, Sassy is healthy at this time.

Sassy was surrendered by her previous owner due to her behavior towards the other resident dog in the home. Her previous owner described her as a very affectionate dog who enjoys being around people, loves long walks in the park, Rope toys, and enjoys eating most food or treats. Sassy is noted to have attacked the other resident dog, reportedly unprovoked, and had to be physically pulled off by her owner in order to stop. The most recent bite was reported to have been two weeks before surrender, and it did break skin, leaving a small puncture to the other dog's face. During her stay in care, Sassy has been highly social with staff and handlers, remaining loose-bodied and readily seeking attention during interactions. Due to the concerns noted in her previous home, we recommend that Sassy be placed in an adult-only home where she can be the only dog and pet through a New Hope Rescue partner that can provide Sassy with behavior modification for her reactivity with the use of a certified professional trainer that uses only positive reinforcement methods.

260678.name: Terry
260678.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

A volunteer writes: Terry has a few signs on his kennel. One requests we use the elevator instead of the stairs and the other requests he gets extra bedding. When I peer inside to see this gorgeous boy, I immediately ache seeing his condition. His hind legs barely straighten, his back is hunched and sloped.

Nonetheless Terry is eager for a break from his kennel and we ride the elevator and walk to the yard. He keeps a slow and steady pace but doesn't stop moving, determined to take his break. Terry was found stray, so while we know nothing of his past we know what future he deserves. A home, a family, infinite soft surfaces to rest on, and a vet to help alleviate his pain. He was neutral in his gate greeting and available to most homes, but I think he deserves the best of homes.

When we return to his kennel I add some more bedding so he doesn't slip on the floors, and sprinkle chicken jerky around and watch him eat. He doesn't argue about going back in, and I'm not sure if that makes me happy or sad. I'd love to see his spark come back.

260681.name: Lucy
260681.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Lucy is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Lucy has shown intense fearful behavior, including trembling, whale eye, shaking, refusing to leave her kennel, and not eating. After leashing and trying to remove the leash from her safely, she has snapped and bitten tools while doing so. Despite patient handling and high-value food, Lucy continues to struggle to acclimate to the shelter environment. Medically, Lucy is apparently healthy.

Lucy was surrendered by her previous owner due to them being ill and not being able to take care of her properly. Her previous family described her as a very active and playful dog, spending most of her time in the living room. She is noted to enjoy bath time/water, any form of food or toys, and has a high energy level. She is noted to not enjoy getting in or being in the car at all. During her stay in care, Lucy has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and is not allowing for any form of handling. During her intake, Lucy was highly fearful and stressed, escalating to thrashing and flailing several times before pancaking and refusing to move when being walked to the kennel. During her stay, Lucy remains highly fearful and shut down, avoiding all interaction, and refuses to leave her kennel. She has not taken high-value treats or responded to any form of coaxing during attempts to remove her from her kennel or interact. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Lucy be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope Rescue partner who can allow her the time and space to decompress and acclimate on her own terms.

260683.name: Gingi
260683.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Gingi looks like a ball of fire in his kennel, a bright orange and timid young cat who went though a frightening event. He was caught in a house fire! Gingi had a smoke inhalation, was treated at an outside veterinary hospital and brought healthy to the Manhattan Care Center. Gingi was quite shy and in hiding for days. I never heard a hiss or saw a swat though. Gingi is feeling better, safer and shows now his very sweet side. He does love food and treats but he appreciates so much more attention, love and cuddles(see photos and video). I really enjoy my time with him, admire his beauty and mostly his gentle manners. Gingi dreams to be home, safe, loved and sharing a wonderful time with a new family. Come and meet gorgeous Gingi at the Manhattan Care Center!

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

260684.name: Luna Beam
260684.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Luna Beam was left behind with friend Lino when their owners moved away. A relative fed them for 2 months until she left too and both kitties were brought to the Manhattan Care Center. Luna Beam had a bit of a hard time in her debuts at the shelter but she fell back on her four....She is quite a pleasant gal, glad to have visitors, not shy and enjoying petting while rolling on her kennel floor, purring and head bunting, hoping to come out on the lap(see video). Luna Beam plays quite well too with catnip toys and feather wands(see photos). She is a sweet, lively, friendly and playful gal, apparently healthy, already spayed and who could go home with you today. Time to meet Luna Beam at the care center! She is waiting for you!





What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

260685.name: Lino Ray
260685.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

A volunteer writes: Lino Ray wants someone to remember he's here. He's been through a number of changes recently and finds himself working a little harder than most to remind us all he's still here and trying. Trying to open his condo door with his fluffy cheek alone, trying to hop onto an open lap, we see his insistence and the heart he so brightly puts on display. Lino Ray was brought here with another cat, with whom he was quite friendly with, when his guardian had to leave the country and while family members did everything they could, finding him a forever family needs a little extra help from us. A sparkling couch potato who loves to play and be around people, we know that the family who remembers Lino Ray's here and is ready to take a chance on him, will be so lucky.

260687.name: Inky
260687.summary: Inky appreciates attention and petting but appears to be somewhat fearful in the shelter. They will likely need time to warm up to their new home, and may be slightly sensitive to noises in their environment. We recommend that they go to a home with some cat experience preferred or at least be well counseled in fearful cat behavior. Inky may be intimidated by small children, any home with older children prepared to adopt this cat should conduct a thorough interaction and endeavor to monitor this cat around their children to prevent these behaviors from being reinforced.

260717.name: Luna
260717.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Luna!
Luna was found roaming on her own and is now looking for a loving family to help her write a much happier next chapter. This gentle girl has a calm, easygoing nature and enjoys quietly exploring her surroundings while checking in with her favorite people. With her sweet personality and soft demeanor, Luna is ready to leave her wandering days behind for good.

My Ideal Home
Luna would love a patient family that can offer her a comfortable place to relax while she settles into her new routine. She enjoys taking life at a slower pace and would thrive with positive reinforcement, gentle encouragement, and plenty of opportunities to explore the world by your side.

Good with Other Pets?
Luna's history with other animals is unknown, but she has shown calm interest in meeting other dogs while at ACC. Slow introductions will help ensure any future canine friendships get off to a great start.

Good with Kids?
Luna's history with children is unknown. As with any new pet, respectful, supervised introductions are recommended to help everyone feel comfortable.

Things to Know
Luna walks beautifully on a loose leash and has a gentle, thoughtful personality that makes spending time with her a joy. She enjoys exploring her surroundings, taking treats from kind people, and getting comfortable at her own pace. If you're looking for a sweet companion who simply wants a safe place to call home, Luna may be the perfect match.

260740.name: Balenciaga
260740.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Balenciaga is on the at-risk list for behavioral concerns. In the care centers, Balenciaga has displayed intense fearful behavior, including trembling, growling, avoiding staff, and attempting to bite during leashing. While she has begun to warm up and seek attention from familiar staff, she remains fearful and can become highly aroused in some situations, causing her to now leash bite at times, or vocalize and paw at her leash. Her previous owner reported that Balenciaga will hard bark and lunge at unfamiliar people. She has shown some interest in staff if allowed to approach on her own time. Medically, Balenciaga has a corneal ulceration. 

Balenciaga was surrendered into care as a stray, so her past behavior in a home environment is limited. From the limited information provided, she was reported to be social with only her family and has escalated to hard barking and lunging at strangers. She reportedly has chewed through muzzles and broken free from collars/leashes. Balenciaga has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. She has escalated to attempting to bite, growling, and being wary of leashing attempts in her kennel. Once leashed, she remains tense with a low tail and does not attempt to interact with handlers, ignoring offered treats. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Sugar Cube is on the at-risk list due to medical and behavioral concerns. At this time, Sugar Cube has been diagnosed with Canine Infectious Respiratory Disease Complex (aka an upper respiratory infection) and conjunctivitis. Sugar Cube has allowed very limited handling while in our care, which limits our ability to treat these infections. He has escalated to higher-level warnings during medical handling, including lunging, growling, and snapping. He did bite a staff member on the hand after being picked up to be returned to his top kennel. The bite resulted in multiple punctures and drew blood.

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

260781.name: Frost
260781.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Frost is a handsome and friendly cat surrendered into our care as his housemate(a female brought at a later date )did not particularly like him, causing him at time not to use his litter box(he uses it perfectly well at the care center). Their owner was overwhelmed by their continuous squabbles as well as the cost of pet care. Frost is said to be a "gentle guy" , a quiet lap cat who might need time to warm up(with all) but is curious, friendly and used to play gently once he felt comfortable. Frost has been a welcoming kitty at the care center, immediately available when someone opens his door, ready for petting and play and coming on the lap. Frost has no experience with dogs and the reason for his poor relationship with his female housemate in unknown. As a result, a new home without other cats is likely preferable and advised. Frost is a very sweet cat, apparently healthy, already neutered and who did well on his behavior evaluation. He is ready to go home today...with you!










FrostWhat my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I prefer to call the shots and enjoy coming to you when I'm ready for pets.
What do you get when you cross a cat with a couch? A cat-potato! And that's me to a T!
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.

260793.name: Dunkin
260793.summary:
Meet Dunkin!
Dunkin arrived at ACC as a stray, so his past is a bit of a mystery. While he may need a little extra time to warm up, this sweet boy has already shown that he is willing to connect with people and happily approaches for treats. Dunkin is looking for a patient family who will help him feel safe, build confidence, and discover all the good things life has to offer.

My Ideal Home
Dunkin would thrive in a calm home with an adopter who understands that trust takes time. He will benefit from slow introductions, positive reinforcement training, daily exercise, and enrichment activities to help him feel comfortable and confident. With patience and plenty of encouragement, Dunkin is ready to become your loyal companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Dunkin's history with other animals is unknown. Since he arrived as a stray, we recommend slow and thoughtful introductions to any furry friends in the home to help everyone feel comfortable and set up for success.

Good with Kids?
Due to Dunkin's fearful behavior and need for gentle interactions, a home without young children under 5 is recommended. He would do best with people who can respect his boundaries and allow him to build confidence at his own pace.

Things to Know
Dunkin is a sensitive sweetheart who may need a little time before showing off his full personality. He enjoys treats, exploring, and taking things one step at a time. If you're looking for a pup who will reward your patience with trust and companionship, Dunkin could be the perfect blend of sweet and special.

260798.name: Leonidus
260798.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
Leonidus tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

A volunteer writes: Leonidus is learning that everyone's business is not necessarily his business, but he doesn't quite see the fun in that so he reaches his paws out to playfully tap anyone walking by. It's as much a way to get involved as it is a way to invite them to play and visit. Leonidus likes to stretch out surrounded by his favorite toys and roll over into the arms of friends, playfully reaching his paws out. Leonidus was brought to us after he was found with a note from his previous guardian. The note explained why they could no longer care for him and ended with a devastating "Signed, Heart Broken." I'd like to think that Leonidus has embraced shelter life the way that they would want them to. He only needs someone to notice and choose him.

A volunteer writes: Signed, Heart Broken. That's how Juniperus' previous guardian signed off on the note they left him with. Though devastated in separation, there is still so much hope for Juniperus and we know it too. His guardian wrote the note with hope in their heart that another person would love him as they did, maybe they would see him right away and instantly know he was theirs. We've set about filling in the blanks, getting to know Juniperus as best we can. We know Juniperus may also feel heart broken and a little confused as we ask him to navigate the shelter but we're cheering him on as he does and waits to find you.

260825.name: Jade
260825.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Jade is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Jade has displayed escalating arousal concerns that have not improved despite efforts to help him acclimate to the shelter environment. He consistently displays high arousal, initially presenting as leash biting and mouthiness, which has progressed to repeated leash biting during handling, in the play yard, and when returning to his kennel. During a recent playgroup session, Jade became frustrated after greeting another dog and redirected onto the handler by grabbing their shoes and pant cuffs with moderate pressure and repeatedly jumping toward their stomach and chest with an open mouth; prompting them to push their treat pouch into his mouth for him to grab and not their limbs/body. Medically, Jade is underweight and has dental disease.

Jade was surrendered into care due to his owner/caretaker moving into a new home and not being able to afford to continue care for Jade. They stated that they had Jade in the home for close to a month after intially finding him as a stray. His previous family described him as a social, affectionate, vocal, very active dog. He would spend most of his time where his people were or in the living room. They did note that he had accidents a few times a week if not taken outside and was fearful of having his paws touched. During his stay in care, Jade has not acclimated well. He has displayed mouthiness, high levels of anxiety, and a concerningly low threshold for arousal, which has manifested as leash biting and recently escalated towards the handler once over his threshold. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Jade be placed in an adult home through a New Hope partner that can provide consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist for guidance to safely manage/modify any behavior Jade presents with outside of the care centers.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some canine body language together!
I'm ready to learn! I need a patient person who has the time to work on training with me.
I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

260851.name: Grumble
260851.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Grumble is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Grumble has shown fearful and defensive behavior, including growling, lunging, hard staring, hard barking, head whipping, and biting at the leash. He has also reacted to handling around his collar and body, escalating when touched near his hind end. Grumble is social on his own terms, approaching handlers to solicit brief petting, but is quick to escalate with staff even when doing so. Medically, Grumble is healthy at this time. 

Grumble was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Rumble has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and is only allowed for minimal handling. One being removed from the vehicle after pickup, he began growling at staff. During his medical exam, Grumble began low growling and hard barking when approached; he continued to escalate, and he was easily leashed from the kennel, requiring sedation. During an enrichment session, Grumble was easy to Leash from kennel and was brought to the behavior office. He approached multiple handlers and nudged their hands to solicit brief petting before walking away. When attempting to remove the collar that he was found in, he began grumbling. When a handler reached down to scratch his hind end, Grumble immediately whipped around, growling and lunging at them. They are able to restrain him but he hard-stared, lunged again, and began biting at the leash. Due to his escalation, he had to be double leashed to be returned to his kennel safely. Due to Grumbles' concerning level of escalation towards handlers, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can address his challenges with the use of a certified professional trainer that uses only positive reinforcement.

260852.name: Starfish
260852.summary:
Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I am playful and cute!

Pre-Screener Form

Nutmeg is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Nutmeg was brought to the Care Centers following a bite incident in the home that resulted in a puncture wound to the victim's finger. In the Care Centers, Nutmeg has demonstrated fearful behavior, including freezing and taking time to interact and become comfortable with staff. When staff approach slowly and allow him time to acclimate, he has displayed a looser body and solicited mild attention from handlers, including permitting brief petting. Medically, Nutmeg has otitis externa.

Nutmeg was surrendered into care as a stray due to a bite incident in his previous home.  Nutmeg has presented as fearful, wary of leashing, and mostly avoidant of interactions. He has slowly begun to approach handlers on his own terms, but does not take treats or show interest in toys. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Nutmeg be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

260870.name: Bambi
260870.summary:
Meet Bambi!
Bambi was found tied to a fence, but despite such a heartbreaking start, this sweet pup is ready to leave the past behind and find a family to call her own. She may be a little shy when meeting new people, but with a bit of patience, her gentle personality begins to shine. Watching her confidence grow is one of the sweetest things you'll ever see.

My Ideal Home
Bambi would thrive in a calm, patient home where she can settle in at her own pace. Gentle encouragement, positive reinforcement, and a predictable routine will help her continue building confidence as she adjusts to her new life. Once she feels safe, she's sure to become a devoted companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Because Bambi arrived as a stray, her history with other animals is unknown. At ACC, she has shown calm curiosity around another dog and responded well to slow introductions, so any future canine friends should be introduced gradually.

Good with Kids?
Bambi would do best in a home with teens or adults only, as she'll be happiest in a quieter environment where she can continue gaining confidence.

Things to Know
Bambi is easy to walk on leash and enjoys taking things one step at a time. She appreciates kind people who let her approach at her own pace, and every small victory helps her blossom a little more. If you're looking for a gentle companion whose trust will be incredibly rewarding to earn, Bambi is waiting to meet you.

My Ideal Home
Superstar would do best with a patient adopter who will continue building his confidence through gentle, reward-based training. He enjoys taking things at his own pace and will thrive with a calm routine, positive experiences, and plenty of encouragement as he settles into home life.

Good with Other Pets?
Superstar may do best with slow, thoughtful introductions to other dogs, and positive reinforcement can help him build confidence around canine companions.

Good with Kids?
Because he can be sensitive to certain types of handling, Superstar would do best in a home with older children or adults only.

Things to Know
Superstar walks beautifully on a loose leash, enjoys checking in with his handler, and is always happy to accept a tasty treat. He's looking for someone who will respect his boundaries and help him continue building positive associations through force-free, reward-based training. With a little patience and a lot of love, Superstar is ready for his happily ever after.

260918.name: Purricane Bianca
260918.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Purricane Bianca was found in an apartment building hallway and brought to the Manhattan Care Center for us to find her a home. P Bianca is one of the most beautiful Torties I have ever met. Her coat is painted with the most vibrant colors and she seems to have been the work of an artist. A little beauty, a shy and reserved one who is waiting without knowing it for the right moment and the right person to come out of her shell. Indeed, one year old P Bianca is very quiet in her cubby, coming at time to the front to eat treats and timidly say hello. She now enjoys cuddles, leans into pets and head bunts. Little by little she is showing what a love she is(see her video). Purricane Bianca has right now a cold but soon, it will be over and she will be able(after her spay) to go home with a new family. Ask about P Bianca when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center!

260946.summary:

Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!

A volunteer writes: This handsome ginger came to the Care Center after his owner passed away. As traumatic as that can be for a young cat, it seems that Calvin is doing his very best to adjust. Our behavior team deemed Calvin to be mellow and relaxed, the kind of good boy (and expert biscuit maker!) who would be a great fit for most households. Calvin's world recently turned upside down, but it hasn't kept him from being the low-key loverboy he clearly is. Meet Mr. Calvin today!

260953.name: Banjo
260953.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Banjo!
Banjo was found as a stray alongside another dog and is ready to start the next chapter of his life with a loving family. This sweet boy enjoys exploring, happily checks in with his people, and loves gentle attention. He can be a little sensitive about being touched over his head, but with patience and kindness, his confidence continues to grow.

My Ideal Home
Banjo is looking for a patient adopter who will let him settle in at his own pace. Slow introductions, positive reinforcement, and a calm environment will help him feel safe as he adjusts. Once he trusts you, Banjo is eager to share his gentle personality and affectionate side.

Good with Other Pets?
Banjo arrived at ACC with another dog and has shown friendly, playful behavior when meeting other dogs. He enjoys mutual sniffing, playful bows, and bouncy play sessions. As with any new companion, slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Banjo's history with children is unknown. 

Things to Know
Banjo enjoys exploring his surroundings, walking nicely on leash, and spending time with people he trusts. He has medical needs that staff will discuss with you when you meet him. Banjo also appreciates gentle handling and may move away if touched over his head, so a patient family committed to reward-based training will help him continue building confidence. If you're looking for a sweet, playful companion with a gentle heart, Banjo is ready to strike the right chord in your life.

A volunteer writes: We got a heads up about Banjo from a fellow volunteer before I even got a chance to lay eyes on him: "Has anyone met Banjo? He's my new boyfriend.  Walked him yesterday and I was in love.  Biggest bulldog I have ever seen..." And I was like a dog head tilting at hearing my favorite words: BULLDOG? BIG? IN LOVE?  Then, the text when another vol was bringing him out a few days later to get content, "You aren't ready for Banjo." And even with advanced notice, I was still not prepared for the absolute wiggly jiggly unit that is this 86 pound marshmallow of love. And for all the build up he exceeded my expectations. Banjo snuggled, played, shook his nub, posed for pictures and did all the things he needed to do to try to get adopted!

Banjo was found in a vacant building with his buddy, Kazooie #260954 who is also adoptable.  He has been friendly and playful with other dogs in the shelter.  Medically, Banjo has a prolapse of his third eye lid for which he is receiving eye drops and will need follow up vet care for.  He is available to Level 2 homes and his adoption fee is waived due to currently living in a pop up crate.

260954.name: Kazooie
260954.summary:
Meet Kazooie!
At 10 years old, Kazooie is ready for a comfy home where she can enjoy her golden years. She was found in a vacant home and is now looking for someone who will give her the patience and security she deserves. Once she's comfortable, she enjoys exploring, greeting her people, and leaning into affection, and she still has a playful side too!

My Ideal Home
Kazooie would love a calm, predictable home where she can take things at her own pace. She's affectionate once comfortable, but may need some time to decompress and build trust in a new environment. Gentle, positive reinforcement will help her feel right at home.

Good with Other Pets?
Kazooie has limited history with other dogs and came into ACC with another dog. She has shown interest in other dogs and even offered play bows, but can become a little too enthusiastic, so slow introductions will be important.

Good with Kids?
Because Kazooie can be fearful and defensive when stressed, ACC recommends an adult-only home at this time.

Things to Know
Kazooie loves gentle affection and has a sweet side that shines when she feels comfortable. She can be protective of her toys, so she'll need some space around her favorite things. Give this senior girl a little patience and she'll have the chance to show you just how special she is!

260957.name: Ocean
260957.summary:
Meet Ocean!
Ocean is ready to make a splash in his forever home! Found as a stray, this sweet, social boy has been winning hearts with his affectionate personality and love of spending time with people. He happily leans in for pets, walks nicely on leash, and is always ready to tide things over with a tasty treat or two. If you're looking for a loyal companion, you'll be shore glad you met Ocean!

My Ideal Home
Ocean would love an adopter who enjoys positive, reward-based training and can help him channel his enthusiasm into good manners. He's eager to interact with people and will thrive with plenty of enrichment, fun training sessions, and opportunities to continue learning. With consistency and patience, this handsome guy is sure to make waves.

Good with Other Pets?
Ocean has shown relaxed body language around other dogs during his shelter assessments. As with any new pet, slow introductions are always recommended.

Good with Kids?
Because Ocean is still learning polite treat manners and can become a little overenthusiastic around snacks, ACC recommends a home without very young children.

Things to Know
Ocean is affectionate, food-motivated, and loves being close to his people. He's still polishing his manners around treats and can get a little too excited when snacks are involved, but that's something positive reinforcement training can help with. Beneath all that enthusiasm is a sweet dog who's ready to dive into his next adventure with a family of his own.

260987.name: Giulia
260987.summary:
Meet Giulia!
Giulia was found with her companion Dee Dee (260988) and is now looking for a quiet place where she can feel safe and settle in. This shy girl can be overwhelmed by new environments, but with patience, gentle encouragement, and time to decompress, she may blossom into a wonderful companion. Giulia is hoping to find someone who understands that the best relationships are built at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Giulia would do best in a calm, low-pressure home with a patient adopter who will allow her to take things slowly. She should never be forced into interactions and will thrive with someone who respects her boundaries, reads her body language, and celebrates her small steps of confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Giulia arrived with another dog, Dee Dee (260988), but her history with other animals is otherwise unknown. Slow introductions are recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to her shy and fearful nature, Giulia would do best in a home without young children. She needs a calm environment where she can build trust at her own pace.

Things to Know
Giulia may take some time to warm up, but a little patience can go a long way with this sensitive girl. She enjoys having the option to approach when she feels comfortable and would appreciate a family who understands that trust is earned one gentle moment at a time.
260987.summaryHtml:
Meet Giulia!
Giulia was found with her companion Dee Dee (260988) and is now looking for a quiet place where she can feel safe and settle in. This shy girl can be overwhelmed by new environments, but with patience, gentle encouragement, and time to decompress, she may blossom into a wonderful companion. Giulia is hoping to find someone who understands that the best relationships are built at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Giulia would do best in a calm, low-pressure home with a patient adopter who will allow her to take things slowly. She should never be forced into interactions and will thrive with someone who respects her boundaries, reads her body language, and celebrates her small steps of confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Giulia arrived with another dog, Dee Dee (260988), but her history with other animals is otherwise unknown. Slow introductions are recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to her shy and fearful nature, Giulia would do best in a home without young children. She needs a calm environment where she can build trust at her own pace.

Things to Know
Giulia may take some time to warm up, but a little patience can go a long way with this sensitive girl. She enjoys having the option to approach when she feels comfortable and would appreciate a family who understands that trust is earned one gentle moment at a time.

260988.name: Dee Dee
260988.summary:
Meet Dee Dee!
Dee Dee was found with her companion Giulia (260987) and is ready to find a home where she can feel safe, loved, and supported. This playful girl has a big personality and lots of energy to share! While shelter life can feel overwhelming for her, Dee Dee is looking for a patient family who can help her learn that the world is a fun and safe place.

My Ideal Home
Dee Dee would do best with an adopter who understands that she may need time and patience as she adjusts to a new environment. A predictable routine, plenty of enrichment, daily exercise, and positive reinforcement training will help her feel more comfortable and confident. She is ready to learn and would love a person who can help her channel her enthusiasm into fun activities.

Good with Other Pets?
Dee Dee arrived with another dog, Giulia (260987), but her history with unfamiliar dogs is unknown. Slow introductions are recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Dee Dee's anxiety and difficulty settling in the shelter environment, she would do best in an adult-only home or a home without young children. Older children may be considered after a proper introduction.

Things to Know
Dee Dee is an active and enthusiastic pup who will benefit from daily physical activity and mental enrichment. Puzzle toys, long walks, and training games can help her stay engaged and build confidence. With patience, structure, and plenty of love, Dee Dee is ready to become someone's playful and devoted companion.

261000.name: Squeaky
261000.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Squeaky seems to have lived a quiet life with her owner who sadly passed away. Very little is known about her except that while shy for a start, she is a very friendly sweet lap cat and gives love "pecks". Squeaky is a senior gal, a bit lost in her kennel. She prefers to stay in her open den. She has saucer eyes that are all on you when you open her kennel. What is going on? who are you? What do you want from me? As my hand  advances toward her head, she first tries to stop me with a very soft and velvety paw, then accepts more petting. She enjoys special treats. The ice is broken. She moves out of her box and even tries to come on my lap. We are friends....Still, a shelter, a cage are no place for an elderly cat. Squeaky needs a home sweet home, peaceful and with a new owner who enjoys senior pets and is willing to make their golden years truly gold... Squeaky is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.









What my friends at ACC say about me:
I am a sweet, social, older gal, looking for the perfect forever home!
I may enjoy casually batting at a toy mouse every now and then, but my favorite activity is snuggling on my favorite person's lap!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

A volunteer writes: Tiller is here from a lack of options but not a lack of trying and certainly not for lack of love. Loved so selflessly, her previous guardian told us they just wanted Tiller to have a better chance at life. That love doesn't come around everyday, but we know that for this special little kitty it'll come around twice. When I opened her condo door, she seemed charmingly baffled by my presence and gently pulled back to sniff a bit as she made sense of me. She's been through considerable changes and while petting wasn't the best way to form a connection with her, playtime was. Leaping after her pipe cleaner feather, Tiller puts her heart into playtime and it shows. We're fully hoping for and committed to doing everything we can to get Ms. Tiller the second chance she deserves. Please come grab a pipe cleaner feather and meet this lovely kitty today.

261046.name: Marble Loaf
261046.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Marble Loaf is a pretty, friendly and girly tigress who was found in a carrier, abandoned in a park. She was brought to the Manhattan Care Center to shelter her and find her a home. Marble Loaf is a curious, social and affectionate little gal who comes right away to meet her visitors, favoring cuddles over treats and rolling on her side for petting(see her video). She would not be a fan of being picked up(like many cats including my own amazing pets) and did hiss at the sight of some other cats when she was being examined. She could have been scared(she tried to flee) by the medical room and the cats overload... I really like Marble Loaf, a pretty cat with lovely eyes and a sweet disposition. Let's keep in mind Marble Loaf(whose past is a total mystery) went through difficult times and needs a new owner who understands to give her time and space to acclimate to her new life. I think she could be a wonderful companion for many years to come....








What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

261071.name: Yogi
261071.summary:
Meet Yogi!
Yogi came to ACC as a stray, so not much is known about his past. Since arriving, he's shown himself to be a sweet, gentle dog who is still learning that the world is a safe place. New people and unfamiliar environments can make him nervous at first, but with a little patience (and a few tasty treats!), Yogi begins to gain confidence and quietly seeks out companionship. He's looking for a family that will let him settle in at his own pace and celebrate the little victories along the way.

My Ideal Home
Yogi would thrive in a calm, patient home with adopters who understand that trust takes time. He'll benefit from a predictable routine, positive reinforcement training, and gentle encouragement while he builds confidence. Because he can be sensitive to sudden movements and handling, allowing him to choose when to interact will help him feel safe and secure.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful nature and need for a quiet environment, Yogi is recommended for a home with children 13 years and older.

Good with Other Pets?
Yogi's history with other animals is unknown. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended for any resident pets.

Overall Health
Yogi is healthy overall. He is currently adjusting to the shelter environment and has shown signs of fear and stress, but he has been friendly and cooperative during his veterinary care.

Behavior Determination Level 4 - Experienced Adopters. Yogi will do best with adopters who can provide a calm home, use reward-based training, and respect his boundaries while he gains confidence. He has shown some potential for resource guarding in the shelter and has been reported to leash-bite when overstimulated, both of which are expected to improve with patient management and training.

Other Fun Facts
Yogi is very food motivated, and treats are a great way to earn his trust! Once he starts to feel comfortable, he willingly comes back for more snacks and gentle interaction. Watching his confidence grow is incredibly rewarding, and his future family will get to enjoy seeing his sweet personality blossom.

261073.name: Sticky Keys
261073.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Sticky Keys!
Sticky Keys may have been abandoned in Central Park, but he's ready to find a place he can finally call home. He's a moderately social guy who enjoys checking out his surroundings and will happily seek out attention from people once he feels comfortable. He's still learning to trust new experiences, so he'll do best with someone who can give him time, patience, and plenty of positive encouragement.

My Ideal Home
Sticky Keys would do best with an adult adopter who can help him build confidence at his own pace. He'll need daily physical and mental enrichment, along with force free, reward based training. Food puzzles, long lasting chews, sniffy walks, and other fun activities will help keep his mind busy and his tail wagging.

Good with Other Pets?
Sticky Keys' interactions with other dogs have been a little complicated, and he can become tense and overwhelmed during play. For now, ACC recommends no dog parks and carefully managed introductions with other dogs. His new family can help him build positive associations with other dogs in a calm, controlled setting.

Good with Kids?
Because Sticky Keys can be fearful and uncomfortable with handling, ACC recommends an adult only home at this time.

Things to Know
Sticky Keys is still learning that the world can be a safe place. He may flinch or become uncomfortable with handling, so it's important to let him choose when he's ready for interaction. With patience, consistency, and plenty of positive reinforcement, this sweet boy can start putting the right pieces together and discover what life is like with a family of his own.

261074.name: Braxton
261074.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Braxton is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center and during intake, Braxton has displayed intense fearful behavior, including growling, baring his teeth, thrashing, and was control poled out of the police car. Braxton continues to struggle to acclimate to the shelter environment despite efforts to minimize stress and allow him time to decompress, remaining extremely shutdown in care. Medically, Braxton is Otitis, Mild dental disease, Superficial lesions to hind paws.

Braxton was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Braxton has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and is not allowing for handling to be removed from the kennel. During his intake, Braxton began growling and baring teeth when staff attempted to remove him from the police car. Due to his behavior, a control pole was used to bring him into the building safely. Since his intake, Braxton has not allowed handlers to remove him from the kennel for walks or interaction. When leashed, he begins thrashing and flailing on his own accord; no pressure is applied by handlers. Due to noted concerns, we recommend that he be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner, who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Peaches!
Peaches was found as a stray, and now she's ready to find the sweet life she deserves. True to her name, she's a peach of a pup who enjoys exploring her surroundings and taking things at her own pace. With a little patience and a lot of love, she's sure to blossom into a wonderful companion.

My Ideal Home
Peaches would love a calm, patient home where she can settle in comfortably and build confidence at her own speed. Gentle introductions, positive reinforcement, and a predictable routine will help this sweet girl feel safe and secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Because Peaches arrived as a stray, her history with other animals is unknown. Slow, thoughtful introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Peaches would likely do best with older, respectful children who understand that she appreciates gentle interactions and the chance to warm up at her own pace.

Things to Know
Peaches walks nicely on a loose leash and enjoys exploring while checking in with her people. She has medical needs that ACC staff will be happy to discuss with you when you meet her. If you're looking for a gentle companion to spoil rotten, Peaches is ready to make life a little sweeter.

She hasn't been too interested in our array of toys but hasn't been one to turn down some pets and scritches. We're all hoping that she can fit in with you.

261109.name: Elena
261109.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Elena is laying in the back of his den, tense with his tail curled tightly around his lower body as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and the den cover is lifted, he remains pressed to the back of the den. Crunchy treats are offered and after a few seconds of hesitation, Elena leans forward to eat them. He is tolerant of all petting, leaning away on initial contact and remaining tense but tolerant, purring for a bit while he is pet. He is softly spoken to and offered some wet food, and after a few seconds begins eating it, occasionally pausing to assess his surroundings with his body held low before beginning to eat again. He is able to be maneuvered forward for pick up and is tolerant of being held, remaining stiff and tense but without further issue. When placed back into the kennel, he walks into his den, returning to laying at the back of it and wrapping his tail tightly around himself again. He continues to tolerate more petting on the head and cheeks but does not engage with the attention. 

Elena tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

261110.name: Bonnie
261110.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I will need daily physical activity to keep me healthy and happy!
I am playful and cute!
Bonnie is laying in the back of his den, slightly tense with his tail curled around his body as the assessor approaches and opens the kennel door. Crunchy treats are offered and he is initially hesitant before slowly getting up and coming forward to eat the treats. Initially when petting is attempted, he leans away to avoid contact. After a few seconds and some soft talk, he allows petting, loudly purring and leaning in as he is pet on the head and cheeks. He is hesitant to leave the den but is able to be slowly coaxed to the front of the kennel, tense with his tail held low. When petting is attempted, he allows and leans into all petting, continuing to purr and body appearing looser and more relaxed. He is able to be easily picked up and remains calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, Bonnie remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting and attention.

Bonnie interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

261121.name: Quinoa
261121.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Quinoa is at risk due to medical reasons. Quinoa is a very friendly and affectionate geriatric cat who came into the shelter underweight, dehydrated and with muscle wasting. He had various wounds, which are all healing. He has a heart murmur and regenerative anemia. While Quinoa is eating well, his abdominal palpation revealing slightly thickened intestines, indicating that he may require further evaluation for underlying GI disease. Quinoa requires supportive care and monitoring and additional diagnostics may be needed.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
My purr motor is always running!
I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

A volunteer writes: Quinoa came right to the front, pushing his little forehead into the door to remind he was there. Unfortunately this sweet senior fellow is no stranger to pleading his case. Quinoa was found on his own for a few days. Injured and alone he waited for someone to notice and when someone did, they brought him to us. We've been filling in the blanks as best we can and have learned a few details about this adorable fellow. First, Quinoa loves to play! He buried his little nose into his pom pom ball and started deconstructing it like a little puppy. After petting and playing with him, I put down some treats and watching him sketch out if he wanted to pause playtime and eat the treats or continue melted my heart. Quinoa's waiting to find a soft place to land.

261137.name: Super Star
261137.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Super Star!
Super Star may have arrived as a stray, but this sweet girl is already proving she has a shining personality. While we don't know much about her past, we do know she is a gentle pup who quickly warms up once she feels comfortable. With her soft body, happy tail wags, and love for pets, Super Star is ready to find a family who will help her shine bright.

My Ideal Home
Super Star is looking for a patient adopter who will give her the time and support she needs to adjust to her new surroundings. She would love a calm home where she can relax, receive plenty of affection, and continue building confidence. Her new family should also be prepared to discuss her medical needs with staff when they meet her.

Good with Other Pets?
Super Star's history with other animals is unknown, but she has not shown any concerns around other dogs while in our care. Since we do not know if she has lived with other pets before, slow and thoughtful introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Super Star's history with children is unknown. She has shown herself to be a gentle and affectionate pup, but respectful introductions are recommended to help her feel comfortable and set everyone up for success.

Things to Know
Super Star is a sweet and sensitive older lady who may be a little shy at first, but she doesn't take long to warm up. Once she feels safe, she is happy to offer tail wags, sit politely, and soak up attention from her favorite people. If you're looking for a loving companion who is ready for her second chance, Super Star may be the perfect match to light up your life.

261166.name: Millie Meowy Brown
261166.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Milie is a beautiful calico girl who seems to live for company. She knows when someone enters her ward and appears at her door, already rolling on her side, making biscuits for extended periods until someone notices. Same when someone opens her kennel..Millie is very welcoming and even ready to come on one's lap if allowed. She loves her cuddles and would stay with her guests for endless amounts of time. She plays nicely with a feather wand and even allows petting when she does so. Millie is said to play rough and this is why she should go to a quiet and experienced home without young children to avoid any scratching incident. Millie was relinquished into our care because she scratched the owners' child(age unknown)and made the parents uncomfortable with having her around with the arrival of a new baby. 
Millie had a hard time in her beginnings at the care center but quickly became the lovely gal you will meet if you open her kennel. She deserves a second chance. Could it be with you?

Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I would do best in a home with only adult humans.
I love to be loved, but on my own terms! Let's brush up on some feline body language together!
I am not one to sit still and will love interactive playtime in my new home!

261168.name: Ms.Pumpkin
261168.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Ms Pumpkin and housemate Niles were brought to the care center as a new and elderly family member became allergic to their dander. Ms Pumpkin is said to be the sweetest kitty, a great cuddler who although very lively plays gently with all, including children and other cats. At the shelter, though, Ms Pumpkin is quite shy, electing to rest at the back of her cubby, a quiet little "mouse" with saucer eyes. Ms Pumpkin never swatted or hissed, she just makes herself small while accepting petting, leaning gently into my hand. No doubt about it...Ms Pumpkin dreams of a home and to be loved again by new owners who understand the loss she went through. Ms Pumpkin is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center.

261169.name: Niles
261169.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Niles and housemate Ms Pumpkin were brought to the care center as a new and elderly family member became allergic to their dander. Niles is said to be an outgoing, smart, curious and affectionate kitty who plays gently with all. When I first met Niles, she was avoiding me "at all costs". I literally was chasing after her in all the areas of her kennel until she understood I meant well. I came with treats, catnip toys, feather wands and a soft voice and touch...Indeed, Niles is a smart gal as related to us by her former owner. Niles opened up and soon enough, we were having a great time together(see her video). Niles is apparently healthy(she did have a hydrometra upon admission prompting her spay) and did well on her behavior evaluation. Loosing her family, her home and her housemate was quite tough for a little gal like Niles and she definitively will need an understanding new owner to make her transition to a new chapter in her life, a success. Come and meet lovely Niles at the Manhattan Care Center!

261183.name: Lightening-Bug
261183.summary:
Meet Corporal Lightening-Bug!
Corporal Lightening-Bug arrived at ACC as a stray, so not much is known about his past. Since arriving, he's shown himself to be a friendly dog who enjoys gentle attention from people. Although the shelter environment has made him feel a bit overwhelmed, he readily approaches handlers, leans into petting, and is looking for a family that will help him build confidence and feel secure.

My Ideal Home
Corporal Lightening-Bug would thrive in a calm, patient home that understands he may need a little time to decompress. A predictable routine, positive reinforcement training, and plenty of opportunities for enrichment will help him settle in and become his best self. He will also benefit from continued leash training, as he can pull strongly when excited or nervous.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearfulness and the stress he's displayed in the shelter, we recommend a home with children 13 years and older who can respect his space and help him adjust at his own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
His history with other animals is unknown. During his behavior assessment, he did not show reactivity toward other dogs, but slow, thoughtful introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Overall Health
Corporal Lightening-Bug is healthy overall. He has shown signs of stress in the shelter, including heavy panting and drooling, which are expected to improve as he settles into a quieter home environment.

Behavior Determination Level 3 - Experienced Adopters. Corporal Lightening-Bug is a sweet dog who is experiencing stress in the shelter. He will do best with adopters who can provide a calm environment, allow him time to decompress, and continue building his confidence using patient, reward-based training.

Other Fun Facts
Despite feeling anxious in the shelter, Corporal Lightening-Bug enjoys affection and happily leans into pets from people he meets. He was friendly with staff at intake, greeting them with a loose, wiggly body and an enthusiastic hello. With a little time and reassurance, this handsome boy has all the makings of a loyal and loving companion.

261253.name: Butter
261253.summary:
Butter is a sweet, affectionate girl who loves being close to her people. With her calm, easygoing personality, she's happiest relaxing by your side or spending time with the family. She enjoys short daily walks, loves car rides, and is easy to groom, making her a wonderful companion for someone looking for a loyal, laid-back dog.

Butter is looking for an adopter who can also provide her with a little extra care. She currently has an aural hematoma (a swelling of the ear flap) that will require follow-up veterinary care after adoption to ensure it heals properly. Her new family should be prepared to continue any recommended treatment and attend follow-up appointments as directed by their veterinarian.

If you're looking for a loving companion and are willing to help Butter through her recovery, she'll reward you with plenty of affection and loyal companionship.

My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Butter was so easy. She was slightly reserved at first but I didn't force anything and before you knew it, we were buddies. She loves to give kisses and lean against you. On walks, she has little to no pulling and was mostly interested in sniffing. She had zero reactivity to anything and appears friendly with other dogs given her body language when passing them (she mostly ignored them but did have a friendly soft body with some). She lit up and wagged her tail when kids walked by. At Petco, she really opened up and loved getting pets/attention from fellow shoppers and employees. Even though she's mellow on walks, she seems like she can go for a while and would make a great hiking buddy. She gets excited in the car because she's happy to be there knowing she's going on an adventure. We were in a pretty quiet area of Staten Island but she seems like she would fine in busy city neighborhoods too given she was unbothered by most things. She easily did her potty business outside in the park. Anyone would be lucky to adopt Butter! My only wish on the borough break was that I could have kept her out longer!

261259.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Peapod is at the front of the kennel, laying down and making soft eye contact with the assessor as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, Peapod gets up and meows softly. He allows and leans into all petting and purrs as he is pet, but does occasionally back away, sitting upright and wrapping his tail around himself. He is able to be picked up and held, trembling a bit but continuing to allow and lean into all further petting. When placed back into the kennel, he sits upright in the middle of the kennel, once again curling his tail tight around his lower body. He leans into all further petting on the head and cheeks and continues to purr.

Peapod interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

261294.name: Onyx Phonics
261294.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Onyx Phonics needs at risk placement for medical reasons. He is a sweet boy who loves had rubs but is not eating in shelter due to a severe upper respiratory infection. He needs supportive care in a veterinary clinic to recover.

A volunteer writes:
Onyx Phonics and housemate Sabby were brought to the Manhattan Care Center as their elderly owner sadly passed away. Onyx, an all ebony handsome gent was a little nervous at the beginning of his stay but quickly settled into a very friendly mode, happy to have company, getting pets and rolling on the kennel floor to show how glad he was to be attended to. Onyx is even sweet and welcoming with the veterinary team and very compliant with the care he is getting. We are all sad to see him so affected by his URI and wish upon a star to see him getting the supportive care he needs at an outside veterinary facility. Onyx is a great guy, let's give him the help he so deserves!

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
Onyx Phonics tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter.  He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home.  We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.
