261295.name: Sabby
261295.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

Sabby is on the at-risk list for medical concerns. Sabby is a cat with a history of attacking her tail. She has now had two tail amputations and continues to self mutilate. Her most recent surgery is not healing properly because she was able to open it back up. She is on multiple pain medications, but will likely need a long-term anxiolytic medication and additional follow up veterinary care to manage the current tail amputation site. Behaviorally, Sabby is sweet and has allowed medical handling.

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Sabby is laying in her den, eyes wide and pupils dilated as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened and the den cover is lifted, Sabby leans forward to sniff the assessor's hand before exiting the den. She allows all petting, leaning into petting on the head and cheeks. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into her kennel, she continues to allow extended petting, raising her back as she is pet. When attempting to end the interaction, Sabby attempts to escape the kennel, appearing interested in exploring. She does this a few times but is able to be easily picked up, held, and placed back into the kennel where she continues to allow all further handling. 

Sabby interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

261298.name: Liutenant Limeade
261298.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Lieutenant Limeade is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Lieutenant Limeade has shown intense fearful behavior, including growling, trembling, whale eye, lip licking, urinating and, pacing in search of an exit, and avoiding interaction with handlers and continues to struggle to acclimate to the shelter environment despite patient handling. Medically, Lieutenant Limeade is apparently healthy.

Lieutenant Limeade was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past history in a home environment is unknown. Lt. Limeade has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and has only been allowing for minimal handling from staff. In the kennel, she begins growling, moving away, or retreating to a back corner of her kennel; at times, he was urinated or defecates on himself. He has begun growling during leashing. Once out of the kennel, he remains highly fearful and shut down, avoiding any form of interaction with handlers. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Lieutenant Limeade be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope Rescue partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification using force-free, positive reinforcement-based training to safely manage/modify any behavior White Lightning presents with outside of the Care Centers.

261303.name: Jamie
261303.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Jamie!
Jamie was found inside a building's lobby and is now looking for a loving home where she can feel safe and comfortable. This sweet girl may need a little time to warm up, but once she feels at ease, her affectionate side shines through. Jamie enjoys treats, gentle attention, and having the chance to approach new friends at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Jamie would do best with a patient adopter who understands that trust takes time. Slow introductions, a predictable routine, and positive reinforcement will help Jamie feel confident as she settles into her new home. She is looking for someone who will respect her boundaries while celebrating all her little victories along the way.

Good with Other Pets?
Jamie's history with other animals is unknown. Slow, careful introductions are recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Jamie's sensitivity when startled, she would do best in a home without young children. Older children may be considered after a proper introduction.

Things to Know
Jamie is a sweet and affectionate pup who enjoys treats, gentle pets, and staying active. She may be unsure in new situations at first, but she recovers quickly and is ready to build a bond with someone who will give her the patience and support she deserves. If you're looking for a companion who will reward your kindness with trust and affection, Jamie may be the perfect match.

261312.name: Gumball
261312.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Gumball is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Gumball has not acclimated well to the shelter environment despite best efforts to keep him comfortable. Gumball intially presented as highly fearful and avoidant of interaction with handlers. In quieter, calmer settings, Gumball engages with snuffle mats, is loose-bodied with familiar handlers, and has been easy to remove from kennel. When trying to return Gumball to his kennel, he plants, thrashes, has leash bit, and has often needed multiple different pathways with multiple handlers and the use of a belly band to get him successfully back into the kennel. Medically, Gumball has diarrhea.

Gumball was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. Gumball has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and has allowed for minimal handling. He is highly avoidant of interaction and is reluctant to return to his kennel despite best efforts to motivate him, often requiring several handlers to get Gumball back into his kennel. Due to Gumball's behavior concerns, we recommend an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

261317.name: Mr. Bing
261317.summary:
Meet Mr. Bing!
At just 6 months old, Mr. Bing is a happy, social pup who thinks everyone he meets is a potential new best friend. His previous owner described him as social and affectionate, and his shelter friends agree! He's got a wiggly body, a wagging tail, and plenty of puppy enthusiasm to share.

My Ideal Home
Mr. Bing is an active young pup who will need plenty of exercise, playtime, training, and enrichment. Puzzle toys, long walks, and games will help him put all that puppy energy to good use while he learns his manners.

Good with Other Pets?
Mr. Bing previously lived with another dog and has been friendly and playful with dogs at ACC. He's enthusiastic when meeting canine friends and will benefit from patient introductions and continued guidance around appropriate play.

Good with Kids?
Because Mr. Bing is still working on his puppy impulse control, ACC recommends a home without children under 5.

Things to Know
Mr. Bing is still very much a puppy and is learning that not every exciting moment calls for maximum enthusiasm. He's highly motivated by people, treats, and fun, making him a great candidate for positive-reinforcement training. If you're ready for a playful, affectionate pup and all the adventures that come with him, Mr. Bing is ready to meet you!

261325.name: Finn
261325.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
My favorite pastime is being visually admired! Pet me with your eyes!

A volunteer writes: Finn has a lot of life experience but right now his experience is centered around trying to make himself small. I played along and pretended I couldn't see Finn as he lowered himself in the corner behind his bed. He was brought to a veterinary hospital with other cats, so his history is a bit of a mystery and he hasn't yet felt up for helping us to fill in the blanks. We can understand and support that, but Finn has something really big going for him and that's his curiosity. Finn sees us trying to build a friendship and I'd like to think he gives us a little credit for trying to go at his pace. We give him treats, share slow blinks, and gently, slowly, patiently offer him pets which sometimes he accepts and other times questions but we know that Finn wants to find a little more certainty in the midst of all of life's uncertainty and we're all hoping he can find that with you.

261338.name: Astrology

It must have been quite a frightening event for the munchkin...Astrology is indeed very timid and handshy, although she accepts brief petting and even pick up. Cute Astrology needs a nurturing, quiet, loving and safe home with an owner experienced in little ones who have started their life in a traumatic way. She is hoping for a new and happy beginning with you!

261349.name: Cashmere
261349.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Cashmere, a beautiful senior Tortie is with us as her owner was displaced. She comes with lovely comments, all pointing to a very sweet, friendly and affectionate pet with all(she has not mingled with cats though). Cashmere is quiet in her kennel. She is a big girl at twenty one pounds, dressed in bright colors, a bit shy for a start and likely wondering what on earth could be going on around her. She looks at first blankly at me but soft words, a gentle touch, some treats somehow get through her. Her forelegs are moving like to make biscuits. She slowly moves forward and accepts clearly with relief and peace my presence. I really like Cashmere. I have no doubt that she is a wonderful companion who will bring joy and warmth to any household. At 11, Cashmere should not be in a cage, but home, safe, cared for and loved. Come and meet this lovely lady at the Manhattan Care Center!

261356.name: Axel
261356.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Axel came into the QUACC after being brought in as a stray. In the care centers, Axel has displayed a low threshold for arousal, including jumping up with his mouth open during activity. When a staff member grabbed his leash near his neck to move him away from another dog, Axel turned, vocalized, and bit the handler's hand, leaving red marks and raised skin without breaking skin. As a result, we recommend Axel is placed with one of our New Hope Partners.

261375.name: Pickles
261375.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
Pickles is standing at the front of the kennel, observing the assessor with dilated pupils as they approach. When the kennel door is opened and he is softly spoken to, he greets them with a soft head bunt, tail held high and allowing/leaning into all petting. Pickles is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm and seeming to enjoy being held, leaning against the assessor's body and looking around the room curiously. When he is placed back in the kennel, he tries to get back out, tail flicking slightly. His focus is easily refocused with further petting, attention, and soft talk, and he continues to allow petting and handling without further issue.

Pickles interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

261406.name: Crissy
261406.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Crissy!
Crissy is a sweet girl who can be a little unsure when things feel new or overwhelming. Her finder says she is comfortable with being handled and cared for, including baths, brushing, and nail trims, but at the shelter she has been feeling nervous and needs some time to settle in. She's hoping for a patient person who will let her take things at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Crissy would do best in a calm home with someone who understands that building trust takes time. She's used to three short walks a day and will need continued help with leash manners, especially around other animals.

Good with Other Pets?
Crissy's history with dogs is limited, and ACC recommends a home without cats or smaller pets.

Good with Kids?
Because Crissy is currently uncomfortable with touch and new experiences, ACC recommends an adult-only home where she can decompress and build confidence at her own pace.

Things to Know
She may be nervous in new situations, but with patience, consistency, and plenty of positive reinforcement, she can start feeling more secure in her new surroundings.

Meet Garden!
Garden has quite the story. He was found on the roof of a building and is now searching for a safe place to finally put down roots. This gentle boy may be shy at first, but with a little patience and a pocket full of treats, he begins to come out of his shell.

My Ideal Home
Garden would thrive in a calm, quiet home with someone who understands that trust takes time. Gentle encouragement, a predictable routine, and letting him set the pace will help him grow into a confident companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Garden's history with other animals is unknown. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended if he'll be sharing his home with other pets.

Good with Kids?
Because he's still gaining confidence, ACC recommends an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Garden can be nervous around new people and situations, but he responds well to a slow, low-pressure approach and plenty of positive reinforcement. Give him the time and space he needs, and you'll help this sweet boy truly bloom.

261434.name: Judy G
261434.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!

A volunteer writes: An exceptionally trusting and hardworking mother cat tried to enter someone's home several times, eventually bringing her kittens along with her. While they didn't get the forever home they hoped for, their efforts brought them one step closer to finding it. This is Judy G! She's the star of the show and really leans into it without forgetting where she came from. She has her fanciful big stretches and regularly attempts to walk right out of her condo herself, but Judy G takes finding a forever family as seriously as she can for a kitten of only eight months. As one might expect, Judy G is terrifically playful and is curiously confident in her multitasking skills. While we were playing with her favorite pipe cleaner feather, she'd get distracted and try to stretch out onto my lap but then decide she wanted to walk around the Care Center. I'd show her the pipe cleaner feather and she'd eagerly return to playtime like she'd simply forgotten. A lot may have happened in her kitten life but one thing is for sure, she's ready and focused on finding a forever family to call her own.

261449.name: Purrlington
261449.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Purrlington, a handsome tabby was found in the street by a Good Samaritan who brought him in their bookbag(he was quite friendly) to the Manhattan Care Center. Purrlington was on his best behavior when he came to destination and with the veterinary team. Once in a kennel, though, this lovely gentlecat with fluffy cheeks became quite shy and just compliant with whatever was asked from him. Purrlington is a sweet guy, though and with patience, will blink back at his visitor, leans gently into pets and more recently, will play with a feather wand. I was very pleased to see how Purrlington enjoyed the game, telling me that understanding and patience on the part of his new owner or family will yield a wonderful, happy and loving pet for many years to come. Purrlington is apparently healthy, is already neutered, did well on his behavior evaluation(beside showing his timid side) and could go home with you today for many years to come!

A volunteer writes: Purrlington, a handsome tabby was found in the street by a Good Samaritan who brought him in their bookbag(he was quite friendly) to the Manhattan Care Center. Purrlington was on his best behavior when he came to destination and with the veterinary team. Once in a kennel, though, this lovely gentlecat with fluffy cheeks became quite shy and just compliant with whatever was asked from him. Purrlington is a sweet guy, though and with patience, will blink back at his visitor, leans gently into pets and more recently, will play with a feather wand. I was very pleased to see how Purrlington enjoyed the game, telling me that understanding and patience on the part of his new owner or family will yield a wonderful, happy and loving pet for many years to come. Purrlington is apparently healthy, is already neutered, did well on his behavior evaluation(beside showing his timid side) and could go home with you today for many years to come!

261458.name: Smoreo
261458.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Smoreo is laying in his den, meowing softly and observing the assessor with wide eyes as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, he leans forward to sniff their hand before softly head bunting it, allowing and leaning into petting on the head and cheeks. Smoreo is hesitant to exit the den, but after a few minutes of soft talk, coaxing, and petting, he exits the den and approaches the front of the kennel, allowing all petting. He is able to be easily picked up but squirms lightly when held for a few seconds. When placed back down, Smoreo remains at the front, continuing to allow all further petting and handling without issue. 

Smoreo interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Smoreo go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in rough play, new home adjustment, decompression and overstimulation.

261595.name: Edward
261595.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Edward is at risk due to behavior concerns. Edward has not adjusted well to the care center environment and has shown fearful shut down behavior when attempts are made when removing out of his kennel for walks. Despite our best efforts to keep him comfortable, Edward displays significant fear including freezing, planting, lowering his body and was noted prior to have thrash, leash biting, growling, and snapping when leash pressure or handling is increased. He is more comfortable when interactions are slow and low pressure, and he will accept treats from familiar handlers and has been observed to have loose and wiggly body language in kennel. Medically, Edward is currently receiving treatment for CIRDC.

Edward was brought to the Care Centers as a stray with another dog. Both dogs were reported to display defensive behavior and lunge in the home environment. In the Care Centers, Edward has been observed thrashing and pancaking when staff attempt to handle him with slip leads. During attempts to remove him, he has occasionally growled and snapped. However, when staff use slow and deliberate movements, Edward has been observed displaying a softer body and wagging his tail. Edward should be placed in a foster home through a New Hope Partner that can provide a low-stress environment and safely manage his fearful behaviors using positive reinforcement-based training.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

I am not one to sit still! I will flourish in a home with someone that will keep me mentally and physically active!

261600.name: Greyson
261600.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Greyson is laying in his den as the assessor approaches, eyes wide, pupils dilated, and body tense. When the kennel door is opened, he stiffens, moving his body as if to flee. As he is softly spoken to, he remains tense inside of his den. Greyson is tolerant of all petting but does not engage with the assessor. He is unable to be coaxed out of the den, so full pickup is not able to be attempted. He is tolerant of light upward pressure being applied to his sides and under his chest, remaining tense but not escalating. When the assessor moves to end the interaction, Greyson runs out of the den, scrambling to the top to avoid contact. When the kennel door is closed, he runs back into the den and presses himself close to the back wall.

Greyson tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents.

261605.name: Narwhal
261605.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Narwhal!
At 10 years old, Narwhal has mastered the art of taking life at his own pace. This sweet senior enjoys leisurely walks, sniffing around, and checking in when there are treats involved. He's a pretty chill guy who may take a little time to warm up, but he's happy to spend time alongside his people.

My Ideal Home
Narwhal would love a calm, comfortable home where he can settle in and enjoy his golden years. He'll appreciate daily walks, plenty of sniffing adventures, and a person who doesn't mind letting him do things at his own pace.

Good with Other Pets?
Narwhal's history with other animals is unknown. He has been neutral around dogs at ACC, but slow introductions are always recommended.

Good with Kids?
Because Narwhal has been known to grab and bite his leash when excited, ACC recommends a home without children under 5. Older, dog-savvy kids may be a possibility with an appropriate introduction.

Things to Know
Narwhal is a senior gentleman with a soft spot for snacks and a nose that loves to explore. He's ready to trade the sidewalk for a cozy couch and spend his next chapter with someone who will give him the love and stability he deserves. Consider this your sign to make Narwhal's golden years truly whale worth it!

Pre-Screener Form

King Kong came into the care center as an owner surrender due to moving to a new home that does not allow pets. His prior owners noted that he is a social, affectionate, very active, and playful dog who spends most of his time in the bedroom. He loves treats and playing with all forms of toys and was fed both a wet and dry food diet. King Kong has not adjusted to the care center environment and has allowed minimal handling; remaning highly fearful and avoidant. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

261619.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Double Dutch is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the care center, Double Dutch has displayed intense and persistent leash biting both during walks and when returning to his kennel. He can become difficult to redirect, at times ignoring treats and toys or quickly returning to biting the leash after being redirected. Double Dutch can be managed with toys and high-value treats at times, but continues to struggle with high arousal and leash biting despite these efforts, making it difficult to remove him from kennel. Double Dutch loves pattern games when he did go out with staff and is social. Medically, Double Dutch has Dental disease.

Double Dutch came into the QUACC after being brought in as a stray. In the care centers, Double Dutch has been intensely leash biting when being leashed, while on walks, and when returning to his kennel. He can be difficult to redirect and will often return to biting the leash after briefly engaging with treats or toys. As a result, we recommend Double Dutch is placed with one of our New Hope Partners.

261622.name: Lainey
261622.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Lainey!
Lainey is a wiggly, affectionate girl who loves being close to her people. She'll happily seek out attention and has a playful, social side, but she's also very good at letting you know when she needs a little space. She's looking for someone who will listen to her signals and let her build trust at her own pace.

My Ideal Home
Lainey would thrive with a patient adopter who can help her practice calm greetings and build her confidence. She'll need positive, reward-based training to help with her enthusiastic jumping and learn some good manners.

Good with Other Pets?
Lainey's history with other animals is unknown. She has shown that she can feel overwhelmed by pushy play, so any dog introductions should be slow and respectful, with plenty of opportunities for her to take breaks.

Good with Kids?
Because Lainey can become uncomfortable when she feels overwhelmed, ACC recommends an adult-only home where her boundaries can be respected.

Things to Know
Lainey is a girl who knows what she wants, and that's not such a bad thing! She gives clear signals when she's uncomfortable and will often choose to walk away rather than escalate. Give her the chance to communicate, plenty of patience, and lots of positive experiences, and she'll have the space she needs to feel safe and confident.

261623.name: Bugs Bunny
261623.summary:
Meet Bugs Bunny!
What's up, doc? Bugs Bunny is a playful, lovable guy who hopped into ACC after being dropped off at a police precinct, and now he's ready to hop right into a forever home. This handsome boy is affectionate with his handlers, happily leaning in for pets and showing off his silly, energetic personality. He may be a little bunny-like when it comes to zig-zagging on leash, but he's ready to learn and would love someone who can help him put his best paw forward!

My Ideal Home
Bugs is looking for a patient adopter who can help him polish his manners through positive, reward-based training. He's an energetic guy who loves being around people and would benefit from plenty of exercise, enrichment, and opportunities to learn. With a little guidance, Bugs is sure to be one hoppy camper.

Good with Other Pets?
Bugs' history with other animals is unknown, and he did not pass his dog assessment at the shelter. Any future introductions should be slow and carefully managed.

Good with Kids?
Bugs can get very excited and jumps up frequently, so ACC recommends a home without young children under 5. Older children may be considered after meeting him.

Things to Know
Bugs is an affectionate, playful guy who enjoys leaning into pets and greeting his people with enthusiasm. He's still working on keeping all four paws on the floor and resisting the temptation to investigate desks and counters, but his friendly nature makes him eager to engage with his handlers. Bugs does have some medical needs, and ACC staff will be happy to discuss them with potential adopters when they come in to meet him. If you're looking for a fun-loving companion who's ready for a fresh start, Bugs might just be your perfect hare-mate!

Meet Sgt. Simba! St. Simba is a quiet dog who may need a little extra time to feel comfortable with new people and surroundings. He is highly fearful while in care, but he seems to be slowly coming around as he becomes more comfortable. Sgt. Simba requires a slow, patient approach and a calm environment where he can build trust at his own pace. Once he feels safe, his personality can begin to shine. He knows the cue "stay," and his previous owner described him as a devoted companion. His groomer also reported that he was very good during grooming. Sgt. Simba would do best with an adopter who understands fearful dogs and is willing to give him the time, patience, and space he needs to feel secure.

261631.name: Jumper
261631.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

Jumper is at the front of the kennel, repeatedly pawing outside of the kennel door to solicit attention and leaning her body against the kennel door as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she begins firmly head bunting the assessor's hand, eyes wide, pupils dilated, tail flicking and displaying piloerection down her back but not escalating with extended petting. She briefly jumps out of her kennel to explore and is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into her kennel, she remains at the front, continuing to firmly head bunt the assessor's hand and remaining tolerant of all further petting and handling. 

Jumper interacts with the observer, solicits/ appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. We recommend that Jumper go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression, and overstimulation. 

A volunteer writes: Jumper hasn't had such a great summer, but she really hopes that you have. She'd love to hear about it, your vacations, time spent out, and time spent in because this summer was just... Well, Jumper spent the long hot summer living in an apartment wall after being left behind. This isn't what she wanted and is lightyears away from what she deserves, but still this very sweet, gentle and tiny cat emphatically pressed her whole neck into my hand in friendship. Brought to us by the kindhearted super who took the time to catch Jumper, we've been trying to get to know her little by little and have received nuzzles in return. Jumper slowly came out of her shell, though not out of her den, when I visited and she seems to know that summer isn't quite over yet, so there's a chance she will get better.

261644.name: Fitz
261644.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Fitz, a middle aged gentleman was found at the entrance of a building, inert and unkempt. A call for help was made and Fitz was brought to the Manhattan Care Center. Fitz is very underweight, was dehydrated, lethargic and looked like he had given up...No, no, no...We have to make you better, sweet Fitz. Fitz is now in adoptions, a quiet and gentle soul who is taking in the peace and the comfort even a shelter cage can bring to a cat who went through such hardship and G-- knows for how long...Fitz is in the recuperating phase, appreciating good food and petting. He is not playing yet but it is ok. What Fitz needs now is a giving, caring and understanding owner. A quiet and low traffic home too without small children. Will you be the one showing Fitz that care and love exists because for sure, he never or may be long forgot what they were all about.










What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

261647.name: Rocket
261647.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Rocket is at risk due to behavior concerns. Prior to arriving at the care centers he was involved in a bite when being put back in his crate the bite did not break skin. He has also shown defensive aggression toward handlers, growling and baring teeth. Rocket also has shown object fixation and has latched onto trees, metal pipes and other objects which air correctors had to be used. Medically Rocket is underweight and suffers from chronic otitis.

Rocket was brought to the Care Centers following a bite incident in the home. He is reported to become easily overstimulated. According to his previous owner, when friends were visiting the home, Rocket bit the owner's daughter when she attempted to place him into a crate. Rocket has also been observed biting a tree and elevator doors. In the Care Centers, Rocket presents as fearful and becomes tense when being walked. Given his bite history and tendency to become overstimulated, Rocket should be placed in a foster home through a New Hope Partner that can provide a low-stress environment and safely manage his behavior using positive reinforcement-based training.

Pre-Screener Form

Moose is a young, intelligent dog who has some significant behavior challenges that will need to be carefully managed. He is reactive on leash to strangers, children, moving objects, and other animals, which can make him difficult to handle in certain situations. At the same time, his previous owners reported that Moose excelled in obedience training and was a quick learner who enjoyed training sessions. With the right person who understands his needs, is committed to consistent training, and uses appropriate positive reinforcement-based methods, Moose has the potential to make meaningful progress. He will need an experienced, patient adopter who is prepared to provide structure, management, and ongoing training to help him succeed.

261672.name: Cheesecake Blondie
261672.summary:
My Borough breaker writes:
This sweet girl is so so precious! She gives the best hugs and leans into your body to show it. I enjoyed my time with her walking in Central Park. She didn't bark once, no aggression towards dogs, and loves loves people. She would love if every person could come and say hi to her and tell her how pretty she is! I fell in love with her instantly and she would be the best soulmate dog ever. This girl deserves to be in a loving home where she can continue to blossom and feel continuous love. She is truly the best!!!!

Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Cheesecake Blondie!
Cheesecake Blondie is as sweet as her name! Found roaming on her own, this lovely girl is now looking for a forever family where she can finally relax. She enjoys exploring at her own pace, checking in with her people for gentle pets, and taking in the world around her with quiet curiosity.

My Ideal Home
Cheesecake Blondie would love a calm, patient home where she can settle in at her own speed. She may be a little shy at first, but with kindness, consistency, and positive reinforcement, she'll have the chance to let her sweet personality shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Cheesecake Blondie's history with other pets is unknown. As with any new companion, slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Because she can be startled easily and prefers to choose when she's ready for affection, ACC recommends a home without young children.

Things to Know
Cheesecake Blondie enjoys gentle attention but appreciates having her space respected, especially while she's getting comfortable. Once she feels safe, she's happy to come over for pets and companionship. If you're looking for a quiet, gentle friend with a heart as sweet as dessert, Cheesecake Blondie may be the perfect match.

261676.name: Donnie Thornberry
261676.summary:
Meet Donnie Thornberry!
Donnie Thornberry is a young, energetic guy who came to ACC as a stray with no known history. He is social and eager to interact with people, but he can become very excited and overwhelmed, especially in the busy shelter environment. Donnie loves attention and will need some guidance learning to keep all four paws on the floor and stay calm when he gets excited.

My Ideal Home
Donnie would do best with an adopter who is ready to help him learn good manners through positive, reward-based training. He will benefit from plenty of exercise, enrichment, and opportunities to decompress in a calm environment. A home with older children and someone comfortable working with an energetic, easily over-aroused dog would be ideal.

Good with Kids?
Donnie's history with children is unknown. Due to his high energy, jumping, and social hyperarousal, ACC recommends a home with children over 13.

Good with Other Pets?
Donnie's history with other dogs is unknown, and he did not pass the dog portion of his behavior assessment. Further guidance from ACC should be followed when considering introductions to other dogs. His history with cats is unknown.

Overall Health
No medical concerns were provided in his behavior assessment. He is currently in ACC's care and should receive a routine veterinary evaluation as part of his placement process.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 - Donnie would do best with an adopter who is prepared to work on basic manners, impulse control, and managing his excitement using positive reinforcement. He is also showing anxiety in the shelter and will benefit from a calm environment and time to decompress.

Other Fun Facts
Donnie is a very enthusiastic people-dog who loves being around his handlers. He can get so excited that he jumps up and tries to lean into people for attention. With patience, structure, and reward-based training, he has plenty of potential to become a wonderful companion.

261702.name: Squidward Tortellini
261702.summary: ​Squid Tortellini is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. He is apprehensive of people and interactions at the start but can be enticed with treats and a slow approach. With a little patience and moving at his pace, he can feel confident enough to show his quirks and remember that he does seem to appreciate attention and petting but may be fearful or skittish at first, and may be intimidated by small children. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people, we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans.  Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

A volunteer writes: Monroe found herself surrounded by curious eyes, perhaps wondering why a tiny little cat with patchy fur was crying out for help in the middle of the sidewalk. This couldn't have been a good feeling for her, but thankfully a Good Samaritan noticed and swooped in to offer assistance by bringing her to us. Monroe has sought to course correct the kind of attention she received before by graciously presenting her friendship to everyone on a little plate. She comes to the front to say hello, is eager to engage with us and does so celebratorily. Picking yourself up and dusting yourself off at any age isn't easy, but Monroe is a senior who has been trying to do this for quite some time. She's patiently waiting to find someone to do this with her and give her the forever family she's always hoped for.

Pre-Screener Form

Treasure Map is at risk due to his behavioral concerns. Treasure Map is noted to have a bite history in the finder's home. When the finder raised their voice to tell him no, to correct him for house soiling and waved their finger at him, he jumped and bit them on the finder's breaking skin. He is also noted to have bitten when his toys are taken; that bite did not break skin. Finder described as playful and affectionate. In the care center, he frequently retreats, lowers his body, avoids eye contact, trembles, refuses to move, and is often unreceptive to treats. While outside, he remains highly fearful and may continue shaking, avoid interaction, and eventually refuse to move. Medically, Treasure Map is currently healthy at this time.

Treasure Map was brought to the care center as a stray; the finder had Treasure Map for 3 weeks and noted a bite incident in the home. In the finder's home, Treasure Map is noted to have had house soil. When the finder raised their voice to tell him no and waved their finger at him, he jumped and bit them on the finder's broken skin. He is also noted to have bitten when his toys are taken; that bite did not break skin. Treasure maps finder described him as playful and affectionate. In the care center, Treasure Map is noted to display fearful behavior and has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

261714.name: Picasso
261714.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Picasso!
Like his famous namesake, Picasso is one of a kind. Found as a stray, this sweet boy is still learning that the world can be a safe place. Beneath his shy exterior is a gentle dog who readily approaches for pets and has a soft, wagging tail for the people he trusts.

My Ideal Home
Picasso would love a calm, patient home where he can settle in at his own pace. A predictable routine, gentle encouragement, and positive reinforcement will help him continue building confidence and feeling secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Picasso's history with other animals is unknown. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended with any future furry family members.

Good with Kids?
Because Picasso can be fearful in new situations, ACC recommends a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Picasso can become anxious in unfamiliar environments, but he responds well to a patient, low-pressure approach. He's also working on his leash manners, and with a little guidance and consistency, he's sure to make great progress. Give Picasso the time he needs, and you'll discover a loyal companion waiting to blossom.

261739.name: Shy Shy
261739.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Shy Shy!
Shy Shy may live up to her name at first, but give her a little time and she'll show you her sweet side. She's a gentle girl who stays close to her people, accepts treats, and enjoys slow, thoughtful pets. Loud noises and sudden movements can make her flinch, so she's looking for someone who understands that a little patience goes a long way.

My Ideal Home
Shy Shy would love a calm home where she can settle in at her own pace. Her new family should give her time to get comfortable with new people and places while using plenty of positive reinforcement to help build her confidence. Once she trusts you, she'll be happy to stay close by and enjoy some gentle attention.

Good with Other Pets?
Shy Shy has shown no reactivity toward other dogs while in our care. Her history with other animals is unknown, so slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Because Shy Shy can be nervous around loud noises and sudden movements, ACC recommends a home without children under 5.

Things to Know
Shy Shy walks nicely with only mild pulling and was able to keep going even when passing construction. She may need a little extra reassurance in busy environments, but she's already showing us that she can handle new experiences with some support. If you're looking for a gentle companion who will appreciate a quiet life and a little patience, Shy Shy could be your perfect match.

261747.name: Senorita Roja
261747.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Senorita Roja is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Senorita Roja has shown defensive behavior during intake and handling, including hard barking, lunging, growling, baring teeth, and snapping at handlers. She redirected and bit the finder's thumb during an attempt to leash her, though the bite did not break skin. During medical handling, she remained tense and snapped when touched, continuing to bare her teeth and snap while awaiting sedation. She has allowed handlers to give her treats and readily accepts enrichment. Medically, Senorita Roja has cherry eye and is emaciated.

Since arriving at the care centers Senorita Roja has displayed concerning behaviors, often escalating to defensive aggression particularly during handling. We recommend placement with a New Hope rescue partner who is able to provide an experienced, adult-only foster home. Force-free, reward based training and/or consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended.

Benz is on the at-risk list due to medical reasons. He has developed CIRDC with possible pneumonia. Due to his level of stress, fear and anxiety in the shelter, his medical care is difficult. He needs to recover in a low stress environment where his anxieties can be alleviated.

He noted to allow petting but will begin to whine and move away. We recommend placement with an experienced home who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

Pre-Screener Form

 Buddy came into the care cneter as an owner surrender; due to this, his behavioral concern in a home environment is unknown. Buddy has not adjusted well to the care center environment during walks he frequently pulls hard on leash and has attempted to jump toward people, including a person offering a poop bag. Buddy is available for rescue through one of our new hope partners.

261812.summary:

Fox came to ACC after her beloved owner passed away, and she is understandably taking some time to adjust to this big change. She is a shy but very sweet girl who would love a patient person willing to let her settle in at her own pace. Once she feels comfortable, Fox has a gentle and affectionate side just waiting to shine.

My Ideal Home

Fox would do best in a calm, quiet home where she can take her time getting comfortable. A patient adopter who understands that trust can take time would be the perfect match for her.

Good with Kids?

Fox's history with children is unknown. Please see her behavior assessment for more information on what ACC recommends.

Good with Other Pets?

Fox's history with other animals is unknown. Slow, gradual introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health

Fox is a spayed senior cat who is ready to find a loving home where she can enjoy her golden years. She is currently diagnosed with Dental Disease

261846.name: Ruby
261846.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ruby was surrendered into care due to his owners' ongoing medical concerns and moving out of state, which made them unable to take him with them. Ruby's previous family described him as a dog that prefers contact on his own terms and spent most of his time outdoors. He is reported to love car rides, loves to play with toys, his favorite game being fetch, and loves treats and chicken. His previous owner did note that he is reactive to other dogs and strangers.  Ruby is noted ot have bitten in the previous home due to resource guarding. The bite did break the skin and drew blood. Due to the concerns reported in the previous home and during his stay in care, we recommend that Ruby be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner that can address his behavioral challenges with the use of a certified professional trainer that utilizes positive reinforcement methods only.

261855.name: Sunshine
261855.summary:
**Meet Sunshine!**
Sunshine is a gentle, quiet boy who came to ACC after his family's allergies made it difficult for him to stay in his home. He can be shy and may need some time to feel comfortable with new people, but once he settles in, he enjoys affection on his own terms. Sunshine is independent, has a low energy level, and especially loves having his coat brushed!

**My Ideal Home**
Sunshine would do best with a patient adopter who will give him the time and space he needs to settle in. He would enjoy a calm home where he can relax, watch the world from a window, and receive gentle affection when he asks for it.

**Good with Kids?**
Sunshine lived with a young child but tended to avoid them and preferred interactions on his own terms. A home with older, respectful children may be a better fit.

**Good with Other Pets?**
Sunshine has no known experience with dogs, so introductions should be slow and supervised. Sunshine has lived with 2 other cats.

**Overall Health**
Sunshine has no known medical concerns and is currently doing well.

261868.name: Ashe
261868.summary:
Meet Ashe

Ashe is a handsome Akita who came into our care as a stray and is now looking for a patient, experienced home where he can feel safe and settle in. Like many dogs, the shelter environment can be stressful and overwhelming for Ashe, and he has been showing some anxiety while in our care.

Despite this, Ashe has been tolerant of handling and is continuing to navigate his new surroundings. He will likely benefit from a calm, predictable home and an owner who understands canine body language and is comfortable giving a dog the time and space needed to decompress.

Because Ashe can be anxious in a shelter setting, we feel he would be best suited for an experienced adopter who can provide consistent structure, patience, and positive guidance. With the right person and environment, Ashe may have the opportunity to relax and show more of his personality outside the shelter.

If you have experience with Akitas or other large, independent breeds and are looking for a dog who needs a patient advocate, Ashe may be worth getting to know.

261874.name: Nala
261874.summary:
A volunteer writes:
You have to meet Nala, our little lioness! She is the sweetest! Her owner sadly passed away(as a result, we know almost nothing about her past life) and the next of kin is unable to adopt her. Nala was found to have a pyometra that was 100% resolved with a spay and she is right now doing very well and able to meet you. Nala loves company. She was an immediate hit among staff and volunteers. She rolls on her side for petting, slow blinks, purrs and is just the cutest kitty on earth. Who would not dream to have such a lovely pet at home? Nala is a senior at ten years of age, has senior teeth but is across the board apparently healthy, is already spayed and super aced her behavior evaluation. Do not make her and you wait any longer! Come and meet Nala at the Manhattan Care Center!







Nala is laying in a loaf position in the back of her kennel as the assessor approaches, observing them with wide eyes and dilated pupils. When she is softly spoken to and petting is attempted, Nala closes her eyes and leans into petting on the head and cheeks, allowing and leaning into all further petting and head bunting the assessor's hand as she is pet. Nala is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into her kennel, she rolls over onto her side, continuing to lean her body against the assessor's hand to solicit further petting and attention and continuing to allow all handling without issue.

Nala interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

Fluffy Mittens is quite a sight, a stately ginger with a "bruised" look one wants to hug ASAP. He came in all matted and it was quite a job to free him from tangled and knotted hair. His natural beauty is a bit affected by his new hairstyle but his inner beauty and goodness make up for it!! Fluffy Mittens is a gentle cat, low key, who goes with the flow, a lover and a total lap cat.I could spend hours with him, may be with a book or watching TV. Fluffy Mittens comes with outstanding recommendations from his former owners, appears reasonably healthy(beside being overweight and in need to loose a few pounds), aced his behavior evaluation and will be able to go home after his neuter. You have to meet Fluffy Mittens. He is a total sweetheart who will gift you with many years of shared happiness. Fluffy Mittens is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!






Fluffy Mittens is laying in his den as the assessor approaches, body and eyes neutral as the kennel door is opened. When he is softly spoken to and petting is attempted, he leans into petting on the head and cheeks. He is able to be coaxed out of the den with a squeeze up treat, eating all of it quickly and being able to be fed by hand. Fluffy Mittens is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when he is held. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front, continuing to allow and lean into all further petting and raising his back as he is pet. 

Fluffy Mittens interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

261967.summary:
A volunteer writes:
When I first met Jaguar, a five month old little gal, she was quite fearful and glued to the back of her kennel. She was tempted by food and curious of toys. After a few days, although still not a socialite, Jaguar has improved. She absolutely loves other kittens and there are many around her(in adjacent kennels) she tries to reach with her paws(see video). It is really cute to watch. She enjoys battling a feather wand but is still a little bit worried of petting. I feel she is getting there though....A quiet, nurturing, experienced and loving home is needed for this cute and lonely little gal who yesterday had a mom and three siblings. Jaguar is waiting for you at the Manhattan Care Center!

Galette is laying in his den, observing the assessor as they approach with neutral eyes and body. Galette interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

261982.name: Bastet
261982.summary:
Meet Bastet!
Bastet is a gentle, quiet girl who came to ACC as an owner surrender. Despite arriving in less-than-ideal condition, she has been calm, observant, and wonderfully tolerant with her caregivers. She is an easygoing cat who seems to appreciate a gentle approach and a little extra TLC.

My Ideal Home
Bastet would do best with a patient adopter who can give her time to settle in and continue helping her feel safe and comfortable. A calm home with someone who can provide plenty of gentle care would be ideal for her.

Good with Kids?
Her history with children is unknown. A respectful, calm approach is recommended while she settles into her new home.

Good with Other Pets?
Her history with other animals is unknown. Slow and gradual introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health
Bastet is currently receiving medical care for dehydration, being underweight, ear irritation, and hair loss. She is being monitored closely by ACC's medical team and will need continued veterinary follow-up.

Behavior Determination
Bastet has been calm and tolerant during her medical examinations and has allowed handling without issue. She may benefit from a patient adopter who can give her time to recover and adjust.

Other Fun Facts
Bastet has been described as calm and observant during her care. Despite everything she has been through, she has been a cooperative patient who allows her caregivers to help her.

262003.name: Ms. Caramel Jelly
262003.summary:
Meet Ms. Caramel Jelly!
Ms. Caramel Jelly may be a little shy at first, but underneath that cautious exterior is a sweet girl who enjoys gentle attention. She accepts pets, gives slow tail wags, and is starting to show us that she can feel comfortable with a little patience. She's looking for someone who will let her take things one step at a time.

My Ideal Home
Ms. Caramel Jelly would do best in a calm, quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace. Her new family should give her plenty of time to get comfortable with new people and surroundings and let her choose when she's ready for attention. A patient adopter who can help her build confidence will be a wonderful match.

Good with Other Pets?
Ms. Caramel Jelly has shown no reactivity toward other dogs while in our care. Her history with other animals is unknown, so slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Because Ms. Caramel Jelly is currently fearful and needs time to feel comfortable, ACC recommends an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Ms. Caramel Jelly is still getting her bearings, but she's already showing us that gentle encouragement goes a long way. She's not looking to rush into anything. She's simply hoping to find someone who will give her the time she needs to feel safe and discover just how sweet life can be.

262009.name: Cub Scout
262009.summary:
Meet Cub Scout! 🐾

Cub Scout is a 52-pound sweetheart who loves people and never misses an opportunity to say hello! He's very friendly with everyone he meets and will happily try to greet everyone he passes in the hall. His social, outgoing personality makes it clear that he loves being around people and getting attention.

Cub Scout was found as a stray alongside another male dog, and now he's ready for a fresh start of his own. With his friendly nature and love of people, he has all the makings of a wonderful companion.

If you're looking for a social, affectionate dog who thinks everyone is a potential new friend, Cub Scout may be just the pup for you! ❤️

Pup Tart is a sweet, friendly 40-pound brindle boy who loves meeting people and getting attention. He's incredibly social and greets everyone he meets with enthusiasm. He's still working on his basic manners and can be a little exuberant when he's excited, but he's eager to connect with his people and would thrive with someone ready to help him learn.

262039.name: Pomegranate Juice
262039.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
Pomegranate Juice is laying on top of his den, pupils dilated and meowing softly at the assessor as they approach. When the kennel door is opened and he is softly spoken to, he briefly hesitates before coming down from the top of the den and greeting the assessor with a soft head bunt. He allows all petting, leaning in and raising his back with his tail held high as he is pet. Pomegranate Juice is tolerant of pickup but squirms after being held for a few seconds. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front and continues to allow all further petting and attention. 

Pomegranate Juice interacts with the observer, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is showing behavior appropriate for cat parents with either an average amount of cat experience or demonstrate a basic understanding of typical cat behavior.

262069.name: Salvador
262069.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Salvador is the nicest cat! He is not only a handsome Ginger but mostly a sweet, welcoming and friendly kitty. Nothing much is known about Salvador's past life but a Good Samaritan rescued him from a very heartbreaking situation. Locked in a box, poor Salvador was being kicked by a bunch of kids. At the care center, he was found to have a painful fracture at the base of his tail, a condition called "tail pull" that can potentially cause elimination issues. Thankfully, it seems that Salvador is regaining control of his bladder and bowel and using his litter box. Through his stay at the care center, Salvador has been a "model" patient, a sweetheart everybody wants to meet and spend time with. Salvador is still being observed in our medical room but dreaming to soon be in a home where he can feel safe, cared for and love. He will be your very best friend in return...

262081.name: Maple
262081.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Maple!
Maple has had a pretty big change of scenery after being found tied to a bench, and she's still figuring out that people can be trusted. She's a gentle girl who starts out timid but warms up with a slow, patient approach. Once she feels comfortable, she'll come closer for treats and attention and even wag her tail for you.

My Ideal Home
Maple is looking for a calm, patient home where she can take her time settling in. She'll do best with someone who understands that trust takes time and will let her choose when she's ready to interact. Predictable routines, positive reinforcement, and plenty of quiet time will help her feel safe.

Good with Other Pets?
Maple has been observed barking at dogs passing her kennel, so she would benefit from careful introductions and plenty of distance from other dogs while she gets comfortable. Her history with other pets is unknown.

Good with Kids?
Because Maple is currently fearful and sensitive to new experiences, ACC recommends a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Maple can become anxious when she's overwhelmed, but she responds well to a gentle approach and treats. She's going to need someone who can give her the time and space to come out of her shell at her own pace. If you're looking for a quiet companion and are willing to let a sweet girl write her own happily ever after, Maple may be your perfect match.

Meet Rio!

Rio's got his eyes on you! You'll see what we mean if you come to visit him at the Staten Island ACC. He'll win any and all staring contests you challenge him to. This handsome tabby is very curious about the goings on outside his kennel and he likes to surveil the world from up-high. The ideal home for Rio would be an adult-only, experienced cat-owning home. He'll need an adopter who knows how to work with a fearful cat who has a low threshold for overstimulation. He may not be the most huggable little guy, but he'll appreciate you showing your love through toys and other positive outlets for his energy. If you're feeling Rio, why not come meet him at SIACC?

262122.name: Rhett
262122.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fee is waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card.

Meet Rhett!
Rhett is a social and affectionate pup who loves being where the people are. He's active and playful but also knows how to settle in for some mellow time, and he already knows sit, stay, and lay down. He even loves water, so he's ready to make a splash with his new family!

My Ideal Home
Rhett would love an active family who can keep him busy with walks, playtime, training, and plenty of time together. He's used to three 30-minute walks a day and does well with a routine.

Good with Other Pets?
Rhett can become excited by cats and may bark or jump when he sees them outside. His history with other dogs is not provided, so slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Rhett's history with children isn't provided. Because he's still working on his impulse control and can jump up when excited, older, dog-savvy children may be the best fit.

Things to Know
Rhett can be fearful of loud noises and may feel anxious when left alone, so he'll appreciate a patient adopter who can help him feel secure. He's also working on his jumping manners and will benefit from positive-reinforcement training. With his loving personality and playful spirit, Rhett has plenty of fun ahead of him.

262140.summary:
Meet Navy!
Navy may have arrived at ACC without much of a backstory, but it didn't take long for him to show us what a sweet guy he is. This affectionate pup has quickly won over his friends at the Care Center with his gentle, easygoing personality. Our veterinary team may have summed him up best during his first exam: "He is so friendly and open and easy going. We all love him!!!"

My Ideal Home
Navy is looking for a patient, loving home where he can settle in at his own pace. He can sometimes be unsure about things like being picked up or handled in unfamiliar situations, so he'll appreciate people who let him make choices and build confidence without rushing him. Once he's comfortable, Navy is wonderfully social and loves being close to his people. A calm introduction to his new life, regular exercise, and plenty of positive experiences will help this sweet boy thrive.

Personality
Navy is an affectionate, people-oriented pup who loves getting pets and isn't shy about asking for more! During his behavior assessment, he readily approached his handlers, leaned into affection, and maintained a loose, relaxed body while being handled. He's also been a nice walking companion, showing only mild leash pulling and no observed reactivity toward people or dogs while out on walks. He can be sensitive to some handling, particularly being picked up, but treats and a gentle approach help him feel more comfortable.

Behavior Assessment
Navy has earned a Behavior Assessment Level 2. He is highly social and affectionate but can show some fearfulness in situations where he feels uncertain. ACC recommends going slowly, allowing Navy to approach interactions on his own terms, and giving him time to decompress in his new home. He has also been observed taking treats with moderate pressure, so adopters can help him practice taking treats more gently through positive reinforcement. Because of these considerations, ACC recommends a home without children under 5.

Overall Health
Navy is neutered, microchipped, vaccinated, and has an overall good prognosis. He arrived with a skin infection and yeast in both ears, which have been treated by ACC's veterinary team. Staff can provide additional information about his medical history and any recommended follow-up when you meet him.

Why You'll Love Him
Navy is the kind of dog who reminds you that a little patience can lead to a wonderful friendship. Beneath those occasional moments of uncertainty is a friendly, affectionate boy who seeks out his people, leans into pets, and has already collected plenty of fans at ACC. Give Navy the chance to feel safe and settled, and you may just find yourself with one very devoted best friend.

Diana is a sweet medium-sized mixed-breed girl who was found as a stray and is now discovering how wonderful it is to have people looking out for her. She has warmed up quickly to both staff and volunteers, showing just how loving and adaptable she can be.

Diana is a food lover, so tasty treats are definitely one of the ways to win her heart! And with her adorable personality and the cutest ears, she's pretty hard to resist.

Diana is ready to leave her stray days behind and find a loving forever home where she can continue to blossom. Come meet this sweet girl and see if Diana might be your perfect match! ❤️

262147.name: Bambi
262147.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Bambi is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Since arriving at the care centers he has been observed to pull very hard on leash and has shown lack of impulse control  during interactions. He has shown a low threshold for arousal and has escalated to leash biting, jumping on and mouthing handlers. Additionally Bambi has shown signs of deterioration in kennel shortly after arriving and will intensely bite his crate bars or kennel walls. Bambi has otherwise shown social behavior toward handlers when interacted with. Medically, Bambi is apparently healthy.

Since arriving at the care centers, Bambi has displayed high levels of arousal paired with a lack of impulse control which has escalated to mouthing, jumping on handlers and leash biting. While in care he has also shown high levels of stress in kennel and has been observed chewing on his kennel bars intensely. We recommend placement with a New Hope rescue partner who is able to provide an experienced, adult-only foster home. Force-free, reward based training and/or consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended.

262149.name: Everett
262149.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Everett came into the care center as a stray. Due to this, his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. In the care center, he displays significant handling sensitivity during leash and defensive behavior during leashing attempts. He may initially accept treats and appear neutral, but becomes tense when the leash is introduced, backing away, barking, baring teeth, and lunging/snapping toward the leash and handler's hand. When successfully leashed, Everett is able to walk with minimal leash tension and has shown social and playful behavior with handlers, including leaning in for pets and engaging in fetch.  Everett would benefit from a slow, low-pressure approach to handling and continued management around leash placement and removal. Everett is available for rescue through one of our new hope partners.

262216.name: Bitty Boots
262216.summary:
Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.
My purr motor is always running!

262218.name: Luce
262218.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
Luce tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she goes to a home with experienced cat parents. Luce is described by her previous owner as a friendly cat who spends most of her time around people. 262221.name: Mister Simba
262221.summary:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Mister Simba is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Mister Simba has not acclimated well to the shelter environment and has been challenging to manage safely when returning him to his kennel. Mister Simba is easy to leash for walks, remaining tense bodied and hard stares at dogs on walks; unable to be redirected with treats or toys. When reaching the kennel room door, Mister Simba begins to balk and thrash. Once in front of his kennel, he continues thrashing, with the addition of kicking off the handler's body as they try to walk him into the kennel. Mister Simba has escalated to snapping at a handler's arm and bolting back out of the kennel, requiring multiple attempts and double leashing to be able to get him back into his kennel safely. Medically, Mister Simba is apparently healthy.

Mister Simba came into the QUACC after being brought in as a stray. In the care centers, Mister Simba has been generally fearful, retreating when approached and appearing sensitive to touch. Staff have been able to leash and bring him into the intake room, where he was described as alert and active, but remained fearful and avoidant of staff. As a result, we recommend Mister Simba is placed with one of our New Hope Partners.

Teaspoon is like a teaspoon full of sugar in your coffee or lemonade. She makes "all things" sweeter....Teaspoon is a lovely senior found under a Good Samaritan's car. She is a quiet soul in her kennel, laying peacefully in her main area and getting up and ready right away when someone is at her door. Such a gentle lady who enjoys petting, soft words  and even lays nonchalantly at the entrance of her kennel(see photos and video), looking at all the volunteers and staff admiring her and likely hoping to make it on my lap. Teaspoon is quite pretty too in her white and grey dress that gives her an even more peaceful look.  Teaspoon dreams to meet you and spend her golden years, loved and loving you. Come and meet her very soon at the Manhattan Care Center!

262372.name: Red Lily Beetle
262372.summary:
**Meet Red Lily Beetle!**

Red Lily Beetle is a 2-year-old female small mixed breed dog, weighing 33 pounds. Her history is a mystery, and her friends at ACC don't know much about her yet!

**What her friends at ACC say about her:**
Red Lily Beetle would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help her feel safe. She loves to be loved, but on her own terms! She has medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet her.

**My Ideal Home**
Red Lily Beetle will need daily mental and physical activity to keep her engaged and exercised. We recommend long-lasting chews, food puzzles, and hide-and-seek games, in addition to physical exercise, to positively direct her energy and enthusiasm.

**Good with Kids?**
Red Lily Beetle would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although she could be open to older human children once she meets them. Due to her fearful disposition at times and need for contact on her own terms, we recommend a home with no young children under 5.

**Behavior Determination**
**Level 2.** Red Lily Beetle is a highly social dog who approaches and greets excitedly, accepts pets and treats from handlers, leans into pets, and explores the room. She walks without issue on a leash.

**Other Fun Facts**
Red Lily Beetle is a sweet dog who seeks contact and accepts handling. She approaches with a loose body and is ready to find her forever home!

262384.name: Cartwheel
262384.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cartwheel is laying in her den as the assessor approaches, eyes wide, pupils dilated, and body tense. She is offered some crunchy treats and after a little bit of soft talk she leans forward and begins eating them. Cartwheel is a bit hesitant to approach, alternating between peeking her head out of the portal exit and leaning forward to sniff the assessor's hand and ducking back into her den. With more soft talk she is able to be coaxed from the den, tail and body held a bit low but fully exiting and approaching the front to greet the assessor. She allows and leans into all petting and is able to be easily picked up, body slightly tense when she is held but without further issue. When she is placed back down, she allows further petting and attention but runs back into her den when noises begin to occur around the room.

Cartwheel is a sweet, shy girl who seems to enjoy petting and attention but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.
