262388.name: Ford Explorer
262388.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Ford Explorer came into the care center as a stray; therefore, his behavioral history in a home environment is unknown. Ford Explorer has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. He is also noted to display fearful behavior, such as growling, staying at the back of his kennel, and being reluctant to be leashed or to leave his kennel. Once out of his kennel, he avoids all forms of interaction and attempts to put as much distance as he can between himself and handlers. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

262394.name: Sarah
262394.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I lived with children in my previous home.
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Sarah is standing upright in her den, eyes wide, pupils dilated and poking her head out of the portal exit as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, she begins stress meowing. With some soft talk and coaxing, she slowly exits the den and approaches the front of the kennel, greeting the assessor with soft head bunts. When noises occur in the room, she cranes her neck to look towards the source of the sound. She is able to be easily maneuvered back into the kennel but will walk back into her den. She continues to be easy to coax out and responds well to soft talk, approaching the front again, tail held high but displaying some piloerection at the base. She allows and leans into all petting, making biscuits as she is pet. She is able to be easily picked up, remaining calm when she is held. When she is placed back into her kennel, Sarah stays at the front, soliciting further attention and petting with soft head bunts and leaning into all further petting and handling. Sarah does stress meow throughout the assessment but remained social and open to interaction.

Sarah interacts with the observer, solicits and appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that Sarah go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment, decompression, and fearfulness.

262398.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Facebook is laying in her litterbox, cuddled up with her sibling and observing the assessor with wide eyes as they approach. When the kennel door is opened, she tenses. Petting is attempted and she is tolerant of all petting but leans away to avoid contact as she is pet before darting into the den. She is able to be coaxed out and approaches the assessor, leaning forward to sniff their hand. Facebook is able to be picked up but is tense as she is held. When placed back into the kennel, she darts back into her den. After the assessor ends the interaction and closes the door, she exits the den and resumes laying in the litterbox. 

Facebook tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend that she go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

262433.name: Aj

What my friends at ACC say about me:
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
AJ is laying in the back of his cubby, pupils dilated and body tense as the assessor approaches. When the cubby door is opened, he remains tense, observing the assessor and flinching as they slowly remove the folded blanket in front of him to access him more easily. He is softly spoken to and offered treats but does not take them. When petting is attempted, he is briefly tense before closing his eyes and leaning into petting on the head and cheeks, lightly kneading as he is pet. He is mildly tense when pet down his back but is tolerant of it. AJ is able to be maneuvered forward and is able to be picked up, slightly tense when held but without further issue. When placed back into his cubby, AJ returns to laying in the back, continuing to allow and lean into petting on the head and cheeks.

AJ interacts with the observer, appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting.  No known history of behavioral problems. We recommend that AJ go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in new home adjustment and fearful behavior.

262469.name: Miami Vice
262469.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!
My purr motor is always running!
Need some biscuits for your breakfast? I'm an expert kneader!
I am playful and cute!

Miami Vice is standing at the front of the kennel, softly meowing to solicit attention as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he walks forward, swishing his tail, purring, and head bunting the assessor's hand. He allows and leans into all petting and is able to be easily picked up, leaning against the assessor, purring, making biscuits, and appearing to enjoy being held for an extended period. When he is placed back into the kennel, he remains at the front and begins to meow again, allowing and leaning into all further petting and handling.

Miami Vice interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

262497.name: Sophia
262497.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Sophia was surrendered as a stray after spending 2 weeks in her finder's home. Her finder did know that it took some time for her to warm up, but she initially was snapping at them. She did show the potential to be social after some time and space in the finder's home. During her staying care, Sophia has been fearful and avoidant of interactions with handlers. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Sophia to be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope Rescue partner that can allow her the time and space to decompress and acclimate on her own.

262498.name: Dolce
262498.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Dolce was surrendered by his previous owner due to his ongoing medical concerns. His previous owner described him as a medium-energy dog that can be shy and prefers contact on his own terms. During his stay in care, Dolce has been fearful and avoidant of interaction. He has escalated to growling when approached in kennel, is avoidant of leashing, and has snapped when attempting to offer him a treat. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Dolce to be placed with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

262550.name: Driver
262550.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!
I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.
I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.
Driver is laying curled up in the back of his cubby, head up and observing the room with dilated pupils as the assessor approaches. When the kennel door is opened, he tenses slightly. When he is spoken to softly and the assessor offers their hand, he hesitates for a few moments before leaning forward to sniff it. He is tolerant of all petting, leaning in slightly when he is pet on the head before pulling away and slowly walking out of the cubby to avoid contact. He is able to be coaxed to the front of the kennel with soft talk, craning his neck to look around the room with his tail held low. He continues to allow all petting but remains tense. Driver is able to be easily picked up and is calm when held. When placed back into his kennel, he is tolerant of all further petting and handling but is still a bit tense and doesn't engage. 

Driver tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in fearful cat behavior.

262555.name: Bluey
262555.summary:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.
Pre-Screener Form

Meet Bluey!

Bluey is a large dog who has been having a difficult time adjusting to the shelter environment. He has been particularly stressed while in his kennel and has escalated to higher-level warning behaviors when feeling overwhelmed. That said, Bluey is slowly beginning to warm up to staff, which is an encouraging sign. His transition into a new home may take some time, and adopters should be prepared to give him patience, space, and consistency as he settles in.

Bluey's former owner had many wonderful things to say about him. He previously lived with older children, loves his chew toys, enjoys playing, and likes going for walks. These positive experiences give us a glimpse of the affectionate, playful companion Bluey can be when he feels comfortable and secure.

Bluey will need an experienced owner who understands canine body language and is willing to work with him at his own pace. A calm, structured home and a patient approach will be important in helping him build trust and feel safe. With time, consistency, and the right person by his side, Bluey may have the opportunity to show just how special he can be.

Pre-Screener Form

Meet Foxy! 🐾
Foxy is a sweet 7-year-old girl who, once she feels comfortable, has a fun, happy personality and a wonderful independent spirit. Her family describes her as a loving companion who enjoys being around people, spending time in the yard, and sharing meals with her family.

Foxy has been very fearful and stressed in the shelter environment, so she may need some time, patience, and a quiet space to decompress. Her true personality may take a little while to shine through. At home, she was comfortable being independent and was friendly and relaxed around other animals.

Foxy is looking for a patient adopter who will give her the time and space she needs to feel safe and confident. With a little understanding and a lot of love, this sweet girl has the potential to be a wonderful companion and show you the happy, playful Foxy her family knows and loves.

33504.name: Ronnie
33504.summary:
Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

My foster writes: Ronnie may be the world's best cuddle buddy. All she needs to be happy is laying next to her person, getting some belly rubs or ear scratches. She enjoys going on long walks but also happy laying around. She's crate trained and will sleep late in the morning, but will do a little tippy-tap dance when she first sees you waking up. She's crate trained and almost completely housetrained. Her face is a little lopsided, which only adds to her appeal as she stares at you with a little wink and head tilt. Ronnie will make the perfect addition to a home, filling it with unending love.

Good with other pets?
Ronnie has lived with other pets in her previous home. At the shelter, she politely greeted another dog through a gate and then kept to herself. We always suggest slow introductions with resident pets, and we offer a 2-week trial adoption to help you see if Ronnie is a good fit with your family. Since ACC doesn't test with cats, we're not sure how she'd do with new feline friends, but we can help you with tips and advice!

Good with kids?
Due to the behavior seen in the care center, we feel that Ronnie may be intimidated by young children. She needs a slow approach and time to warm up. She should never be forced to interact with new people, and should be allowed to greet and initiate an interaction at her own pace. Older, gentle children should have an in-depth interaction prior to adoption.

How is my health?
Ronnie has some health concerns that our staff will discuss with you.

How are my leash manners?
Ronnie pulls moderately on the leash and is nonreactive to humans and dogs on walks.

What is my behavior assessment?
Ronnie has been assessed as a Level 2 dog. She would love to meet an adopter that will allow her to decompress at her own pace. With patience and understanding, Ronnie would make a very special companion!

70570.name: Camila
70570.summary:
A volunteer writes:
Camila is a lovely dame sporting the iconic"little black dress". She is seven year old, already spayed and known to us from kitten hood when she arrived into our care as there were too many kitties in her house. Camila was adopted but after a few years, she survived a house fire and was adopted again as her family had to relocate. And now, Camila is back to her "alma mater", this time found in the street by a Good Samaritan. So much happening in just seven years...Camila is a real trooper. She has a little independent streak which I guess helped her to shine though all the changes in her life. She is assertive while friendly and welcoming, loving her cuddles, playing excitingly(without overstimulation) and reigning over the community(playroom)room she shares with two(neutered) gentle cats. Camila has lots of character and there is so much to say about her. Camila is a bit on the thin side. She has a good appetite and her weight will catch up while in our care and when she will be hopefully once again a cherished pet. Camila is already spayed, aced her behavior evaluation and is reasonably and apparently healthy beside having senior teeth. She could go home today for still many years of shared fun and love. Come and meet Camila very soon at the Manhattan Care Center.


A volunteer writes: There are currently 4 cats (mixed gender) in our community cat room. When I was in there, there were all very relaxed and peacefully coexisting. They had relaxed body language and accepted all pets. They were all sweet a bit reserved at first but gentle souls.

79206.name: Nerra
79206.summary:
Pop-Up Promo! ACC is over capacity, so I'm currently living in a pop-up crate. My adoption fees are waived, and my adoption comes with a $50 Chewy gift card. 

Meet Nerra!
Nerra is an older, active, and affectionate girl who was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her. She enjoys being close to her people and has a cuddly side, especially at night, but she is still learning how to feel safe and comfortable in the world around her.

My Ideal Home
Nerra would do best in an adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace. She is looking for a calm, structured environment with someone who understands she may need time to adjust and feel secure. She is already crate trained and knows several cues including sit, come, down, paw, and more, which can be a great foundation for continued positive reinforcement training.

Good with Other Pets?
Nerra has shown strong reactions to other dogs and cats on walks, including lunging and vocalizing. She has also been noted to become distressed when smelling other dogs in the home environment. Because of this, she would do best as the only pet in the home.

Good with Kids?
Due to her reported reactivity and handling sensitivities, ACC recommends an adult-only home for Nerra at this time.

Things to Know
Nerra is a smart dog with a medium energy level who enjoys routines like daily walks and time spent with her people. She can pull on leash and react to other animals and strangers, so she will need patient handling, slow introductions, and ongoing training using only force free, reward based methods. She is crate trained and generally does well in structured environments, but she can become reactive when restrained or when her paws are handled, so respectful, choice-based care is important.

Fun Fact
Nerra's favorite place is wherever her people are, especially if that means she gets to curl up and cuddle at the end of the day.

80205.name: Geneva
80205.summary:
What my friends at ACC say about me:
The staff think I would do best in a home where there are no other cats.
I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.
I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!
I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles! I enjoy being held and carried around.
I may enjoy casually batting at a toy mouse every now and then, but my favorite activity is snuggling on my favorite person's lap!

A volunteer writes: Geneva has Cerebellar Hypoplasia and it might be the first thing you notice about her. Cerebellar Hypoplasia means a wobbly gait, but there's nothing wobbly about Geneva's heart. Originally brought to us after being found by a building garbage, she was adopted and, since she cherishes people, was able to make her way for a little while. Geneva found living with another kitty to be a tad bit too stressful and additional factors outside of anyone's control has brought her here. She was loved and adored, her previous guardian even describing her as clingy in her efforts to get close to the people she loves. I think a lot of people would love a clingy cat and we are determined to help Geneva find her forever people. Geneva is certainly doing her part by making her way to the front of her condo whenever someone shows a glimmer of interest in her. She's hoping the next person to show interest in her will be the one who chooses to bring her home with them.

Another foster writes: A lovely chonkster with beautiful golden eyes that match her beautiful fur. A very playful gal that loves toys and treats, but most importantly a good scritch. She would be a loving companion as she keeps you company around the house, asking for pets with her adorable meows.

My foster writes:

92577.name: Damu
92577.summary:
As a part of OG's Starting Five, I will receive a year of free pet food from Royal Canin. VCA will also provide one free year of unlimited exams with a CareClub Access Plan.

A volunteer writes:
Damu is a handsome and well groomed  senior, a Tuxedo who has been beautifully cared for by his former family who owned him since kittenhood. Life changes lead to Damu being surrendered to the care center. Damu is said to love being loved. He would be friendly, loves to be loved, well mannered, smart, gently playful and all together a nice cat with all. His former owner describes him as purrfect!I met Damu the day after his arrival at the care center. He was very sweet, a little shy but trusting, coming for pets and leaning his head into my hand, even purring softly. He looks a little sad now(I hope it is temporary), not eating much and may be realizes that he lost all what really mattered to him:his people and his home. Damu is already neutered, looks great and active, did very well on his behavior evaluation, is apparently healthy (he does have senior teeth though), has a normal senior panel and could go home today, with you, as your very own beloved best friend. Ask to meet Damu when you visit us at the Manhattan Care Center.






What my friends at ACC say about me:
I love getting pets!
I'll need daily interaction with you as I get used to my new life.
I am a sweet, social, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!
Cheek and chin scratches make me so happy!
I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.
I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

93247.name: Kipu
93247.summary:
My foster writes: These two 4 and 5 year old boys are lovers ready to settle down into a forever home. While shy at first, these two have settled in nicely to our life wanting pets and food, and not afraid to use their voice to tell you. They have loud engine purrs that start immediately when you pet them. They'd do well in a quieter home, one that is patient and will allow them to come out of their shell in their own time.

My foster writes: Kipu and Shakul are sweet, loving, calm cats who would make an excellent addition to any home. They love to snuggle each other, and provide a very comforting presence in the room. I have loved my time with them dearly.

These two boys are a bit shy at first but with lots of love they won't take long to start asking for pets and being the cutest pair! Shakul is a bit braver than his brother and won't hesitate to rub his face on everything in site. They both love scratches and will purr as loud as can be. Patience and love is all these two need to be the best companions ever.

They both loveeee to get their butts scratched and stick it way up in the air when getting them. Very playful once they've warmed up

93251.name: Pich-Kim
93251.summary:
My foster writes: While I am initially very, very shy, I am a top notch love bug! I need a safe, hidden space to feel safe, but will warm up from there. The key to my heart (and letting my nervous system know I am safe) is to brush me- I love being brushed! Once I get used to that, I will be open to pets. Before you know it, I will be ready to cuddle, especially before bedtime.

My foster writes: Meet Pich-Kim, a shy but curious little explorer! This quiet, gentle kitten loves finding cozy spots to rest and slowly warms up to new friends. Once he feels safe, his playful and adventurous side shines-he's ready to discover a forever home full of patience, love, and cozy corners to explore!

Pich-Kim tolerates attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Pich-Kim may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.
What my friends at ACC say about me:
I have lived with cats in my previous home.
I would like a home where there is another cat that I can play with!
I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.
I am looking for a home with a patient person.
I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

95683.name: Tigress
95683.summary:
My foster writes: Tigress is a sweet and confident kitty with the cutest trills! She will greet you at the door and will go up to visitors to ask for pets. When she arrived at the apartment, she immediately popped out of her carrier and explored the whole place. She loves head and cheek rubs and will sometimes jump up on your lap for cuddles and see what you are doing. You will always have a furry shadow following you around the apartment or laying beside you!

A volunteer writes: Tigress hopes she's wording her questions the right way and if she isn't, she hopes you'll give her the chance to try again. Asking only for our time the best way she knows how, by reaching her paws out her door to tap people walking, Tigress is feeling the pressure to stand out in the busy shelter. This is her second time here and though it's through no fault of her own, Tigress had a lot to tell me about it. She stretched out her paws to rest them on my arm as a helpful little reminder when I visited with her neighbor but she simply glittered with joy when I opened her door. Tucking her chin to her chest, she kind of flopped on her side for some cuddles when I opened the door. A cuddly girl who is really only asking for a chance, we hope you'll come in and offer her one soon.
